founderRule: a mistake observed once must be permanently registered and prevented across every later applicable attempt

entries.mistake: The selected Mool control on the Personal root was visible but non-interactive.
entries.rootCause: The dock used a decorated Container without button semantics or a tap owner.
entries.prevention: Mool is a semantic button that opens the shared main-action panel on root, chooser and downstream owners.

entries.mistake: Downstream Mool navigation jumped directly to the root and Back restored only a safe chooser instead of the exact current step.
entries.rootCause: Main-action launch and Mool-home navigation were conflated in one dock tap.
entries.prevention: Dock Mool first opens a modal panel; Close, system Back and gesture Back dismiss without route or session mutation.

entries.mistake: Cab to Chat to Back returned to Bike because the Ride type query was lost.
entries.rootCause: The Chat return route reused an incomplete Ride URI instead of the canonical selected type.
entries.prevention: Canonicalize the Ride booking return route from session.selectedType and test Bike, Auto and Cab independently.

entries.mistake: A legacy journey test expected removed standalone Pay and direct Mool-root behavior after the MVP projection changed.
entries.rootCause: The test duplicated an old action list instead of following the locked six-action projection and current navigation contract.
entries.prevention: Run the Personal projection gate and traverse the production Mool panel in the legacy journey regression.

entries.mistake: Windows PowerShell 5.1 converted a benign Flutter Kotlin warning on stderr into a terminating NativeCommandError after Gradle completed the APK but before wrapper packaging.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper was invoked through powershell.exe with ErrorActionPreference Stop and stderr redirection.
entries.prevention: Invoke Android build wrappers only through PowerShell 7 pwsh, verify shell major version before Flutter, and never retry merely because Windows PowerShell classified native stderr as an exception.

entries.mistake: The profile APK contained the correct define, version and checksum but emitted no candidate or ready-state marker.
entries.rootCause: main.dart and JourneySession guard provenance logs with kDebugMode, which is false in profile mode.
entries.prevention: Device-review mode must emit non-secret candidate and ready-state markers in profile, with source tests and the connected-device runtime gate required before acceptance.

entries.mistake: The regression-check self-test wrapped an external pwsh invocation in try/catch and then reported its own false failure after the child correctly exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: A native process nonzero exit sets LASTEXITCODE but is not reliably a catchable PowerShell exception in the parent process.
entries.prevention: All external-process pass and expected-rejection checks capture and assert LASTEXITCODE explicitly; try/catch is reserved for in-process PowerShell exceptions.

entries.mistake: Widget and host tests passed the proposed Mool interaction, but the production-router path in the installed APK sent a real Ride-chooser Mool tap to Social.
entries.rootCause: The acceptance tests proved isolated callback/harness behavior without requiring the same transition through the production router and installed device screen.
entries.prevention: Every bottom-rail transition requires a production-router test and a real OPPO tap with before/after UI trees; host-only evidence cannot qualify device navigation.

entries.mistake: Social used Mool to toggle its rail into main-action mode and used Back to open that mode instead of returning through route history.
entries.rootCause: Social owned a local _moolOpen state that conflated main-action navigation with Social sub-action presentation.
entries.prevention: Social keeps only Social sub-actions in its rail; Mool pushes the stable hub and Back handles content depth before normal route history.

entries.mistake: Buy replaced its sub-action rail with main actions and defaulted root exit to Social with openMool=1.
entries.rootCause: The Buy dock and JourneySession exit owner encoded Mool as a transient menu hosted by Social rather than the stable Mool hub.
entries.prevention: Buy keeps only Buy sub-actions; Mool pushes the hub, exact Buy state is retained, and root fallback is the hub rather than Social.

entries.mistake: Codex implemented a modal main-action panel even though a transient pop-up/menu is not the founder-approved production Mool navigation model.
entries.rootCause: The prior fix optimized the local missing-tap symptom without first freezing one global hub/rail/back behavior matrix across Social, Buy and all downstream owners.
entries.prevention: The stable existing Mool hub is the only Personal main-action owner; modal, palette and rail-toggle main-action menus are statically rejected.

entries.mistake: Different Mool controls used push, go, Social aliases, modal sheets and local toggles, so identical user intent produced incompatible history and state preservation.
entries.rootCause: There was no single versioned global Mool destination and return contract enforced across all reachable production owners.
entries.prevention: Apply the 22-case global contract, preserve exact origin with stack navigation, and reject every inconsistent destination pattern before build/device work.

entries.mistake: A Dart formatter command used Unix backslash line continuation and failed at PowerShell parse time.
entries.rootCause: Shell syntax from a different platform was used in the Windows PowerShell workspace.
entries.prevention: Multi-file PowerShell commands define an explicit string array and invoke the native command with argument splatting, then assert LASTEXITCODE.

entries.mistake: The C02 Mool fallback referenced requestedOrigin from a sibling branch where that local variable was out of scope, causing compilation failure.
entries.rootCause: The origin was declared inside the first section-is-mool conditional but reused inside the following production-Mool conditional.
entries.prevention: Resolve the route origin once in the shared route-builder scope and require the production-router C02 test to compile before broader tests.

entries.mistake: A historical evidence test expected a full prose sentence that Markdown wrapped across a newline.
entries.rootCause: The assertion coupled the regression identity to presentation line wrapping instead of a stable evidence token.
entries.prevention: Evidence tests assert stable state identifiers and short invariant phrases or normalize whitespace before matching.

entries.mistake: The C02 expected-rejection wrapper searched raw colored PowerShell exception output and missed a blocker phrase split by ANSI formatting and line wrapping.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper treated terminal-rendered output as plain stable text.
entries.prevention: Strip ANSI escape sequences and collapse whitespace before asserting expected native or PowerShell failure messages.

entries.mistake: The revised C02 wrapper normalized the in-memory join of redirected child PowerShell error objects, but the detailed blocker text existed only in their rendered output.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell ErrorRecord conversion differed between in-memory string joining and formatting during Set-Content.
entries.prevention: Invoke PowerShell-script negative gates in-process and inspect the caught Exception.Message; reserve redirected text plus LASTEXITCODE for native processes.

entries.mistake: The widened C02 suite retained an Eat exposure test that tapped personal-mool-panel-home after the production modal owner had been deleted.
entries.rootCause: The focused test selection covered the new global contract but did not include every older vertical exposure test that encoded the rejected modal interaction.
entries.prevention: Every global navigation child runs the complete ui_v2/universal test directory; vertical tests assert one Mool tap invokes the hub callback and never search for a deleted modal control.

entries.mistake: The widened C02 suite retained a compact accessibility test that tapped personal-mool-panel-home after the production modal owner had been deleted.
entries.rootCause: The accessibility matrix validated target sizes but also carried an obsolete two-tap modal sequence outside the focused navigation tests.
entries.prevention: The complete compact accessibility matrix is mandatory for navigation children and treats Mool as a single operable hub transition with no popup dependency.

entries.mistake: A correction patch placed an accessibility-test context block under the Eat-test file update, so apply_patch rejected the entire edit.
entries.rootCause: Two independently inspected source excerpts were combined into one target-file hunk without rechecking the file boundary.
entries.prevention: After a context rejection, register it and retry with one narrowly scoped target-file patch per inspected excerpt; never transpose context between files.

entries.mistake: The first corrected universal-suite attempt launched flutter test from the repository root, where no pubspec.yaml exists.
entries.rootCause: A repository-level regression gate and an app-level Flutter command were combined without changing the command working directory.
entries.prevention: Flutter and Dart app commands always run with apps/mobile as the explicit working directory; repository PowerShell gates use an absolute repository root when combined in the same evidence cycle.

entries.mistake: The complete journey suite retained a Work return test that expected the deleted personal-mool-panel-buy control.
entries.rootCause: A legacy journey test encoded Mool as a transient palette and was outside the earlier universal-directory regression run.
entries.prevention: Global navigation children run the complete production-router journey list; Work Mool must assert stable-hub arrival followed by exact Back restoration.

entries.mistake: The complete intent suite retained a Social-hosted Mool palette scenario and then failed to reach the stable hub from the Book screen.
entries.rootCause: One mixed test combined the later-child Social rail defect with a C02 Book return assertion, hiding which production owner controlled the failed transition.
entries.prevention: Split stable-hub Book return from the later Social child; C02 proves Book-to-hub-to-exact-Back through its production route and never treats Social as a main-action palette.

entries.mistake: The first isolated Book production test opened /app/book/home, which production legacy-route containment intentionally redirects to the safe Book chooser.
entries.rootCause: The replacement test reused a legacy Book-home route without checking the production containment map, then mistook the absent legacy book-search widget for a Book Mool wiring failure.
entries.prevention: Production navigation tests use an allowed exact production owner such as /app/book/doctor and assert its owner before testing Mool; contained legacy routes are tested only as containment cases.

entries.mistake: After the chooser stopped opening the deleted Mool popup owner, mvp_action_choice_root_v2.dart retained an unused personal_mool_root_v2.dart import.
entries.rootCause: The behavior hunk removed the last symbol use but did not remove its adjacent import in the same edit.
entries.prevention: Every navigation-owner removal runs affected-file static analysis; imports of the removed owner are deleted in the same ticket before completion.

entries.mistake: The first C03 scope-state patch used a long C02 necessityProof sentence that did not exactly match the stored JSON, so apply_patch rejected the complete update.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-field JSON patch relied on copied rendered output rather than verifying each exact target string immediately before editing.
entries.prevention: Scope-state transitions use small independently verified hunks; exact JSON values are queried immediately before each patch and the scope gate validates the result.

entries.mistake: A C03 read-only rg inventory included a guessed uaw_personal_mvp_dock_projection_parity_fix2_test.dart path that does not exist.
entries.rootCause: A presumed successor filename was passed to rg without first discovering it from the filesystem.
entries.prevention: Test inventories are built from rg --files or Get-ChildItem discovery; guessed successor filenames are never passed as required paths.

entries.mistake: A C03 static absence check found zero removed Social-menu symbols as intended, but unhandled rg exit 1 was surfaced as a failed command.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper treated ripgrep's no-match status as an execution failure instead of the success condition for a forbidden-pattern absence check.
entries.prevention: Forbidden-pattern checks explicitly accept rg exit 1 as zero matches, reject exit 0 as a found blocker, and reject exit codes greater than 1 as execution errors.

entries.mistake: The rewritten Social dock parity test imported flutter/semantics.dart for Tristate, but the current Flutter SDK exposes Tristate from dart:ui.
entries.rootCause: The import was inferred from semantic usage instead of reusing the proven dart:ui show Tristate pattern already present in C02 tests.
entries.prevention: Tests comparing SemanticsData flagsCollection values import dart:ui show Tristate and affected-file analysis runs before widget tests.

entries.mistake: The first C03 parity test searched for a standalone semantics node labeled Open Mool home, but the label was merged around the keyed rail control and the finder returned none.
entries.rootCause: The test asserted semantic tree shape rather than reading the SemanticsData of the stable keyed interaction owner.
entries.prevention: Accessibility tests read semantics from the keyed production control with tester.getSemantics and assert its label, button and selection properties without assuming merge boundaries.

entries.mistake: The first C03 active-video test tapped the visible title text at a point covered by the fixed bottom rail, so no video watch owner opened.
entries.rootCause: ensureVisible considered the text within the scroll viewport but did not reserve the fixed rail's bottom occlusion zone.
entries.prevention: Social list interaction tests use the proven scroll-to-clear-bottom helper, reserving the fixed rail height before tapping a card target.

entries.mistake: The corrected keyed Mool semantics assertion expected only Open Mool home, while the merged SemanticsData label correctly also contained the visible child label Mool.
entries.rootCause: The assertion changed finder strategy but remained coupled to the exact merged label serialization.
entries.prevention: Keyed merged-label assertions verify the invariant navigation phrase and required visible label tokens rather than exact newline serialization.

entries.mistake: After system Back correctly closed an active Social video, a subsequent Social Mool push followed by Back did not restore the Social screen in the production-router test.
entries.rootCause: The stable Mool hub delegated system Back with PopScope.canPop=true. In this chained GoRouter case the platform pop left the hub mounted, while the header's explicit leaveMool callback popped exact history correctly; the hub did not own both Back sources through one contract.
entries.prevention: The stable Mool hub uses PopScope.canPop=false and routes every system Back through the same leaveMool callback as its header. C03 asserts visible owner, PopScope ownership, Navigator stack state and exact Videos restoration before device work.

entries.mistake: The first REG-033 diagnostic assumed GoRouter 17.3.0 routeInformationProvider URI must change after context.push, so it failed on the still-visible Social URI even though the Personal hub had opened.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic conflated the externally reported URI with imperative push-stack state; this app does not opt into URL reflection for imperative APIs.
entries.prevention: Imperative push and Back tests prove the visible route owner and Navigator.canPop stack state; routeInformationProvider URI is asserted only for go/replace transitions or when URL reflection is explicitly enabled and gated.

entries.mistake: The first REG-033 fix deferred the Personal hub's veto callback by one frame, but system Back still left the hub mounted after the Social inline-video sequence.
entries.rootCause: The attempted fix changed the destination hub callback even though the source-isolation diagnostic later proved header Back already worked and the stale system-Back registration belonged to Social's prior inline PopScope state.
entries.prevention: When system Back fails but the same owner's header Back succeeds, isolate and replace stale source PopScope registration before changing the destination owner's working onBack callback.

entries.mistake: The first post-edit C03 formatter used --set-exit-if-changed, so dart format correctly normalized one changed test file but surfaced exit 1 as a failed command.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed the mutating initial-format step with the later no-diff verification mode.
entries.prevention: After edits, run dart format in normal mutating mode first; only the subsequent clean-tree formatting verification uses --output=none --set-exit-if-changed.

entries.mistake: The second REG-033 fix replaced Social's PopScope element when inline depth closed, but the following hub system-Back still left the hub mounted.
entries.rootCause: The investigation blamed stale source registration even though the destination hub still delegated platform Back with canPop=true; changing the source could not unify the hub's system and header Back paths.
entries.prevention: When a destination header Back succeeds but its system Back fails, first compare whether the destination PopScope delegates or explicitly owns platform Back; do not mutate the prior screen unless destination ownership is already identical.

entries.mistake: The first expected C03 boundary-rejection wrapper matched the exact three blockers, then failed because 2>&1 was placed after a completed if statement and PowerShell parsed it as a command name.
entries.rootCause: Stream redirection and Tee-Object were appended to a compound statement instead of wrapping the complete script block or attaching redirection to an invoked command.
entries.prevention: Evidence wrappers place compound logic inside an invoked script block and redirect that invocation, or write validated output with Tee-Object inside the block; redirection never trails a completed if/try statement.

entries.mistake: REG-20260806-028 recurred when an exploratory search for a reusable qualified-matrix runner found no source match and raw rg exit 1 was again surfaced as command failure.
entries.rootCause: The earlier prevention wording and usage were applied only to forbidden-pattern checks, not to every ripgrep search where zero matches is a valid discovery outcome.
entries.prevention: Every rg invocation declares whether zero matches is valid. Discovery and absence searches wrap exit 1 as an explicit ZERO_MATCH result, while required-match inventories reject it; raw rg is used only when at least one match is contractually required.

entries.mistake: The first C03 qualified-matrix classification used Windows path prefixes directly in PowerShell -match patterns, so sequences such as \u were parsed as invalid regex escapes and emitted repeated non-terminating errors.
entries.rootCause: Literal normalized test paths were classified with regex even though no pattern matching was required, and their backslashes were not regex-escaped.
entries.prevention: Literal path inventories use StartsWith/Contains with OrdinalIgnoreCase or normalize separators to forward slashes before regex; raw Windows paths are never inserted into -match patterns.

entries.mistake: After the C03 affected git diff check passed, its success marker was appended to the evidence log with PowerShell Add-Content instead of apply_patch.
entries.rootCause: Command-generated log capture and authored evidence text were conflated; the latter remains a file edit even when the target is only an artifact log.
entries.prevention: Tool stdout may be captured by the invoking test/gate command, but any authored or appended evidence text is created with apply_patch; Add-Content, Set-Content and shell write helpers are not used.

entries.mistake: The first C04 multi-file line-range inventory treated a single nested range as a different PowerShell array shape, so later files produced Argument types do not match and were not read.
entries.rootCause: The inspection wrapper depended on PowerShell's implicit unrolling of nested arrays and passed ambiguous object types into Math.Min instead of normalizing every range and numeric bound.
entries.prevention: Multi-file excerpts use explicit per-file Get-Content/Select-Object commands or normalize every bound to [int] inside a strongly shaped range object; a generic nested-array switch wrapper is never used for required complete inventory.

entries.mistake: The first C04 widget test set the Buy session to Medicine before mounting BuyV2Screen, then incorrectly expected that state to survive the screen's declared initial Shop state application.
entries.rootCause: The test bypassed the production interaction sequence and did not account for BuyV2Screen.initState applying its initialDestination contract during mount.
entries.prevention: Buy state-preservation tests establish the nested destination after mounting through the real Buy rail, or pass the matching initialDestination explicitly; they never seed a conflicting session state before screen initialization.

entries.mistake: The first C04 focused run retained screen04-rail-eat in a Buy continuity test even though C03 removed Social's main-action palette and Mool now opens the stable Personal hub.
entries.rootCause: The test's first Mool tap was updated conceptually but its next interaction key was not reconciled against the current hub owner before the run.
entries.prevention: Any journey rewritten from the deleted Social or Buy palette asserts personal-mool-root-v2 immediately after Mool, then uses mool-action-* keys; forbidden old palette keys are included in the child static check.

entries.mistake: The C04 final gate batch first discovered that the clean-at-HEAD Screen 01 source already mismatched its accepted SHA-256 lock, so a pre-existing repository invariant surfaced late and caused the parallel final-gate wrapper to report C04 failure without the other gate results.
entries.rootCause: C04 did not capture the approved-UI-lock gate as a distinct pre-implementation baseline before dependency-graph work, and independent final gates were combined with Promise.all where one rejection masked direct reporting of the others.
entries.prevention: Any ticket touching the application dependency graph runs and preserves check-approved-ui-locks.ps1 before implementation and again after it. A clean-at-HEAD pre-existing mismatch remains a separately reported release blocker, is never repaired by editing an accepted screen, and does not replace an affected-path diff proving the child made no protected-file change. Independent final gate results are collected without fail-fast masking.

entries.mistake: REG-045 referenced the intended 21-locks-projection-gates.log path before checking whether the fail-fast parallel wrapper had actually created it, causing the regression-memory gate itself to reject the registry.
entries.rootCause: The expected Tee output path was treated as durable evidence based on command construction rather than verified with Test-Path after the failed orchestration call.
entries.prevention: Every evidence path is verified as an existing repository file before it is added to the regression registry. If a failed wrapper did not retain its log, the observed failure is reconstructed with apply_patch first and only then referenced.

entries.mistake: The first authored C05 static test forbade the stable shared-dock-mool key itself rather than only the rejected context.go('/app/social') behavior inside that action block.
entries.rootCause: The assertion targeted an easy source token without distinguishing stable interaction identity from the obsolete route callback that C05 must remove.
entries.prevention: Navigation source tests retain stable keys and scope forbidden-route assertions to the exact action block or callback pattern; a behavior removal never asserts deletion of the interaction identity unless the contract removes the control.

entries.mistake: A C06 provenance search supplied docs/quality/*C06* as a Windows path argument, so Windows rejected the path with error 123 and the required discovery command exited nonzero after returning only partial results.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style wildcard was embedded inside a required Windows path component instead of using rg file discovery or a -g include glob against the containing directory.
entries.prevention: Windows filename discovery uses rg --files followed by an explicit pattern, or searches a literal containing directory with -g include globs; wildcard path components are never passed as required rg path arguments, and required discovery must exit zero.

entries.mistake: The first C06 U01-U22 inventory repeated REG-048 by supplying artifacts/quality/uaw-personal-mvp-global-mool-bottom-rail-navigation-fix1-* as an rg path argument, producing Windows error 123 after the new regression had already been registered.
entries.rootCause: The prevention was remembered for the docs argument but not mechanically applied to every path token in the later compound command; useful output from other components also obscured the nonzero overall result.
entries.prevention: Before execution, every rg path token is verified as a literal file or directory with no wildcard. Wildcards are permitted only in -g include filters or a second rg pattern over rg --files output, and no compound discovery is accepted if any component exits nonzero.

entries.mistake: The first C06 protected-boundary wrapper reached the exact Screen 01 hash rejection but falsely failed its own assertion because a dot-wildcard regex did not bridge PowerShell line wrapping between the expected and actual hashes.
entries.rootCause: Expected-failure output was matched in its formatted multiline form instead of first stripping ANSI sequences and collapsing whitespace as the permanent memory already requires.
entries.prevention: Expected-failure process output is converted to plain text, ANSI controls are removed and all whitespace is collapsed before invariant tokens are matched; dot wildcards never bridge formatted PowerShell lines.

entries.mistake: A C06 pre-build inspection combined a successful prior-wrapper read with an optional rg search for state-transition tokens, but did not explicitly accept zero matches, so the overall command exited 1.
entries.rootCause: The optional absence search was appended to a compound inspection without capturing rg exit 1 as a valid zero-result outcome, despite the permanent zero-match rule.
entries.prevention: Every optional or absence rg call is isolated, captures its exit code, reports exit 1 as an explicit zero-match result and rejects only codes above 1; required-match inventories still require exit 0.

entries.mistake: A final standalone C06 APK gate was launched through pwsh -File with a parent-shell RuntimeDefine array; the native process boundary flattened later values into positional arguments and parameter binding failed.
entries.rootCause: An array-valued PowerShell parameter was treated as though it retained array identity across a new native pwsh process instead of being constructed or splatted inside that process.
entries.prevention: Array-valued PowerShell parameters are passed in-process with named splatting or constructed inside a repository runner; parent-shell arrays are never supplied directly through pwsh -File.

entries.mistake: The first C06 OPPO capture helper printed PACKAGE_PRESENT=False even though the retained XML contained the package, because a single-quoted PowerShell literal unnecessarily escaped its double quotes with backslashes.
entries.rootCause: Backslashes were treated as PowerShell escape characters inside a single-quoted string, where they remain literal and therefore changed the token being searched.
entries.prevention: Exact XML token checks use single-quoted PowerShell strings with unescaped double quotes, and helper self-reporting is reconciled against the retained XML before acceptance.

entries.mistake: C01-C06 gates classified PersonalMoolRootV2 as a stable Mool home because it used a dedicated route and preserved Back history, but the real OPPO screen remained a navigation-only launcher/menu rejected by the founder.
entries.rootCause: Acceptance distinguished modal versus route mechanics without distinguishing a durable product home from a page whose primary and only purpose is choosing another route.
entries.prevention: Mool-home acceptance forbids the rejected launcher copy and navigation-only root structure, requires a durable Mool home/content contract, and treats a dedicated route that only chooses another route as a launcher/menu regardless of modal mechanics.

entries.mistake: The first read-only Mool-home screenbook search spanned the entire screenbook and produced thousands of irrelevant matches, so tool output was truncated and could not serve as a complete inventory.
entries.rootCause: Filename discovery and content inspection were combined without limiting content search to the exact approved Screen 04 and directly relevant generated audits.
entries.prevention: Screenbook discovery enumerates filenames first, then reads exact approved files; content searches use restrictive filenames/patterns and bounded results, and truncated output is never accepted as complete evidence.

entries.mistake: A narrowed C07 screenbook inventory piped directly from a statement-form foreach block to Format-List, causing a PowerShell empty-pipeline parser error before any file was read.
entries.rootCause: Statement-form foreach output was treated like a parenthesized pipeline expression without first assigning or wrapping its results.
entries.prevention: Statement-form loop output is assigned to an explicit array or wrapped in a subexpression before piping; small required inventories prefer explicit per-file reads.

entries.mistake: The first post-REG-056 verification guessed config/codex-development-regression-memory.json, so the evidence check ran but the required registry parse targeted a nonexistent file.
entries.rootCause: The repository-owned registry filename was reconstructed from memory instead of being taken from AGENTS.md, the owning checker or exact filename discovery.
entries.prevention: Required machine-state and registry paths are read from the repository contract or owning checker, or discovered exactly; guessed config filenames are forbidden for acceptance checks.

entries.mistake: Repeated founder instructions required production-grade Mool bottom-rail navigation with complete main/sub-action wiring and no pop-up/menu launcher, but C01-C06 still qualified host-side while OPPO showed the same navigation-only question-and-grid launcher.
entries.rootCause: Founder language was not converted into a durable instruction-to-assertion scenario ledger, forbidden-behavior contract and blocking device acceptance matrix before implementation and build; route ownership and Back history were incorrectly treated as proof of the requested product outcome.
entries.prevention: Every founder-visible navigation directive must map to a versioned scenario-ledger row, a static forbidden-implementation contract, a production-router visible-owner/state test, a named OPPO screenshot/hierarchy step and a machine state that remains unimplemented_or_unverified until all are green. Route existence, dispatch or canPop alone cannot prove implementation.

entries.mistake: An ad hoc post-gate summary queried the nonexistent regressions property instead of entries, so PowerShell null coercion misleadingly reported one entry and false membership even though the authoritative checker passed with 58 entries.
entries.rootCause: The JSON collection name was assumed and the query did not assert that the property existed before coercing it to an array.
entries.prevention: JSON summaries enumerate or schema-check root properties before querying collections, fail explicitly when the required property is absent, and never accept null-to-array coercion as count or membership evidence.

entries.mistake: The C07 preimplementation gate correctly rejected the launcher, but its outer wrapper searched formatted child-PowerShell error text and falsely missed an expected multiword token split by rendering controls and line formatting.
entries.rootCause: REG-050 normalization was approximated at the rendered-output layer instead of avoiding formatted output and asserting the caught structured exception message.
entries.prevention: Expected PowerShell rejection gates run in-process and assert caught Exception.Message or another structured field; formatted error-stream output is evidence only and is never the acceptance source.

entries.mistake: A C07 Mool-route source inventory combined quoted alternatives in one rg command, returned exit 1 with no output, and had not declared whether zero matches was acceptable.
entries.rootCause: REG-051's explicit required-versus-optional search rule was not applied before launching the compound route inventory.
entries.prevention: Route inventories use isolated literal rg searches. Required searches assert exit 0 and at least one match; optional absence explicitly maps exit 1 to a named zero-result and rejects codes above 1.

entries.mistake: A C07 command running from apps/mobile gave dart format repository-root-relative apps/mobile paths; formatting failed, then a successful app-relative analyzer masked the compound command's earlier failure.
entries.rootCause: REG-021's working-directory rule was not applied to every command component and the compound wrapper did not capture each component exit independently.
entries.prevention: Commands running in apps/mobile use only lib and test relative paths; repository-relative paths run only from the repository root. Every compound validation component records and checks its own exit before the next component runs.

entries.mistake: A required search for a proposed Social production owner key included lib and test; its only match was the new test assertion itself, producing a false-positive source validation.
entries.rootCause: Production implementation proof and test-coverage discovery were combined in one search scope.
entries.prevention: Required production-owner, route and implementation-token searches target lib only. Test matches are reported separately and can never satisfy production-source existence proof.

entries.mistake: The C07 Continue test guessed a nonexistent social-tab-feed key; the follow-up source-only required search returned exit 1 but was appended to an unrelated excerpt read without explicit zero-result handling.
entries.rootCause: The selected-control key was inferred from wording rather than copied from production source, and the isolated required-search rule was not applied to the verification retry.
entries.prevention: Widget keys are copied from lib source or an already-proven contract. Required source-key searches run alone, capture exit status and report a named missing-key failure for exit 1 before any replacement assertion is authored.

entries.mistake: A C07 suite inventory listed the real ui_v2 directories, then attempted a required read of guessed test/ui_v2/social and failed after partial output because that directory does not exist.
entries.rootCause: A category name was inferred from product ownership instead of selecting only paths returned by the verified filesystem inventory.
entries.prevention: Test-suite paths come only from the immediately verified directory or rg --files inventory. When no category directory exists, protected suites are selected by exact discovered filenames in a separate required step.

entries.mistake: The first C07 protected-Social cycle selected files by product wording and included screen04_social_operational_baseline_test.dart, a matchesGoldenFile screenshot suite, instead of the established non-golden 16-case runtime owner.
entries.rootCause: Protected-suite membership was inferred from filenames instead of reusing the exact prior qualified suite and checking each candidate for matchesGoldenFile.
entries.prevention: Protected runtime cycles reuse exact previously qualified test owners and exclude every matchesGoldenFile source unless the current ticket explicitly authorizes golden verification. Failed golden output and diagnostics are preserved without baseline updates.

entries.mistake: A C08 prebuild inspection attempted to read a guessed C06 numbered build-runner filename and returned a missing-path error before showing only a separate wrapper excerpt.
entries.rootCause: The prior artifact filename was inferred from an expected evidence sequence instead of selected from an exact directory inventory.
entries.prevention: Prior evidence and runner filenames are discovered first with an exact literal directory inventory or rg --files. Only a path returned by that inventory is used in a separate required read, and a missing guessed path invalidates the compound inspection.

entries.mistake: The new C08 OPPO capture helper initially used package=double-double-quote-com.moolsocial.app-double-double-quote as its UIAutomator XML needle, which could falsely report that the app package was absent.
entries.rootCause: Double quotes were unnecessarily doubled inside an already single-quoted PowerShell string literal.
entries.prevention: UIAutomator XML needles use the exact raw attribute token with unescaped double quotes inside a single-quoted literal. Every new device helper is source-inspected for its exact package token before first execution.

entries.mistake: The first C08 pure-capture helper invocation unconditionally checked LASTEXITCODE even though its capture branch executed no native action, causing a false OPPO action failure before capture.
entries.rootCause: Native-process status was read outside the branch that owned the process, allowing a null or stale value to represent the current action.
entries.prevention: Device helpers initialize an explicit action exit code to zero and assign it immediately after every branch-owned ADB command. A pure capture branch never consults LASTEXITCODE from unrelated prior work.

entries.mistake: During Chat-thread qualification, a Mool coordinate was used while the Android IME visibly covered the bottom rail because UIAutomator still exposed hidden app semantic bounds and did not reliably inventory the keyboard package.
entries.rootCause: App accessibility bounds were treated as visible hit-test proof through a system overlay, and keyboard absence was inferred from incomplete UIAutomator package data.
entries.prevention: After composer focus or text entry, visually confirm or query active IME state. When the IME is present, Back closes it first and a fresh screenshot/hierarchy must prove the app control is visible before its coordinate is used. Hidden app semantics never establish tappability through an overlay.

entries.mistake: After REG-070 was registered, the next draft-thread return visibly reopened the IME, but three device actions were batched without inspecting the new frame, so none of the named Mool or Chat route captures actually changed the app route.
entries.rootCause: The newly registered IME prevention was not applied immediately because navigation actions were batched across a focused draft-thread return without an intermediate screenshot decision.
entries.prevention: After a composer draft exists, device navigation uses a strict one-action, one-screenshot, one-IME-decision loop. Route coordinates are never batched across a draft-thread return, and any capture whose visible owner does not match its intended name is rejected as route evidence.

entries.mistake: A planned reversible 140 percent OPPO font-scale check attempted a protected system-setting write without first proving shell WRITE_SETTINGS authority; after the write was rejected, finally attempted an unnecessary restore write even though no mutation succeeded.
entries.rootCause: ADB connectivity was mistaken for global settings write authority, and cleanup was unconditional instead of guarded by a verified mutation-success flag.
entries.prevention: Global device-setting tests require a read-only capability or permission preflight, or explicit founder-performed setup. Cleanup runs only when a verified mutationSucceeded flag is true. A security rejection is a final no-bypass device hold and is never retried by escalating or weakening device policy.

entries.mistake: The checksum-matched r60.8 candidate exposed a clickable in-bounds Shorts rail control while Create was selected, but a real OPPO tap left the Create owner and selection unchanged; C07 host qualification had not made this cross-subaction device sequence an explicit acceptance row.
entries.rootCause: Visual inspection proved that Social Create had auto-focused its composer and the Android IME covered the bottom rail. UIAutomator exposed stale hidden app bounds, and the coordinate hit the IME. The process root cause was declaring a product failure without visual hit-test confirmation.
entries.prevention: Social rail acceptance still requires pairwise visible-owner transitions, but every composer-capable source first proves the rail is visually exposed. If an IME is present, Back closes it and a fresh frame is captured before the rail tap. Accessibility bounds behind an overlay can never establish a product defect.

entries.mistake: Social Create auto-focused its composer and opened the IME, but the existing hidden-control prevention was not applied; a tap on stale rail semantics was then misclassified as an r60.8 product defect and premature device rejection.
entries.rootCause: The IME prevention was scoped too narrowly to Chat drafts, device actions were batched into Create without visual inspection, and a visible-owner mismatch was classified before confirming that the intended control was physically exposed.
entries.prevention: Every composer-capable owner uses one action, one screenshot and one IME decision. A device rejection requires visual proof that the intended target is exposed at the tap coordinate. Social Create-to-any-rail transition closes IME first and captures the newly visible rail before tapping.

entries.mistake: The post-C08 queue inspection rendered the complete parsed universal-action batch as JSON, exceeding the output boundary and truncating the result, so it could not establish complete queue state.
entries.rootCause: A large repository queue object was serialized wholesale instead of discovering root property names and reading only bounded status fields or one child record at a time.
entries.prevention: Large JSON state is never fully rendered for planning or acceptance. Inspect root property names first, then query named scalar summaries and bounded child projections with explicit counts; a truncated rendering is rejected and never used as evidence.

entries.mistake: A post-registration wrapper invoked the PowerShell regression-memory checker, which visibly passed, then inspected stale LASTEXITCODE and falsely threw before the bounded queue inspection.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper treated LASTEXITCODE as the status of a PowerShell script invocation even though no new native process status was owned by that invocation.
entries.prevention: Capture the success of a PowerShell script or function immediately with the PowerShell success channel or an explicit returned result. LASTEXITCODE is consulted only immediately after a native executable invocation that owns it; a visible checker pass cannot be overwritten by stale native status.

entries.mistake: A post-C08 reconciliation command printed the complete large ACTIVE-CODEX-HANDOFF.md file together with machine-state discovery, exceeded the output boundary and was truncated.
entries.rootCause: The known large append-only handoff was read as one unbounded output instead of using its table of contents or exact current-section markers and bounded ranges.
entries.prevention: Large append-only handoffs are never printed wholesale into a tool result. Discover headings first, then read only exact current sections in bounded ranges; if a complete read is mandated, page through bounded non-overlapping ranges and verify line coverage before relying on it.

entries.mistake: The first Superadmin/workspace-membership discovery searched guessed top-level services and functions paths that do not exist, so ripgrep returned exit 2 and invalidated the compound discovery despite valid matches from other paths.
entries.rootCause: Repository category names were inferred instead of selecting search roots from a verified top-level directory inventory.
entries.prevention: Every multi-root repository search uses only literal paths returned by an immediately preceding directory inventory. Missing-root exit 2 invalidates the compound result; useful partial matches are retained only as leads and the required search is rerun separately against verified roots.

entries.mistake: The first REG-078 registration patch omitted the required leading plus marker on two Add File content lines, so apply_patch rejected the entire atomic patch before any file changed.
entries.rootCause: A multiline patch string was not mechanically inspected to ensure every added-file content line carried an addition marker.
entries.prevention: Before applying a patch that adds a file, inspect the patch payload so every content line, including wrapped prose, begins with plus. An atomically rejected patch is registered and its unchanged target state is confirmed before retry.

entries.mistake: The first SAM-R01 focused typecheck failed because the immutability test cast a readonly membership projection directly to a mutable array type, which TypeScript correctly rejected.
entries.rootCause: The negative mutation test expressed an intentionally unsafe runtime operation without first crossing an explicit unknown boundary, so the test harness violated the strict type contract it was meant to verify.
entries.prevention: Negative tests that intentionally violate readonly or branded compile-time contracts cross an explicit unknown boundary into the smallest structural mutation interface. Focused strict typecheck must pass before any compiled test execution.

entries.mistake: The first SAM-R01 focused-test wrapper included recursive temporary-directory cleanup in the same command and was rejected by command policy before any compile, test or filesystem mutation occurred.
entries.rootCause: A disposable compilation strategy was chosen even though ticket-scoped compiled test output can be retained safely as evidence, introducing an unnecessary destructive cleanup action.
entries.prevention: Focused compiled tests write to a new exact ticket-evidence directory and retain outputs. Test commands contain no recursive delete or cleanup; any later removal requires a separately authorized, exact, verified target and is never needed for acceptance evidence.

entries.mistake: The first retained SAM-R01 focused-test command passed the guessed phase name tests to the regression-memory checker, whose declared ValidateSet permits only general, implementation, build and device, so the command stopped before compilation.
entries.rootCause: The gate parameter vocabulary was inferred from the current activity instead of read from the checker declaration or reused from an already passing invocation.
entries.prevention: Gate parameter values are copied from the checker's declared ValidateSet or an immediately preceding passing command. Test execution uses the verified implementation phase unless the checker adds a dedicated test phase.

entries.mistake: The first complete SAM-R01 backend regression used the default per-test reporter for 332 tests twice, exceeded the tool output boundary and produced a truncated rendering even though the wrapper completed with exit zero.
entries.rootCause: Full-suite result volume was not estimated and the command emitted every passing test directly instead of retaining full TAP logs and printing only bounded summaries.
entries.prevention: Complete test suites capture each cycle's full reporter output into a separate retained ticket log, record the native exit code immediately, and emit only the bounded final summary. A truncated rendering is never the sole acceptance evidence.

entries.mistake: The first SAM-R01 final identity command emitted hashes through an auto-sized table that hid the SHA-256 column and piped ADB directly into Select-String, which rendered InputStream objects instead of package identity lines.
entries.rootCause: Machine identity evidence relied on presentation formatting and native pipeline coercion instead of explicit scalar key-value output captured immediately after each native process.
entries.prevention: Hashes, versions, codes and device identity are emitted as explicit one-field key=value lines. Native output is first captured into a string array with its exit code recorded immediately, then filtered as strings; tables and native-to-cmdlet streaming are not acceptance evidence.

entries.mistake: The initial SAM-R05 test helper represented an omitted optional category or service-area query by explicitly passing undefined, which would violate the repository's exactOptionalPropertyTypes contract; review caught it before the first compiler attempt.
entries.rootCause: Missing-field behavior was modeled as an undefined value instead of structural property absence.
entries.prevention: Tests for absent optional fields use explicit omit controls and conditional object spreads so the property is not present. Helpers never pass explicit undefined to exact optional properties.

entries.mistake: The initial SAM-R06 transition test helper spread approve defaults after caller overrides, so a negative test's invalid expiresAt value would have been silently replaced by the valid default; review caught it before compilation.
entries.rootCause: Test object construction order allowed defaults to shadow the exact invalid field the test intended to exercise.
entries.prevention: Negative-test helpers apply defaults first and caller overrides last. Every negative test verifies that its intended invalid field reaches the production function, either through construction-order review or an explicit captured-input assertion.

entries.mistake: The first Buy acceptance-policy reuse search combined source and planning roots but omitted docs/delivery, so its four-match count did not cover the exact ticket contract and could not establish a complete inventory.
entries.rootCause: Implementation-owner discovery and human-contract discovery were combined in one manually assembled path list with different completeness requirements.
entries.prevention: Reuse assessment runs two explicit searches: production source roots only for implementation ownership, and the complete exact docs/config roots for authority and contract references. Counts are labeled separately and neither can satisfy the other's proof.

entries.mistake: The first Buy ticket activation combined a new evidence document and two JSON state transitions in one large patch whose tool result was truncated during context compaction, leaving success unknown until a separate read-only reconciliation.
entries.rootCause: Independent durable state mutations were bundled into one oversized operation without an immediate per-file parse-and-value verification boundary.
entries.prevention: Create evidence and mutate each durable state owner in separate small patches, then parse and verify every changed file immediately. A truncated or missing tool result never establishes mutation success.

entries.mistake: A resumed Buy-ticket command passed guessed parameter -Activity to the regression-memory checker even though REG-082 already requires the declared -Phase interface; PowerShell rejected it before the checker ran.
entries.rootCause: The active context relied on remembered checker semantics instead of mechanically rereading and copying the script parameter declaration before invocation.
entries.prevention: At every resumed context boundary, read the checker parameter block and copy its exact parameter names and allowed values into the invocation. Prior memory or summaries never substitute for the declaration.

entries.mistake: The initial Buy policy receipt hashed a revision with direct JSON.stringify, so a semantically identical normalized revision with different property insertion order failed receipt-integrity validation in the first focused cycle.
entries.rootCause: A persisted integrity digest was coupled to JavaScript object construction order instead of a canonical serialization contract.
entries.prevention: Every persisted or cross-boundary JSON digest uses a recursively key-sorted canonical projection, and tests revalidate the digest after reconstructing or normalizing the same semantic object.

entries.mistake: The first green Buy SLA contract rejected effectiveFrom equal to command occurredAt even though the exact ticket offers Effective now for future orders and rejects only backdating.
entries.rootCause: A condensed preselection phrase was interpreted more narrowly than the explicit tap-to-tap human journey and failure-state contract.
entries.prevention: Before acceptance, map every explicit human-journey choice and failure state to a named assertion. Exact ticket semantics outrank condensed planning paraphrases; green tests are superseded when their expectation encodes the wrong product rule.

entries.mistake: The first Ticket 2 authority read combined a 208-line portfolio and 449-line parent journey in one complete-output command, exceeded the tool budget and was truncated, repeating REG-077.
entries.rootCause: Per-file line counts were treated as evidence that their combined rendered output would remain bounded, and the established paged-read rule was not applied at the resumed ticket boundary.
entries.prevention: Complete reads of multiple substantive documents use separate verified non-overlapping pages with explicit total-line coverage. Individually manageable files are never combined when aggregate output may cross the tool budget.

entries.mistake: A Ticket 2 source search printed that apps/superadmin did not exist but still passed the absent path to rg, which exited 2 and invalidated the compound result.
entries.rootCause: The existence preflight was presentation-only; the search argument list was separately hard-coded instead of derived from successful preflight objects.
entries.prevention: Search arguments are mechanically derived only from verified root objects filtered to exists=true. A printed failed preflight path can never remain in the subsequent command.

entries.mistake: The first complete dirty-inventory fingerprint used ordinary git status -uall, causing retained Chrome-profile long paths to emit a massive warning stream and truncate the tool rendering.
entries.rootCause: The inventory command neither enabled invocation-local long-path support nor separated and bounded Git stderr before rendering results.
entries.prevention: Dirty inventory uses invocation-local Git long-path support, captures stdout and stderr separately, and emits only scalar count, digest and warning count. Status bodies and warning streams are never rendered unbounded.

entries.mistake: The initial Ticket 2 resolver normalized authorization, aggregate and time but trusted typed context IDs and declaredBusy without runtime validation; post-cycle review caught the adapter-boundary gap.
entries.rootCause: Compile-time request types were treated as runtime evidence for a public domain boundary.
entries.prevention: Every public command or query normalizes every runtime field after authorization and before business-data selection. Negative tests cross an explicit unknown boundary to exercise malformed adapter input.

entries.mistake: The initial Ticket 3 source shallow-froze deserialized snapshot provenance without exact nested schema validation and did not bind the audit source fingerprint back to the selected provenance revision.
entries.rootCause: A nested persisted discriminated union was treated as trustworthy after its containing snapshot had been typed.
entries.prevention: Every nested persisted union gets exact key, discriminator, identifier, version and digest normalization after deserialization; audit source hashes are explicitly rebound to the normalized selected provenance.

entries.mistake: Two Ticket 3 assertions called the progress projector separately in a discriminator condition and variant-field expression, so TypeScript could not narrow the second independent result and stopped the first test typecheck.
entries.rootCause: A discriminated-union result was treated as though narrowing applied across repeated function evaluation.
entries.prevention: Capture each union-returning function result exactly once, assert or branch on its discriminator, and read variant-only fields only within that same narrowed value. This also prevents accidental double evaluation.

entries.mistake: The initial Ticket 3 restart normalizer cross-linked createdAt, receipt completedAt and audit occurredAt but did not reassert that creation was no later than assignmentStartsAt, allowing coordinated timestamp tampering to preserve equality.
entries.rootCause: Evidence-field equality was treated as a substitute for revalidating the underlying business-time ordering after deserialization.
entries.prevention: Restart normalization revalidates every original temporal business invariant in addition to format and evidence-field equality. Coordinated-tamper tests change all linked timestamps together.

entries.mistake: The initial Ticket 3 override source exposed only the override revision effective time, so a future required global revision could be paired with an earlier override and bypass composite source-effectiveness validation.
entries.rootCause: A composite source inherited the leaf override's time instead of calculating the conjunction boundary across every required revision.
entries.prevention: Composite source eligibility becomes effective only at the maximum effective time of all required components, with fixtures where the base is later than the leaf override.

entries.mistake: A 482-line Ticket 4 test Add File patch exceeded the tool-result context, so its success or failure was unknown until a separate read-only existence, size and tail reconciliation, repeating the unknown-result class registered by REG-088.
entries.rootCause: The test was emitted as one oversized atomic patch instead of a scaffold followed by bounded section updates with immediate verification.
entries.prevention: Any new source or test expected to exceed about 300 lines is created as a small scaffold plus bounded section patches. Verify line count or tail after each section and strict-typecheck after the final section; a truncated result never proves success.

entries.mistake: The first REG-100 registration patch omitted an addition marker on wrapped Add File prose, so apply_patch rejected the atomic patch, exactly repeating REG-079.
entries.rootCause: The Add File patch was submitted without a mechanical per-line marker check even though the permanent memory already required it.
entries.prevention: Keep every Add File patch file-local and inspect every content line, including blank and wrapped prose lines, for a leading plus marker before submission; verify target existence immediately afterward.

entries.mistake: Ticket 4 focused-cycle output used ../../../artifacts from backend/functions, which resolved to the authorized workspace root rather than the production repository's durable artifacts tree.
entries.rootCause: A parent-traversal path was counted mentally and passed to an evidence-producing command without printing and validating its resolved full path first.
entries.prevention: Durable evidence-producing commands use absolute canonical production-repository paths, or preflight and validate the resolved full path before execution; relative parent traversal is prohibited for retained evidence.

entries.mistake: The Ticket 4 cycle-2 command passed guessed phase tests to the regression checker, which rejected it before execution, repeating REG-089 despite the exact resumed invocation being available.
entries.rootCause: The command substituted an activity label for a declared checker phase instead of copying the immediately available ValidateSet value.
entries.prevention: Print the checker ValidateSet, copy the chosen value, and emit it before every invocation. Ticket test work always uses -Phase implementation; tests is never a valid phase.

entries.mistake: A comparative replay-path rg command lost nested quotes, reached ripgrep as an invalid regular expression and established no evidence.
entries.rootCause: An exact code phrase was unnecessarily expressed as a regex through nested JavaScript and PowerShell quoting layers.
entries.prevention: Exact code comparisons use rg --fixed-strings with a PowerShell single-quoted literal. A nonzero search is inspected for syntax or path errors and never accepted as absence by itself.

entries.mistake: The initial provider-readiness replay returned before rechecking exact operator and supply-workspace binding, while the new-command path performed those checks.
entries.rootCause: Idempotent command authorization was treated as sufficient for external domain bindings that are supplied separately from the command envelope.
entries.prevention: Every replay validates all tenant, actor, workspace and participant bindings supplied outside the idempotency envelope before returning; only time-varying capability eligibility may remain new-command-only.

entries.mistake: The initial provider-readiness restart normalizer spread typed runtime objects, allowing undeclared aggregate, revision, receipt or audit fields to survive normalization and be returned as accepted state.
entries.rootCause: Required-field validation was mistaken for an exact runtime schema, and object spread preserved data that the TypeScript interface could not describe.
entries.prevention: Persisted aggregate roots and every nested record require a plain-object exact key set before field validation. Restart tests inject personal telemetry at every schema level and require rejection.

entries.mistake: A hardened Ticket 4 typecheck attempted ../../../scripts from backend/functions, resolved outside the repository and stopped before compilation, repeating the parent-counting failure in REG-102.
entries.rootCause: The canonical-path rule was applied to generated evidence but not generalized to the gate script in the same qualification command.
entries.prevention: All remaining gate, source, output and reporter paths in qualification commands are absolute canonical production-repository paths. Relative parent traversal is prohibited for every operand, not only outputs.

entries.mistake: A direct strict TypeScript compile used absolute backend source paths but ran from the repository root, so package-local Node types were not discovered and the ticket source was not meaningfully checked.
entries.rootCause: Absolute file operands were mistaken for a substitute for the package working directory and TypeScript type-resolution context.
entries.prevention: Direct package compiler calls run with the exact package root as working directory, or explicitly declare package type roots. Checker/compiler/source operands remain absolute and dependency state is not changed.

entries.mistake: The Ticket 4 completion Add File patch escaped a patch marker into prose, creating the literal joined text paused+declarations until immediate read-back caught it.
entries.rootCause: Patch-syntax ambiguity was handled by escaping the marker into content rather than rewriting the content line and verifying the rendered file.
entries.prevention: Read the opening and closing sections after every prose Add File and inspect for marker contamination or joined words. Patch markers are never escaped into intended content.

entries.mistake: A Ticket 5 qualification command ran from backend/functions but prefixed diagnostic reads with backend/functions again, producing missing-path errors and false zero line/test counts even though the later absolute-path TypeScript compile passed.
entries.rootCause: The absolute-path rule covered the compiler operands but not every diagnostic operand in the combined command, and nonterminating PowerShell errors did not control the final native exit code.
entries.prevention: Every operand in a combined qualification command uses an absolute canonical path. Any PowerShell read error invalidates its scalars and is checked independently; a later native success cannot overwrite it.

entries.mistake: The first Ticket 5 source validator assumed Ticket 1 and Ticket 2 shared the commandFingerprint:revisionId result-digest formula; Ticket 1 hashes its complete canonical revision, causing authentic global sources to fail 15 of 18 focused tests.
entries.rootCause: A receipt convention observed in Ticket 2 and Ticket 4 was generalized across an existing owner without reading Ticket 1's actual completion and restart validation code.
entries.prevention: Before composing contract receipts, inspect every owner's exact digest rule. A cross-owner validator asserts only common evidence and digest format unless each owner exports a verifier; owner-specific digest semantics remain owner-owned.

entries.mistake: The first green Ticket 5 aggregate was scoped to a source set but not to the exact global family or override ID, allowing independent policy subjects to share one approval lineage.
entries.rootCause: The containing policy set was treated as the independently effective governance target even though global families and override IDs evolve independently within it.
entries.prevention: Every governance lineage binds an immutable smallest target subject: exact family for global policy and exact override ID for schedule policy. Proposal and restart validation reject cross-subject references.

entries.mistake: The first REG-112 append retyped an expected test path with governance in mixed case, so apply_patch rejected the entire registry mutation.
entries.rootCause: Stable registry context was retyped from memory instead of copied exactly from an immediate tail read.
entries.prevention: Registry append context is copied verbatim from an immediate tail read. Parse JSON and verify the exact final ID after every append before dependent work.

entries.mistake: The Ticket 6 dependency assessment invented implementationDisposition dependency_hold, which the delivery-lock checker rejected before it could evaluate execution authorization.
entries.rootCause: Human business-state language was placed in a closed machine enum without reading the checker's declared allowed values.
entries.prevention: Machine enum values are copied from the checker's declared allowed set. Dependency holds use dedicated state, missing-dependency and backendWriteAuthorized fields; they never invent implementation-disposition values.

entries.mistake: The corrected Ticket 6 state validation passed guessed -TicketId to the delivery-lock checker, which has no such parameter, repeating the declared-interface failure class in REG-089 and REG-103.
entries.rootCause: The scope gate's CandidateId concept was transferred to a different checker without reading that checker's parameter block.
entries.prevention: Read and copy each checker parameter block immediately before its first invocation. Delivery lock uses -RequireTicketSelectionAssessment; ticket identity uses only the scope gate's declared -CandidateId.

entries.mistake: Ticket 6 remained installed as a disclosed scope-gate ticket while all execution flags were false, violating the checker's canonical closed-state model.
entries.rootCause: A dependency-held successor was treated as an active execution selection instead of a portfolio-level hold outside the one active scope slot.
entries.prevention: Dependency candidates stay in dedicated ticket and portfolio hold state. The MVP scope gate returns to awaiting_next_ticket_classification with no ticket ID and no registered successor until dependencies clear.

entries.mistake: The 08:00 dirty-inventory command redirected Git stdout and stderr to two files under the user temp directory outside the exact authorized C:\GUARANTEED OUTCOME workspace.
entries.rootCause: A generic temporary-directory capture pattern was used without applying the workspace scope boundary to intermediate diagnostic files.
entries.prevention: Diagnostic output is captured in PowerShell variables or canonical repository artifact paths. Environment temp directories and all out-of-workspace intermediates are prohibited; exact accidental files are verified and removed.

entries.mistake: The Ticket 5 public source inspector trusted typed source-set version and target revision/audit schema values enough to allow coercible deserialized runtime scalars before post-qualification review caught it.
entries.rootCause: Cross-owner structural checks validated relationships but did not normalize every primitive at the public adapter boundary, repeating the class guarded by REG-095.
entries.prevention: Public source composition normalizes source-set version, target revision position and schema, audit schema, common receipt scope and discriminators before returning any reference. Negative tests cross unknown with coercible and tampered runtime values.

entries.mistake: The durable YouTube sequencing state still described the 5 August compliance reply as prepared_unsent after Gmail showed that it was sent and YouTube had issued a later 6 August request for a valid Android application link.
entries.rootCause: Repository machine state was treated as current external-mailbox authority without reconciling the live thread, current draft inventory and provider reply chronology.
entries.prevention: Before reporting or acting on an external-provider email state, reconcile the live thread, Gmail draft inventory and repository machine state. A sent message, later provider reply or empty draft inventory supersedes an older prepared_unsent scalar and requires a durable state update before another reply or distribution decision.

entries.mistake: The authorized Firebase Hosting deployment was attempted only after source qualification, without first proving that the saved Firebase CLI session could resolve the exact hosting target, and the attempt stopped on expired credentials.
entries.rootCause: Deployment authentication readiness was treated as an implicit environment property instead of a read-only preflight condition that must be reconciled before announcing the live-write phase.
entries.prevention: Before any authorized Firebase Hosting release, run a non-mutating authenticated project or hosting-target resolution preflight, record the exact project and site, and stop before the deploy command if reauthentication is required. Never bypass or source alternate credentials.

entries.mistake: A read-only live/local normalization audit was submitted with malformed nested escaping for CRLF replacement and PowerShell rejected the command before execution.
entries.rootCause: A JavaScript-composed PowerShell command mixed backtick escapes and nested quoted strings without first reducing or mechanically validating the expression.
entries.prevention: Inline PowerShell passed through another language avoids nested escape-sensitive newline literals. Use environment newline normalization, byte-level comparisons, or a repository script; if composition is unavoidable, inspect the exact rendered command before execution.

entries.mistake: The first post-deploy live audit searched only for the dotted spelling SuperMandi Tech Pvt. Ltd. and incorrectly reported zero matches while production still served the undotted spelling SuperMandi Tech Pvt Ltd.
entries.rootCause: Retired-brand absence was asserted with one fixed literal instead of a normalized family covering punctuation, spacing and case variants, even though the founder's request was identity-semantic rather than character-literal.
entries.prevention: Every retired public identity or forbidden-copy gate uses a case-insensitive normalized regex covering optional punctuation and whitespace variants, and also positively extracts the surviving footer and structured legal-name values from every live route. Zero matches for one literal is never sufficient evidence.

entries.mistake: After the founder offered approval, firebase login --reauth was invoked directly in the non-interactive task runner and Firebase rejected it before opening the sign-in flow.
entries.rootCause: User authorization was present, but terminal interactivity was assumed without preflighting whether the execution channel exposed a TTY.
entries.prevention: Interactive CLI authentication is never invoked in the non-interactive runner. With explicit founder approval, launch a visible user-controlled terminal for the exact reauthentication command, let the founder complete sign-in privately, and verify success afterward with a non-mutating project-resolution preflight.

entries.mistake: A bounded ripgrep search passed a Windows path containing * directly to rg, which does not expand that path glob in PowerShell and rejected it as an invalid filename.
entries.rootCause: Shell wildcard expansion behavior was assumed instead of using ripgrep's own -g filter against a real directory root.
entries.prevention: Ripgrep receives only existing directory or literal file roots. Filename selection uses rg -g patterns, while PowerShell-expanded path sets are avoided for evidence commands unless each resolved path is validated first.

entries.mistake: The 7 August retired-brand production release changed five canonical public pages but left their sitemap lastmod values pinned to 26 July or 5 August, and completion was claimed before checking the indexed Google snippet; Google continued to show the retired identity from its 26 July copy.
entries.rootCause: Character-level page qualification and live byte identity were treated as complete public-surface acceptance, while crawl freshness metadata and the indexed-result surface were omitted. The regression test reinforced the stale dates instead of binding lastmod to the latest significant page change.
entries.prevention: Every significant canonical public-page change updates that URL's truthful sitemap lastmod in the same ticket, tests the exact modified-date set, verifies the live sitemap after hosting release, and checks the indexed-vs-live state through Search Console when authorized. Live HTML correctness is not evidence that a search snippet has refreshed.

entries.mistake: The Google index refresh selection assessment added external_service_submission to implementationDisposition even though the delivery lock permits only reuse, configuration, thin_policy_adapter, test_only_acceptance and new_necessary_work; the scope gate failed before source edit.
entries.rootCause: An activity description was incorrectly treated as a machine enum without first copying the checker's closed allowed set, repeating the class prohibited by permanent machine-state rules.
entries.prevention: Before writing any closed machine enum, read the enforcing checker's exact allowed set and use only those copied values. External-service work remains in scope, dependencies and evidence fields; it never creates an unrecognized implementationDisposition value.

entries.mistake: The first Google index refresh ticket qualified and requested indexing only for the founder-screenshot Privacy URL, while current Google results still cross-associated MoolSocial and SuperMandi through the MoolSocial AI Overview and stale Home and YouTube API indexed copies.
entries.rootCause: Indexed-identity acceptance was scoped to one observed result rather than the semantic entity-separation outcome across both query directions, AI-generated result surfaces, and a domain-restricted retired-identity query.
entries.prevention: Every public identity disassociation release audits the primary brand query, the retired-entity query, and a site:owner-domain retired-identity query; records every owner-controlled URL and AI/result surface that still cross-associates the entities; clears only stale snippets rather than hiding valid pages; and requests reindexing for each affected canonical URL before completion.

entries.mistake: A YouTube Android-link readiness lookup searched the full repository root despite the workspace containing very large retained artifact trees, and the read-only command timed out before returning evidence.
entries.rootCause: The exact identifiers were bounded, but the search root was not. Known configuration, quality-document and candidate-evidence owners were not searched first.
entries.prevention: Evidence reconciliation searches known config, docs/quality and exact candidate directories first. Large artifacts/quality or repository-root searches require an explicit filename inventory and narrow -g filters; a full-dot recursive search is prohibited for routine readiness lookup.

entries.mistake: The first C09 OPPO audit command captured the read-only current-focus diagnostic by piping PowerShell output through Set-Content instead of using the repository-required patch or an owning evidence tool.
entries.rootCause: A diagnostic log was treated as ordinary command output even though redirecting it into a local repository file is still a file edit governed by the apply_patch-only rule.
entries.prevention: Shell commands may create tool-owned binary/device captures through adb pull, but may not create or edit local text evidence with Set-Content, Out-File or redirection. Text evidence is added with apply_patch after bounded in-memory inspection; command diagnostics remain in tool output unless an owning repository script writes them.

entries.mistake: C07 and C08 were qualified as a durable Mool Home even though the connected OPPO still showed a header Back arrow and a dominant Continue Social/Buy/Ride card after the user selected the bottom-rail Mool control.
entries.rootCause: Acceptance treated truthful area content, route preservation and scripted OPPO reachability as sufficient, but did not compare visible top-level ownership against the Buy root or reject return-sheet language and chrome on a selected Home destination.
entries.prevention: A bottom-navigation Home is qualified by visible ownership as well as routing: it has no header Back control, no dominant Continue-origin action, no origin-specific return-sheet copy and no selected-tab side effect. OPPO acceptance starts from at least Social, Buy and one nested non-Buy owner and compares the resulting Home frame against a first-class main-action root before any pass is recorded.

entries.mistake: C07/C08 declared all six Mool main actions reachable while the 720px OPPO initially exposed only Social, Buy and Eat plus a clipped Ride edge; Book and Work required an unannounced horizontal swipe.
