entries.rootCause: The compact widget test called ensureVisible on every keyed action and the device script deliberately swiped the rail, proving mechanical reachability while bypassing the first-frame discovery problem faced by a real user.
entries.prevention: Scrollable primary navigation must expose a persistent finite overflow or position cue, a meaningful next-action peek and semantic scroll context on first entry. Tests first inspect the untouched compact frame, then prove user-driven swipe, focus traversal and all-action reachability; programmatic ensureVisible is not accepted as discoverability evidence.

entries.mistake: A C09 dependency lookup was combined with an optional search for an existing CustomTransitionPage owner; the valid zero-match returned ripgrep exit 1 and made the compound read-only command fail.
entries.rootCause: The existing required-versus-optional search rule was not applied before composing the duplicate-owner lookup, repeating the zero-match ambiguity class.
entries.prevention: Required dependency searches and optional duplicate-owner searches run as separate commands. Every optional ripgrep search explicitly maps exit 0 to matches, exit 1 to a named zero-result and any higher exit to failure before its result is used.

entries.mistake: The first C09 host-gate command used apps/mobile as the working directory for Flutter while invoking repository PowerShell gates through unresolved relative scripts paths, so execution stopped before the first gate.
entries.rootCause: Two commands with different owning roots were combined without converting every repository-gate operand to its absolute canonical path, repeating the wrong-workdir class.
entries.prevention: Repository PowerShell gates always use absolute canonical script and repository-root paths. Flutter commands run separately with apps/mobile as their working directory; commands with different owner roots are never combined through relative operands.

entries.mistake: The first C09 focused Flutter cycle could not compile because the new Mool Home header used a const Row containing Flutter's non-const Semantics constructor.
entries.rootCause: Const was applied to the mixed parent subtree for optimization without verifying that every descendant constructor was const-capable.
entries.prevention: Mixed interaction and semantics subtrees keep their parent non-const; const is applied only to individually verified leaf widgets. Every UI patch runs focused compilation before a broad multi-file test cycle is treated as evidence.

entries.mistake: REG-20260807-134 put the command label flutter test in its gates array, and the regression-memory checker rejected it as a missing repository file.
entries.rootCause: The gates field was treated as a free-form list of enforcement activities instead of an existing-path list owned by the machine checker.
entries.prevention: Before appending a regression entry, copy the gates field shape from a current valid entry and verify every gate value resolves to an existing repository file. Command labels belong in prevention prose or test evidence, never in the path array.

entries.mistake: The first compiled C09 multi-file cycle failed the R15 fitment matrix because the Home summary repeated exact per-action labels such as Social while the bottom rail already owned the same visible labels.
entries.rootCause: Discoverability was addressed by adding non-interactive action chips without checking the existing single-label copy and semantics contract across the whole mounted screen.
entries.prevention: A persistent navigation rail is the only per-action visible and semantic label owner on its screen. Supporting Home content may describe the available family in a sentence, but does not duplicate individual navigation labels as separate chips, buttons or semantics nodes. The full copy/fitment matrix runs with every navigation change.

entries.mistake: The first C09 connected regression produced six failures because screen04_universal_v2_conformance_test.dart still expected Social Mool to expose the deleted screen04-world-ribbon and screen04-rail main-action controls.
entries.rootCause: C03 removed Social's main-action palette in production and added focused replacement tests, but the broader Screen 04 conformance file was not included or reconciled before C08 qualification.
entries.prevention: Every global navigation change searches the complete mobile test tree for removed owner keys, runs the full Screen 04 conformance file, routes cross-main-action journeys through PersonalMoolRootV2 mool-action keys and limits Social rail assertions to Shorts, Videos, Feed and Create.

entries.mistake: A follow-up optional search for the removed screen04-world-ribbon owner found zero production source matches, but the ripgrep exit 1 was not explicitly mapped and appeared as a failed command.
entries.rootCause: The optional-absence rule was again omitted from a single-purpose follow-up search despite REG-132.
entries.prevention: Every absence lookup uses an explicit three-way ripgrep wrapper: exit 0 reports matches, exit 1 reports a named zero-result and any higher exit throws. No bare optional rg command is allowed.

entries.mistake: The production router still passed the untrusted world query parameter into SocialUniversalV2, allowing /app/social?world=work to reactivate a removed non-Social presentation after C03 deleted the main-action ribbon.
entries.rootCause: Visible rail ownership was corrected, but the deep-link initialization boundary retained the legacy multi-world selector and was omitted from the static containment gate.
entries.prevention: Production Social initialization is canonical and ignores world overrides; only Social subactions may be selected from its query contract. Native Eat, Ride, Book and Work owners remain separately routed. The global navigation gate statically rejects queryParameters['world'] feeding SocialUniversalV2 and production-router tests cover adversarial world values.

entries.mistake: An optional search for existing Tristate or flagsCollection use in the Screen 04 conformance test returned the expected zero matches, but bare ripgrep surfaced exit 1 as a failed command.
entries.rootCause: The explicit optional-search wrapper was not used during a quick import decision, repeating REG-132 and REG-138.
entries.prevention: For the remainder of C09 no optional lookup uses bare ripgrep. Use a bounded file read when the target file is known, or the exact exit 0 matches / exit 1 named-zero / exit greater than 1 throw wrapper.

entries.mistake: The first rewritten Screen 04 Buy journey expected one Back from Mool -> Buy to return directly to Social, skipping the intentionally retained Mool Home route layer.
entries.rootCause: The test outcome was copied from the removed Social-hosted main-action ribbon instead of deriving the current explicit stack Social -> Mool -> Buy.
entries.prevention: Every navigation assertion writes the exact pre-action route stack first. Mool-launched main actions pop to Mool Home, and only the next platform Back restores the pre-Mool origin.

entries.mistake: The parameterized Social subaction restoration test pumped repeated MoolSocialApp widgets without unique keys or an unmount boundary, allowing the prior State object to override the next initial subaction.
entries.rootCause: New owner/session objects were created, but Flutter widget identity and State retention were not independently reset between loop cases.
entries.prevention: Parameterized app-router widget cases use a unique root key or pump an empty owner between cases, then assert the initial selected owner before the action under test.

entries.mistake: The Social world-query containment test guessed screen04-feed-workbench as its visible owner key, but that key does not exist in the production source.
entries.rootCause: A semantically plausible key was authored without first copying an exact existing source key or visible contract marker.
entries.prevention: Before asserting a production widget key, perform a required exact-source inventory and copy the owner key verbatim. Guessed keys are prohibited even when their names appear consistent.

entries.mistake: After REG-141 corrected one Social -> Mool -> Buy test, a second test in the same file retained the identical one-Back-to-Social expectation and failed with Mool Home correctly visible.
entries.rootCause: The new prevention was applied only at the reported line rather than searching and reconciling every same-file occurrence of the route sequence before retry.
entries.prevention: After registering a test-pattern regression, search the bounded target file for every structurally equivalent action sequence and update all occurrences before retry. A newly registered gate is applied globally within scope, not only to the first failing line.

entries.mistake: A read-only source-manifest lookup passed a Windows path ending in an asterisk as a secondary ripgrep operand, so native ripgrep rejected the filename and the diagnostic command exited 1.
entries.rootCause: The existing literal-root and -g prevention was applied to the primary roots but missed on one secondary documentation operand.
entries.prevention: Every ripgrep operand is verified as an existing literal file or directory. Filename matching uses -g filters even for secondary roots; one invalid operand invalidates the complete command and its output is never used as evidence.

entries.mistake: An optional bounded search for prior qualified-mobile runner summary strings found no matches, but bare ripgrep surfaced its normal exit 1 as a failed diagnostic command.
entries.rootCause: The mandatory exit 0 match, exit 1 named-zero and exit greater than 1 error wrapper was omitted again despite three earlier registered occurrences.
entries.prevention: For the remainder of C09 every optional ripgrep call uses explicit three-way exit handling. A bare rg invocation is reserved only for a lookup where at least one match is a required invariant.

entries.mistake: The first candidate-fingerprint probe used git status -uall at repository root, traversed the huge retained artifact tree and emitted Windows long-path warnings even though Git exited 0.
entries.rootCause: Dirty-state sealing was treated as one global enumeration instead of separating tracked status from a bounded untracked inventory for actual candidate inputs.
entries.prevention: Candidate sealing uses tracked status without untracked traversal plus explicit scoped untracked inventories for production runtime, active contracts, tests, scripts and current evidence. Retained historical artifacts are never globally traversed and are never APK inputs.

entries.mistake: The C09 positive-gate batch invoked the repository-global Buy backend boundary before reconciling a separately ticketed dirty acceptance-policy test, and the gate correctly rejected that unapproved backend owner.
entries.rootCause: The immediately preceding C07 global gate result was assumed to remain structurally reusable even though other authorized tickets had added backend contract files to the shared dirty workspace.
entries.prevention: Before global gate execution, inventory newly dirty owners and bind each to its active or completed ticket. Out-of-candidate protected-boundary failures are recorded as explicit expected rejections, excluded from the mobile source aggregate and never relabeled as passing applicable gates.

entries.mistake: The selected Mool Home item implemented its required no-op reselection with onPressed: () {}, which avoided navigation but violated the production interaction contract for empty visible callbacks.
entries.rootCause: The shared MoolDockAction model required a non-null callback and had no explicit disabled selected-root representation.
entries.prevention: MoolDockAction callbacks are nullable, dock semantics expose enabled state from callback availability and selected root items omit the callback. Empty callbacks are prohibited; no-op navigation is represented as an explicitly disabled current item.

entries.mistake: A multi-file apply_patch for C09 pre-build evidence contained an extra hunk delimiter before a new Update File header, so patch verification rejected the entire operation.
entries.rootCause: Too many independent evidence edits were composed into one patch without validating each file boundary and hunk transition.
entries.prevention: Pre-build evidence updates use small patches with one bounded hunk per file. Every file is read back and the source-manifest hash is recomputed only after all regression registrations and evidence edits settle.

entries.mistake: The C09 runtime aggregate included ignored machine-generated android/local.properties, so the wrapper's expected version rewrite appeared as post-build source drift.
entries.rootCause: The aggregate enumerated the Android tree without carrying forward the C08 exclusion for local.properties and other machine-specific generated metadata.
entries.prevention: Source seals exclude android/local.properties and ignored generated build metadata, assert their expected candidate values separately, and compare authored runtime aggregates before and after build. Generated transitions require an explicit disposition and never trigger an unapproved rebuild.

entries.mistake: The postinstall verifier piped a multiline dumpsys package scalar to Select-String, so one matching scalar caused the complete package dump to be emitted instead of four bounded identity lines.
entries.rootCause: Out-String collapsed line ownership before filtering, and the evidence formatter treated a multiline scalar like a line collection.
entries.prevention: Device evidence splits package output into lines before filtering or extracts anchored scalar values directly. Multiline Out-String values are never piped to Select-String for bounded evidence output.

entries.mistake: The installed-APK pull preflight piped adb pm path through Select-Object before testing LASTEXITCODE; the PowerShell terminal stage left the native exit scalar unset and a valid package path was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Native exit status and PowerShell output normalization were combined in one expression instead of preserving the native command boundary.
entries.prevention: Capture native output first, check LASTEXITCODE immediately, and only then pipe or normalize the validated array. Never evaluate native exit status after a PowerShell pipeline stage.

entries.mistake: The r60.9 Mool Home exposed internal engineering commentary including main rail, navigation available, stay fixed and without inventing as founder-visible customer copy.
entries.rootCause: Defensive implementation rationale was written into visible and semantic strings; R15 checked copy presence and fitment, the finite copy gate did not classify production language, and device qualification reviewed navigation before wording quality.
entries.prevention: Every visible and semantic string must express a customer goal, action, benefit or plain-language reassurance. The user-facing-copy gate blocks the C09 implementation phrases, C09 tests assert approved replacement copy and forbidden-term absence, and OPPO qualification requires an untouched-frame copy review before pass.

entries.mistake: A one-line design-system semantics patch included an explicitChildNodes context line that belongs to a different Semantics widget, so apply_patch rejected it before mutation.
entries.rootCause: Nearby context was inferred instead of copied from the exact current bounded source block.
entries.prevention: Even small patches copy their immediate current source context verbatim. Similar widgets elsewhere never supply assumed hunk context.

entries.mistake: The user-facing-copy PowerShell checker printed a pass, but orchestration then tested stale LASTEXITCODE and falsely threw Copy gate failed.
entries.rootCause: A native-command exit scalar was incorrectly used to validate a PowerShell script whose failure contract is a terminating error.
entries.prevention: Repository PowerShell checkers run independently and succeed when they return without a terminating error. LASTEXITCODE is checked only immediately after native executables and never after a PowerShell script invocation.

entries.mistake: The global Mool navigation checker bound the persistent horizontal overflow contract to the literal internal phrase Scrollable main actions, so replacing the rejected copy with customer-facing semantics caused a false navigation failure.
entries.rootCause: One compound static condition treated an exact implementation-oriented sentence as proof of behavior instead of checking customer-facing semantics and the overflow mechanics as separate invariants.
entries.prevention: Navigation gates require the approved customer-facing semantic prefix and independently require the horizontal scroll container, minimum tap target, persistent overflow cue and initial-frame overflow activation. Rejected internal copy is blocked by the user-facing-copy gate.

entries.mistake: The focused Flutter command used the inferred nonexistent path personal_mool_root_v2_r15_copy_test.dart, so C09 and C07 executed but the combined run failed during R15 test loading and produced no acceptable suite evidence.
entries.rootCause: A shorthand test label from prior evidence was expanded from memory instead of resolving its literal current path from the repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Every manually assembled multi-file test command resolves each literal path through rg --files first. A load-path failure invalidates the whole combined run even when other named tests pass, and the corrected command is rerun from the beginning.

entries.mistake: An affected-test discovery command repeated the registered Windows wildcard-operand failure by passing docs\quality\UAW-C09*.md directly to rg; the command returned exit 1 after partial matches from other operands.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed one intended filename filter into a list of literal roots instead of applying the already-registered literal-root plus -g rule uniformly to every operand.
entries.prevention: No rg command is accepted until every path operand is checked for wildcard characters. All filename patterns are expressed only with -g against existing literal roots, and any multi-root command with one invalid operand has all output discarded.

entries.mistake: An optional search for test paths inside the C09 source-aggregate manifest used bare rg and returned exit 1 when the manifest contained no matching test path.
entries.rootCause: The discovery probe incorrectly treated the presence of a test-path match as a required invariant even though the file's content type had not yet been inspected.
entries.prevention: Optional discovery never uses bare rg. Inspect bounded file content first or use an explicit wrapper that accepts exit 0 as matches, exit 1 as no matches, and rejects only exit greater than 1.

entries.mistake: The installed r60.9 journey exposed three incompatible bottom-navigation owners: Work subactions, Mool main actions and Social subactions; Work also retained a top-level header Back arrow and fresh launch restored a stale Workspace destination.
entries.rootCause: C09 corrected Mool destination and history behavior but qualified each destination-owned rail independently instead of enforcing one invariant global shell across every main destination and launch state.
entries.prevention: C10 statically and behaviorally requires one stable Mool/main-actions/Chat global dock on every main root, moves subactions into destination-local content controls, forbids top-level header Back, defaults fresh authenticated no-deep-link launch to Social, and qualifies exact state restoration on OPPO.

entries.mistake: A startup-route search included the nonexistent literal operand apps/mobile/lib/app.dart, causing rg to exit 1 after printing partial results from valid files.
entries.rootCause: Candidate filenames were assembled from a conventional Flutter layout assumption instead of being resolved from the current repository inventory before the multi-file command.
entries.prevention: Every explicit multi-file rg operand is existence-checked or sourced from rg --files before execution. One missing literal operand invalidates all partial output from the command.

entries.mistake: A required constructor inventory and an optional old-owner absence probe were grouped in one shell command; the expected zero-match exit from the second rg made the complete command fail after valid constructor output.
entries.rootCause: Required-presence and optional-absence queries with different exit contracts were composed without an explicit boundary and result mapping.
entries.prevention: Presence searches and absence searches run as separate commands. Every absence probe explicitly accepts rg exit 1 as a clean zero-match result and rejects only exit greater than 1 before it can become containment evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C10B analysis found an unused mool_theme import in the new shared navigation owner and an unused design-system import in the rewritten R14 cold-launch test.
entries.rootCause: Symbol ownership and the final test assertion changed, but the source and test import lists were not reconciled immediately after the move.
entries.prevention: Every source-owner move and test assertion replacement performs an import-usage review before qualification. Flutter analysis must pass with zero warnings before any focused widget output is accepted.

entries.mistake: REG-164 listed the command label flutter analyze in its gates array, but the regression-memory schema requires every gate value to be a repository-relative file path.
entries.rootCause: A validation command and its durable enforcing configuration were conflated while the registry entry was written.
entries.prevention: Registry gates reference only existence-verified repository files. Human-readable commands belong in evidence prose; analysis enforcement is represented by apps/mobile/analysis_options.yaml and the memory checker path.

entries.mistake: A C10B multi-file test reconciliation patch placed an empty hunk marker immediately before a new Update File header, so apply_patch rejected the complete operation before mutation.
entries.rootCause: Too many independent contract and test rewrites were composed into one patch and the final file transition was not structurally checked.
entries.prevention: Contract and test reconciliation patches are split into small file-bounded operations. Each patch ends with a complete hunk, is applied and read back before the next file group begins.

entries.mistake: Nine parameterized FIX2 route tests still tapped mvp-action-<section>-<subaction> keys after C10B moved those subactions from the retired chooser dock to local content cards.
entries.rootCause: The first test reconciliation updated the direct chooser and fitment blocks but missed a later parameterized downstream-owner block in the same file.
entries.prevention: When a navigation owner is retired, every key reference in the complete test file is inventoried before rerun. Subaction route tests tap mvp-action-choice-<id>, while only global destinations use mool-action-<section>.

entries.mistake: The first C10B static-gate edit used a double-quoted mvp-action-$id-back pattern, which would expand an unset PowerShell variable instead of testing the Dart source literally.
entries.rootCause: A Dart interpolation-shaped token was placed in a PowerShell double-quoted string without using a literal-safe invariant.
entries.prevention: Static source gates prefer exact literal owner tokens that contain no cross-language interpolation. The top-level Back rejection now checks the unique retired arrow icon token in the bounded action-choice source.

entries.mistake: The first C10C implementation moved Buy subactions into a new 50-pixel local tab row while also replacing the old Buy dock with the taller shared global dock, causing 13 compact-layout, overflow, geometry and hit-test failures in the full Buy screen suite.
entries.rootCause: Global and local navigation ownership was separated structurally without preserving the existing compact-screen vertical budget or reusing the established Buy header owner.
entries.prevention: Buy local destinations reuse existing header height instead of adding a second full navigation row. The complete Buy screen fitment suite, C10C journey tests and Flutter analysis must pass before C10C qualification or any APK/device action.

entries.mistake: A registry inspection queried a guessed regressions property and reported count zero even though the durable registry uses the entries property.
entries.rootCause: The JSON schema was inferred from the filename instead of reading the document's actual top-level properties first.
entries.prevention: Registry automation reads and validates the top-level schemaVersion, registryId and entries properties before counting, selecting or appending entries.

entries.mistake: A required registry read and an optional documentation lookup were grouped in one shell command, so the expected no-match exit from the optional lookup marked the complete command failed after valid registry output.
entries.rootCause: The already-recorded required-presence versus optional-absence command boundary was not applied to a documentation lookup during regression registration.
entries.prevention: Required registry reads and optional documentation searches always run separately; optional rg calls explicitly accept exit code 1 and reject only exit codes greater than 1.

entries.mistake: A Dart format command ran from apps/mobile but supplied paths prefixed with apps/mobile, so formatting reported that both files did not exist.
entries.rootCause: The command working directory and its path namespace were composed independently instead of resolving file operands relative to the selected working directory.
entries.prevention: Commands executed from apps/mobile use lib/... and test/... operands; repository-prefixed operands are reserved for commands whose working directory is the repository root.

entries.mistake: The header integration declared Semantics as const even though the repository's current Flutter SDK does not expose that construction as a const expression, preventing the focused test from compiling.
entries.rootCause: Const eligibility was assumed during a nested widget rewrite instead of being validated against the active Flutter SDK.
entries.prevention: Accessibility wrappers use the active SDK's supported const boundary, leaving Semantics non-const while keeping eligible leaf widgets const; focused compilation is mandatory before qualification.

entries.mistake: A patch payload intended to register the next C10C failures was assigned inside a tool script but never passed to apply_patch, producing no mutation and no useful output.
entries.rootCause: The orchestration wrapper omitted the final tool invocation after constructing the patch string.
entries.prevention: Every patch orchestration ends with and returns an awaited apply_patch call; the changed file is then read or validated before subsequent work.

entries.mistake: The first reconciliation of the repeated Help-tab test replaced the first matching Help tap with system Back instead of replacing the second tap after Help had opened, so the test returned to catalogue before asserting the assist view.
entries.rootCause: A repeated identical line was patched without enough surrounding state assertions to uniquely identify the intended occurrence.
entries.prevention: Edits to repeated interaction sequences use a bounded hunk containing the before-and-after view assertions; selected destination tabs remain no-op and system Back closes Help only after assist is asserted open.

entries.mistake: A grouped dock inspection supplied the nonexistent literal operand apps/mobile/lib/core/design/mool_tokens.dart, so the complete command failed after printing partial valid design-system output.
entries.rootCause: A conventional token filename was assumed and included without resolving it from the repository inventory, repeating the explicit-operand existence failure pattern.
entries.prevention: Every explicit search operand is existence-verified before use, and required source reads are not grouped with speculative token-file searches. Partial output from a command containing any missing operand is discarded as evidence.

entries.mistake: The first compact global-dock geometry used a 48-pixel surface with 2-pixel internal padding, but the glass border consumed another pixel per edge and reduced rendered navigation targets from the required 44 pixels to 42.
entries.rootCause: The nominal child constraint was calculated from padding alone without including the decorated surface border in the final rendered content box.
entries.prevention: Persistent navigation qualification measures the rendered keyed target, not only declared constraints. Compact glass insets include border width while preserving at least 44 by 44 pixels for every action.

entries.mistake: A combined command invoked scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 from apps/mobile, where that relative path is unresolved; PowerShell emitted a non-terminating command-not-found error while the stale process exit code allowed a misleading successful command result and the intended Flutter tests did not run.
entries.rootCause: Repository-root and app-root commands with different path namespaces were combined, and native-process LASTEXITCODE was incorrectly used to validate a PowerShell invocation lookup failure.
entries.prevention: Repository gates run in a repository-root command and Flutter commands run separately in apps/mobile. PowerShell script invocation success is enforced with ErrorAction Stop or a terminating wrapper rather than stale LASTEXITCODE alone.

entries.mistake: The compact shared dock preserved a 44-pixel middle action but retained 4-pixel vertical content padding, leaving 36 pixels for a 37-pixel icon-and-scaled-label column and causing a 1-pixel RenderFlex overflow at 140 percent text scale.
entries.rootCause: External tap-target fitment was measured before the internal icon-and-label stack was exercised at the required enlarged text scale.
entries.prevention: The 44-pixel hit target remains unchanged while internal vertical padding is text-scale-safe. Full 320-by-568 and 140-percent fitment tests must run for every shared navigation geometry change.

entries.mistake: After Buy adopted the shared 48-pixel navigation surface, the category sheet retained the retired BuyV2Metrics.dockHeight inset of 54 pixels and ended 6 pixels above the actual dock boundary.
entries.rootCause: The local dock widget and keys were reconciled, but a layout inset coupled to the retired owner's height token remained in buy_v2_catalogue.dart.
entries.prevention: Overlays that terminate above persistent navigation consume the shared MoolMetrics compact navigation token, and the category surface-to-dock seam remains qualified within one pixel.

entries.mistake: The first C10C affected-suite inventory included the nonexistent exact filenames buy_home_delivery_flow_test.dart and buy_theme_transition_test.dart from a compacted summary rather than resolving their current paths from the repository inventory.
entries.rootCause: Human-readable test labels were treated as exact file operands before inventory resolution, although the preflight existence check prevented test execution.
entries.prevention: Affected test operands are sourced from rg --files and then existence-verified. Summaries provide intent and labels, not authoritative exact filenames.

entries.mistake: A repository test inventory filtered on the broad word candidate and matched hundreds of candidate-capture PNG artifacts in addition to Dart tests, producing truncated noisy output.
entries.rootCause: The discovery predicate targeted semantic fragments instead of restricting results to Dart files and exact test basenames before output.
entries.prevention: Test discovery first restricts rg --files output to .dart paths, then matches exact or tightly bounded basenames and caps displayed results. Truncated broad inventory output is not qualification evidence.

entries.mistake: A bounded test-source inspection assigned file content to the variable name $home, which PowerShell treats case-insensitively as the protected read-only $HOME variable, terminating the command after partial output.
entries.rootCause: A short semantic variable name was chosen without applying the workspace rule that HOME, home and CODEX_HOME must never be repurposed.
entries.prevention: Every shell variable uses a task-specific prefix such as $c10cHomeDeliveryLines. Protected environment and automatic variable names are never used for task data. Partial output from the failed inspection is not complete evidence.

entries.mistake: The scoped Cart and Checkout continuity test still required every Buy-local tab, including the selected current tab, to expose a tap action and used a selected-tab retap to leave purchase depth.
entries.rootCause: The old Buy dock used destination taps as depth exits, while C10 requires selected destinations to be disabled no-ops and system Back to restore exact prior depth.
entries.prevention: Selected local and global destinations expose selected semantics with no tap action. Cart and Checkout close through system Back, which restores the exact prior destination rather than repurposing a selected destination retap.

entries.mistake: A Buy route-continuity test expected readyRoute to return the latest Buy subroute after a language refresh, contradicting C10A's founder-approved invariant that a fresh authenticated launch without a pending route opens Social.
entries.rootCause: The runtime in-session router assertion and the cold-launch readyRoute assertion were not separated when lastReadyRoute became diagnostic-only.
entries.prevention: In-session Buy route changes remain asserted through GoRouter and visible state; readyRoute separately asserts Social for a fresh launch unless an explicit pending deep link exists.

entries.mistake: When the context CTA moved into the Buy brand area, the larger promo tap aperture remained later in the header Stack paint order and intercepted pointer events at the visible CTA's centre.
entries.rootCause: The two controls intentionally dispatch the same context action, but their hit-test z-order was not reconciled after they began sharing the brand region.
entries.prevention: The broad truthful promo aperture is painted below the header row; the visible 30-pixel CTA is painted above it and owns its own centre hit path, while the remaining brand aperture stays tappable.

entries.mistake: Two context-header tests asserted that copy such as Flexible packs was absent from the entire screen, even though that truthful copy is valid in destination-local catalogue content and only prohibited as visible header CTA text.
entries.rootCause: Header-specific copy containment assertions used global find.text lookups instead of descendant queries bounded to the header owner.
entries.prevention: Header copy tests scope absence assertions to buy-contextual-glass-header; customer-facing destination content remains free to use truthful wording outside that owner.

entries.mistake: The compact home-delivery fitment test still required the retired buy-back top control, which C10 deliberately removes from top-level destinations in favour of system Back and the persistent global dock.
entries.rootCause: The cross-flow accessibility inventory was not reconciled when the top-level Back owner was removed from the production navigation model.
entries.prevention: Top-level Buy fitment asserts local destinations and the global Mool/Chat rail but forbids dependence on a header Back control; exact depth restoration is exercised through system Back tests.

entries.mistake: Five Buy-local destinations were distributed with Expanded inside the header's remaining width, producing cells narrower than the 44-pixel minimum on compact phones even though their height remained 56 pixels.
entries.rootCause: The first header integration preserved vertical target size but did not enforce the shared minimum width when the brand and account owners reduced horizontal space.
entries.prevention: Buy-local tabs use a horizontally scrollable, finite header rail with each cell at least MoolMetrics.minimumTapTarget wide; wider screens distribute spare width and compact screens retain swipe access without shrinking targets.

entries.mistake: After replacing selected-tab retap with system Back, the scoped Checkout test expected one Back action to skip the intermediate Cart and return directly to catalogue.
entries.rootCause: The test reconciliation corrected the navigation owner but did not preserve the session's two distinct purchase-depth frames: Checkout above Cart above catalogue.
entries.prevention: Exact Back tests assert each frame independently: Checkout returns to Cart, a second Back returns to the prior catalogue destination, and no action skips a valid purchase state.

entries.mistake: C10C initially replaced the BuyV2 dock but left the reachable /app/buy/grocery and order-flow BuyPageScaffold using a destination-owned BuyBottomDock with buy-dock-* keys and a top buy-back arrow.
entries.rootCause: The first runtime-owner inventory was bounded to ui_v2/buy and did not follow the production grocery route into features/buy/widgets/buy_widgets.dart.
entries.prevention: Every reachable Buy route uses the shared MoolGlobalNavigationV2 bottom owner; Shop, Basket and Orders are local header actions, selected items are no-op, system Back owns nested depth, and static C10C containment scans both ui_v2/buy and features/buy.

entries.mistake: Five scoped Cart and Checkout golden baselines still represented the retired Buy-owned dock and therefore produced material pixel differences after the founder-approved shared global navigation redesign.
entries.rootCause: Behavioral and fitment tests were reconciled before the historical golden baselines were visually requalified against the accepted new navigation contract.
entries.prevention: Navigation goldens are updated only after the new states pass semantic, fitment and journey gates and their generated images are visually inspected. Failure artifacts are removed after accepted baselines are written.

entries.mistake: A second C10C format command ran from apps/mobile while supplying apps/mobile-prefixed operands, so all four formatter paths were unresolved.
entries.rootCause: The already-registered workdir path namespace rule was not applied when formatting the newly migrated reachable Buy scaffold.
entries.prevention: Formatting runs from the repository root with apps/mobile/... operands or from apps/mobile with lib/... and test/... operands, never a mixture. C10C uses separate root-format and app-analysis commands.

entries.mistake: The migrated BuyPageScaffold AppBar actions used an explicit if-null pattern for its optional trailing widget, triggering the repository's use_null_aware_elements analysis rule.
entries.rootCause: The optional trailing action was transcribed with a conventional collection if instead of the active Dart analyzer's null-aware collection element syntax.
entries.prevention: Optional collection elements use the analyzer-supported null-aware element form, and Flutter analysis must be clean before any focused result qualifies.

entries.mistake: The first minimum-width repair used 44-pixel local header cells; visual inspection at 320 pixels showed Wholesale, Medicine and Orders labels visually running together and no clear indication that Help remained horizontally reachable.
entries.rootCause: The accessibility minimum was treated as the preferred visual width, and the local rail did not implement the selected-item reveal and overflow-cue behavior already required of the global rail.
entries.prevention: Buy-local header destinations use readable 60-pixel minimum cells, finite horizontal motion, left/right overflow cues and automatic selected-item reveal. Navigation goldens cannot be accepted until compact visual inspection confirms separated labels and discoverable overflow.

entries.mistake: The compact enlarged-text navigation test directly tapped the Orders local action after readable 60-pixel cells made its centre intentionally off-screen at 320 pixels, so the pointer missed and the destination remained Shop.
entries.rootCause: The test retained an all-destinations-simultaneously-visible assumption after visual qualification required a discoverable horizontal local rail.
entries.prevention: Compact navigation tests assert the overflow cue, swipe the keyed local rail, verify the target is hit-testable, then tap Orders and assert the destination transition.

entries.mistake: The first selected-item reveal implementation scheduled a reveal from every local-rail build, so cue-state updates after a manual swipe animated the rail back to selected Shop before Orders could be tapped.
entries.rootCause: Auto-reveal was keyed to widget rebuilds rather than to an actual change in the selected local destination identifier.
entries.prevention: The local rail stores the last revealed selection and schedules centering only when that identifier changes. Manual scrolling and overflow-cue setState calls never reset user scroll position.

entries.mistake: An attempted PowerShell deletion of exactly 20 generated R58.8.7 golden-comparison PNGs was rejected by execution safety policy before mutation.
entries.rootCause: Cleanup selected permanent deletion even though a recoverable evidence move was sufficient and better aligned with immutable quality history.
entries.prevention: Generated failure comparisons are moved from the app test tree into the ticket's quality artifact directory after verified path containment; deletion is not required for runtime cleanliness.

entries.mistake: Six Buy journey assertions selected find.byType(Scrollable).first after the new local destination rail introduced another valid scroll owner, so the tests scrolled the horizontal navigation rail instead of the active product, order or tracking page.
entries.rootCause: The tests identified a scroll surface by global tree order instead of the stable PageStorageKey owned by the active destination page.
entries.prevention: Every Buy journey scroll resolves the Scrollable descendant of the exact keyed page owner. Tests must never use a global first-Scrollable selector when persistent navigation can add independent rails.

entries.mistake: The 360x800 Cart navigation golden passed alone but differed by 8.34 percent in the combined qualification run because one capture contained fallback product symbols while the other contained asynchronously decoded product images.
entries.rootCause: The golden assertion did not establish a deterministic product-image decode state before capture, so asset readiness depended on suite timing and concurrency.
entries.prevention: Navigation goldens must settle and precache all image providers visible in their capture owner, then render one deterministic frame before comparison. A strict isolated pass is insufficient until the combined qualification batch also passes.

entries.mistake: The first exact-owner repair matched every Scrollable descendant of a product page, including nested horizontal galleries and recommendation rails, so scrollUntilVisible failed with Too many elements.
entries.rootCause: Owner containment was added without also constraining the intended vertical page axis.
entries.prevention: The reusable Buy page-scroll finder requires both exact keyed owner containment and a vertical Scrollable axis; nested horizontal rails are never eligible journey-page scroll owners.

entries.mistake: After REG-187 repaired unscoped header-copy assertions in the R51.11 and R51.13 tests, R51.10 retained the same global find.text absence pattern and failed when the destination catalogue truthfully displayed Flexible packs.
entries.rootCause: The earlier repair named two observed files instead of inventorying every test for the prohibited assertion pattern.
entries.prevention: A regression repair searches the full affected test family, and every header-copy absence assertion is bounded to buy-contextual-glass-header. The gate family includes R51.10, R51.11 and R51.13.

entries.mistake: The first C10C host-qualification state patch closed the hostQualification JSON object with an array delimiter.
entries.rootCause: A hand-edited nested object was not parsed before the patch result was treated as complete.
entries.prevention: Every edited config JSON is parsed immediately after patching and before any ticket state is reported; repository memory validation remains mandatory after state updates.

entries.mistake: The reachable Chat inbox used ChatPageScaffold with a top chat-back arrow and no MoolGlobalNavigationV2, so selecting global Chat changed the app's navigation model and made a main root look like content depth.
entries.rootCause: Chat was implemented as a destination-owned page scaffold before the C10 single-global-shell contract and was not included in C10B main-root migration.
entries.prevention: Chat inbox is a top-level global destination: it has Chat selected in the shared dock, no header Back control, and system Back restores a pushed origin or its protected return route.

entries.mistake: Chat exposed separate chat-open-mool and chat-thread-mool controls in the header and composer even though Mool is a fixed edge of the shared global dock.
entries.rootCause: Legacy destination-local launcher shortcuts remained reachable after the global dock became the sole top-level navigation owner.
entries.prevention: Chat has exactly one Mool navigation owner through mool-root-selected in MoolGlobalNavigationV2; chat-open-mool and chat-thread-mool are forbidden from compiled reachable source.

entries.mistake: Opening a thread from Chat inbox used context.go, replacing the inbox route and risking loss of its search controller, scroll position and exact local filter state.
entries.rootCause: Thread navigation encoded a fallback return URI but did not preserve the live inbox route instance as content-depth history.
entries.prevention: Inbox opens thread depth with push; visible and system Back pop the live route when possible and use the protected fallback only for direct/deep-linked entry. Global switches also push so draft, focus, IME and scroll owners survive round trips.

entries.mistake: The first Chat bottom-stack implementation wrote the null-aware collection element as bottom? instead of the supported ?bottom syntax, producing parser errors.
entries.rootCause: The optional collection-element syntax direction was recalled incorrectly while avoiding the registered explicit null-check lint.
entries.prevention: Optional Dart collection elements use the repository-supported ?element form, and formatting plus apps/mobile analysis run immediately before tests.

entries.mistake: C10D launched flutter analyze from the repository root, so the analyzer traversed preserved artifact trees and emitted thousands of irrelevant diagnostics in addition to the real Chat parser error.
entries.rootCause: The formatting command used repository-relative operands and analysis was appended without switching its working directory to apps/mobile.
entries.prevention: Repository-root formatting and apps/mobile analysis are separate commands with explicit working directories; root analysis output never qualifies or disqualifies the mobile app.

entries.mistake: The first C10D selected-Chat semantics test deferred SemanticsHandle disposal with addTearDown, but Flutter verified active handles before that deferred cleanup ran.
entries.rootCause: Resource cleanup timing was assumed to be equivalent to explicit disposal inside the widget-test body.
entries.prevention: Semantics handles used for selected/no-tap assertions are explicitly disposed before the widget test body returns.

entries.mistake: The first C10D IME round-trip test called Focus.of on the TextField widget context, which is above the internal Focus widget and therefore has no Focus ancestor.
entries.rootCause: Focus ownership was queried from presentation context instead of the TextField's EditableText focus node.
entries.prevention: Text input focus assertions read the descendant EditableText.focusNode.hasFocus value before and after global route round trips.

entries.mistake: The first C10D static gate required the literal single-line token context.push(chatRoute( even though dart format split the nested call across lines.
entries.rootCause: A structural route-owner contract was encoded as exact presentation whitespace.
entries.prevention: The C10D gate uses a whitespace-tolerant regex for nested push(chatRoute()) and reserves literal checks for stable identifiers and keys.

entries.mistake: Three historical navigation test files still tapped chat-open-mool, chat-thread-mool or the top-level inbox chat-back after C10D made the shared global dock and system Back the sole owners.
entries.rootCause: The initial C10D focused test reconciliation covered chat_flow_test but did not inventory all prior global-navigation regression suites before running the affected batch.
entries.prevention: C10D source and test inventory searches the complete mobile test tree for retired Chat navigation keys; inbox return tests assert no top Back and use system Back, while Mool round trips use mool-root-selected.

entries.mistake: The broader C10D affected batch exposed two universal Buy intent journeys that still tapped the retired buy-back header control removed under C10C.
entries.rootCause: C10C qualification covered Buy-specific and selected router suites but did not inventory universal_intent_completion_test for the retired key.
entries.prevention: The complete mobile test tree is searched for buy-back whenever top-level Buy navigation changes; universal catalogue and medicine intents assert the top control is absent and use system Back.

entries.mistake: The first C10E execution preflight invoked the delivery-discipline checker while the MVP scope state still selected completed C09 and pinned its now-stale ticket manifest hash.
entries.rootCause: The continuation advanced from C10D host qualification to C10E preflight before replacing the predecessor selection with C10E's own verified robustness/reuse assessment and settled manifest digest.
entries.prevention: A successor preflight first creates and verifies its assessment, settles its manifest, pins the exact SHA-256 and disclosure in mvp-scope-gate-state.json, then invokes the delivery lock with -RequireTicketSelectionAssessment and the scope gate with the exact candidate ID.

entries.mistake: A compound source read included the guessed path apps/mobile/lib/core/design/mool_motion.dart, which does not exist, making the command's partial output unusable.
entries.rootCause: The motion filename was composed from memory instead of selected from an immediately verified rg --files inventory.
entries.prevention: Motion-source reads begin with the exact design-root inventory, filter to existing literal files, and reject the complete compound result if any operand is missing.

entries.mistake: The approved UI lock preflight rejects the remediation branch's committed Screen 01 app_splash_screen_v2.dart hash even though the path has no worktree or HEAD diff.
entries.rootCause: The branch baseline contains SHA-256 D08DBA928B884554984D28891F5E465B1F7FA910D3884EBE49B6466D199147BE while the accepted production lock expects B0E7B099B70BE7240A4E7699596AB7F16B77285FBA9C23C4F3708AFDA7AE218D; this predates C10E and cannot be silently repaired inside navigation scope.
entries.prevention: C10E excludes boot, setup and sign-in routes and any global router transition that could affect locked Screens 01-03; it records the protected path's exact before/after hash and preserves the independent lock rejection until a separately authorized locked-reference reconciliation occurs.

entries.mistake: The first Book navigation migration patch anchored terminal BookBottomDock deletion to a remembered following BookEmptyState class that is not in the file.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-hunk patch assumed adjacent context instead of copying the immediate numbered file tail; BookBottomDock is the final class.
entries.prevention: Book migration uses separately verified small hunks for imports/scaffold changes and an end-of-file deletion anchored to the exact current terminal class.

entries.mistake: REG217 named the planned C10E static checker in its gate list before that checker file had been created.
entries.rootCause: A future prevention mechanism was recorded as if it were already existing repository evidence.
entries.prevention: A new registry entry references only existing literal evidence and gate paths; a later checker is attached only after the file exists, parses and passes independently.

entries.mistake: The first Shared navigation migration combined four changes with a terminal _SharedDock removal whose context did not verify atomically.
entries.rootCause: Valid earlier hunks were coupled to deletion context copied from a prior compound view instead of the immediate exact numbered tail.
entries.prevention: Shared migration applies and verifies import, bottom owner, in-content local rail and obsolete class deletion as independent small patches.

entries.mistake: The /app/:section route retained a Widget builder after its Mool, action-root, Social and fallback branches began returning CustomTransitionPage<void>.
entries.rootCause: The branch-return migration did not include the encompassing dynamic GoRoute declaration in the same verified hunk.
entries.prevention: Every moolMainDestinationPage return is enclosed by a pageBuilder route declaration, enforced by complete mobile analysis and the C10E router contract test.

entries.mistake: A C10E route inspection combined a required fixed-string rg with an optional symbol rg, and the optional zero-match exit invalidated the compound command after useful output had already rendered.
entries.rootCause: The command did not isolate the optional probe or explicitly translate rg exit 1 to a valid zero-result outcome.
entries.prevention: C10E route inventories run required and optional searches independently; every optional rg maps exit 1 to an explicit zero-result value and rejects codes above 1 before any output is used as evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C10E focused journey threw on system Back from Mool because a pageBuilder closure called Navigator.of on its above-Navigator context.
entries.rootCause: The transition migration preserved a Navigator-context assumption that was valid for an in-tree widget callback but not for a GoRoute pageBuilder callback.
entries.prevention: Page-builder route callbacks query and pop history through GoRouter context extensions; the C10E Social-Mool-Social-Mool system-Back journey must pass without an exception.

entries.mistake: The first C10E reduced-motion test expected the pushed Work owner after the same frame that dispatched the tap, even though GoRouter had not yet mounted the new page.
entries.rootCause: The test conflated removal of visual Fade/Slide motion with synchronous imperative route mutation.
entries.prevention: Reduced-motion coverage asserts the visual transition wrapper is absent, advances the minimal route-scheduling frame, then proves the destination and selected global action before settling.

entries.mistake: A 16-file C10E focused Flutter command returned 180 passes and 5 failures, but its combined compact output was truncated before every exact failure section could be retained.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic batch was larger than the available rendered result budget and did not first partition likely failing historical owners into bounded processes.
entries.prevention: Diagnostic Flutter runs use the same verified literal inventory partitioned into bounded groups with independent exit status; acceptance cycles preserve full output in separate exact artifact logs.

entries.mistake: Four historical C02 chooser journeys still tapped mvp-action-<section>-mool after the chooser-owned Mool control was replaced by the stable global mool-root-selected action.
entries.rootCause: The first C10E retired-key inventory covered destination dock prefixes but omitted the earlier chooser-specific Mool key family.
entries.prevention: C02 chooser journeys use mool-root-selected, and C10E inventory forbids mvp-action-*-mool across production and affected tests.

entries.mistake: A Ride booking-root local type switch updated RideSession and pushed a second booking page, whose initState notification reached the outgoing page during the same build.
entries.rootCause: Destination-local navigation was implemented uniformly as route push even though Bike, Auto and Cab are in-place choices owned by one live booking screen and one session.
entries.prevention: The booking root marks its active Ride local action; switching type updates that owner in place with no new route, while non-booking depths navigate only when a trip does not block the switch.

entries.mistake: A bounded APK-state inspection printed postBuildCount=1 by coercing an absent postBuildGates property through PowerShell @($null).Count.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic did not verify the required root property existed before array coercion and counting.
entries.prevention: APK-state summaries enumerate root properties first and access only verified owners; absent optional properties are reported as absent and never array-counted.

entries.mistake: The first C10E build-seal calculation guessed config/codex-development-regression-memory.json, and a follow-up inventory guessed config/codex-regression-registry.json; neither path exists.
entries.rootCause: The compound calculation and recovery command inferred the registry filename from memory instead of reading the enforcing checker's literal owner first.
entries.prevention: Build-seal registry reads use the exact config/codex-development-regression-registry.json owner discovered from scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1; similar state owners are read from their checker before compound calculations.

entries.mistake: The first C10E source-manifest patch combined a new file and two evidence updates with an invalid empty update hunk boundary.
entries.rootCause: A compound multi-file patch was composed without validating that every update hunk contained prefixed context or change lines.
entries.prevention: Candidate manifest creation and evidence enrichment use separate small apply_patch operations with complete literal context and immediate readback.

entries.mistake: The first post-authorization C10E scope check used a new descriptive authorization.state value that the enforcing schema does not accept.
entries.rootCause: An enum-like machine-state field was expanded for readability instead of preserving one of the checker's accepted authority tokens.
entries.prevention: MVP authorization.state remains founder_acknowledged_mvp_scope; exact build/install authorization is expressed through its evidence path, checkpoint state and execution booleans.

entries.mistake: The first C10E wrong-fingerprint self-test passed a string array through external pwsh -File, causing positional-parameter binding failure before the intended gate assertion.
entries.rootCause: The self-test assumed an in-memory PowerShell array would preserve one parameter's array binding across an external process boundary.
entries.prevention: PowerShell gate self-tests invoke check-apk-regression-gate-state.ps1 in-process so RuntimeDefine string-array binding and terminating errors remain exact.

entries.mistake: The sole C10E build wrapper was launched under a short shell timeout that returned exit 124 while its wrapper, Flutter and Gradle children remained active.
entries.rootCause: A command maximum runtime was used where a yielded long-running execution cell was required for an Android profile build.
entries.prevention: Long build wrappers run in a yielded cell and are awaited; a timeout is reconciled by original PID and reserved evidence and never permits a second build invocation.

entries.mistake: The one authorized C10E r60.10 build attempt terminated after its host timeout without producing the reserved APK or provenance file.
entries.rootCause: The original build process was launched under a short command timeout; after the timeout it did not complete a wrapper-owned candidate artifact.
entries.prevention: The candidate consumes its one-build authorization and install remains closed; future authorized successor wrappers use a yielded long-running execution cell on their sole invocation, and old generated APKs are never substituted.

entries.mistake: The first post-timeout reconciliation declared no candidate output after wrapper and Flutter exit, before the original Gradle descendant completed a new generated profile APK.
entries.rootCause: Terminal build status was inferred from parent-process exit and absent reserved files without monitoring every descendant or waiting for generated-output timestamp stability.
entries.prevention: Timeout reconciliation watches the complete descendant tree and a quiet output interval; a late generated APK remains unaccepted until package, version, signature, source and single-build lineage checks pass.

entries.mistake: A validation-tool lookup searched the full retained artifact tree for apksigner and aapt examples and timed out without a usable result.
entries.rootCause: The search scope included large historical artifact trees instead of using the exact SDK owner already recorded in android/local.properties or narrow text globs.
entries.prevention: APK validation uses exact deterministic build-tools paths from scoped SDK configuration; evidence searches use narrow text globs and known candidate directories.

entries.mistake: The postbuild source-drift command guessed a shortened protected Screen 01 path after correctly proving the authored runtime aggregate, repeating the registered unverified-operand class.
entries.rootCause: The protected owner path was recalled from its logical screen name instead of selected from a bounded apps/mobile/lib inventory before composing the command.
entries.prevention: Protected checks use the inventory-verified literal apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/screens/screen01_app_splash/app_splash_screen_v2.dart and execute separately from runtime aggregate proof.

entries.mistake: With the Android IME visibly covering the global rail, UIAutomator retained off-screen rail semantics and the first Mool-coordinate tap hit the keyboard symbol key instead of navigation.
entries.rootCause: The device harness trusted semantic bounds without cross-checking whether the current screenshot and IME made that target visibly actionable.
entries.prevention: OPPO automation cross-checks screenshot and IME state; Back dismisses an IME before a visibly restored global rail is tapped, and hidden semantics never count as a real-user hit target.

entries.mistake: After the Buy scroll to Mool to Back journey and both evidence pulls succeeded, the verifier appended a leaf suffix outside Join-Path and looked for a malformed 32\+ path.
entries.rootCause: The compound verification expression mixed path joining and string concatenation without first constructing one complete literal leaf filename.
entries.prevention: Device evidence comparison uses exact complete leaf names, verifies both files exist, then parses them; successful journeys and captures are never repeated solely for verifier path mistakes.

entries.mistake: An optional final OPPO screenrecord process did not create the expected remote MP4, but the journey was started before recorder/file readiness had been proven.
entries.rootCause: The recorder launch was treated as ready without checking that its process remained active and the exact remote file existed before the first tap.
entries.prevention: Optional device recording verifies the recorder process and remote file before a journey; absent video is reported truthfully and never substituted for required host timing or screenshot/hierarchy evidence.

entries.mistake: Codex moved destination sub-actions into the top header or first content row even though that zone is reserved for advertising and promotional video, forcing routine actions outside comfortable one-handed reach and weakening their visual hierarchy.
entries.rootCause: C10 removed competing bottom-navigation owners, but the replacement placement was chosen without a founder-approved reachability and reserved-zone contract; tests proved route wiring and semantics without measuring thumb reach, tap budget or promotional-media ownership.
entries.prevention: Reserve the top promotional-media zone; keep destination sub-actions local, visually coherent and available in the lower thumb-reachable content zone with one direct tap; preserve the accepted global bottom rail; block More menus, modals and multi-tap default paths; require compact, large-text, reduced-motion, production-router and real one-handed OPPO evidence after the founder approves the exact placement.

entries.mistake: A C11 protected-gate diagnostic searched the complete retained artifacts/quality tree and timed out, repeating the registered unbounded-artifact search class.
entries.rootCause: Documentation, configuration and the large evidence archive were grouped into one routine lookup without first proving that the archive was necessary.
entries.prevention: Routine authority discovery searches known docs and config owners only; artifacts are searched only through an exact candidate directory or a bounded filename inventory.

entries.mistake: The app brand gate falsely rejected Chat and then the Social consumer after C10 because it expected direct Mool icons in retired screen-local owners even though both now correctly reuse the shared global navigation owner.
entries.rootCause: The static gate retained old direct-screen ownership assumptions and did not validate the ChatPageScaffold and Social consumer to MoolGlobalNavigationV2 to MoolBrand launcher chains.
entries.prevention: The brand gate validates that migrated Chat and Social consumers use MoolGlobalNavigationV2 and that the shared component renders MoolBrand.moolLauncherIcon; only unmigrated protected owners require direct launcher checks.

entries.mistake: The first C11 Dart formatter command repeated REG-013 by using Unix backslash line continuation inside PowerShell and failed before Dart started.
entries.rootCause: A multiline native-command layout was composed with shell syntax from the wrong host instead of using an explicit PowerShell argument array.
entries.prevention: Multi-file formatter and analyzer invocations pass exact literal paths through a PowerShell string array and check the native exit code immediately; Unix continuation syntax is forbidden.

entries.mistake: The global-navigation gate falsely rejected the approved C11 Social composition because it required MoolGlobalNavigationV2 directly in the destination instead of through the new shared shelf owner.
entries.rootCause: The static assertion encoded the old direct widget topology even though the product invariant is that the unchanged global rail remains the shared composition's final bottom owner.
entries.prevention: The gate accepts MoolDestinationNavigationV2 only after the placement gate proves the local shelf and the shared source proves MoolGlobalNavigationV2 is its final child; destinations never duplicate the global owner.

entries.mistake: The first C11 Social shelf rendered a keyed action only 38 logical pixels high and overflowed vertically at 320x568 with 140 percent text.
entries.rootCause: The existing fixed 48-pixel context-tabs shell constrained a nominal 52-pixel action and left insufficient inner height for provider attribution plus its scaled label.
entries.prevention: The Social shelf allocates a real minimum 44-by-44 action region after padding, fits attributed labels at 140 percent, uses finite 160-240 ms selection motion and removes scale and sheen under reduced motion; C11 tests measure actual geometry and reject render errors.

entries.mistake: The first C11 test repeated REG-209 by deferring SemanticsHandle disposal through addTearDown, which Flutter verifies too late.
entries.rootCause: The test treated deferred resource cleanup as equivalent to explicit disposal before widget-test end verification.
entries.prevention: Every ensureSemantics handle is disposed inside a test-body try/finally before return; addTearDown is never used for semantics handles.

entries.mistake: The C11 compact 320x568 at 140 percent matrix exposed six vertical overflows in Eat context choices and restaurant cards because their heights were fixed for normal text.
entries.rootCause: The four-choice grid and restaurant carousel used fixed aspect/height values without deriving vertical extent from effective text scale.
entries.prevention: Eat fixed-height decision rows scale their vertical extent for supported large text while the page remains scrollable; the complete C11 destination matrix rejects any render exception.

entries.mistake: The first C11 Eat text-scaled grid correction reduced the large-text overflow but under-allocated the rendered post-padding action height by two pixels.
entries.rootCause: The first estimate added only the observed overflow delta and no deterministic allowance for scaled line metrics inside the padded action.
entries.prevention: Fitment sizing uses rendered post-padding constraints plus a bounded allowance, and the unchanged 320x568 at 140 percent matrix must report zero exceptions before closure.

entries.mistake: The C10B static gate rejected the C11 Social composition because it still required Social to instantiate MoolGlobalNavigationV2 directly after the global rail moved behind the shared contextual shelf owner.
entries.rootCause: The older gate encoded a direct-widget spelling instead of the invariant composition chain from Social local navigation through MoolDestinationNavigationV2 to the unchanged MoolGlobalNavigationV2 owner.
entries.prevention: C10B validates Social's localNavigation slot and the shared destination-navigation owner before proving that the shared owner contains MoolGlobalNavigationV2; behavioral C10B and C11 tests remain mandatory so a wrapper cannot weaken rail geometry or meaning.

entries.mistake: After C11 moved Buy's four primary sub-actions into the lower shelf and restored Help to contextual recovery, the C10C static gate still required five header tabs including Help and a direct global-rail call.
entries.rootCause: The C10C gate preserved the superseded r60.10 placement and tab inventory rather than the founder-approved C11 invariant: four primary Buy destinations in the shelf, contextual Help, and the unchanged global rail below it.
entries.prevention: C10C now requires the shared lower-shelf call site, rejects primary Help tokens, and proves that MoolDestinationNavigationV2 terminates in MoolGlobalNavigationV2; Buy and C11 behavioral tests cover direct taps and recovery Assist.

entries.mistake: The C10E static gate rejected Eat, Ride, Book and Work because it required each destination owner to call MoolGlobalNavigationV2 directly after C11 introduced the shared lower-shelf composition owner.
entries.rootCause: C10E encoded the pre-C11 direct-call layout rather than proving the current composition chain while retaining its local-owner, page-transition, reduced-motion and no-top-Back invariants.
entries.prevention: C10E requires each destination to compose MoolDestinationNavigationV2 with MoolLocalNavigationRail and separately proves the shared destination owner terminates in MoolGlobalNavigationV2; its motion and journey assertions remain unchanged.

entries.mistake: The first C10E composition-gate correction applied the C11 contextual shelf requirement to shared_screens.dart even though Shared is not one of the six approved C11 destination shelf owners.
entries.rootCause: The existing C10E owner array combined four C11 destination owners with one non-C11 shared owner, and the correction treated that heterogeneous inventory as uniform.
entries.prevention: C10E distinguishes the non-C11 Shared owner by exact filename: Eat, Ride, Book and Work must use the destination shelf, Shared must keep its direct global owner, and every listed owner must retain its local rail.

entries.mistake: The brand integrity gate rejected C11 Social because its canonical Mool-launcher check still required Social to call the global rail directly instead of following the new shared shelf composition.
entries.rootCause: The brand invariant and navigation composition were coupled at one direct source call site, so a valid shared wrapper appeared to remove canonical launcher ownership.
entries.prevention: The brand gate proves Social uses MoolDestinationNavigationV2, that the shared destination owner terminates in MoolGlobalNavigationV2, and that the global owner still renders MoolBrand.moolLauncherIcon.

entries.mistake: The initial C11 affected batch covered the dedicated shelf and C10C journeys but did not run the complete 47-file Buy suite; the first voluntary complete run then surfaced 14 failures after 348 passes and 20 skips.
entries.rootCause: The inherited 25-file navigation batch was treated as the complete affected boundary even though C11 structurally changed BuyV2Screen header and bottom-navigation composition used by wider Buy fitment and journey tests.
entries.prevention: Any structural change to a feature root must run that feature's complete test directory before APK sealing, then two identical complete passes after correction; failing names and errors are extracted with a bounded JSON reporter before product-versus-assertion disposition.

entries.mistake: The first bounded Buy diagnostic command repeated REG-076, REG-156 and REG-178 by checking LASTEXITCODE after the in-process PowerShell regression-memory checker; the stale scalar skipped Flutter while the wrapper misleadingly exited zero.
entries.rootCause: A repository PowerShell gate and a native Flutter diagnostic were combined in one command with native exit semantics incorrectly assigned to the PowerShell call.
entries.prevention: Repository PowerShell gates execute in their own repository-root command and succeed by returning without a terminating error. Native Flutter diagnostics execute separately in apps/mobile, capture LASTEXITCODE immediately, and only then parse their captured JSON lines.

entries.mistake: A C11 search combined one valid file with apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/buy/*.dart as a ripgrep operand on Windows; ripgrep rejected the literal wildcard path and the orchestration discarded the otherwise valid parallel read.
entries.rootCause: The search repeated the registered Windows wildcard-operand class instead of using the existing Buy directory as a literal root with a glob filter.
entries.prevention: Every ripgrep operand is an inventory-verified literal file or directory. Windows file patterns use a literal directory plus --glob, and parallel diagnostic reads do not share one failure boundary when partial output would be needed.

entries.mistake: The first C11 complete-Buy correction removed nine of twelve functional failures but the focused five-file run still ended with three failures after 84 passes and one protected-reference exclusion.
entries.rootCause: The first correction was based on the complete-suite failure summary and selected focused stack traces, but did not re-inventory every remaining failure before treating the correction set as complete.
entries.prevention: After a multi-failure correction, run the exact affected files with protected references explicitly excluded, capture any remaining failed test names and errors with the bounded JSON reporter, and register each second-order cause before another implementation retry.

entries.mistake: A combined mobile-root command passed repository-relative apps/mobile paths to dart format, so formatting rejected both operands while the following correctly relative flutter analyze succeeded and left the overall shell exit zero.
entries.rootCause: Two tools with different operand spellings were combined under apps/mobile, and the final command exit obscured the earlier formatter rejection.
entries.prevention: Formatting runs separately in its declared working directory with inventory-verified relative paths and its own exit result. Analysis runs only after formatting succeeds; a later command can never relabel an earlier rejection as pass evidence.

entries.mistake: The second Buy correction replaced a failing scrollUntilVisible call with a fixed negative 520-pixel drag, which overshot the Wholesale terms panel and left the visible-finder assertion empty.
entries.rootCause: The test approximated a destination offset after the C11 viewport changed instead of targeting the already built exact panel element.
entries.prevention: When the exact target exists with skipOffstage false, assert its ownership and use tester.ensureVisible on that target; fixed drag distances are reserved for testing scroll behavior itself, not locating a known semantic destination.

entries.mistake: After correctly bringing Wholesale terms into view, the product-detail test still required the earlier inline purchase action to remain onscreen, which is impossible on the smaller C11 content viewport after scrolling down.
entries.rootCause: The test mixed persistence ownership with simultaneous viewport visibility and used default skipOffstage finders for content intentionally scrolled above the viewport.
entries.prevention: Assert the purchase action is visible before scrolling, then use skipOffstage-false ownership finders for persistence checks after a lower panel is brought into view; do not require mutually distant content to be visible at once.

entries.mistake: After the C11 compact Buy search correction passed, brand integrity still required the pre-fix 150-pixel control and 162-pixel band, rejecting the overflow-safe 162-pixel control and 174-pixel band.
entries.rootCause: Buy accessibility search geometry was duplicated in runtime, the brand contract and the brand checker, but the product correction initially updated only runtime and its behavioral assertion.
entries.prevention: An authorized accessibility fitment change updates the runtime, exact brand contract and static checker atomically; the 320x568 at 140 percent search journey and brand gate both remain required before sealing.

entries.mistake: Host qualification state and results were written into the founder-authorized C11 ticket manifest, changing its approved SHA-256 and causing the delivery-discipline lock to reject the selected-ticket assessment.
entries.rootCause: The immutable scope/authorization manifest was used as a mutable execution-status ledger even though separate qualification contract and evidence owners already existed.
entries.prevention: Founder-authorized ticket manifests remain byte-identical after approval. Host, build, device and founder-review status live only in separate state contracts and retained evidence; a checksum rejection is resolved by restoring the authorized manifest, never by silently updating its approval hash.

entries.mistake: The first C11 install preflight applied PowerShell -notmatch to the complete adb devices output array; the header line was nonmatching, so a connected exact OPPO was falsely rejected before adb install executed.
