entries.rootCause: Array comparison semantics were treated as an all-lines predicate instead of selecting and counting exact matching device rows.
entries.prevention: Capture adb output and native exit first, then filter rows with Where-Object and require exactly one anchored serial-plus-device match. Header and blank lines never participate in the boolean connection decision; predecessor version is rechecked before the still-unconsumed install.

entries.mistake: The checksum-matched r60.11 OPPO candidate used an almost opaque 56-70 pixel contextual shelf that passed host reachability tests but visually crowded Buy product grids and the other primary destination content.
entries.rootCause: The C11 contract enforced lower placement, one-tap reachability and minimum targets but did not bound the complete shelf envelope or maximum surface opacity, allowing a technically reachable yet visually heavy stacked control.
entries.prevention: Every destination composes one shared translucent family rail no taller than 48 logical pixels; every action remains at least 44 by 44, a family marker and semantics identify ownership, the global rail remains unchanged, and the complete OPPO screenshot matrix must pass before acceptance.

entries.mistake: The first C12 analyzer run rejected the shared navigation fallback accent because it referenced MoolColors through an assumed transitive import.
entries.rootCause: mool_global_navigation_v2.dart imports mool_design_system.dart, but Dart does not re-export the design system library's private mool_colors.dart import.
entries.prevention: Every new symbol must be available through a direct import or an already public token in the file's current imports; the fallback uses the established explicit navy color and full analysis remains mandatory.

entries.mistake: A combined C12 command ran from apps/mobile but invoked the repository regression-memory checker through the nonexistent apps/mobile/scripts path before continuing to Flutter analysis.
entries.rootCause: A repository-root PowerShell gate and a mobile-root native tool were combined despite having different working-directory ownership and exit semantics.
entries.prevention: Repository PowerShell gates run alone from the repository root; Flutter and Dart tools run alone from apps/mobile, and each command has one independently checked exit result.

entries.mistake: The first C12 focused run measured Social and the shared Eat/Ride/Book/Work keyed sub-action targets at 43 logical pixels inside the exact 48px rail, while Buy passed.
entries.rootCause: A nominal two-pixel vertical inset on each side left 44 pixels, but final layout rounding removed one pixel from the interactive owner.
entries.prevention: The shared 48px envelope uses one-pixel vertical insets, every cell retains an explicit 44px minimum, and the actual keyed target is measured across all six normal and compact large-text destinations.

entries.mistake: The first C12 source-seal probe used unscoped git ls-files --others, traversed every retained artifact including historical browser profiles, and timed out with filename-too-long warnings.
entries.rootCause: A dirty-source fingerprint inventory was treated as a repository-wide untracked inventory even though artifacts and tmp are retained evidence rather than authored production source.
entries.prevention: Source fingerprints enumerate only explicit production scopes: AGENTS.md, apps/mobile, apps/web, config, docs, scripts and tests; retained artifacts and tmp are excluded unless one exact evidence directory is intentionally named.

entries.mistake: The first bounded C12 contract aggregate included a guessed nonexistent config/mvp-personal-action-projection.json operand and the helper printed an invalid hash despite the PowerShell error.
entries.rootCause: The aggregate list was reconstructed from a remembered concept name instead of the repository file inventory, and the helper did not throw on a missing file before hashing its line set.
entries.prevention: Every aggregate operand is resolved from rg --files or an exact already-read path; the helper throws on any missing file, and no aggregate is accepted when the command emits an error record or nonzero exit.

entries.mistake: C12 host qualification mounted destination-owned sub-action routes but did not tap every global main action through the production router, so r60.12 reached legacy Eat, Ride, Book and Work chooser roots without the approved family rail and required an extra tap.
entries.rootCause: Coverage proved deep-route presentation instead of each PersonalMoolActionSpec route and the first production frame it reached; no static gate rejected retired root routes or production rendering of MvpActionChoiceRootV2.
entries.prevention: Every supported global main action names an existing default sub-action route, stale affected roots resolve to the same default in production, a router test taps each global action once and requires the correct family rail plus selected default with chooser copy absent, and OPPO captures every untouched first landed frame.

entries.mistake: REG270 named the planned C13 production-router test as a gate before that test file existed, so the first implementation-phase regression-memory check rejected the registry before any runtime write.
entries.rootCause: The intended successor test was treated as current machine evidence during prewrite registration instead of being added only after its exact path existed.
entries.prevention: A new regression entry initially references only inventory-proven existing gates. A planned test is added to the permanent gate list only after apply_patch creates it and a read-only exact-path check passes.

entries.mistake: The first focused C13 analyzer run rejected the test because a const map used indexed values from another const list, which are not Dart constant expressions.
entries.rootCause: Collection immutability was expressed with const without verifying that the reused record lookup itself was valid at compile time.
entries.prevention: Derived test lookups that index another const collection are declared top-level final; the exact focused analyzer reruns before widget execution or build.

entries.mistake: The first six-file connected C13 batch ended with 15 failures because inherited FIX2 production-router cases still mounted retired root routes and expected mvp-action-choice controls after C13 correctly redirected those roots to default family owners.
entries.rootCause: Production route configuration and the dedicated successor tests were changed before all inherited chooser-based acceptance assertions were migrated atomically to the founder-approved direct-landing contract.
entries.prevention: Production-router tests for retired roots assert the default family owner on the first frame and use the local family rail to reach a non-default sub-action. Component-only chooser tests remain legacy-bound and never qualify production navigation; the complete connected batch restarts after migration.

entries.mistake: The first migrated FIX2 retry passed 22 cases but expected Ride Auto and Cab local switches to create Back history and restore Bike, even though the shared booking owner intentionally changes RideSession.selectedType in place.
entries.rootCause: The generic non-default sub-action assertion ignored Ride's established no-duplicate-route behavior and applied pushed-route Back semantics to an in-place state transition.
entries.prevention: Ride type tests assert the exact in-place selected semantics without inventing Back history; separate Chat and Mool round trips remain mandatory and restore the exact Bike, Auto or Cab state.

entries.mistake: The post-migration six-file compact Flutter batch ended with 61 passes and six failures, but startup logging caused output truncation and hid the exact failing names and stack context.
entries.rootCause: A multi-file connected batch was used for diagnosis with an output format that was not bounded against application startup logs, despite the established per-owner and bounded-reporter rules.
entries.prevention: A truncated batch is a failed lead only. Each inventory-proven file runs independently with its own exit and visible expanded result; complete durable cycles use the established bounded reporter after all individual owners pass.

entries.mistake: Four FIX1 Mool-action tests still expected retired mvp-action-root chooser owners after C13 correctly opened Eat Home, Ride Booking, Book Doctor and Work Earn.
entries.rootCause: The first inherited-test migration covered direct retired-root cases but missed the separate Mool-origin action matrix that asserted the same superseded chooser owners.
entries.prevention: Every Mool and global main-action matrix uses the same C13 default-owner contract and retains its Back-to-Mool assertion; retired chooser keys are forbidden as production expectations.

entries.mistake: Direct C13 default routes reached the correct owners but bypassed moolMainDestinationPage, so an Eat-to-Work global switch lost the finite route transition; the reduced-motion test also retained the retired Work chooser expectation.
entries.rootCause: The dynamic chooser root had owned the shared transition page, and changing action routes to exact deep GoRoutes did not automatically move that transition ownership to the four default destinations.
entries.prevention: Eat Home, Ride Booking, Book Doctor and Work Earn exact routes use moolMainDestinationPage; normal mode proves the finite 240ms transition, reduced motion renders without it, and both modes assert the real destination owner.

entries.mistake: After direct default routes gained shared page motion, C10E found both a settled outgoing and active incoming keyed FadeTransition but still required exactly one keyed widget.
entries.rootCause: The assertion treated a transition-time Navigator stack as a single mounted page instead of distinguishing the active animation from the retained settled route.
entries.prevention: Motion tests select the exactly one keyed FadeTransition with opacity strictly between its 0.92 start and 1.0 end, then validate its paired slide; multiple mounted route owners remain valid.

entries.mistake: The r60.12 48px family rail met its numerical maximum but the separate family tile, per-action boxes and filled selected tile still looked large and visually competed with destination content.
entries.rootCause: C12 bounded total height and opacity but allowed every action and the family marker to render as its own raised or filled object, so visual weight remained high despite the smaller envelope.
entries.prevention: All six destinations use one maximum-44px transparent unboxed strip; every keyed target remains at least 44-by-44, selection uses tint plus a two-pixel line, family ownership uses a thin connector and selected global action, and OPPO first frames prove content dominance.

entries.mistake: The first focused C14 analyzer run rejected MoolRadii.sm because that radius token does not exist in the shared design system.
entries.rootCause: A spacing-family abbreviation was assumed to exist in the radius-token family instead of copying the exact declaration before use.
entries.prevention: Design-token names are read from their declaring owner; C14 reuses the existing MoolRadii.control token and reruns the identical focused analyzer before widget execution.

entries.mistake: The first C14 geometry run measured every keyed destination action at 43px because a one-pixel decorated top border deflated the 44px strip child area.
entries.rootCause: The exact 44px envelope was treated as usable child height even though Container applied decoration border padding before laying out the interactive child, recurring the registered nominal-envelope mistake class.
entries.prevention: The wrapper has no layout-consuming border; its two-pixel family connector is a Positioned paint layer over a full 44px child, and all six keyed controls are measured directly in normal and compact large-text tests.

entries.mistake: A lookup for the prior 26-file command searched all retained artifacts/quality Markdown, text and log content and timed out without producing accepted evidence.
entries.rootCause: Historical command reconstruction began with repository-wide artifact content instead of one exact candidate directory, a bounded filename inventory or the live test-owner inventory.
entries.prevention: Historical evidence searches use one exact known evidence directory or filename inventory; current affected tests are derived from live source owners and exact rg --files results, and timed-out broad output is discarded without retry.

entries.mistake: A read-only lookup for bounded Flutter reporters began its ripgrep pattern with --machine, which was parsed as an unsupported option and prevented the search.
entries.rootCause: The command did not use ripgrep's explicit end-of-options separator before a pattern beginning with a hyphen.
entries.prevention: Option-leading ripgrep patterns always follow an explicit -- separator; the failed output never establishes absence and the corrected lookup runs as a separate exact command.

entries.mistake: The corrected ripgrep command placed -- before its --glob filters, so the filters were treated as path operands and ripgrep exited with code 2.
entries.rootCause: The end-of-options separator was understood for the pattern but ordered before remaining options instead of after every option and glob.
entries.prevention: Ripgrep command order is all options, all globs, explicit --, pattern, then verified literal roots; code-2 output is discarded and never used as absence evidence.

entries.mistake: The first complete universal JSON cycle reported 210 passes and 38 failures but rendered most failed testDone entries as numeric IDs without joining their testStart names and URLs.
entries.rootCause: The bounded parser counted testDone events but did not build the required ID-to-test metadata map before printing failures.
entries.prevention: JSON diagnostics join testDone.testID to testStart.test.name and test.url; until the next complete cycle, visible descriptions map to exact live test files and each owner runs independently, while numeric IDs alone authorize no mutation.

entries.mistake: R06 and the complete universal cycle exposed inherited Eat, Ride, Book and Work production-route tests that still expected retired chooser owners or synthetic root Back-to-Mool history.
entries.rootCause: Chooser migration stopped at FIX1/FIX2 and dedicated C13 coverage, leaving the role-specific vertical exposure suites attached to the superseded production root contract.
entries.prevention: Every vertical root asserts its default owner and family strip; non-default local pushes Back to default, top-level roots create no chooser history, and explicit Mool navigation returns to the exact prior destination. Direct deep links never qualify through a chooser.

entries.mistake: While migrating the R07 vertical suite away from the chooser, the first C14 test edit again expected Auto and Cab to create Back history and restore Bike even though Ride intentionally switches vehicle type inside one booking owner.
entries.rootCause: The generic non-default-subaction Back rule was applied to Ride without reconciling the already registered Ride-specific in-place state contract.
entries.prevention: Ride Bike, Auto and Cab never qualify through invented duplicate route history; each selected type is proved in the session and survives an explicit Mool visit and system Back to the exact booking owner.

entries.mistake: The second complete universal JSON cycle built a test-ID map but used invalid PowerShell braced-expression interpolation, so all 19 failure labels rendered as blank URL and name fields.
entries.rootCause: The parser fix addressed the missing map but did not independently validate the exact PowerShell metadata string before the long complete cycle.
entries.prevention: Bounded JSON parsing uses the exact subexpression form $($event.test.url) and $($event.test.name), validates a non-empty mapped label on testStart, and prints unmapped IDs explicitly; blank labels authorize no mutation.

entries.mistake: After C13 retired chooser roots, C02, C10B, R03, R11, R12 and Social-to-Work compatibility still named chooser owners or compatibility roots as canonical destinations; legacy recovery buttons also routed through those retired roots.
entries.rootCause: The initial contract migration covered vertical exposure and dedicated C13 suites but did not inventory every ancillary config, Chat, hub, compatibility and legacy-containment consumer of the old root routes.
entries.prevention: All canonical action and Chat contracts name exact default owners, Mool and Chat return tests assert those owners, and legacy recovery buttons route directly to the truthful supported owner (Workspace for Onboard/Verify) without a chooser hop.

entries.mistake: The first complete Buy cycle passed 426 cases and failed one continuity case because it still expected the retired Eat chooser after the global Eat action.
entries.rootCause: The retired-root consumer inventory initially stopped at the universal test directory and missed one cross-destination expectation owned by the Buy regression suite.
entries.prevention: Chooser retirement inventory includes cross-destination suites outside universal; Buy continuity now proves Eat Home plus selected Order Food, absence of the chooser, Mool restoration, then Buy restoration.

entries.mistake: The C10E static gate required pageBuilder immediately after /app/:section and rejected the valid C13 pre-render default-owner redirect even though the same GoRoute retained its motion page owner.
entries.rootCause: The checker encoded the old route declaration shape rather than separately proving the C13 redirect, the retained dynamic page owner, and exact default routes using the shared motion page.
entries.prevention: C10E validates exact Eat, Ride, Book and Work default routes as page-owned, bounds the dynamic route before the next GoRoute, requires its C13 redirect token, then separately proves its retained pageBuilder and Back owner.

entries.mistake: A pre-build provenance lookup passed docs/quality/UAW-C13* and UAW-C12* as ripgrep path operands on Windows, producing path-syntax errors and discarding the grouped lookup output.
entries.rootCause: Shell wildcard expansion was again assumed for a native Windows ripgrep path operand instead of deriving exact files from rg --files or using ripgrep globs before the pattern.
entries.prevention: Windows ripgrep receives exact literal roots; wildcard discovery starts with rg --files and a second bounded filename filter, while any grouped output containing a path error is discarded in full.

entries.mistake: The checksum-matched r60.14 candidate met the 44px unboxed one-tap rules, but its flat local row still looked separate from the selected global main action during founder OPPO review.
entries.rootCause: C14 required only a static family line and did not bind a visible connection endpoint to the selected local index and selected global action anchor.
entries.prevention: The shared destination wrapper has no side-to-side surface and owns one noninteractive semantics-excluded transparent gradient wave that joins the selected global anchor to the exact selected local action, moves finitely left or right on selection, and settles immediately under reduced motion while preserving 44px targets.

entries.mistake: A combined C15 placement-contract patch was rejected atomically because it assumed rejectedCandidate.versionCode was numeric while the exact live JSON stores it as a string.
entries.rootCause: Remembered semantic type was used as patch context instead of separately copying the exact bounded source lines after parsing the value.
entries.prevention: JSON state edits parse the value for meaning, read the exact bounded source context, and use small owner-specific hunks; an atomically rejected combined patch is confirmed unchanged before retry.

entries.mistake: The first C15 focused run rejected all six normal-motion cases by expecting exactly one IgnorePointer ancestor even though the required ignoring owner and an unrelated non-ignoring framework ancestor were both present.
entries.rootCause: The test counted an entire ancestor widget type instead of selecting the ancestor whose behavioral property established the noninteractive overlay contract.
entries.prevention: Overlay tests enumerate matching ancestors and require exactly one IgnorePointer with ignoring true; unrelated non-ignoring ancestors do not count as interaction owners, and semantics exclusion is asserted by an excluding ancestor.

entries.mistake: Eat, Book and Work route-mounted wave controllers remained at zero through the first measured transition frame because their start was deferred by an extra post-frame callback.
entries.rootCause: Incoming route wrappers postponed finite motion even though didChangeDependencies had already resolved the accessibility motion policy, unlike in-place selection updates that started immediately.
entries.prevention: Route-mounted waves start their finite controller immediately in didChangeDependencies when motion is enabled, reduced motion settles immediately, and intermediate-frame tests cover both in-place and cross-route selection.

entries.mistake: The first final-state vertical cycle failed 26 journeys after extendBody was combined with bottom-disabled body SafeAreas, laying primary controls beneath the 92px fixed navigation stack.
entries.rootCause: Visual canvas continuation and interactive content insetting were collapsed into one layer; a transparent navigation background was incorrectly implemented by removing bottom safety from real content.
entries.prevention: Destination Scaffolds extend the visual canvas behind the transparent wave while body SafeAreas keep bottom protection enabled; Buy paints its destination gradient behind the safe content layer, and complete vertical and Buy cycles prove hit testing.

entries.mistake: The isolated Buy analyzer rejected passing the repository MoolBrandGradient enum directly to Flutter BoxDecoration.gradient, which requires a Gradient.
entries.rootCause: The semantic design-token type was assumed to be a Flutter rendering type without first inspecting its declaring owner and authoritative colors projection.
entries.prevention: MoolBrandGradient is rendered through MoolFiniteGradientTransition or an explicit LinearGradient from its .colors; focused analysis runs before test replay.

entries.mistake: A Search Console noindex reason can be mistaken for a current canonical-site defect even when its only example is a historically crawled HTTP URL that now permanently redirects to an indexable HTTPS canonical.
entries.rootCause: Reason labels and notification dates were previously considered without first reconciling each exact example URL, its last-crawl date, the current redirect chain, live response headers, canonical metadata, robots.txt and sitemap state.
entries.prevention: Every indexing alert is resolved example-first: preserve intentional utility noindex directives, prove the current Googlebot-visible HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect and canonical indexability, run the SEO regression suite, avoid an unchanged deploy, and submit validation only for the exact stale reason group while Google-controlled processing remains pending.

entries.mistake: C15 standardized transparent 44px one-tap sub-actions and a main-to-sub-action wave, but founder OPPO review found that the six destination families still lacked one professional adaptive visual system: Buy could read as a full-width strip, low-count families were overstretched, text/icon sizing and spacing varied, background content could be displaced or obscured, and destination switches could feel like unrelated pages instead of one native shell.
entries.rootCause: Qualification proved geometry and family connection per destination but did not require cumulative OPPO visual comparison of all six families, one shared tokenized variable-count distribution, or a stable anchored global rail with destination and local content transitioning behind the same shell.
entries.prevention: Social, Buy, Eat, Ride, Book and Work must use one shared adaptive native-Flutter owner with global typography, icon, spacing and selected-state tokens; variable counts must never stretch into an edge-to-edge strip or occlude content or hit targets; the approved global rail stays visually anchored while destination and sub-action content transitions finitely behind one shell; predecessor and successor OPPO screenshot matrices, complete real-user journeys, reduced-motion coverage and founder device acceptance are mandatory.

entries.mistake: A C16 required helper-script filename inventory was grouped with an optional ripgrep content search; the valid zero-match exit from the optional search surfaced the complete compound discovery as failed.
entries.rootCause: The optional ripgrep probe did not classify exit 1 as a valid zero-match result before sharing the required inventory command boundary.
entries.prevention: Required filename inventories and optional content probes run in separate boundaries; every optional ripgrep call captures its native exit immediately, accepts 0 as matches and 1 as an explicitly declared zero-match result, and rejects only values above 1.

entries.mistake: The first intended Social predecessor capture was named from the planned tap even though the OPPO remained on Eat / Book Table after the horizontally revealed rail snapped, so the PNG and XML did not prove Social.
entries.rootCause: Artifact naming trusted the intended interaction instead of requiring the fresh device semantics to confirm the resulting main family and selected sub-action.
entries.prevention: Every predecessor and successor screenshot is admitted only after its paired fresh UIAutomator dump proves the expected main family and selected sub-action; navigation misses remain preserved as explicitly rejected evidence and are never renamed or overwritten into valid proof.

entries.mistake: A read-only registration command guessed config/regression-test-registry.json, which does not exist, instead of using the durable config/codex-development-regression-registry.json owner.
entries.rootCause: The registry basename was recalled rather than resolved from the repository before the first read.
entries.prevention: Regression registration uses the reconciled durable owner path or performs exact workspace-bounded filename discovery before reading; a guessed-path failure is recorded and not retried until the authoritative owner is discovered.

entries.mistake: After Back on Social Create, the first OPPO IME sample reported mInputShown=false but mIsInputViewShown=true; treating the first false flag as sufficient would have allowed a rail tap during an unproven input-view transition.
entries.rootCause: Input-method dismissal signals can briefly diverge while the input view settles after Back.
entries.prevention: C16 samples fresh OPPO input-method state after a bounded settling interval and permits family navigation only when both mInputShown=false and mIsInputViewShown=false converge; a persistent mismatch remains a device-gate rejection.

entries.mistake: The first corrected IME policy required mIsInputViewShown=false, but this ColorOS build kept that secondary flag true after mShowRequested=false and mInputShown=false while a fresh screenshot proved Gboard absent and both rails reachable.
entries.rootCause: A vendor input-method service diagnostic flag was assumed to be authoritative visible-surface state after dismissal.
entries.prevention: C16 requires mShowRequested=false and mInputShown=false, retains mIsInputViewShown as diagnostic context, and separately proves the rail unobscured with a fresh device screenshot plus supported window-state evidence before navigation.

entries.mistake: A read-only OPPO probe invoked dumpsys window insets, but this ColorOS window service does not support that subcommand and returned a bad-command hint.
entries.rootCause: An Android window-service subcommand was assumed portable across vendor builds without reading the device service help first.
entries.prevention: C16 reads dumpsys window -h before selecting a supported read-only window-state command, and unsupported output is discarded rather than treated as IME evidence.

entries.mistake: The optional predecessor motion-video attempt assumed the OPPO exposed Android screenrecord; the hidden process exited 127, command discovery found no screenrecord binary, the remote MP4 did not exist, and the interaction end state was Ride / Cab rather than the intended sequence.
entries.rootCause: Device recording capability and the resulting selected state were not proven before selecting the capture workflow.
entries.prevention: C16 discovers device capture capability first, admits no background recording without a real artifact and successful native exit, and uses individually checksummed semantics-verified screenshot frame sequences for left, right and cross-route motion when screenrecord is unavailable.

entries.mistake: After the valid Ride left-motion frame sequence and Bike-selected semantics proof, checksum reporting passed a wildcard to Get-FileHash -LiteralPath, which rejected the path syntax and invalidated only the grouped hash output.
entries.rootCause: Literal-path mode was incorrectly combined with wildcard discovery during evidence reporting.
entries.prevention: C16 enumerates exact evidence files first and hashes each resolved literal path separately; a grouped checksum failure is discarded and no hash is claimed until an explicit-list retry succeeds.

entries.mistake: A C16 Hero-owner search passed scripts/check-personal-* and scripts/check-*navigation* as ripgrep path operands on Windows, producing path-syntax errors; the grouped lookup was discarded despite an earlier exact test hit.
entries.rootCause: Shell wildcard expansion was again assumed for native Windows ripgrep path operands.
entries.prevention: C16 passes only exact literal roots to ripgrep; filename narrowing starts with rg --files and a separate explicitly classified filter, and any grouped output containing a path error is discarded in full.

entries.mistake: An optional test inventory for legacy local-rail distribution and scroll tokens found no matches and returned ripgrep exit 1, but the command boundary did not classify the valid zero-match result.
entries.rootCause: The established C16 ripgrep zero-match handling was not applied to this new optional query.
entries.prevention: Every optional ripgrep call captures its native exit immediately, accepts 0 as matches and 1 as an explicitly declared zero-match result, and rejects only values above 1.

entries.mistake: The first C16A focused test failed to compile because math.max(0, a double layout expression) inferred num, which was then passed where clusterWidth required double.
entries.rootCause: An integer zero literal was mixed with double layout operands in the shared adaptive owner.
entries.prevention: Shared layout math uses double literals throughout and the focused C16A owner test must compile and pass before any destination-conformance ticket opens.

entries.mistake: A compound C16A retry launched from apps/mobile while using repository-root-relative registry and PowerShell gate paths; those paths were not found and Flutter never launched.
entries.rootCause: Repository governance and Flutter project commands with different path owners were combined under one working directory.
entries.prevention: C16 runs repository governance from the production-repository root and Flutter commands from apps/mobile in separate command boundaries, without reinterpreting relative paths across them.

entries.mistake: The shared local action declared enabled semantics and excluded descendant semantics, but omitted onTap on the outer Semantics node, so an available 44px action exposed no assistive tap action.
entries.rootCause: The physical InkWell owned the callback while excludeSemantics prevented that descendant action from reaching the accessibility node.
entries.prevention: Available local actions assign the same callback to the outer Semantics owner and the physical InkWell; selected actions keep both null, and focused coverage proves available semantic tap and selected inertness.

entries.mistake: The first C16A static gate searched source for runtime-expanded 2/3/4 test names, but the Dart test generates those labels from actionCount, causing a false rejection after all focused cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The checker conflated generated runtime display strings with literal source tokens.
entries.prevention: The static gate proves the explicit const [2, 3, 4] case set and the interpolated test-name source token, while runtime output proves each expanded case.

entries.mistake: A large hand-copied deletion hunk for the 317-line legacy Social rail block did not exactly match current file context and was rejected atomically after the new shared callsite had already been connected.
entries.rootCause: A long current-source block was manually reconstructed instead of deriving the deletion hunk byte-for-byte from the bounded file content.
entries.prevention: The retry reads the exact block between the legacy class start and following immutable model marker, constructs the deletion hunk from those exact lines, and applies it once; atomically rejected patches are confirmed unchanged before retry.

entries.mistake: The exact-block deletion workflow assumed the fresh V8 tool isolate exposed atob; decoding failed before apply-patch was called and the Social source remained unchanged.
entries.rootCause: A browser Base64 helper was assumed in a minimal orchestration isolate.
entries.prevention: The retry uses an explicit in-isolate Base64 decoder plus TextDecoder, validates decoded legacy boundary markers, and calls apply-patch only after exact payload validation succeeds.

entries.mistake: After explicit Base64 byte decoding, the exact-block workflow assumed the minimal tool isolate exposed TextDecoder; it did not, and execution stopped before apply-patch.
entries.rootCause: A second web-runtime global was assumed in the orchestration isolate.
entries.prevention: The bounded ASCII-only Dart block is decoded from validated bytes in small character chunks, legacy boundary tokens are verified, and apply-patch is called only after validation succeeds.

entries.mistake: The byte-derived deletion hunk treated the synthetic final empty element from splitting a newline-terminated block as an extra real blank line, so apply-patch expected one additional blank before the immutable marker and rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: Terminal string-split representation was mistaken for physical source-line representation.
entries.prevention: When the exact decoded block ends in newline, the generator drops exactly one synthetic terminal element, preserves the real blank source line, and uses the following immutable marker as unchanged context.

entries.mistake: The first C16B static gate searched for a contiguous MoolLocalNavigationTokens.providerIconWidth expression even though Dart format legally split the receiver and property across lines, causing a false rejection.
entries.rootCause: The checker encoded source presentation formatting instead of semantic token ownership and consumption.
entries.prevention: The gate proves providerIconWidth and providerIconHeight declarations plus SvgPicture.asset consumption independently of line wrapping.

entries.mistake: A combined Screen 04 plus C11 Flutter invocation passed C11 and all but one Social case, but the cross-main-action loop did not find mvp-action-root-eat after the Eat tap.
entries.rootCause: The failure source was not established by the combined potentially concurrent multi-file invocation and cannot be attributed to C16B without isolated reproduction.
entries.prevention: C16B replays the full Screen 04 conformance file in isolation before any source mutation; only an isolated reproducible owned regression may justify a fix, while combined-run-only interference remains recorded evidence.

entries.mistake: The isolated Screen 04 conformance file reproduced the repeated Mool main-action loop failure: mvp-action-root-eat was absent after the Eat tap while every other case in the file passed.
entries.rootCause: The symptom is isolated and reproducible, but the actual tapped action, router location and rendered owner still require bounded reconciliation before attributing the fault.
entries.prevention: C16B captures the loop's tapped global action, resulting router location and rendered destination owner before changing source; the correction must preserve Social, Mool, Eat, Back and global-rail behavior and pass isolated plus focused navigation coverage.

entries.mistake: The Screen 04 cross-main-action test still expected retired pre-C13 generic mvp-action-root-eat, ride, book and work owners even though the authorized defaults now render Eat home, Ride booking, Book doctor and Work earn directly.
entries.rootCause: The cross-navigation test was not migrated when C13 moved exact customer defaults before the generic action-choice owner.
entries.prevention: Screen 04 expects eat-home-screen, ride-booking-screen, book-doctor and work-earn-screen in line with current personalMoolRootActions and C10E/C13 coverage; production routes are never changed to satisfy stale generic-owner expectations.

entries.mistake: The first C16D focused 320px/140%-text replay reached Book Table but its fixed 124px horizontal restaurant cards overflowed their vertical Columns by 12px.
entries.rootCause: The card lane had a fixed height sized for default text even though the title and two-line availability copy scale with the platform text setting.
entries.prevention: The Eat table owner derives a bounded restaurant-card lane height from the active TextScaler, while C16D focused and existing Eat suites exercise 320px/140% text and content reachability without a render exception.

entries.mistake: The first C16D focused test attempted to tap eat-back after selecting Book Table, but the existing table owner explicitly sets showBack false and therefore renders no app-bar Back key.
entries.rootCause: The new family-conformance test assumed every Eat depth route exposes the optional app-bar control instead of reading the selected screen's existing navigation contract.
entries.prevention: C16D proves the required Back continuity through the platform/system pop route for Book Table, preserves showBack false, and never changes production navigation merely to satisfy an invented test control.

entries.mistake: The first combined C16D source/test/gate/registry patch contained an empty update hunk marker after the test Back replacement and was rejected atomically before any file changed.
entries.rootCause: Several independent file edits were assembled into one long patch without validating every update-hunk boundary.
entries.prevention: C16D records registry and evidence first, then applies a separate bounded source/test/gate patch with no empty hunk; atomic rejection is confirmed before retry.

entries.mistake: The first C16E focused test called ensureVisible on the selected Cab package before the lazy booking ListView had built that off-screen child, producing a Bad state: No element failure after the rail and in-place state assertions passed.
entries.rootCause: The new test treated a lazy sliver child as if it were already present in the element tree.
entries.prevention: C16E scrolls the keyed ride-booking-screen in bounded steps until the existing selected-package key is built, then uses ensureVisible and proves it is hit-testable above the local rail.

entries.mistake: The first C16F static gate required a literal const Key('doctor-care-clinic') in production even though DoctorBookingScreen correctly generates each care key from DoctorCare.values, causing a false rejection before the focused test ran.
entries.rootCause: The checker confused the runtime-expanded concrete finder used by the test with the interpolated source owner used by production.
entries.prevention: The static gate proves the generated doctor-care-${care.name} owner and DoctorCare.values inventory, while the focused Flutter test proves the concrete doctor-care-clinic control is present, reachable and preserved after Back.

entries.mistake: The first C16G focused test required the Earn info control to start wholly above the local rail at 320px/140% text even though the scrollable content initially placed its bottom 21px behind the anchored transparent shell; the control remained hit-testable.
entries.rootCause: The reachability proof conflated initial compact-viewport position with the required ability to reveal a target above the fixed navigation shell.
entries.prevention: C16G uses bounded drags on the keyed Earn and Workspace content owners until each existing primary control is wholly above the unchanged rail, then proves it is hit-testable; failure to reveal within the bound remains a rejection.

entries.mistake: The C16 placement-gate reconciliation attempted to read config/personal-subaction-placement-regression-state.json, a guessed companion state file that does not exist, after the authoritative checker had already identified its actual contract path.
entries.rootCause: A plausible state filename was inferred instead of enumerating the bounded config inventory and following the checker's declared contractPath.
entries.prevention: Placement reconciliation reads scripts/check-personal-subaction-placement-regression.ps1 first, follows only its exact mvp-personal-subaction-reachability-promotion-zone-regression.json contract, and uses rg --files for any additional bounded discovery.

entries.mistake: The first complete C16 positive-gate sweep stopped at the historical C10C checker because it still required _BuyDestinationTabs, readableNavigationCellWidth, selected reveal scheduling and an overflow cue that C16C intentionally removed.
entries.rootCause: The historical gate encoded its accepted C10C renderer implementation rather than only the durable four-destination, one-global-dock, route/key, selected-inert and one-tap behavior contract.
entries.prevention: C10C now proves the same Shop, Wholesale, Medicine and Orders meanings, public keys, callbacks, one runtime lower-shell call site, selected inertness and global Mool/Chat owner through _buildBuyLocalNavigation and MoolLocalNavigationRail, while explicitly rejecting the retired lane/cue classes.

entries.mistake: After C10D passed, the complete C16 gate sweep stopped at C10E because its local-navigation owner inventory still mandated moolsocial-local-navigation-scroll, a key removed with the forbidden horizontal lane.
entries.rootCause: The historical motion-containment checker encoded the former scroll wrapper rather than the durable local owner, finite motion, selected semantics and global-shell containment behavior.
entries.prevention: C10E now requires the adaptive layout and compact-cluster keys plus shared token owner and explicitly rejects the retired scroll key, while retaining every main-route transition, reduced-motion and Back/global-shell assertion.

entries.mistake: The first attempted complete C16 host cycle passed 250 universal/Social and 58 shared-family/vertical tests, but the Buy shard ended at 360 active passes with one failure because buy_v2_navigation_motion_test still required the removed overflow cue and horizontal scroll key.
entries.rootCause: The existing compact large-text navigation case encoded the rejected C15 Buy lane interaction instead of the durable requirement that all four destinations remain directly visible, at least 44px, fixed-shell and overflow-free.
entries.prevention: The test now proves the Buy owner is MoolLocalNavigationRail, the compact cluster is 304px at 320px/140% text, no descendant Scrollable or overflow cue exists, Orders is directly hit-testable in one tap and fixed chrome/state remain intact. Both qualifying cycles restart from zero after this correction.

entries.mistake: The first post-host APK-contract inspection placed an explicit exit 0 immediately after the optional APK-script inventory, so the intended trailing pubspec version read never executed even though the command reported success.
entries.rootCause: Optional ripgrep exit normalization used process termination in the middle of a multi-step read-only command instead of validating the code and continuing.
entries.prevention: C16H validates optional inventory status without process exit before later statements, then reads the exact APK gate, wrapper and pubspec version in separate bounded command sections before any authorization mutation.

entries.mistake: The first post-host regression-memory rerun invoked scripts/check-codex-regression-memory.ps1, a guessed shortened filename that does not exist, so the parallel read-only inspection stopped before returning the other requested outputs.
entries.rootCause: The checker name was recalled from its purpose instead of being resolved from the bounded scripts inventory or the registry's exact gate path.
entries.prevention: C16H resolves the checker through rg --files or follows the registry's exact scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 path before invocation, and keeps independent inspection outputs from being hidden behind one failed parallel aggregate.

entries.mistake: The first C16H source-aggregate calculation unnecessarily piped a here-string into a nested powershell -Command process; it returned exit code zero but no aggregate lines, so no fingerprint could be sealed.
entries.rootCause: A script that was already running in PowerShell added a second command-parser/process boundary instead of executing the bounded read-only calculation directly.
entries.prevention: C16H runs the aggregate function directly in the workspace shell, requires all four labeled aggregate lines plus branch and HEAD before accepting the result, and does not seal an empty or partially emitted manifest.

entries.mistake: The direct aggregate retry embedded PowerShell newline backticks inside a JavaScript raw template literal, so the orchestrator parser rejected the tool script before the shell ran.
entries.rootCause: Two languages used the same backtick delimiter and the inner PowerShell tokens were not removed before constructing the JavaScript template.
entries.prevention: C16H uses a PowerShell command that contains no backtick tokens when passed through a JavaScript template, joins lines with [Environment]::NewLine, and treats parser rejection as no aggregate result and no authorization progress.

entries.mistake: The first post-build signer-tool evidence lookup passed a wildcard inside an rg root directory path on Windows, which rg rejected as an invalid filename before searching.
entries.rootCause: A shell-glob path pattern was used where Windows rg requires an existing literal root plus a -g file filter or a prior bounded file enumeration.
entries.prevention: C16H searches the literal artifacts/quality and docs/quality roots and uses rg -g filters or an exact known predecessor directory; no signer conclusion is drawn from the rejected lookup.

entries.mistake: During the C16H cumulative OPPO journey, a tap derived from the global rail's vertically clipped UIAutomator bounds was intended for Eat but selected Ride/Cab instead.
entries.rootCause: The global rail semantics nodes are clipped to a 10-pixel vertical interval in the XML while the visible native shell extends below it; combining those XML x-bounds with a visual-shell y-coordinate did not represent the actual transformed hit region after automatic rail centering.
entries.prevention: C16H registers the wrong-route event, admits no mislabeled capture, uses the truthful Ride/Cab state as diagnostic only, and derives subsequent global taps from a fresh screenshot plus verified selected semantics after each tap. Every matrix capture must validate the expected family and local selected state.

entries.mistake: A C16H Work/Workspace capture was attempted after a screenshot appeared to show Work, but the fresh paired semantics at admission time had already settled on Mool Home; the validator correctly rejected the capture.
entries.rootCause: The prior global-rail coordinate event had not produced a proven stable destination identity, and a visual diagnostic frame was treated as a sufficient starting-state signal before a second stable semantics sample.
entries.prevention: C16H admits no rejected Work file, requires two consecutive fresh semantics samples with the same family/local state before every post-global-transition matrix capture, and uses only explicit verified events from the stable state. Unexpected route movement is investigated before further family capture.

entries.mistake: After admitting the valid Eat/Order Food screenshot, the Book Table tap command omitted one character from the OPPO serial, so adb rejected the event and the subsequent validator found Order Food still selected.
entries.rootCause: The serial was retyped inside a long capture command instead of reused from one validated device-serial variable.
entries.prevention: All remaining C16H device commands bind the exact serial 2b3e0f71 once and reuse that variable. The resulting mislabeled 10-eat-book-table files are preserved as rejected evidence and excluded; the truthful retry uses a unique filename and validates Eat plus Book Table semantics.

entries.mistake: The checksum-matched r60.16 successor made the six families structurally uniform but still presented their subactions as minimally decorated icon-and-label cells without a professional, intentional button-level visual design for each action.
entries.rootCause: C16 optimized shared ownership, compact geometry and uniform tokens while treating removal of the rejected strip/panel as sufficient visual resolution; it did not establish a founder-acceptable action-control composition, hierarchy and affordance system.
entries.prevention: Any successor must begin with a new founder-authorized visual contract that specifies the complete per-action control anatomy and proves it on the real OPPO across all six families before build qualification. Structural uniformity alone cannot pass.

entries.mistake: The r60.16 family/theme colour treatment is founder-rejected: Buy is the clearest example, where the coloured trapezoid/wave/rail treatment uses the wrong colours and visually blocks or competes with the destination background; the same systemic issue is present across main-action families.
entries.rootCause: Family accent tokens were applied to the connection and selected treatment without a device-proven colour/opacity/contrast composition against the actual content and global-shell backgrounds for every family.
entries.prevention: A successor must separately qualify family palette, surface transparency, connector shape and content preservation on real destination backgrounds, with Buy as an explicit rejection fixture and all six families checked for zero visual blocking before one candidate is authorized.

entries.mistake: Subaction labels in r60.16 are not professionally visible or legible on the real device across the main-action families, despite passing host geometry and semantics tests.
entries.rootCause: The shared 10.5 logical-pixel label token and accent/neutral state rules were accepted from host fitment evidence without a founder-accepted device-level typography, contrast and background-interference threshold.
entries.prevention: Any authorized successor must introduce machine-readable device-oriented label size, weight, contrast and state-visibility acceptance criteria, then prove every current label in all 17 selected states without truncation, low contrast or background competition.

entries.mistake: The first C17B clear-glass control painted its border in the child-padding decoration, so the nominal 48px control exposed a 46px keyed InkWell and large-text content overflowed vertically by up to two pixels.
entries.rootCause: Flutter's decorated Container includes a border's dimensions in decoration padding; the implementation verified the outside constraint but initially failed to measure the final interactive and text descendants.
entries.prevention: The shared owner paints the glass fill in the background decoration and the border in a non-deflating foreground decoration. Focused tests directly measure every keyed InkWell at 48px or larger and admit no large-text overflow at 320px before any family ticket advances.

entries.mistake: The first C17B large-text test expected a 316px four-action cluster at a 320px viewport even though the authoritative layout preserves 4px on each side and correctly produced 312px.
entries.rootCause: The test duplicated a hand-calculated width instead of calling the shared MoolLocalNavigationTokens.clusterWidth function used by production.
entries.prevention: Responsive expectations are derived from the shared layout token function and separately assert centering and minimum 48px targets; no copied magic width may contradict required rail insets.

entries.mistake: The first C17B press-state test asserted the .985 target immediately after pointer-down and read 1.0 before InkWell's press highlight recognizer had activated.
entries.rootCause: The test treated raw pointer-down as synchronous InkWell highlight activation and did not advance the finite recognizer interval before inspecting AnimatedScale.
entries.prevention: The focused interaction test holds the gesture through the InkWell recognition interval, asserts the finite .985 target, releases it and proves exactly one action callback; reduced motion remains separately immediate.

entries.mistake: The first combined C17B correction patch reused a pre-format multiline test context, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch after dart format changed the expression's shape.
entries.rootCause: The retry patch was composed from remembered context instead of a fresh bounded read of the formatter's current output.
entries.prevention: After formatting or any failed combined patch, inspect exact bounded snippets and retry in narrow hunks. An atomic apply_patch rejection is confirmed as no mutation and never treated as partial success.

entries.mistake: The first C17B static-gate command used a repository-relative scripts path from apps/mobile; PowerShell rejected it, while the following successful analyzer caused the aggregate shell to return exit code zero.
entries.rootCause: Two independently admissible checks were chained under one final exit status without first resolving their paths against the command working directory.
entries.prevention: Run repository PowerShell gates separately from the exact repository root and admit each gate only from its own exit status and pass line. Flutter commands run separately from apps/mobile; a later success never masks an earlier rejection.

entries.mistake: The first C17C Social/Buy coverage lookup included the nonexistent apps/mobile/test/features root, so ripgrep rejected that path while returning results from a different valid root.
entries.rootCause: A presumed test-directory convention was added without first deriving real paths from the repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: C17C derives candidate tests from rg --files apps/mobile/test and searches only verified literal paths. Mixed-root output containing any path rejection is not complete inventory evidence.

entries.mistake: After the shared rail advanced to 52px with 48px controls, Social's Screen04ContextTabs family wrapper still imposed a hard-coded 44px height and could clip the successor control composition.
entries.rootCause: The C17B standalone owner changed its authoritative geometry, but a family-local historical wrapper duplicated the predecessor height instead of consuming the shared rail-height token.
entries.prevention: C17C binds every Social wrapper to MoolLocalNavigationTokens.railHeight and focused tests measure the wrapper, rail and all four final keyed targets at 320px with large text. Static family gates reject numeric 44px wrapper duplication.

entries.mistake: C17C regression entry 350 named a planned focused-test path before that sequential ticket had authority to create the test, so the permanent memory checker rejected the missing path.
entries.rootCause: Planned acceptance coverage was recorded as an already-existing gate instead of being kept in the ticket test plan until file creation.
entries.prevention: Regression entries reference only files that exist at registration time. Future tests remain in ticket plans and are added to static gates only after their authorized creation is verified.

entries.mistake: The first C17C Social test forbade every FittedBox below the rail and falsely rejected the two retained YouTube SVG widgets, whose renderer legitimately fits vector artwork inside its icon box.
entries.rootCause: A label no-shrink acceptance rule was applied to the entire family subtree instead of the real Text label ancestor chains.
entries.prevention: C17C checks no FittedBox ancestor for each real label while separately requiring exactly two provider SvgPicture owners. Provider artwork containment cannot satisfy or violate label typography rules.

entries.mistake: The first C17C Buy test applied 200% text scaling to the entire route and triggered fourteen unrelated catalogue and global-dock overflows, obscuring the local-navigation conformance signal.
entries.rootCause: The test applied the isolated local rail's external stress scale to all application owners even though C17 authorizes subaction changes only and specifies a 130% navigation acceptance threshold.
entries.prevention: Full Social/Buy routes qualify local navigation at the founder-approved 130% maximum navigation scale; the isolated shared rail separately proves 200% system input is clamped locally. Unrelated full-route overflow findings authorize no out-of-scope mutation.

entries.mistake: The C17 shared glassFill token used Color.alphaBlend for selected tinting, which raised Social media glass from the approved .58 base alpha to about .631 and weakened background visibility.
entries.rootCause: The tint operation composited an additional translucent accent layer over a translucent base instead of changing only the glass RGB while retaining its alpha contract.
entries.prevention: Selected and pressed glass interpolate color toward a family accent whose alpha equals the base glass alpha, so light stays .52 and media stays .58 in every state. Focused tests inspect selected and available final decoration alphas for both tones.

entries.mistake: The first registration patch for C17C's selected-glass alpha defect used an inexact remembered evidence-document line wrap, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch.
entries.rootCause: The registration retry targeted prose context without first reading its exact current wrapped form.
entries.prevention: When evidence prose context is uncertain, create a uniquely named evidence file and patch the exact current registry tail. An atomic patch rejection is registered and treated as no mutation before any runtime retry.

entries.mistake: A C17C command placed focused Flutter analysis and the Social/Buy test replay under one final shell exit status, repeating an already registered aggregate-admission risk even though both printed pass lines.
entries.rootCause: Independent qualification checks were optimized into one shell call despite the permanent rule that each result must own its exit status.
entries.prevention: Flutter analysis and test suites run as separate shell commands and each is admitted only by its own exit status plus explicit pass output. Successful combined output is preserved as diagnostic only.

entries.mistake: A C17E evidence lookup embedded a wildcard in a Windows ripgrep path operand, so that path was rejected while a different source operand still returned lines.
entries.rootCause: A filename discovery wildcard was supplied where ripgrep requires an existing literal root and a separate -g filter.
entries.prevention: C17E evidence discovery uses verified literal directories with -g filename filters or rg --files plus a bounded filter. Any mixed command with a path rejection is discarded for the rejected evidence conclusion.

entries.mistake: The first C17E matrix command read repository config paths from apps/mobile and aggregated JSON validation, formatting and tests under one final shell status.
entries.rootCause: Repository-root and Flutter-package operations were combined without resolving each path or preserving independent exit status ownership.
entries.prevention: Validate repository JSON independently from the repository root; run formatter, analyzer and tests as separate package-root commands; admit each qualification check only from its own exit status and explicit output.

entries.mistake: The first C17E matrix attempted to read width and height getters from AnimatedContainer, so the test failed compilation before any selected state ran.
entries.rootCause: The test treated AnimatedContainer like a SizedBox API even though its dimensions are represented by animated constraints rather than public width and height getters.
entries.prevention: C17E measures the rendered selected-indicator size through tester.getSize and uses the AnimatedContainer widget only for duration and decoration inspection. Focused analysis must compile before matrix execution.

entries.mistake: A C17E predecessor-cycle lookup appended a read of the guessed nonexistent apps/mobile/dart_test.yaml path, invalidating the aggregate configuration lookup.
entries.rootCause: A conventional Flutter test-config filename was assumed instead of derived from the repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: C17E derives test configuration and shard inputs from rg --files under verified literal roots. Historical shard counts remain documentary evidence, but guessed-path failures cannot establish exact current commands.

entries.mistake: The first attempted C17E host-cycle shard 1 outlived its yielded execution cell, and neither the cell nor an attached desktop terminal retained its final completion output or exit status.
entries.rootCause: A long Flutter shard was allowed to yield without a durable final-result capture; partial running output was available, but the execution cell disappeared before its terminal status could be collected.
entries.prevention: A host shard counts only from its own retained final exit code and explicit Flutter completion line. A missing cell is registered as evidence loss and the entire shard is rerun as a new uncounted attempt with bounded output and repeated waits until final completion.

entries.mistake: C17E host-cycle shard 1 included screen04_social_operational_baseline_test.dart despite the permanent rule that excludes golden-capture owners from protected runtime cycles without explicit golden-verification authority; its seven preserved predecessor comparisons rejected the intentional C17 pixels.
entries.rootCause: The shard was copied from an inferred historical Screen04 file group instead of filtering every discovered source for matchesGoldenFile and applying existing registry entry REG-20260807-066.
entries.prevention: C17E countable runtime shards exclude every source containing matchesGoldenFile. No predecessor golden is updated or re-accepted; C17's separately authorized successor visual evidence remains the later cumulative OPPO screenshot matrix.

entries.mistake: A C17E diagnostic command combined scoped git status and a candidate-capture ripgrep search; the later no-match exit code produced one empty aggregate result that could not independently establish either conclusion.
entries.rootCause: Two distinct read-only checks were joined under one shell invocation even though each result required its own exit-status interpretation.
entries.prevention: Repository status and file-content inventories run as separate commands with independent exits. Ripgrep exit 1 is interpreted only for its own verified literal input and never masks or invalidates an adjacent check.

entries.mistake: The first C17E Buy shard ran the whole test/ui_v2/buy directory and therefore included 18 matchesGoldenFile owners; two candidate-capture suites rejected the intentional C17 rail pixels against preserved predecessor images.
entries.rootCause: The directory was treated as a homogeneous runtime suite without filtering its Dart inventory for golden capture calls, repeating the protected-Social selection class across Buy.
entries.prevention: C17E builds the countable Buy runtime shard only from verified Dart files that do not contain matchesGoldenFile. Accepted predecessor images remain unchanged and golden failures cannot count toward a host cycle.

entries.mistake: Two non-golden Buy tests still expected the predecessor 304px four-action cluster at 320px and rejected the authorized C17 312px shared-token result before their remaining navigation and overflow assertions completed.
entries.rootCause: The C17 compatibility update missed literal cluster-width expectations in buy_v2_navigation_motion_test.dart and uaw_personal_mvp_buy_subaction_professional_conformance_c16c_test.dart.
entries.prevention: Both tests derive the expected width from MoolLocalNavigationTokens.clusterWidth for four actions and 320px. The C17C static gate rejects a literal closeTo(304) expectation in Buy navigation owners.

entries.mistake: A parallel C17E Buy source inspection used package-relative test paths while every command ran from the repository root, so the test reads were rejected as missing.
entries.rootCause: The orchestration reused one repository working directory for both repository-root scripts and apps/mobile-relative test paths.
entries.prevention: Parallel cross-root inspections use exact absolute workspace paths for every source, or assign each command its verified owner directory independently. A missing-path result is discarded before patch composition.

entries.mistake: The first Buy stale-width correction invoked MoolLocalNavigationTokens.clusterWidth with invented named arguments, so both corrected tests failed compilation before assertions ran.
entries.rootCause: The patch was written from a remembered conceptual signature instead of the existing positional declaration clusterWidth(double maxWidth, int actionCount).
entries.prevention: Buy tests call the exact shared API as clusterWidth(320, 4), and the C17C static gate requires that real expression. Focused compilation runs before any whole-shard retry.

entries.mistake: Two focused Buy tests were replayed through a fail-fast parallel aggregate, and the first nonzero tool result prevented the sibling command's exit and output from being retained independently.
entries.rootCause: Promise.all was used for qualification commands even though any rejection aborts aggregate result collection.
entries.prevention: Qualification replays run as separate shell calls, one test per retained exit status. Parallel orchestration is limited to read-only inspections whose rejected siblings do not need admission evidence, or uses explicit all-settled capture when appropriate.

entries.mistake: The first C17F reconciliation used git status --porcelain=v1 -uall across preserved Chromium-profile artifacts, emitted filename-too-long warnings, and then derived a count and hash that could not prove complete whole-repository dirty identity.
entries.rootCause: An unbounded full-untracked traversal was used even though historical evidence contains deeply nested Windows paths outside the build source manifest.
entries.prevention: C17F preserves every artifact and seals the established bounded source/status inventory instead. Tracked status is read with untracked traversal disabled, current-ticket untracked roots are inventoried explicitly, and any path-warning command is inadmissible for identity even at exit zero.

entries.mistake: The first C18 provenance audit requested a combined Screen01 source-and-test historical diff with eighty context lines, and the tool truncated the output before it could establish the divergence.
entries.rootCause: Potentially large historical diffs were combined without first measuring their size or bounding each file and output slice.
entries.prevention: Historical comparisons first inventory numstat and stat, then inspect one verified file at a time in explicit non-overlapping bounded slices. Truncated output is rejected as evidence.

entries.mistake: The first bounded C18 test comparison used a guessed directory-shaped Screen01 test path that does not exist, so its empty diff could not establish equality or divergence.
entries.rootCause: The test operand was inferred from the source directory instead of derived from the immutable v3 lock manifest or verified file inventory.
entries.prevention: Protected-owner comparisons use exact paths declared by the accepted lock record; an empty diff is admitted only after both operands are verified.

entries.mistake: A C18 repository-wide search for the current shared brand-motion SHA traversed all historical artifact manifests and returned truncated output that could not establish provenance.
entries.rootCause: The search was not constrained to the earliest post-R50 ticket window or to filename-only bounded results.
entries.prevention: Hash provenance first narrows candidate artifact roots by ticket/date and returns only bounded filenames or explicit first/last matches. Truncated artifact-tree output is discarded.

entries.mistake: The first C18A installed-launch screenshot was captured while the OPPO display was asleep and produced an entirely black inadmissible image.
entries.rootCause: The capture sequence did not verify awake and unlocked device state before force-stop, launch and screencap.
entries.prevention: Device visual replays prove awake and unblocked display state before launch. Black or asleep captures are preserved as rejected evidence and never establish presentation equivalence.

entries.mistake: The C18A awake-device precondition screencap returned nonzero without retaining a useful device-side diagnostic, and no successor image could be admitted.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper threw immediately on screencap failure without independently retaining raw output or verifying remote-file creation.
entries.prevention: Device capture retries retain screencap output and exit status, verify the exact remote file, and only then pull. Failed captures never establish visual equivalence.

entries.mistake: The current Screen01 presentation diverges from all three immutable v3 goldens even though its direct source and test are the exact R50 manifest bytes; treating the mismatch as a stale hash would falsely accept normal, slow and recovery pixel drift together.
entries.rootCause: R50 changed the direct Screen01 owner for an accepted progressive launch treatment while the v3 production lock and three-state goldens remained active; the later state was never separated into accepted R50 pixels and unrelated protected-state drift.
entries.prevention: A successor Screen01 acceptance requires exact state-by-state provenance. No v4 reference or golden update may occur until founder-accepted R50 normal-launch change is isolated from slow/recovery drift, the protected runtime correction scope is authorized, and the unlocked installed device is replayed.

entries.mistake: One nominal 2800 ms ADB Screen01 capture sampled an incomplete active-compositor frame with the wordmark layer absent, so it cannot establish a stable user-visible state.
entries.rootCause: Device-side screencap was not synchronized to a Flutter frame boundary while multiple reveal layers were actively compositing.
entries.prevention: Active-motion device frames require a unique same-stage repeat plus a complete settled control. A one-off partial compositor capture is preserved but inadmissible unless the state repeats.

entries.mistake: A same-stage Screen01 screencap repeat restored the wordmark but omitted a different independently painted footer layer, proving isolated screencaps are not reliable continuity evidence during active composition.
entries.rootCause: C18A continued sampling individual compositor snapshots after the first asynchronous partial-layer frame instead of switching immediately to consecutive-frame recording.
entries.prevention: Active-motion continuity is qualified from one bounded screen recording spanning the full reveal. Single screencaps remain usable only for stable settled states and are not used to infer flicker.

entries.mistake: The first C18A screen-recording orchestration used a hidden local ADB process that exited 127 before Wait-Process and retained no standard output or error diagnostic.
entries.rootCause: Recording capability and Android-shell invocation were not proven in the foreground before local background-process orchestration.
entries.prevention: Run a foreground device-side screenrecord capability check first; start the qualified recording inside Android shell, verify the remote file independently, then pull and hash it. Diagnostic-less hidden ADB processes are prohibited.

entries.mistake: The first C18A VM-capture lookup included the guessed nonexistent apps/mobile/tool path, so its mixed ripgrep result could not establish reusable capture ownership.
entries.rootCause: A conventional Flutter tool directory was assumed instead of derived from the repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: VM-capture discovery uses rg --files under verified literal roots; evidence reads and source searches run separately, and missing-path aggregates are rejected.

entries.mistake: A cosmetic hash-case cleanup appended a code expression outside a SHA-256 JSON string in the new unqualified v4 production-acceptance file, making it syntactically invalid.
entries.rootCause: String normalization syntax was mistakenly written into data instead of replacing the literal with a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal value.
entries.prevention: Acceptance hashes are literal hexadecimal strings only; every new machine-readable reference file is independently parsed before checksum or manifest generation.

entries.mistake: After Screen01 v4 reconciliation, the protected UI gate advanced and revealed that Screen03's active lock expects a different platform_configuration_test.dart hash from the current workspace.
entries.rootCause: The earlier Screen01 fail-fast rejection masked a later independent protected Screen03 owner divergence, whose accepted-successor lineage has not yet been proven.
entries.prevention: Reconcile protected owners sequentially and screen-specifically. Do not retry, restore, rebaseline or mutate Screen03 until clean status, Git lineage and applicable founder-accepted evidence prove the correct disposition.

entries.mistake: The first all-owner Screen03 hash audit named its helper H, which resolved as the PowerShell Get-History alias and returned blank hashes for every path.
entries.rootCause: A single-letter helper name collided with a built-in PowerShell alias, and the audit did not validate its computed hash shape before comparison.
entries.prevention: Hash helpers use descriptive non-alias names and assert every result is exactly 64 hexadecimal characters before any mismatch conclusion.

entries.mistake: The first C19 profile-marker owner inspection combined a valid test diff with a guessed nonexistent ui_v2/journey/journey_session.dart path and exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: A conventional UI directory was assumed even though the displayed test diff named the actual features/journey01 source owner.
entries.prevention: Derive source-owner paths from literal test references or rg --files before inspection; do not mix guessed paths into an otherwise valid evidence command.

entries.mistake: The first C19 manifest patch matched a generic production-accepted status token and superseded Screen01 v4 instead of Screen03 v2, temporarily leaving zero active Screen01 and two active Screen03 versions.
entries.rootCause: The patch hunk did not include screen id, version and lineage context even though the target status value occurs in multiple manifest entries.
entries.prevention: Manifest status patches include unique screen id, version and adjacent lineage context; immediately parse and assert exactly one active production version for every affected screen before any gate replay.

entries.mistake: The first focused C19 gate resolved approved-reference manifest links from the repository root and falsely reported the existing v3 interaction contract missing.
entries.rootCause: Repository-relative production-owner paths and approved-reference-root-relative manifest links were passed through one resolver without an explicit base boundary.
entries.prevention: Reference gates use an approved-references base for manifest contract, checksum and acceptance links, while production owners use the repository base; both resolvers enforce containment.

entries.mistake: The first C19 gate-parameter inspection queried a guessed nonexistent scripts/check-customer-copy-machine.ps1 path and made the mixed command exit nonzero.
entries.rootCause: A prose gate label in historical ticket metadata was treated as a verified filesystem owner without inventorying scripts.
entries.prevention: Resolve gate scripts from rg --files scripts before reading or invoking them; do not reconstruct filenames from prose labels.

entries.mistake: A C19 host-qualification command passed the unsupported value testing to the regression-memory Phase parameter after two preceding gates had passed.
entries.rootCause: A conceptual activity label was used instead of the script's declared general, implementation, build or device ValidateSet.
entries.prevention: Use Phase implementation for host test and qualification work, and retain the inspected parameter contract rather than inventing semantic phase names.

entries.mistake: The first C18D pre-cycle C17E gate allowed the refresh ticket only at the top-level entry point and then rejected in nested C17B's original C17-only sequence gate.
entries.rootCause: The host-gate call graph was not fully inventoried before adding the exact successor-ticket compatibility rule.
entries.prevention: Inventory every nested C17E gate and apply the exact C18D successor allowance consistently while preserving all design assertions and closed runtime, backend, build, install and external authority.

entries.mistake: The first C18D full pre-cycle chain passed Flutter analysis and scope but Screen03's focused gate rejected because it allowed only C19 as the active ticket.
entries.rootCause: The protected-lock gate had no exact successor qualification allowance after its owner ticket completed.
entries.prevention: Protected-lock gates may allow only explicitly named successor qualification tickets while retaining every owner hash, package, lineage and closed runtime/build/install assertion.

entries.mistake: The first C18D cycle-1 shard-1 command added seven top-level Social suites to the established boundary and passed 307 tests instead of the required 252, so the run could not qualify.
entries.rootCause: The evidence statement separating 30 Universal/Social files from the one Screen04 conformance owner was misread as permission to include every non-golden top-level Social suite.
entries.prevention: C18D shard 1 is exactly 29 ui_v2/universal files, one ui_v2/social file and screen04_universal_v2_conformance_test.dart; validate 31 files, zero golden owners and exactly 252 passing tests before counting a cycle.
