entries.mistake: The first C18D completion-metadata read used two reconstructed C17 and C18 ticket filenames that do not exist, causing an otherwise read-only inspection command to report path errors.
entries.rootCause: Ticket display names were converted into conventional filenames instead of resolving the durable config owners from the repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve ticket configuration paths with rg --files config and exact ticketId content before reading or patching them; never reconstruct production ticket filenames from prose titles.

entries.mistake: The first r60.17 uniqueness lookup recursively searched the repository-wide evidence tree and timed out before returning a complete result.
entries.rootCause: Candidate-identity discovery was mixed with an unbounded historical-artifact text scan even though uniqueness can be established from durable config, quality documents and bounded top-level artifact names.
entries.prevention: Successor uniqueness checks use bounded literal roots and top-level artifact-directory inventories, exclude binary/build/tmp trees, and run candidate-id and version checks separately with explicit timeouts.

entries.mistake: The first C17F prebuild chain directly replayed the host-only C17B gate while C17F held reference/evidence-write authority, so the gate correctly refused the non-host ticket after earlier prebuild checks passed.
entries.rootCause: A completed C18D host-seal dependency was treated as a gate that must be re-executed under the later build/evidence ticket, despite its explicit authority boundary and unchanged qualified source fingerprint.
entries.prevention: C17F consumes the passed C18D C17B/C17C/C17D/C17E evidence and independently recomputes the unchanged qualified source fingerprint. Host-only gates are not weakened, patched or replayed under build/evidence authority after qualification.

entries.mistake: The C17F guarded wrapper was launched through a shell call with an insufficient orchestration timeout; the caller returned exit 124 while the original PowerShell, Flutter/Dart and Gradle/Java child processes remained active.
entries.rootCause: A short tool-yield timeout was incorrectly supplied as the command lifetime for a production APK build instead of using a persistent yielded execution cell with a build-appropriate runtime.
entries.prevention: Never retry a timed-out build while any original wrapper or child process remains or build outcome is ambiguous. Monitor that exact process tree and reserved artifact/provenance paths to terminal completion; future builds use a persistent execution cell with at least 120 seconds initial yield and wait on the same cell.

entries.mistake: The first C17G postbuild validation passed a repository-relative Windows path to aapt, which could not load the APK, and the aggregate command did not inspect aapt's exit code before continuing to signature validation.
entries.rootCause: The APK variable was joined from a relative artifact root rather than resolved to an absolute literal path, and native-tool exit validation was deferred across independent commands.
entries.prevention: Resolve APK paths to absolute filesystem paths before Android build-tool invocation and check LASTEXITCODE immediately after each aapt or apksigner command. Missing badging output is a rejection even when later signer and source checks pass.

entries.mistake: The second C17G badging attempt used the correct absolute reserved-artifact path, but aapt still rejected the existing APK because the candidate's descriptive Windows path exceeded the tool's asset-path handling boundary.
entries.rootCause: Absolute-path correction did not account for aapt's legacy Windows path-length limitation on the deeply nested descriptive artifact filename.
entries.prevention: When the reserved artifact and Flutter generated output have proven identical SHA-256 and byte length, run aapt against the shorter generated-output path and bind the result to the reserved artifact by that checksum identity. Never rename, rebuild or substitute unmatched bytes to work around aapt.

entries.mistake: The first C17G preinstall gate falsely rejected the live 100 percent battery because an exact end-of-line regex was applied to CRLF-bearing adb text captured through Out-String.
entries.rootCause: Device readiness was parsed as one platform-sensitive text blob instead of extracting the numeric battery level independently of line endings and terminal formatting.
entries.prevention: Parse the battery level with a whitespace-tolerant numeric capture such as 'level:\s*(\d+)' and validate the captured integer; never use a CRLF-sensitive exact-line assertion on adb Out-String output.

entries.mistake: The follow-up C17G battery-policy lookup combined a successful live battery read with an optional ripgrep query that found no registry text and made the aggregate command exit nonzero.
entries.rootCause: A diagnostic no-match result was not normalized separately from the authoritative live device read.
entries.prevention: Run optional registry searches independently or explicitly treat ripgrep exit 1 as a valid no-match result; never let an optional inventory miss invalidate successful device evidence.

entries.mistake: The single C17G adb install command used the deeply nested reserved artifact path; adb failed its local stat before transmitting package bytes, so the command was consumed with zero device mutation.
entries.rootCause: The earlier aapt long-path rejection was not generalized to adb's local Windows path handling before the one authorized install invocation.
entries.prevention: Before an authorized install, prove the actual adb input path with a read-only local existence/stat and keep it within adb's Windows path boundary. A shorter generated-output path may be used only after exact byte length and SHA-256 equality to the reserved candidate are re-proven and a separate install-recovery ticket is selected.

entries.mistake: The first C17H installed-state metadata patch expected an installAuthorized true line in the APK buildResult block, but the verified current file retained false there; apply_patch rejected the entire patch without mutation.
entries.rootCause: Ticket execution authority and APK build-result install readiness were conflated, and the multi-file patch was composed without reading the exact current machine-state contexts after the C17H recovery transition.
entries.prevention: Before installed-state reconciliation, inventory exact ticket execution, successor, buildResult and installResult fields independently. Patch only verified literal contexts and parse every affected JSON file immediately afterward.

entries.mistake: The first C17H family capture batch used static tap coordinates and captured a screenshot before waiting for two stable route states; screenshot pixels and the later UI hierarchy diverged, leaving filenames that did not truthfully identify every selected state.
entries.rootCause: Coordinates were inferred from a previous screen and capture considered a single timed delay sufficient even though destination transitions and UIAutomator sampling complete asynchronously.
entries.prevention: Navigate by the current semantic button bounds, wait until the expected selected semantic appears in two consecutive UI hierarchies, then capture screenshot and final hierarchy. Preserve but reject every static-coordinate or mismatched screenshot/XML pair; qualifying replacements use unique q-prefixed names.

entries.mistake: The first semantic capture orchestration embedded PowerShell backtick and regex quoting inside the JavaScript tool wrapper and failed JavaScript parsing before any command or device action started.
entries.rootCause: A complex multi-function PowerShell program was inlined through two parser layers instead of stored as evidence-local tooling with literal syntax.
entries.prevention: Complex device-capture PowerShell lives in an artifact-local .ps1 created with apply_patch and is invoked with simple literal arguments. Inline exec commands remain short and contain no nested backtick/regex parser boundary.

entries.mistake: The first artifact-helper capture assumed the previously observed Work/Earn state was still current; the state had changed before invocation, so the helper correctly timed out without saving qualifying evidence.
entries.rootCause: A prior inventory result was carried across an asynchronous device interval instead of re-inventorying immediately before the first semantic target.
entries.prevention: Every semantic capture session begins with an inventory-only live hierarchy read. Navigate from an exact currently exposed semantic target, then wait for the destination's selected semantic twice before capture; never assert a carried-over starting state.

entries.mistake: After a semantic Open Wholesale tap, the capture helper waited for the guessed label 'Wholesale, current'; that exact label was not proven from the post-tap hierarchy, so the helper timed out and saved no Wholesale evidence.
entries.rootCause: The action semantic was verified before tapping, but the destination's selected semantic wording was inferred from the button copy instead of inventoried from the resulting live hierarchy.
entries.prevention: After each new destination type or family is tapped for the first time, run inventory-only and record its exact selected semantic. Only then invoke the two-consecutive-dump capture using that literal label; do not derive selected wording from the action label.

entries.mistake: A tap computed from UIAutomator's bottom subaction bounds did not activate Open Wholesale and the next inventory showed Social/Shorts, proving those clipped hierarchy coordinates do not map directly to adb input space on the OPPO system-bar layout.
entries.rootCause: The hierarchy root ends at 1442 while the physical screenshot/display is 1600 pixels high; bottom navigation semantics are clipped and cannot serve as literal physical tap coordinates without a proven transform.
entries.prevention: Audit physical display size, screenshot size and application viewport before bottom-rail input. Derive and prove the coordinate transform on a reversible known target with post-tap semantic inventory; do not capture or name a state until the intended destination is confirmed twice.

entries.mistake: The first measured-transform correction added the 82-pixel status inset to every semantic tap; applying it to Open Workspace moved the physical tap into the main rail and selected Book/Doctor instead.
entries.rootCause: The hierarchy's clipped bottom extent was interpreted as an app-relative coordinate system, even though upper content and subaction bounds already align with physical screenshot coordinates; only the main rail bounds are clipped by the accessibility viewport.
entries.prevention: Use literal semantic centers for subactions whose bounds end at or above y=1424. Use a separately measured physical main-rail center only for clipped main-family semantics beginning at y=1432. Confirm every tap result with inventory before capture.

entries.mistake: The first founder-gallery inventory embedded an Android shell loop variable inside a PowerShell double-quoted adb argument; PowerShell consumed the variable before adb ran, leaving four empty directory tests and no file inventory.
entries.rootCause: A command intended for Android sh crossed the PowerShell expansion boundary without literal quoting.
entries.prevention: Gallery discovery uses literal device roots or an Android-shell program protected from host expansion. Validate the emitted adb argument whenever both PowerShell and Android shell variables would otherwise share a command.

entries.mistake: The second founder-gallery inventory assumed Android's bundled find supported desktop find's -printf formatter; the device command emitted an incomplete record and stopped without identifying gallery evidence.
entries.rootCause: Desktop GNU find capabilities were assumed for the OPPO Android shell without a capability check.
entries.prevention: Use Android-compatible find output and obtain timestamps and byte sizes with toybox stat, or use literal ls output. Never select evidence from partial or unparsed inventory output.

entries.mistake: The r60.18 main-rail side chevron visually resembled a disappearing/reappearing control for the subaction row, but it was a 22px IgnorePointer overflow cue with no tap behavior or show/hide semantics.
entries.rootCause: Global main-action overflow indication and local subaction disclosure were represented by one ambiguous arrow language, while no actual disclosure owner existed.
entries.prevention: Default-expanded subactions gain an explicit stateful disclosure on the selected main action with a 48px target and exact Hide/Show family semantics. Any main-rail arrow is separately interactive at 44px or larger and cannot overlap action hit targets; a noninteractive cue is an arrowless edge fade.

entries.mistake: Every r60.18 destination permanently reserved a second 52px local navigation row above the 48px global rail, compressing content and making subactions feel like another app-level bar.
entries.rootCause: The local rail had no user-controlled visibility state even though the global shell must remain persistent.
entries.prevention: Subactions remain expanded by default and one tap when visible, but the selected main action can collapse only its local rail to zero layout height and restore it without route, content, history or Back changes. Reduced motion settles immediately.

entries.mistake: The six r60.18 families used lavender, burnt orange, green, blue, purple and ochre selected-control treatments above one navy selected-main state, fragmenting MoolSocial's selection language.
entries.rootCause: Family belonging was delegated to custom accent hues instead of hierarchy, labels, icons, selected-main alignment and the existing Mool identity palette.
entries.prevention: Use neutral glass across all families and restrict selected controls to existing Mool identity colors appropriate to light or media tone. Custom family-selected fills are statically rejected; family ownership is structural rather than hue-dependent.

entries.mistake: The same r60.18 glass tokens composited as an opaque gray row over Social, an orange blocking region over Buy and inconsistent pale/beige controls over the remaining light families.
entries.rootCause: Source alpha and blur assertions were treated as sufficient without real composited-pixel checks on representative media, commerce and light destination backgrounds.
entries.prevention: Keep the rail transparent, use only individual neutral glass controls, and qualify background visibility plus 4.5:1 composited label contrast on representative light and media pixels. Full-width bands, trapezoids and family-tinted fills remain forbidden.

entries.mistake: Although r60.18 shared numeric tokens, four-action long labels were cramped, two-action controls became visually dominant, provider SVGs looked smaller than Material icons and selected text changed weight more aggressively than inactive text.
entries.rootCause: Tests asserted raw height, radius, font and icon-box values but not optical size, label fit, control aspect rhythm or cross-family screenshot parity at two, three and four actions.
entries.prevention: Freeze one 48px control height, common radius, 13px/700 navigation label target, optical icon box and compact count-specific widths; add 320/360/412 layout, 130 percent text-scale, long-label, provider-icon and screenshot-matrix assertions.

entries.mistake: Each r60.18 selected subaction combined tinted fill, colored border, colored icon, shadow and underline above an already prominent navy selected main action, creating two competing primary selections.
entries.rootCause: Multiple redundant selection signals were added to compensate for a low-visibility connector instead of making the subaction clearly subordinate through layout and restrained state treatment.
entries.prevention: Use one primary brand selection signal plus a restrained indicator, keep inactive controls clearly available, and prove the selected main action remains the dominant owner in all six family screenshots while the connector remains visible but subordinate.

entries.mistake: The first C20 permanent-memory check rejected REG411 because its gate list named scripts/check-brand-identity-token-regression.ps1, a guessed file that does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The brand policy concept was translated into a plausible checker filename instead of selecting the exact existing script from a bounded scripts inventory.
entries.prevention: Before a regression entry references any checker, inventory the exact repository path with rg --files and use only that literal result. C20 brand regressions reference scripts/check-brand-integrity.ps1.

entries.mistake: The first C20B scope-gate attempt used the descriptive implementation disposition 'shared_owner_extension', which is not in the founder-locked reuse-checkpoint vocabulary, so selection failed before runtime mutation.
entries.rootCause: A conceptually accurate free-form label was used instead of the exact machine-authorized disposition enumeration.
entries.prevention: Every successor selection reads the delivery-lock allowedDispositions list before writing scope state and uses only reuse, configuration, thin_policy_adapter, test_only_acceptance or new_necessary_work. Shared-owner extensions are recorded as reuse plus new_necessary_work and focused validation as test_only_acceptance.

entries.mistake: The first C20B focused cycle measured all selected main-action targets and the overflow affordance at 46 logical pixels even though the enclosing dock remained 48 pixels high.
entries.rootCause: MoolGlassSurface painted its one-pixel border inside the AnimatedContainer decoration; Flutter decoration padding deflated the shared dock child by one pixel on both vertical edges despite explicit zero content padding.
entries.prevention: The fixed-height global dock paints its glass border as a non-insetting foreground decoration, keeps its outer geometry at 48 pixels and focused tests measure the keyed selected main action plus both reserved overflow regions at the full 48-pixel height.

entries.mistake: The first C20B normal-motion assertion treated the first 80-millisecond pump after a tap as an animation midpoint and rejected the unchanged 52-pixel initial frame.
entries.rootCause: The widget test did not establish the post-state-change animation frame before advancing simulated time, so the controller began on the frame being misclassified as its midpoint.
entries.prevention: Finite-motion tests pump once after the tap to establish the animation, then advance to a bounded midpoint and settle; the paired reduced-motion case continues to assert zero-height settlement on the first post-tap frame.

entries.mistake: The second C20B focused cycle found exact enabled button labels for selected-family disclosure but no semantic tap action, and could not discover the exact Next main actions overflow node.
entries.rootCause: The shared wrappers used excludeSemantics without owning an onTap semantic action, which discarded the child InkWell action; the overflow container also omitted explicitChildNodes and allowed its interactive child label to merge.
entries.prevention: Every shared interactive wrapper owns the same onTap callback exposed by its InkWell, and overflow containers preserve explicit child nodes. Focused tests assert the exact selected-family and Previous/Next labels plus SemanticsAction.tap on their independent nodes.

entries.mistake: The second C20B reduced-motion scenario reset the static disclosure-session map but retained the already-collapsed destination State, so its verification tap expanded to 52 pixels and produced a false failure.
entries.rootCause: The paired test changed MediaQuery configuration on the same widget identity without unmounting the first scenario; resetting process memory does not reinitialize a mounted State object.
entries.prevention: Independent normal-motion and reduced-motion scenarios explicitly unmount and pump the prior destination before resetting session-only memory and remounting, then assert immediate first-frame settlement.

entries.mistake: The third C20B focused cycle expected a label-based widget finder to stop locating the local rail's declarative Semantics widget after an ancestor ExcludeSemantics removed that subtree from active semantics.
entries.rootCause: The assertion conflated widget-tree discovery of a Semantics configuration with inclusion of its node in the composed accessibility semantics tree.
entries.prevention: Collapsed disclosure tests assert zero layout height plus ExcludeSemantics.excluding and IgnorePointer.ignoring on the region; they never use widget-finder absence beneath an exclusion wrapper as proof of accessibility-tree absence.

entries.mistake: A C20B static-gate inspection requested scripts/check-personal-subaction-clear-glass-controls-c17c.ps1, which does not exist, after the same command had already listed the exact available C17 gate names.
entries.rootCause: The inspection translated the C17C concept into a plausible filename instead of copying a literal path from the completed bounded inventory.
entries.prevention: Static-gate reads select an exact literal result from rg --files, verify Test-Path first and never combine a guessed path with otherwise valid required reads.

entries.mistake: The first REG422 registration patch reconstructed the focused-test path with hyphens instead of underscores, so apply_patch rejected its registry context and wrote nothing.
entries.rootCause: A long literal registry line was retyped from memory rather than copied exactly from a bounded tail inspection.
entries.prevention: Registry append patches use the exact final entry context returned by a fresh literal tail read; long evidence and gate paths are not reconstructed in patch anchors.

entries.mistake: The C20B placement and chained global-navigation closure gates rejected before design checks because the historical C17B shared-owner gate recognized the C17 sequence and exact C18D refresh but not the active founder-authorized C20 sequence.
entries.rootCause: The historical compatibility allowance was hard-coded for one immediate successor refresh rather than validating a later ticket against an exact authorized successor parent sequence and its active scope checkpoint.
entries.prevention: The C17B gate recognizes a current ticket only when it appears at or after C20B in the exact C20 parent sequence, retains active scope/checkpoint identity, and continues to reject build, install, backend and external authority while running every unchanged C17 design assertion.

entries.mistake: A C20B diagnostic passed scripts/check-personal-*.ps1 as an rg path, causing Windows OS error 123, then a later successful command masked that component failure behind an overall zero exit.
entries.rootCause: A wildcard was embedded in a required Windows path argument and the compound diagnostic did not assert the rg component exit before continuing.
entries.prevention: Enumerate with rg --files on a literal directory, filter the returned names separately, and assert each required component's exit code before any later command can replace it.

entries.mistake: After C17B compatibility passed, the C20B placement and chained global-navigation gates rejected at C17C because that independent historical scope check also omitted the active founder-authorized C20 sequence.
entries.rootCause: C17C duplicated the C17/C18D-only sequential allowance instead of validating later authorized successor tickets against their exact parent sequence.
entries.prevention: C17C recognizes a current ticket only when it appears at or after C20B in the exact C20 parent sequence, preserves active scope/checkpoint identity and closed build/install/backend/external authority, then runs every unchanged Social/Buy conformance assertion.

entries.mistake: After C17B and C17C compatibility passed, the C20B placement and chained global-navigation gates rejected at C17D because its independent historical scope check also omitted the active founder-authorized C20 sequence.
entries.rootCause: C17D duplicated the C17/C18D-only sequential allowance instead of validating later authorized successor tickets against their exact parent sequence.
entries.prevention: C17D recognizes a current ticket only when it appears at or after C20B in the exact C20 parent sequence, preserves active scope/checkpoint identity and closed build/install/backend/external authority, then runs every unchanged adaptive-family conformance assertion.

entries.mistake: The C20B compatibility shard rejected seven C10E cases because its shared helper still required every selected main destination to have no tap action, contradicting the founder-authorized Hide/Show disclosure owner.
entries.rootCause: The historical motion-containment acceptance encoded selected-destination inertness as permanent navigation behavior even though it was only the prior absence of a destination-local disclosure outcome.
entries.prevention: C10E retains selected-state and anchored-shell checks but requires the current selected family to expose the exact Hide-family-options semantic tap; C20B focused coverage separately proves that tap mutates no route, content or history.

entries.mistake: The reconciled C10E Eat-to-Work journey used framework ensureVisible instead of the new real-user Next main actions control, so active-action synchronization left Work beneath the reserved overflow region and its synthetic center tap missed.
entries.rootCause: The historical test bypassed persistent-rail overflow UX with programmatic scrolling and assumed a located render box was necessarily hit-testable after the rail resynchronized its active item.
entries.prevention: Journeys exposing an off-screen main action tap the exact Next main actions semantic control until the destination is hit-testable, then tap the destination; ensureVisible is not used as a substitute for user-reachable rail overflow behavior.

entries.mistake: A C20C token lookup correctly located MoolBrand in mool_design_system.dart, then guessed and read a nonexistent separate mool_brand.dart path in the same command.
entries.rootCause: A conventional file split was assumed after exact symbol discovery had already identified the actual shared owner.
entries.prevention: Brand-token work uses the literal file returned by the symbol search, verifies any additional path with Test-Path and never infers a separate owner from a class name.

entries.mistake: The first C20C focused press test sampled neutral glass alpha 80ms after touch-down, before InkWell's touch highlight delay elapsed, and falsely expected the pressed alpha target.
entries.rootCause: The test treated animation duration as the only timing owner and omitted the framework's preceding touch-highlight gesture delay.
entries.prevention: Touch press tests advance beyond the InkWell highlight delay while remaining within the finite shared state transition, then assert neutral RGB, increased alpha, 0.985 scale, one release action and immediate reduced motion.

entries.mistake: A C20C compatibility inspection supplied four plausible shortened historical gate filenames that do not exist instead of using the repository's literal C16A, C17B, C17D and C17E filenames.
entries.rootCause: Conceptual ticket names from the working summary were expanded into assumed script paths without first selecting exact paths from a bounded scripts inventory.
entries.prevention: Every historical-gate inspection first runs rg --files on the literal scripts directory, filters by ticket suffix, then copies only returned paths into the read command; descriptive ticket labels are never converted into filenames.

entries.mistake: A C20C diagnostic discovered the exact machine registry config/codex-development-regression-registry.json but also attempted to read a guessed docs/quality/PERMANENT-REGRESSION-MEMORY.md file that does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The permanent-memory concept was translated into a conventional Markdown filename even though the exact repository inventory had already identified its authoritative JSON owner.
entries.prevention: Regression-memory reads use the literal config/codex-development-regression-registry.json owner and repository-returned evidence paths only; no parallel prose-memory filename is inferred.

entries.mistake: A C20C compatibility inspection inferred a plausible C20B disclosure/overflow checker filename that does not exist instead of selecting the exact predecessor checker from the scripts inventory.
entries.rootCause: The ticket's descriptive title was converted directly into a script path after the current turn had already reinforced the literal-path inventory requirement.
entries.prevention: All predecessor C20 checker reads begin with rg --files scripts filtered by c20 and use a returned literal path; ticket titles are never assumed to map one-to-one to checker filenames.

entries.mistake: The first C20C static-gate run passed C20B but rejected five paraphrased focused-test descriptions and one glassFill call token that did not match the exact formatted Dart source.
entries.rootCause: The new checker encoded intended coverage wording from memory and assumed a method call remained on one line instead of copying stable literals from the already passing focused test.
entries.prevention: Static focused-coverage checks use exact test descriptions and formatting-independent symbol fragments copied from the current formatted source; source tokens are verified with a bounded literal search before the gate is rerun.

entries.mistake: A C20C correction diagnostic ran the regression-memory gate and then a focused rg query without asserting the latter's exit code, so the successful first command masked a no-match search and the overall tool call returned zero.
entries.rootCause: Two independently required checks were placed in one command while only the first command's exit code was asserted, repeating the compound-diagnostic failure already prohibited by REG-20260808-425.
entries.prevention: Every required rg source check runs as a single-purpose command or captures and asserts its own LASTEXITCODE immediately; no later or earlier success may determine the compound call result.

entries.mistake: A C20C protection run added the legacy Social file-inventory baseline checker even though C20C mutates no Social-owned file and the ticket's applicable approved-UI and brand gates were already selected; the legacy checker rejected the pre-existing repository count of 177 against its historical 119-file baseline.
entries.rootCause: A broad protected-baseline script discovered by name was treated as universally applicable without reading its inventory scope or reconciling its historical count against the current accepted dirty tree and the ticket's planned files.
entries.prevention: Gate selection follows the ticket and delivery-lock required set. Legacy whole-surface inventory baselines are run only when their scope is mutated and their current applicability has been established; an unrelated historical count rejection is recorded truthfully and never represented as C20C qualification or bypassed.

entries.mistake: The first C20C-to-C20D state-transition patch was rejected in full because one long C20C exclusion was reconstructed with a missing underscore between 'or' and 'business' and therefore did not match the exact scope-state context.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-file transition combined many independent replacements and retyped a long machine-state literal instead of copying exact current context from a bounded read.
entries.prevention: Ticket transitions patch manifests, parent/regression state and scope sections in small independent exact-context edits. Long machine-state arrays are copied from a fresh bounded read and never reconstructed in patch anchors.

entries.mistake: The first C20D focused run reused the same Stateful Social harness identity across width and text-scale scenarios, so the prior scenario's final Create selection persisted while the next scenario expected a fresh Shorts selection.
entries.rootCause: Replacing MediaQuery and viewport configuration does not remount a stateful child of the same runtime type and key; the matrix changed scenario inputs without assigning a scenario identity or unmounting the previous harness.
entries.prevention: Each responsive Social matrix scenario owns a unique widget key or is explicitly unmounted before remounting. Focused assertions begin only after the scenario-local initial selected state is verified.

entries.mistake: The first C20F aggregate test failed to compile because the intended literal C20B source tokens containing '$label' lost their backslash while passing through the JavaScript patch string and were interpreted as undefined Dart interpolation.
entries.rootCause: A source-token assertion relied on nested JavaScript-to-patch-to-Dart escaping instead of using Dart raw string literals, so the intermediate representation consumed the escape.
entries.prevention: Dart assertions for source tokens containing dollar signs use raw string literals. Cross-language patch inputs do not rely on backslash preservation for interpolation-sensitive text.

entries.mistake: After C20G passed both host cycles, its selected-ticket manifest was truthfully changed from selected to complete, but the scope checkpoint still held the pre-execution manifest SHA-256, so the first post-completion delivery-lock run rejected the stale hash.
entries.rootCause: The completion seal updated the ticket lifecycle state and qualification result without treating the checkpoint's manifest digest as a coupled derived value that must be refreshed in the same transition.
entries.prevention: Every ticket-manifest lifecycle mutation recomputes the literal current manifest SHA-256 and updates the selected-ticket assessment before retrying the delivery lock. The delivery-discipline lock remains the machine-detectable stale-hash prevention gate.

entries.mistake: A C20H provenance lookup recursively searched scripts, config, the full artifacts tree and quality docs for source-manifest construction tokens and exceeded the command timeout.
entries.rootCause: The lookup included a large immutable evidence tree even though the already-read C17G manifest supplied the required format and any reusable generator could only need discovery under the bounded scripts/config owners.
entries.prevention: Build provenance searches start with rg --files in scripts/config and inspect explicit known evidence files directly. Full recursive artifacts searches are forbidden unless a bounded artifact directory is first selected.

entries.mistake: C20H dirty-state reconciliation used git status with --untracked-files=all, which descended into historical browser-profile artifacts and emitted Windows filename-too-long warnings, making its 51,998-line inventory incomplete despite exit zero.
entries.rootCause: A request for full dirty state was interpreted as recursive enumeration of every file inside already-untracked artifact directories instead of Git's path-safe directory-level untracked representation plus exact tracked changes.
entries.prevention: APK dirty seals use git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=normal, hash every returned tracked path and untracked directory entry, and separately preserve exact C20 planned/source owners. Any filename-too-long warning invalidates an all-untracked inventory even when Git exits zero.

entries.mistake: The first C20H delivery-lock run rejected the selected-ticket assessment because implementationDisposition included the invented label 'build_evidence', which is outside the delivery lock's allowed enum.
entries.rootCause: The assessment described the intended work semantically without first reading the machine gate's literal implementation-disposition allowlist.
entries.prevention: Ticket assessments copy implementationDisposition values only from the delivery lock's current allowed enum; descriptive build/device evidence remains in robustness coverage and planned scope, not in invented enum values.

entries.mistake: The first C20H active-build-process probe reported one process because the PowerShell probe's own command line contained the literal Flutter/Gradle search pattern.
entries.rootCause: The process filter matched command-line text across every executable without excluding the current PowerShell process or constraining Gradle patterns to Java and Flutter patterns to Flutter/Dart executables.
entries.prevention: Prebuild process inventory excludes the current PID and applies executable-specific rules: GradleWrapperMain only on java processes and Flutter build only on flutter/dart/cmd processes. A shell command containing the detection regex cannot count itself.

entries.mistake: The first post-install identity command converted dumpsys package to one multiline string and then piped it to Select-String, causing a matching pattern to print the entire package dump instead of four identity lines.
entries.rootCause: Select-String preserves and returns the whole input object; Out-String collapsed all dumpsys lines into one object before filtering.
entries.prevention: ADB text is filtered line-wise before Out-String, or exact values are extracted with anchored regex matches. Multiline package dumps are never passed as one object to Select-String in evidence commands.

entries.mistake: The first C20H semantic tap calculated the center of [204,1328][356,1424] by adding regex capture strings before casting, producing out-of-range coordinates 102178,6640712; the tap was ignored and Social/Shorts remained current.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell used string concatenation for $matches operands because each regex capture remained a string at the point of addition.
entries.prevention: Every parsed bound coordinate is individually cast to int before addition: ([int]x1 + [int]x2) / 2. The helper rejects centers outside the physical display and requires two post-tap selected-semantic confirmations before capture.

entries.mistake: A C20H device-helper lookup repeated the registered Windows ripgrep mistake by supplying docs/quality/UAW-C17H-* as a search root; rg returned an invalid filename error even though a separate literal artifact root produced one useful line.
entries.rootCause: The desired filename prefix was again placed in the positional root list instead of using the literal docs/quality root with a -g filename filter.
entries.prevention: Every Windows rg command uses only verified literal directory/file roots. Filename patterns are expressed with -g. Any mixed command with one invalid root is discarded even if another root returns matches.

entries.mistake: The first C20H matrix capture assumed the earlier Social/Shorts start state was still live, but the fresh hierarchy showed Buy/Shop; the helper correctly refused the stale expected state and saved no screenshot.
entries.rootCause: Device state was carried forward from an earlier capture across an interval in which the OPPO could change, instead of treating each matrix action as beginning from a fresh selected-semantic inventory.
entries.prevention: Every C20H capture begins with an immediate live inventory. The helper requires two consecutive exact selected semantics and a matching final hierarchy; no prior screen, tap intention or filename supplies the current state.

entries.mistake: The first C20H Previous main actions tap reused the predecessor helper's top>=1432 transform rule, but the r60.19 global-rail arrow bounds begin at y=1428; it tapped clipped y=1435 and did not change rail exposure.
entries.rootCause: A device-specific transform threshold from r60.18 was copied without reconciling the new hierarchy's literal global rail start coordinate.
entries.prevention: C20H maps every semantic node whose top is at least y=1428 to the measured physical global-rail center y=1480. Scroll controls must additionally prove a changed exposure inventory before any destination tap or capture.

entries.mistake: After issuing an inventory-only Open Social tap, the C20H helper called Wait-SelectedState with its default empty ExpectedSelected array; PowerShell rejected binding the empty array to a mandatory parameter before live inventory could print.
entries.rootCause: The caller unconditionally invoked the wait function even though the function's internal empty-array guard could never run because parameter binding fails first for an empty mandatory collection.
entries.prevention: The helper calls Wait-SelectedState only when ExpectedSelected.Count is greater than zero. Inventory-only navigation can therefore report the fresh post-tap state without guessing a destination label.

entries.mistake: After capturing Social/Create, an Open Buy tap was attempted at the physical global-rail coordinate while Create's auto-focused composer had the keyboard covering the bottom shell; the selected state correctly remained Social/Create.
entries.rootCause: The workflow relied on still-exported rail semantics without reconciling the visibly active IME and physical occlusion shown in the just-saved Create screenshot.
entries.prevention: Before every global-rail tap, device evidence checks IME visibility. If the keyboard is active, one system Back dismisses only the IME, the exact local/main selection is re-proved twice, and a rail-visible screenshot is saved before navigation continues.

entries.mistake: A guarded Cab sequence reached two stable Cab/Ride confirmations, but state changed before the final hierarchy. The helper rejected the mismatch only after it had already pulled 13-ride-cab.png and .xml into final-looking local names.
entries.rootCause: Save-CurrentState wrote local evidence before parsing and validating the remote final hierarchy, so its rejection was logically correct but not file-atomic.
entries.prevention: The helper captures screenshot/XML to remote temporary paths, reads and validates the remote XML against exact selected semantics, and only then pulls both into never-overwritten local names. Any previously written mismatch is preserved with an adjacent REJECTED marker and never reused.

entries.mistake: Doctor capture and Salon navigation/capture were chained in one host invocation. Salon reached two stable exact semantic confirmations, but the final UIAutomator hierarchy did not confirm the state and the capture was correctly rejected.
entries.rootCause: Chaining independent device evidence states in one host process increased the interval and coupling between UIAutomator dumps, navigation, and final validation on a live device whose UI state can change independently.
entries.prevention: Run each accepted device state as its own fresh helper invocation. Re-inventory immediately before every retry, require two exact selected confirmations, validate the remote final hierarchy before local pull, and never reuse a rejected filename.

entries.mistake: The first normal-motion evidence attempt assumed Android's screenrecord binary existed on the connected OPPO CPH2375. The remote shell returned exit 127 and produced no local or remote video.
entries.rootCause: Recorder capability was inferred from generic Android behavior instead of being probed on the exact founder device before starting a unique evidence attempt.
entries.prevention: Probe the exact device for the chosen recording binary before launch. If screenrecord is unavailable, use a host-side connected-device recorder only after proving that tool exists; preserve the failed attempt as rejected and never claim a motion artifact from it.

entries.mistake: The first host-side motion fallback treated Activity gfxinfo framestats as the source of Flutter-rendered navigation frames. A proven Doctor-to-Salon tap produced zero rows newer than the baseline in that stream.
entries.rootCause: On this OPPO profile runtime, the Flutter scene is presented through a SurfaceView BLAST surface whose compositor timestamps are not represented as new Activity gfxinfo rows for the tested transition.
entries.prevention: Inventory the exact MoolSocial SurfaceFlinger layer and use that layer's compositor latency timestamps for on-device frame evidence. Every measured transition must still end in two exact semantic selected-state confirmations.

entries.mistake: The first SurfaceFlinger latency probe passed the BLAST layer name as an unquoted adb argument. Android's remote shell parsed the layer-name parentheses and rejected the command with an unexpected-parenthesis syntax error.
entries.rootCause: Host PowerShell argument separation did not preserve literal quoting through adb into the remote shell for a layer name containing brackets, slashes, parentheses, and a hash suffix.
entries.prevention: Construct one remote shell command whose exact inventoried layer name is wrapped in remote single quotes. Probe latency output before using that command in an evidence measurement.

entries.mistake: OPPO CPH2375 serial 2b3e0f71 disconnected during the guarded SurfaceFlinger motion measurement, before the local destination could be re-proved. The measurement produced no accepted result.
entries.rootCause: The device transport became unavailable during an active qualification step; the cause is external to the repository and was not inferred.
entries.prevention: Stop all device mutation, preserve every already accepted screenshot and installed identity, mark the machine state device-disconnected, and resume only after adb visibly reports the same serial as device and a fresh installed-identity gate passes.

entries.mistake: A read-only subaction geometry audit attempted to pipe directly from a PowerShell foreach language statement. The parser rejected the empty pipe position before any audit ran.
entries.rootCause: The foreach statement's output was not first assigned or wrapped as an expression before Format-List was applied.
entries.prevention: Collect foreach output in an explicit array variable, then format or validate that variable. Parse and execute the corrected read-only audit before citing geometry results.

entries.mistake: A read-only final-gate discovery command allowed ripgrep's expected no-match exit code to become the overall shell failure even though the preceding script header read succeeded.
entries.rootCause: The discovery query did not distinguish no matches from an execution error before returning control to the shell runner.
entries.prevention: Use an explicit no-match-safe search or inspect the known evidence files directly. Do not treat ripgrep exit code 1 as a command failure when absence is an admissible discovery result.

entries.mistake: The C20H final state lookup repeated the Windows ripgrep wildcard-root mistake by using config/*.json as a search root, causing exit code 2 before any result was accepted.
entries.rootCause: The known REG-448 prevention was not applied to a later state-seal discovery command.
entries.prevention: Always pass the literal config directory as the root and use --glob '*.json'. Treat any ripgrep exit above 1 as a tooling rejection and register recurrences before retrying.

entries.mistake: The first final seal read preTicketSelectionCheckpoint.candidateTicket.manifestSha256, a nonexistent property, and falsely reported ticket hash drift because the lookup returned empty.
entries.rootCause: The seal invented a shorthand property path instead of using the authoritative preTicketSelectionCheckpoint.selectedTicketAssessment.manifestSha256 field.
entries.prevention: Read the exact selectedTicketAssessment property from the scope schema and require both stored and computed hashes to be nonempty before comparing. Report the observed values before any hash refresh decision.

entries.mistake: The initial C21 read-only evidence-size inventory repeated the registered PowerShell mistake by piping directly from a foreach statement. Parsing failed before any required file inventory ran.
entries.rootCause: REG-459's explicit-array prevention was not applied when composing the successor audit inventory.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell foreach whose output needs formatting is collected in an explicit array variable before any pipeline. The corrected inventory must run before screenshot copying or ticket selection.

entries.mistake: The first C21 regression-memory call used unsupported phase 'planning'. The gate rejected parameter binding because its allowed phases are general, implementation, build and device.
entries.rootCause: A narrative workflow phase was passed without reading the script's literal ValidateSet.
entries.prevention: Use Phase general for preselection and audit work, implementation for runtime edits, build for APK work and device for OPPO qualification. Never invent phase labels.

entries.mistake: The initial C21 evidence inventory repeated the registered placement-state mistake by probing nonexistent config/personal-subaction-placement-regression-state.json instead of first following the checker-owned contract path.
entries.rootCause: The successor inventory reused a guessed filename despite the permanent registry already naming the authoritative mvp-personal-subaction-reachability-promotion-zone-regression.json contract.
entries.prevention: Read scripts/check-personal-subaction-placement-regression.ps1 first and follow only its literal contract path. No guessed companion state filename may enter a ticket assessment.

entries.mistake: The C21 read-only inspection attempted to open nonexistent shortened scope-gate and APK-machine-state filenames.
entries.rootCause: The inspection guessed abbreviated filenames instead of selecting the repository's authoritative mvp-scope-gate-state.json and apk-regression-gate-state.json paths through discovery or their checker scripts.
entries.prevention: Discover state paths with rg --files config or follow literal checker-owned paths. Reject guessed or abbreviated state filenames before accepting ticket evidence.

entries.mistake: r60.19 passed host and device qualification even though its sub-action geometry, silhouette, row structure and perceived second-navigation-bar hierarchy remained materially indistinguishable from the rejected predecessor.
entries.rootCause: Qualification treated selection-token changes as a professional redesign without requiring a real-device predecessor-to-successor structural and optical delta.
entries.prevention: Every sub-action successor must pass an explicit predecessor/successor crop audit covering geometry, silhouette, visual weight, compositing and hierarchy before professional qualification can pass.

entries.mistake: C20 accepted a transparent rail and translucent control tokens as proof of professional glass even though Buy page colours flooded the final OPPO sub-action pixels and destabilized legibility.
entries.rootCause: The gate validated source declarations and theoretical foreground/fill contrast rather than the complete backdrop-filter and destination-background composition.
entries.prevention: Require declared surface-tone normalization plus rendered light/media/commerce compositing tests and crop evidence; literal transparency alone cannot satisfy the legibility contract.

entries.mistake: The C20H device audit called the system professional while explicitly retaining Buy's strong backdrop tint as a founder-review focus.
entries.rootCause: An unresolved material visual defect was downgraded to a review note instead of failing the professional-quality gate.
entries.prevention: Any material founder-review focus affecting legibility, content dominance, cross-family consistency or professional appearance is a qualification rejection until resolved and re-evidenced.

entries.mistake: The C20 suite had no machine-readable requirement that a successor visibly differ from rejected predecessor crops in structure, optical treatment and hierarchy.
entries.rootCause: Tests were optimized for invariant preservation and token presence, leaving perceptual redesign acceptance unmeasured.
entries.prevention: C21G must add an evidence-backed optical-delta contract and fail qualification when only token values change while device-visible structure remains effectively unchanged.

entries.mistake: REG-467 through REG-470 referenced a planned optical-delta checker before the repository contained that file, so the regression-memory gate rejected the registry.
entries.rootCause: The intended future gate name was registered before C21G created and proved the gate owner.
entries.prevention: Registry gate paths must already exist. Use the current exact C20F gate until C21G adds a proven successor, then update the registry with evidence in the same mutation.

entries.mistake: The C21A reference-only APK state check passed unsupported BuildMode none even though the checker accepts only debug, profile or release.
entries.rootCause: The regression-memory phase vocabulary was incorrectly reused as an APK checker build-mode value without reading the APK checker's ValidateSet.
entries.prevention: Do not call the build-only APK checker during non-build phases. Supply every mandatory candidate/build parameter, including debug, profile or release, only within the corresponding separately authorized prebuild workflow.

entries.mistake: C21A invoked the build-only APK regression checker without its mandatory candidate/build parameters during a reference-only audit.
entries.rootCause: The pre-build authorization gate was mistaken for a general read-only APK state validator.
entries.prevention: During non-build tickets, parse and reconcile the APK JSON state without invoking the build gate. Run the checker only after C21H has a sealed candidate, every mandatory value and an approved one-build state.

entries.mistake: The combined C21A completion and C21B selection patch contained an extra empty update hunk and was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: A file-update delimiter remained after the intended additions, leaving no context or changed line before the next file header.
entries.prevention: Split multi-file state transitions into bounded patches, require explicit context in every hunk and parse each changed manifest before continuing.

entries.mistake: The first C21B test command ran from apps/mobile while still passing apps/mobile-prefixed paths, so the path was duplicated and no test ran.
entries.rootCause: The command changed working directory without changing its file arguments from repository-relative to mobile-relative paths.
entries.prevention: From apps/mobile use lib/... and test/... paths; from repository root use apps/mobile/... paths. Print or validate the resolved test path before long test runs.

entries.mistake: The corrected C21B focused-test command used a one-second shell timeout, killing Flutter before any test result and yielding no acceptable evidence.
entries.rootCause: A short orchestration-yield intent was incorrectly implemented as a process execution timeout.
entries.prevention: Give Flutter a normal bounded execution timeout. Use yielded running-cell waits for progress instead of terminating the test process early.

entries.mistake: Static review found the new C21B gate placed Dart's ${action.id} key fragment in a double-quoted PowerShell token, which would interpolate to the wrong search string.
entries.rootCause: A cross-language source token containing a dollar expression used PowerShell interpolation syntax instead of a literal invariant.
entries.prevention: Use single-quoted PowerShell literals or smaller interpolation-free invariants for Dart source searches containing dollar expressions. Review the gate text before first execution.

entries.mistake: The first C21C reuse search included nonexistent apps/mobile/lib/features/social instead of using only repository-discovered roots.
entries.rootCause: A conventional feature-directory layout was assumed even though Social is owned under apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/social.
entries.prevention: Discover source roots with rg --files apps/mobile/lib before content searches and pass only literal existing directories to ripgrep.

entries.mistake: The first C21C assessment named Instagram and Facebook as Social sub-actions even though the authoritative owner contains Shorts, Videos, Feed and Create.
entries.rootCause: Reference-provider examples were mistaken for implemented local outcomes instead of deriving the ticket list from the actual native Flutter action-spec owner.
entries.prevention: Derive every family outcome name from its current shared action-spec owner before ticket selection. Provider assets and semantic qualifiers never create a sub-action; filler outcomes remain prohibited.

entries.mistake: The first C21C static gate required provider glyph width and height expressions on one line, so Dart formatter wrapping caused a false rejection after analysis and focused tests passed.
entries.rootCause: A formatter-controlled Dart expression was validated with exact string containment instead of whitespace-tolerant structure matching.
entries.prevention: Use whitespace-tolerant regexes for formatted multi-line Dart expressions and exact literals only for stable declarations. Reject the failed gate run and rerun after parser review.

entries.mistake: The initial C21D manifest named Trade and Refill as Buy sub-actions even though the authoritative owner exposes Shop, Wholesale, Medicine and Orders.
entries.rootCause: Illustrative commerce vocabulary was mistaken for implemented destination outcomes instead of deriving the ticket list from BuyV2Destination and _buildBuyLocalNavigation.
entries.prevention: Derive every Buy outcome name from the live native Flutter action-spec owner before selection. Supporting trade/refill vocabulary cannot create a local destination or filler action.

entries.mistake: The first C21C-to-C21D scope transition patch expected an obsolete generic Social scope line after the file had been corrected to actual outcome wording, so the patch was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: A large transition patch reused pre-correction context instead of rereading the current scope state after REG-479 changes.
entries.prevention: Reread current scope segments after every correction and apply bounded field-group hunks. Treat atomic patch rejection as no transition and register before retry.

entries.mistake: The C21C predecessor gate required its transient contract state exactly and rejected the valid C21D successor even though Social's qualification field remained passed.
entries.rootCause: The gate conflated its durable acceptance invariant with the aggregate workflow's current transient state.
entries.prevention: A sequential predecessor gate accepts its own and later C21 states while requiring its exact immutable family-qualification field. Earlier, missing and unrelated states remain rejected.

entries.mistake: The first C21E test inventory passed a wildcard-bearing Windows path as a ripgrep search root, repeating the registered invalid-root mistake and returning error 123.
entries.rootCause: The search composed a filename glob in the root position instead of using a literal directory with --glob or selecting files from rg --files.
entries.prevention: On Windows, pass only literal existing ripgrep roots. Apply filename patterns with --glob or filter rg --files results before content search.

entries.mistake: Parser review rejected the first C21E gate because a double-quoted diagnostic used $relative: and PowerShell parsed the colon as an invalid scoped-variable reference.
entries.rootCause: A variable was followed immediately by punctuation without braces in an interpolated PowerShell string.
entries.prevention: Use ${variable}: when punctuation immediately follows an interpolated variable. Require parser review before first gate execution or citation.

entries.mistake: The first C21F gate required the default-expanded null-coalescing expression as the exact adjacent text ?? true, so Dart formatter line wrapping caused a false rejection after analysis and all ten focused tests passed.
entries.rootCause: A formatter-controlled Dart expression was validated with exact string containment rather than a whitespace-tolerant structural check.
entries.prevention: Validate the null-coalescing default with a whitespace-tolerant regex, keep the behavioral default-expanded test mandatory, and reject the failed gate run before retry.

entries.mistake: The first C21G obsolete-test migration replaced removed flat-fill assertions but left predecessor expectations for pressed scale 0.985 and two-action cluster width 212, so the focused suite rejected two tests.
entries.rootCause: The migration inventory searched for the removed glassFill API first but did not simultaneously compare every predecessor geometry and interaction token against the C21 contract.
entries.prevention: Before rerunning evolved historical tests, search the selected files for all predecessor token values and bind expectations to current C21 tokens or explicit successor contract values. A partial migration is rejected and cannot count toward either host cycle.

entries.mistake: REG-487 initially named the planned C21G optical-delta checker before that file existed or had positive and negative proof, recurring the premature-gate-reference defect.
entries.rootCause: The planned final prevention owner was entered during regression registration instead of waiting for the checker creation and proof step.
entries.prevention: Until the C21G checker exists and has positive and mutation-negative evidence, registry entries use the existing C20F aggregate gate. Update them to C21G only in the same mutation that records its proof.

entries.mistake: The C21G stale-token correction searched for 212 and an assumed 276 but omitted the actual predecessor three-action value 272, so one historical inventory test rejected the retry against C21's 268 px contract.
entries.rootCause: The numeric scan was based on recalled predecessor values instead of reading all clusterWidth expectations from the selected files and comparing each with the C21 machine contract.
entries.prevention: Inventory every clusterWidth expectation directly from the full selected test set, reconcile two/three/four-action values to 200/268/304, and require zero retired glassFill, 0.985, 212 or 272 expectations before retry.

entries.mistake: The first C21G rendered-pixel proxy awaited RenderRepaintBoundary.toImage directly under the widget test fake-async clock and did not complete within the bounded execution window, so the process was terminated.
entries.rootCause: GPU/image byte work was treated like an ordinary pumped animation future instead of crossing WidgetTester.runAsync for real asynchronous completion.
entries.prevention: Raw RepaintBoundary image capture and byte conversion run inside WidgetTester.runAsync, every image is disposed, and a terminated or timed-out process is never counted as optical-delta or host-cycle evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C21G checker run assigned the hostQualification object to $host, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's read-only $Host automatic variable after C21B–F had passed.
entries.rootCause: A concise domain variable name reused a shell-owned automatic variable despite the workspace rule to avoid common system names.
entries.prevention: Use a task-specific name such as $hostQualificationContract and parser/run-test all new PowerShell gates before citing them. Failed runs do not qualify the gate.

entries.mistake: The first C21H read-only OPPO reconciliation guessed com.supermandi.moolsocial for pm path, returned no package path and therefore did not inspect the installed app.
entries.rootCause: The product name was translated into a conventional Android application ID instead of reading the exact applicationId from the production Gradle owner or prior accepted install evidence.
entries.prevention: Resolve the literal applicationId from apps/mobile/android/app/build.gradle or accepted machine evidence before every ADB package command, require one non-empty package path and never hash a missing path.

entries.mistake: The compound C21H reconciliation continued after a null pm-path result, invoked sha256sum without an APK path and printed the empty-input SHA-256, while a later successful machine-state read left the overall shell call at exit zero.
entries.rootCause: Independent required ADB checks were placed in one command without asserting each native exit code and output before dependent operations, allowing later success to mask earlier failure.
entries.prevention: Run package path, dumpsys and checksum as separately asserted steps; stop on nonzero exit or empty output, validate the path begins with /data/app/, and compare only the checksum returned for that exact path.

entries.mistake: The C21H application-ID lookup repeated the registered Windows error by passing apps/mobile/android/app/build.gradle* as a ripgrep search root; the valid directory search still found com.moolsocial.app and masked error 123.
entries.rootCause: A filename wildcard was again placed in the root-argument position rather than using the already available literal Android directory with a --glob filter.
entries.prevention: Use only literal existing ripgrep roots on Windows and apply filename patterns with --glob. Treat mixed success plus error 123 as a rejected diagnostic and separately verify the literal build.gradle.kts file.

entries.mistake: The first r60.20 collision search ran content ripgrep from the repository root and traversed the large artifact/binary tree, timing out after 124 seconds without a result.
entries.rootCause: Candidate identity collision search mixed text-owner validation with artifact inventory and did not separate binary/path-name inspection from bounded config, docs, scripts and build-file content search.
entries.prevention: Search candidate strings only in bounded text-owner roots and use rg --files for artifact/path-name collisions. A timeout is a rejected result and cannot reserve a version.

entries.mistake: The first C21H closed-preflight memory call guessed -Phase prebuild, which is outside the gate's general, implementation, build and device ValidateSet.
entries.rootCause: The workflow concept 'prebuild' was assumed to be a literal CLI phase without reading the checker's declared parameter set.
entries.prevention: Use implementation/none while build authorization is closed, build/profile only inside the authorized build phase, and device/profile during post-install qualification. Read ValidateSet values before invocation.

entries.mistake: A C21H C20H-reference lookup listed the real source/prebuild/gate files but also attempted to read a guessed 04-prebuild-validation.md path that does not exist, causing the command to fail.
entries.rootCause: A conventional sequence number and descriptive name were inferred instead of selecting the literal 09-prebuild-validation-seal.md returned by the same inventory.
entries.prevention: Artifact evidence reads use only literal filenames returned by Get-ChildItem or rg --files; sequence numbers and descriptive names are never inferred.

entries.mistake: The first C21H aggregate probe concatenated category records and sorted the formatted hash-plus-path strings, yielding AE9F... instead of C21G's sealed 3E77... fingerprint.
entries.rootCause: The reimplementation sorted by the record's leading file hash rather than globally sorting FileInfo objects by FullName before constructing each record, which changed the deterministic byte stream.
entries.prevention: Reuse the exact C21G algorithm: gather all files from lib, test and scripts, globally sort by FullName, then emit SHA256 two-spaces relative-path records joined with LF. Any mismatch rejects prebuild authorization.

entries.mistake: Terminating the first hung raw-pixel shell cell left child dart.exe PID 9536 running the exact optical-delta test, which was discovered by C21H's no-active-build/test preflight.
entries.rootCause: The shell termination stopped the orchestrating process but did not verify or reap its spawned Flutter test child.
entries.prevention: After terminating any Flutter command, enumerate matching child command lines, stop only the exact verified orphan, and require zero active Flutter build/test commands before build authorization. Idle Gradle daemons are classified separately from active builds.

entries.mistake: The cleanup command required previously observed PID 9536 to still exist, but the Flutter test child had exited naturally before the stop attempt, so the command rejected a changed target.
entries.rootCause: Process identity was treated as stable between observation and action rather than being re-enumerated immediately before cleanup with an already-gone success disposition.
entries.prevention: Re-enumerate matching command lines immediately before cleanup; stop only still-present exact matches, record already-gone as no action performed, and then independently require zero active Flutter build/test processes.

entries.mistake: The first post-authorization C21H verification guessed a nonexistent parent state filename and queried buildName, buildNumber and status fields that are not present at those candidate/build-result paths, producing one file failure and empty diagnostics.
entries.rootCause: A compacted handoff description was treated as an exact filesystem and schema authority instead of selecting literal paths from the repository inventory and enumerating the JSON property names before reading values.
entries.prevention: Select state files only from a literal rg --files inventory, parse every JSON owner, enumerate the relevant object properties, and then query the exact versionName, versionCode and state fields. A missing file or empty expected value rejects that verification and cannot authorize a build.

entries.mistake: The first authorized-install precheck rejected immediately after the device-phase regression-memory script printed a pass because the caller inspected stale native-process LASTEXITCODE instead of the PowerShell invocation result; adb install was never reached.
entries.rootCause: LASTEXITCODE was assumed to describe a completed PowerShell script even though it is only reliably updated by native executables and may retain an earlier value.
entries.prevention: For PowerShell script invocations use the invocation success signal or terminating-error behavior under ErrorActionPreference Stop; reserve LASTEXITCODE assertions for the immediately preceding native executable. Prove the install command was not reached before retaining the one-attempt authorization.

entries.mistake: The first r60.20 launch-evidence pull used two Test-Path calls around -or without parenthesizing each command, causing PowerShell to bind the second LiteralPath to the first Test-Path and stop after the remote PNG/XML capture but before local pull.
entries.rootCause: A compound boolean expression embedded cmdlet invocations without explicit subexpression boundaries.
entries.prevention: Parenthesize each Test-Path invocation before applying boolean operators, verify both local targets are absent, and when the remote capture already succeeded pull those exact remote files rather than recapturing or overwriting evidence.

entries.mistake: The corrected launch-evidence pull completed both local files and hashes, but an optional trailing rg expression assumed a specific XML attribute order, found no match, and made the overall shell call exit 1.
entries.rootCause: A non-required exploratory diagnostic was left as the final native command and its no-match status was allowed to override the already successful required evidence operations.
entries.prevention: Keep required capture/pull assertions separate from optional diagnostics, parse UIAutomator XML structurally instead of depending on attribute order, and never recapture or overwrite evidence that already passed checksum recording.

entries.mistake: After the accepted Social/Create captures, the first attempted Buy capture tapped the painted vertical center of the global rail at y=1476 and landed on Eat; the selected-state semantic correctly rejected the mislabeled 05-buy-shop evidence.
entries.rootCause: The coordinate was inferred from pixels instead of using the live UIAutomator bounds, whose global-rail hit regions are vertically clipped to y=1428..1442 on this OPPO rendering.
entries.prevention: Drive global-family navigation from the exact current UIAutomator content description and its live semantic-bound center, assert the destination current-state semantic before accepting a pair, and preserve any mislabeled capture with an explicit REJECTED disposition rather than overwriting it.

entries.mistake: The first correction treated the center of the OPPO-clipped global-rail UIAutomator bounds as a real hit center; tapping the reported Previous main actions center while Eat was current moved the app to Work instead of producing a controlled previous-window result.
entries.rootCause: The semantics rectangles are clipped diagnostic projections only 14 pixels high and do not identify the painted Flutter control's stable touch center on this device.
entries.prevention: Do not use clipped global-rail semantic rectangles as input coordinates. Calibrate against the device logical/physical display mapping and painted control geometry, drive one probe at a time, and accept a navigation result only after the exact destination semantics pass.

entries.mistake: The provisional 04b Social/Create capture was labeled IME dismissed after one Back and a Create-current semantic check, but visual inspection proved the keyboard still occupied the lower screen and the global shell was not physically tappable.
entries.rootCause: Route selection semantics were treated as sufficient evidence of keyboard dismissal even though hidden app semantics can persist while the IME covers the rail.
entries.prevention: A Create IME-dismissal capture requires both stable Create-current semantics and an explicit no-IME visual/window-state proof before any global-rail input. If one Back is consumed without hiding the keyboard, repeat only the IME-dismissal action and re-prove the unchanged route before navigation.

entries.mistake: The first C21H matrix helper captured and pulled local PNG/XML files after only one final selected-state check, recurring the registered requirement for two consecutive stable destination inventories and remote validation before local evidence admission.
entries.rootCause: The compact batch helper optimized capture latency but omitted the permanent C17H/C20H stability and atomicity safeguards already present in regression memory.
entries.prevention: Every qualifying replacement uses a unique q-prefixed name, waits for the exact main/local selected semantics in two consecutive remote hierarchies, captures remotely, validates the final remote hierarchy, and only then pulls PNG/XML locally. Provisional files remain preserved and excluded from the accepted manifest.

entries.mistake: The r60.20 C21 implementation kept a full-width 52 px subaction layer whose transparent material revealed a continuous orange, white or dark family band, so the predecessor left-to-right strap still dominated the background.
entries.rootCause: C21 removed an explicit fill from the shared rail but retained a full-width layout/surface owner directly over family-colored page chrome, producing the same visual band through composition.
entries.prevention: C22 renders only individually clipped capsules and a narrow parent connector; no full-width decoration, tint, blur, opacity layer or family-colored surface may exist behind or between capsules. Raw-pixel tests require untouched destination pixels in every inter-capsule and outer-gap sample.

entries.mistake: r60.20 still used dark media controls for Social and light controls for the other five families, so the six main-action families did not share one transparent professional capsule language.
entries.rootCause: The shared primitive accepted a surfaceTone and mapped family identity to two different glass gradients, borders, foregrounds and shadows instead of using one neutral optical base.
entries.prevention: C22 removes family surface-tone styling from the capsule base. All six families use the same neutral transparent glass, white foreground, border, shadow, height, radius, icon and label tokens; family color is permitted only as selected/pressed inner emission.

entries.mistake: C21 changed local control width with the family action count, leaving two-, three- and four-action families with visibly different capsule mass while middle main actions retained a separate size and text scale.
entries.rootCause: Adaptive cluster filling was solved by preferred per-count widths rather than one fixed capsule metric with a centered fixed-gap cluster.
entries.prevention: C22 uses one 72x48 capsule, 24 px radius, 18 px icon and 12 px/800 label token for every middle main action and every subaction. Counts change only total centered cluster width; no sparse spreading or per-family resizing is allowed.

entries.mistake: The r60.20 selected state remained a brighter fill plus border, shadow and underline marker; it did not create the requested color emission originating inside the transparent medicine capsule on tap/selection.
entries.rootCause: C21 selection increased neutral glass alpha and reused a bottom indicator instead of defining an internal chroma light source and finite emission animation.
entries.prevention: C22 selection/press uses a clipped internal radial chroma emission, specular highlight and restrained exterior bloom while leaving the universal capsule base unchanged. Reduced motion snaps immediately and selection remains non-color-only through semantics and optical elevation.

entries.mistake: The r60.20 thin diagonal wave and tiny endpoint dot did not clearly show that tapping a selected main action reveals its family of subaction capsules.
entries.rootCause: The connector targeted only the currently selected local action and was too faint and oblique to express parent-to-family ownership.
entries.prevention: C22 draws a restrained reverse-U family bridge from the selected main capsule to the outer capsules of the revealed centered cluster, with no panel fill and no overlap of hit targets. Disclosure hide/show animates the same bridge and capsules as one finite family unit.

entries.mistake: The first C22B stale-width verification passed wildcard expressions as ripgrep search roots on Windows, producing error 123 after the literal scope file had already revealed four stale 78 px strings.
entries.rootCause: Filename globs were again placed in root-argument positions instead of searching literal existing config/docs directories with --glob filters.
entries.prevention: Every Windows ripgrep call uses literal existing roots only and applies filename filters through --glob. A mixed useful match plus error 123 is rejected and must be registered before a literal-root retry.

entries.mistake: The first C22B implementation removed lightForeground while three existing conformance tests still referenced that public token, so full analysis rejected with undefined-getter errors.
entries.rootCause: The visual family-tone split was removed together with its source-compatible token alias instead of separating runtime output consolidation from test/API migration.
entries.prevention: Keep lightForeground and mediaForeground as deprecated-compatible aliases to the one neutralForeground until C22G completes all historical test migration. Runtime methods must return the neutral token regardless of alias name.
