entries.mistake: The first C22B transparency test required every top-gradient state below 0.55 alpha, but the intentional selected-plus-pressed additions produce 0.550588 from the quantized 0x78 base, rejecting by 0.000588.
entries.rootCause: The assertion used a rounded decimal target without accounting for 8-bit color-channel quantization and the maximum combined state increment.
entries.prevention: Assert the exact base alpha separately and bound every combined state below 0.56, which admits the specified 0x78 plus 0.08 maximum while still rejecting an opaque capsule.

entries.mistake: The first C22B verification ran flutter test and flutter analyze before several successful PowerShell gates but did not assert each native exit code, so the overall shell call exited 0 despite one failed test and three analyzer errors.
entries.rootCause: ErrorActionPreference Stop does not convert native nonzero exit codes into terminating PowerShell errors, and later successful commands overwrote the final process disposition.
entries.prevention: Assert LASTEXITCODE immediately after every dart/flutter/native invocation and throw before any later gate. A mixed-output run never counts even when the outer shell reports exit 0.

entries.mistake: The first fail-fast C22B retry reached dart format after the alpha assertion patch and found the focused test formatter-dirty; the check returned nonzero, so tests were correctly not run.
entries.rootCause: The narrow apply-patch edit was assumed to preserve formatter output even though the surrounding multiline expression was reformatted on the previous pass.
entries.prevention: After any post-format source or test patch, run formatter write mode deliberately and then run the check-only gate. Count the cycle only when the check reports zero changed files.

entries.mistake: After REG-518, the same check-only dart format --output=none command was rerun under the false assumption that the first call had repaired the file; it predictably reported the same change again.
entries.rootCause: The formatter's 'Changed' diagnostic was interpreted as a filesystem write even though --output=none explicitly suppresses formatted output and is suitable only as a cleanliness check.
entries.prevention: Use dart format without --output=none for an authorized mechanical formatting write, then separately use --output=none --set-exit-if-changed as the required idempotent verification. Evidence must distinguish write mode from check mode truthfully.

entries.mistake: The first C22C combined patch assumed a -65 scroll callback appeared inside the same broad context as the action-width loop; apply_patch rejected the nonexistent adjacency and changed no source.
entries.rootCause: Multiple distant dock owners were grouped into one large context-sensitive patch after only reading slices rather than anchoring each exact current block.
entries.prevention: Patch the <=3 layout, non-overflow loop, reveal math, scrollable loop, cue deltas and middle capsule body as separate exact hunks selected from the current file. Verify each mutation before formatting.

entries.mistake: The first C22C focused test referenced SemanticsFlag.isSelected without importing dart:ui, so the test compiler rejected before analysis or later gates.
entries.rootCause: Flutter widget/material imports were assumed to re-export the low-level SemanticsFlag enum used by the direct SemanticsNode assertion.
entries.prevention: Tests that inspect SemanticsFlag directly import dart:ui with a narrow show clause, then formatter and focused compilation run before the full suite.

entries.mistake: The first rendered C22C main capsule requested 72x48 but placed its one-pixel border in AnimatedContainer.decoration, whose decoration padding deflated the keyed InkWell to 70x46; the focused test rejected the actual hit surface.
entries.rootCause: The main capsule did not mirror the local capsule's non-deflating foregroundDecoration border placement.
entries.prevention: Capsule borders render through foregroundDecoration outside the child layout, leaving both local and middle-main InkWell surfaces exactly 72x48. Focused tests measure the keyed tappable child, not only an outer requested box.

entries.mistake: After all six middle capsules reached 72x48, the focused test still failed because it expected the preserved Mool and Chat endpoint InkWells to change from 44x44 to 48x48.
entries.rootCause: The shared-capsule metric was overgeneralized to fixed endpoint controls even though C22C explicitly preserves Mool/Chat geometry and applies only to the six middle main actions.
entries.prevention: C22C tests assert 72x48 only for Social/Buy/Eat/Ride/Book/Work and assert Mool/Chat remain at MoolMetrics.minimumTapTarget. Endpoint changes require separate founder authority.

entries.mistake: The C22C focused tests passed, but full analysis rejected the new direct SemanticsNode.hasFlag assertion because this Flutter SDK deprecates hasFlag in favor of flagsCollection.
entries.rootCause: The test copied an older semantics assertion idiom without checking the current SDK analyzer contract.
entries.prevention: New semantics tests use node.flagsCollection.contains(SemanticsFlag...) and must pass full analysis after focused behavior passes.

entries.mistake: The first deprecation fix treated SemanticsNode.flagsCollection as a Set and called contains, but this SDK exposes typed tristate properties such as flagsCollection.isSelected; test compilation rejected.
entries.rootCause: The analyzer replacement name was followed without inspecting the established workspace examples for the concrete SemanticsFlags API.
entries.prevention: Before migrating a Flutter API, search literal workspace roots for accepted usage. Selected semantics use flagsCollection.isSelected with Tristate.isTrue, requiring no dart:ui enum import.

entries.mistake: The typed flagsCollection.isSelected assertion was correct, but the C22C focused test did not import dart:ui Tristate, so focused compilation rejected before analysis.
entries.rootCause: Removing the obsolete SemanticsFlag import also removed the only dart:ui import without adding the different Tristate symbol required by the accepted SDK pattern.
entries.prevention: Typed SemanticsFlags assertions import dart:ui with show Tristate and run focused compilation before any later gate.

entries.mistake: A read-only inspection addressed an app-relative test path from the repository root and then a successful rg masked the Get-Content error; a follow-up inspection also tested LASTEXITCODE after a PowerShell cmdlet where that variable is not authoritative.
entries.rootCause: The inspection mixed repository-root and app-root relative paths and reused native-process exit handling for cmdlets.
entries.prevention: Resolve literal paths against the declared workdir before inspection. Use ErrorAction Stop or direct cmdlet error handling for PowerShell cmdlets, and reserve immediate LASTEXITCODE assertions for native processes only.

entries.mistake: The first protected-gate wrapper checked LASTEXITCODE after invoking a PowerShell ps1 script, causing the wrapper to terminate after the passing delivery lock instead of executing the remaining six gates.
entries.rootCause: Native-process exit-code handling was incorrectly reused for PowerShell script invocation, whose failure contract is terminating errors and PowerShell success state.
entries.prevention: Set ErrorActionPreference to Stop and invoke protected ps1 gates sequentially without LASTEXITCODE checks; reserve LASTEXITCODE for native tools such as dart and flutter.

entries.mistake: The C22 successorPreselection block named C22 but retained the r60.19 predecessor checksum, installPerformed true, and a C21H successor-ticket pointer even though r60.20 is the founder-rejected installed predecessor and C22 has not been built or installed.
entries.rootCause: The prior candidate's pre-build template fields were only partially transitioned when the C22 parent was registered after the r60.20 rejection.
entries.prevention: Each successor ticket transition reconciles candidate id, installed predecessor checksum, build/install booleans, successor ticket pointer and evidence as one machine-readable identity set before runtime mutation or qualification.

entries.mistake: The C22D overlay duplicate search legitimately found no OverlayPortal, CompositedTransformFollower or LayerLink owner, but the combined inspection surfaced rg's no-match exit code as a failed tool call.
entries.rootCause: The inspection did not explicitly normalize rg exit code 1 as an accepted no-match result after printing the source header.
entries.prevention: Duplicate searches that allow zero matches handle rg exit code 1 explicitly while still rejecting exit codes above 1; the no-match result is recorded as inventory evidence rather than a gate failure.

entries.mistake: The first C22D pixel gate reported nearly white outer pixels across all six families and initially attributed them to runtime overlay paint.
entries.rootCause: The test used a childless ColoredBox as Scaffold.body; under the loose Scaffold body constraint it collapsed vertically, so the sampled rail area exposed the default Scaffold canvas instead of the intended destination fixture.
entries.prevention: Zero-strap pixel fixtures use an explicitly expanding destination layer, assert the capture dimensions and coordinates, then require rendered outer and inter-capsule pixels to equal the known destination background.

entries.mistake: The first REG-531 retry clipped global-rail painting based on an unverified shadow-bleed hypothesis, but every outer-pixel result remained exactly [254,247,255].
entries.rootCause: The attempted runtime fix preceded verification of the capture boundary's raster width, coordinate origin and sampled rail coordinates.
entries.prevention: When a raw-pixel failure is spatially ambiguous, first assert the captured image dimensions and translate global widget coordinates into boundary-local raster coordinates. Do not mutate runtime from color value inference alone.

entries.mistake: The combined C22D shadow-revert and raster-coordinate diagnostic patch was rejected atomically because its helper-function context reflected the pre-format test layout.
entries.rootCause: A multi-file patch was composed without rereading the formatter-produced helper block after the failed test cycle.
entries.prevention: After formatting or a failed test, reread each exact target block and apply independent runtime and test hunks so one stale context cannot reject unrelated corrections.

entries.mistake: The C22D raw-pixel fixture assumed a childless ColoredBox would fill Scaffold.body, but it collapsed to zero height and produced a false white-canvas rejection at otherwise correct rail coordinates.
entries.rootCause: The fixture did not provide SizedBox.expand or another tight vertical constraint and did not validate the destination render object's rect before interpreting pixels.
entries.prevention: Pixel fixtures explicitly expand background layers, assert capture size and widget coordinates, and distinguish fixture paint from production overlay paint before runtime changes.

entries.mistake: The first C22E contract search again passed wildcard path roots to rg on Windows, which rejected the paths before reading any contract file.
entries.rootCause: Filename filtering was placed in positional roots instead of rg --glob filters despite REG-514.
entries.prevention: All Windows rg searches use literal existing root directories and one or more --glob filters; wildcard positional roots are prohibited.

entries.mistake: The first C22E focused run passed reverse-U geometry and non-interaction checks, but tapping the selected Buy or Work main capsule left the disclosure region at 52 px in both animated and reduced-motion cases.
entries.rootCause: The selected-main callback did fire and the disclosure controller changed; the local overlay's Positioned supplied a tight 52 px height, so Align.heightFactor could not reduce the region's geometry.
entries.prevention: Disclosure children inside a fixed overlay use loose natural-height positioning. Tests verify callback semantics, controller opacity and region geometry in normal and reduced-motion modes.

entries.mistake: C22E constrained the local disclosure child with Positioned height 52, so Align.heightFactor remained 52 even when opacity reached .5 or 0 and semantics correctly changed to Show options.
entries.rootCause: A fixed paint-zone height was incorrectly applied to the animated disclosure child instead of only to the containing overlay canvas.
entries.prevention: The outer bridge overlay keeps its fixed 60 px canvas, while the local disclosure child is top-positioned with loose natural height so heightFactor can animate from 52 to 0 and snap in reduced motion.

entries.mistake: The first REG-536 cause correction plus REG-537 insertion patch was rejected atomically because a later hunk searched for the C22E entry after using field-level context from that same tail entry.
entries.rootCause: The registry tail was not reread before composing multiple overlapping hunks against one object.
entries.prevention: Registry corrections and adjacent insertions use one exact current-tail replacement after rereading the file; overlapping hunks against the same object are prohibited.

entries.mistake: After C22E correctly restored the new reverse-U connector, all six C22D zero-strap cases failed before pixel assertions because the C22D test still required the connector key to be absent.
entries.rootCause: A transient between-ticket implementation state was encoded in the durable zero-strap test even though C22E was already authorized to replace the old diagonal wave with a new connector under the same stable key.
entries.prevention: Sequential ticket tests assert only their durable contract. C22D owns no full-width surface and untouched pixels; C22E exclusively owns connector existence, geometry, anchor, noninteraction and disclosure.

entries.mistake: The first REG-539 registration plus C22D test migration patch was rejected atomically because it expected the pre-format multiline ValueKey finder while the current file used a formatter-compressed line.
entries.rootCause: The exact test block was not reread after the prior formatter run before composing a multi-file patch.
entries.prevention: Read formatter-owned test context immediately before patching and keep registry registration separate from the exact test hunk.

entries.mistake: All six C11 family cases rejected the new bridge because they expected the old painter main anchor at global-stack dy 0 and later expected a directional wave to animate between selected local indices.
entries.rootCause: The C11 test encoded the superseded diagonal selected-local painter architecture rather than the durable customer outcome after C22E changed the connector to a stable full-family bracket in a 60 px overlay.
entries.prevention: Cumulative connector tests assert overlay-relative selected-main termination, first-to-last capsule span, stable bracket geometry across local selection, one-tap selected semantics, disclosure and reduced motion. Selected local chroma motion belongs to C22F cells, not the family bridge.

entries.mistake: The first migrated C11 compile referenced MoolLocalNavigationTokens for reverse-U first/last centers without importing the shared design-system library.
entries.rootCause: The legacy test previously consumed only the global-navigation library and the new cross-owner token dependency was not added with the assertions.
entries.prevention: When migrating tests to a shared token owner, add a direct package import in the same patch and run focused compilation before behavior assertions.

entries.mistake: After the C11 assertions were migrated and passed, all six test names still described a transparent directional wave rather than the new reverse-U family bridge.
entries.rootCause: Behavior assertions were updated without updating the generated test description used in qualification logs.
entries.prevention: Contract migrations update test names, assertions and completion evidence together so logs truthfully identify the qualified design.

entries.mistake: The first C22F palette audit assumed the current shared design-system path existed in HEAD and piped git show into rg, but the command returned no historical object or token evidence.
entries.rootCause: A current dirty-tree owner was treated as a guaranteed HEAD path without first checking its tracked/history status.
entries.prevention: Historical lookups first verify the exact path with git status and git cat-file. If unavailable, design selection uses current accepted owners and ticket contracts without inventing historical evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C22F press tests read the pressed AnimatedOpacity immediately after startGesture and saw 0 because InkWell had not yet dispatched its scroll-aware onHighlightChanged callback.
entries.rootCause: The harness confused pointer-down with the framework's recognized press/highlight state and did not hold through the press timeout.
entries.prevention: InkWell press-state tests hold the pointer through the framework press timeout before asserting the 100 ms target duration/opacity, then release and verify return to zero.

entries.mistake: After press-timeout correction, local and reduced-motion press cases passed but the main case still targeted Social while the six-action dock had scrolled to active Buy, so the keyed center was not a reliable visible hit target.
entries.rootCause: The fixture chose a nonselected action without proving its center was inside the horizontally clipped action viewport.
entries.prevention: Main press tests target the active, centered, callback-enabled capsule or explicitly ensure visibility and verify its rect before starting the gesture.

entries.mistake: The first C22G qualifying host cycle aborted before format, analysis, tests or gates because the qualifier assigned the contract hostQualification object to `$host`, which case-insensitively collided with PowerShell's read-only automatic `$Host` variable.
entries.rootCause: A generic local name was selected without checking PowerShell automatic and reserved variables.
entries.prevention: PowerShell qualification scripts use domain-specific local names such as `$hostQualificationContract`; any assignment collision aborts and the invocation cannot count as a host cycle.

entries.mistake: The first registration diagnostic guessed `config/regression-memory-registry.json` and failed because that path does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The durable registry filename was inferred rather than discovered from a bounded repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Discover the exact regression registry with `rg --files` and then use the verified literal `config/codex-development-regression-registry.json` path for every read or patch.

entries.mistake: After cycle 1 reached and rejected in the required Flutter suite, assigning the throwing qualifier invocation to an output variable under Stop discarded access to the already-produced native output and exposed only the wrapper exception.
entries.rootCause: Failure diagnostics depended on successful completion of a PowerShell script that intentionally throws after a native nonzero exit.
entries.prevention: Reproduce the rejected native phase directly with verified literal inputs, record LASTEXITCODE immediately, and emit bounded output before any wrapper throw can short-circuit assignment.

entries.mistake: The first direct diagnostic ran from apps/mobile, guessed a repository-relative config path from that directory, obtained no contract or required tests, and invoked `flutter test` with an empty list, which started the entire mobile test tree.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic did not bind an absolute repository root, did not make the missing contract read terminating, and did not assert the required test count before invoking Flutter.
entries.prevention: Resolve the repository root and contract with verified literal paths, require exactly 14 derived test files, and abort before Flutter when the list is empty or wrong-count.

entries.mistake: The combined `Get-Process -Name dart,flutter` probe printed the existing Dart process but returned failure because Flutter was absent.
entries.rootCause: Multiple optional process names were passed to one cmdlet, allowing one normal no-match result to contaminate the whole probe status.
entries.prevention: Enumerate processes once and filter optional names, or probe each name separately and explicitly normalize absence; never accept a partial combined-name result as a passing gate.

entries.mistake: The first corrected C22G required suite had 12 failures because cumulative C16/C20 tests still required 13px local labels and searched for the removed AnimatedContainer selection owner after C22 standardized 12px/800 typography and shared inner-chroma motion.
entries.rootCause: C22B/C22F implementation and focused tests were completed without migrating every superseded assertion in the complete 14-file C22G required suite before the first qualifying cycle.
entries.prevention: When a shared primitive replaces typography or selection widget architecture, migrate every cumulative required-suite assertion to the authoritative token and durable customer outcome before host qualification; never change the accepted runtime back to satisfy legacy implementation-shape tests.

entries.mistake: After stale C16/C20 assertions were migrated, the focused suite exposed that white labels over the C22 neutral glass could fall to 3.56:1 on accepted bright destination backgrounds in Social, Buy, Eat, Ride, Book and Work.
entries.rootCause: The first neutral glass alpha and inner-emission intensity were selected for transparency without a cumulative 4.5:1 composite legibility gate across light, bright and dark destination backgrounds.
entries.prevention: Freeze a transparent smoked-glass base and internal emission ceiling that preserve at least 4.5:1 white icon/label contrast across accepted background probes, while retaining nonopaque destination transmission and internal-only family chroma.

entries.mistake: The first runtime-ticket authority audit guessed shortened C22F and parent C22 filenames plus a generic ticket-queue path; all three were missing, so the combined read was incomplete despite printing valid C22G and scope data.
entries.rootCause: Supporting manifest names were inferred from labels instead of discovered through a bounded config file inventory.
entries.prevention: Discover ticket owners with `rg --files config` before literal reads; any missing operand rejects the whole authority inventory and authorizes no mutation.

entries.mistake: After C22F1 focused tests and full analysis passed, the permanent placement aggregate still classified the active design as C21 and invoked C21B, which rejected because current C22F1 is correctly absent from the historical C21 sequence.
entries.rootCause: The durable placement contract/checker was not migrated when C22 replaced C21 optical-glass tokens with fixed capsules, zero strap, reverse-U and internal chroma.
entries.prevention: The placement registry explicitly owns a C22 branch with current geometry, placement, legibility and connector rules, dispatching to C22F1 during remediation and C22G after restart while leaving historical C21 gates unchanged.

entries.mistake: The first C22H process audit counted the long-lived GradleDaemon Java process as one active build/test command even though no Gradle client, wrapper, Flutter build or Flutter test was running.
entries.rootCause: The process filter matched any Java command line containing `gradle` instead of binding active work to GradleMain/GradleWrapperMain client classes and treating GradleDaemon separately.
entries.prevention: Prebuild probes count Java only for exact Gradle client/wrapper main classes and Dart/Flutter only for actual build/test commands; idle GradleDaemon processes are reported separately and never classified as active builds.

entries.mistake: The first C22H post-state validation invoked repository scripts as `scripts/check-*.ps1`; PowerShell did not search the current directory and stopped after validating only the APK-state JSON.
entries.rootCause: The gate batch treated a repository-relative script path like an executable on PATH instead of using an explicit current-directory-qualified or literal absolute path.
entries.prevention: Invoke every repository PowerShell gate with an explicit `./scripts/...` path (or a verified literal absolute path), and treat any partial aggregate as authorizing no qualification progress.

entries.mistake: A C22H prebuild-evidence audit guessed a C21 artifact directory containing `subaction-optical-liquid-glass`; the immutable predecessor directory actually uses the `global-subaction` ticket identity already recorded in the APK state.
entries.rootCause: The historical artifact path was reconstructed from a design label instead of reading the exact selected predecessor evidence path from the current machine contract or a bounded artifact inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve historical artifact directories from exact machine-state evidence fields and confirm them with `rg --files` under the literal existing directory; never synthesize a predecessor directory name from a ticket description.

entries.mistake: The first C22H authority-state inventory appended `-parent-ticket` to the C22 parent manifest name; the actual verified owner is `config/uaw-personal-mvp-global-capsule-subaction-recovery-fix5-c22-ticket.json`.
entries.rootCause: A logical parent role was incorrectly treated as a filename suffix instead of discovering the exact configured manifest owner.
entries.prevention: Before reading or mutating a ticket hierarchy, discover every exact ticket manifest with a bounded `rg --files config` inventory and use only the returned literal paths.

entries.mistake: The first post-install matrix transition assumed the Social Shorts hierarchy captured earlier was still the live OPPO state; the helper found zero tappable `Open YouTube Videos` nodes and correctly aborted before tapping or accepting evidence.
entries.rootCause: The transition batch used the prior accepted screenshot as an implicit navigation precondition instead of reacquiring and validating the live hierarchy immediately before the next journey.
entries.prevention: Every device transition begins with a fresh hierarchy acquisition and an explicit current-state precondition; if the device state has changed, deterministically reopen the app/family before tapping and never accept a screenshot from an inferred state.

entries.mistake: After Buy Shop was accepted, the Wholesale transition did not reach two stable confirmations because the live OPPO state changed to Mool Home during the bounded post-tap sampling window.
entries.rootCause: A valid pre-tap hierarchy cannot guarantee exclusive ownership of a founder-held device throughout the later stability window; another device interaction can replace the target after the automation tap.
entries.prevention: Treat any post-tap family replacement as an interrupted journey, accept no target evidence, reacquire the actual live state, then deterministically reopen the required family and repeat the one-tap journey under fresh preconditions.

entries.mistake: The first C22H Social Create capture requested an IME-hidden acceptance immediately after tapping Create even though its editor auto-opened the keyboard; the helper correctly rejected the obscured state and stopped the later Eat steps.
entries.rootCause: The journey did not insert an explicit keyboard-dismissal and selected-state revalidation between opening an editor destination and capturing the full capsule system.
entries.prevention: For editor subactions, use Android Back once to dismiss only the IME, then prove the same local selection remains current and the input method reports hidden before accepting screenshot/XML evidence.

entries.mistake: A progress update said Social's four subactions and Eat Order Food were stable while the running batch had not returned; it later showed the first Create step rejected, so Eat had never run.
entries.rootCause: The update inferred sequential progress from elapsed time instead of reporting only tool output already received from the live cell.
entries.prevention: While a device batch is running, report only confirmed output delivered by the cell; describe all undisclosed steps as still pending until the command returns explicit pass lines.

entries.mistake: The checksum-proven r60.21 C22H candidate kept a persistent four-button subaction layer immediately above a persistent multi-action global rail; the founder rejected the result as unprofessional, cluttered and too dominant over product content.
entries.rootCause: C22 optimized the appearance of individual capsules while preserving two simultaneous navigation layers, so component polish could not fix the higher-level information-hierarchy and content-competition defect.
entries.prevention: C23 removes both persistent rails, leaves one compact Mool Home launcher on destinations, and moves six families plus all truthful subactions into the existing Mool Home action hub where any target is reachable in one tap from Home or two taps from another destination.

entries.mistake: The first C23A-to-C23B transition patch was rejected before mutation because one wrapped line in an Add File section omitted the required leading `+` patch marker.
entries.rootCause: A long multi-file patch was composed without validating every added documentation line retained unified-diff syntax.
entries.prevention: Keep transition patches bounded and verify every Add File content line begins with `+`; a parser-rejected patch is treated as no mutation and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The first C23B scope transition patch was rejected before mutation because a dependency-list context line did not exactly match the current scope JSON.
entries.rootCause: A broad incremental patch mixed many replacements and relied on remembered surrounding context instead of replacing the verified complete scope document.
entries.prevention: For dense selected-ticket scope transitions, reread the exact current JSON and replace the complete validated document through apply_patch rather than coupling many hunks to fragile context lines.

entries.mistake: The first C23B qualification invoked `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` directly on newly patched unformatted files; Dart reported both would change, returned exit 1, and the batch stopped before analysis/tests without writing them.
entries.rootCause: The no-output format gate was used before a separate mechanical formatting pass even though new Dart code had not yet been normalized.
entries.prevention: After authorized Dart edits, run the formatter as an explicit mechanical normalization step, then run a separate no-diff format gate before analysis and tests; never interpret the expected first normalization as completed qualification.

entries.mistake: After the first format rejection, the report incorrectly claimed `dart format --output=none` had normalized the files; the repeated gate proved it had only reported pending changes and had written nothing.
entries.rootCause: The word `Changed` in formatter output was interpreted without respecting the explicit `--output=none` option semantics.
entries.prevention: Use plain `dart format <files>` for the authorized mechanical write, verify its native exit immediately, and only then use `--output=none --set-exit-if-changed` as a read-only no-diff gate; describe tool effects from option semantics, not output wording alone.

entries.mistake: The first C23C shell change bypassed the dual-rail render tree but left the old global-rail LayerLink field and local-disclosure toggle method unreferenced; focused analysis rejected both warnings.
entries.rootCause: The render path was replaced before performing a complete analyzer-driven cleanup of legacy state members that were entered only from that path.
entries.prevention: After removing a navigation architecture, run focused analysis before tests and remove every newly unreachable private owner while preserving only state still referenced by lifecycle behavior.

entries.mistake: The C23E reconciliation command requested `config/mvp-delivery-lock.json`, which does not exist, after already printing valid repository, device, ticket and scope state.
entries.rootCause: A descriptive shorthand was substituted for the exact repository-owned robust delivery lock filename instead of resolving the path from AGENTS.md or a bounded config inventory.
entries.prevention: Read delivery authority only from the exact mandated `config/mvp-robust-60-75-day-delivery-lock.json` path or a bounded discovered literal; any missing operand rejects the combined authority audit and authorizes no mutation.

entries.mistake: The first C23E scope transition retried a broad multi-hunk edit and was atomically rejected because one remembered C23D exclusion line did not exactly match the current JSON.
entries.rootCause: The edit repeated the already registered REG-566 failure mode instead of first replacing the verified complete dense scope document.
entries.prevention: For every C23 selected-ticket scope transition, read the current scope JSON to an exact bounded artifact and replace its complete content through apply_patch; do not retry fragile multi-hunk context edits.

entries.mistake: The first C23G aggregate and placement pre-cycle validation assigned Home-screen source text to `$home`; PowerShell variables are case-insensitive, so both scripts attempted to overwrite the read-only `$HOME` automatic variable and rejected.
entries.rootCause: A generic domain noun was used despite the permanent rule forbidding `$HOME`, `$home` and other automatic-variable collisions.
entries.prevention: PowerShell gates name Home-screen source variables `$moolHomeSource` or another ticket-specific identifier and never assign to `$HOME`, `$home`, `$Host` or `$host`.

entries.mistake: The migrated R03 one-tap test tapped C23 family controls but compared results to `personalMoolRootActions`; Eat, Ride, Book and Work therefore expected their older default destination routes instead of C23's exact family routes.
entries.rootCause: The test's interaction owner was migrated to C23 keys while its expected-route owner remained the superseded R03 projection.
entries.prevention: C23 Home-hub tests bind main-family expectations to the six routes in the C23 contract and bind the 17 direct targets to the C23 action matrix; older projections may still be tested independently but cannot define C23 tap results.

entries.mistake: A read-only `rg` command put the literal `$home` search token inside a PowerShell double-quoted argument; PowerShell expanded it to the user profile path and ripgrep rejected the resulting escape sequence.
entries.rootCause: The command did not protect a dollar-prefixed source token from shell interpolation.
entries.prevention: PowerShell ripgrep patterns containing dollar-prefixed source identifiers use a literal single-quoted argument or fixed-string mode; never place them in an interpolating double-quoted command argument.

entries.mistake: C23G cycle 1 passed clean complete analysis but the 13-file required suite had 16 failures because retained Buy, Social, Eat, Ride, Book and Work journey assertions still searched for removed C22 keys such as `mool-action-buy` and `mool-root-selected`.
entries.rootCause: The C23 focused Home tests and R03 contract were migrated before the first cycle, but every selected vertical/continuity test that encoded the rejected persistent global rail was not migrated in advance.
entries.prevention: Before retrying C23G, inventory all required-test references to C22 global/local rail keys and migrate them to durable C23 outcomes: one 56px destination Mool launcher, zero persistent rail/Chat controls, exact Home routes, content reachability and Back continuity. Never restore rejected runtime widgets to satisfy stale tests.

entries.mistake: After the C23G stale-key inventory, the regression-memory gate was invoked with `-Phase testing`; the script admits only general, implementation, build or device and rejected the argument.
entries.rootCause: A conceptual activity label was guessed instead of reading the gate's declared ValidateSet or reusing the known host-qualification `implementation` phase.
entries.prevention: C23 host and test migration invokes regression memory with `-Phase implementation -BuildMode none`; phase arguments must come from the script's verified ValidateSet and are never inferred from prose.

entries.mistake: The first post-migration required-test batch tapped `mool-home-family-eat` directly; the control existed below the 800x600 test viewport, the tap missed, and the expected Eat destination never opened.
entries.rootCause: A former always-visible bottom-rail tap was mechanically replaced with a vertically scrolling Home-hub control without adding `ensureVisible` and a settled-state precondition.
entries.prevention: Every migrated C23 Home family or subaction tap first finds the exact key, calls `ensureVisible`, settles, then taps and validates the resulting route; former persistent-rail visibility assumptions are forbidden.

entries.mistake: After global-rail key migration, the isolated Buy continuity file still failed two tests that tapped removed `buy-local-tab-medicine` and `buy-local-tab-wholesale` controls.
entries.rootCause: The stale-key inventory searched global C22 patterns but did not include every family-specific local tab prefix selected by the complete suite.
entries.prevention: C23 required-suite inventory searches all family local prefixes, including `buy-local-tab-`, and migrates cross-subaction continuity to the exact two-tap destination launcher -> Home subaction journey with visible-target preconditions.

entries.mistake: The migrated Buy continuity test called `BuyV2Session.openDestination` with `BuyV2Destination` values but did not import the existing `buy_v2_models.dart` owner, so the test failed to compile.
entries.rootCause: The session import was incorrectly assumed to re-export its destination enum.
entries.prevention: Before running a migrated Dart test, focused analysis or source-owner lookup verifies every newly referenced type's defining import; `BuyV2Destination` comes from `features/buy/buy_v2_models.dart`.

entries.mistake: The migrated Buy continuity test reached the Medicine experience through Mool Home but the live GoRouter URI reported `/app/buy` with no `sub=medicine` query, rejecting the route-continuity assertion.
entries.rootCause: The test read GoRouter's base route-information URI after imperative navigation and treated it as the visible top-page route. The visible page's `GoRouterState` truthfully retained `/app/buy?sub=medicine`.
entries.prevention: C23 imperative-route continuity is asserted through `GoRouterState.of` on the visible page before and after refresh. Base provider/delegate URIs remain separate stack-base evidence and cannot create a false subaction failure.

entries.mistake: The first C23E1 origin-aware Home replacement still produced `/app/buy` without `sub=medicine` because the new target and older Buy page retained the same path-derived `state.pageKey`.
entries.rootCause: Route dispatch was corrected without updating the shared main-destination page identity to distinguish query-specific visible states.
entries.prevention: The shared `moolMainDestinationPage` key binds the complete current URI so different query-selected states cannot collapse onto an older same-path page; origin-aware replacement remains responsible for prior-context Back behavior.

entries.mistake: After selecting origin-aware Home replacement, the canonical Eat continuity test still expected Back to show Mool Home instead of restoring the prior Social destination specified by C23E1.
entries.rootCause: Runtime policy and the ticket were updated but the older post-Back assertion was not migrated in the same patch.
entries.prevention: C23E1 tests distinguish root Home, which remains below pushed targets, from destination-opened Home, which is replaced so Back restores the prior exact destination.

entries.mistake: The first source check for Dart's `moolsocial-main:${state.uri}` token used a PowerShell double-quoted string, which would interpolate `$state` instead of comparing the literal Dart source.
entries.rootCause: A dollar-prefixed Dart interpolation token was added without applying the already registered literal-pattern escaping rule.
entries.prevention: PowerShell source gates wrap Dart interpolation tokens in single-quoted PowerShell strings and double any embedded Dart single quotes; review the exact gate line before execution.

entries.mistake: Even after complete-URI page identity was added, C23E1 still lost `sub=medicine` because `context.replace` preserves the current page identity by design when replacing Home.
entries.rootCause: The first route-dispatch correction selected GoRouter's identity-preserving replace API instead of its new-entry replacement API.
entries.prevention: Destination-opened Home uses `context.pushReplacement(route)`: it removes Home, creates the exact target as a new route entry, preserves the prior destination below it, and keeps root Home on ordinary `context.push`.

entries.mistake: The bounded C23E1 format/analyze/test process returned a live execution cell immediately before context compaction, but the cell was no longer available afterward and no attached terminal retained its final result; the verification outcome was therefore unknowable.
entries.rootCause: The verification batch's only result owner was an ephemeral execution cell, and its completed output was not persisted to a repository evidence file before compaction detached the cell.
entries.prevention: A verification result that cannot be recovered is never inferred. The exact bounded checks are rerun from the preserved tree, and long qualification cycles write their complete output to ticket evidence so process-cell loss cannot create a false pass.

entries.mistake: The C23E1 verification rerun invoked `./scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate-state.ps1` while the shell working directory was `apps/mobile`; PowerShell could not find the repository-root script and stopped before Dart or Flutter ran.
entries.rootCause: A repository-root gate and mobile-package commands were combined under one mobile working directory despite the permanent rule that repository gates need a verified root-relative or literal absolute owner.
entries.prevention: Run repository PowerShell gates in the repository root as their own command, confirm their result, and only then run Dart or Flutter with `apps/mobile` as the working directory. Never combine both path domains under one relative script path.

entries.mistake: The corrected C23E1 mobile verification used a one-second shell timeout. No-diff formatting completed, but the shell killed focused Flutter analysis before it returned and the tests never ran.
entries.rootCause: The shell command's process timeout was confused with the orchestrator's early-yield interval; the former terminates work while the latter safely returns a live execution cell.
entries.prevention: Flutter analysis and tests receive a realistic shell timeout. Use the execution orchestrator's yield interval for responsive progress, retain the returned cell, and never shorten the nested process timeout to force an early update.

entries.mistake: The C23E1 correction assumed `context.pushReplacement` plus complete-URI page identity would preserve the Home Buy Medicine target, but the focused real-router test still rendered Medicine while GoRouter reported `/app/buy` with no `sub` query.
entries.rootCause: No visible-route rewrite occurred. The failing assertion compared the imperative top page to the underlying base URI; a retained trace proved the visible Buy page owned `/app/buy?sub=medicine` throughout.
entries.prevention: Visible-page `GoRouterState` and visible customer content must agree before and after refresh. Provider/delegate base URIs are not substituted for imperative top-page state, and no navigation workaround is added to satisfy that false owner.

entries.mistake: The first bounded diagnosis proposed that only GoRouter's route information provider was stale after imperative navigation. The retained trace proved both provider and router delegate active configuration were `/app/buy` while Medicine remained visible.
entries.rootCause: The diagnosis attributed divergence to reporting before checking the active configuration, then incorrectly treated `currentConfiguration.uri` as the top imperative page owner. REG-20260809-590 retains the successor correction.
entries.prevention: Routing diagnosis compares provider URI, delegate base URI, visible-page `GoRouterState` and shared session state in the same frame. Provider/delegate URIs must not be described as top-page owners until a before-tap imperative-page trace proves that assumption.

entries.mistake: The second C23E1 diagnosis called `routerDelegate.currentConfiguration.uri` the active top-page URI and inferred a route collapse. Frame tracing proved it already remained `/app/buy` while the imperatively pushed Mool Home page was visibly active before the Medicine tap.
entries.rootCause: The base route-list URI was mistaken for the `GoRouterState` attached to the visible imperatively pushed page.
entries.prevention: For imperative push/pushReplacement journeys, inspect `GoRouterState.of` from the visible page context as the top-page route owner. Retain base provider/delegate measurements only as separate evidence and never infer a collapse from them alone.

entries.mistake: The C23E1 Buy continuity test asserted `routeInformationProvider.value.uri` as the current Buy subaction route. A retained trace proved that owner stayed at base `/app/buy` while visible Home owned `/app/mool?from=buy` and visible Buy owned `/app/buy?sub=medicine`.
entries.rootCause: The test conflated GoRouter's underlying base route with the `GoRouterState` attached to the top imperatively pushed page.
entries.prevention: Assert exact imperative route/state through `GoRouterState.of` on the visible keyed page, both before and after refresh. Retain provider/delegate readings only when the test is explicitly about the base route list.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to append C23E1 successor corrections to two retained rejection records used remembered closing prose for the C23G document. `apply_patch` rejected the unmatched context and changed no file.
entries.rootCause: The evidence amendment was drafted from registry wording instead of reading the exact retained Markdown owner first.
entries.prevention: Read the exact tail of every retained evidence file before amendment, then anchor a bounded patch on text that actually exists. A parser-rejected patch is registered before any corrected retry.

entries.mistake: The C23E1 sealing inspection guessed `config/uaw-personal-mvp-mool-home-action-hub-regression-fix6-c23g-ticket.json`; that path did not exist, so the read batch stopped after the C23E1 manifest and no ticket state changed.
entries.rootCause: The child identifier and aggregate gate label were converted into an assumed filename instead of using a bounded config inventory.
entries.prevention: Before any ticket-state transition, inventory `config/*c23*.json`, match the exact ticketId inside candidates, and patch only the returned literal manifest owner. Child role or gate name never implies filename wording.

entries.mistake: The first fresh C23G cycle 1 invocation piped output to a relative `Tee-Object` path. The qualifier changes into `apps/mobile`, so the sink resolved under that directory and failed to open; no host cycle qualified.
entries.rootCause: The log destination was not resolved to an absolute repository evidence path before a nested script changed the process location.
entries.prevention: Resolve the cycle log with `[IO.Path]::GetFullPath` from the repository root before invoking any script that uses Push-Location. Qualification counts only after the complete retained log ends with the exact cycle-pass seal.

entries.mistake: Fresh C23G cycle 1 passed no-diff format, complete analysis, all 98 required-suite tests, the aggregate gate, placement gate and protected UI locks, then `check-brand-integrity.ps1 -Surface App` rejected that shared global navigation did not use the canonical Mool launcher.
entries.rootCause: The C23 runtime correctly rendered `MoolBrand.moolLauncherIcon` inside a direct `Icon(...)`, but the retained brand gate required the obsolete named-parameter text `icon: MoolBrand.moolLauncherIcon` from the removed rail-style owner.
entries.prevention: The brand gate extracts the actual `_MoolHomeLauncher` source boundary and requires `MoolBrand.moolLauncherIcon` there, independent of whether the canonical icon is passed as a named parameter or rendered directly. The mandatory gate remains active.

entries.mistake: The brand-owner diagnosis included `apps/mobile/lib/core/design/*.dart` as a literal ripgrep path on Windows. Ripgrep rejected the wildcard path and returned exit 1 after the needed exact source evidence had already printed.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style filename wildcard was passed as a Windows literal path instead of using a directory operand or ripgrep `--glob`.
entries.prevention: On Windows, give ripgrep the verified directory and constrain filenames with `--glob`, or pass exact literal files. Treat any nonzero search exit as a rejected command even when earlier output is useful.

entries.mistake: After sealing C23G logs, the C23H audit guessed `docs/quality/UAW-PERSONAL-MVP-HOME-HUB-OPPO-QUALIFICATION-FIX6-C23H-PRESELECTION-ASSESSMENT-20260809.md`. The path did not exist, so the batch stopped before APK and device reconciliation.
entries.rootCause: The exact ticket filename was incorrectly assumed to imply an identically worded preselection evidence filename.
entries.prevention: Before C23H selection, inventory bounded `docs/quality/*C23H*` candidates and use the literal preselection owner returned by that inventory. Ticket and evidence naming are independently discovered.

entries.mistake: The first C23H dirty-tree fingerprint used `git status --untracked-files=all`, forcing traversal of protected untracked browser-evidence trees. Git emitted filename-too-long warnings, so the reported 52,659-entry fingerprint was incomplete and inadmissible despite exit 0.
entries.rootCause: A deep per-file untracked enumeration replaced the established path-safe porcelain inventory, which records every tracked change and each untracked owner without descending into retained evidence directories.
entries.prevention: APK prebuild uses the established default path-safe `git status --porcelain=v1` inventory, rejects any stderr warning, sorts the returned records and hashes their LF-joined UTF-8 representation. Deep untracked evidence trees remain preserved and are never traversed for the seal.

entries.mistake: The first positive C23H machine-gate invocation returned only an output-truncation notice, no execution-cell identifier, no bounded pass line and no retained positive-gate evidence.
entries.rootCause: A large compound gate invocation was allowed to render unbounded output directly, so the execution result could not be recovered or admitted after the context boundary.
entries.prevention: Before retry, prove the candidate APK and provenance are absent and the authorization remains unconsumed. Rerun the read-only machine gate with output captured to a verified ticket-local log and print only its exit status and bounded final pass lines; invoke the unique build wrapper only after that evidence passes.

entries.mistake: The C23H registration inspection guessed a shortened REG598 evidence filename that did not exist. PowerShell emitted path errors while the compound command still reported exit code zero.
entries.rootCause: The exact evidence owner was inferred from the regression description instead of being selected from a bounded filename inventory, repeating the class already prohibited by REG597.
entries.prevention: Inventory bounded evidence filenames first and read only literal returned owners. Treat any PowerShell error record as a rejected compound inspection even when the process exit code is zero, and keep discovery separate from required reads.

entries.mistake: The first bounded full-memory paging command asserted the 953-line count observed before two new lessons were added; the current owner contained 961 lines, so the read rejected before printing its page.
entries.rootCause: A pre-mutation file metric was reused as a current paging invariant immediately after the same file had been amended.
entries.prevention: Discover the current line count immediately before complete-file paging and derive verified non-overlapping ranges from that current value. Never hardcode a count observed before a repository mutation.

entries.mistake: The first post-registration reseal patch used an indented ConvertTo-Json projection as context for the authoritative one-line minified C23H ticket, so apply_patch rejected the complete multi-file patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: A diagnostic object rendering was mistaken for the file's literal current representation, and three independent state owners were coupled into one patch attempt.
entries.prevention: Read literal current source from each owner, preserve minified-versus-formatted representation and patch each state owner independently. Diagnostic JSON projections never provide edit context.

entries.mistake: After the installed r60.22 Mool tap successfully transitioned to Home and pulled unique PNG/XML evidence, the read-only parser assigned the XML document to `$home`, colliding with PowerShell's read-only `$HOME` automatic variable and rejecting only the remaining summary step.
entries.rootCause: The already-registered ticket-specific variable rule was not applied to a device-evidence parser, even though PowerShell variable names remain case-insensitive in that context.
entries.prevention: Device parsers use ticket-specific names such as `$moolHomeHierarchy`. When post-capture parsing fails, preserve and parse the existing unique evidence instead of repeating the user action or overwriting the capture.

entries.mistake: Installed r60.22 emitted the Mool launcher, Home Chat, all six family buttons and all 17 direct subactions as Android buttons with `clickable=false`, although a sighted coordinate tap on the launcher still worked.
entries.rootCause: Each affected native owner wrapped an actionable InkWell in `Semantics(button: true, excludeSemantics: true)` but omitted an outer `onTap`, thereby excluding the only accessibility click action while retaining only the label and button flag.
entries.prevention: The successor outer semantic owner exposes `SemanticsAction.tap` directly or preserves the nested InkWell action. Strengthen the existing C23B/C23C/C23F tests for launcher, Chat, six families and 17 subactions, then require OPPO UIAutomator `clickable=true` and one real tap before the full matrix resumes. Coordinate-only automation is forbidden as a bypass.

entries.mistake: The first C24 reference-to-production inventory used a declaration pattern that returned no line and combined it with a 1,184-match multi-root route/token search whose output was truncated.
entries.rootCause: Exact owner discovery and category-specific duplicate searches were collapsed into one compound inspection without an anchor-count assertion or bounded result budget.
entries.prevention: Prove the exact declaration line first, then run separate bounded Eat, Ride, Book, Work, Medicine and Bus searches with independent counts and explicit zero-match handling. Truncated output and blank anchors authorize no ticket selection.

entries.mistake: The C24 retry launched Book, Work and Medicine/Bus searches independently but recombined their verbose results into one 719-line tool response, which was truncated before all independent results could be verified.
entries.rootCause: Concurrency was treated as sufficient output isolation even though the orchestration layer applies one aggregate response budget to every parallel result.
entries.prevention: Each C24 category search must return only machine-counted owner paths, route declarations and a small capped match sample in its own tool response. Never aggregate verbose category inventories into one response, even when the underlying calls are independent.

entries.mistake: The C24 state inspection guessed `config/uaw-personal-mvp-parent-scope-state.json`; that file does not exist, so the compound read exited nonzero after the valid scope state had already printed.
entries.rootCause: A plausible state-owner filename was composed from memory instead of being resolved from the repository's literal tracked and untracked filenames.
entries.prevention: Before opening any C24 state owner whose exact path has not already been proven, resolve it with a bounded `rg --files config` filename search and open only a returned literal path. One missing optional file must not be combined with authoritative state reads.

entries.mistake: The corrective bounded filename search for a separate C24 parent/current ticket state returned no matches, but the pipeline did not explicitly accept ripgrep exit code 1 and therefore surfaced as a failed tool call.
entries.rootCause: Explicit zero-match handling was applied to the Bus duplicate search but not generalized to repository filename discovery.
entries.prevention: All bounded discovery searches whose truthful result may be empty must capture ripgrep output and explicitly distinguish exit code 0, accepted exit code 1 and actual errors greater than 1. A proven zero result is recorded as zero, not retried as a failure.

entries.mistake: Immediately after REG608 was registered, the exact `/app/book` route-owner search again allowed ripgrep's truthful zero-match exit code 1 to fail the tool call.
entries.rootCause: The prevention rule had been recorded but was not applied to the very next optional exact-match search.
entries.prevention: For the remainder of C24, optional ripgrep searches are wrapped in a PowerShell result array with explicit `$LASTEXITCODE` branches before any output is emitted. Bare `rg` is permitted only where at least one match has already been proven.

entries.mistake: The first C24A verification command placed PowerShell's `-cjoin` operator after a closed array expression inside an `if`, producing a parser error before any verification ran.
entries.rootCause: The join comparison was written as though `-cjoin` were a pipeline method rather than an operator that must be contained inside the compared expression.
entries.prevention: C24 PowerShell collection comparisons assign the joined value to a ticket-specific variable using `-join` inside parentheses, then compare that scalar in a separate statement. Parser rejection authorizes no completion evidence and the original references remain untouched.

entries.mistake: The first C24B shared primitive used nonexistent `MoolRadii.md` and `MoolRadii.lg` members, so the focused test batch rejected at compilation while the three repaired C23 semantic suites passed.
entries.rootCause: Spacing-style token names were assumed for the radius owner instead of reading its literal `control`, `card`, `sheet`, `floating` and `capsule` API before authoring the new primitive.
entries.prevention: New design-system code must inventory and use literal existing token members before compilation. C24B maps compact icon corners to `MoolRadii.control` and search/primary surfaces to `MoolRadii.card`; invented token aliases are forbidden.

entries.mistake: The first inventory for the founder's new OPPO Home amendment combined bounded Home structure matches with a broad Buy/MoolSocial search; the 617-line response was truncated and cannot authorize branding-owner selection.
entries.rootCause: The already-registered category-isolation rule was not applied when the founder expanded the active Home scope to include Buy header branding.
entries.prevention: Home structure, destination launcher, Buy header, and product-copy occurrences are searched in separate tool calls with exact literal roots and capped owner-only output. Broad Buy trees and product catalogue copy are never combined with Home contract discovery.

entries.mistake: The installed r60.22 Home vertically stacks six full family rows and 17 actions in a ListView beneath a large branded header and arrival content, making the primary entry feel unprofessional and requiring vertical scrolling.
entries.rootCause: C23 optimized for direct visibility of every action by rendering every family expanded at once instead of using one fixed-viewport main-family selector with only the selected family's direct actions.
entries.prevention: The successor Home uses no vertical or horizontal scroll owner, fits six main families and only the selected family's two-to-four actions in one adaptive viewport, and proves no overflow at 320/390/430 widths and 1.4 text scale.

entries.mistake: After entering Buy or another destination in r60.22, the only route to another main family or subaction is to navigate back to the separate Home page first.
entries.rootCause: C23 changed the global shell to one launcher that navigates to Home, but did not provide an in-place connected action chooser above the current destination.
entries.prevention: The single MoolSocial launcher opens a shared connected navigator over the current destination, preserves destination state underneath, exposes all six families and the selected family's direct actions, and routes directly without an intermediate Home-page transition.

entries.mistake: The installed Home repeats MoolSocial, Home, Your Mool and 'Products, services and your place—ready when you are' and retains decorative cat/arrival content, while destination chrome labels the central launcher only 'Mool' and some top surfaces repeat MoolSocial branding.
entries.rootCause: Brand reinforcement, welcome copy and navigation identity were implemented by separate header, arrival and launcher owners without one space-budget or single-focal-brand contract.
entries.prevention: The central launcher is named MoolSocial and becomes the sole persistent brand/navigation focal point. Home removes the redundant named copy, Home icon/pill, decorative cat/arrival content and scrolling header; feature headers remove redundant MoolSocial wordmarks without altering truthful product/service copy.

entries.mistake: REG613 through REG615 initially named planned C24B1/B2/B3 test files as machine gates before those files existed, so the permanent regression-memory gate rejected the registry.
entries.rootCause: The desired future acceptance owner was recorded as if it were an already present machine-detectable prevention artifact.
entries.prevention: A regression entry may reference only literal existing files. Before focused tests exist, the entry pins the current machine-readable C24 contract and memory gate; once the test is created and passes, the registry can be strengthened to include that proven literal path.

entries.mistake: The first C24B2 scope-state transition patch guessed two literal exclusion strings with different underscore/space boundaries, so apply_patch rejected the entire scope transition atomically.
entries.rootCause: A large C24B1-to-C24B2 object rewrite was composed from remembered semantic content instead of the file's literal current source after several prior transitions.
entries.prevention: Read the complete current selected-assessment and ticket blocks immediately before a scope transition, then replace those literal blocks in one patch. Do not mix remembered projections with source context; atomic rejection authorizes no selection gate.

entries.mistake: The first shared-catalogue consolidation derived `personalMoolRootActions` from each family's first subaction and retained older private family routes, which would change Social/Buy main defaults to query routes and leave Eat/Ride/Book/Work defaults inconsistent.
entries.rootCause: Two historical route meanings—main-action default landing and old C23 main-family button route—were collapsed without first freezing which contract survives the new in-place family-selection model.
entries.prevention: The shared family `route` is the accepted personal main-action default from `personalMoolRootActions`; the compatibility projection derives from that explicit field, never from `actions.first`. C24B2 main-family taps select in place and do not consume a route.

entries.mistake: The first fixed-viewport direct-action button specified nonexistent `FontWeight.w850` before compilation.
entries.rootCause: An intermediate visual weight was chosen descriptively without checking Flutter's discrete w100-through-w900 API.
entries.prevention: C24 typography uses only literal Flutter FontWeight members and the shared contract scale; compact direct actions use `FontWeight.w800` and selected family labels use `w900`.

entries.mistake: The first private-catalogue removal deleted the private type declarations but temporarily retained their 151-line value list under a `List<Never>` placeholder, leaving unresolved constructors and an uncompilable source tail.
entries.rootCause: A large owner move was split at the type/list boundary without making the intermediate patch independently valid.
entries.prevention: Catalogue-owner moves must leave every individual patch compile-valid: add and validate the new owner, switch consumers, then remove the complete old type-and-value block atomically. Placeholder retirement lists using deleted types are forbidden.

entries.mistake: A context-light gate-array patch correctly added the new fixed-Home test to REG613 but matched REG614 as the second identical array instead of REG615, falsely implying the Home layout test prevents the still-unimplemented destination-switch regression.
entries.rootCause: Repeated JSON arrays were patched without anchoring each change to its unique regression id and acceptance meaning.
entries.prevention: Regression gate updates include the unique `id` in each patch hunk and verify the resulting id-to-gate mapping. A test is attached only to the regression behavior it directly exercises.

entries.mistake: The first C24B2 test attempt combined seven files; repeated real-router logs and eleven failures produced a 395-line truncated response, so unseen failure detail cannot guide mutation.
entries.rootCause: A broad compatibility batch was run before the new focused Home tests and each known legacy owner had passed independently.
entries.prevention: C24B2 retries one focused owner or a small related group at a time, starting with fixed Home layout, semantics, then legacy default-landing compatibility. The broader affected batch runs only after each independent failure is resolved.

entries.mistake: The C24B2 all-actions semantics test used `find.bySemanticsLabel('Social')`, which matched both the outer selected Semantics node and the visible RichText, rejecting with two candidates although the tap action was present.
entries.rootCause: A label finder was treated as an identity finder after the fixed tile intentionally rendered the same visible label as its accessibility label.
entries.prevention: Home semantic assertions find the uniquely keyed family/action widget and call `tester.getSemantics` on that owner; visible and accessibility copy may remain the same without creating ambiguous test identity.

entries.mistake: The C13 direct-default test still expected removed `mool-action-*` main buttons and translucent local-rail keys, producing ten failures after C24B2 even though those owners had already been superseded by the C23 single-launcher shell.
entries.rootCause: The compatibility test retained implementation-specific UI keys from C13 instead of following the later accepted route outcome through the current Home family-selection and direct-action interaction.
entries.prevention: C13 compatibility now proves each shared family's explicit default route and reaches it by selecting the family then tapping its first direct action. Direct `/app/eat`, `/app/ride`, `/app/book` and `/app/work` landings assert their current screen and single MoolSocial launcher, never retired local rails.

entries.mistake: The first rendered C24B2 Home candidate expanded each direct-action row to consume the full remaining panel height, placing a four-action family's rows near opposite ends of a tall card and leaving an unprofessional field of dead space.
entries.rootCause: The adaptive action panel used Expanded for both the row collection and every row, which distributed available height instead of preserving a compact content-driven action group.
entries.prevention: The selected-family surface is top-aligned and content-driven: two-to-four actions remain a compact one- or two-row group with uniform tap height and spacing, while unused viewport space stays outside the card. A permanent OPPO-class candidate capture and focused viewport test guard the composition.

entries.mistake: The first C24B3 shared chooser move introduced `MoolColors` references in the global-navigation owner without importing the theme library that declares them, producing six analyzer errors before tests.
entries.rootCause: The chooser code was moved from `personal_mool_root_v2.dart`, which already imported both design-system and theme libraries, into an owner that previously needed only the design-system import.
entries.prevention: Shared widget moves compare the source and destination import sets before compilation. The global chooser explicitly imports `mool_theme.dart`, and the affected-source analyzer remains a required gate.

entries.mistake: The first C24B3 launcher kept the former 132 px icon-and-short-label width after changing its label to `MoolSocial`, causing horizontal overflow at the default test font and all 320/390/430 adaptive cases, with larger overflow at 1.4 text scale.
entries.rootCause: The focal button's copy changed without re-budgeting intrinsic label width, icon width, inter-item gap and scaled typography.
entries.prevention: The sole brand launcher is text-only and retains a uniform 56 px capsule height while its bounded width adapts from 164 px through large text scales. Focused tests prove no overflow at 320/390/430 widths and 1.4 text scale.

entries.mistake: The first C24B3 OPPO-class chooser capture used a MaterialApp test harness with the debug banner enabled, leaving diagonal debug chrome in the top-right corner and making the image inadmissible as production visual evidence.
entries.rootCause: The functional test host relied on MaterialApp's default debugShowCheckedModeBanner value when it was reused for a permanent candidate capture.
entries.prevention: Every production candidate capture host explicitly sets `debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false`; the captured PNG is visually inspected before being cited as qualification evidence.

entries.mistake: The broad Buy screen suite retained assertions and tap journeys for removed `buy-local-tab-*`, `mool-root-selected`, `mool-root-chat` and `moolsocial-global-navigation` owners, yielding 13 failures and truncated output after the accepted C23 single-launcher shell had already stopped rendering those rails.
entries.rootCause: C23 updated focused global-navigation coverage but did not migrate the older comprehensive Buy screen suite from implementation-specific rail keys to the accepted destination session and single-launcher boundary.
entries.prevention: Buy behavior tests change Buy destination state through the session unless navigation itself is under test; connected-navigation tests use `mool-home-launcher` and `mool-navigator-buy-*`. Layout boundary assertions use the current launcher-area key. No test may require a retired rail owner.

entries.mistake: The first shared chooser placed each direct action inside a 60 px row but allowed the keyed DecoratedBox/Semantics owner to shrink-wrap to 35 px, so the effective action surface failed the 44 px tap-target gate.
entries.rootCause: A Row supplies loose cross-axis constraints; the direct-action widget did not explicitly expand to the row's height and therefore sized itself from icon/text content.
entries.prevention: The shared direct-action owner uses `SizedBox.expand` inside every one- or two-column row, making the actual semantic and visual tap surface 60 px. Home and connected-navigator tests assert every direct action is at least 44 px.

entries.mistake: The first REG630 correction patch placed a connected-navigator test assertion after the shared-source hunk without a new file marker, so apply_patch searched for test lines in the source file and rejected the entire patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: Registry, evidence, runtime and test edits were combined into one large patch and the transition from source to test owner was omitted.
entries.prevention: Cross-owner corrections use bounded patches: register/evidence first, runtime source second, focused test third. Every hunk is anchored by an explicit file marker and verified independently.

entries.mistake: The historical Buy motion batch retained one whole-screen `Flexible packs` absence assertion even though the contract concerns header copy, and one `mool-root-selected` assertion after the accepted single-launcher shell, causing two failures while 19 motion cases passed.
entries.rootCause: Later FIX14 tests narrowed promotional-copy assertions to the header owner, but FIX13 remained global; the theme-transition test was not migrated with the C23 launcher change.
entries.prevention: Header copy tests use `find.descendant` under `buy-contextual-glass-header`, and global-navigation reachability uses `mool-home-launcher`. Historical motion assertions must follow the latest accepted owner boundary without deleting truthful body copy.

entries.mistake: Four real-router continuity tests still expected tapping the global launcher to unmount Social or Buy and navigate to `personal-mool-root-v2`, then interacted with `mool-home-*` targets. C24B3 intentionally preserves the current destination and opens `mool-connected-action-navigator` instead.
entries.rootCause: The router suite encoded the C23 intermediate-Home implementation as the outcome, while the founder's C24 navigation rejection requires direct connected switching without Home.
entries.prevention: Real-router tests assert the destination remains mounted under the modal, use `mool-navigator-*` targets for direct switches, prove System Back dismisses without changing destination state, and verify no intermediate Home owner renders.

entries.mistake: The five-file Social/Eat/Ride/Book/Work batch passed 54 tests and failed two Eat/Work journeys that still expected `personal-mool-root-v2` after launcher tap and then used `mool-home-*` actions.
entries.rootCause: The feature vertical slices were written for the C23 Home detour and were not yet migrated to the C24B3 connected chooser contract.
entries.prevention: Eat and Work vertical slices assert their current destination remains mounted under `mool-connected-action-navigator`, choose `mool-navigator-eat-table` or `mool-navigator-work-workspace` directly, and never require an intermediate Home owner.

entries.mistake: Removing Social's top MoolSocial wordmark and PrototypeIdentityLine left the `journey_frame.dart` import unused, producing one analyzer warning.
entries.rootCause: The visual owner was removed without immediately reconciling the source import list.
entries.prevention: Brand-chrome removal includes an affected-source analyzer pass and deletes imports whose last consumer was removed.

entries.mistake: The targeted Screen 04 conformance test still required the C23-removed `screen04-context-tabs` owner and failed before it could assert the C24B3 top-brand removal and single launcher.
entries.rootCause: The older conformance test encoded a retired persistent Social tab rail while the current Social continuous batch already validates direct choices and the one launcher shell.
entries.prevention: The entry conformance test asserts no retired context-tabs owner, retains the current Shorts content surface and direct-route contract, proves no exact top MoolSocial semantic label, and requires one `mool-home-launcher`.

entries.mistake: The final combined C24B3 compatibility cycle exposed one C23F launcher-motion test that still required `onOpenMool` to fire after a tap, even though C24B3 intentionally opens the connected action chooser over the mounted destination.
entries.rootCause: The C23F press-feedback assertion was preserved, but its post-tap navigation expectation was not migrated with the later founder-approved no-Home-detour contract.
entries.prevention: The launcher-motion test retains finite press feedback, then proves one tap opens `mool-connected-action-navigator`, preserves the destination shell, and does not invoke the retired Home callback.

entries.mistake: The first C24C Eat recomposition used `MoolSpacing.xxxl` for two bottom insets even though the production spacing scale ends at `MoolSpacing.xxl`, causing four analyzer errors.
entries.rootCause: The new layout referenced a familiar token name without first verifying the exact shared spacing catalogue.
entries.prevention: C24 service-home layouts use only declared `MoolSpacing` tokens; affected-source analysis remains mandatory before focused widget tests.

entries.mistake: The first focused C24C adaptive test required every Scrollable below the discovery ListView to be vertical, so the search field's legitimate internal horizontal EditableText scrollable falsely failed all three viewports while the two route journeys passed.
entries.rootCause: The finder asserted a page-layout contract against all nested framework scroll owners instead of the keyed customer-facing page owner.
entries.prevention: The no-horizontal-page gate reads `scrollDirection` directly from the keyed Eat discovery `ListView`; text editing internals are outside that presentation contract.

entries.mistake: The first OPPO-class C24C render used the shared emphasized state on the Book Table card and the session's default restaurant, creating two large pale-red blocks instead of the contract's quiet light foundation with white cards and one restrained Eat accent.
entries.rootCause: A selection/emphasis state intended for a compact control was applied to full discovery cards before the customer had made an explicit choice.
entries.prevention: Eat discovery cards remain white; the family accent is limited to icons, arrows, chip outlines and the explicit table-selection check. Permanent OPPO-class captures are visually audited before ticket qualification.

entries.mistake: The first Book Table golden command printed only the last 12 lines, hiding the Flutter exception and leaving only a generic failed-test summary.
entries.rootCause: The output bound was chosen before knowing how many exception lines the new render could produce.
entries.prevention: First-run visual evidence commands retain at least the final 80 lines or full failure output; subsequent successful reruns may use a shorter summary.

entries.mistake: The first Book Table OPPO-class capture placed `Kitchen open · instant confirmation` in a compact non-flexible metadata row beside the trailing selection icon, producing a visible RenderFlex overflow stripe across the selected card.
