entries.rootCause: Sentence-length availability copy was assigned to the shared short-metadata slot, whose icon-label row is intended for compact rating, distance and price values.
entries.prevention: Sentence-length service status belongs in the wrapping card subtitle; metadata rows remain compact. Both Eat entry captures and the 320px/1.4-text test must render without exception before qualification.

entries.mistake: The first REG642 correction combined registry, two evidence documents and runtime source in one patch, but its source hunk expected a multiline metadata constructor that `dart format` had already collapsed; apply_patch rejected the entire change atomically.
entries.rootCause: The correction repeated REG631's oversized cross-owner patch pattern and did not reread the formatted source immediately before constructing the runtime hunk.
entries.prevention: Regression and evidence are recorded first; the runtime correction follows in a separate patch anchored to freshly read formatted lines, then the registry gate runs before retry.

entries.mistake: The historical C16D Eat conformance test required `eat-local-navigation`, compact-cluster geometry and local selection AnimatedContainers that C24B3 no longer renders, so both cases failed with `Bad state: No element`.
entries.rootCause: C16D encoded its then-current persistent local rail as the outcome instead of following the later founder-approved single MoolSocial connected chooser and direct action routes.
entries.prevention: C16D compatibility now opens the one MoolSocial launcher, asserts the two Eat actions in the connected chooser, routes directly to Book Table without Home, verifies System Back/dismiss continuity, 44px targets and immediate reduced-motion modal presentation.

entries.mistake: The first C24C machine gate assigned source text to `$home`; PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive, so this attempted to overwrite the protected read-only `$HOME` variable and the gate failed before validation.
entries.rootCause: The script used a short domain label without applying the repository rule that `$HOME`, `$home` and `$CODEX_HOME` must never be repurposed.
entries.prevention: PowerShell gate variables use task-specific names such as `$homeSource`; regression-memory and PSScriptAnalyzer-style source checks reject assignments to protected environment variable names.

entries.mistake: The second C24C gate run falsely reported both location owners missing because it searched for `key: const Key(...)`; inside an already-const MoolServiceCard Dart formats the arguments as `key: Key(...)`.
entries.rootCause: The static token gate encoded optional redundant Dart syntax instead of the semantic key token retained by the formatter.
entries.prevention: Machine gates match formatter-stable key tokens inside const widget invocations and pair static checks with focused widget tests that mount the actual keys.

entries.mistake: A six-file C24C compatibility batch combined intent, wording, exposure, global-motion and default-route owners before isolating their C24B3 navigation expectations; it produced 54 failures and the 100-line output window omitted most first failures.
entries.rootCause: The batch repeated REG622's broad-first pattern even though multiple historical global-navigation suites were likely to retain pre-C24 implementation keys.
entries.prevention: C24 compatibility is rerun one historical owner at a time, starting with the smallest failing plain-name case. Only independently passing owners are recombined after stale contracts are registered and migrated.

entries.mistake: Running the full universal-intent owner after REG647 still yielded five failures, while a 40-line tail retained only the last `Book Doctor Mool hub Back` failure and hid the first four diagnostics.
entries.rootCause: One file contained many independent legacy and production journeys, so file-level isolation was still too broad for first-failure diagnosis; the visible case also retained removed `mool-root-selected` and intermediate Home expectations.
entries.prevention: Universal-intent failures are isolated by exact `--plain-name`; no source or test mutation is inferred for the four unseen cases. Each diagnosed stale contract is registered before correction, then the whole owner is rerun once every case passes independently.

entries.mistake: The universal-intent Work production case still expected `/app/work` to render `mvp-action-root-work` and then used removed `work-local-*` controls; the current route lands directly on Earn Today and uses the connected MoolSocial chooser for Workspace/Earn switching.
entries.rootCause: The test encoded the pre-C23 intermediate action-root and local rail instead of the accepted direct-default route plus C24B3 connected chooser outcome.
entries.prevention: The Work intent case starts on `work-earn-screen`, switches directly through `mool-navigator-work-workspace` and `mool-navigator-work-earn`, and asserts no intermediate Home/action root.

entries.mistake: The first connected-navigation ownership search used Bash-style `{eat,ride,book,work}` path expansion in PowerShell, causing a parser error before ripgrep ran.
entries.rootCause: A cross-shell shorthand was used without translating it to PowerShell's explicit argument list.
entries.prevention: PowerShell ripgrep searches pass each workspace path as a separate quoted argument; no Bash brace expansion is used.

entries.mistake: The connected chooser could switch Earn Today to Workspace, but selecting Earn Today again invoked a global callback that pushed a route already beneath the current page, causing duplicate GoRouter page-key and root Navigator GlobalKey assertions instead of restoring Earn.
entries.rootCause: C24B3 proved one-way direct switches but did not cover cyclic A-to-B-to-A exploration. Global family switches used stack-push semantics even when the target route already existed below the current destination.
entries.prevention: Connected family/action switching uses a non-duplicating destination policy and permanent tests cycle A-to-B-to-A without Home, duplicate page keys or lost launcher state. Modal dismissal still preserves the mounted destination unchanged.

entries.mistake: The connected-navigation verification command ran from `apps/mobile` but passed `apps/mobile/...` paths to `dart format`; formatting therefore found no files even though the subsequent analyze and exact Work test passed.
entries.rootCause: The compound command mixed repository-root-relative formatter paths with a mobile-package working directory, and its final successful test masked the formatter's earlier non-zero result.
entries.prevention: Formatter paths are resolved against the declared command working directory, and formatting is run as a separately checked command before analyze/test chains so a later success cannot mask an earlier failure.

entries.mistake: A test-name ownership search embedded a double-quote branch inside a PowerShell double-quoted ripgrep regex, so PowerShell terminated the string and failed before ripgrep ran.
entries.rootCause: The regular expression was composed for regex semantics without first making its quoting safe for the active PowerShell parser.
entries.prevention: PowerShell ripgrep patterns containing literal double quotes are passed in a single-quoted PowerShell string or simplified into separate searches before execution.

entries.mistake: The universal-intent Book production case still expected `/app/book` to render `mvp-action-root-book` and used its removed Doctor and Salon choice cards, even though the accepted route lands directly on Doctor and the connected MoolSocial chooser owns cross-destination access.
entries.rootCause: The test retained the pre-C23 intermediate Book action-root contract after direct-default landing and C24B3 connected navigation became production behavior.
entries.prevention: The Book production intent case starts on `book-doctor`, confirms the removed action root is absent, and switches Doctor-to-Salon-to-Doctor through the one-tap connected chooser without Home or duplicate routing state.

entries.mistake: The universal-intent Eat production case mounted the legacy shell and tried `sub-action-eat-order-food`, a removed intermediate intent control, instead of exercising the C24C native discovery Home and its direct restaurant and Book Table outcomes.
entries.rootCause: The test name claimed production behavior while its setup deliberately enabled `legacyPresentationForTestsOnly`, so it missed the accepted direct `/app/eat/home` route and current production controls.
entries.prevention: The Eat production intent case mounts the real production route, opens Order Food from a visible restaurant card, returns to the discovery owner, opens Book Table directly, and confirms postponed Tiffin remains hidden.

entries.mistake: The universal-intent Ride production case enabled the legacy shell and used removed `sub-action-ride-*` intermediaries plus Back-to-Home cycles instead of the native direct Ride owner and connected chooser.
entries.rootCause: The test retained pre-direct-default navigation and did not cover the production requirement that Bike, Auto and Cab remain reachable from the current destination without returning Home.
entries.prevention: The Ride production intent case mounts the real direct Bike route and switches Bike-to-Auto-to-Cab with the connected MoolSocial chooser, asserting each package owner without Home or legacy subaction keys.

entries.mistake: Connected Bike-to-Auto/Cab switching replaced `/app/ride/book` with a new query while `RideBookingScreen.initState` called `prepareBooking`; that method notified the shared RideSession twice during route build and triggered `setState() or markNeedsBuild() called during build` on the outgoing AnimatedBuilder.
entries.rootCause: Ride initialization mixed synchronous state preparation with public listener notification. It was only exercised by prior Home-mediated flows, so same-owner query switching through the connected navigator exposed the overlapping lifecycle.
entries.prevention: Ride route initialization prepares and clears session state silently for the first frame, public mutations still notify exactly once, and a permanent real-router Bike-to-Auto-to-Cab test rejects build-phase notifications.

entries.mistake: A multi-file diagnostic loop let the final ripgrep invocation's expected no-match status become the whole command's failing exit code even though the required Ride ownership output had already been returned.
entries.rootCause: The read-only loop did not normalize ripgrep exit code 1 for files where the queried symbol was legitimately absent.
entries.prevention: Multi-file ownership searches either target only known owners or explicitly treat ripgrep no-match as a non-error while preserving real parser and I/O failures.

entries.mistake: The historical R06 Eat exposure owner still expected `mool-root-selected`, `mool-root-chat`, `eat-local-*`, and the removed translucent subaction rail across eight cases after C24B3 replaced the old dock with one MoolSocial connected launcher and C24C moved actions into contextual discovery content.
entries.rootCause: The suite combined a still-valid versioned action contract with presentation assertions from several superseded navigation systems and was not migrated when the accepted launcher and discovery-home owners changed.
entries.prevention: R06 retains its action-count/route contract but current UI cases assert one connected launcher, unchanged-owner modal dismissal, contextual Book Table access, no legacy rail, no Tiffin, and adaptive current production owners.

entries.mistake: The historical action-wording Fix1 owner used removed `mool-action-*`, `mool-root-selected`, and `mool-root-chat` controls in eleven tests, expected destination Back to restore Home, and therefore failed every navigation case after the accepted compact Home chooser and one connected MoolSocial launcher replaced those systems.
entries.rootCause: The durable wording projection remained current, but its route tests encoded obsolete Home cards, global dock controls, and Home-mediated return behavior that conflict with the founder-approved direct connected exploration model.
entries.prevention: Fix1 keeps the locked 6+17 wording projection, exercises every Home family/action through current `mool-home-*` keys, verifies destination chooser dismissal preserves the exact owner, and verifies Home header Chat returns to Home without reintroducing a destination dock.

entries.mistake: The first Fix1 migration used the versioned projection id `order-food` to build a Home chooser key, but the connected navigation owner deliberately uses its compact action id `order`; only the Eat Home direct-route case failed.
entries.rootCause: The migration assumed action identifiers were interchangeable across the historical projection contract and the newer connected-navigation view model even though their route/label outcomes, not internal ids, are the shared contract.
entries.prevention: Connected chooser tests use the connected owner's formatter-stable action ids and independently keep the projection test for wording/route parity instead of synthesizing one owner's keys from another owner's ids.

entries.mistake: The historical Fix2 compatibility owner produced 23 failures because it required the removed eight-item global dock, local Eat/Ride/Book/Work rails, their selected semantics, and Chat/Mool round trips through obsolete controls.
entries.rootCause: The suite's durable route and lifecycle outcomes were coupled to a superseded presentation implementation instead of being migrated when C24B3 established one connected MoolSocial launcher and C24C established contextual action entry.
entries.prevention: Fix2 retains its immutable historical contract assertions but current runtime acceptance uses one 56px launcher, adaptive connected chooser, direct destination outcomes, A-to-B-to-A dismissal continuity, reduced motion, and no legacy dock or local rail keys.

entries.mistake: The connected navigator sent Ride Bike/Auto/Cab routes through the generic global destination callback, bypassing `openRideType`, the domain owner that prevents an active trip from being silently reset or abandoned.
entries.rootCause: C24B3 unified destination routing at the shell boundary but did not delegate same-family Ride actions back through Ride's existing lifecycle guard.
entries.prevention: Connected Ride booking actions are parsed and delegated to `openRideType`; an active trip remains mounted with its exact type/trip identity and a visible notice, while inactive Ride type switches stay one tap and in place.

entries.mistake: Seven of eight historical C10E motion-containment cases required removed `moolsocial-global-navigation`, `mool-action-*`, `mool-root-selected`, and local-rail owners, so they no longer measured the accepted anchored single-launcher shell or connected destination motion.
entries.rootCause: Motion acceptance was coupled to the geometry and selected semantics of the superseded rail implementation rather than the invariant user outcome: one stable shell anchor, finite content motion behind it, exact modal dismissal, and immediate reduced motion.
entries.prevention: C10E asserts one stable MoolSocial launcher/Hero across contextual and cross-family navigation, no legacy rail owners, exact connected-chooser dismissal, immediate reduced-motion switching, and the finite 180-320ms production motion token.

entries.mistake: The first C10E migration opened the connected chooser from Eat and immediately searched for `mool-navigator-work-earn`; the chooser correctly renders only the selected Eat family's actions until Work is selected.
entries.rootCause: The migrated test skipped the explicit family-selection step even though the adaptive chooser intentionally avoids displaying all 17 actions at once.
entries.prevention: Cross-family chooser tests first tap `mool-navigator-family-*`, settle or pump according to motion mode, and only then tap that family's direct action.

entries.mistake: The first C24C closure-state read guessed two config filenames that do not exist and passed wildcard-bearing Windows path arguments directly to ripgrep, producing path errors after the selected ticket was read.
entries.rootCause: The read skipped repository filename discovery and treated shell wildcard patterns as ripgrep path expansion on Windows.
entries.prevention: Ticket/state records are discovered with `rg --files` before reading exact literal paths; content filtering is then applied to the discovered file list without wildcard path arguments.

entries.mistake: REG660 referenced a guessed `mool_home_information_architecture_c24b2_test.dart` gate path; the real durable owner is `mool_home_fixed_viewport_hub_c24b2_test.dart`, so regression-memory correctly rejected the qualification cycle.
entries.rootCause: The regression entry was written from the ticket outcome name without discovering the formatter-stable repository filename first.
entries.prevention: Every registry gate/evidence path is confirmed with `rg --files` before insertion, and regression-memory remains the first qualification gate so invalid references stop the cycle immediately.

entries.mistake: The recombined C24C qualification group passed 117 tests with three skipped captures but was marked failed because the C16D compatibility owner was supplied under a guessed `test/ui_v2/universal` directory; its actual path is directly under `test`.
entries.rootCause: The qualification manifest was composed from memory instead of resolving every test owner with `rg --files`, repeating the filename-discovery class guarded by REG667.
entries.prevention: Every test path in a recombined qualification command is discovered and existence-checked first; the corrected C16D owner is rerun alone and then included only by its exact repository path.

entries.mistake: The first C24D composition gave the payment summary card key `ride-payment-card`, duplicating the Card payment choice key, and placed all three payment chips in a service-card trailing slot that is too narrow at 320px and 1.4 text scale.
entries.rootCause: A shared title/subtitle card was used outside its bounded trailing-content contract, and the summary key was chosen without checking the existing payment-choice namespace.
entries.prevention: Payment choices remain in a full-width wrapping white surface with a unique summary key; trailing slots are limited to compact icons, prices or one 44px action, and focused tests reject duplicate keys and overflow at compact scaled viewports.

entries.mistake: The C24D focused-test inventory passed `apps/mobile/test/ui_v2/ride` directly to ripgrep before confirming that the directory existed, producing an I/O error instead of a clean inventory result.
entries.rootCause: The proposed new focused-test location was treated as an existing owner directory rather than first discovering current paths from the test root.
entries.prevention: Test-owner discovery starts at an existing parent with `rg --files`; a new bounded ticket directory is created only by the authorized patch that adds its first focused owner.

entries.mistake: The first C24D package-card composition relied on the shared card's default semantic label, which included title and capacity/note but omitted the visually shown fare, arrival time and nearby-captain availability required before booking.
entries.rootCause: Visual metadata and trailing fare were passed as separate card properties without supplying the explicit combined semantic label needed when descendant semantics are excluded for one-tap ownership.
entries.prevention: Every Ride package card supplies one explicit action label containing type, package, fare, arrival, capacity, note, availability and selected state; focused semantics tests require those facts and a tap action.

entries.mistake: The first C24D compact-viewport test expected `ride-place-home` to already exist in a vertical ListView at 320x568 and 1.4 text scale, although the intentionally lazy off-screen card had not been scrolled into the widget tree.
entries.rootCause: The assertion confused immediate construction with reachable vertical content and therefore rejected the adaptive list for behaving normally on the smallest supported viewport.
entries.prevention: Compact Ride tests first prove the primary pickup/search surface, then scroll the keyed list until the saved-place card is visible and assert its reachability, launcher continuity and absence of overflow.

entries.mistake: The first C24D saved-place test correctly proved that a real tap changed `RideSession.drop` to `Sardarpura, Jodhpur`, then falsely failed by searching for destination text while the search surface was off-screen after scrolling to the place card.
entries.rootCause: The outcome assertion checked global widget presence instead of returning to the destination owner and reading its explicit selected-destination semantics.
entries.prevention: One-tap Ride tests assert the session outcome, scroll back to the keyed destination surface, and require its semantic label to expose the newly selected destination.

entries.mistake: A compound C24D diagnostic first looked for the regression owner below the mobile working directory and then repeated the nonexistent filename `codex-development-regression-memory.json` from repository root after discovery had already revealed the actual registry filename.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed mobile-relative source inspection with repository-relative state inspection and did not substitute the exact discovered `config/codex-development-regression-registry.json` path before the retry.
entries.prevention: Regression-state reads run from repository root against the exact discovered registry path; mobile source/test diagnostics remain separate commands and no guessed memory filename is retried.

entries.mistake: After correcting the off-screen destination assertion, the test reused a forward-only `scrollUntilVisible` helper to return to an already constructed earlier search surface; its descendant-Scrollable finder became empty during the session rebuild and threw before reading the valid selected-destination semantics.
entries.rootCause: The helper was designed to discover later lazy children with a fixed positive scroll delta, not to reveal a known earlier element after a stateful list rebuild.
entries.prevention: Forward lazy discovery keeps the bounded list helper; backward verification never reuses its descendant-scrollable finder. REG676 adds the required bounded reverse reacquisition when the earlier keyed owner has been evicted.

entries.mistake: The first REG675 correction called `ensureVisible` for the earlier destination surface without proving it still existed; after scrolling to the saved-place card and rebuilding, the lazy ListView had evicted that owner, so `ensureVisible` threw `Bad state: No element`.
entries.rootCause: The correction treated an earlier logical child as a currently constructed element, overlooking that `ensureVisible` can only operate on a finder that already resolves.
entries.prevention: Backward verification performs bounded positive drags on the persistent keyed ListView until the earlier target is rebuilt, asserts exactly one target, and only then uses `ensureVisible` before reading semantics.

entries.mistake: The C24D booking CTA supplied a local `FilledButton.styleFrom(textStyle:)` without `fontFamily: 'Inter'`; the replacement ButtonStyle no longer inherited the themed family and the retained widget capture rendered its label as Ahem glyph blocks.
entries.rootCause: The local text style was treated as a partial merge even though the button style resolves it as the full state property, dropping the brand font owned by `MoolTheme.filledButtonTheme`.
entries.prevention: Any local button text-style override supplies the canonical Inter family together with size and weight; the C24D visual capture must render the complete `Book <vehicle> · <fare>` label legibly.

entries.mistake: The first C24D machine gate guessed `Ride type`, `Choose your ride`, `package.availableCaptains`, `void updateRoute(` and an Inter token inside the shared service-home primitive; current owners use `Choose a ride`, `nearbyCaptains`, `bool updateRoute(`, while the explicit local Inter fix belongs to RideBookingScreen.
entries.rootCause: The gate was drafted from conceptual acceptance wording instead of reading each exact formatter-stable declaration and its actual ownership boundary first.
entries.prevention: Machine gates bind only to exact tokens confirmed from current source: section labels and nearby-captain truth in RideBookingScreen, boolean route validation in RideSession, geometry tokens in the shared primitive, and local brand-font retention in the CTA owner.

entries.mistake: Both C16E cases required removed `ride-local-navigation`, compact-cluster and selected-indicator owners, so the suite no longer exercised the C24D contextual Ride choices or C24B3 connected MoolSocial launcher.
entries.rootCause: The historical compact-family contract remained coupled to the superseded local rail after founder rejection removed all old stripe/rail presentation.
entries.prevention: C16E now proves three contextual Bike/Auto/Cab choices inside the destination home, one-tap in-place type change, minimum targets, selected semantics, content reachability, one connected launcher, no legacy rail, and immediate reduced-motion state.

entries.mistake: The universal-intent Ride production case used the generic `tapVisible` helper for package cards and required each lazy vertical package owner to exist at first paint after a type switch.
entries.rootCause: The test was migrated to connected Bike/Auto/Cab routing before C24D introduced a destination-first vertical hierarchy, but package reachability was not given a bounded Ride-list scroll owner.
entries.prevention: Ride production intent uses a keyed bounded vertical scroll helper to construct, reveal and tap each package card after every connected type switch; other generic intent controls retain their stricter immediate-presence helper.

entries.mistake: Seven R07 Ride UI cases still required the rejected translucent family rail, `ride-local-*`, `mool-root-selected` and a Home-root round trip even though current production owns contextual vehicle choices and one connected MoolSocial chooser without returning Home.
entries.rootCause: The immutable three-action route contract was conflated with presentation owners from the rejected rail era and was not migrated when C24B3/C24D established the accepted navigation and destination-home model.
entries.prevention: R07 retains exact Bike/Auto/Cab contract projection while current UI cases switch types through the connected chooser, prove direct route/session ownership and chooser-Back continuity, and explicitly reject all removed rails and Home-root controls.

entries.mistake: The migrated C16E test registered `SemanticsHandle.dispose` with `addTearDown`; Flutter's end-of-test semantics verification ran before that teardown callback and rejected the otherwise passing case for an active handle.
entries.rootCause: Resource cleanup timing was assumed to match ordinary session teardown even though the widget-test binding requires semantics handles to be disposed before its end-of-body verification.
entries.prevention: Tests that call `ensureSemantics` wrap their assertions in `try/finally` and dispose the handle synchronously in the test body; session teardown may remain registered separately.

entries.mistake: The first REG682 registration-and-fix patch included C16E source context from before `dart format`; the formatter had compacted a multiline finder, so the compound patch was rejected and none of its registry, evidence or test changes applied.
entries.rootCause: A multi-owner patch mixed durable registration with a source edit without rereading the exact post-format file immediately before mutation.
entries.prevention: After formatting, read the literal current test before patching; apply regression registry/evidence separately from the exact source correction so one context mismatch cannot obscure either result.

entries.mistake: The first repository-wide C24D gate loop invoked PowerShell scripts and then compared `$LASTEXITCODE` with zero; after the first passing script the native-process variable was null, so the wrapper threw a false failure before running later gates.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper used the exit-status channel for native executables instead of PowerShell's success state for invoked `.ps1` scripts.
entries.prevention: PowerShell-script loops use `$?` immediately after invocation with `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'`; `$LASTEXITCODE` is inspected only for native commands that actually set it.

entries.mistake: The repository brand gate still required Buy's removed 104px MoolSocial title owner and scene-embedded identity outcome after C24B3 reduced the contextual action slot to 44px and made the connected MoolSocial launcher the only persistent destination-brand focal point.
entries.rootCause: C24B3 updated production and focused tests but did not migrate the older brand contract/source gate, so host qualification remained bound to rejected redundant destination branding.
entries.prevention: The brand contract preserves the canonical app wordmark and launcher globally while Buy-specific acceptance requires a 44x56 contextual action slot, no destination wordmark/logo tile, and the one connected MoolSocial launcher as focal point.

entries.mistake: C24B3 removed Buy's widget brand tile and MoolSocial semantics, but `_HeaderScenePainter.paint` still called `_paintPromotionalTitle` and `_paintSettledBrand`, drawing visible `Mool` and `Social` text into the header bitmap; this could make the successor look unchanged despite passing widget-tree assertions.
entries.rootCause: The cleanup audited widgets and semantics but did not inventory custom-painter text, allowing redundant visual branding to survive outside the element tree.
entries.prevention: Buy's scene painter contains no Mool/Social title or settled wordmark methods/calls; the contextual promo/safety/business action remains, and the connected bottom MoolSocial launcher is the single persistent brand-navigation focal point.

entries.mistake: The brand gate found the current `_MoolHomeLauncher` class but still required `MoolBrand.moolLauncherIcon`; founder-approved C24B3 intentionally makes the single central focal point a text-only `MoolSocial` control so destination logos and duplicate marks are unnecessary.
entries.rootCause: The gate conflated the canonical Mool service glyph retained for legacy/generic navigation meaning with the newer connected-launcher presentation contract.
entries.prevention: Brand integrity records both contracts separately: the canonical Mool glyph remains defined, while the connected launcher requires the exact `MoolSocial` label, 56px control, tap semantics and no logo/glyph inside its private owner.

entries.mistake: C24D repository qualification reached the protected Buy baseline and found 43 governed runtime files against the 31-file founder-approved R40.3 baseline; the current tree includes 12 added owners and changes across at least 10 common predecessor owners, a scope larger than the authorized redundant header-wordmark cleanup.
entries.rootCause: The durable protected baseline was never replaced after later Buy runtime evolution, so current production cannot prove that all post-R40.3 business-content changes share one founder-approved protected identity.
entries.prevention: Do not weaken, bypass or overwrite the R40.3 protection. The explicit founder follow-up authorizes a separate 43-owner successor candidate seal pending OPPO acceptance; the original baseline remains preserved and the gate binds to the exact successor portable tree.

entries.mistake: C24D repository qualification reached the protected Social/YouTube baseline and found 178 governed source/test owners against the 119-file founder-approved 2026-07-29 baseline.
entries.rootCause: The protected Social baseline predates later accepted Social/YouTube and cross-surface test evolution, so the current tree has no exact successor identity even though C24 forbids Social business-content changes.
entries.prevention: Preserve the original baseline, inventory and test the complete current protected Social/YouTube boundary, then bind a separate founder-authorized successor candidate seal pending OPPO acceptance; never weaken the root/test filters or silently bless later mutation.

entries.mistake: The first 34-file Social/YouTube test wrapper invoked Flutter inside `try/finally`; the final `Pop-Location` became the compound command's successful result, so the shell reported exit 0 despite 17 Flutter failures.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper preserved working-directory cleanup but did not capture and rethrow the native Flutter exit code before leaving the `finally` block.
entries.prevention: Grouped native test wrappers capture `$LASTEXITCODE` immediately after Flutter, always restore location, and explicitly exit/throw with the captured code after cleanup.

entries.mistake: The Social-to-Work compatibility owner still tapped removed `mool-root-selected` and Work local-rail keys to reach Earn/Workspace through Home.
entries.rootCause: The route outcome was not migrated when C24B3 established connected cross-family navigation without a Home return and C24G queued contextual Work actions.
entries.prevention: Compatibility starts on Social, opens the connected MoolSocial chooser, selects Work then Earn/Workspace directly, and proves the exact existing destination owner while all removed root/local keys remain absent.

entries.mistake: Multiple Screen04 conformance journeys required `mool-root-selected`, `mool-root-chat`, a separate `personal-mool-root-v2` visit and legacy rail visibility after the accepted one-launcher connected shell removed those owners.
entries.rootCause: The Screen04 business-content assertions were coupled to several superseded navigation presentations instead of the durable outcomes: direct connected family/action access, Chat return, exact Social substate continuity and no Home detour.
entries.prevention: Screen04 retains feed/create/watch/profile content contracts while navigation cases use the MoolSocial connected chooser and destination Chat entry, dismiss back to the exact owner, and reject legacy root/dock keys.

entries.mistake: C16B, C17C and C20D retained exact translucent local-rail geometry, 13px label, glass-container and selected-indicator assertions; current production uses contextual Social/Buy actions and one connected launcher, while the shared legacy harness itself now resolves a 12px label and no separate selected indicator.
entries.rootCause: Historical token-level component conformance was treated as current product acceptance after the founder rejected the rail/stripe design and subsequent shared-token evolution changed its internal composition.
entries.prevention: Current production conformance verifies contextual actions, 44px targets, semantics, adaptive wrapping, finite/reduced motion and legacy-rail absence. Any retained isolated compatibility harness binds only to current shared constants, never hard-coded superseded pixels or missing internal keys.

entries.mistake: The protected Screen04 operational golden rejected the current rendering after C24B3 changed shared destination chrome; the initial grouped output did not preserve enough diff detail to distinguish authorized launcher chrome from any Social business-content change.
entries.rootCause: The golden predates the connected-launcher shell and was rerun in a large batch without first capturing and inspecting its exact current/diff images.
entries.prevention: Run the operational golden alone, preserve its generated diff files, inspect every changed region, and update the golden only if the delta is limited to authorized shared chrome with Social content/layout otherwise unchanged.

entries.mistake: The C24B3 single MoolSocial launcher connected every main-action family and subaction but ignored its existing `onOpenChat` callback, leaving no global Chat entry inside the only persistent destination control.
entries.rootCause: The connected chooser was designed around `MoolDirectActionSpec` family routes only; the separate global utility contract was forwarded through `MoolDestinationNavigationV2` and `MoolGlobalNavigationV2` but never rendered or invoked.
entries.prevention: The connected chooser owns one explicit 48px Chat utility action that invokes the existing callback, dismisses the chooser before routing, and returns by system Back to the exact originating destination/substate; no second bottom button or destination header icon is introduced.

entries.mistake: After the first C16B stale-rail migration, the isolated compatibility test still hard-coded a 20px Feed icon and 20px optical box although the current shared navigation token is 18px.
entries.rootCause: The prior rejection inventory captured stale label and indicator assumptions but missed two adjacent hard-coded icon dimensions in the same historical component test.
entries.prevention: Any retained isolated navigation compatibility assertion binds label, provider and icon geometry to `MoolLocalNavigationTokens`; current product acceptance remains based on the connected launcher and absence of legacy local rails.

entries.mistake: The first connected-navigation migration used `screen04-youtube-attribution` as if it were a unique Videos owner, but the discovery list truthfully renders that attribution on three visible YouTube cards.
entries.rootCause: A repeated item-level key was selected as the Videos state witness without checking its finder cardinality.
entries.prevention: Videos state assertions accept one-or-more attribution owners while the unique Screen04 root and requested connected subaction route prove the destination state; unique-owner expectations remain limited to genuinely unique keys.

entries.mistake: The first corrected Social-suite command filtered each absolute path for `social|youtube|screen04`; every path contains the repository name `MOOLSOCIAL-PRODUCTION`, so all 223 tests were selected and Windows rejected the oversized command line.
entries.rootCause: The discovery predicate was applied to the absolute repository path instead of the path relative to `apps/mobile/test`.
entries.prevention: Protected suite discovery derives each path relative to the test root before applying Social/YouTube/Screen04 matching and prints the qualifying file count before Flutter runs.

entries.mistake: The protected Social customer-copy matrix still navigated Videos, Feed and Create through removed `screen04-rail-*` controls, so its content audit stopped after Shorts in the connected-launcher product shell.
entries.rootCause: The broader copy gate was not included in the first explicit list of historical Screen04/local-rail conformance owners even though it embedded the same superseded navigation mechanic.
entries.prevention: Copy qualification mounts each named Social subaction directly and audits the rendered customer copy independently of presentation-specific navigation; connected access is covered by the dedicated navigator and Screen04 route tests.

entries.mistake: The first C24E scope-state transition attempted one large multi-hunk replacement and failed on an exact C24D assessment sentence before changing the file.
entries.rootCause: The transition patch coupled many independently addressable JSON fields to a long context line, making the whole mutation brittle even though the intended selected-ticket values were valid.
entries.prevention: Scope-state transitions use bounded exact replacements for the assessment object, ticket object and state markers, then validate JSON and the scope gate before runtime mutation.

entries.mistake: The first C24E affected Book run found C16F and R08 still requiring the founder-rejected Book local glass rail/Mool root, while universal-intent assertions required the replaced form-first headings `Choose care` and `1. Select service`.
entries.rootCause: Historical Book exposure and intent tests encoded superseded navigation presentation and numbered form copy instead of the durable Doctor/Salon route, state and booking outcomes.
entries.prevention: Book acceptance uses the single connected MoolSocial chooser for Doctor/Salon discovery, rejects legacy rail/root owners, and asserts the new professional search/provider hierarchy while preserving all downstream booking, failure, payment, cancellation and support contracts.

entries.mistake: The C24E affected-suite retry guessed two historical test paths under `test/ui_v2/universal`; Flutter rejected both missing owners while all four correctly addressed test files passed.
entries.rootCause: The rerun command reused descriptive filenames from prior notes without resolving their current repository paths before invocation.
entries.prevention: Every affected Flutter suite is assembled from `rg --files test` results and each intended owner is proven present before Flutter is invoked; a missing path is a rejected cycle and never counts toward qualification.

entries.mistake: The first C24E focused adaptive test measured every Doctor and Salon choice immediately at 320x568 with 140% text, although later wrapped choices were not yet constructed by the vertical lazy list.
entries.rootCause: The target-size audit assumed all children of the discovery ListView were present in the initial viewport instead of proving each off-screen choice was reachable before measurement.
entries.prevention: Adaptive service-home tests scroll the keyed vertical list to each ordered target within a bound, then assert its 44px minimum. Initial presence is asserted only for genuinely above-the-fold owners.

entries.mistake: The first C24E Salon focused test guessed Facial at ₹599, while the existing BookSession truth owner sets Facial to ₹499.
entries.rootCause: The new UI assertion was written from memory without reading the exact retained price switch before binding the expected session and provider copy.
entries.prevention: Price assertions derive from the existing BookSession selection outcome and verify the same exact amount in session state, provider semantics and fixed review CTA; no reference-screen amount is imported into production truth.

entries.mistake: C24E focused qualification exposed right-edge RenderFlex overflows in Doctor and Salon provider metadata at 320x568 with 140% text; long truth labels were owned by a non-flexible horizontal Row.
entries.rootCause: The shared `_ServiceMetadata` primitive put its Text directly after the icon inside a minimum-width Row, so the Wrap could position metadata items but could not wrap text inside an item when its finite card width was smaller than the scaled label.
entries.prevention: Shared service metadata gives the label a Flexible owner with soft wrapping, retaining the icon and complete truthful copy while adapting item height. The 320px/140% Doctor and Salon matrix remains mandatory.

entries.mistake: Manual C24E capture inspection found Doctor and Salon fixed CTA labels rendered as white Ahem glyph blocks because `MoolServicePrimaryButton` repeated REG677's local ButtonStyle text-family omission.
entries.rootCause: The shared primitive introduced after REG677 still supplied a local `FilledButton.styleFrom(textStyle:)` with size and weight but without the canonical Inter family, so the permanent regression rule was not applied at the reusable owner.
entries.prevention: Every shared or local button textStyle override includes `fontFamily: 'Inter'`; C24E captures are regenerated and visually inspected for complete Doctor and Salon CTA text before the gate can pass.

entries.mistake: The first C24E machine gate required `key: const Key` for empty cards whose const parent owns `key: Key`, and required `title: 'Available today'` although Doctor selects that string through a conditional expression.
entries.rootCause: The gate encoded conceptual constness and label ownership instead of copying the formatter-stable literals from the final Doctor and Salon sources.
entries.prevention: Source gates are compared against the literal formatted owners after implementation and visual correction; const propagation and conditional expression layout are never reconstructed from memory.

entries.mistake: The first attempted full C24E Book matrix selected every relative Dart path containing `book`, which incorrectly included Retailer business-books screens and their unrelated goldens; three stale Retailer golden deltas and one Retailer compact overflow rejected the compound run.
entries.rootCause: A filename keyword was treated as a product-family boundary even though `Book` personal services and `books` business records are distinct domains in the same test tree.
entries.prevention: C24E qualification uses the explicit personal Book owner manifest: Book vertical slice, C16F, R08, C20E, action wording, universal intent and C24E focused tests. Retailer books remain visible for the later complete-suite audit but cannot be relabeled as C24E Doctor/Salon coverage.

entries.mistake: A C24E compound diagnostic again searched repository-root `scripts` from `apps/mobile`; ripgrep failed, but a later successful Dart analyzer became the process exit status and masked that first failure.
entries.rootCause: Repository gate discovery and mobile analysis were combined under one working directory with no immediate `$?` check, repeating two permanent regression rules in one diagnostic.
entries.prevention: Repository script discovery runs from the exact repository root and mobile analysis runs in a separate invocation from `apps/mobile`; every PowerShell/native step is checked immediately and an earlier failure cannot be overwritten by a later success.

entries.mistake: The first C24F preselection read guessed `uaw-personal-mvp-book-bus-home-fix7-c24f-ticket.json`; that path is absent, and the compound PowerShell diagnostic continued to print parent/scope owners instead of stopping at the rejected read.
entries.rootCause: The child outcome name was converted into a filename without inventorying config manifests by exact `ticketId`, and the inspection command did not set stop-on-error or check each read immediately.
entries.prevention: C24 child manifests are discovered by bounded `rg -l` of the exact ticketId, exactly one result is required, and each subsequent file read runs under stop-on-error before selection or mutation.

entries.mistake: C24F pre-test inventory found Book conformance manifests and journeys still enumerated only Doctor and Salon, including an explicit `only doctor and salon` production assertion and a nine-action historical family total.
entries.rootCause: Those accepted owner lists correctly described the pre-amendment Book family but were not yet migrated for the founder-authorized third Bus action.
entries.prevention: Every current Book action manifest enumerates Doctor, Salon and Bus exactly once, verifies the Bus direct route/owner and 44px semantics, and keeps Get It Done and Medicine excluded. Historical isolated rail totals remain predecessor compatibility data and are never mistaken for the current product manifest or restored product UI.

entries.mistake: The first bounded search for stale Book action counts used a complex alternation whose escaping produced an unclosed regex group, so ripgrep rejected the inventory.
entries.rootCause: Several PowerShell, JSON and Dart spellings were compressed into one fragile expression instead of searched as separate fixed strings and simple patterns.
entries.prevention: Cross-language count inventories use multiple fixed-string queries or independently validated simple regexes with explicit exit handling; a regex parse error authorizes no acceptance-owner patch.

entries.mistake: The first C24F 320x568/140% adaptive loop requested `bus-to` before the earlier `bus-swap`, then reused a forward-only scroll helper after the earlier target had been evicted; the helper failed with no element.
entries.rootCause: The target manifest did not follow the literal top-to-bottom widget order, and the above-the-fold From field was remeasured after the loop had advanced to the date section.
entries.prevention: Compact lazy-list target manifests follow exact production order. Above-the-fold geometry is measured before advancing, and a forward helper is never used for a later backward assertion.

entries.mistake: The first C24F machine gate required `contains('₹649')` and `contains('confirmed only at checkout')`, while the focused test stores both values in a truth-literal loop and calls `contains(truth)`.
entries.rootCause: The gate reconstructed the semantic assertion form instead of binding the formatter-stable literal list and the shared loop assertion actually present in the final test.
entries.prevention: Machine gates separately require the exact truth literals and `contains(truth)` when tests use a data-driven assertion loop; conceptual per-value matcher syntax is never invented.

entries.mistake: C24F qualification changed the 43-owner protected Buy aggregate tree from `a81375...` to `43f8b633...` because the protected shared journey router gained the founder-authorized `/app/book/bus` route; the prior successor seal correctly rejected the new tree.
entries.rootCause: The Buy protection boundary explicitly includes the shared journey router, so even a non-Buy Book route changes protected identity and requires a separately tested successor seal.
entries.prevention: Preserve both the founder-approved R40.3 baseline and C24B3/C24D successor seal, prove the exact shared-router-only authorized delta plus the complete Buy suite, then create a new candidate seal pending the same OPPO acceptance. Never overwrite or bypass an earlier seal.

entries.mistake: The first per-file C24F delta audit required every predecessor `RUNTIME-MANIFEST.txt` hash to contain 64 hexadecimal characters and stopped on `buy_v2_saved_products_store.dart`, whose retained line contains only 62 characters.
entries.rootCause: The prior candidate's aggregate portable tree is enforced by the gate, but its auxiliary per-file manifest was not validated for individual hash width when recorded.
entries.prevention: Treat the retained aggregate BASELINE tree as predecessor identity, report malformed auxiliary lines explicitly, and generate the C24F successor manifest mechanically with exactly 64 lowercase hex characters per file before computing its aggregate tree.

entries.mistake: The first C24F protected-Buy qualification discovered 53 files by a broad filename glob and reported 20 failures, including three Medicine golden deltas and historical local-rail, Mool-root and Screen04-key expectations. The retained C24D seal described a 76-pass/one-skip Buy matrix but did not record its exact file manifest, so the broader run could not be compared as the same qualifying suite.
entries.rootCause: A prose test total was treated as a reproducible suite definition. The broad discovery mixed durable Buy business/state tests with presentation-specific predecessor tests that had not been migrated after the founder-approved single connected MoolSocial launcher replaced local rails and destination wordmarks.
entries.prevention: Protected runtime reconciliation records an exact test-file manifest and independently runs the complete current Buy inventory. Every current test must assert durable Buy outcomes or the accepted connected launcher; obsolete rail/root/key assertions and their goldens are migrated explicitly, never silently excluded or used to overwrite accepted behavior.

entries.mistake: The complete Buy continuity run proved that selecting Eat from the connected MoolSocial chooser while Social was visible used route replacement; system Back could not restore the exact Social source and the user remained in the destination family.
entries.rootCause: Connected main-action callbacks used `context.go`, which discards the visible route even though the chooser is an in-place exploration affordance whose Back contract requires restoration of the prior main action or subaction.
entries.prevention: All six production family shells open a different connected main/subaction with push semantics, retain one-tap access without Home, and prove source restoration through real-router cycles. Home entry behavior remains separately owned and no extra user tap is introduced.

entries.mistake: The first stale-test migration changed the legacy home-delivery compact test to Buy V2 search/scanner/category keys even though that test intentionally mounts the isolated legacy presentation to protect the established delivery flow; the first V2 key was absent.
entries.rootCause: Removal of the rejected local/global rail expectations was incorrectly treated as authority to replace unrelated content-owner keys in a legacy behavioral fixture.
entries.prevention: Legacy behavioral fixtures retain their genuine basket, address, pickup and product controls while asserting only the shared shell delta: one MoolSocial launcher and no rejected local rail. V2 controls are asserted only in V2 fixtures.

entries.mistake: The first connected-router helper skipped tapping the Buy family whenever its requested destination was Buy. When invoked from Social, the chooser still showed Social actions and `mool-navigator-buy-shop` was absent.
entries.rootCause: The helper compared the requested family with a hard-coded destination name rather than the chooser's actual initial family context.
entries.prevention: Cross-family helpers always select the requested visible family button before resolving its action. Selecting an already-current family is an idempotent no-op and avoids hidden initial-state assumptions.

entries.mistake: The first post-Buy gate loop invoked PowerShell scripts and then compared `$LASTEXITCODE` with zero. The script produced a passing result but did not own a native-process exit code, so the null/stale value caused the loop to exit successfully after only C24F and skip the remaining gates.
entries.rootCause: Native-process exit state was used for PowerShell script invocation instead of immediate PowerShell success/exception semantics.
entries.prevention: PowerShell gate loops run under stop-on-error and test `$?` immediately after each script, or invoke scripts separately. Every expected gate name and result must appear before the compound cycle qualifies.

entries.mistake: C24F qualification changed the protected Social tree from `ff69d6...` to `beac95...` because the shared router gained the authorized Bus route and Social connected-action switching gained history-preserving Back behavior; the existing Social seal correctly rejected the new identity.
entries.rootCause: The Social protection boundary includes the shared journey router and Social consumer, so both cross-family C24F changes require the complete protected Social suite and a separate successor candidate seal.
entries.prevention: Preserve every predecessor Social seal, prove the exact authorized delta plus the complete Social/YouTube matrix, then create a new candidate seal pending the same OPPO acceptance. Never overwrite, bypass or relabel the earlier accepted evidence.

entries.mistake: The initial Social material-gate record attributed the aggregate delta partly to `journey_router.dart` and the Bus route, but the Social gate does not include that router. Exact 178-line manifest comparison proved one changed owner only: `social_v2_consumer.dart` from `e3e0ca...` to `10cdf9...`.
entries.rootCause: The protected boundary was inferred from the Buy gate and task context instead of reading the exact Social gate inventory before writing the rejection cause.
entries.prevention: Every protected-tree rejection is followed by exact gate-source inventory and per-file predecessor comparison before causal attribution. The Social successor is authorized only for the one proven history-preserving consumer delta and the full protected matrix.

entries.mistake: The first protected Social test command applied the `(social|youtube|screen04)` regex to each absolute path. Every path contains the repository folder `MOOLSOCIAL-PRODUCTION`, so 225 Dart tests were selected and Flutter rejected the overlong command line before running any test.
entries.rootCause: The qualifying name predicate was evaluated against an ancestor-bearing absolute path rather than the test-relative path used by the protection gate.
entries.prevention: Protected Social discovery computes each path relative to `apps/mobile/test` before applying the name regex, proves the exact 34-file count, and only then invokes Flutter.

entries.mistake: The first Back-restoration fix used `push` for every connected action. Repeated Social subaction changes pushed multiple locations owned by the same GoRoute path, triggered duplicate Navigator page-key assertions, and cascaded into 16 failures in the Screen04 conformance file.
entries.rootCause: Cross-family history preservation and same-family state replacement were treated as one navigation operation even though GoRouter reuses the same route-owned page key for query-only subaction variants.
entries.prevention: Connected navigation pushes only when crossing family boundaries. Within the active family it uses push-replacement semantics, preserving the cross-family source below the current page while preventing duplicate same-route keys. Real Social-to-Eat Back and repeated same-family cycles are both mandatory.

entries.mistake: After same-family replacement was introduced, the full real-router sequence still failed when it returned to the exact earlier `/app/social?sub=shorts` URI. `moolMainDestinationPage` explicitly keyed pages by URI, so two separate history entries received the same Navigator page key.
entries.rootCause: The custom `ValueKey('moolsocial-main:${state.uri}')` encoded destination identity but not navigation-entry identity. An exact destination revisit in retained history is valid and therefore cannot use the URI alone as a page key.
entries.prevention: Main destination pages use GoRouter's navigation-entry page key while route/state truth remains in the URI and sessions. Qualification cycles across all families, revisits the exact Social URI, then proves Back restoration without duplicate keys or stale owners.

entries.mistake: The first successor-manifest apply_patch used paths relative to the production repository even though the patch tool was rooted one directory higher at C:\GUARANTEED OUTCOME, creating four new evidence files outside MOOLSOCIAL-PRODUCTION.
entries.rootCause: The shell working directory and apply_patch root were assumed to be identical even though apply_patch resolves from the turn workspace root.
entries.prevention: Every production-repository apply_patch path is explicitly prefixed with MOOLSOCIAL-PRODUCTION/ and the exact repository target plus absence of a workspace-level duplicate are verified before the next mutation.

entries.mistake: The first post-seal aggregate command guessed ticket-derived repository gate filenames and stopped at the absent check-uaw-personal-mvp-book-bus-booking-fix7-c24f.ps1.
entries.rootCause: Known gate purposes were translated into assumed filenames instead of using the literal saved script inventory.
entries.prevention: Before any aggregate gate cycle, inventory scripts with rg --files and invoke only exact returned paths; every expected result must be present before the cycle qualifies.

entries.mistake: The first C24G shared-service comparison guessed a doctor_booking_screen.dart owner that does not exist, while the compound read continued to print other valid files.
entries.rootCause: A semantic screen name was converted into an assumed filename instead of inventorying the literal Book screen directory.
entries.prevention: Every cross-family source comparison starts with rg --files on the exact feature directory and opens only literal returned owners; compound output never masks a missing-path failure.

entries.mistake: The first My Work refactor patch had a malformed concatenated JavaScript string and failed with Unexpected token return before apply_patch ran.
entries.rootCause: A large generated patch mixed code-shaped replacement text with manual JavaScript concatenation, making one missing string operator hard to see.
entries.prevention: Large owner refactors are split into bounded literal apply_patch calls against freshly read source context; generated JavaScript patch strings remain short and syntactically auditable.

entries.mistake: The first C24G format command ran from apps/mobile with repository-root-prefixed paths; dart format found no files, and the later successful analyzer masked that failure in the compound exit code.
entries.rootCause: Formatter paths were not resolved against the command working directory and separate tool outcomes were inferred from only the final process status.
entries.prevention: Formatter and analyzer use literal paths relative to their actual working directory and are invoked independently; both outputs must explicitly qualify.

entries.mistake: The first focused C24G test passed a latency parameter to ReviewWorkGateway even though the Work gateway owns a zero-argument constructor.
entries.rootCause: A common zero-latency test-fixture pattern was copied from other feature gateways without reading the exact Work constructor.
entries.prevention: Focused fixtures use the literal constructor already proven by the feature vertical slice; gateway parameters are inventoried from the exact owner and never inferred across features.

entries.mistake: The first C24G semantics checks read the stable keyed wrapper around each primary action and expected that noninteractive wrapper itself to own SemanticsAction.tap.
entries.rootCause: The stable layout/scroll key and the descendant FilledButton semantic owner were treated as the same render-semantics node.
entries.prevention: Size and scroll assertions use the stable parent key, while tap-semantics assertions address the literal descendant FilledButton; both owners are proven separately.

entries.mistake: The first C24G Earn capture placed a large explanatory card before search, repeating opportunity truth and pushing the first review action below the OPPO-class viewport.
entries.rootCause: A design-system card was added to demonstrate the new hierarchy even though the app bar and opportunity cards already communicated the same decision standard.
entries.prevention: Earn Today begins with search, adaptive filters and truthful matches; no explanatory, promotional or aggregate panel may precede the customer decision flow. OPPO-class captures must be manually inspected before the gate is sealed.

entries.mistake: After REG731, a verification command from apps/mobile again used an apps/mobile-prefixed Get-Content path; the read failed and a later successful formatter masked it with final exit zero.
entries.rootCause: The command was assembled with mixed repository-root and mobile-root path conventions, and independent outcomes were still combined.
entries.prevention: Commands from apps/mobile use only lib/... and test/... paths; read, format and analyze operations run separately so no later process can mask an earlier failure.

entries.mistake: The first 20-file affected Work suite reported 155 passes, 2 retained capture skips and 34 failures; C16G required the removed local rail and Journey01 required the superseded intermediate Home section and local-root round trip.
entries.rootCause: Historical presentation contracts remained mixed with durable Work business and recovery journeys after the one-launcher connected shell replaced local rails and intermediate Home navigation.
entries.prevention: Inventory every failing owner, retain all business/state/recovery assertions, and migrate only superseded presentation steps to the connected MoolSocial chooser. The exact affected Work manifest and final totals are recorded before C24G closes.

entries.mistake: A repository-root owner-key search used apps/mobile/lib together with the mobile-relative test alias; ripgrep returned partial matches plus a missing test path.
entries.rootCause: Repository-root and apps/mobile-root path conventions were mixed in one inventory command despite the earlier CWD regressions.
entries.prevention: Repository-root inventory uses apps/mobile/lib and apps/mobile/test only; mobile-root inventory uses lib and test only. A command with any missing search root is rejected regardless of useful partial matches.

entries.mistake: The initial C11 connected-chooser rewrite used nonexistent screen04-feed-list and buy-v2-root source-owner keys.
entries.rootCause: Semantic source descriptions were translated into new-looking keys instead of reusing literal current keys from the protected Social and Buy matrices.
entries.prevention: Cross-family compatibility rewrites inventory each production owner key from current source or a passing protected matrix before the first test run.

entries.mistake: A Ride owner-key inventory command named an inferred C16F test path that does not exist; ripgrep returned useful partial matches but correctly failed the command.
entries.rootCause: The test filename was derived from ticket naming instead of being selected from the repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files to resolve every optional historical test filename before passing it to a content search, and reject an inventory command when any named input is missing.

entries.mistake: The first Journey01 migration replaced the retired section-work assertion with work-earn-screen by inference, but the protected setup/sign-in harness follows a distinct legacy-presentation recovery path and did not expose that owner.
entries.rootCause: A passing direct signed-in /app/work mount was treated as proof for a protected pre-authentication deep-link journey with different router state and a test-only legacy-presentation flag.
entries.prevention: Inspect the protected redirect route builder and its actual completion owner before changing the assertion; keep the returnTo clearance proof and never borrow owner keys from a different startup state.

entries.mistake: The first Journey01 migration assumed the universal search-result-ride tap opened ride-booking-screen, but that legacy test harness completes the search intent inside its owned universal result surface.
entries.rootCause: A search result label was interpreted as a canonical connected-navigation route without inspecting its bound tap handler and active presentation mode.
entries.prevention: Trace the exact search result callback and assert the resulting owned intent state. Use the connected launcher only after reaching a destination that actually owns it.

entries.mistake: After reaching the legacy Ride action root, the migrated Journey01 test inferred that the connected Social Shorts action would expose mvp-action-root-social; that owner was absent.
entries.rootCause: The selected connected action route and its higher-priority Social route builder were not traced before choosing the destination key.
entries.prevention: Read the literal connected action route and the exact matching router branch, then reuse a current passing owner key from that branch before retrying the Journey01 assertion.

entries.mistake: A three-hunk registry patch matched the repeated active_material_gate_rejected value without unique regression-ID context, prematurely marked REG736 resolved and left REG742 active.
entries.rootCause: The patch targeted a repeated status literal instead of anchoring each edit inside its exact immutable regression ID block.
entries.prevention: Every registry status mutation includes the exact regression ID and current status in the same patch hunk, followed by a parsed ID-to-status verification before any gate decision.

entries.mistake: The first C24H scope-state patch wrote an explicit-exclusion identifier with an accidental space before skipped_material_gate.
entries.rootCause: A prose phrase was edited directly inside a machine-readable identifier list without validating underscore-only identifier form.
entries.prevention: Machine-readable scope identifiers use lowercase underscore-delimited tokens only and are searched for whitespace before qualification fingerprints are sealed.

entries.mistake: A C24H evidence search passed Windows path strings containing filename wildcards directly to ripgrep, which rejected them as invalid path syntax.
entries.rootCause: Shell-style glob expansion was assumed for ripgrep input paths on PowerShell/Windows.
entries.prevention: Search the real containing directory and express filename selection with rg -g patterns, or resolve files first with rg --files.

entries.mistake: The first C24H aggregate gate rejected the valid maximum text scale 1.4 because it cast the JSON value to integer before comparing it with 1.4 inside a combined assertion.
entries.rootCause: Minimum tap size and maximum text scale were treated as the same numeric type even though one is integral and the other is fractional.
entries.prevention: Gate tap sizes as integers and text scales as doubles in separately named checks, and report the exact rejected value rather than one combined drift message.

entries.mistake: The C24H aggregate gate assigned Home-screen source text to $home, which aliases PowerShell's read-only $HOME variable and stopped execution before product checks.
entries.rootCause: A concise domain name was chosen without accounting for PowerShell's case-insensitive reserved automatic variables or the workspace rule prohibiting $HOME/$home reuse.
entries.prevention: Use task-specific variable names such as $homeSource and scan new PowerShell scripts for $HOME or $home assignments before first execution.

entries.mistake: The first C24H cycle command stopped before fingerprinting because the qualifier assigned the host-qualification contract to $host, which aliases PowerShell's read-only $Host automatic variable.
entries.rootCause: The new scripts were scanned only for the previously observed HOME collision instead of all common read-only automatic variables.
entries.prevention: Use $hostContract for qualification data and scan assignment names in every new PowerShell script against HOME, Host, PID, PSVersionTable and other automatic variables before execution.

entries.mistake: The first substantive C24H cycle passed formatting, complete analysis and 888 tests with 35 retained skips, then rejected before its first gate because the wrapper call splatted -RepositoryRoot and its value as separate positional arguments.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper's object[] Arguments parameter was invoked with array splatting at the call site instead of binding the array explicitly to -Arguments.
entries.prevention: Invoke every wrapper call with named -RelativePath and bind optional tokens through -Arguments @(...); preserve this cycle as rejected and require two new complete unchanged-source cycles.

entries.mistake: The first C24H gate inventory included C24C through C24G child gates even though those gates correctly require their own ticket to be the currently selected scope; C24C rejected under selected C24H during preflight.
entries.rootCause: Child focused test coverage was conflated with replaying historical ticket-selection gates whose identity assertions are intentionally phase-specific.
entries.prevention: C24H runs every child focused test, but only cumulative/permanent gates whose contract is valid under selected C24H. Historical child-selection gates remain preserved and are not weakened or invoked out of phase.

entries.mistake: The first C24H child-gate inventory correction patch contained an empty hunk boundary before the next file update, so apply_patch rejected the entire mutation.
entries.rootCause: Multiple file edits were assembled into one patch without validating that every @@ hunk contained only valid context/add/remove lines.
entries.prevention: Split contract, qualifier and registry/document corrections into bounded patches and never leave a standalone @@ marker between file updates.

entries.mistake: C24H preflight invoked the placement regression gate with -RequireImplemented, whose source-string assertions are still bound to the superseded C23 launcher implementation and reject the current C24 connected navigator.
entries.rootCause: The durable placement contract/state check was conflated with an implementation-mode snapshot from an earlier navigation generation.
entries.prevention: C24H uses the placement gate's state validation without the stale C23 implementation switch, while the C24H aggregate gate owns exact current fixed-Home and connected-navigator source checks.

entries.mistake: C24H preflight invoked check-apk-regression-gate-state.ps1 without its mandatory candidate ID, build name, build number, mode, fingerprint and runtime define parameters, which cannot exist while C24H build authority is closed.
entries.rootCause: A candidate-registration gate was misclassified as a read-only predecessor-state gate.
entries.prevention: C24H validates the exact r60.22 identity and closed successor authorities in its aggregate gate; the candidate-specific APK gate remains reserved for the single authorized C24I build.

entries.mistake: The restarted C24H cycle again passed format, complete analysis and 888 tests with 35 skips, then rejected because array-splatted strings beginning with hyphens were still treated positionally by the invoked gate script.
entries.rootCause: The call site bound the token array to -Arguments correctly, but the wrapper itself used array splatting where dynamic named PowerShell parameters require hashtable splatting.
entries.prevention: Represent gate parameters as a hashtable and splat that hashtable into each script. Add and pass a gate-only qualifier preflight before any further full cycle.

entries.mistake: The gate-only preflight passed the aggregate gate but the wrapper treated null LASTEXITCODE from a successful PowerShell script as nonzero failure.
entries.rootCause: External-process exit-code semantics were applied to PowerShell scripts, whose failures already propagate as terminating exceptions under ErrorActionPreference Stop.
entries.prevention: Do not inspect LASTEXITCODE after invoking repository PowerShell gates; rely on terminating errors or host exit, and reserve LASTEXITCODE checks for native executables such as dart and flutter.

entries.mistake: The read-only C24I OPPO readiness audit called Trim on the result of an optional mInteractive power-dump match, producing a non-terminating null-value error even though the required wakefulness signal was captured.
entries.rootCause: The audit parser assumed every Android build exposes the optional mInteractive field in dumpsys power.
entries.prevention: Treat optional dumpsys fields as nullable and derive device readiness only from explicitly present, recorded fields; power-audit retries must use null-safe selection without method calls on missing matches.

entries.mistake: After listing the exact C23H artifact files, the audit still requested three inferred filenames instead of the listed build-validation and preinstall-validation owners, causing avoidable file-not-found errors.
entries.rootCause: The follow-on read reused conceptual evidence labels rather than binding to the authoritative directory listing returned in the same command.
entries.prevention: Artifact workflow reads must use exact enumerated filenames; do not translate conceptual build/install stages into guessed path names.

entries.mistake: The initial C24I compact dirty audit repeated REG598 by forcing `--untracked-files=all`, producing filename-too-long warnings and an inadmissible 52,961-entry inventory.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor summary described a full dirty-state reconciliation, and the audit incorrectly interpreted full scope as recursive enumeration of every retained untracked evidence leaf despite the permanent path-safe owner-level rule.
entries.prevention: C24I seals the full workspace state with default path-safe `git status --porcelain=v1`: all tracked changes plus every untracked owner, warning-free, sorted and LF-hashed. The rejected deep inventory and its hash are never admitted to build evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C24I omission audit appended the nonexistent `apps/mobile/test/features` root to an otherwise valid bounded ripgrep query; the downstream Select-Object pipeline masked ripgrep's path error with an overall zero exit.
entries.rootCause: A conventional Flutter test directory was inferred instead of selecting only repository-enumerated roots, and the native command exit was not captured before piping its output.
entries.prevention: Omission audits use only exact inventoried paths under `apps/mobile/test/ui_v2`; when native output is piped, capture and validate the native exit code immediately before downstream formatting.

entries.mistake: The corrected C24I omission audit repeated REG747 by assigning source text to `$home`, PowerShell's case-insensitive read-only HOME variable. The non-terminating assignment error left the environment path in place and made downstream forbidden-token results inadmissible.
entries.rootCause: A domain-convenient variable name was used despite the permanent ban on `$HOME`/`$home`, and ErrorActionPreference was not set to Stop in the audit snippet.
entries.prevention: Use task-specific variable names such as `$homeSourceText`, set ErrorActionPreference to Stop, and reject all output from any compound audit that emits an error record even when the process exit is zero.

entries.mistake: The first C24I fixed-Home evidence setup attempted to start the supported HTTPS app route through a compound ADB command, but the host command policy rejected the command before execution.
entries.rootCause: A deep-link setup path was chosen even though the acceptance journey requires visible in-app navigation and the shell policy did not admit the compound external-URI command form.
entries.prevention: Reach Home through installed-app visible controls and verified clickable Android nodes. Do not retry the rejected deep-link command or use a coordinate-only bypass.

entries.mistake: After tapping the verified Android-launcher MoolSocial icon, the journey assumed the relaunched app would expose the prior Social profile control. The fresh hierarchy contained no such clickable node, so execution stopped before the proposed profile tap.
entries.rootCause: Persisted/top-level app routing was inferred from the pre-exit screen instead of inspecting and classifying the actual relaunched hierarchy first.
entries.prevention: After every launch, Back or route transition, dump and classify the current hierarchy before selecting a visible control. Coordinates may be used only from the same verified hierarchy and owner state.

entries.mistake: After tapping the verified profile-sheet Close node, the journey assumed the Social launcher would be present after a fixed 800 ms delay. The next hierarchy had no matching clickable launcher, so execution stopped before any chooser or Buy tap.
entries.rootCause: A fixed delay was treated as transition readiness instead of polling for one stable, classified accessibility owner within the finite production-motion budget plus device instrumentation latency.
entries.prevention: After modal dismissal or route motion, poll bounded fresh hierarchies for the expected unique clickable owner and stop on timeout. Never chain a subsequent tap from an unclassified transition frame.
