entries.mistake: The first reusable Android-bounds center helper added regex capture strings before integer conversion, concatenating values such as `596` and `692` and producing an off-screen coordinate. The profile sheet therefore remained open.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell string addition occurred inside the arithmetic expression; the final cast was applied only after concatenation/division.
entries.prevention: Convert each captured bound to an integer before addition, assert the computed center lies inside both the node bounds and the 720x1442 display, then tap only that verified center and confirm the expected hierarchy transition.

entries.mistake: After tapping Buy from the Social-selected connected navigator, the hierarchy remained in the overlay with Buy selected and its four direct actions visible. The resulting screenshot/XML were incorrectly named `22-buy-main` before that state was classified.
entries.rootCause: The family tap was assumed to route to the main destination instead of first selecting the cross-family action set in the connected navigator.
entries.prevention: Classify every post-tap hierarchy before naming evidence. Preserve the mislabeled files as rejected evidence, capture a correctly named Buy-selected state, and derive the next tap from that verified hierarchy.

entries.mistake: On installed r60.23, selecting Eat from Chat opened the connected navigator with Eat, Order Food and Book Table visible, but `Open Chat` was absent from both the screenshot and the Android accessibility hierarchy. The non-scroll panel consumed the remaining viewport and did not expose the required global Chat action.
entries.rootCause: The connected navigator's fixed-height family grid and selected-family action region were composed above Chat without a device-proven adaptive height allocation that guarantees the trailing global action remains inside every OPPO-class safe viewport.
entries.prevention: A successor must reserve a fixed reachable 48 px Chat action inside the safe viewport for every family/action count and text scale, keep all family/direct actions reachable without horizontal strips or coordinate bypasses, add focused layout/semantics tests for Social, Buy, Eat, Ride, Book and Work, pass two unchanged-source host cycles, and prove Android `clickable=true` for Chat in every selected family before installation acceptance.

entries.mistake: REG766 placed the descriptive identifier `device_OPPO_CPH2375_connected_navigator_matrix` in the registry `gates` array, but the permanent-memory validator requires every gate entry to resolve to an existing repository path.
entries.rootCause: A conceptual device gate label was conflated with the registry's path-backed gate-owner field.
entries.prevention: Registry gate entries must be literal existing repository files; descriptive device conditions belong in appliesTo, mistake/prevention text and evidence documents. Validate permanent memory immediately after adding every device rejection.

entries.mistake: The first C25 governing-state audit requested two inferred config filenames for the personal action projection and subaction placement records; neither path existed, so those reads were rejected before ticket selection.
entries.rootCause: Conceptual record names from prior gate output were translated into plausible filenames instead of binding follow-on reads to a fresh repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Inventory exact config paths with rg --files before reading action-projection or placement state. Bind every later read and ticket dependency to an enumerated path and never retry guessed variants.

entries.mistake: The first exact-path C25 governing-file read completed its shell calls but attempted to extract a nonexistent output property from each returned tool payload, emitting only undefined markers and no admissible file content.
entries.rootCause: The orchestration wrapper assumed a nested shell-result shape without validating the actual return type used by the execution composer.
entries.prevention: Forward complete shell results directly with text(), or issue a single bounded shell read whose stdout is returned without manual property extraction. A file is not considered read when the transcript lacks its full content.

entries.mistake: The first C25 reuse audit repeated the established unbounded-search failure by searching Medicine and Bus across broad documentation and source roots in one aggregate call. The 706-line output was truncated and cannot serve as complete duplicate-search evidence.
entries.rootCause: A bounded runtime-owner query was combined with historical documentation inventory even though the durable C24 rejection already requires separate narrow searches by owner class and feature.
entries.prevention: Limit C25 duplicate searches to exact runtime, test, config or gate-owner roots one concern at a time. Record only concise matched file lists or counted summaries; never aggregate verbose historical documentation matches into implementation evidence.

entries.mistake: The C25 scope-gate audit passed two inferred delivery-lock and preselection checker paths to ripgrep; those script files do not exist, so the combined command exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: Config record names were mechanically converted into checker filenames without first enumerating the repository's actual script owners.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files scripts and filter the returned inventory before reading or invoking any delivery, scope or preselection gate. Never infer a checker path from a config filename.

entries.mistake: The first C25A selection assessment used the disposition value test_only because the human checkpoint describes test-only acceptance, but the active delivery checker rejected that value as unsupported.
entries.rootCause: The assessment was authored from the checkpoint narrative without first binding its enum value to the machine checker's exact accepted implementation-disposition vocabulary.
entries.prevention: Inspect the active delivery checker for its literal allowed disposition set before sealing a successor manifest or scope assessment. Recalculate every manifest hash after correcting a hashed manifest.

entries.mistake: The first C25B focused test imported the shared navigation owner from a guessed package name, moolsocial_mobile. Flutter could not resolve that package, so the test failed at compilation before executing assertions.
entries.rootCause: A repository/product-derived Dart package identifier was assumed without reading the mobile pubspec or copying an existing test import.
entries.prevention: Before adding a Dart package import, read the exact pubspec name or reuse an existing adjacent test import. Register and correct compilation failures before rerunning any focused test.

entries.mistake: The post-rejection regression gate was invoked as a repository-root relative scripts path while the shell working directory was apps/mobile, so PowerShell could not find the gate and the compound audit stopped before reading the pubspec.
entries.rootCause: Flutter test working-directory context was carried into a repository gate call without rebasing the relative path or switching back to the repository root.
entries.prevention: Invoke repository scripts only with the repository root as workdir or an explicit verified absolute path. Keep mobile Flutter commands and repository gate commands in separate calls with deliberate working directories.

entries.mistake: The first C25C popup replacement inserted the new main-only body but left the tail of the old family/subaction/Chat body after the new class closing brace, and passed initialFamilyId to a widget that names the property selectedFamilyId.
entries.rootCause: A large context patch replaced only the leading portion of the old widget body rather than sealing the exact class bounds, and the new call site reused the predecessor parameter name.
entries.prevention: After replacing a large Dart class body, inspect the complete class-to-next-class boundary before formatting. Remove the exact predecessor tail and bind named arguments to the new constructor before compilation.

entries.mistake: The first compiled C25C popup overflowed its header row by 69 logical pixels at the required 320 px viewport and 140 percent text scale, although the six main controls and direct selection logic mounted.
entries.rootCause: The header placed an unconstrained MoolSocial Text beside its icon inside a nested Row; the outer Expanded constrained the row but the inner text did not ellipsize or scale down.
entries.prevention: Constrain the brand text with Flexible or Expanded, one line and ellipsis or scale-down while preserving the independent 44 px Close target. Keep 320 px at 140 percent in the focused widget gate.

entries.mistake: The first C25E Travel/Bus patch was rejected because its Previous/Next context matched the pre-format Ride source rather than the currently formatted file.
entries.rootCause: A multi-hunk patch was composed from an earlier transcript after dart format had mechanically changed line wrapping in the same block.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current bounded Ride blocks after formatting, then patch smaller independently anchored hunks. A failed patch makes no runtime change and must not be retried from stale transcript context.

entries.mistake: The first C25E predecessor regression run combined six large vertical-slice files. Thirteen presentation assertions failed and the 511-line output was truncated, so the aggregate cannot prove the complete failure inventory or authorize broad test edits.
entries.rootCause: Business-journey suites with verbose startup output were grouped before their predecessor navigation assertions had been reconciled to C25, exceeding the bounded evidence envelope.
entries.prevention: Rerun each affected test file separately and capture its complete failure set. Migrate only exact rejected-navigation assertions, preserve all business-outcome assertions, then rerun each file independently before a bounded combined cycle.

entries.mistake: Existing Buy, Eat, Ride, Book, Work and Social tests still required the removed 164x56 mool-home-launcher, direct Home subaction keys or predecessor rail visibility, so they rejected the founder-approved compact launcher and main-only Home despite business journeys continuing.
entries.rootCause: C25 runtime composition was implemented before the exact presentation-only assertions in the protected journey suites were migrated to the new keys and tap sequence.
entries.prevention: Inventory failures one file at a time. Replace only predecessor navigation keys and two-stage Home subaction taps with compact MoolSocial plus direct domain or local-rail taps; retain every cart, session, payment, provider, recovery and Back assertion unchanged.

entries.mistake: The Buy test-migration verification used a plain ripgrep command to prove removed predecessor keys were absent. Ripgrep correctly returned exit code 1 for no matches, but the shell call was reported as a failed script instead of an explicit passing negative assertion.
entries.rootCause: Expected no-match semantics were not wrapped in an explicit conditional that distinguishes ripgrep exit 1 from a command error.
entries.prevention: For absence checks, capture ripgrep output and exit code explicitly: exit 0 is a rejected match, exit 1 is a pass, and any other exit is an error. Do not use a bare negative ripgrep as qualifying evidence.

entries.mistake: The corrected Eat file was formatted and tested in one PowerShell command separated by a semicolon, contrary to the workspace command-output discipline requiring separate focused invocations.
entries.rootCause: A short mechanical formatter step and its test retry were combined for convenience instead of preserving one explicit command purpose per shell call.
entries.prevention: Run formatting and tests as separate shell calls. Never chain repository commands with semicolons or other separators, even when both commands are non-destructive and pass.

entries.mistake: The first exact-file search for _BuyHeader( returned an unusable output-truncation response instead of bounded symbol locations, so it could not serve as current source evidence.
entries.rootCause: The tool response failed to preserve the expected tiny result, and no explicit match cap had been supplied as a defensive bound.
entries.prevention: Retry exact-file symbol searches with an explicit match cap and then read only bounded current source blocks. Never mutate from a truncated or otherwise unusable search response.

entries.mistake: The predecessor Social header returned an empty widget on immersive surfaces at 650 logical pixels or less, which would remove the newly standardized one-tap Chat action on compact-height devices.
entries.rootCause: Immersive space recovery was implemented by removing the complete header rather than preserving a compact utility row with global reachability controls.
entries.prevention: Keep the Social compact action row mounted at every supported height; reduce padding for immersive content but never remove Chat or established global header utilities. Gate the 44px target at a compact-height viewport.

entries.mistake: A bare exact ripgrep search was used to validate a proposed work-page key. No such key exists, so the expected exit code 1 was again surfaced as a command failure despite the active REG-20260809-780 prevention rule.
entries.rootCause: The proposed assertion key was checked with a plain search instead of an explicit three-way exit-code wrapper, repeating the already registered negative-search mistake.
entries.prevention: Do not use the nonexistent key; prove Work restoration through its established local controls. Wrap all expected no-match searches so exit 1 passes, exit 0 rejects, and other exits error.

entries.mistake: Three repository record reads were issued in one PowerShell command separated by semicolons, repeating the active command-chaining prevention rule.
entries.rootCause: Related read-only inputs were grouped for convenience instead of retaining one explicit command purpose per shell call.
entries.prevention: Issue each repository record read or gate as its own shell call. Do not use semicolons or other command separators even for read-only operations.

entries.mistake: The C25F selection audit attempted to read the inferred path config/mvp-scope-manifest.json, which does not exist.
entries.rootCause: A generic scope-manifest filename was guessed instead of following the exact selected ticket manifestPath stored in the active scope-gate record.
entries.prevention: Use the scope-gate state’s exact manifestPath or enumerate config files before reading. The selected ticket JSON is the sealed manifest; do not infer a generic manifest path.

entries.mistake: The first C25F shortcut test required an exact 44x44 rendered Chat target, but Material AppBar correctly expanded the interactive slot to 48x48 and the compliant control was rejected.
entries.rootCause: The acceptance minimum was encoded as equality rather than a lower bound, ignoring platform-provided target expansion.
entries.prevention: Assert both target dimensions are greater than or equal to 44 logical pixels. Never reject a larger platform-compliant interactive target unless it causes a separately proven layout defect.

entries.mistake: The first real-route Chat test requested tap semantics from the keyed Social styling wrapper rather than its descendant IconButton, so it reported no SemanticsAction.tap despite a functional button.
entries.rootCause: A shared assertion assumed every family placed its key on the semantic control itself; Social places the key on the composite Stack that owns its visual badge treatment.
entries.prevention: Measure the family-keyed outer hit target, but resolve the unique Open Chat tooltip/semantic button for SemanticsAction.tap validation across heterogeneous existing header owners.

entries.mistake: The C25F protected Social gate found that the whole-tree hash changed from the predecessor seal after authorized navigation/header work. The changed tree cannot qualify until every protected delta is audited and an explicitly authorized successor seal is recorded.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor whole-tree seal includes navigation chrome files, so even approved one-tap Chat and compact-header changes invalidate it alongside any possible business mutation.
entries.prevention: Pause mutation, inventory every protected Social delta, prove the changes are limited to founder-authorized chrome and tests, preserve business owners, then record a successor seal with exact evidence before rerunning the gate.

entries.mistake: The C25F protected Buy gate found that the runtime-tree hash changed from the predecessor seal after authorized Care/Medicine projection, compact rail and Chat-header work. The changed tree cannot qualify until every protected delta is audited and an explicitly authorized successor seal is recorded.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor whole-tree seal includes Buy navigation composition, so approved shared-rail and header changes invalidate it alongside any possible business mutation.
entries.prevention: Pause mutation, inventory every protected Buy delta, prove catalogue, cart, order, payment, provider and session business behavior remains unchanged, then record a successor seal with exact evidence before rerunning the gate.

entries.mistake: The first read-only Buy manifest comparison required exactly two spaces after every SHA-256 and rejected the accepted manifest before comparing any owner.
entries.rootCause: The audit copied the Social manifest separator assumption instead of accepting the Buy manifest's actual one-or-more whitespace separator.
entries.prevention: Validate the 64-hex prefix and split accepted hash manifests on one-or-more whitespace characters. Do not rewrite accepted evidence merely to satisfy an audit parser assumption.

entries.mistake: The second Buy manifest comparison still required every historical per-file token to contain exactly 64 hex characters, but at least one accepted line contains a shortened token and the audit again stopped before producing the delta inventory.
entries.rootCause: The historical manifest was treated as if it had already passed a per-line schema gate, although the active Buy protection checker uses the independent sealed whole-tree hash and does not parse this manifest.
entries.prevention: Preserve predecessor evidence unchanged. Parse every path, compare lines whose token is valid, report malformed historical tokens separately, and rely on the active protection gate's independently computed whole-tree hash for seal enforcement.

entries.mistake: The explicit negative scroll-owner audit was wrapped in invalid orchestration JavaScript using let followed directly by a block, so the shell command never executed.
entries.rootCause: A terse block-scoping form was mistyped instead of using a standard declared constant in the tool orchestration module.
entries.prevention: Use normal JavaScript declarations and statements around tool calls. A tool-wrapper syntax failure produces no audit evidence and must be registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The first C25F machine gate required a guessed exact ValueKey constructor spelling for the compact rail and rejected the equivalent production key before behavioral checks ran.
entries.rootCause: The stable key value was coupled to an unverified Dart constructor representation in the static gate.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current bounded source before sealing static patterns. Gate the stable key value and behavior, not interchangeable Key versus ValueKey constructor syntax.

entries.mistake: The retained R11 Chat continuity tests still required the removed large launcher and predecessor second-tap Chat menu item on Eat, Ride, Book and Work, rejecting the founder-approved direct family header Chat action.
entries.rootCause: C25 added successor reachability coverage but the earlier exact-return suite's presentation entry step had not yet been migrated from the rejected connected-navigator contract.
entries.prevention: Tap each origin's direct family Chat header control, retain the inbox and exact system-Back return assertions unchanged, and include Social and Shop in the origin inventory.

entries.mistake: Eight retained C24B3 navigator tests still required the removed large destination launcher and one test retained the rejected two-tap menu Chat path, so they rejected the C25 compact launcher and direct Chat header action.
entries.rootCause: The new C25 focused tests were added before the complete predecessor connected-navigator presentation suite was migrated to the successor shell keys and tap budget.
entries.prevention: Use mool-compact-launcher for the destination main-only menu, use the family header Chat key for one-tap Chat, and preserve routing, Back, adaptive viewport and reduced-motion outcomes unchanged.

entries.mistake: The migrated C24B3 Chat test repeated REG-20260809-788 by resolving the outer Open Chat semantics node instead of the interactive IconButton, while the other seven active tests passed.
entries.rootCause: The already corrected C25F tooltip-based semantics pattern was not reused when migrating the predecessor test file.
entries.prevention: Use find.byTooltip('Open Chat') for the unique interactive node in shared Chat shortcut tests and retain the keyed outer control only for hit-target measurement.

entries.mistake: Four retained C24B2 Home tests still required the rejected in-Home family detail grid and Home subaction keys, so they rejected the C25 fixed main-domain-only Home menu.
entries.rootCause: The Home viewport suite was not migrated when C25 moved subactions to destination-local rails and reduced Home selection to one direct main-domain tap.
entries.prevention: Keep fixed no-scroll/adaptive/Chat/Back checks, assert the shared six-domain main-only menu, assert Home subactions are absent, and verify a main-domain tap emits its default route in one tap.

entries.mistake: The retained C16 service conformance contract still asserted that destination-local rails were absent and opened subactions through the removed large connected launcher; Eat C16D exposed both stale expectations and the same contract governs Ride C16E, Book C16F and Work C16G.
entries.rootCause: The professional-conformance suites retained the predecessor centralized-subaction placement after C25 deliberately moved every subaction into its family destination rail to remove the Home detour.
entries.prevention: Migrate the bounded C16D/C16E/C16F/C16G presentation group to assert exact visible local controls, direct one-tap selection, Back continuity and 44px targets; use the compact launcher only for the main-only menu and reduced-motion checks.

entries.mistake: The first migrated Eat C16D test required SemanticsAction.tap on the already selected Order Food control, which is intentionally disabled as a redundant navigation target; the same loop pattern would misclassify selected Doctor and Earn Today controls.
entries.rootCause: Direct reachability was encoded as every control always tappable instead of every unselected destination being one tap while the current destination truthfully exposes selected/current state.
entries.prevention: Assert 44px sizing for every local control, selected/current semantics for the active control, and SemanticsAction.tap for every unselected direct destination. Apply the same rule to bounded Eat, Care and Work conformance tests.

entries.mistake: The first C16F migration required a guessed book-local-navigation owner key, but the current C25 Care rail is keyed care-book-local-navigation; the other reduced-motion test passed.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor absent-key spelling was mechanically inverted to a presence assertion without reading the exact current production owner key.
entries.prevention: Read the bounded current scaffold key before migrating an absence assertion to presence. Bind tests to the exact owner key and do not infer renamed customer-facing family keys.

entries.mistake: Three Eat C24C adaptive cases passed service layout behavior but still required the removed large launcher, and the bounded sibling C24D/C24E/C24F/C24G service-home suites share the same predecessor launcher contract.
entries.rootCause: Service-home business tests retained a cross-cutting destination-shell presentation assertion after C25 replaced only that shell control with the compact launcher.
entries.prevention: Migrate only launcher key, minimum target and semantic-label assertions across the bounded C24 service-home group; preserve every search, card, booking, provider, payment, safety, opportunity and business assertion.

entries.mistake: Three Doctor adaptive tests still required Medicine to be absent, rejecting the founder-approved Care local rail while all Salon and business-interaction cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor Doctor content-isolation assertion did not distinguish service content from the new persistent destination-local Care navigation control.
entries.prevention: Preserve Doctor content/provider assertions while requiring the direct care-local-medicine control at a 44px minimum. Do not use global text absence to reject an authorized navigation label.

entries.mistake: Three Earn Today adaptive tests still required the Work local navigation owner to be absent, rejecting C25's exact Earn Today and Workspace direct controls while all business cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The service-home viewport suite retained the predecessor centralized Work subaction placement after the approved destination-local rail was added.
entries.prevention: Require the Work rail and both 44px direct controls while preserving every search, opportunity, Workspace and reduced-motion service-content assertion.

entries.mistake: The retained Fix1 wording/wiring suite produced eleven failures because it still locked Buy/Eat/Ride/Book labels, two-tap Home subaction keys and the removed large destination launcher.
entries.rootCause: The earlier action-word and wiring contract was not migrated when the founder approved Shop/Food/Travel/Care, main-only one-tap Home defaults and the compact destination launcher.
entries.prevention: Update only the superseded domain labels and shell tap sequence; retain exact production-owner routes, destination Back preservation and Home Chat exact-return assertions.

entries.mistake: An exact search for an inferred Screen04 content lookup spelling returned no matches and was again issued as a bare ripgrep command, repeating REG-20260809-780.
entries.rootCause: The lookup declaration spelling was guessed and a possible no-match was not wrapped in the required explicit exit-code handling.
entries.prevention: Search positively for the known content-spec map symbol with a match cap. For any expected absence, explicitly treat ripgrep exit 1 as pass, exit 0 as rejected match and other exits as errors.

entries.mistake: The live Screen04 compatibility catalogue still presented Buy/Eat/Ride/Book and the predecessor action placement, including Medicine under Buy, no Bus under Ride and no Medicine under Book, despite the C25 shared catalogue being correct.
entries.rootCause: C25 updated the shared menu and real route scaffolds but missed the protected Social compatibility catalogue and its contextual eyebrow copy, leaving a second customer-visible projection inconsistent.
entries.prevention: Gate every live projection owner against Shop/Food/Travel/Care and the exact 18 actions. Reuse /app/book/bus under Travel and the existing Buy Medicine route/content under Care; update the protected successor seal after a bounded delta audit.

entries.mistake: The first Fix1 Screen04 label-assertion correction used the pre-format multiline block, so apply_patch rejected the stale context and made no test change.
entries.rootCause: The test file's current formatted shape was not reread before composing the follow-up patch.
entries.prevention: After formatting, read the exact bounded current block and patch the smallest independently anchored assertion. A rejected patch is non-evidence and must not be retried from transcript context.

entries.mistake: The bounded Fix2 file produced 19 failures and 563 output lines, and the tool truncated the middle of the log so the run could not prove the complete failure inventory.
entries.rootCause: A historically broad single file was assumed to be a bounded evidence unit even though repeated router startup and stack traces made its failure output exceed the envelope.
entries.prevention: Audit every affected helper in the single source file, migrate only superseded navigation presentation, rerun smaller named groups when needed, then run the complete file after failures are reconciled.

entries.mistake: The Fix2 suite retained centralized Eat/Ride/Book/Work subactions inside the connected chooser and the removed large launcher, rejecting C25's main-only menu and destination-local rails.
entries.rootCause: The earlier route wiring suite's tap helpers were not migrated when C25 changed shell placement without changing business destinations or safety behavior.
entries.prevention: Use the compact launcher only for main-domain selection and use exact family-local keys for every subaction; preserve exact routes, non-default Back state and active-ride safety assertions.

entries.mistake: Two Journey01 tests retained predecessor shell taps: Work exact-owner Back used the removed large launcher and the universal visible-controls journey selected a Home subaction after a main family.
entries.rootCause: Core journey tests preserved superseded presentation steps after C25 introduced the compact destination launcher and one-tap main-only Home defaults.
entries.prevention: Migrate only the launcher and Home default-route tap sequence; retain setup, authentication, deep-link, intent, Chat, account and sign-out outcomes unchanged, then rerun the complete Journey01 file.

entries.mistake: The first Journey01 migration assumed a main-family tap from the retained universal action-choice owner would navigate to Screen04, but that owner intentionally switches its section in place; the other ten tests passed.
entries.rootCause: Main-menu behavior was generalized from real destination scaffolds to a retained compatibility owner without reading its callback contract.
entries.prevention: Preserve the compatibility owner's in-place section switching, assert section-social and section-buy, use its existing main-only launcher, and retain one-tap legacy Chat exact-return behavior.

entries.mistake: The second Journey01 migration assumed the in-place Social compatibility section retained the generic MoolSocial launcher, but its Social-specific shell does not expose that key.
entries.rootCause: Launcher availability from the Ride compatibility section was incorrectly generalized across the Social-specific section state.
entries.prevention: Use the already-proven universal search result to switch the compatibility journey from Social to Buy, while retaining the C25 main-only Social selection and existing Chat exact-return checks.

entries.mistake: Eight Screen04 conformance cases retained the predecessor absent-local-rail, large-launcher, menu-subaction and menu-Chat contract, while the other eighteen content/media/adaptive cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The protected Social conformance suite was not migrated when C25 made the four Social actions directly visible, the MoolSocial menu main-only and Chat a one-tap header action.
entries.prevention: Migrate only superseded navigation assertions/helpers, preserve every Social business/media outcome, rerun the complete 26-case file and regenerate the protected Social successor seal after the bounded test delta.

entries.mistake: The Screen04 Flutter process identifier saved before context compaction no longer existed, and the recovery inspection then guessed a nonexistent JSONL registry path and a nonexistent regressions property before reading the real registry shape.
entries.rootCause: A transient execution-cell identifier and remembered conceptual registry name were treated as durable evidence instead of revalidating the process and the repository-owned registry contract.
entries.prevention: After compaction, probe a saved execution cell once; if absent, register the evidence loss and rerun the bounded command. Resolve registry files with repository inventory and inspect top-level properties before reading entries; never infer a pass from missing process output.

entries.mistake: Three Screen04 conformance cases looked for the real Social destination keys `social-local-*`, but the retained Screen04 compatibility owner exposes the same direct actions under its own `screen04-rail-*` key namespace; 23 other cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The C25 behavior contract was correctly shared, but the test migration incorrectly generalized widget identity from the real Social scaffold to an independently retained compatibility owner.
entries.prevention: Assert the compatibility owner's actual `screen04-rail-*` keys while retaining the same action IDs and one-tap behavior; never require unrelated owners to share widget keys. Rerun the complete Screen04 file and reseal the exact protected Social successor tree.

entries.mistake: All seven C11 contextual-subaction tests retained the rejected no-local-strip and large `mool-home-launcher` contract, so they rejected the C25 direct compact family rail or failed before measuring its controls.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor thumb-shelf suite was not migrated when the founder required each destination to keep its own direct subactions and the global MoolSocial menu became main-actions-only behind a compact launcher.
entries.prevention: Retain the six-family, 320px, 140% text, 44px and reduced-motion coverage; assert each real local rail/action and compact launcher, verify the main-only menu overlays without removing the destination, Back closes it, and the local action remains one tap to its exact existing owner.

entries.mistake: A main-menu key inventory used bare ripgrep with a guessed literal/regex and returned exit 1 when no line matched, producing a rejected diagnostic instead of a truthful zero-match result.
entries.rootCause: The established bounded-search wrapper was omitted while exploring a generated widget-key owner.
entries.prevention: For exploratory searches, capture ripgrep output and explicitly accept exit code 1 as zero matches, or use a repository read that cannot confuse absence with command failure. Never retry the bare negative search.

entries.mistake: Eleven C13 direct-default assertions retained Home subaction buttons, the large destination launcher and absent local rails; its route manifest also expected `/app/buy` instead of the now-explicit Shop default `/app/buy?sub=shop`.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor default-landing suite was not reconciled with the C25 main-actions-only Home and direct destination-local subaction architecture.
entries.prevention: Keep the exact six default route/owner and four legacy-root redirect guarantees, update Shop's explicit default route, tap each Home family once directly to its default owner, and require the compact launcher plus the correct family-local rail on every resulting destination.

entries.mistake: The first C13 migration added equality between every main-family route and its first local-action route; Social truthfully uses canonical `/app/social` for the main action and explicit `/app/social?sub=shorts` for the local action while both resolve to the same owner.
entries.rootCause: Equivalent route outcomes were reduced to literal string identity even though the existing router intentionally supports a canonical default alias.
entries.prevention: Assert the main projection's exact declared route separately, then prove one-tap owner and local-rail reachability. Do not require a canonical family route and an explicit default-subaction route to be identical strings.

entries.mistake: Ten C02 cases retained the large launcher, asserted direct local actions were absent, or required a second Home subaction tap; the two stable Home-owner/uniqueness cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The oldest global navigation suite still encoded the rejected centralized-subaction shell after C25 moved subactions onto each real destination and made Home main-actions-only.
entries.prevention: Preserve exact owner continuity, menu dismissal, deep-route state, Ride Auto state, direct Home-origin fallback and native Back history; use the compact launcher, require each actual local action, assert the corresponding main-only family menu item, and make Home family selection one tap.

entries.mistake: Seven C10E motion-containment cases retained the removed noncompact Hero/large-launcher anchor or centralized menu subactions; the finite 240ms production-motion contract passed.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor motion suite measured an obsolete navigation widget instead of the current single 60px compact destination shell and its main-actions-only menu.
entries.prevention: Preserve exact owner/Back continuity, equal anchor geometry across families, direct local switching, one-tap main-family switching, single-shell ownership, finite motion and immediate reduced motion; measure `moolsocial-single-home-launcher-shell`/`mool-compact-launcher` and remove only superseded second taps.

entries.mistake: After the C10E presentation migration, reduced-motion switching reached Work immediately but retained both old and new compact launchers during the route's fixed 240ms lifetime, despite returning the child without visual animation.
entries.rootCause: `moolMainDestinationPage` disabled its transition widgets under accessibility settings but always assigned 240ms transition and reverse-transition durations, so Navigator retained overlapping route subtrees invisibly.
entries.prevention: Resolve platform accessibility features when creating the destination page and use zero transition/reverse duration for disableAnimations or accessibleNavigation; retain the 240ms standard duration otherwise, then require one destination shell after the immediate reduced-motion switch.

entries.mistake: The single C10B Social-to-Work history test retained the large launcher, absent Social/Work local rails and a second Work subaction tap, failing before its Feed restoration assertion.
entries.rootCause: The shared-root regression test still encoded the predecessor centralized chooser instead of the C25 compact shell and destination-local controls.
entries.prevention: Keep the exact Social Feed owner, one shared compact shell, one-tap Work main-family switch, Work local-action presence, native Back restoration to Feed and absence of a Home detour; update only obsolete shell finders and taps.

entries.mistake: Both Social-to-Work compatibility cases used one stale helper that opened the large launcher and selected Earn/Workspace as global-menu subactions; Earn/Workspace local controls were also asserted absent.
entries.rootCause: The shared test helper was not migrated to the main-actions-only compact menu plus Work-local action contract.
entries.prevention: Open Work with one compact-menu family tap; retain Earn as the default owner, tap `work-local-workspace` only for Workspace, require both Work local controls to remain visible, and preserve exact owner and legacy-owner absence assertions.

entries.mistake: Three R03 root cases retained historical Buy/Eat/Ride/Book labels and Buy route, an in-place selected-family marker, or a second Home Shop subaction tap; the other eight root, Chat, Back, reduced-motion and adaptive cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The historical durable-Home suite compared runtime presentation to the superseded R03 action projection instead of the current founder-approved C25 domain contract.
entries.prevention: Preserve historical R03 safety boundaries, but compare current runtime domains to the C25 projection, assert each Home family emits its declared route in one tap, keep Chat one tap in an independent mount, and require the real app route to reach Shop directly then Back to Home.

entries.mistake: The C25 projection declared a finite-motion maximum of 220ms while the retained production standard and passing predecessor C10E contract require 240ms, and the C25F machine gate did not compare those values.
entries.rootCause: The new projection range was frozen without reconciling the established MoolMotion.standard duration or adding a machine-readable cross-check.
entries.prevention: Set the C25 finite range to the established approved 180-320ms interval, retain the 240ms standard, and make the C25F gate parse both the projection bounds and runtime literal so future drift rejects qualification.

entries.mistake: The first motion-range correction updated the projection and C25F gate but did not inspect the transitive C25A gate, which still rejected any maximum other than 220ms.
entries.rootCause: The dependent gate invocation at the end of C25F was known, but its exact presentation assertions were not read before modifying the shared contract value.
entries.prevention: Before changing a gate-owned contract, inspect every transitively invoked gate for hardcoded values; update the active projection and both machine checks together, then run C25A and C25F separately before resolving the regression.

entries.mistake: R03 and C25F were launched through fail-fast `Promise.all`; the immediate C25F rejection ended orchestration before the R03 result was returned, so no R03 outcome can be counted.
entries.rootCause: Independent commands were parallelized with an orchestration primitive that discarded sibling evidence on one rejection.
entries.prevention: Use all-settled result capture for independent diagnostics or run qualification evidence commands separately. After any fail-fast parallel rejection, rerun every sibling whose completed result was not explicitly returned.

entries.mistake: After the Social/Work compatibility test passed, C25F was rerun before resealing the protected Social successor inventory; the gate rejected expected tree `a8c7...` versus audited tree `9d79...`.
entries.rootCause: The test filename contains `social` and is included by the protected Social inventory, but the reseal checkpoint was not applied immediately after its bounded navigation-only migration.
entries.prevention: After every changed test whose protected-inventory path matches Social, run the complete focused file, audit the exact navigation-only delta, update the pending-successor baseline and every expected-hash gate, then run the protected seal before any aggregate gate.

entries.mistake: Four production R06 cases retained absent Food-local controls and the large launcher; eight contract, one-tap, Back, reduced-motion and adaptive cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The R06 production-owner assertions were not migrated when Food's two actions became directly persistent in the compact destination rail.
entries.prevention: Keep exact Order Food and Book Table owners, one-tap switching, forbidden Tiffin/legacy owners, native Back and menu dismissal; require `eat-local-navigation`, both direct controls and the compact launcher on each production route.

entries.mistake: All seven R07 production cases failed through shared helpers that required the large launcher, hid the Travel rail and selected Bike/Auto/Cab as global-menu subactions; the historical three-ride projection case passed.
entries.rootCause: R07's production helpers were not reconciled with the C25 Travel family, where Bike/Auto/Cab and reused Bus are directly persistent local actions.
entries.prevention: Retain RideSession state, exact Bike/Auto/Cab routes, legacy-owner absence and menu Back dismissal; require the compact launcher, four-action Travel rail including Bus, and switch nondefault vehicles directly through `ride-local-*` without a Home/global-menu detour.

entries.mistake: Seven R08 production cases retained the predecessor Book grouping Doctor/Salon/Bus, large launcher and global subactions; the historical Doctor/Salon R08 projection case passed.
entries.rootCause: R08 production coverage was not reconciled after the founder approved Care as Doctor/Medicine/Salon and moved reused Bus to Travel while preserving existing business owners.
entries.prevention: Keep the historical R08 projection as evidence; production tests require Care's Doctor/Medicine/Salon local rail, route Medicine to the existing Buy owner, exclude Bus from Care, use the compact launcher, and preserve direct-route/menu-Back continuity without new owners.

entries.mistake: Five R10 production cases retained an absent Work rail, large launcher and global-menu Earn/Workspace subactions; the historical R10 projection case passed.
entries.rootCause: R10 production coverage was not migrated to Work's persistent two-action destination rail and main-actions-only compact menu.
entries.prevention: Preserve exact Earn Today and Workspace owners, forbidden Delivery Work/Onboard/Verify items, direct routes and menu Back; require both Work local controls, keep Earn as the default, and use one local tap only for Workspace.

entries.mistake: Four of eighteen universal intent cases retained the large launcher/global subactions for Ride, Book and Work or the predecessor Doctor/Salon/Bus grouping; fourteen Buy/Food/Pay/Chat/Social/recovery/accessibility cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The comprehensive intent suite's production-only branches were not migrated to the C25 local rail and current Travel/Care ownership split.
entries.prevention: Keep all existing package/service/route owners and the fourteen passing journeys; switch Auto/Cab and Earn/Workspace locally, cover Care Doctor/Medicine/Salon with Medicine's Buy owner, cover Bus through Travel's local rail, and use the compact menu only for main-family change or Back dismissal.

entries.mistake: A full porcelain dirty-tree count returned the required branch/HEAD/counts but also emitted hundreds of known long-path directory warnings, truncating the diagnostic output.
entries.rootCause: The count command did not suppress Git's non-actionable traversal warnings in this intentionally huge preserved artifact tree.
entries.prevention: For future bounded dirty-state counts, capture Git stdout and stderr separately, require exit code zero, suppress only the already-audited long-path warning stream, and never print the full preserved status list into task output.

entries.mistake: The C25F-to-C25G transition mutation returned truncated tool output, leaving its result unknown until every intended owner was read back exactly.
entries.rootCause: The multi-file state mutation was large enough that its result exceeded the available tool-output context; treating the truncated response as either success or failure would have guessed durable state.
entries.prevention: After any truncated mutation result, perform bounded exact-owner readback before retrying or proceeding, verify every intended state and evidence path, and apply only confirmed missing deltas.

entries.mistake: A C25G registry-discovery diagnostic again used a bare ripgrep match command whose legitimate no-match exit code made the overall read-only command fail.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic did not wrap the optional search in explicit no-match handling even though this failure mode was already registered.
entries.prevention: Use PowerShell Select-String for optional searches or capture and explicitly accept ripgrep exit code 1; reserve an unhandled nonzero exit for an actual required-match gate.

entries.mistake: A C25G reuse diagnostic guessed a C25F conformance-manifest filename that does not exist instead of discovering the exact repository owner first.
entries.rootCause: The lookup reconstructed a plausible name from the ticket title rather than selecting the existing path from the repository inventory or C25F gate source.
entries.prevention: Discover versioned manifest paths with bounded repository inventory or read the owning gate before opening them; never synthesize a durable path from naming convention alone.

entries.mistake: The first REG839 registration patch used an invalid update-hunk boundary immediately before an Add File section and was rejected without applying.
entries.rootCause: The update hunk included a stray hunk marker without valid context, so the patch parser correctly refused the entire mutation.
entries.prevention: Close each update hunk with valid context before an Add File section, keep bounded patches syntactically complete, and confirm all-or-none rejection before retrying once.

entries.mistake: A bounded inventory discovered the exact C25F gate filename, but the same diagnostic still supplied the earlier guessed filename to Select-String and failed.
entries.rootCause: The command combined discovery and inspection while hardcoding the inspection target instead of deriving it from the discovered result.
entries.prevention: Complete path discovery first, then inspect only the exact returned owner in a separate bounded command; never keep a guessed path in a later expression after discovery has contradicted it.

entries.mistake: The completed C25F gate still required C25F to be the currently selected parent/scope child, so C25G could not replay it as predecessor evidence after the lawful state transition.
entries.rootCause: The C25F gate encoded only its active-execution state and omitted a completion-aware branch tied to the parent's exact completed child record.
entries.prevention: Versioned child gates support both their strictly sealed active state and an exact completed-child replay state; replay still enforces every product, motion, protection and installed-identity assertion while accepting only the lawful successor ticket.

entries.mistake: The C25G ticket and scope assessment used implementation disposition `gate_only`, which the strict delivery-discipline preselection checkpoint does not support.
entries.rootCause: The assessment used descriptive wording without validating it against the machine-readable allowed disposition vocabulary before host preflight.
entries.prevention: Before sealing a selected-ticket assessment, read the delivery checkpoint's exact allowed disposition set and use the narrowest supported value consistently in ticket, scope and evidence owners.

entries.mistake: The first C25G disposition correction patch guessed a multiline JSON array, while the ticket stores its reuse inventory on one compact line, so the patch was rejected without applying.
entries.rootCause: The patch context was written from converted JSON output rather than the file's exact raw formatting.
entries.prevention: Before patching compact machine state, read the exact target line and match its literal formatting; converted-object output is evidence of values, not patch context.

entries.mistake: The new C25G aggregate initially accepted only active C25G selection, which would make its qualified evidence unreplayable immediately after lawful C25H selection.
entries.rootCause: The aggregate inherited a selection-only identity block before its required successor replay path was modeled.
entries.prevention: Before closing any host-qualification child, add and test an exact parent-bound completed replay branch for the named device-qualification successor while retaining all contract, inventory, seal and predecessor identity assertions.

entries.mistake: The C25G aggregate gate was corrected for successor replay after two qualifying cycles had sealed the earlier source fingerprint, so those otherwise passing cycles no longer qualified the final gate source.
entries.rootCause: Successor replay readiness was audited after, rather than before, the final two-cycle source seal.
entries.prevention: Finish active-state and completed-successor replay validation for every fingerprinted gate before cycle 1; any later file change inside the fingerprint scope supersedes all earlier cycles and requires a fresh evidence directory with two new unchanged-source cycles.

entries.mistake: The C25G aggregate's completed-state identity branch passed under C25H, but a later unconditional check still required the C25G parent child to be `selected`, rejecting the lawful `complete` state.
entries.rootCause: Successor replay was added to the primary identity predicate without auditing every downstream state-specific assertion in the same gate.
entries.prevention: When adding a second state path, audit the entire gate for unconditional predicates and derive each expected value from the active versus completed branch; prove both branches before sealing host cycles.

entries.mistake: Correcting the contradictory completed-state assertion after the `-02` cycles again changed a fingerprinted functional gate, so the `-02` evidence cannot qualify the final replay-ready source.
entries.rootCause: Only the primary replay predicate was tested before the `-02` seal; the full completed execution path was not exercised until after C25H selection.
entries.prevention: Exercise the complete successor replay path, including every nested predecessor gate and qualifier state check, before final cycles. A functional post-cycle correction always requires a new evidence set and two fresh cycles.

entries.mistake: The first C25H APK machine-state authorization patch contained a malformed escaped evidence-line marker, so patch verification rejected the entire machine-state mutation.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-section patch joined a removed-line prefix to the preceding JSON line instead of preserving a valid patch boundary.
entries.prevention: Mutate critical APK machine state in small exact sections, verify all-or-none failure before retry, and rerun the machine gate only after every section plus manifest checksum is consistent.

entries.mistake: The immediate C25H preinstall audit found one active Java process after the successful single Gradle build, so the candidate did not meet the zero-active-build-process install condition.
entries.rootCause: A Java/Gradle process remained active when the separate install gate was evaluated; its harmlessness could not be assumed and the process was not killed or bypassed.
entries.prevention: After the single build is consumed, require a fresh zero Flutter/Dart/Gradle/Java process audit before opening install authority. On any active process, preserve the built candidate and installed predecessor, record evidence, keep install closed and stop mutation.

entries.mistake: REG850 listed `C25H immediate preinstall process audit` as a gate even though registry gate entries must resolve to repository files, causing the permanent-memory checker to reject it.
entries.rootCause: A human-readable audit label was placed in the machine-readable gate-path array instead of remaining in the mistake/evidence description.
entries.prevention: Every regression `gates` value is an existing repository-relative file path; descriptive audit names belong only in prose and evidence documents.

entries.mistake: After the preinstall rejection, C25H reference authority was set false with all execution authorities, so the scope gate interpreted the active held ticket as a closed state that must await next-ticket classification.
entries.rootCause: Install/build closure was incorrectly generalized to reference/evidence closure even though C25H remains the selected ticket pending a future fresh preinstall audit.
entries.prevention: For an active held device ticket, keep only the minimum reference/evidence authority required by the scope contract while runtime/backend/build/install/external remain false; reserve fully closed execution for a completed ticket awaiting successor selection.

entries.mistake: On the installed r60.24 OPPO candidate, Care Medicine kept the correct Care actions but inherited the dark Buy commerce rail surface, reducing Previous, Next and MoolSocial contrast compared with Doctor and Salon.
entries.rootCause: The shared destination rail projected action membership from the selected Care family while its background treatment still followed the reused Buy destination surface, splitting family identity across two owners.
entries.prevention: Derive the complete rail surface and navigation-control contrast from the projected main family, then require side-by-side OPPO evidence for every cross-owner action such as Care Medicine and Travel Bus before device qualification can pass.

entries.mistake: The temporary navigation prototype validator required static `Shop Home`, `Food Home`, `Travel Home`, `Care Home` and `Work Home` literals even though the valid interface composes each heading from the complete domain data and `${domain.label} Home` template.
entries.rootCause: A source-text assertion was incorrectly treated as rendered-DOM validation for dynamically composed customer copy.
entries.prevention: Use static source checks only for syntax, required data and renderer ownership; verify dynamic visible copy by executing the rendered state or by testing the template against the complete domain input set.

entries.mistake: The temporary prototype verification repeated the stale-LASTEXITCODE regression by treating the native-process variable as the result of a PowerShell regression-memory script that had explicitly passed.
entries.rootCause: The repository PowerShell gate and native HTML validator were combined despite the permanent rule that each has different exit-status ownership.
entries.prevention: Run repository PowerShell gates alone and rely on terminating errors; run the native HTML validator separately and inspect only its immediately owned exit code.

entries.mistake: The inline Node validator used backslash-escaped double-quoted terms inside a PowerShell double-quoted argument, passing an invalid stray backslash to JavaScript before prototype syntax could be checked.
entries.rootCause: A single inline command mixed PowerShell string interpolation with unnecessary JavaScript quote escaping and source-owner assertions.
entries.prevention: Keep inline native validators minimal and single-quoted internally; validate JavaScript extraction/compilation in Node and run literal HTML source-owner assertions separately with PowerShell.

entries.mistake: The category-led family Home prototype stacked a large family heading, explanatory copy, full search field and category row before discovery content, leaving only a small fragment of the first Shop card visible on the founder's phone-scale review.
entries.rootCause: Validation checked category completeness and 44px control targets but did not measure the cumulative vertical chrome or require meaningful customer content above the fold at the smallest supported phone viewport.
entries.prevention: Family Homes use one compact top toolbar containing fixed Search and Chat access plus horizontally scrollable filters; large heading, lead and full search blocks are forbidden before the feed. Small-screen review must prove a complete discovery visual begins in the first viewport, and the toolbar must dismiss on downward scroll and return on upward scroll.

entries.mistake: The REG857 correction removed the large heading stack but replaced it with a persistent Search, Chat and category toolbar that still consumed roughly one hundred rendered pixels including its surrounding space before the Shop discovery card.
entries.rootCause: The mitigation optimized the amount of permanent chrome instead of applying the founder's literal zero-tolerance rule that family-home discovery content must lose no vertical layout space to filters or utilities.
entries.prevention: Family-home Search, Chat and Filter controls occupy zero normal-flow height: they live in a reserved safe overlay region inside the first discovery media surface. Category choices open only as a transient dismissible overlay and never as a persistent row; closing or selecting restores the complete content surface immediately.

entries.mistake: The REG858 zero-height revision overlaid Filter at the top of the discovery hero, forcing a one-handed user to reach upward, open the category sheet and then move back down to select the actual product or service action.
entries.rootCause: The design optimized vertical content area but treated reachability and journey-effort as separate concerns; it preserved a category-selection step that was unnecessary for reaching the customer outcome.
entries.prevention: Family Homes expose a mixed vertically scrollable content feed with category identity embedded in cards and sections, never a category picker. Customers scroll naturally and tap the product or service directly; destination subactions remain in the persistent bottom thumb rail. No top Filter, transient category sheet or filter-before-action journey is allowed.

entries.mistake: After removing category selection, the standard family Home still rendered a `Start in Shop/Food/Travel/Care/Work` action grid that duplicated the persistent bottom subaction rail and required an intermediate action-selection tap before the customer could reach the actual product or service.
entries.rootCause: The feed was changed from filtered to mixed content without removing the earlier family-action launcher, leaving two parallel navigation owners between Home discovery and the customer outcome.
entries.prevention: A family Home card is the actual product, restaurant, ride, provider or work opportunity and routes directly to its exact detail/booking state in one tap. Remove every `Start in` grid and other in-content subaction gateway; the bottom rail remains the only optional family-mode switcher and never becomes a prerequisite for tapping feed content.

entries.mistake: A prototype CSS token search passed the pattern `--shadow-soft|--shadow:` directly to ripgrep, which parsed it as an unsupported command option and returned a false validation failure.
entries.rootCause: The command omitted ripgrep's `--` end-of-options delimiter before a pattern beginning with hyphens.
entries.prevention: Every ripgrep pattern that begins with `-` is preceded by the exact `--` end-of-options delimiter, and its native exit code is evaluated only for that immediately owned search.

entries.mistake: A retired-gateway source check embedded escaped HTML quotes and the JavaScript `${action.id}` template expression inside a PowerShell double-quoted ripgrep pattern, producing a malformed native invocation and an unrelated `unrecognized file type` rejection.
entries.rootCause: The validator repeated the mixed-shell quoting class already prohibited by REG856 instead of separating simple literal checks from native regular-expression discovery.
entries.prevention: Do not pass JavaScript template expressions or escaped HTML quotes through PowerShell double-quoted ripgrep patterns. Use PowerShell raw-string `Contains`/`Select-String` checks for exact literals and reserve ripgrep for simple shell-safe patterns.

entries.mistake: The direct-card mapping validator built a PowerShell double-quoted regex containing `$family:`; PowerShell parsed the colon as part of a scoped-variable expression and rejected the checker before it read the prototype.
entries.rootCause: A dynamic regex was used where five exact raw-string mapping literals were sufficient, repeating the avoidable interpolation class recorded by REG856 and REG862.
entries.prevention: PowerShell validators never place a colon immediately after an interpolated variable unless the variable is explicitly delimited. Prefer an explicit raw-literal array and `Contains` for fixed source-owner mappings.

entries.mistake: The REG859 correction solved top-filter reach by removing the founder-required YouTube-style visible categories from family Homes, so Food, Travel, Care and Work again lacked the explicit All/category discovery model requested from the OPPO YouTube reference.
entries.rootCause: Space, thumb reach and direct-outcome requirements were handled as mutually exclusive alternatives instead of one combined interaction contract; removing a mandated feature was incorrectly treated as simplification.
entries.prevention: Every Social, Shop, Food, Travel, Care, Work and Videos Home shows its categories at the top of the first media surface, overlaid in a reserved safe artwork region so normal-flow height remains zero. All is the default transaction-ready feed; tapping a chip is optional because a one-thumb horizontal swipe anywhere on the hero changes category. No filter sheet, launcher grid or category-before-action prerequisite is allowed.

entries.mistake: Prototype review discovery piped an unsuitable in-memory Split result into Select-String and later searched the complete docs tree together with the prototype, producing oversized output in the first case and a timeout in the second instead of a bounded relevant result.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic did not constrain source ownership, result count and timeout cost before running a text search against a large dirty repository.
entries.prevention: Search exact known owner files, use Select-String -Path or ripgrep against those paths, cap displayed matches, and never pipe an entire in-memory source document through an ambiguous Split overload for line discovery.

entries.mistake: A prototype owner audit supplied many patterns with Context to Select-String and relied on Select-Object -First to bound it, but each selected match expanded into multiple context records and again produced truncated output.
entries.rootCause: The command bounded selected match objects rather than the rendered context lines and combined unrelated owners in one diagnostic.
entries.prevention: Inspect one exact owner or one verified numeric line range per command. Do not combine multiple context-expanding patterns; a displayed-record cap must be applied only after rendering has a proven bounded shape.

entries.mistake: The temporary prototype kept all six main families in a persistent top rail while also keeping destination subactions in the bottom rail, consuming content height and forcing two always-visible navigation layers instead of a single thumb-reachable family rail.
entries.rootCause: Main-family discovery and destination-local action switching were both implemented as permanent chrome rather than assigning each to one authoritative owner.
entries.prevention: Main families exist only in the compact Mool menu. Every destination bottom rail begins with its family Home and contains all truthful local actions in one horizontally scrollable 44px-or-larger rail with an initial overflow cue. The family Home feed remains transaction-ready, so local navigation never becomes a prerequisite for a direct product or service action.

entries.mistake: The first connected-glass prototype source gate reported zero direct actions because its regex assumed each action literal always declared id, label, icon and eyebrow in one fixed field order, even though the valid data objects use a different order.
entries.rootCause: The validator coupled a semantic count to incidental source formatting instead of counting a stable object signature already owned by all direct action records.
entries.prevention: Source-contract counts use a verified stable signature from the actual direct-action object shape or parse the data model structurally; validators must not infer missing product data from an unverified property-order regex.

entries.mistake: The first correction to the direct-action count replaced one unverified regex with another and described `eyebrow` as a stable action key even though the prototype action records use `title`.
entries.rootCause: The proposed stable signature was inferred from memory instead of being verified against one bounded source-owner block before the retry.
entries.prevention: Before retrying a structural source assertion, inspect one exact bounded owner block and copy the actual object signature. For this prototype, count the verified `{ id, label, icon, title }` direct-action record shape and keep the six family records excluded by their additional domain fields.

entries.mistake: The family-root HTML revision branch gate ran `git status --short --branch` against the complete heavily dirty repository, producing thousands of irrelevant paths and truncated output instead of the intended bounded branch, HEAD and scoped-target state.
entries.rootCause: The mandatory branch gate was combined with an unbounded full dirty-tree rendering even though the preserved tree had already been reconciled and only four exact prototype/memory owners were relevant to this revision.
entries.prevention: For this established dirty workspace, obtain branch and HEAD with their exact commands, count and hash the complete porcelain state without rendering it, and display status only for the exact files in the current change scope. Never render the complete dirty tree in a routine successor gate.

entries.mistake: A duplicate search placed the JavaScript `${icon('home')}` template expression inside a PowerShell double-quoted argument. PowerShell consumed the expression, leaving an empty fixed-string pattern that matched and printed the complete HTML document.
entries.rootCause: A literal JavaScript template fragment was passed through an interpolating shell context despite the existing permanent rule to use single-quoted literals or bounded exact source ranges.
entries.prevention: Never place `${...}` JavaScript fragments in PowerShell double-quoted search arguments. Use a single-quoted PowerShell literal after verifying its quoting shape, or inspect the already-known bounded numeric owner range without another search.

entries.mistake: The C26A-to-C26B transition patch placed a new file-update header where the preceding update hunk still expected prefixed context, so apply_patch rejected the complete patch before mutation.
entries.rootCause: Several unrelated JSON state changes and new evidence files were combined into one oversized patch without validating each file boundary and hunk closure.
entries.prevention: Apply successor ticket-state transitions in small independent patches: parent state, child manifest state and evidence documents separately. Every hunk must include exact surrounding context and end before another file header begins.

entries.mistake: C26B removed Previous and Next from the rendered destination rail but initially left the private `_MoolRailStepButton` implementation in the shared navigation file, causing the focused analyzer to fail on an unused element.
entries.rootCause: The rendered call sites were replaced before the now-unowned private presentation class was removed from the same change boundary.
entries.prevention: When an approved navigation replacement removes a private control from every call site, run a bounded reference search immediately and remove the orphaned private class in the same ticket before analysis. Never suppress the analyzer warning.

entries.mistake: REG873 listed the command label `flutter analyze` in its `gates` array, but the permanent memory checker resolves every gate value as a repository-relative file and therefore rejected the registry before the analyzer retry.
entries.rootCause: Command evidence and repository gate-owner paths were conflated while registering the analyzer failure.
entries.prevention: Every regression `gates` value must be an existing repository-relative file. Record ad hoc commands in evidence text, not in the machine gate-path array, unless a real repository wrapper owns that command.

entries.mistake: During C26C validation, an inspection command guessed `config/codex-development-regression-memory.json` and a matching evidence filename even though the permanent owner is `config/codex-development-regression-registry.json`, producing avoidable missing-path errors.
entries.rootCause: The registry filename and evidence path were reconstructed from memory instead of being resolved from the already-known machine gate or a bounded repository file listing.
entries.prevention: Never guess permanent regression-owner filenames. Reuse the exact path from prior verified state; if unavailable, inspect the bounded `config` and `docs/quality` filename lists before reading, then use only returned literal paths.

entries.mistake: The first C26C focused suite included a predecessor test that still required the old 44-by-44 launcher and removed close button, so two assertions rejected the founder-approved 54-by-58 Mool control and outside/gesture/Back dismissal contract.
entries.rootCause: The shared runtime contract was replaced before all focused predecessor assertions for that same owner were migrated to the approved C26 interaction contract.
entries.prevention: Before retrying a shared navigation suite, search focused tests for every removed key and superseded dimension, migrate them to the immutable approved interaction contract, and add a C26C-specific test covering outside tap, swipe and Back dismissal. Do not restore obsolete close chrome to satisfy stale tests.

entries.mistake: The first C26C gate invocation from `apps/mobile` used `../../../scripts`, escaping one directory above the repository instead of the correct `../../scripts`, so both gate scripts were not found.
entries.rootCause: The relative depth from the explicitly selected command working directory was inferred instead of resolved before invocation.
entries.prevention: Invoke repository gate scripts from the repository root whenever possible. If a nested workdir is necessary, resolve the exact candidate path with a non-mutating literal-path check before execution and never infer parent depth.

entries.mistake: The first C26C widget test asserted that no `ModalBarrier` widget existed after opening the embedded switcher, but the enclosing MaterialApp/Navigator already owns one route barrier independently of the switcher, causing a false failure.
entries.rootCause: The test treated a framework widget-type count as component provenance without recording the baseline before the interaction.
entries.prevention: For framework-owned overlay types, compare the before-and-after count and separately enforce a static owner-slice gate that forbids component creation of ModalBarrier, showGeneralDialog and barrierColor. Never assert a global zero count without a baseline.

entries.mistake: The first C26C swipe-up test did not open the switcher because the launcher accepted only an end-velocity threshold; a deliberate drag can have adequate travel but a low or null terminal velocity.
entries.rootCause: The habitual swipe contract was implemented using velocity alone instead of accepting either directional travel or directional fling velocity.
entries.prevention: Track cumulative vertical drag distance and accept a 24px directional travel threshold, while retaining the 80px/s velocity shortcut. Test both drag-open and drag-close at the compact launcher/dock owners.

entries.mistake: The first C26D scope-state transition retried an oversized multi-region JSON patch and included one mistyped expected-context line, so apply_patch rejected the complete transition before mutation.
entries.rootCause: The verified C26A lesson to use small independent state patches was not applied to a long nested scope-gate document.
entries.prevention: Transition the scope-gate document in bounded blocks: selected assessment, checkpoint/ticket and protected successor separately. Read each exact bounded block immediately before patching and never include reconstructed expected context.

entries.mistake: The C26D test-only scope transition set every scope-state execution flag false because runtime source mutation was prohibited, but the scope schema has no separate test-write field and therefore correctly treated the selected ticket as closed.
entries.rootCause: The child manifest's distinct runtime/test authorization fields were assumed to exist in the older shared scope-state schema without checking its execution-authority calculation.
entries.prevention: For test-only tickets, keep the child manifest runtime source authority false and test/gate authority true, while setting shared scope-state `runtimeWriteAuthorized` true as the schema's local implementation/test authorization umbrella. Confirm the scope script's field model before closing a selected ticket.

entries.mistake: The first C26D static gate looked for the `social-global-chat` key in `social_v2_consumer.dart`, but the verified Chat shortcut key is owned by `screen04_universal_components.dart`, so the gate rejected a valid projection.
entries.rootCause: A runtime key observed through SocialUniversalV2 was attributed to its parent consumer file without a bounded source-owner search before the assertion was written.
entries.prevention: Before encoding a static cross-file ownership assertion, locate the exact literal with a bounded search across the already-inventoried owner set. Assert it only in the file that actually declares it; use the integration test for parent composition.

entries.mistake: The first C26D integration test looked for predecessor `moolsocial-local-*-glass-control` keys even though C26B intentionally removed rendered glass cells and the current stable control key is `moolsocial-local-*-selection`.
entries.rootCause: A key pattern was copied from C25E without verifying it against the completed C26B shared owner before the new test was written.
entries.prevention: Every successor test must resolve shared component keys from the current implementation after the preceding ticket closes. C26 conformance tests use `*-selection` and independently assert that no BackdropFilter or scrolling owner exists.

entries.mistake: A Screen04 conformance case still used `_openConnectedAction` to select a family and then a subaction inside the Mool menu; C26 exposes only main families there and keeps direct subactions in the destination bottom rail, so the helper could not reach Shop.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor two-stage menu helper survived the C26 navigation ownership change even though the approved contract makes a family tap route directly to its truthful root.
entries.prevention: Main-family integration helpers tap only `mool-navigator-family-<id>` and then verify the family destination rail. Local subaction helpers operate only on the rendered destination rail; never search for subactions inside the Mool switcher.

entries.mistake: The C26D affected suite reported two Buy continuity rejections: Medicine destination ownership was not found while the switcher was open, and the predecessor account-hub key was not found after opening Account.
entries.rootCause: The combined run did not preserve enough bounded output to distinguish a current test-key mismatch from an overlay visibility defect; the account assertion also precedes switcher opening and may be an independently stale presentation contract.
entries.prevention: Do not mutate runtime or weaken continuity assertions from truncated combined output. Run each named case in isolation, inspect the current accepted Buy owner keys and destination tree, then resolve every case as either a migrated presentation assertion or a real shared-shell defect with a focused machine-detectable regression test.

entries.mistake: The new C26D shared-shell integration test filename contained `social`, so the protected Social gate deliberately added it to the protected test inventory and rejected the unapproved 178-to-179 file-count change even though no protected Social runtime owner changed.
entries.rootCause: The protected Social gate's path-based test selection contract was not checked before naming a new cross-family shared-owner test under the universal test directory.
