entries.prevention: Cross-family shared-shell tests that do not replace the protected Social baseline use a neutral C26 ticket filename without `social`, `youtube` or `screen04`. Protected Social-specific tests require a separately authorized successor seal; never auto-reseal to absorb an accidental filename.

entries.mistake: On a real pushed Shop route, system Back while the embedded switcher was open closed the overlay but also activated the destination route's outer Back owner, removing Shop instead of preserving it.
entries.rootCause: A nested PopScope veto broadcasts a failed-pop callback to other route-level PopScope owners; those existing destination owners also reacted, so the overlay did not exclusively consume the first Back. The standalone C26C test used an unpoppable root route and could not expose this fallthrough.
entries.prevention: Opening the switcher must add a LocalHistoryEntry to the current ModalRoute. System Back removes only that entry and closes the overlay; programmatic close removes the entry safely. A real GoRouter pushed-family test must assert the destination remains mounted after first Back and only a later Back reaches destination navigation.

entries.mistake: After LocalHistoryEntry preserved the Buy screen route, first Back from the open Mool switcher on Care Medicine still removed the `care-local-tab-medicine` state, proving the underlying Buy PopScope reacted to the same failed-pop callback.
entries.rootCause: Local route history prevented route removal but did not exclusively consume the platform Back dispatch before descendant/ancestor PopScope callbacks observed it. The prior real Shop test protected route identity but not a cross-owned destination's exact internal state.
entries.prevention: While Mool is open, a router-level BackButtonListener must return true after closing the switcher, preventing the event from reaching destination PopScope owners. Keep LocalHistoryEntry as route-local fallback and require exact Medicine rail key/state preservation after first Back.

entries.mistake: The first BackButtonListener implementation awaited the 180ms reverse AnimationController before returning `true`; widget-test Back dispatch awaited the callback while no pump could advance that animation, hanging the suite.
entries.rootCause: Platform Back consumption was coupled to completion of a frame-driven visual animation instead of acknowledging the event synchronously and letting the UI close continue independently.
entries.prevention: When Mool is open, the Back listener must initiate `_closeConnectedNavigator()` without awaiting its frame animation and immediately return `Future<bool>.value(true)`. Tests then pump the finite close motion and assert exact state preservation.

entries.mistake: The first C26G suite prevalidation ran from apps/mobile but read the C25G contract through a repository-root-relative config path. PowerShell emitted non-terminating path/null errors, the intended predecessor inventory became empty, and only the five appended C26 tests ran while the shell reported exit zero.
entries.rootCause: The test-list construction command changed working directory without resolving the contract path first, and it did not use ErrorActionPreference Stop to convert setup failures into a rejecting exit.
entries.prevention: Host qualification commands resolve every contract and owner from an explicit repository root, set ErrorActionPreference Stop and verify the exact unique test count before invoking Flutter. A successful Flutter exit cannot qualify a cycle when test-list construction emitted any error or the count differs from the sealed contract.

entries.mistake: The first correct 47-file C26G suite prevalidation passed 335 tests with 11 skips but reported 13 failing predecessor assertions after the approved shared navigation replacement.
entries.rootCause: The combined output was too large to retain the individual failure owners, so it is not yet proven whether each rejection is a superseded C25 presentation assertion, a combined-run isolation issue or a real C26 runtime regression.
entries.prevention: Before sealing or retrying C26G, run the predecessor inventory in isolated files, retain the exact failing test names and assertions, and classify each against the immutable C26 contract. Migrate only truly superseded shared-navigation assertions; fix and gate any real runtime defect. Never omit a failing file merely to make qualification green.

entries.mistake: The first FIX2 reduced-motion migration replaced the removed close-button tap with platform Back in a plain MaterialApp harness, but that harness has no Router BackButtonDispatcher, so the embedded switcher remained visible and the migrated assertion failed.
entries.rootCause: The test migration reused the production-router Back contract in a deliberately router-less presentation harness instead of selecting the approved dismissal mechanism available in both environments.
entries.prevention: Router-backed real-route tests own exact platform Back consumption and state preservation. Router-less presentation harnesses use the approved outside-tap or swipe dismissal, and reduced-motion tests assert it resolves after one pump. Never restore removed close chrome or infer Router behavior from a plain MaterialApp.

entries.mistake: A retry command treated LASTEXITCODE as the success signal after invoking the PowerShell regression-memory script. The script passed, but LASTEXITCODE was null because no native process exit was owned by that call, and the comparison falsely threw before Flutter tests ran.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell script success was checked through the native-process LASTEXITCODE variable instead of normal terminating-error semantics or the automatic success variable.
entries.prevention: With ErrorActionPreference Stop, invoke repository PowerShell gates directly and let terminating errors reject the command; do not inspect LASTEXITCODE for a .ps1 call. Reserve LASTEXITCODE checks for native tools such as flutter and dart immediately after their invocation.

entries.mistake: The first REG885 resolution patch declared a second documentation file update but provided no hunk content for it, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch before mutation.
entries.rootCause: A planned documentation append was left as an empty file-update section while combining it with the registry status change.
entries.prevention: Every apply_patch file-update section must contain at least one complete exact hunk. Apply a registry status change separately, inspect the evidence file ending, then append documentation in a second bounded patch; never leave a placeholder update header.

entries.mistake: The first C26G gate preflight included the predecessor C25F adaptive-reachability gate, which is intentionally sealed to the C25F active/completed ticket transition and rejected the selected C26G state after all C26 gates had passed.
entries.rootCause: The C25G gate inventory was reused by path without distinguishing durable runtime assertions from predecessor ticket-state seals that cannot authorize a successor ticket.
entries.prevention: A successor host contract includes predecessor test coverage but excludes a predecessor gate whose identity logic is sealed to an earlier ticket. C26G retains the complete C25F adaptive test file plus C26B through C26F successor gates; the aggregate contract asserts the exact 18-gate inventory so no coverage is silently removed.

entries.mistake: The second C26G gate preflight reached the brand-integrity gate, which still required the predecessor semantics label `Open MoolSocial actions` and rejected the approved current `Open MoolSocial main menu` launcher contract.
entries.rootCause: The shared navigation semantics changed with the approved embedded main-family switcher, but the permanent brand gate literal was not migrated with the runtime and focused tests.
entries.prevention: Brand integrity must assert the current approved accessible launcher name `Open MoolSocial main menu`, while the C26C tests and gate prove it opens only the six main families. Search permanent gates for removed semantics whenever a shared accessible control contract is replaced.

entries.mistake: The first brand-gate migration searched for one contiguous `label: 'Open MoolSocial main menu'` token, but the runtime label is a conditional expression whose `label:` and open-string literal are on different lines, so preflight rejected again.
entries.rootCause: The current source structure was searched only for the semantic words before editing; the gate token retained the predecessor assumption that the label property and literal were contiguous.
entries.prevention: Inspect the complete current source slice before encoding static literal adjacency. The brand gate asserts the exact open-string literal independently, while focused widget semantics tests prove it is the active Semantics label; do not depend on formatting-specific adjacency across a conditional expression.

entries.mistake: After the semantics migration, the brand gate next rejected because it still required the predecessor `child: Text(` text-only launcher structure, while the founder-approved Home/Mool control is the four-square grid icon with `Mool` label.
entries.rootCause: Only the first failing brand literal was migrated, leaving later tokens in the same source-contract loop tied to the rejected text-only MoolSocial presentation.
entries.prevention: When a permanent source-contract loop rejects after a presentation replacement, audit every token in that bounded loop against the approved current owner before retry. The brand gate now requires the four-square `Icons.grid_view_rounded` and exact `Mool` label while continuing to forbid a duplicate custom logo glyph.

entries.mistake: The first C26H dirty-tree audit used `git status --untracked-files=all`, expanding historical browser-profile evidence into 53,292 leaf records and emitting Windows filename-too-long warnings.
entries.rootCause: Leaf-level untracked enumeration was substituted for the established path-safe owner-level dirty inventory used by predecessor release gates.
entries.prevention: Prebuild dirty reconciliation uses `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=normal`, which preserves tracked file records and untracked owner-directory records without recursively opening historical browser profiles. Any warning-bearing inventory is rejected and never sealed as evidence; no files are deleted or ignored to reduce the count.

entries.mistake: The first C26H APK machine-state authorization patch accidentally embedded an escaped minus marker before the existing evidence line, so apply_patch could not match the expected JSON and rejected the complete patch before mutation.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-section machine-state patch was composed with a malformed diff prefix in one context line, repeating the C25H REG849 failure pattern.
entries.prevention: Apply APK machine-state transitions in small bounded top-level sections, with every removed line beginning with exactly one diff minus and no escape characters. Inspect the literal current slice before each patch and validate JSON after every accepted section; never retry the oversized patch unchanged.

entries.mistake: The first C26H Social-root screenshot retained the transient splash while the subsequently captured UI hierarchy already described the loaded Social destination, creating a falsely paired visual and semantic state.
entries.rootCause: The screenshot was captured without a pre-capture foreground/readiness barrier and was followed by the UI dump, so an earlier transient frame could be labeled using later semantics.
entries.prevention: All C26H matrix captures use the stable evidence owner, which requires the production activity in foreground, two consecutive native-ready dumps separated by 700 ms, explicit splash absence, screenshot capture only afterward, and a third ready dump plus foreground verification. It refuses to overwrite evidence.

entries.mistake: The first stable-capture invocation falsely rejected foreground ownership because the OPPO firmware reports topResumedActivity and ResumedActivity rather than mResumedActivity.
entries.rootCause: The new gate encoded only one Android dumpsys activity key even though authoritative resumed-activity labels vary by platform build.
entries.prevention: The capture owner accepts an exact production MainActivity match only under mResumedActivity, topResumedActivity or ResumedActivity, and repeats the same check after capture; the gate asserts both calls remain present.

entries.mistake: An estimated visual-center rail coordinate failed to activate Mool, while the next truthful hierarchy still exposed the closed Open MoolSocial main menu state.
entries.rootCause: The device workflow guessed a coordinate from the screenshot instead of deriving the exact current clickable semantic bounds from a fresh OPPO hierarchy.
entries.prevention: Subsequent matrix actions use the exact semantic-tap owner, which retains a fresh pre-tap hierarchy, requires exactly one clickable case-exact text or content description, validates nonempty bounds, taps their computed center and refuses to overwrite evidence.

entries.mistake: On Social Create, Gboard covered the native rail while Flutter accessibility still exposed off-screen rail semantics, so an exact semantic-center Mool tap landed on the IME and had no navigation effect.
entries.rootCause: The semantic evidence driver trusted application accessibility bounds without rejecting an active system input-method overlay.
entries.prevention: The semantic-tap owner queries dumpsys input_method immediately before resolving any target and rejects mInputShown=true. The journey dismisses IME through one normal Back and proves exact route/selection continuity before navigation resumes.

entries.mistake: The first semantic-tap IME-hardening patch used a context line copied from the separate stable screenshot helper, so apply_patch rejected the complete patch before mutation.
entries.rootCause: A multi-file patch was composed without first inspecting and anchoring the exact current semantic-tap owner slice.
entries.prevention: Inspect the literal current owner before editing and use small owner-specific exact hunks; never reuse nearby-looking variables from another new helper.

entries.mistake: A C27A combined inspection command included the nonexistent docs/quality/codex-development-regression-registry.json path even though REG875 already records the exact permanent config owner.
entries.rootCause: A guessed documentation candidate was mixed into a verified multi-file read instead of reusing only config/codex-development-regression-registry.json.
entries.prevention: Use the exact config registry owner only, never add a second registry candidate to combined reads, and run the permanent regression-memory gate before and after registry mutation.

entries.mistake: The C26 shared personal dock renders Mool, family root, local actions and switcher rows with four separate hardcoded width, icon, label, weight, radius and indicator vocabularies.
entries.rootCause: The approved architecture was centralized without consolidating predecessor capsule tokens and component-local presentation constants into one successor token contract.
entries.prevention: C27 must make every visible personal navigation metric resolve from one shared token owner and add a static gate rejecting component-local rail and switcher dimensions.

entries.mistake: The same transparent dock exposes pale, peach, white or dark feature canvases across C26H screenshots, so its background and foreground legibility are not globally uniform and Care Medicine becomes materially weak when the switcher is open.
entries.rootCause: Transparency was tested as widget structure but not as a contrast contract over every real family canvas and temporary overlay state.
entries.prevention: C27 must own one neutral clear dock canvas at the shared shell, forbid family theme inheritance, and test light, media, commerce and dark-transition underlays without adding capsules, gradients, shadows or scroll.

entries.mistake: C26 starts bottom labels at 9.5 logical pixels and wraps family and local labels in FittedBox.scaleDown, allowing truthful long labels to render smaller than short labels while Mool, family, local and switcher weights differ.
entries.rootCause: Fit-at-320 validation measured control boxes but did not assert the rendered fixed type size or prohibit automatic label shrinkage.
entries.prevention: C27 uses one explicit Inter navigation type token with fixed size and line height, removes scale-down boxes from personal navigation labels, and tests every production label at 320px and 1.4 text scale.

entries.mistake: Mool, the family root and a local action can all present as active at once, using home-hub emission colour, a separate family-navigation colour and fixed navy selection, so one current destination is not visually dominant.
entries.rootCause: Context, overlay-open and destination-selected states were styled independently instead of being assigned mutually exclusive hierarchy roles.
entries.prevention: C27 defines one accent map and one hierarchy: local destination owns the selection indicator, Mool owns it only while the switcher is open, and the family root remains a quiet context cue without a second selected marker.

entries.mistake: Two- and three-action local clusters are centered in the remaining dock while four-action clusters fill it, moving the first subaction away from its family root and creating unnatural empty space in Food and Work.
entries.rootCause: Adaptive logic optimized isolated cluster symmetry rather than preserving the approved family-to-subaction relationship and compact leading continuity.
entries.prevention: C27 keeps sparse local clusters compact and leading-aligned after the family context cell, using adaptive equal widths only when four truthful actions must fit at 320px.

entries.mistake: On the connected OPPO the C26 bottom Mool, family-root and local-action nodes export only 32 to 38 physical pixels of vertical accessibility bounds at density 320, or 16 to 19 logical pixels, despite nominal 58px host widget sizes.
entries.rootCause: Qualification asserted Flutter layout boxes and semantic tap success but did not gate Android-exported bounds against the 44 logical pixel minimum near the system-navigation inset.
entries.prevention: C27 must correct shared dock inset/semantics ownership and add host plus OPPO hierarchy gates that divide exported physical bounds by device density and reject every bottom target below 44 logical pixels.

entries.mistake: The current destination dock still initializes the removed disclosure animation, overlay, anchor keys and up to 20 post-frame anchor measurements although none participate in the approved C26 render tree.
entries.rootCause: C26 replaced the rendered rail architecture but did not remove predecessor state and measurement owners from the shared StatefulWidget lifecycle.
entries.prevention: C27 removes only proven-unreferenced predecessor lifecycle owners, adds a static source gate for their absence, and retains any separately tested painter API until its consumers are intentionally migrated.

entries.mistake: The first C27A evidence-and-registry patch omitted the required plus prefix on one line inside a new-file hunk, so apply_patch rejected the complete patch before mutation.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-file patch was composed before the evidence documents had been added and verified independently.
entries.prevention: Add and validate each evidence document in a bounded patch, require exactly one plus prefix on every add-file line, and append registry entries only after all referenced evidence exists.

entries.mistake: Social Screen04 wraps the shared 58px destination-local rail in the predecessor 52px railHeight constraint, so one shared component receives different vertical geometry from the other five families.
entries.rootCause: The destinationRailHeight successor token was added without aliasing or removing the older wrapper-height token used by the protected Social projection.
entries.prevention: C27 centralizes one 58px rail height and aliases the predecessor railHeight token to it, with a six-family projection test rejecting any wrapper that constrains the shared rail to another height.

entries.mistake: The C26H Travel and Work root screenshots have an empty first dock cell where the persistent Mool launcher must render, although later switcher screenshots and accessibility semantics expose the control.
entries.rootCause: Qualification proved launcher semantics and later interaction but did not assert first-root visual paint before any overlay state; the launcher portal/compositing path can therefore pass while its initial icon and label are absent.
entries.prevention: C27 gives the compact launcher an explicit shared icon-label paint owner inside the persistent dock and adds six-family root assertions plus device screenshots proving Mool is visible before the switcher opens.

entries.mistake: The first C27B source gate required key: const Key for the compact launcher icon-label even though Dart formatting kept the parent component const and emitted the equivalent child as key: Key, causing a false rejection.
entries.rootCause: The static contract encoded redundant const placement rather than the stable key value and independently tested runtime behavior.
entries.prevention: Source gates assert stable key values without formatter-dependent redundant const adjacency, while focused widget tests remain the authority for rendered geometry and paint ownership.

entries.mistake: The first C27C focused test mounted an opaque full-body ColoredBox in a synthetic extendBody Scaffold, so the binding hit-tested that extending body at the compact Mool centre and the switcher did not open.
entries.rootCause: The visual-token component test reproduced an extending content owner even though extendBody interaction is already covered by real family and C26C suites and was not part of this test's purpose.
entries.prevention: Component visual-token tests use a non-extending Scaffold unless extendBody ownership is the behavior under test; production family integration and device tests retain responsibility for real extending bodies.

entries.mistake: REG918 was initially appended with the planned C27C gate path before that gate file existed, temporarily violating the registry requirement that every referenced gate already exist.
entries.rootCause: A future prevention owner was recorded instead of the existing permanent regression-memory gate during implementation sequencing.
entries.prevention: New registry entries reference only existing gate files; a successor gate may be added to an entry only after the file exists and passes.

entries.mistake: The C27C visual-token matrix repeated the launcher hit-test failure after extendBody was removed, proving the first harness diagnosis incomplete while the separate drag interaction case continued to pass.
entries.rootCause: Presentation assertions were unnecessarily coupled to a synthetic pointer hit even though dedicated C26C and C27C interaction tests already own tap, drag, outside and Back behavior.
entries.prevention: Presentation-only matrices invoke the already-tested launcher InkWell callback directly and assert the rendered overlay; pointer and gesture behavior stay in dedicated interaction tests.

entries.mistake: Directly invoking the launcher callback still did not materialize the portal in the 360x800 presentation matrix while the independent 320x568 reduced-motion drag test passed.
entries.rootCause: The visual token matrix remained coupled to OverlayPortal lifecycle and follower geometry instead of mounting the public MoolConnectedActionNavigator presentation owner directly.
entries.prevention: Visual token matrices mount the public panel owner directly at the shared width; dedicated interaction tests alone own the complete launcher, portal, tap, swipe, outside, Back and reduced-motion path.

entries.mistake: The first C27C source gate required the MoolLocalNavigationTokens qualifier and selected-indicator property on one line, but Dart formatting wrapped the legal chain and caused a false rejection.
entries.rootCause: The static check depended on formatting adjacency instead of the distinctive property suffix within the already-bounded menu owner.
entries.prevention: Bounded source gates match distinctive property suffixes when Dart may wrap qualifier chains, while widget tests prove the exact rendered 2 by 18 indicator.

entries.mistake: The switcher-radius token patch changed the earlier direct-action button's identical radius expression while the actual MoolConnectedActionNavigator still hardcoded 16, which the bounded C27C gate rejected.
entries.rootCause: The patch used generic method-body context instead of anchoring the exact switcher class, so the first matching radius owner was changed.
entries.prevention: For repeated literals in a large Dart file, patches anchor the exact class declaration and bounded source gates prove the token appears inside the intended owner.

entries.mistake: The C26C predecessor gate rejected the shared switcher row-height token and also retained hardcoded blur, alpha, motion and 142px width literals superseded by the founder's thinner uniform C27 standard.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor gate mixed durable interaction invariants with exact presentation spellings instead of resolving presentation through shared tokens independently sealed by C27C.
entries.prevention: Migrate the complete bounded predecessor literal loop together: preserve vertical order, six 56px rows, 180ms motion, no modal/dimming, outside dismissal, gestures and Back, while accepting the C27 shared presentation tokens.

entries.mistake: After C27B completed and C27C became active, the durable C27B source gate rejected because it required the global scope ticket to remain C27B although its source and test contract was still applicable.
entries.rootCause: Selection-time authorization checks were copied into a durable component gate without distinguishing active from complete manifest state, repeating the REG895 state-bound pattern.
entries.prevention: Component gates require exact active scope authorization only while their manifest is active; after completion they validate the completed manifest and durable source/test contract without pinning global scope to the earlier child.

entries.mistake: The first C27D real-route assertion rejected every FittedBox under the rail, so approved Social provider SVG icons were mistaken for the forbidden destination-label scaleDown regression.
entries.rootCause: The integration query crossed the shared label owner's boundary and inspected an implementation detail of SvgPicture rather than proving the actual Text and token owner.
entries.prevention: Real-route tests prove each MoolDestinationIconLabel owns a fixed two-line Inter Text and 44px-plus control geometry; the bounded shared-source gate remains responsible for rejecting label FittedBox scaling.

entries.mistake: The completed C27C switcher gate still required global scope to remain C27C with runtime writes open, which would falsely reject the test-only C27D successor despite unchanged completed switcher owners.
entries.rootCause: C27C retained selection-time authorization checks after the equivalent C27B state-bound gate had already been made successor-safe.
entries.prevention: Durable component gates require exact global scope and write authorization only while their own manifest is active; complete manifests validate durable owners without pinning a successor's scope.

entries.mistake: The C27D combined qualification command invoked the nonexistent stale path scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate.ps1 after every preceding navigation and regression gate had passed.
entries.rootCause: The command used a recalled shorthand instead of resolving the repository's exact durable scope-gate filename.
entries.prevention: Resolve gate paths with rg --files before composing a qualification command; the canonical owner is scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate-state.ps1.

entries.mistake: The first C27D durable gate required testOrGateWriteAuthorized to remain true unconditionally even though completion correctly closes that authorization.
entries.rootCause: The gate separated active scope checks from the test-write assertion but left the latter outside the active-state branch.
entries.prevention: Test/gate authorization is required only for an active test-only ticket; a completed ticket must close it while the durable acceptance gate remains runnable by successors.

entries.mistake: C27E inventory attempted to read a nonexistent monolithic C27 parent manifest even though C27A through C27D are standalone durable tickets.
entries.rootCause: The C26 parent-child ticket shape was assumed to apply to C27 without first resolving actual config owners.
entries.prevention: Resolve ticket manifests with rg --files before reading; C27E validates the four actual C27A-D manifests directly and does not invent a replacement parent owner.

entries.mistake: The first C27E scope transition used one oversized patch whose exclusion-string context did not exactly match current JSON, so apply_patch rejected the entire mutation.
entries.rootCause: Assessment, ticket and protected-candidate sections were coupled into one hunk instead of being patched through their exact bounded owners.
entries.prevention: Patch scope transitions in small exact owner-bounded sections and verify each resulting JSON/hash before proceeding; never relax unrelated delivery or authority fields.

entries.mistake: The C27F scope-detail patch repeated the oversized multi-list hunk pattern after REG931; one differing current string caused a safe whole-patch rejection.
entries.rootCause: The corrective action was not applied narrowly enough: assessment arrays and ticket arrays were still coupled in one patch.
entries.prevention: After a scope hunk rejection, patch exactly one JSON array or scalar owner per apply_patch call and validate the JSON before the next owner.

entries.mistake: The first C27F source aggregate manifest contained 12 intended records plus one trailing blank record, so its audited line count was 13.
entries.rootCause: The add-file patch included an explicit empty added line after the version record rather than only the file-ending newline.
entries.prevention: Count and reject blank source-manifest records before hashing or registering machine state; seal only the exact nonblank record inventory.

entries.mistake: The C27F selection assessment invented device_only_acceptance as an implementation disposition, so the closed-authority wrapper self-test rejected at the delivery lock before reaching APK machine state.
entries.rootCause: Device acceptance workflow semantics were encoded as a new disposition value instead of reusing the delivery lock's supported reuse and configuration values.
entries.prevention: Select implementation dispositions only from the durable delivery-lock allowlist; device qualification reuses existing owners through configuration.

entries.mistake: The first C27F one-build authorization patch coupled ticket and scope files with generic buildAuthorized context and was rejected before mutation.
entries.rootCause: Two authority owners were changed in one patch instead of opening and verifying each exact bounded owner independently.
entries.prevention: Patch ticket build authority first, reconcile its manifest hash, then patch scope build authority through an exact execution block; verify both before changing APK machine state.

entries.mistake: The read-only C27F ticket-hash command used a malformed JavaScript wrapper and did not execute after ticket build authority opened.
entries.rootCause: An unnecessary compact let-expression replaced the established direct awaited shell-call form.
entries.prevention: Use a direct awaited shell_command call for manifest hash reads and verify scope plus APK machine state remain closed until reconciliation completes.

entries.mistake: C27B host tests proved 54 by 58 or wider Flutter semantic controls, but installed r60.26 exported every Mool, family and local Android semantic at only 38 physical pixels high on the 320-dpi OPPO, equal to 19 logical pixels and below the required 44.
entries.rootCause: The host assertion owned Flutter semantics geometry but did not prove Android's exported accessibility-node bounds; the full visual cell and exported semantic owner diverged on device.
entries.prevention: A successor must make the full constrained navigation cell the exported Android semantic owner and run the density-normalized OPPO bound gate before continuing any family screenshot matrix; every Mool, family and local node must be at least 44 by 44 logical pixels.

entries.mistake: The first C27F rejection-state patch coupled scope and APK machine owners and assumed a live evidence value incorrectly, causing a safe whole-patch rejection.
entries.rootCause: Final device disposition used a cross-file multi-owner patch instead of readback-driven exact patches after the material gate stopped execution.
entries.prevention: After device rejection, read back ticket, scope and APK states and patch each owner separately with exact context before running final permanent gates.

entries.mistake: The first C28A read-only reconciliation query piped a bare PowerShell foreach language statement to Format-Table, causing a parser rejection before any state was changed.
entries.rootCause: File inventory reporting and repository identity were coupled into an unnecessarily complex one-line command.
entries.prevention: Use simple independent read-only commands for branch, HEAD, dirty counts and file inventories; never pipe a bare foreach statement without an explicit collection wrapper.

entries.mistake: A combined MainActivity read and duplicate-search reported command failure only because rg correctly found no edge-to-edge override.
entries.rootCause: Expected rg no-match exit code 1 was allowed to determine the whole command status.
entries.prevention: When no-match is an expected audited result, normalize only rg exit code 1 to success while retaining real rg failures.

entries.mistake: The first C28B scope transition coupled many assessment owners and assumed timelineImpactDays was 2 although exact C28A state still held 1, causing a safe whole-patch rejection.
entries.rootCause: The transition repeated the REG931 and REG932 oversized-scope-hunk pattern instead of using exact readback-driven bounded owners.
entries.prevention: Read back the complete selected assessment, then patch one bounded object group at a time with exact current values and validate JSON after every group.

entries.mistake: The first C28B static gate required both expected overlay strings on one line, but dart format legally expanded the list and caused a false rejection.
entries.rootCause: The static assertion depended on formatting adjacency instead of two independent tokens, repeating the REG922 pattern.
entries.prevention: Check the top and bottom overlay tokens independently in the static gate; retain the method-channel test as proof of exact ordered arguments.

entries.mistake: Four C28B PowerShell gates used repository-root paths from the apps/mobile working directory and never ran, while the final successful Flutter test masked those errors with exit code 0.
entries.rootCause: Gate paths were not resolved against the command working directory and the combined command did not fail fast, recurring the REG928 path-safety class.
entries.prevention: Run repository gates from repository root or exact ../../scripts paths with ErrorActionPreference Stop, and never accept a combined phase unless every gate exit status is checked.

entries.mistake: C28B proposed a MainActivity window-fit adapter, but the approved UI lock rejected that file because accepted Screens 01-03 checksum-lock it.
entries.rootCause: C28A necessity analysis did not intersect the proposed native owner with every immutable Screens 01-03 production-file lock before selection.
entries.prevention: Resolve protected file membership before selecting a runtime owner; never mutate or re-seal MainActivity for this successor, use the unprotected shared Flutter system-UI owner and require the protected lock unchanged.

entries.mistake: The combined C28C read-only harness passed the aggregate gate but stopped before the qualifier preflight because it inspected a retained native-process LASTEXITCODE after invoking a PowerShell script.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell script success was incorrectly inferred from LASTEXITCODE, which the invoked script did not own or reset.
entries.prevention: Invoke PowerShell gates under fail-fast terminating-error semantics and do not inspect LASTEXITCODE after script invocations unless an explicit native process owns that status; retry the qualifier preflight independently.

entries.mistake: The first C28C cycle-1 launch used a one-second shell timeout and was terminated during the initial gate set before formatting, analysis, tests or evidence creation.
entries.rootCause: A short hard command deadline was incorrectly used in an attempt to obtain a resumable execution cell.
entries.prevention: Give complete host cycles a sufficient command timeout, use yielded cells only when returned naturally, and never count or preserve evidence from a prematurely terminated cycle.

entries.mistake: The C28D read-only owner inventory found the current shared navigation source but then attempted to read two guessed legacy filenames that do not exist.
entries.rootCause: Owner filenames were assumed instead of being resolved from the live repository file inventory and search result.
entries.prevention: Resolve exact owner paths with rg --files or the live search output before reading them; never append guessed historical navigation filenames to an audit command.

entries.mistake: The C28D read-only APK machine-state blueprint audit repeated REG939 by piping directly after a PowerShell foreach statement, causing a parser rejection before its evidence-path check executed.
entries.rootCause: Inventory objects were not first captured in a named or explicit collection before the pipeline.
entries.prevention: Capture foreach output in a named array or explicit collection and pipe that collection separately; never retry this audit shape before permanent registration.

entries.mistake: The C28D read-only APK machine-state blueprint audit searched the entire cumulative artifacts archive for historical one-build states and exceeded its read deadline.
entries.rootCause: The search was not bounded to the known current machine config, C27F predecessor and C26H precedent owners.
entries.prevention: Search only named current and recent predecessor authority files for machine-state precedent; never retry or broaden an all-artifacts scan after timeout.

entries.mistake: The C28D wrapper rejected correctly before build, but its postcondition check placed -or inside one Test-Path call and caused a duplicate LiteralPath parameter error.
entries.rootCause: Two absent-output predicates were not parenthesized as separate PowerShell cmdlet expressions.
entries.prevention: Evaluate each Test-Path call separately, combine the resulting booleans, and seal the expected negative result only after both reserved output paths are proven absent.

entries.mistake: The first C28D preinstall audit required a literal mInteractive=true field that the OPPO CPH2375 power service does not emit, falsely rejecting an awake interactive unlocked device.
entries.rootCause: A generic Android power-field assumption was used instead of the live CPH2375 power-service vocabulary.
entries.prevention: For this OPPO require mWakefulness=Awake, mHalInteractiveModeEnabled=true, mHoldingDisplaySuspendBlocker=true and keyguard not showing; never wake or bypass a genuinely noninteractive device.

entries.mistake: The C28D first-device-gate evidence formatter repeated the REG939 and REG948 parser shape by piping directly after foreach, so its read-only table did not execute.
entries.rootCause: Loop output was not captured in a named collection before formatting.
entries.prevention: Assign foreach output to a named collection and pipe only that collection; never retry this evidence read before permanent registration.

entries.mistake: The corrected C28D bounds-table command still failed before execution because a diagnostic string used an unbraced variable immediately followed by a colon.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell parsed $semantic: as an invalid scoped variable reference.
entries.prevention: Brace interpolated variables before a colon, and do not retry this optional table because the material gate output already supplies sufficient exact rejection evidence.

entries.mistake: The C28B shared visible-overlay SystemChrome policy passed host tests but installed r60.27 exported the exact same clipped 54 by 19 logical Mool node as rejected r60.26.
entries.rootCause: Requesting visible Android overlays did not change the OPPO exported Flutter accessibility viewport; the r60.27 and r60.26 UIAutomator XML files are byte-identical, so the selected shared owner was insufficient.
entries.prevention: A successor must reselect an unprotected owner that changes the actual Android exported semantics viewport or full-cell semantic ownership, then prove the first installed XML differs and every Mool, family and local node is at least 44 by 44 logical pixels before any matrix interaction.

entries.mistake: The founder-correction read-only line-count inventory repeated the direct foreach-to-pipeline parser shape and did not complete.
entries.rootCause: Loop output was not captured in a named collection before formatting.
entries.prevention: Capture foreach output into a named collection and pipe only that collection; never retry the direct foreach pipeline shape.

entries.mistake: A combined read of multiple Flutter ranges and a full diff exceeded the tool output boundary, leaving the source audit truncated.
entries.rootCause: Multiple source owners and an unbounded diff were requested in one diagnostic instead of being read separately.
entries.prevention: Read one exact owner or numeric range per command and inspect bounded diffs independently; truncated output is never accepted as evidence.

entries.mistake: The audit guessed a permanent regression-memory Markdown filename that does not exist before resolving the exact durable owners.
entries.rootCause: A descriptive filename was inferred from workspace terminology instead of using repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve registry and memory owners with rg --files first, then use only the returned paths in every subsequent diagnostic.

entries.mistake: An optional ripgrep lookup for recent registry IDs returned valid no-match exit code 1 but was surfaced as a failed shell script.
entries.rootCause: Optional discovery did not explicitly accept ripgrep's no-match status.
entries.prevention: Use Select-String or explicitly normalize ripgrep exit code 1 for optional searches so an empty result cannot masquerade as a diagnostic failure.

entries.mistake: The first Screen 04 source read guessed a stale feature-layer path and failed before reading the live owner.
entries.rootCause: A remembered filename was combined with an assumed directory instead of using the repository inventory result.
entries.prevention: Resolve every exact live source path with rg --files before reading it, and use only that returned path for bounded owner inspection.

entries.mistake: The Shop Offers audit passed Windows wildcard path arguments directly to ripgrep, which rejected those arguments while a pipeline masked the nonzero native status.
entries.rootCause: Shell wildcard expansion was assumed for ripgrep path operands and the native exit status was not inspected before piping.
entries.prevention: Inventory candidate files first or search exact directories on Windows, and run native validators without a masking pipeline when their exit status is evidence.

entries.mistake: The first machine-ticket JSON readback again piped directly after foreach and was rejected before validating either ticket document.
entries.rootCause: REG956's named-collection prevention was not applied at the formatting site.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell loop used for evidence must first assign its output to a named collection and only then pipe that collection; enforce this mechanically before execution.

entries.mistake: A directory-wide universal test run mixed current shared-shell coverage with stale historical matrices, failed 87 legacy tests and exceeded bounded output even though FSC01's focused cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The aggregate was selected by directory rather than exact current-owner dependency and output size was not bounded to an attributable suite.
entries.prevention: Select impacted tests from exact references to the current shared owner, run them in bounded groups, and never accept a truncated historical directory aggregate as ticket evidence.

entries.mistake: Two current shared-shell tests still required a root cell and family label for Social after the founder explicitly removed that duplicate.
entries.rootCause: Uniform predecessor assertions did not encode the new Social-only exception while retaining all unaffected-family coverage.
entries.prevention: Assert Social root absence and four direct actions, preserve root size/route assertions for every other family, and retain the common geometry and visual-token checks for all six.

entries.mistake: A second test group treated direct construction of the shared shell as sufficient relevance and included C20/C22/C23 suites for already-removed strap, capsule, bridge and Home owners, producing 22 unrelated failures and truncated output.
entries.rootCause: Test selection used constructor references without checking each suite's asserted keys, routes and live production contract.
entries.prevention: Select completion tests only when their assertions target live keys/routes or current C24+ production contracts; historical removed-owner suites remain diagnostic and are not migrated by an unrelated Social-cell ticket.

entries.mistake: A third current conformance assertion in the C27D helper still called getSize on Social's founder-removed family-root cell.
entries.rootCause: The initial changed-key audit found direct expectations but missed a shared helper that asserted a root for all six real families.
entries.prevention: Search every current production-conformance helper for the changed family-root key, assert Social absence there, and retain exact root geometry for the other five families.

entries.mistake: The first atomic FSC01-completion and FSC06-selection patch was rejected because one long expected MVP-scope JSON section did not exactly match live punctuation.
entries.rootCause: A multi-owner transition depended on a large hand-copied context block instead of small exact live sections.
entries.prevention: Read each live raw owner, patch ticket manifest, batch and scope in small exact steps, and verify the rejected patch changed nothing before retrying.

entries.mistake: Two current conformance tests still required a local Shop cell and selected indicator after FSC06 assigned Shop state exclusively to the retained family root.
entries.rootCause: The initial FSC06 test migration removed direct tab navigation but missed generic real-family helpers that assumed every default route had a corresponding local action.
entries.prevention: Assert the retained Shop root, no local Shop/Products cell and no selected local indicator on Shop; Wholesale and Orders retain their exact local selected indicators and routes.

entries.mistake: The C25E six-domain route projection still included local shop after FSC06 retained Shop exclusively as the family root.
entries.rootCause: The initial changed-key audit missed one helper input list that encoded default roots together with local actions.
entries.prevention: For Buy route projection assert the Shop family-root key separately and list only Wholesale and Orders as local actions.

entries.mistake: The predecessor protected Buy tree correctly rejected FSC06 because the founder-authorized Products-cell removal changes buy_v2_screen.dart.
entries.rootCause: The immutable C25F baseline encodes the former Shop plus Products/Wholesale/Orders navigation projection.
entries.prevention: Preserve the C25F baseline, audit the single protected owner delta, create an additive founder-authorized FSC06 successor seal in pending-OPPO state, and keep build/install authority closed.

entries.mistake: The repository-wide Windows PowerShell compatibility sweep rejects numerous pre-existing historical and device qualification scripts that use banned modern APIs.
entries.rootCause: The global static gate scans every top-level script, including unrelated owners added before FSC06 that have not been migrated to Windows PowerShell 5.1 APIs.
entries.prevention: Do not hide the aggregate rejection or expand FSC06 into historical gate repair; run the changed Buy baseline gate directly under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and ticket the global migration separately.

entries.mistake: The Buy backend-boundary gate rejects a preserved acceptance_policy_governance_contract.test.ts owner not present in its approved inventory.
entries.rootCause: An unrelated backend test exists in the dirty tree without a corresponding boundary-inventory update from its owning ticket.
entries.prevention: Preserve the owner, disclose the gate rejection, and do not expand navigation-only FSC06 into backend inventory or contract changes.

entries.mistake: An unbounded git diff --check covered the entire preserved dirty tree and exceeded the bounded tool output, leaving an unknown aggregate result.
entries.rootCause: The whitespace gate was invoked without the selected ticket's exact path boundary in an inherited workspace containing hundreds of modified files.
entries.prevention: Run git diff --check only against the exact selected-ticket runtime, test, authority and evidence paths and reject truncated aggregate output as completion evidence.

entries.mistake: The first REG973 entry placed the command label git diff --check in its gates array, and the regression-memory validator rejected it as missing repository evidence.
entries.rootCause: A command description was treated as a machine gate even though every registry gates value must resolve to an existing repository file.
entries.prevention: Keep command-only checks in prevention text; include only existing repository gate-script paths in the machine-readable gates array and run the regression-memory validator after each append.

entries.mistake: The required full dirty-tree inventory did not suppress known Windows long-path warnings, so counts completed but warning output exceeded the bounded evidence channel and was truncated.
entries.rootCause: The inventory captured stdout for counting while leaving Git stderr unbounded in a repository containing retained browser-profile paths beyond Windows path limits.
entries.prevention: For full inherited-tree counts redirect Git warning stderr into a bounded in-memory count or suppress only display after preserving the numeric result; never print the long-path warning stream as completion evidence.

entries.mistake: An optional protected-owner lookup again surfaced ripgrep's valid no-match exit code 1 as a failed shell script.
entries.rootCause: Two optional rg commands were invoked without the permanent REG959 no-match handling rule.
entries.prevention: Use Select-String for optional discovery or explicitly accept ripgrep exit code 1; never wrap an optional no-match lookup in a shell harness that reports it as a task failure.

entries.mistake: The first C28E machine-scope transition used an oversized copied JSON patch, and one non-matching FSC06 context block caused the whole transition to be rejected.
entries.rootCause: The transition repeated the large multi-owner context pattern already prohibited by REG967 instead of patching small exact live sections.
entries.prevention: Read and patch the currentTicket, assessment, ticket, authorization, execution and protected-state sections independently; validate JSON and hashes only after every small transition applies.

entries.mistake: The first focused C28E widget test failed to compile because the rail and test referenced Flutter platform globals without directly importing flutter/foundation.dart.
entries.rootCause: The edit assumed material.dart re-exported defaultTargetPlatform and debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride in the required libraries.
entries.prevention: Import package:flutter/foundation.dart in every production or test owner that directly references Flutter platform globals, format, and rerun the same bounded tests before expanding the suite.

entries.mistake: The first clearance implementation read MediaQuery.viewPadding inside Scaffold's bottom-navigation subtree, where Scaffold had removed the top inset, so the calculated Android clearance was zero.
entries.rootCause: A window-level accessibility correction used a subtree-adjusted MediaQuery owner rather than the raw FlutterView inset owner.
entries.prevention: Read View.of(context).viewPadding, divide physical pixels by the view DPR, and fake TestFlutterView.viewPadding in the focused OPPO test before trusting clearance geometry.

entries.mistake: The non-Android widget case changed debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride inside the test and relied on teardown, so Flutter's earlier foundation invariant rejected the leaked value.
entries.rootCause: The widget test used a manual foundation global instead of the framework-owned TargetPlatformVariant lifecycle.
entries.prevention: Use TargetPlatformVariant.only for platform-specific widget tests and never rely on teardown to restore a foundation debug global after widget-test invariant verification.

entries.mistake: The first correction for the raw-view-inset and platform-variant failures again grouped four files, and one formatted test context mismatch rejected the whole patch.
entries.rootCause: The correction immediately repeated REG977's oversized cross-owner patch pattern instead of applying the newly recorded small-file rule.
entries.prevention: Patch evidence and registry first, then patch runtime and each test file independently from current formatted readback; validate after every file before retrying tests.

entries.mistake: The raw-view-inset test pinned a nominal 27-pixel clearance, 129-pixel shell and 735 rail bottom, while the Android platform variant truthfully supplied a more conservative 31-pixel clearance and 731 rail bottom.
entries.rootCause: The assertion encoded an illustrative OPPO arithmetic total instead of the customer requirement of at least 44 exported logical pixels with unchanged 58-pixel cells.
entries.prevention: Assert exported intersection height is at least 44, the Flutter cell remains exactly 58, and the rail bottom is no lower than the accepted reach bound; test the pure OPPO formula separately without pinning platform-variant totals.

entries.mistake: The clearance formula used the 48-pixel compactTapTarget token instead of the 44-pixel minimumTapTarget contract, adding four unnecessary logical pixels.
entries.rootCause: Two nearby design tokens were treated as interchangeable without reading their definitions after the test exposed the arithmetic mismatch.
entries.prevention: Use MoolMetrics.minimumTapTarget for the 44-pixel Android exported-bounds contract and reserve compactTapTarget for components whose accepted geometry explicitly requires 48 pixels.

entries.mistake: The first complete C28E preflight stopped because the live C27D static gate still required Buy local shop and Products after founder-authorized FSC06 removed that duplicate.
entries.rootCause: FSC06 migrated focused runtime tests but omitted the historical C27D source-literal gate from its complete gate inventory.
entries.prevention: Require the full successor host gate preflight after catalogue changes; migrate C27D to Wholesale and Orders only and explicitly reject local shop and Products literals.

entries.mistake: The restarted C28E preflight stopped because C26D still required the Products label and reported three Shop actions after FSC06.
entries.rootCause: The FSC06 completion inventory omitted the older C26D Social/Shop source gate in addition to C27D.
entries.prevention: Migrate C26D to require Wholesale and Orders, focused Shop-root proof, and explicit absence of Products and buy-local-tab-shop; require the entire host preflight before future catalogue completion.

entries.mistake: The first complete C28E qualification cycle reached Flutter analysis and stopped because the widget test retained an unnecessary direct flutter/foundation.dart import.
entries.rootCause: The focused compile fix added foundation imports to both owners, but Material already supplied every foundation symbol used by the test; the preflight did not run full analysis.
entries.prevention: Treat all analyzer diagnostics as host-cycle failures, remove redundant test imports, assign a fresh evidence-directory identity after source correction, and require both unchanged-fingerprint cycles again.

entries.mistake: The first post-correction validation command ran from apps/mobile while retaining repository-root-relative config and scripts paths, so it failed before any validator ran.
entries.rootCause: Repository gate checks and a Flutter analyzer invocation with different required working directories were incorrectly grouped into one shell command.
entries.prevention: Run repository-relative PowerShell gates from the repository root, run Flutter commands separately from apps/mobile, and never combine path owners with incompatible working directories.

entries.mistake: A C28E contract readback assigned the parsed object to $host, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's read-only $Host automatic variable before any gate or cycle ran.
entries.rootCause: A generic local name was used despite multiple permanent registry entries and memory rules prohibiting PowerShell automatic-variable aliases.
entries.prevention: Use ticket-specific variable names such as $c28eHostQualificationContract and never assign to $Host, $host, $HOME, $home or other automatic-variable aliases.

entries.mistake: The restarted C28E cycle passed gates, formatting and analysis but its 53-file parallel Flutter suite ended with two failures whose diagnostic blocks were truncated from the bounded tool output.
entries.rootCause: A high-volume compact reporter invocation did not retain machine-readable failure details separately from progress output, leaving the failing owners unidentified in the returned channel.
entries.prevention: Register the failed-suite event before rerun, isolate exact failing owners with structured output or bounded unchanged-catalogue partitions, and never accept a cycle from summary counts when any test failed.

entries.mistake: Two required Screen 04 connected-navigation journeys still requested the removed Buy local Shop action, causing both full-suite failures at buy-local-tab-shop.
entries.rootCause: FSC06 migrated focused runtime tests and two static gates but omitted the required legacy Screen 04 journey owner from its complete test inventory.
entries.prevention: Migrate required connected-navigation journeys to the retained Wholesale action while preserving the shared Shop family root, and never recreate a redundant local Shop cell to satisfy historical tests.

entries.mistake: After the required Screen 04 journey migration, the next C28E cycle reached the protected Social gate and found the 178-file tree no longer matched the retained FSC01 seal.
entries.rootCause: The required legacy test is inside the protected Social tree, but its authorized FSC06 migration had not yet been represented by a separate immutable C28E successor seal.
entries.prevention: Never overwrite the retained Social baseline; verify explicit test-owner authority, create a separately traceable immutable successor seal when authorized, and point only the successor host contract and replay gate at it.

entries.mistake: A C28E seal readback listed the C25F candidate directory but then guessed a RUNTIME-MANIFEST.txt child that does not exist there.
entries.rootCause: A historical predecessorManifest field was mistaken for evidence that the active candidate directory shared the predecessor's file inventory.
entries.prevention: List each evidence directory first, read only proven children, and never infer a manifest path from a field that explicitly points to a different predecessor directory.

entries.mistake: A C28E closure readback guessed config/mvp-delivery-discipline-lock.json even though the live scope contract already referenced the authoritative robust delivery-lock filename.
entries.rootCause: A shorter path was inferred from a field label instead of resolving the exact path stored in the live machine contract.
entries.prevention: Resolve delivery-lock owners from the live scope contract, prove the referenced file exists, and never derive filenames from gate or field labels.

entries.mistake: The first C28F bounds self-test stopped because the strict-mode gate accessed the optional visible-to-user XML attribute as a PowerShell property on synthetic nodes that omitted it.
entries.rootCause: The C28D filter expression was copied into a strict-mode successor without replacing optional XML property access with an attribute API.
entries.prevention: Read optional UIAutomator XML attributes with GetAttribute, treat absent as eligible and exact false as excluded, and require positive and negative self-tests to reach geometry validation.

entries.mistake: After the visible-to-user fix, the C28F self-test stopped again because semantic filtering still accessed optional content-desc and text XML attributes as PowerShell properties on the hierarchy root.
entries.rootCause: REG994 was applied only to the first failing attribute instead of auditing every optional attribute read in the strict-mode gate.
entries.prevention: Convert every optional UIAutomator attribute read in the gate to GetAttribute in one audited pass, including package, visibility, content-desc, text and bounds.

entries.mistake: The C28F bounds self-test next stopped because strict mode accessed Buy-only forbiddenLocalLabels on Social, where the optional field is intentionally absent.
entries.rootCause: The prior strict-mode audit covered XML attributes but not optional JSON contract properties read for every family.
entries.prevention: Check PSObject property presence before reading optional JSON fields and resolve absent non-Buy forbidden-label lists to an empty array.

entries.mistake: The C28F contract copied a C28D rejection fixture filename and checksum from human prose before proving the retained evidence directory's exact live child identity, so the self-test stopped at its preserved-fixture check.
entries.rootCause: Narrative evidence was treated as sufficient filesystem identity proof when sealing a machine contract.
entries.prevention: List the bounded retained evidence directory, select only a proven immutable XML child, hash it directly, and then seal that exact path and checksum in the successor contract.

entries.mistake: The first fresh C28F read-only OPPO audit command completed with exit zero but its yielded execution cell returned no key-value scalar output, so no identity evidence could be admitted.
entries.rootCause: Too many native probes and scalar projections were grouped into one yielded shell invocation without a separately retained output boundary.
entries.prevention: Run small independent read-only ADB probes that each return bounded key-value scalars, require visible tool output, and never infer device or package identity from exit zero alone.

entries.mistake: The path-safe C28F Git probe indexed single-line branch and HEAD strings, producing System.Char values without Trim and blank identity output while other dirty-count scalars printed.
entries.rootCause: Native PowerShell output cardinality was assumed to remain an array when a one-line result is a scalar string.
entries.prevention: Coerce one-line native identity output to string and trim it directly without indexing; reject every scalar from a compound audit that emits any PowerShell error.

entries.mistake: The first item-25 evidence patch used remembered closing prose that did not match the current wrapped document and was atomically rejected.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined a new numbered item and distant prevention text without first copying an immediate literal tail context.
entries.prevention: Read the literal evidence tail immediately before patching, keep file-local exact context, and register an atomically rejected patch before a smaller retry.

entries.mistake: The first C28F negative APK-machine self-test truthfully rejected the retained C28D machine state but its wrapper accepted only an explicit later build-authorization phrase and reported a false negative.
entries.rootCause: The self-test assumed the gate would advance past machine-state identity before rejecting, ignoring the valid earliest closed boundary.
entries.prevention: Before successor machine transition, require any exact current earliest rejection among stale candidate identity, non-prebuild machine state or closed one-build authority, and always forbid an unexpected pass.

entries.mistake: The first post-transition C28F machine-state readback rendered several large nested JSON sections together and the tool channel truncated the result, so none of those sections could be accepted as verified.
entries.rootCause: A compact JSON file was parsed correctly but multiple verbose nested objects were serialized into one evidence projection without a bounded scalar output contract.
entries.prevention: Read and verify one machine-state section at a time, emit only exact named scalars and counts, and reject every field from a projection whose returned output is truncated.

entries.mistake: A lookup for newly expected C28F rejection identifiers used required rg exit semantics for optional discovery, so the valid zero-match exit code 1 failed the compound command.
entries.rootCause: The lookup did not declare zero matches valid even though it was discovering whether an identifier had already been persisted.
entries.prevention: For optional fixed-string discovery, capture ripgrep exit code 1 as an explicit zero-match result, reject only codes above 1, and isolate optional lookups from required reads.

entries.mistake: The first C28F build-authority readback guessed config/mvp-personal-scope-state.json, which does not exist, so the compound scope projection failed after the ticket read.
entries.rootCause: The live scope owner filename was reconstructed from its logical role instead of resolved from the bounded config inventory or a proven contract reference.
entries.prevention: Resolve the exact active scope-state path from a bounded config scope inventory or an already verified reference before reading or patching it; never infer the filename from an owner label.

entries.mistake: The first post-activation registry-count projection queried a nonexistent regressions property and emitted a misleading count of one instead of counting the registry entries array.
entries.rootCause: The registry root schema was assumed from memory rather than verified before selecting the collection property.
entries.prevention: Inspect the parsed registry root property inventory, require the exact entries property, count that array, and reject a missing property rather than coercing null into a one-element projection.

entries.mistake: The provisional C28F source-manifest registry count was advanced to 1005 before the corrected live query proved the registry still contained 1004 entries.
entries.rootCause: The manifest line was incremented from an assumed prior total rather than derived after all required failure registrations and compared to the parsed entries array.
entries.prevention: Persist every required regression entry first, then derive both live registry count and manifest value, require exact equality, and only then compute the source-manifest checksum.

entries.mistake: The first post-activation scope validation invoked scripts/check-mvp-personal-scope.ps1, which does not exist, so no scope result was obtained.
entries.rootCause: A plausible validator filename was inferred from the scope owner rather than selected from a bounded live scripts inventory.
entries.prevention: Enumerate scripts matching the exact scope owner first, invoke only a proven path, and never treat a logical contract label as a script filename.

entries.mistake: The first build-phase regression-memory gate rejected REG1004 because its prevention gate list repeated the same nonexistent guessed scope script path.
entries.rootCause: The failure was registered before the bounded scope-script inventory completed, and its gate list preserved the rejected guess instead of only proven existing owners.
entries.prevention: Existence-check every gate path in a new registry entry against the live repository before retry, and bind scope prevention to scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate-state.ps1.

entries.mistake: The first final C28F zero-process and artifact-absence audit placed Boolean -or inside an unparenthesized Test-Path invocation, causing duplicate LiteralPath binding and invalidating all printed scalars.
entries.rootCause: Two cmdlet invocations were combined directly in an if condition instead of first assigning their Boolean results to named variables.
entries.prevention: Assign every Test-Path result to a named Boolean, combine only those booleans with -or, and reject all earlier audit scalars if any PowerShell error occurs.

entries.mistake: After the one authorized C28F build, aapt dump badging could not load the very long immutable evidence-artifact path, so no package or version metadata was admitted.
entries.rootCause: The validator was pointed at the maximum-length cumulative evidence path instead of the checksum-identical generated APK path under the shorter mobile build directory.
entries.prevention: Prove generated and evidence APK SHA-256 and byte length are identical, run aapt against the absolute short generated path, check native exit immediately, and never rebuild or relocate immutable evidence to bypass path handling.

entries.mistake: Successive C28F reseal patches changed qualificationResult.evidence while preBuildValidation.evidence remained on 09 because the patch matched a repeated generic evidence field in the wrong nested object.
entries.rootCause: The patch hunk did not include the unique parent-object key and immediate bounded readback focused on another machine section.
entries.prevention: Patch repeated nested JSON fields only with unique parent-object context and immediately read back that exact bounded object before relying on the transition.

entries.mistake: The resumed C28F reconciliation rendered the complete inherited git status path list and the tool channel truncated it, so the body was not accepted as a bounded dirty-tree inventory.
entries.rootCause: The repository-required literal status command was combined with visible full output instead of immediately projecting only path-safe counts and digests for durable evidence.
entries.prevention: Run the required status check but retain only branch, HEAD, staged/tracked/untracked counts and path-safe digests; never render the inherited path list as evidence.

entries.mistake: Gradle --stop reported one daemon stopped, but the exact proven Gradle Java PID 14516 remained present for more than 30 seconds and the zero-process gate remained closed.
entries.rootCause: The Gradle client acknowledgement describes a stop request, not OS-level process disappearance, and the daemon did not complete termination within the bounded wait.
entries.prevention: Require OS-level disappearance of the exact PID; with explicit founder cleanup authority terminate only the proven Gradle daemon PID, then rerun the global Flutter/Dart/Gradle/Java zero-process audit before any ADB mutation.

entries.mistake: The exact-PID cleanup wrapper threw when the previously proven Gradle daemon had already exited naturally immediately before termination, even though no process needed to be killed.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper treated an already-absent narrow cleanup target as an error instead of a safe no-op followed by the authoritative global process audit.
entries.prevention: Record an already-absent exact target as a no-op, perform no termination, and require the subsequent global Flutter/Dart/Gradle/Java audit to decide install readiness.

entries.mistake: The first C28F adb install -r command passed the very long immutable evidence-APK path and Windows adb failed to stat it before reaching Android Package Manager.
entries.rootCause: The known long-path rejection discovered by aapt was not applied to the install transport even though the shorter generated APK had already been proven byte/checksum identical.
entries.prevention: Before install, prove evidence and short generated APK identity, pass the absolute short generated path to Windows adb, and treat any host-side stat rejection as consumed command authority with device install count zero until separately sealed recovery and fresh audit.

entries.mistake: After tapping Open Shop in the switcher, the first C28F capture incorrectly required Wholesale current even though the route correctly opened the distinct shared Shop family home.
entries.rootCause: The historical C26H Products-default journey was generalized into a first-local selection assumption after FSC06 removed Products and preserved Shop as a separate family root.
entries.prevention: Treat switcher selection as shared-family-home navigation only; when the matrix plans a local action, preserve intermediate evidence, tap the exact local semantic, and capture selected state without inferring a default.

entries.mistake: After selecting the Food family, the C28F matrix guessed the clickable semantic Open Order Food and the exact semantic helper found zero matches without tapping.
entries.rootCause: A contract label was converted into an assumed Open-prefixed device semantic instead of reading the fresh retained pre-tap hierarchy to determine whether the destination was already selected or exposed under another exact semantic.
entries.prevention: Read every fresh pre-tap hierarchy, use only a proven exact clickable semantic, and capture directly when the planned local destination is already current.

entries.mistake: The first workspace-after-swipe-down capture required only Workspace current, which remained visible behind the still-open switcher, so the capture false-passed until the next closed-Mool semantic tap found zero matches.
entries.rootCause: Dismissal validation asserted destination continuity but not the closed Mool semantic and explicit absence of switcher shell semantics.
entries.prevention: For every dismissal state require Open MoolSocial main menu, forbid MoolSocial main actions and Close MoolSocial main menu, and separately require the retained destination semantic.

entries.mistake: After the C28F matrix passed, all scope execution authorities were set false while the top-level scope contract remained active, so the final scope gate rejected the inconsistent closed projection.
entries.rootCause: The closure patch updated ticket and execution fields but did not read and apply the scope gate's required top-level closed/founder-review lifecycle branch and checkpoint together.
entries.prevention: Before closure patch the top-level scope state, checkpoint and all execution authorities as one verified lifecycle projection, then rerun the exact scope gate before founder handoff.

entries.mistake: The first corrective C28F scope-closure patch grouped top-level, ticket and checkpoint changes under remembered checkpoint context that did not match the live wrapped JSON, so the complete patch was atomically rejected.
entries.rootCause: A multi-section lifecycle patch relied on remembered prose instead of immediate literal live lines for each small owner section.
entries.prevention: Patch top-level state, ticket identity and checkpoint as separate small exact hunks after bounded live reads, and verify each section immediately.

entries.mistake: The final C28F handoff ran git ls-files for the complete inherited untracked tree without stderr suppression, producing long-path warnings and truncated output; its untracked count was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Tracked status warnings were suppressed, but the separate untracked inventory repeated the known long-path scan class and was grouped with otherwise valid final scalars.
entries.prevention: Do not enumerate the inherited untracked tree at final handoff; report it retained and unbounded, and collect branch, HEAD, tracked count and staged count in independent warning-suppressed projections.

entries.mistake: A bounded successor-planning inventory attempted to pipe directly from a PowerShell foreach statement and stopped at parser validation before reading the requested files.
entries.rootCause: The command did not wrap the foreach output in an array or assign it to a named collection before Format-Table.
entries.prevention: For multi-file metadata projections, assign foreach results to a named array and format that array only after enumeration completes; a parser error proves no file inventory.

entries.mistake: The post-registration regression-memory replay passed reconciliation as the Phase value, which is not in the validator's allowed phase set.
entries.rootCause: The registry entry's appliesTo vocabulary was incorrectly treated as the gate script's Phase parameter contract instead of inspecting or reusing its proven ValidateSet.
entries.prevention: Use only the gate's proven Phase values general, implementation, build or device; host-only successor planning uses Phase general and BuildMode none.

entries.mistake: The first FSC03 native-owner inventory repeated the direct PowerShell foreach-to-Format-Table parser shape, so the read-only metadata projection stopped before any file owner was inspected.
entries.rootCause: The command constructed projected objects inside a statement-form foreach and placed the pipeline immediately after its closing brace instead of collecting the objects first.
entries.prevention: Every multi-file PowerShell projection assigns foreach output to a ticket-specific array and formats only that array after enumeration; the corrected inventory must complete before FSC03 selection or reference mutation.

entries.mistake: The first combined FSC03 HTML-owner search passed a double-quoted alternation expression containing escaped double quotes through PowerShell, and ripgrep rejected the resulting unclosed group before reading the source.
entries.rootCause: The command relied on cross-layer quote escaping for a complex regular expression instead of using shell-safe literal patterns or separate exact searches.
entries.prevention: For bounded HTML-owner discovery on PowerShell, pass each target as a single-quoted ripgrep fixed-string pattern with repeated -e options, then inspect exact numeric ranges separately; a regex parser rejection proves no owner read.
