entries.mistake: The first browser CTA navigation assertion supplied a regular expression for expectNavigation.url even though the in-app browser contract requires a string; the wrapper rejected the assertion after the click navigated to the intended Create page.
entries.rootCause: A familiar Playwright URL matcher shape was used instead of the browser skill's documented serialized string contract.
entries.prevention: In in-app browser expectNavigation calls, pass an exact absolute URL string; after any wrapper rejection, inspect the current URL before deciding whether the user action executed and never repeat the click blindly.

entries.mistake: The installed Computer Use skill instructed the session to call sky.documentation, but the loaded @oai/sky object exposed no documentation method and rejected the call before Windows automation.
entries.rootCause: The skill entrypoint documentation and the installed runtime API surface were inconsistent.
entries.prevention: After this exact mismatch, read the skill-owned docs/guidance.md, docs/confirmations.md and docs/api.md files directly before any Windows action; never guess the missing method or UI-control signature.

entries.mistake: A founder-requested visible Microsoft Edge Start-Process launch was blocked by host policy before execution, so no Edge window opened.
entries.rootCause: The shell launch path was not permitted by the active host policy even though the requested URL and visible browser review were in scope.
entries.prevention: Do not retry a host-policy-blocked visible browser process launch through alternate shell syntax; use the supported Computer Use app inventory/launcher or the visible in-app Chromium browser and give the founder the exact local URL.

entries.mistake: The supported Computer Use inventory found Microsoft Edge as MSEdge, but two bounded sky.launch_app calls failed with an unavailable execution context and the follow-up inventory proved Edge remained stopped with zero windows.
entries.rootCause: The Windows Computer Use launcher did not have a valid action execution context although read-only installed-app inventory remained available.
entries.prevention: After one documented launcher retry and a fresh inventory proving zero target windows, stop Computer Use, preserve the failure, and show the validated local reference in the visible in-app Chromium browser instead of guessing another Windows input path.

entries.mistake: The FSC03 Feed HTML candidate was designed as a generic polished empty-state CTA without first grounding the destination in the founder's earlier X journey screenshots and the complete provider-versus-MoolSocial Social ownership model, so the founder rejected it.
entries.rootCause: The candidate optimized an isolated empty state before completing founder-reference inventory, whole-Social ownership classification and a screen-specific interaction/state contract.
entries.prevention: Before each Social successor candidate, inventory every founder-supplied reference for that destination, classify content and action ownership, record the complete screen-specific state/tap contract, and reject generic filler or isolated CTA composition that is not traceable to those findings.

entries.mistake: A read-only handoff lookup combined three optional ripgrep probes and allowed a valid zero-match exit code 1 to fail the compound inspection, so it produced no reliable current-state inventory.
entries.rootCause: Optional absence discovery was not isolated from required reads and its declared exit-code semantics were omitted despite the active permanent rule.
entries.prevention: Run optional ripgrep probes independently, capture the native exit code immediately, treat 0 as matches, 1 as an explicit zero-match result and values above 1 as command errors; never let one optional absence invalidate separate successful required reads.

entries.mistake: The first generated native Shorts patch helper assumed the functions.exec JavaScript isolate exposed atob, so patch generation stopped before apply_patch received any mutation.
entries.rootCause: A browser-global decoding API was used without proving it existed in the documented tool orchestration runtime.
entries.prevention: Generate bounded apply_patch text directly from inspected source or use only documented isolate helpers; never assume browser or Node decoding globals exist in functions.exec.

entries.mistake: The second generated native Shorts patch helper replaced atob with TextDecoder, but the functions.exec isolate exposed neither API and again stopped before apply_patch received a mutation.
entries.rootCause: The retry substituted another unverified runtime global instead of returning to the documented direct patch interface.
entries.prevention: After an unavailable orchestration global, stop generated decoding retries and use literal apply_patch hunks grounded in a fresh exact source read.

entries.mistake: A subsequent native Shorts apply_patch bundled overlapping stale cleanup hunks after the main widget rewrite, and verification rejected the patch because its copied context no longer matched the live source.
entries.rootCause: Cleanup was composed against an earlier source snapshot instead of re-reading the just-mutated owner and applying non-overlapping exact hunks.
entries.prevention: After any material source rewrite, re-read the exact live ranges and apply cleanup as small non-overlapping hunks; a verification rejection authorizes no speculative retry against stale context.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02A test migration bundled three files and one source-test hunk required a blank line that was absent in the live file, so apply_patch rejected the whole mutation before any test changed.
entries.rootCause: The source-test replacement used a larger hand-composed context block instead of the freshly read minimal exact lines.
entries.prevention: Patch each affected test independently with minimal exact context from the live file, and verify each mutation before moving to the next test owner.

entries.mistake: The first focused Flutter analysis after replacing fabricated Shorts reported twelve warnings because seven legacy Shorts widgets/methods and five fixture-only optional fields remained unreferenced in the live owner.
entries.rootCause: The initial cleanup removed fake catalogue construction and top-level builders but did not remove every newly orphaned widget and data-model parameter revealed by the analyzer.
entries.prevention: Treat every focused analyzer warning introduced by a surface replacement as incomplete implementation: prove zero references, remove the orphaned owner and fixture-only fields, then rerun the same bounded analyzer set.

entries.mistake: The post-implementation FSC02A evidence update changed the top-level MVP scope state from ticket_disclosed_and_authorized to a descriptive progress string, and the scope gate rejected authorized execution after the delivery lock passed.
entries.rootCause: A gate-owned enumerated authorization state was reused as free-form implementation progress instead of preserving it and recording progress in the selected-ticket assessment and checkpoint fields.
entries.prevention: Keep mvp-scope-gate-state.json top-level state at the gate-required ticket_disclosed_and_authorized value for an active authorized ticket; record source, test, host and device progress only in dedicated evidence fields.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02B handoff lookup supplied a guessed founder-batch manifest filename that did not exist, so ripgrep exited 2 after the exact FSC02B ticket itself was read.
entries.rootCause: A likely machine-owner path was passed directly instead of first resolving the durable batch filename through rg --files.
entries.prevention: Resolve every batch or ticket owner through rg --files before content search; keep exact known ticket reads separate so a missing optional owner cannot invalidate them.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02B MVP scope transition bundled the assessment, ticket, authorization and protected-candidate sections, but one hand-copied test-plan string did not match the live FSC02A state and apply_patch rejected the full transition.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-block state transition depended on unverified copied context instead of independently replacing freshly read bounded sections.
entries.prevention: Transition MVP scope in small exact blocks: assessment identity first, ticket contract second, authorization/protected state last; parse and gate after all blocks are complete.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02B Videos widget replacement was embedded as one large JavaScript string for functions.exec, and the orchestration parser rejected the literal before apply_patch ran.
entries.rootCause: A long punctuation-rich source replacement crossed an unnecessary JavaScript string layer instead of using smaller bounded literal patch hunks.
entries.prevention: Split punctuation-rich Flutter replacements into small exact apply_patch hunks and keep each orchestration literal bounded; a JavaScript parse rejection proves no file mutation.

entries.mistake: The bounded FSC02B retry used a JavaScript template literal but left a Windows backslash path in the patch header, so the parser treated the path as an invalid Unicode escape and stopped before apply_patch.
entries.rootCause: The patch input changed string form without normalizing the Windows path for JavaScript template-literal parsing.
entries.prevention: Use forward-slash absolute paths in every apply_patch header carried by a JavaScript template literal; never expose a C-backslash path to template-literal escape parsing.

entries.mistake: The generated apply_patch deletion for the fixture video catalogue omitted the terminal newline after the End Patch marker, and the patch validator rejected it before mutation.
entries.rootCause: The generated patch assembly treated the visible end marker as sufficient without satisfying the apply_patch line-termination contract.
entries.prevention: Every generated patch string must end with the exact End Patch marker followed by one newline; validate the final suffix before invoking apply_patch.

entries.mistake: The generated catalogue-deletion retry added and asserted a terminal newline, but apply_patch still reported that the End Patch marker was not the last parsed line and rejected the mutation.
entries.rootCause: The retry changed marker termination without first inspecting the exact generated tail and therefore did not identify the parser-visible extra line or hunk shape.
entries.prevention: After an end-marker rejection, inspect the exact serialized patch tail before any retry; do not alternate newline assumptions blindly. Fall back to bounded literal hunks if the generated shape remains ambiguous.

entries.mistake: The first focused FSC02B analysis found that migrating the global navigation test away from a fixture video orphaned scrollToClearBottomAndTap in that test file.
entries.rootCause: The test assertion migration removed the helper's last call but did not remove the now-dead helper in the same patch.
entries.prevention: After migrating fixture-driven tests, run focused analysis and remove every helper whose final reference disappeared before replaying the test group.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02B combined test replay included the predecessor C03 global Mool navigation suite after changing one fixture-video case; all six cases failed on removed keys such as mool-root-selected and mool-action-social, while the current C28F conformance and FSC02B tests passed.
entries.rootCause: A historical predecessor suite was selected because it mentioned the removed fixture title, without first proving that its global-navigation key contract remained current under the accepted C28F system.
entries.prevention: Restore the untouched predecessor test, exclude the stale C03 suite from FSC02B completion, and rely on current Screen 04/C28F connected-navigation tests that assert live keys and the provider-owned destination.

entries.mistake: The first bounded FSC03A class-replacement generator assumed the functions.exec V8 isolate exposed the browser atob helper; the script stopped before apply_patch ran.
entries.rootCause: The generated-patch path selected an unverified JavaScript decoding primitive instead of using a runtime-neutral text transport or checking the isolate capabilities first.
entries.prevention: Do not assume browser base64 globals exist in functions.exec. Prefer shell-returned JSON text or a verified TextDecoder-compatible byte transport, and validate the decoder before constructing a mutation patch.

entries.mistake: The first generated FSC03A FeedActions deletion supplied the following class marker without the required unified-diff context prefix, so apply_patch rejected the hunk before mutation.
entries.rootCause: The generator prefixed removed and added lines but did not prefix the unchanged anchor line with one space.
entries.prevention: Every generated unified-diff hunk must prefix unchanged anchors with one space; validate the first and last hunk lines before calling apply_patch.

entries.mistake: The corrected FeedActions deletion still failed because the extracted segment retained trailing blank-line structure and the generated hunk expected a different number of blank lines before the following class anchor.
entries.rootCause: The generator normalized CRLF but did not strip trailing line breaks before mapping the deletion lines and appending its own context anchor.
entries.prevention: Strip all trailing line breaks from extracted deletion segments, emit deleted content only, and add the exact following anchor as a separately prefixed context line.

entries.mistake: The first FSC03A analyzer replay found four private helpers orphaned when the fixture Feed, inline composer and its actions were removed: _unavailable, _openComments, _openProfile and _openReport.
entries.rootCause: The visible Feed owner deletion removed the final references to shared-looking private helpers without completing a same-pass reference audit.
entries.prevention: After deleting a bounded UI owner, search every removed callback and run focused analysis; delete only helpers with zero remaining references before the next test replay.

entries.mistake: A combined FSC03A stale-key audit correctly found expected negative assertions in tests and no forbidden Feed-owner symbols in runtime source, but the final no-match ripgrep exit code made the shell command fail.
entries.rootCause: The verification command treated ripgrep exit 1 for an expected empty source result as an execution error instead of an asserted no-match outcome.
entries.prevention: For expected-empty ripgrep audits, capture output and explicitly accept exit codes 0 or 1 while rejecting only codes above 1; do not let a successful no-match proof fail the shell batch.

entries.mistake: The first compact FSC03A widget replay mounted an indeterminate LinearProgressIndicator through a helper that always called pumpAndSettle, so the bounded test never became idle and had to be terminated.
entries.rootCause: The new loading state introduced a perpetual animation while the shared test mount helper still assumed every rendered state eventually settled.
entries.prevention: Mount intentional indeterminate loading states with a finite pump, and reserve pumpAndSettle for states with no perpetual animation or for transitions after the loading widget is removed.

entries.mistake: After replacing the shared loading-state mount with a finite pump, the full isolated FSC03A test file still emitted no buffered result for more than eighty seconds and was terminated before identifying which named case stalled.
entries.rootCause: The retry reran all three cases as one buffered shell process, so it did not isolate whether the remaining stall was source setup, review-only publication seeding, Create transition or state iteration.
entries.prevention: After a test-file stall, run each named case separately with an explicit test timeout and inspect relevant async owners before retrying the combined file.

entries.mistake: Terminating the two stalled shell cells did not terminate their Dart compiler and flutter_tester descendants, leaving two verified copies of the same FSC03A test active in the workspace.
entries.rootCause: The shell-cell termination boundary stopped the wrapper but did not guarantee Windows descendant-process cleanup.
entries.prevention: After terminating a Flutter test cell, inspect exact command lines and parent chains; stop only descendants proven to belong to that test before starting another Flutter process.

entries.mistake: The first exact cleanup required all eight previously observed FSC03A process IDs, but the two root dart wrappers exited before cleanup while six verified descendants remained, so the safety count rejected the stop.
entries.rootCause: The mutation gate used a stale observed process count instead of re-resolving the live descendant set immediately before stopping it.
entries.prevention: Re-read the exact live process set and command lines immediately before cleanup; validate every remaining target rather than requiring already-exited IDs to remain present.

entries.mistake: The second descendant cleanup assumed every verified process command line contained the absolute MOOLSOCIAL-PRODUCTION path; the dartvm test runners carried the relative test path and failed that uniform predicate.
entries.rootCause: The safety rule ignored that Flutter's Windows process tree represents workspace identity differently in the dartvm runner versus compiler and flutter_tester descendants.
entries.prevention: Validate each process role with its own exact evidence: dartvm by the Flutter test snapshot plus relative test path, and compiler/tester descendants by repository package or asset paths and verified parent IDs.

entries.mistake: The isolated review-only Feed test awaited SharedSession.publishSocialContent directly inside testWidgets; ReviewSharedGateway uses Future.delayed, so fake time never advanced and the named case stalled before rendering.
entries.rootCause: The test seeded review-only state through a real delayed gateway without tester.runAsync or explicit fake-clock pumping.
entries.prevention: Wrap delayed gateway calls used for widget-test setup in tester.runAsync, assert their result, and only then mount the widget under the fake test clock.

entries.mistake: The bounded OPPO screenshot listing successfully read /sdcard/Pictures/Screenshots but also queried /sdcard/DCIM/Screenshots, which does not exist on the connected CPH2375 and made the combined command exit 1.
entries.rootCause: The discovery batch assumed a second common Android screenshot directory without first testing whether it existed.
entries.prevention: Resolve candidate device directories with a read-only existence check and list only directories confirmed on the exact device; keep each optional location from failing successful evidence reads.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02A1 focused analyzer replay failed because the new Shorts metadata widget required non-null view and publication strings while the reused provider-shaped Short model correctly exposes both fields as nullable.
entries.rootCause: The composition rewrite inferred that admitted provider records always carry optional metrics and dates instead of preserving the model's truthful nullability contract at the renderer boundary.
entries.prevention: New provider metadata renderers accept the exact nullable model fields and conditionally omit absent values; they never force non-null values or invent fallback metrics, dates or engagement claims. Focused analysis runs before widget tests.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02A1 source-test replay still required the channel key and playback-ownership sentence inside _buildLiveYouTubeShort after both moved into the dedicated _YouTubeShortsStageMetadata production widget.
entries.rootCause: The composition test was partly migrated to the new owner classes but two stable-contract assertions retained the predecessor method-substring boundary.
entries.prevention: After extracting a production widget, audit every source-boundary assertion for keys and copy moved with that widget; assert stable contracts against the exact new class or complete source while retaining widget tests for rendered ownership.

entries.mistake: The FSC02A1 source replay could not form its Videos substring because the test still ended that slice at the removed _quickPostReady Feed getter after paused FSC03A source work changed the adjacent production owner.
entries.rootCause: A cross-surface source test used an internal getter from the following Feed implementation as its Videos boundary instead of the stable next production method declaration.
entries.prevention: Source slices end at the next stable peer method or class declaration owned by production, never at an unrelated following surface's private helper. Paused-source changes still require affected shared-source tests to be reconciled before qualification.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02A1 ticket manifest recorded an incorrect remembered hash suffix for the second retained OPPO YouTube screenshot, so the declared evidence path did not exist even though the screenshot itself remained intact.
entries.rootCause: The filename was copied from summarized conversation memory instead of an immediate literal directory inventory during ticket creation.
entries.prevention: Every manifest evidence filename is copied from an immediate literal directory listing and each declared path is existence-checked before the manifest hash is sealed.

entries.mistake: A read-only FSC02C source-set inventory passed a backslash-escaped double-quote pattern through PowerShell, causing ripgrep to parse part of the pattern as a missing path and exit 2.
entries.rootCause: The command used shell escaping from another environment instead of PowerShell single-quoted fixed-string arguments already mandated by permanent regression memory.
entries.prevention: PowerShell ripgrep patterns containing double quotes are enclosed in single quotes with no backslash escaping; independent fixed-string searches declare and handle their own exit status.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02C Gradle configuration gate failed because the Android library plugin has only debug and release build types by default, so getByName("profile") could not resolve a profile source set.
entries.rootCause: The packaging edit inferred that the Flutter app's profile variant automatically creates a matching build type in the isolated Android library project.
entries.prevention: A plugin library that needs distinct profile packaging explicitly creates its profile build type before configuring the profile source set, and Gradle project configuration must pass before any compile task or APK gate.

entries.mistake: The first corrective FSC02C multi-file patch placed an extra hunk marker before the third file header, so apply_patch rejected the entire input and none of the Gradle, gate or test changes applied.
entries.rootCause: Three independent corrections were bundled without validating that every update hunk was syntactically closed before the next Update File header.
entries.prevention: After a configuration failure, re-read each exact owner and apply one small complete patch per file; verify each change before touching the next owner.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02C profile Kotlin compile reached the reused native player but failed because AGP 9 did not generate the library BuildConfig class, leaving the new BuildConfig.DEBUG reference unresolved.
entries.rootCause: The implementation relied on a generated Android library BuildConfig without first enabling that build feature under the current AGP configuration.
entries.prevention: Any library source that uses BuildConfig explicitly enables android.buildFeatures.buildConfig, and the exact profile Kotlin compile must pass before packaging evidence closes.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02C final delivery gate ran after completion evidence changed the ticket manifest but before the selected-ticket assessment was resealed with the new SHA-256, so the gate rejected the stale hash.
entries.rootCause: The closure sequence invoked dependent gates before finalizing all ticket evidence fields and updating the single dependent manifest digest.
entries.prevention: Finalize ticket evidence first, compute its final SHA-256, patch the selected assessment digest, verify exact equality, and only then run delivery, scope and regression closure gates.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02D scope-state rewrite accidentally combined the prefix of the unchanged pre-ticket checkpoint digest with the new ticket digest while replacing the selected-ticket assessment.
entries.rootCause: The whole scope-state file was reconstructed manually and an invariant checkpoint hash was transcribed beside the new manifest hash instead of being copied and independently verified from the prior state.
entries.prevention: A ticket transition changes only the selected manifest digest; every invariant lock and checkpoint digest is copied verbatim from the read-back prior state and exact-equality checked before any delivery or cloud gate runs.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02D scope gate stored a founder-message label in authorization.evidence even though the gate requires that field to resolve to an existing repository evidence file.
entries.rootCause: The selected ticket was reconstructed from semantic authorization context without rechecking the scope gate's path-existence contract for authorization evidence.
entries.prevention: Every founderDisclosure.evidence and authorization.evidence value is a repository-relative existing file path verified before the first scope gate; message provenance belongs in founderAcceptance or the evidence document body.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02D CLI identity preflight assumed gcloud.cmd or gcloud was callable from the active PowerShell PATH, but neither command resolved and execution stopped before any cloud request.
entries.rootCause: The current desktop shell tool inventory was not checked independently before composing the bounded identity probe, despite historical evidence referring to a different Cloud SDK session.
entries.prevention: Cloud qualification begins with repository-local launcher discovery and explicit Get-Command checks for every required CLI; an unavailable tool is reported as machine state and no cloud script is invoked until an authorized executable is resolved.

entries.mistake: The first exact-project Firebase inventory returned nonzero, but stderr was suppressed and the wrapper replaced the real diagnostic with a generic exception before the cause was known.
entries.rootCause: The read-only probe optimized its output before the command contract and authenticated project access had been proven in the current shell.
entries.prevention: Before a first Firebase CLI subcommand in a new shell, read the installed command help and preserve bounded diagnostic stderr until the exact command succeeds; redact output only after its structure is known.

entries.mistake: The computer-control skill locator supplied to the session did not exist on disk when the founder offered to enter an interactive Cloud password, so the skill could not be loaded.
entries.rootCause: The installed plugin cache version no longer matched the session's advertised filesystem locator, and the authorized workspace boundary did not permit broad searching of unrelated user directories for a replacement.
entries.prevention: If an advertised interactive-control skill cannot be read at its exact locator, stop using it, disclose the fallback, and use a founder-visible terminal or official browser flow only when authentication is required; never type, capture, copy or echo founder credentials.

entries.mistake: The supported exact-project firebase apps:list ANDROID command reached the installed CLI but returned only a generic failure and wrote firebase-debug.log without listing the Dev app.
entries.rootCause: The active login identity alone did not prove the current Firebase CLI session could complete an authenticated management API request for the exact Dev project.
entries.prevention: Treat login:list as identity evidence only; prove one bounded exact-project API command separately, inspect only sanitized error/status lines on failure, and use founder-entered interactive reauthentication if the session is expired or invalid.

entries.mistake: The first Google Cloud CLI installation attempt combined an executable download, signature verification and visible launch in one PowerShell command, and the desktop execution policy rejected the command before it ran.
entries.rootCause: The installation workflow used a direct executable-download pattern that the host policy blocks even though the founder authorized the SDK installation.
entries.prevention: Prefer the host package manager's named verified package for required SDK installation; separate package discovery, installation and interactive authentication, and verify the resulting executable before use.

entries.mistake: The first winget Google.CloudSDK install requested --scope user, but version 579.0.0 has no installer applicable to that forced scope and stopped before installation.
entries.rootCause: The workflow assumed the verified package exposed a user-scope installer even though winget show did not declare a supported scope.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact package manifest, avoid forcing an undeclared scope, and retry only with the package's supported default installer contract while preserving visible UAC or installer prompts for the founder.

entries.mistake: The winget Google.CloudSDK install used --interactive inside the tool-hosted shell, but no installer window became visible to the founder and the command timed out after 64 seconds.
entries.rootCause: Interactive winget execution inside the shell tool did not guarantee a founder-visible desktop process even though the package requested interactive mode.
entries.prevention: Use silent package installation for non-credential SDK setup, verify the installed package afterward, and reserve a separately launched visible Windows terminal/browser for founder-controlled authentication only.

entries.mistake: The isolated moolsocial-dev-fsc02d configuration was created and the authorized account selected, but setting the exact project required a token refresh and non-interactive execution stopped because the saved gcloud credential needs reauthentication.
entries.rootCause: The historical hello@moolsocial.com account identity remained configured while its current Cloud SDK token could not be refreshed without founder interaction.
entries.prevention: Create a separate project configuration first, then use a founder-visible official gcloud auth login flow for the authorized account; do not enter, capture, copy or echo founder credentials and do not target the project until authentication succeeds.

entries.mistake: The exact Dev Android app inventory was probed again while the founder-visible Firebase reauthentication process was still open and before founder confirmation, reproducing the same generic failure.
entries.rootCause: Process liveness was treated as ambiguous progress and the read-only command was used as a premature completion probe instead of waiting for the explicit authentication success signal.
entries.prevention: After launching founder-controlled authentication, do not retry an authenticated project command until the founder confirms the official flow succeeded or provides the current visible prompt for diagnosis.

entries.mistake: The founder-requested Firebase Console URL was launched through Start-Process using the default URL handler, but the desktop command policy rejected the command before any tab opened.
entries.rootCause: The fallback assumed the shell tool permits generic URL-handler launches even though earlier direct executable-download launch patterns had already shown a restrictive desktop policy.
entries.prevention: For a founder-requested Chrome tab, resolve Chrome only through its registered Windows App Path and invoke that exact executable with a bounded HTTPS URL; do not use generic URL handlers or interact with credential tabs.

entries.mistake: A help-only probe for gcloud alpha firebase extensions discovered the alpha component was absent and gcloud attempted to offer its installation, which was denied because the system-wide SDK directory requires elevation.
entries.rootCause: The workflow tested an optional alpha surface before confirming that a supported stable Firebase CLI path was sufficient for the empty Extensions inventory.
entries.prevention: Do not install or elevate for alpha/beta Cloud components when a stable Firebase CLI or exact REST/metadata control exists; keep the production qualification on supported stable commands.

entries.mistake: A read-only signing-fingerprint evidence search passed artifacts/quality/youtube-private-dev-* as a ripgrep path, which Windows did not expand and ripgrep rejected as an invalid filename.
entries.rootCause: The command used a shell-style wildcard directory argument instead of ripgrep's --glob filter over the literal artifacts/quality root.
entries.prevention: On PowerShell, pass a literal existing root to ripgrep and express directory/file selection through --glob; do not rely on wildcard expansion in a positional path.

entries.mistake: The corrected optional signing-fingerprint evidence search returned ripgrep exit 1 for no matches, but the shell wrapper did not normalize that expected optional-search result and reported it as a failure.
entries.rootCause: The command treated all nonzero ripgrep exits alike instead of distinguishing no matches from invocation or I/O failure.
entries.prevention: Every optional ripgrep search handles exit 0 as matches, exit 1 as a valid empty result, and exit 2 or higher as a real command failure before choosing another evidence source.

entries.mistake: The next optional apksigner owner search again let ripgrep exit 1 propagate as a shell failure immediately after the no-match prevention was registered.
entries.rootCause: The command template was reused without implementing the newly recorded 0/1/2+ exit-code branch at the call site.
entries.prevention: Optional searches must be wrapped at composition time: capture output, accept exit 0 or 1, throw only for exit 2+, and print the captured result afterward. Do not issue another bare optional rg command.

entries.mistake: An ad-hoc App Check inventory counted the empty REST response as one item and incorrectly reported one registered debug token before the raw response and Firebase Console were reconciled.
entries.rootCause: The probe applied array counting directly to an empty Invoke-RestMethod result instead of first checking whether the debugTokens property exists and is non-null.
entries.prevention: App Check debug-token evidence must preserve and parse the raw JSON shape: an empty object or absent debugTokens property means zero; count only an explicitly present array, then cross-check the console or the repository verifier before declaring a security issue or deleting anything.

entries.mistake: The full PublicDataReview verifier passed its local stage and entered the nested cloud preflight, but that preflight still depended on the stale Firebase CLI session for ext:list and stopped at the empty Extensions inventory check.
entries.rootCause: The stable gcloud authentication and no-secret security verifier were qualified, but the older preflight retained one separate Firebase CLI management-session dependency that was not production-grade or necessary for a read-only inventory.
entries.prevention: Use the authenticated stable Firebase Extensions management API for the exact project inventory, keep access tokens in memory only, and remove the independent Firebase CLI login dependency from cloud preflight before rerunning the full verifier.

entries.mistake: The first local test for clearing extensionAccessToken used a double-quoted regex containing backslash-dollar-null, so PowerShell expanded $null to empty and left an illegal trailing backslash.
entries.rootCause: The assertion used shell-style dollar escaping inside a PowerShell interpolated string instead of escaping a literal fixed string with regex::Escape.
entries.prevention: PowerShell source assertions containing dollar-prefixed variable names use single-quoted literals passed through [regex]::Escape; never rely on backslash to suppress PowerShell interpolation.

entries.mistake: The corrected full verifier entered its nested cloud preflight, but gcloud emitted the informational active-configuration line on native stderr and Windows PowerShell promoted it to a terminating NativeCommandError.
entries.rootCause: The verifier process relied on the globally active non-default configuration instead of pinning CLOUDSDK_ACTIVE_CONFIG_NAME for every nested gcloud process.
entries.prevention: Cloud qualification exports CLOUDSDK_ACTIVE_CONFIG_NAME=moolsocial-dev-fsc02d before invoking any nested verifier or preflight and separately verifies that configuration's account, project and region first.

entries.mistake: The direct cloud preflight still failed at gcloud config get-value account because that command itself emits the active-configuration notice on native stderr, even after CLOUDSDK_ACTIVE_CONFIG_NAME was pinned.
entries.rootCause: The first prevention addressed configuration selection but did not replace the specific gcloud config get-value subcommand that generates the informational notice under Windows PowerShell.
entries.prevention: Resolve the active deployer through gcloud auth list filtered to status ACTIVE, require exactly hello@moolsocial.com, and never call config get-value inside strict nested Windows PowerShell gates.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02D local control-test rerun invoked PowerShell 7 from the assumed C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe path, but this host provides PowerShell 7 through its WindowsApps package path and the test never started.
entries.rootCause: The command used a conventional installation path without first resolving the executable through Get-Command on the current qualified host.
entries.prevention: Resolve pwsh with Get-Command before every PowerShell 7-only gate, record the resolved executable identity, and invoke that exact path; never assume the conventional Program Files path.

entries.mistake: The permanent regression-memory gate rejected two FSC02D Firebase CLI entries because their evidence arrays still referenced transient firebase-debug.log even though the durable quality record already preserved the relevant sanitized findings.
entries.rootCause: The original failure registration treated a temporary tool log as durable repository evidence instead of limiting the evidence pointer to the accepted quality record.
entries.prevention: Permanent regression entries may reference only durable repository evidence files verified to exist; transient CLI debug logs can inform diagnosis but must not be registered as required evidence.

entries.mistake: A read-only focused-test evidence search was wrapped in malformed JavaScript, so the tool orchestration failed before PowerShell or ripgrep ran.
entries.rootCause: The compact wrapper removed required JavaScript token separation and was not kept in the already-qualified standard const/result/text form.
entries.prevention: Use the standard multiline const result = await tools.shell_command(...) orchestration form for every exec call; do not compress JavaScript control syntax around tool calls.

entries.mistake: A focused-test evidence search passed docs\quality\MOOLSOCIAL-FSC02* and config\moolsocial-fsc02* as positional ripgrep paths, repeating the registered Windows wildcard-path failure.
entries.rootCause: The search narrowed filenames by embedding wildcard syntax in positional paths instead of using literal directory roots and ripgrep --glob filters.
entries.prevention: On Windows, every ripgrep search uses literal existing directory roots; filename narrowing is expressed only with one or more --glob arguments. Never pass wildcard characters in positional paths.

entries.mistake: The FSC02D selected-ticket assessment used verification and conditional_external_write as implementation-disposition values, and the delivery discipline gate rejected verification after the approved UI locks passed.
entries.rootCause: The ticket described operational activity rather than using the delivery lock's closed implementation-disposition vocabulary.
entries.prevention: Selected-ticket implementationDisposition uses only the exact lock enum. FSC02D maps to reuse, configuration and test_only_acceptance; conditional Dev authority remains in dependencies and execution fields, not the implementation enum.

entries.mistake: The first disposition correction patch expected a multiline JSON array, while mvp-scope-gate-state.json stores the array on one line, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch without changing files.
entries.rootCause: The mutation context was inferred from converted JSON output instead of the exact source-file text.
entries.prevention: Before patching machine-readable state, inspect the exact literal source lines and build the smallest patch against that representation; never infer patch layout from ConvertTo-Json output.

entries.mistake: The Android Firebase metadata probe correctly found no google-services.json but then passed settings.gradle*, build.gradle* and app\build.gradle* as positional ripgrep paths, repeating the registered Windows wildcard-path failure again.
entries.rootCause: The Gradle search assembled wildcard-bearing file paths instead of searching the literal Android root with --glob filters.
entries.prevention: All remaining repository searches use only literal directory roots. Gradle filename selection uses --glob '*.gradle' and --glob '*.gradle.kts'; no positional argument may contain an asterisk.

entries.mistake: The first YouTube public Dev build-control test expected the entire Firebase Android getConfig route as one contiguous source string, while the production wrapper composes its fixed prefix and encoded app path across two expressions.
entries.rootCause: The static assertion bound to formatting layout instead of independently proving the official fixed endpoint and encoded resource suffix.
entries.prevention: Static endpoint tests assert the immutable HTTPS service/version prefix and encoded resource suffix separately, while parse and runtime identity gates prove composition; do not couple a security assertion to harmless line layout.

entries.mistake: C29A's delivery lock passed, but the MVP scope gate treated the host-only ticket as closed because its execution-authorized calculation omitted the declared testOrGateWriteAuthorized field.
entries.rootCause: The scope gate's execution enum predated host-only tickets and considered runtime, backend, build, device and external writes but not test/evidence gate work.
entries.prevention: The scope gate includes the explicit testOrGateWriteAuthorized field in its authorization calculation. Host tickets set only that field true while runtime, backend, build, device and external writes remain false.

entries.mistake: C29A host cycle 1 stopped because the earlier build-boundary work edited accepted production-lock file apps/mobile/test/platform_configuration_test.dart.
entries.rootCause: The new runtime-boundary assertion was added to a broadly relevant existing test without first checking whether that exact test file was protected by an accepted production lock.
entries.prevention: Before editing any existing test, run the approved UI lock inventory. New configuration-boundary assertions live in the dedicated unprotected C29A control test; locked tests remain byte-identical and runtime messages retain their accepted substring.

entries.mistake: The first C29B Java-process CPU diagnostic piped directly after a foreach statement in a form PowerShell parsed as an empty pipe element, so no sample ran.
entries.rootCause: The compact diagnostic mixed statement output and a trailing formatting pipeline without first assigning the generated objects to a collection.
entries.prevention: Process diagnostics assign foreach output to an explicit array variable and pipe that variable to formatting only after the loop completes; parse-safe commands are required before build authorization.

entries.mistake: The C29B no-value Firebase Android client-key metadata gate found that the current key restriction did not match the exact com.moolsocial.app plus installed signing SHA-1 boundary.
entries.rootCause: The Firebase Android SDK configuration can be retrieved, but its auto-associated client key has not yet been qualified as application-restricted to the exact review package and certificate.
entries.prevention: Before the one APK build, inspect only key metadata, require one exact Android package/SHA-1 application restriction and Firebase-only API targets, and stop for a separately authorized bounded Dev correction if the metadata is absent or mismatched. Never read or print the key string.

entries.mistake: The follow-up Firebase Android key diagnostic called GetType on allowedApplications even though that property is absent/null, producing an InvalidOperation after the access-token request.
entries.rootCause: The first diagnostic's array coercion made a null restriction appear as one blank object, and the follow-up did not test for null before inspecting type.
entries.prevention: API-key restriction probes test property existence and null before array conversion or method calls. An absent allowedApplications property is recorded as zero exact Android applications and blocks the build without further ambiguous probes.

entries.mistake: The post-registration regression-memory check invoked a stale shorthand filename that does not exist, so PowerShell stopped before running the repository gate.
entries.rootCause: The command was recalled from memory instead of resolving the repository's exact script filename first.
entries.prevention: Regression-memory checks use the discovered literal path scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1; script names are resolved with rg --files before invocation when not already present in durable evidence.

entries.mistake: The FSC02E gate-discovery command again passed scripts/check-mvp*.ps1 as a Windows path to ripgrep, which rejected the invalid literal path before the search ran.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style filename glob was embedded in the path operand despite the existing Windows wildcard-path prevention entries.
entries.prevention: All remaining ripgrep discovery passes a literal directory root and uses --glob for filename filtering; no wildcard character may appear in a Windows path operand.

entries.mistake: The FSC02E API-key restriction patch and its postwrite assertions completed, but the final safe-summary object used false instead of PowerShell $false, so reporting stopped after the mutation.
entries.rootCause: A JSON boolean literal was used inside PowerShell object construction rather than the PowerShell boolean variable syntax.
entries.prevention: External-write commands use $true and $false in PowerShell output objects, and a reporting-only failure after a completed mutation is never retried as a mutation; completion is established by a separate read-only no-value verification.

entries.mistake: The first full C29B machine-state patch helper attempted to decode a base64 read with TextDecoder, which is not available in the isolated exec JavaScript runtime, so it stopped before apply_patch was called.
entries.rootCause: The helper assumed a browser-standard decoding global without checking the exec isolate's documented helpers.
entries.prevention: ASCII-only repository JSON reads use the base64 binary string from atob directly; unsupported JavaScript globals are not used in patch orchestration, and the target is re-read before retry.

entries.mistake: The second C29B full machine-state patch helper replaced TextDecoder with atob, but atob is also unavailable in the isolated exec JavaScript runtime, so it again stopped before apply_patch.
entries.rootCause: The retry substituted another unverified decoding global instead of eliminating encoding from the orchestration path.
entries.prevention: Patch orchestration reads ASCII repository text directly with PowerShell Get-Content -Raw and extracts the shell output payload; it does not use base64 or JavaScript decoding globals.

entries.mistake: The final C29B prebuild process guard classified any nonzero three-second CPU delta from an existing Java daemon as an active build and stopped before resolving daemon command line or repeated samples.
entries.rootCause: The guard used an over-strict single-sample activity threshold even though earlier evidence identified long-lived Gradle/Kotlin daemons and the registry forbids killing or misclassifying idle daemons.
entries.prevention: Before the sole build, process qualification combines command-line ownership, reserved-output absence and repeated bounded CPU samples. Existing Gradle daemons are acceptable only when no build task process or output exists and activity settles; no daemon is killed merely to force zero CPU.

entries.mistake: The sole C29B wrapper invocation stopped before Flutter because build-buy-device-review.ps1 rejected the active-account inventory under the isolated gcloud configuration.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper's exact Get-Command gcloud plus auth-list boundary was not replayed in the same PowerShell 7 child-process context during C29A; the preflight used an absolute gcloud.cmd call instead.
entries.prevention: C29B authority is consumed with no retry. A separately ticketed successor must diagnose the exact child-process gcloud resolution and output shape without secret access, correct the shared wrapper if required, and pass that exact runtime preflight in two fresh host cycles before any new build authorization.

entries.mistake: The first C29C executable context preflight requested both Application and ExternalScript command types, so Get-Command returned gcloud.ps1, gcloud.cmd and gcloud; casting the collection concatenated their paths into one invalid command.
entries.rootCause: The new context gate treated a multi-command discovery result as a single CommandInfo instead of relying on PowerShell's normal highest-precedence single resolution.
entries.prevention: The context gate uses one ordinary Get-Command gcloud result and validates its nonempty Source before invocation; executable preflight must pass in fresh PowerShell 7 processes before host-cycle qualification.

entries.mistake: The corrected C29C context gate returned a PowerShell object, but the parent harness launched it as an external pwsh process and then attempted ConvertFrom-Json on PowerShell's formatted text output.
entries.rootCause: Serialization was applied in the parent after PowerShell had already rendered the cross-process object for display.
entries.prevention: Fresh-child executable preflight converts the context object to compact JSON inside the child PowerShell 7 process; only that JSON string crosses the process boundary for parent validation.

entries.mistake: C29C host cycle 1 invoked npm run verify from the repository root instead of backend/functions, causing ENOENT and npm to write its automatic failure log under the user npm cache outside the authorized workspace.
entries.rootCause: The reconstructed C29A command retained the isolated Node invocation but omitted the backend/functions working-directory boundary and did not redirect npm cache/log artifacts into the repository.
entries.prevention: Backend qualification Push-Locations into backend/functions before invoking npm and sets NPM_CONFIG_CACHE to a ticket-scoped directory inside artifacts/quality. The outside-workspace npm log is not read, copied or mutated.

entries.mistake: C29C host cycle 1 passed backend, Flutter, player compilation and local provider controls, then invoked the official capability-registry verifier with its default historical expected revisions and stopped on current governed revision drift.
entries.rootCause: The reconstructed C29A cycle included a live official Discovery drift gate whose local governed revision pins had become stale; the verifier intentionally has no bypass arguments.
entries.prevention: C29C pauses for a separate official-registry reconciliation ticket. That ticket may update only governed discoveryRevision fields after the verifier proves identical method counts and no added, removed, scope, HTTP-method or classification drift; C29C then restarts both full host cycles.

entries.mistake: The first FSC02F revision-only patch helper tried to round-trip the full capability registry through shell tool output, which was truncated before the helper could observe all 102 qualified old revision occurrences.
entries.rootCause: A large-file bulk mechanical rewrite was routed through the conversational output channel instead of performed and counted inside one bounded filesystem process.
entries.prevention: The 102-occurrence revision-only rewrite runs in-process with exact before/after counts, UTF-8 without BOM and immediate JSON/semantic-diff verification. Large registry content is never round-tripped through tool output.

entries.mistake: Fresh C29C cycle 1 exited nonzero after component output was redirected, but the harness did not check and label every PowerShell gate immediately, so the failing owner was not surfaced in the terminal result.
entries.rootCause: Only external build/test commands and the official registry command had explicit exit checks; later PowerShell gates relied on global ErrorAction behavior while their output was redirected.
entries.prevention: After ticket-scoped log diagnosis, every host-cycle step runs through a named wrapper that records start/pass/fail, checks invocation success immediately and prints the failing log tail before stopping. A cycle is never counted from partial logs.

entries.mistake: Fresh C29C cycle 1 observed YouTube Data Discovery revision 20260806 minutes after FSC02F observed and pinned 20260810, while the method inventory remained exactly 83/83.
entries.rootCause: The public Google Discovery endpoint can serve inconsistent cached revision markers across requests even when its complete method contract is unchanged; a single exact live-revision pin makes the host gate nondeterministic.
entries.prevention: Do not chase the latest marker with repeated registry rewrites. After registration, sample only allowlisted credential-free Discovery documents, preserve method-contract hashes, and ticket any verifier policy change separately so revision inconsistency cannot bypass method, scope, HTTP-operation or classification drift detection.

entries.mistake: The FSC02G multi-step verification command produced all three durable live-verifier logs, but its exec cell handle was unavailable after context compaction, so the command's final aggregate exit receipt could not be recovered.
entries.rootCause: A long verification sequence depended on an ephemeral orchestration-cell completion result instead of persisting a bounded local receipt for every named step before compaction.
entries.prevention: Long gate sequences write a repository-local named-step receipt with individual exit codes and a final aggregate result. Existing successful step logs are preserved and are not regenerated merely because an orchestration handle is lost.

entries.mistake: The FSC02G status probe assumed the MVP scope state filename was mvp-scope-governance-state.json and produced a read-only path-not-found error.
entries.rootCause: The probe inferred a filename instead of discovering the repository's exact owner, config/mvp-scope-gate-state.json, with rg --files.
entries.prevention: Discover governance-owner filenames with rg --files before reading them; use the exact discovered config/mvp-scope-gate-state.json path for all later scope-state reads and writes.

entries.mistake: The first append patch for FSC02G regressions assumed pretty-printed multiline arrays at the registry tail, so apply_patch rejected the patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: Converted JSON display output was mistaken for the source file's compact array formatting instead of inspecting the exact source tail first.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact literal registry tail before appending and build patch context from that source formatting; rejected atomic patches are never treated as mutations.

entries.mistake: The prior C29C source aggregate included the governed capability registry but omitted scripts/verify-youtube-official-api-capability-registry.mjs even though each host cycle executes that verifier and FSC02G changed it.
entries.rootCause: The earlier manifest expansion tracked the governed data file while treating the verifier as an external gate rather than qualification-affecting repository source.
entries.prevention: C29C's fresh source aggregate includes both the capability registry and its official verifier, validates every listed hash before and after each cycle, and refuses to count a cycle if the 26-file manifest changes.

entries.mistake: The first C29C scope-restore patch combined many distant replacements and assumed compact array formatting, so apply_patch rejected the edit atomically when the exact current state formatting differed.
entries.rootCause: A large state transition patch was prepared from earlier converted output instead of the exact latest source after FSC02G sealing.
entries.prevention: Read the exact latest scope-state source, then replace the bounded selected-ticket block and remaining transition fields with small exact-context patches. Rejected atomic patches are never treated as state changes.

entries.mistake: The second C29C scope-restore attempt still replaced the full nested selection assessment in one long context and was rejected atomically despite a fresh read.
entries.rootCause: The retry reduced distant contexts but retained an unnecessarily large exact-match block with too many formatting-sensitive lines.
entries.prevention: Apply only short one-line or tightly bounded field replacements, validate JSON after each bounded transition, and avoid whole-object apply_patch contexts for large governance state files.

entries.mistake: A later C29C scope-restore patch again grouped three logically separate array and state hunks; one dependency hunk did not match and caused the complete patch to be rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: The transition still bundled unrelated exact replacements rather than using the registered one-field-at-a-time prevention.
entries.prevention: After rereading the exact affected lines, apply each exclusion, dependency and state group independently; validate the complete JSON only after all bounded edits land.

entries.mistake: The C29C command-availability probe invoked default PATH tools, revealing Node 24.14.1 instead of the qualified Node 22 runtime and then failing because Java was not on PATH.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic did not resolve the workspace-bundled dependency runtime paths before invoking version checks.
entries.prevention: Load the configured workspace dependency paths, invoke the exact Node 22 and Android/Gradle-owned Java runtimes by absolute path, and never qualify from ambient PATH versions.

entries.mistake: The C29C Node-runtime evidence search again passed wildcard-bearing Windows directory operands to ripgrep, causing invalid-path errors after an unrelated package.json read succeeded.
entries.rootCause: The search repeated the permanently registered Windows wildcard-path error instead of using literal roots plus --glob filename filters.
entries.prevention: Every remaining ripgrep search uses literal repository directories as operands and --glob filters for filenames or path fragments; wildcard-bearing Windows path operands are forbidden.

entries.mistake: The read-only search for the ticket-scoped npx Node 22 executable returned no files because ripgrep honored ignore rules inside the npm cache's node_modules tree.
entries.rootCause: The probe used default ignored-file behavior for a deliberately vendored ticket evidence cache.
entries.prevention: For the exact repository-contained npm cache only, use rg --files -uu or a literal bounded Get-ChildItem query; never broaden the search outside the ticket evidence directory.

entries.mistake: Fresh C29C qualifying cycle 1 exited nonzero after 228 seconds, but the orchestration result exposed no named failing owner or log tail even though the harness intended to print both.
entries.rootCause: The outer shell tool returned only its aggregate nonzero status, so relying on terminal propagation remained insufficient for diagnosis despite per-step durable logs.
entries.prevention: The failed cycle remains uncounted and immutable. Diagnose only its repository-local step logs, then use a new cycle prefix whose harness always writes a partial machine-readable receipt in a top-level catch before exiting nonzero.

entries.mistake: Uncounted C29C cycle 1 passed backend 471, Flutter 82, both player compiles, controls and the official 99-method gate, then its fresh PowerShell child could not resolve gcloud from the long-running Codex process's inherited PATH.
entries.rootCause: Google Cloud CLI was installed after the Codex desktop process started, so its exact SDK bin directory was not inherited by child shells even though the CLI and isolated configuration exist.
entries.prevention: Every successor host cycle and the later one-build wrapper invocation prepend the exact installed Google Cloud SDK bin directory to that bounded process PATH, verify the resolved source, and make no system PATH, gcloud configuration, token or cloud mutation.

entries.mistake: The first successor C29C qualifying cycle after gcloud PATH remediation still exited nonzero after 230 seconds and therefore cannot be counted.
entries.rootCause: The exact failing owner is intentionally deferred until after permanent registration; unlike the prior attempt, a durable partial machine-readable receipt now preserves every completed step and the error message.
entries.prevention: Preserve this failed prefix, diagnose only its partial receipt and named failing log, correct the exact owner if in scope, and restart both required complete cycles under new prefixes with the same immutable 26-file manifest.

entries.mistake: Uncounted C29C cycle A passed all runtime, compile, provider and context steps, then invoked the accepted global-navigation contract with -RequireImplemented and failed on unrelated incomplete C23 Home-hub owners.
entries.rootCause: The reconstructed C29A gate call strengthened a reusable accepted-contract check with a portfolio-wide implementation flag that C29C neither owns nor changes.
entries.prevention: C29C invokes check-personal-mool-global-navigation-contract.ps1 without -RequireImplemented, while retaining the focused Social/Shop navigation and exported-semantics gates. Unrelated incomplete portfolio owners cannot be used to qualify or reject this unchanged Social runtime source.

entries.mistake: The first C29D structural prebuild gate launched check-apk-regression-gate-state.ps1 through pwsh -File and passed a PowerShell string array to -RuntimeDefine; the child CLI treated the second define as an unsupported positional argument.
entries.rootCause: In-process array binding was incorrectly assumed to survive the external PowerShell command-line boundary.
entries.prevention: Invoke the APK gate directly in the current PowerShell process with -RuntimeDefine $defines, or use explicit argument-list serialization owned by the build wrapper. No wrapper invocation or Flutter build occurred before this failure.

entries.mistake: The first authorized C29D launch succeeded, but uiautomator dump /dev/tty returned no XML on the OPPO, so the launch hierarchy and screenshot sequence stopped before capture.
entries.rootCause: This Android 13 uiautomator build does not emit the hierarchy document to /dev/tty in the form assumed by the host parser.
entries.prevention: Use one ticket-scoped filename under /sdcard/Download, pull the generated XML into the immutable evidence directory, and never clear app data or reinstall merely to recover a hierarchy capture.

entries.mistake: The first bounded C29D app-log capture assigned the package process id to $pid, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's read-only automatic $PID variable and stopping before logcat capture.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic reused a common process identifier name that is reserved by PowerShell.
entries.prevention: Use the task-specific $moolAppProcessId variable for all device log captures, retain credential redaction before persistence, and never repurpose PowerShell automatic variables.

entries.mistake: A bounded read-only search for player-state UI consumers included apps/mobile/lib/features/social, which does not exist, so ripgrep returned nonzero after producing excessive output from the valid YouTube core root.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic inferred a feature-directory owner instead of first resolving exact files from the repository file list, and its broad term set made the valid-side output unnecessarily large.
entries.prevention: Resolve relevant owner files with rg --files under the exact mobile lib root, then search only literal existing files with a narrow pattern and bounded output; this read-only failure does not authorize any build, install or runtime mutation.

entries.mistake: A read-only ripgrep extraction of text and content-desc attributes embedded nested double quotes inside the PowerShell command string, causing a parser error before the evidence file was read.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic mixed regular-expression quoting and the outer PowerShell quoting layer without using a literal single-quoted pattern.
entries.prevention: Use PowerShell literal single-quoted regular-expression arguments or parse the ticket-scoped XML as XML; validate command quoting before any retry and keep all operands exact and literal.

entries.mistake: A read-only attempt to locate node.exe inside the C29C evidence root returned no match because that immutable evidence retained receipts and caches but not an executable at the inferred path.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic inferred that the previously qualified Node binary was copied into evidence instead of reading its exact path from the C29C receipt or using a runtime-independent diagnostic.
entries.prevention: Read the exact qualified runtime path from the preserved C29C machine receipt before invoking it, or use built-in PowerShell/.NET for the bounded diagnostic; never broaden filesystem search beyond the workspace.

entries.mistake: The required computer-use skill resource could not be read at the exact registered SKILL.md path because that versioned installation path is absent on the host.
entries.rootCause: The available-skills catalog referenced a stale or unavailable versioned plugin-cache path.
entries.prevention: Do not infer or install a replacement plugin. Report the unavailable skill, retain the exact failure, and use only a founder-authorized read-only ADB screenshot inventory and local image inspection fallback inside the MoolSocial scope.

entries.mistake: The bounded YouTube owner inventory passed inferred services and functions roots that do not exist at the repository top level, causing ripgrep to return nonzero even though valid app and deployment matches were printed.
entries.rootCause: The audit assumed common backend directory names instead of resolving repository owners from the root file list first.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files from the exact repository root, filter the resulting paths for YouTube/provider owners, then inspect only verified literal files; never infer missing roots or suppress their errors as qualification evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C29E scope transition grouped the assessment, ticket, authority and protected-candidate replacements into one overlong patch; one test-plan line differed from the expected context and the entire patch was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: The transition relied on a large stale copied block instead of independently patching freshly inspected short sections.
entries.prevention: Apply the C29E scope transition as small independent hunks: assessment block, checkpoint/ticket block, disclosure/authority block and protected-state block, validating JSON and manifest hash after each complete transition.

entries.mistake: The second C29E scope transition still grouped four ticket arrays and later authority blocks; apply_patch rejected the group despite the visible ticket lines because the compound verification context was not minimal.
entries.rootCause: The correction reduced the patch size but did not isolate each mutable array and later object into independent hunks.
entries.prevention: Patch each ticket array and each disclosure, authority or protected-state field independently with the shortest exact neighboring context, then validate the completed JSON once all required fields are aligned.

entries.mistake: The isolated C29E test-plan patch repeated the stale APK evidence string from the earlier failed compound patch instead of the current badging-version-and-source-audit line, so apply_patch rejected it.
entries.rootCause: The retry reused remembered text rather than copying the freshly printed exact five-line array.
entries.prevention: For every rejected state hunk, re-read and copy the exact current lines immediately before the next patch; never reuse a previously rejected expected block.

entries.mistake: The first C29E permanent-regression gate call used Phase runtime, but the script accepts only general, implementation, build or device; parameter binding stopped before gate execution.
entries.rootCause: The phase name was inferred from scope authority rather than read from the gate's ValidateSet.
entries.prevention: Use Phase implementation for C29E Flutter source and test execution, build only for a separately authorized build candidate, and device only for separately authorized device work.

entries.mistake: The corrected C29E regression-memory call added a TicketId parameter, but this gate accepts only Phase, BuildMode and RepositoryRoot, so binding stopped before execution.
entries.rootCause: The invocation borrowed a ticket-scoping convention from other gates without first reading this script's param block.
entries.prevention: Invoke check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 with only its declared parameters; use Phase implementation and the default repository root for C29E source work.

entries.mistake: The first focused C29E Home-and-dock analyzer run found the legacy navy _YouTubeSurfaceBar declaration unreachable after the new provider-owned Home and watch headers replaced every call site.
entries.rootCause: The first source patch replaced all uses but retained the private legacy widget while keeping the analyzer's zero-warning contract.
entries.prevention: When a bounded UI owner is fully superseded, confirm its remaining reference count with ripgrep and remove only the now-unreachable private declaration before rerunning the focused analyzer.

entries.mistake: The first full-bleed Shorts patch placed an object-pattern case expression directly after the false branch of a ternary, which Dart does not parse as an expression in that position.
entries.rootCause: A valid pattern-if idiom was incorrectly transferred into a nested conditional expression while selecting the nullable thumbnail fallback.
entries.prevention: Use an explicit null comparison and non-null assertion for a nullable thumbnail inside a ternary, or extract a small widget builder; run dart format and the focused analyzer immediately after structural UI rewrites.

entries.mistake: The first full-bleed focused source-contract test still ended the Shorts source slice at the removed _openShortDiscussion method, so indexOf returned -1 before the redesigned assertions ran.
entries.rootCause: The production patch truthfully removed the old embedded MoolSocial action owner, but the test's structural delimiter was not advanced to the next surviving method in the same source patch.
entries.prevention: When deleting a private method that is also a static test delimiter, update the delimiter to the next stable surviving owner and retain direct assertions that the removed method and UI keys stay absent.

entries.mistake: A bounded reuse search for social comment or reply mutation methods in SharedSession and shared models returned no match and ripgrep exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The published-content presentation exposes a reply callback, but the current shared persistence owner has no matching durable reply mutation under the searched social-comment vocabulary.
entries.prevention: Do not invent reply persistence or treat a presentation callback as backend authority. Render real stored published items, keep reply submission truthfully unavailable, and only enable it after a genuine shared-session or provider owner and focused tests exist.

entries.mistake: The first C29E creation test stored a genuine MoolSocial post and navigated to Feed, but Feed rendered only its empty-state shell instead of projecting SharedSession.socialPublishedItems.
entries.rootCause: The prior Feed redesign established ownership branding and truthful empty states without reconnecting the existing real published-content presentation owner.
entries.prevention: Project non-Reel SharedSession publications through SocialPublishedContentCardV2 before showing the empty state, and keep a focused publish-to-Feed test on the exact customer-visible card key.

entries.mistake: A predecessor Create test still required the Reel tool after the founder explicitly constrained MoolSocial Create to text, image, carousel, image poll, quick poll and quiz, with YouTube video distribution separately gated.
entries.rootCause: The older direct-workbench contract conflated MoolSocial-hosted Reel creation with the newly separated YouTube-owned Shorts distribution journey.
entries.prevention: Keep the reusable workbench Reel feature opt-in for other owners, pass allowReel false from SocialUniversalV2, and assert the Social Create surface exposes only the founder-approved MoolSocial formats.

entries.mistake: The first bounded-pagination suite retained a static assertion for the removed single-page expression final eligible = page.items even though the new collector tests already passed target, deduplication and shortfall behavior.
entries.rootCause: The empty-vs-error source contract was coupled to an implementation-specific local variable from the predecessor one-page loader.
entries.prevention: Assert the stable collectScreen04YouTubeCatalogue and unmodifiable empty-return contract, and rely on behavioral page tests for target, dedupe, limits and shortfall instead of predecessor local-variable text.

entries.mistake: The first post-C29E regression-memory gate found new registry gates entries containing command labels such as flutter analyze, dart format and flutter test, which are not repository paths.
entries.rootCause: Focused commands were recorded as if the gates field were a descriptive command list, but the registry validator treats every gate value as a literal repository evidence owner that must exist.
entries.prevention: Record only existing repository-relative scripts or test files in the gates field; keep command outcomes in execution evidence or prose, and validate the registry immediately after adding a new schema pattern.

entries.mistake: A grouped four-file legacy Social matrix reached its 240-second command timeout without emitting a terminal test owner in the captured shell result.
entries.rootCause: Slow and potentially incompatible legacy suites were grouped under one outer timeout, so the orchestration boundary could not identify which file owned the delay or preserve partial reporter output.
entries.prevention: Run each legacy Social file as an individually bounded expanded-reporter command, identify and reconcile the exact owner, then run an accepted combined manifest only after every file has an independent terminal result.

entries.mistake: A read-only Get-Process dart,flutter probe returned nonzero because flutter was absent even though PowerShell printed one unrelated long-lived dart process.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic passed multiple literal process names to Get-Process with a shared error boundary, causing a missing optional name to control the command exit code.
entries.prevention: Use Get-Process followed by a Where-Object name filter when optional process names are expected, and never terminate an existing process unless its exact test-runner ownership is proven and termination is authorized.

entries.mistake: The first individual Screen 04 conformance run had eleven failures because the suite still assumed fresh Social opened on Shorts, a shared four-choice ribbon owned Social, Reel belonged to MoolSocial Create, and MoolSocial action overlays lived on YouTube Shorts.
entries.rootCause: The broad file mixed durable route, Back and compact-fitment contracts with presentation and ownership assumptions explicitly superseded by the founder-approved C29E Home, five-item dock, full-bleed Shorts and separated creation model.
entries.prevention: Retain every durable route, Back, provider-fail-closed and compact-fitment assertion; migrate only the superseded Social presentation checks to Home-first, the C29E dock, no Short overlays and no Social Reel, and independently prove the Mool button reaches the accepted global navigator.

entries.mistake: A bounded source read targeted apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/screen04/mool_global_navigation_v2.dart, but the accepted Mool navigation owner is stored at a different repository path and Get-Content returned nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The read reused a logical component namespace as a filesystem directory without first resolving the concrete tracked path.
entries.prevention: Resolve source owners with rg --files before line reads whenever the exact path has not already been proven in the current execution record; then read only the matched repository path.

entries.mistake: The first C29E shared-navigator integration kept the accepted compact Mool launcher in the rightmost dock cell, but its connected menu retained the predecessor left-edge anchoring and extended beyond the viewport, making family actions unhittable.
entries.rootCause: MoolGlobalNavigationV2 previously exposed only a left-aligned compact overlay geometry because all accepted predecessor placements anchored the launcher near the left edge; the new five-cell Social dock truthfully places Mool at the right edge.
entries.prevention: Add an explicit opt-in end-aligned compact overlay geometry to the shared navigator, preserve the default for every existing caller, use the end alignment only in the C29E dock, and keep route, Chat, Back and compact-size tests on that placement.

entries.mistake: The second Screen 04 migration run retained a predecessor family-specific social-global-chat finder and an immediate all-actions owner assertion that did not observe the current accepted connected-navigation key and route lifecycle.
entries.rootCause: The earlier broad migration changed superseded Social presentation contracts but did not re-resolve the connected navigator's durable Chat key or independently settle each successive Social route before asserting its provider owner.
