entries.prevention: Resolve current connected-action keys from the shared navigator source, preserve the genuine Chat callback journey, and pump each route transition to its terminal state before checking the selected Social owner without weakening route exactness.

entries.mistake: The C29E consumer and local dock opened YouTube Home first, but the shared Mool action catalogue still listed Shorts first and labelled the videos action Videos, so default-action helpers and connected navigation disagreed with the approved Home-first model.
entries.rootCause: The first implementation updated the Screen 04 world catalogue without reconciling the independent shared MoolActionFamilySpec catalogue used by connected navigation.
entries.prevention: Keep the Social action catalogue ordered Home, Shorts, Create, Feed with Home mapped to the existing videos route, and verify both direct local taps and connected-family default navigation against the same approved order.

entries.mistake: The third Screen 04 migration run expected the MoolSocial workbench immediately after the local center Create control, even though the approved C29E center plus intentionally opens the MoolSocial-versus-YouTube ownership gateway.
entries.rootCause: One all-actions test conflated the local dock Create journey with the explicit sub=create route; only the latter truthfully selects MoolSocial Create before entry.
entries.prevention: Assert the ownership gateway for the center plus journey, retain direct-route and gateway-selection tests for the MoolSocial workbench, and never bypass the YouTube authorization gate by treating all Create entry points as equivalent.

entries.mistake: The individually bounded social_v2_moolsocial_feed_ownership_test.dart process emitted no test reporter output and reached its 300-second outer timeout.
entries.rootCause: The file has a non-terminal runner or teardown condition that is independent of the previously resolved grouped-matrix orchestration problem; the captured process did not identify a failing assertion.
entries.prevention: Do not immediately repeat the same whole-file invocation. First reconcile the founder-approved global Chat dock correction, inspect the file's test boundaries and asynchronous owners, then run individually filtered tests with bounded reporters to isolate the non-terminal case.

entries.mistake: The focused C29E test still expected a simple compact Mool tap to invoke the direct onOpenMool callback after the dock had been corrected to reuse the accepted connected switcher.
entries.rootCause: The original custom dock cell navigated directly, while MoolGlobalNavigationV2 correctly uses the first tap to open the connected family navigator without increasing the eventual family-action tap count.
entries.prevention: Assert the connected navigator overlay on the launcher tap, keep the direct callback false at that stage, and rely on route-level conformance tests to select a family and prove the destination journey.

entries.mistake: The Screen 04 suite still asserted that social-global-chat was absent on YouTube Home after the founder explicitly confirmed Chat should remain common on Social.
entries.rootCause: That assertion was introduced during the brief design state where YouTube surfaces removed all prior header controls, before the founder resolved the global-navigation question in favor of retaining Chat.
entries.prevention: Require exactly one bottom-dock Chat control on every Social owner, keep it outside the official player, and prove Chat plus system Back restores the exact YouTube Home provider state.

entries.mistake: The individually filtered stored-publication Feed widget test reached its 120-second outer timeout without a terminal reporter result, while the same file's static ownership test passed independently.
entries.rootCause: The non-terminal owner is now bounded to the widget test's direct SharedSession publication setup or its lifecycle, rather than file loading or the static source contract.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact publishSocialContent persistence path and existing passing publication-test setup before retry; do not repeat the same direct await or weaken the requirement that a genuine stored post appears in Feed.

entries.mistake: The isolated Feed state test found the Retry control but tapped it at y=593 on a 568-high viewport because the ensureVisible scroll had not been pumped to its settled position.
entries.rootCause: The test awaited Scrollable.ensureVisible but omitted pumpAndSettle before hit testing the compact-layout control.
entries.prevention: After ensureVisible on an off-screen compact control, settle the scroll animation before measuring or tapping, and retain the post-retry empty-state assertion.

entries.mistake: The first individual continuous Social batch retained two predecessor assumptions: a fresh consumer should expose the Shorts provider gate and the old Screen04Header profile key should exist on YouTube Home.
entries.rootCause: C29E intentionally makes Home the fresh Social destination and removes old MoolSocial top chrome from YouTube-owned surfaces while preserving the same account owner behind a provider-styled Home affordance.
entries.prevention: Pass sub=shorts for Shorts-specific fail-closed tests, use the YouTube Home account key for Home account journeys, and retain downstream Creator workspace and Plans assertions to prove owner reuse.

entries.mistake: The migrated account-owner test searched for the provider-styled Home account key while its default test setup deliberately had no YouTube public provider access, so _buildVideos returned the provider gate before the available-catalogue Home header.
entries.rootCause: The test changed the finder without changing its provider-gated fixture, conflating account-owner verification with available-provider Home presentation.
entries.prevention: Verify the shared account owner from MoolSocial Feed's always-present header in the continuous batch, and leave available-provider YouTube Home account presentation to the focused C29E fixture with real catalogue overrides.

entries.mistake: The first post-C29E protected Social baseline check stopped because the current authorized inventory contains 180 files while the accepted predecessor baseline records 178.
entries.rootCause: C29E introduced necessary ticket/test evidence within the protected Social inventory, and the baseline gate correctly requires an explicit successor-baseline audit rather than silently accepting new files.
entries.prevention: Resolve the exact inventory delta, read the repository's founder-approved baseline replacement procedure, update only through that procedure when current authority covers the successor, and never weaken or bypass the gate.

entries.mistake: A bounded C29 protected-baseline search passed wildcard path expressions directly to ripgrep after a successful directory listing, and the combined command returned nonzero without search matches.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell did not resolve the mixed docs/config/artifacts wildcard operands into the intended existing file set for ripgrep's path handling.
entries.prevention: Search proven parent directories with ripgrep include globs and filter result paths by C29 in the pattern or pipeline; do not pass shell wildcard path operands whose expansion semantics are unverified.

entries.mistake: The first extra protected-test batch found two named-state parity failures because it still required a Reel source inside MoolSocial Create and expected a fresh Social consumer to show the Shorts provider gate.
entries.rootCause: The parity matrix had not been migrated to the founder-approved separation where MoolSocial hosts no Reel or Shorts and Social opens YouTube Home first.
entries.prevention: Remove Reel-specific MoolSocial Create states from the parity map, retain all six approved MoolSocial formats, and pass an explicit Shorts subaction for Shorts fail-closed coverage.

entries.mistake: A compact protected-tree recomputation named its relative-path helper R, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's r alias for Invoke-History and producing repeated history errors plus an invalid zero-file hash while the shell exit remained zero.
entries.rootCause: The shortened helper name was a common PowerShell alias and error records inside the pipeline did not control the final command exit code.
entries.prevention: Use a task-specific non-alias helper such as Get-C29ERelativePath, require the expected 180-file count before accepting any hash, and validate the result with check-social-protected-baseline against the additive seal.

entries.mistake: A historical C16B Social conformance script was invoked during C29E acceptance even though its own guard requires the C16B MVP selection and disclosure to be the active sequential ticket.
entries.rootCause: The gate was selected by its broad Social filename rather than first auditing whether its ticket-specific precondition matched the current C29E scope state.
entries.prevention: Run current ticket, shared invariant and explicitly reusable gates for C29E; inspect historical gate preconditions before invocation and never force or bypass an inactive ticket guard.

entries.mistake: The first post-build C29F aapt badging command passed the long repository-relative APK path; aapt reported that the asset path was neither a directory nor a file even though PowerShell had already proved the file existed.
entries.rootCause: The Android build-tools process did not resolve the long relative path under its native path handling in the same way as PowerShell.
entries.prevention: Resolve candidate and predecessor APKs to absolute paths before every aapt or apksigner invocation, retain the already-built checksum, and never rebuild or install in response to an artifact-inspection path failure.

entries.mistake: The second C29F badging attempt resolved the APK to its full absolute repository path, but aapt still rejected the existing file because the native asset path exceeded its supported Windows path handling.
entries.rootCause: Absolute-path resolution corrected relativity but not the build tool's long-path limitation for the deeply nested immutable evidence filename.
entries.prevention: Map the existing candidate and predecessor artifact directories to temporary unused drive letters, inspect the same checksum-bound files through short native paths, remove both mappings in finally, and never copy, rebuild or install to work around path length.

entries.mistake: The first C29F runtime semantic capture requested uiautomator dump /dev/tty after a successful app launch, but Android returned no XML hierarchy for in-memory parsing.
entries.rootCause: This OPPO Android 13 uiautomator build did not stream the hierarchy through /dev/tty even though the activity was running successfully.
entries.prevention: Use one exact candidate-specific temporary XML path outside app storage, read it immediately into memory, remove only that verified temporary path, and never infer an app failure from missing /dev/tty output.

entries.mistake: The first C29F Home-to-video semantic command assigned its parsed hierarchy to $home, which PowerShell resolved case-insensitively as the read-only $HOME variable and rejected before any video tap.
entries.rootCause: The task-local variable name collided with a protected common shell variable under PowerShell's case-insensitive variable semantics.
entries.prevention: Use task-specific names such as $c29fHomeXml and $c29fWatchXml, never repurpose $HOME or $home, and treat the stopped command as tooling-only rather than an app failure.

entries.mistake: The corrected C29F Home-to-video command required a video card from a single immediate hierarchy and stopped when the real public provider was still in a truthful loading or transition state.
entries.rootCause: The runtime check treated asynchronous provider availability as instantaneous after returning from Shorts instead of gating the tap on an actual loaded video semantic.
entries.prevention: Poll the semantic hierarchy for a bounded interval, continue while the truthful loading state is present, tap only a real loaded Watch card, and preserve error/shortfall states as evidence rather than fabricating availability.

entries.mistake: The first C29F bounds evidence capture mapped the artifact directory to Q: and passed Q:\04-first-runtime-home.xml as the adb pull destination, but adb reported that it could not create the destination.
entries.rootCause: ADB's Windows destination handling did not accept the substituted-drive target even though aapt and apksigner accepted the same short-drive technique for reads.
entries.prevention: Run adb pull with the exact artifact directory as the process working directory and a short filename destination, verify checksums there, and do not copy, move, rebuild or mutate app data to work around the destination quirk.

entries.mistake: C29F reached the OPPO with a visually full-width YouTube player, but the Shorts body remained below an opaque 41dp status strip and the six bottom controls exported only 20.5-24dp semantic heights instead of the locked 44dp minimum.
entries.rootCause: The Social-only dock bypassed the accepted Android exported-semantics clearance owner used by the shared destination navigation, while the YouTube-owned Scaffold still applied a top SafeArea and opaque status color to Shorts.
entries.prevention: Reuse moolAndroidExportedSemanticsClearance for the Social dock, require every exported Social control including Mool to be at least 44 logical pixels high, draw only the Shorts playback surface behind a transparent status bar, and reject every future APK before founder review when OPPO bounds or edge-to-edge geometry differ.

entries.mistake: C29F exposed internal delivery commentary to customers, including GATED, owner OAuth, provider capability, authorization requirements, Firebase-authenticated, upload scope, lifecycle requirements and will-not-simulate language.
entries.rootCause: The unavailable future YouTube upload dependency was designed as a visible customer card and diagnostic sheet instead of remaining an internal machine gate, and the rendered-copy suite did not mount that reachable center-plus journey.
entries.prevention: Never render roadmap, gate, provider, API, OAuth, Firebase, scope, lifecycle, simulation, persistence, test-target or implementation commentary in customer UI. Hide unavailable future capabilities, route the center plus directly to the truthful available MoolSocial creator, mount every reachable Social state in the customer-copy gate, and retain plain benefit or recovery copy only.

entries.mistake: A C29G read-only diagnostic combined full device-gate documents, a complete script and a broad documentation-tree search in one bounded shell call and reached the outer timeout before returning reliable evidence.
entries.rootCause: The search scope still included the large docs/quality tree even though the exact C28D document, C28F script and source owner had already been identified.
entries.prevention: Read one exact evidence owner or one verified source range per command, keep searches inside named source/test files, and never combine a large documentation-tree scan with full-file reads in the same process.

entries.mistake: The first C29G MVP scope-state patch combined the assessment, ticket, authorization and execution transitions while assuming an earlier rejected-ticket scalar still matched the current dirty file; apply_patch rejected the entire mutation.
entries.rootCause: The current JSON was inspected before C29F rejection registration, but the broad patch was composed against a stale quoted block instead of rereading the exact post-registration state.
entries.prevention: Confirm the rejected patch changed nothing, read the exact current assessment and ticket blocks, patch one bounded section at a time, parse JSON after each section, and recompute the selected-ticket manifest hash before running the scope gate.

entries.mistake: A bounded source-range locator searched for the prefix class _SocialOwnershipDock and matched both that class and _SocialOwnershipDockItem, producing an Object[] arithmetic error before the intended read.
entries.rootCause: The anchored regular expression stopped at the shared class-name prefix and did not include the exact extends signature or opening delimiter.
entries.prevention: Resolve class ranges with exact full signatures such as '^class _SocialOwnershipDock extends', assert exactly one start and one end line, and stop before indexing when either result is not scalar.

entries.mistake: The first post-removal prohibited-copy search found zero matching strings as intended, but the command did not accept ripgrep exit code 1 and surfaced the valid empty result as a failed diagnostic.
entries.rootCause: A verification search was treated like a required-match discovery command even though absence was the acceptance condition.
entries.prevention: Use Select-String for optional absence checks or explicitly accept ripgrep exit code 1, while still failing on exit codes above 1.

entries.mistake: The first Screen 04 customer-copy matrix used pumpAndSettle after each mount and timed out on a continuously scheduled Social visual state before reaching the later copy assertions.
entries.rootCause: Rendered-copy inspection requires stable text and semantics, not global animation quiescence; the generic helper inherited a settle strategy that is unsuitable for continuous loading or decorative animation.
entries.prevention: Use a bounded number of fixed-duration pumps for Social copy snapshots, explicitly advance only the asynchronous loader transitions under test, and keep pumpAndSettle out of continuous loading states.

entries.mistake: The first C29G edge-to-edge test set FakeViewPadding on the test view but did not inject the corresponding MediaQuery padding, so the non-Shorts owner measured at y=0 instead of the expected OPPO top inset.
entries.rootCause: The test assumed MaterialApp would derive the exact synthetic padding used by the accepted C28F harness, while that harness explicitly supplies padding and viewPadding through MediaQuery.
entries.prevention: Wrap the tested Social root in MediaQueryData with the exact OPPO padding and viewPadding, then assert Shorts consumes the top padding and MoolSocial owners retain it.

entries.mistake: The first Social clearance assertion hardcoded a 29dp lift and expected a 95dp wrapper, while the accepted shared token calculation correctly produced a 27dp lift and a 93dp wrapper.
entries.rootCause: The expectation inferred destinationRailHeight instead of calling the shared moolAndroidExportedSemanticsClearance owner used by production.
entries.prevention: Compute the expected Social clearance with the shared function and exact OPPO view padding; never duplicate or infer its token arithmetic in a successor test.

entries.mistake: The first passing C29G semantic-bounds run registered SemanticsHandle.dispose with addTearDown, but Flutter's end-of-test verification ran while the handle was still active and failed the suite.
entries.rootCause: The handle lifecycle was tied to general teardown rather than the bounded semantics-inspection phase inside the test body.
entries.prevention: Dispose the SemanticsHandle immediately after the last semantic rectangle assertion, before continuing non-semantic navigation checks or returning from the test.

entries.mistake: A post-compaction verification used shorthand permanent-regression filenames from the handoff and attempted two reads at paths that do not exist in the repository.
entries.rootCause: The compacted context described the registry by role instead of preserving its exact repository filenames, and the read did not first resolve those filenames with the repository file index.
entries.prevention: Treat compacted path summaries as contextual hints, resolve regression owners with a bounded rg --files lookup when their exact names are not preserved, and then reuse the resolved codex-development registry and memory paths for the rest of the ticket.

entries.mistake: The first C29G host cycle reused moolAndroidExportedSemanticsClearance from Social production code while the accepted shared function still carried a visibleForTesting annotation, so full Flutter analysis rejected the production call.
entries.rootCause: The clearance owner originated as a shared-navigation test seam and its API annotation was not promoted when the successor established a second production consumer.
entries.prevention: When an accepted test seam becomes a cross-owner production token, remove only the test-only annotation at its shared owner, retain one implementation, and require full Flutter analysis before a host cycle can qualify.

entries.mistake: REG1187 initially placed the human-readable command label flutter analyze in its gates array, and the permanent-memory checker rejected it as a missing repository file before the focused retry.
entries.rootCause: The entry described the intended validation command in a machine field whose repository contract permits only existing repository-relative gate paths.
entries.prevention: Keep command names and audit labels in prose; every regression gates array contains only verified repository-relative files that exist before the entry is saved.

entries.mistake: The first complete C29G protected Social test batch retained three assertions for provider-access and unverified-video delivery commentary that the founder rejected and the customer-copy gate now prohibits.
entries.rootCause: Focused copy tests and the main C29G journey were updated first, but two older broad conformance owners were not included in the initial copy-expectation audit.
entries.prevention: When customer copy is permanently rejected, search every protected Social test owner for the old exact literals, replace expectations with finished recovery copy, assert the rejected commentary is absent, and run the full protected batch before qualification.

entries.mistake: A post-cycle evidence read appended an unrestricted git status --short to an otherwise bounded 18-file manifest query and flooded the result with the repository's large preserved dirty inventory.
entries.rootCause: The branch and HEAD reconciliation needed no full status replay because the complete dirty tree had already been preserved and the cycle fingerprint explicitly named the C29G source owners.
entries.prevention: During successor evidence sealing, report branch and HEAD separately and inspect only the named ticket paths; do not emit the full dirty status after the tree has already been reconciled and preserved.

entries.mistake: The first C29H live source audit reused the C29G host aggregate manifest, but that manifest included mvp-scope-gate-state.json and therefore drifted when C29H became the selected device ticket.
entries.rootCause: A host-cycle evidence aggregate was treated as an APK build-source manifest even though it contained mutable ticket-selection and regression-record metadata rather than only runtime and protected test owners.
entries.prevention: APK build-source manifests exclude candidate ticket, MVP selection, regression registry, memory and qualification evidence. Derive a separate manifest from runtime and protected test owners, qualify it twice after candidate selection, and bind the APK gate only to that stable manifest.

entries.mistake: The single C29H wrapper invocation was opened after recording a no-token gcloud-context pass that had not actually run in the final post-manifest prebuild sequence; the wrapper then stopped because Get-Command gcloud could not see the installed x86 CLI path.
entries.rootCause: Google Cloud CLI was installed after the Codex process started, so its well-known path existed but the long-lived shell PATH was stale. The prebuild seal inferred the context from earlier evidence instead of requiring a same-shell executable-path check immediately before candidate authorization.
entries.prevention: Resolve gcloud from PATH or the exact installed well-known x86 path inside the shared context gate, add a self-test assertion for that fallback, require the exact same-shell no-token context gate after the final source manifest is live, and consume a failed wrapper candidate without retry.

entries.mistake: The final C29I prebuild replay invoked the permanent-regression checker with Phase prebuild, but the gate accepts only general, implementation, build or device and stopped before executing any prebuild check.
entries.rootCause: The workflow stage label was reused as a command parameter instead of selecting the gate's declared build phase, recurring the already registered unsupported-phase class.
entries.prevention: APK prebuild replays invoke check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 with Phase build and BuildMode profile; phase arguments must be taken from the script ValidateSet before the combined command is formed.

entries.mistake: Three C29I artifact qualification attempts passed the retained APK to Android build-tools aapt through the long repository-relative path, absolute path and artifact-directory basename; aapt reported each as neither a directory nor a file and stopped before badging inspection.
entries.rootCause: The C29I evidence directory plus descriptive APK filename exceeds this Windows aapt asset-path handling boundary; changing only the argument form cannot shorten the resolved filesystem path even though PowerShell can read and checksum the exact file.
entries.prevention: Keep the sealed APK immutable, create one short-path repository-local hard link using the extended-length form for the long source, require its SHA-256 and byte length to equal the sealed owner, and pass that short alias to aapt and apksigner. Provenance remains bound to the sealed owner, and a path rejection never counts as artifact evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C29I Home-to-video device parser assigned its already captured hierarchy to $home, recurring the exact C29F protected HOME-variable failure and stopping before the video card tap.
entries.rootCause: A generic screen-domain noun was used despite the explicit workspace rule and permanent REG1173 device-journey prevention; PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell device parser uses a candidate-specific name such as $c29iHomeHierarchy and never assigns to $HOME, $home, $Host or $host. Preserve the existing capture and resume from it without repeating already completed actions.

entries.mistake: C29I's Social dock and switcher rows passed OPPO bounds, but the shared non-compact Mool toggle on Chat exported only 46 physical pixels, or 23 logical pixels at 320 dpi, below the permanent 44 logical-pixel minimum.
entries.rootCause: MoolDestinationNavigationV2 applies moolAndroidExportedSemanticsClearance around compact destination rails, while standalone non-compact MoolGlobalNavigationV2 consumers such as Chat reach the launcher without that shared clearance.
entries.prevention: Reuse moolAndroidExportedSemanticsClearance for standalone non-compact global launcher placement, keep compact rails single-applied by their destination owner, protect both paths with OPPO viewPadding widget tests, and require real Chat UIAutomator bounds before founder handoff.

entries.mistake: The first C29J viewport test run stopped in the existing C28E case because its four-label loop still searched for the pre-redesign Social semantics instead of the accepted current Social navigation projection.
entries.rootCause: The C29G redesign updated its focused and broad Social tests but this older Android viewport owner was not included in the label-inventory migration.
entries.prevention: Protected navigation geometry tests source current accepted semantics from the shared owner or assert the current explicit inventory; every Social navigation redesign audits all viewport and exported-semantics tests before host qualification.

entries.mistake: The first C29J standalone widget model supplied bottom viewPadding but left MediaQuery.padding.bottom at zero, so SafeArea did not model the real OPPO inset and the exported-root calculation reported only 14 logical pixels despite the 27-pixel clearance being present.
entries.rootCause: The new helper copied an older incomplete synthetic MediaQuery instead of applying the permanent rule that OPPO SafeArea geometry injects both padding and viewPadding.
entries.prevention: Every OPPO SafeArea widget model sets matching top and bottom padding and viewPadding, also sets the synthetic View padding, asserts the 27-pixel clearance explicitly, and separately proves the compact and standalone exported-root intersections.

entries.mistake: A bounded C29J source read placed $i immediately before a colon inside an interpolated string, and PowerShell rejected the variable reference before reading either owner range.
entries.rootCause: The command repeated the permanent interpolation rule even though only a formatted line-number prefix was needed.
entries.prevention: Bounded PowerShell source reads use the format operator such as '{0}:{1}' -f $lineNumber,$line or explicitly delimited variables; never place a colon immediately after an interpolated variable name.

entries.mistake: The expanded C29J protected batch reached 116 passes but the C10E Social self-route case still required moolsocial-single-home-launcher-shell, which the accepted native Social dock no longer owns.
entries.rootCause: The test's route-continuity assertions were still valid, but its shell-ownership key was not migrated with the C29G Social dock redesign.
entries.prevention: Social connected self-route tests require exactly one current moolsocial-compact-destination-rail, reject the removed destination-shell owner, and retain the existing Back and switcher-dismissal assertions.

entries.mistake: The first C29K switcher-to-Home device command asserted real provider cards after a fixed 12-second wait, while the app still truthfully rendered its loading state, and rejected before provider completion.
entries.rootCause: A fixed delay was treated as the provider transition contract instead of polling the existing loading-to-content state machine within a bounded deadline.
entries.prevention: After a completed navigation action, preserve the loading capture and poll the same screen for provider content or a truthful terminal empty/error state within a bounded deadline; never repeat the tap merely because the external response is still loading.

entries.mistake: A read-only C29L required-reading inventory piped directly from a foreach statement without wrapping or first collecting the loop output, and PowerShell rejected the command with an empty-pipe parser error before listing any files.
entries.rootCause: The command placed a pipeline after the foreach statement as though the statement were already a pipeline expression; PowerShell requires the loop output to be wrapped or collected before piping.
entries.prevention: Multi-file PowerShell inventories collect the foreach output into a candidate-specific array and pipe that array only after the loop completes, or wrap the loop explicitly as an expression; never append a bare pipeline directly after the loop block.

entries.mistake: A read-only C29L duplicate-owner search supplied assumed top-level functions and services directories to ripgrep even though neither path exists, causing the combined inventory to stop with an operating-system path error.
entries.rootCause: The search command inferred conventional backend directory names instead of deriving exact repository owners from the bounded file index first.
entries.prevention: Run rg --files to resolve exact repository owners, then search only confirmed paths; never include an optional or conventional directory as a positional ripgrep input unless its existence has already been verified.

entries.mistake: The first C29L scope-gate run encoded descriptive implementation labels that are outside the founder-locked delivery checker's closed implementationDisposition vocabulary, so execution authorization was rejected before product source changed.
entries.rootCause: The ticket used free-form topology descriptions in a machine-enforced classification field without first reading the checker's accepted enumeration.
entries.prevention: Before selecting a ticket, read the delivery checker's disposition enumeration and use only reuse, configuration, thin_policy_adapter, test_only_acceptance or new_necessary_work; record detailed native presentation and shared-core topology in the dedicated owner and necessity-proof fields.

entries.mistake: A C29L audit supplied a wildcard filename as a positional ripgrep path on Windows, and ripgrep reported that the unexpanded filename was invalid while the command's other searches completed.
entries.rootCause: The command relied on shell glob expansion for a Windows positional path instead of using ripgrep's include filter or an exact file inventory.
entries.prevention: On Windows, use rg -g include filters against confirmed directories or pass exact files resolved by rg --files; never pass a wildcard filename as a positional ripgrep path.

entries.mistake: The very next C29L test inventory repeated REG-1205 by passing another wildcard filename as a positional ripgrep path, so Windows rejected the search before it inspected the tests.
entries.rootCause: The newly registered exact-path and -g filter rule was not applied to every positional path in the immediate follow-up command.
entries.prevention: Before every ripgrep call on Windows, inspect each positional argument and reject any containing wildcard characters; use only confirmed directories or exact files, with every pattern restriction expressed through -g.

entries.mistake: The first C29L creator-screen analysis reported one redundant import, one unbraced conditional and four deprecated RadioListTile group-management members.
entries.rootCause: The new presentation used a familiar older radio pattern instead of reusing the current RadioGroup pattern already present in the workspace, and it was not lint-clean before the first focused analysis.
entries.prevention: New Flutter presentation code reuses current workspace widget idioms such as RadioGroup<T>, braces every conditional branch and removes redundant imports before the focused analysis gate.

entries.mistake: The C29L RadioGroup migration passed a nullable callback to a constructor that requires ValueChanged<bool?>, leaving one compile-time analysis error.
entries.rootCause: The deprecated-member migration inferred that RadioGroup used the old nullable disable contract without verifying the current constructor signature.
entries.prevention: RadioGroup keeps a non-null callback, guards state changes explicitly and uses an interaction-blocking ancestor while busy; current constructor types are verified before rerunning analysis.

entries.mistake: The first C29L creator widget batch exposed a 30-pixel connected-status overflow at 412 pixels, hidden ListTile ink surfaces above a colored DecoratedBox and cancellation feedback that was not locally visible beside the long-form upload action.
entries.rootCause: The new screen was analysis-clean but its narrow-width flex budget, Material ancestry and lazy-list recovery-message placement were not verified before the focused widget run.
entries.prevention: Creator forms test the exact 412x915 viewport, constrain connected-status text inside Expanded, give every interactive tile group a local Material ancestor and render cancel/failure feedback beside the originating upload control.

entries.mistake: The C29L category dropdown overflowed by 33 pixels at the exact 412-pixel mobile viewport because its long labels used intrinsic rather than expanded field width.
entries.rootCause: The dropdown was placed inside nested mobile card padding without enabling DropdownButtonFormField's expanded layout contract.
entries.prevention: Mobile dropdown fields with customer labels set isExpanded true and remain covered by the exact 412x915 viewport test.

entries.mistake: The first protected Social batch retained eight direct-workbench assertions that attempted MoolSocial text entry or workbench keys immediately after the common Create action, without traversing the new explicit hosting choice.
entries.rootCause: The product source added the founder-required MoolSocial-versus-YouTube hosting boundary, but the existing publication and named-state test navigation was not migrated in the same implementation step.
entries.prevention: Protected Create tests retain every publication and format assertion while first choosing the explicit social-create-moolsocial-post action; separate tests protect the capability-gated YouTube-hosted choice.

entries.mistake: The migrated C29E test asserted MoolSocial carousel controls after confirming the creator gateway but before selecting the MoolSocial hosting action, leaving one failure while 42 protected cases passed.
entries.rootCause: The broad legacy-test migration changed the C29E owner key but did not complete the new customer interaction sequence before its format assertions.
entries.prevention: C29E capability-enables and asserts both creator hosting choices, deliberately selects MoolSocial, and only then checks MoolSocial format controls and prohibited customer copy.

entries.mistake: A C29L copy-gate audit guessed a companion config filename that is absent, causing a path error after the real Flutter copy test had already been read.
entries.rootCause: The read inferred a conventional machine-gate filename instead of resolving companion files from the repository index.
entries.prevention: Resolve every optional companion gate through rg --files before Get-Content; when no indexed companion exists, use the confirmed focused test without inventing a path.

entries.mistake: The first full C29L Flutter analysis found one redundant dart:async import in the new creator widget test after focused product-source analysis and protected tests had passed.
entries.rootCause: The initial focused analysis target set covered the modified product owners but omitted the newly added widget test file.
entries.prevention: Focused analysis includes every new and modified Dart test as well as product source, and removes imports reexported by flutter_test before the full analysis gate.

entries.mistake: A C29L backend verification ran from backend/functions but prefixed its read-only Git paths with backend/functions again, producing a doubled nonexistent path warning before the TypeScript typecheck passed.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed repository-root-relative paths with a package-local working directory in the same shell invocation.
entries.prevention: Use repository-relative Git paths only from the repository root, or package-local dot/lib paths from backend/functions; never mix both coordinate frames in one command.

entries.mistake: A C29L qualification audit listed the actual C29J evidence files but also attempted a pre-guessed result filename that is absent, causing a path error after the listing.
entries.rootCause: Directory discovery and content reading were combined before the exact returned filenames were known.
entries.prevention: Inventory an evidence directory first, then read only exact filenames returned by that completed inventory; never precompose a guessed result filename.

entries.mistake: The first C29L host cycle stopped immediately after its successful ticket gate because the wrapper read LASTEXITCODE under strict mode even though an in-process PowerShell script had not set that native-process variable.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier used one exit-code contract for both PowerShell scripts and native executables instead of relying on terminating errors for in-process gates.
entries.prevention: In-process PowerShell gates are invoked with the repository-wide Stop error preference and are considered successful when they return without a terminating error; LASTEXITCODE is checked only immediately after native tools such as npm, dart or flutter.

entries.mistake: The second C29L cycle-1 attempt added the repository-global approved UI lock to a ticket-local qualifier without first reconciling that a user-owned Screen 03 customer-copy test already differed from the immutable hash, so qualification stopped before ticket analysis and tests.
entries.rootCause: The new qualifier expanded from C29L's bounded source owners to an unrelated pre-existing dirty accepted-lock owner even though C29L had neither authority nor scope to restore or reseal it.
entries.prevention: C29L fingerprints and qualifies only its enumerated creator, Social, YouTube, route, test and machine-state owners. Any global immutable-lock mismatch remains independently reported and is never overwritten, waived, resealed or misrepresented as a C29L defect or pass.

entries.mistake: The first source-qualified C29L UI required ownerConnect and privateUpload simultaneously, but the existing Dev proof controller permits exactly one expiring capability profile; therefore the real creator action and exact-channel status could never become reachable under a truthful runtime.
entries.rootCause: Injected widget capabilities modeled an impossible combined state and the host qualifier checked source shape without cross-checking the mutually exclusive provider profile contract and backend action guard.
entries.prevention: Private Short creation is gated by the single privateUpload profile. That profile owns upload-purpose OAuth plus the minimum exact-channel connection-status read needed for consent/reconnect/disconnect; unrelated read-only owner surfaces remain behind ownerConnect. Provider-profile tests and the C29L source gate reject any renewed conjunction.

entries.mistake: The new provider-capability regression entry named backend/functions/src/index.test.ts even though no such test owner exists, causing regression-memory validation to reject the entry before implementation.
entries.rootCause: A test filename was inferred from the production index.ts owner instead of being resolved through the repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Every regression gate path is selected only from a completed rg --files inventory. C29L uses the confirmed config, request-contract and provider-service test owners and never infers a sibling test filename.

entries.mistake: The first least-privilege correction patch guessed an Authority boundary heading in the C29L findings file; apply_patch rejected the complete atomic patch because that heading is absent.
entries.rootCause: The patch anchor was composed from expected document semantics instead of reading the exact current heading inventory first.
entries.prevention: Before a multi-file patch references an existing prose anchor, inventory that file's exact headings or surrounding lines. Apply product and evidence updates in smaller verified patches so an optional prose mismatch cannot block unrelated code changes.

entries.mistake: The first read-only gcloud context check passed account and project as separate positional arguments to gcloud config list, which accepts a single optional section/property filter and rejected the command locally.
entries.rootCause: The CLI syntax was composed from the intended output fields rather than verified against the installed command's filter contract.
entries.prevention: Use gcloud config list with no positional property list and a bounded output projection, or one verified section filter. Read only non-secret account/project metadata and never request credential or token values.

entries.mistake: The corrected C29L -02 source aggregate included the living regression registry, regression memory, ticket scope and protected device metadata, so registering a later CLI mistake changed the aggregate even though product, backend, test and gate source did not change.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier mixed stable executable source ownership with independently evolving audit and machine-state snapshots in one fingerprint domain.
entries.prevention: The final C29L product source seal contains only stable executable product, backend, test and gate owners. Ticket, scope, regression registry and protected-device files are gate-validated and recorded as separate per-cycle SHA-256 state snapshots, never folded into the product drift hash.

entries.mistake: Two bounded C29N inventory commands appended an absence-expected ripgrep search to otherwise successful format or file-list work. Ripgrep correctly returned exit code 1 for no obsolete symbols or no pre-existing C29N registry entry, but the compound shell call was surfaced as a failed script.
entries.rootCause: Expected-empty absence checks were composed as terminal native commands without converting the documented no-match result into an explicit successful assertion.
entries.prevention: Run absence-expected ripgrep checks as dedicated commands that capture LASTEXITCODE, treat 1 as the required empty result, treat greater than 1 as a tool error, and fail explicitly only when forbidden output is returned. Never append an expected-empty search to a formatting, inventory or evidence-read command.

entries.mistake: The first no-match-safe C29N absence check ran from apps/mobile but still supplied apps/mobile/test and apps/mobile/lib, so ripgrep resolved doubled nonexistent paths and stopped before Flutter analysis began.
entries.rootCause: The verification and Flutter-analysis steps were combined under the package working directory without translating the preceding repository-root-relative search inputs into package-local paths.
entries.prevention: C29N source searches run from the repository root with repository-relative paths. Flutter commands run separately from apps/mobile with package-local lib and test paths. A shell call never mixes both coordinate frames.

entries.mistake: The first C29N white-surface implementation inset both fixed 58-pixel edge controls by 3 pixels on every side, leaving only 46-47 pixels after nested label padding and producing 5-6 pixel vertical RenderFlex overflows for Mool and Chat.
entries.rootCause: A decorative card inset was added inside already-fixed learned rail geometry without accounting for the minimum icon-plus-label content height owned by MoolDestinationIconLabel.
entries.prevention: Global edge controls keep the full destinationRailHeight content box. White contrast is provided by the Material surface and radius without an additional vertical inset. The C29N widget test renders both the generic destination rail and Social rail at exact mobile viewports and rejects every layout exception while retaining at least 44 logical semantic height.

entries.mistake: C29N cycle 1 added a third 54-pixel fixed cell to the global destination rail. At 320x568 and 140 percent text, Mool, family root, Chat and gaps left less than the local rail's required 182 logical pixels, producing 12 protected fitment failures before evidence was written.
entries.rootCause: The shared successor preserved desktop-width fixed-cell geometry at the smallest supported mobile width instead of applying the already accepted 44-logical-pixel minimum consistently to all three fixed cells.
entries.prevention: At viewport widths of 340 logical pixels or less, Mool, family root and Chat use one shared 44-pixel adaptive fixed-cell width; above that boundary they retain the accepted 54-pixel width. Height and exported semantics remain at least 44. C29N renders the complete generic rail at 320x568 and 140 percent text, and the protected Screen 04 fitment matrix remains in both host cycles.

entries.mistake: After compact fitment was corrected, the next C29N cycle 1 attempt passed the full Screen 04 matrix but nine older navigation assertions still required a 54x58 Mool or family cell at 320 pixels and did not model the new fixed right-edge Chat successor.
entries.rootCause: The shared adaptive production contract and its new C29N test were updated, while inherited C25D/C27B and related navigation inventories retained the superseded unconditional-width expectation.
entries.prevention: Every protected navigation test derives compact fixed-cell expectations from destinationFixedCellWidthFor(viewportWidth), asserts Chat at the right edge when rendered, and keeps the 54-pixel token assertion only as the non-compact default. The complete protected navigation set remains in both C29N cycles.

entries.mistake: A post-failure navigation inventory passed apps/mobile/test/ui_v2/universal/mool_* as a ripgrep positional path on Windows. Exact preceding file reads completed, but ripgrep rejected the wildcard path with operating-system error 123.
entries.rootCause: The search command bypassed the existing confirmed-directory plus -g rule while combining exact reads and a final convenience wildcard search.
entries.prevention: Windows ripgrep calls use an exact confirmed directory with -g 'mool_*' or a completed rg --files list; wildcard filenames are never positional paths. Search runs separately from evidence reads so a search-shaping rejection cannot obscure completed output.

entries.mistake: After navigation compatibility was corrected, C29N cycle 1 reached seven inherited Social failures. Protected batches still expected the removed universal Social header, superseded provider-unavailable copy, or the former two-step MoolSocial creator host gateway.
entries.rootCause: The production Social successor and focused C29N/C29E tests were updated first, while older continuous, professional-conformance and named-state journeys retained assertions for UI elements intentionally removed by founder direction.
entries.prevention: Every protected Social journey asserts the C29N customer contract: no universal utility header in Social, current provider fail-closed copy/state, seven direct plus outcomes, direct Feed-to-Text, and hidden rail during composition. Rejected internal commentary and the removed host intermediary remain explicit absence assertions in the two-cycle protected suite.

entries.mistake: The rewritten C16B successor test referenced MoolLocalNavigationRail while importing only mool_global_navigation_v2.dart, so focused Dart analysis rejected the undefined symbol before tests ran.
entries.rootCause: The edit assumed a Dart library's own import of mool_design_system.dart made that design symbol transitively visible to its consumers.
entries.prevention: Every Dart test directly imports the library that declares each referenced public type. Focused analysis includes every rewritten test immediately after formatting, before any host-cycle retry.

entries.mistake: After adding the correct direct design-system import to C16B, focused analysis found the former mool_global_navigation_v2.dart import unused because the test no longer referenced a type declared there.
entries.rootCause: The test was rewritten from a component harness to a production Social consumer, but its import inventory was corrected additively instead of reconciled as a complete owner set.
entries.prevention: After a protected test is structurally rewritten, reconcile the entire import block against referenced declaring libraries and require zero-warning focused analysis before tests or qualification.

entries.mistake: The first rewritten C16B run hardcoded a 44x58 rendered Social edge-cell size. At the exact compact scaffold the edge cell rendered 44x57 after host layout while preserving the shared 58-pixel rail owner and exceeding the 44-pixel target, so one test failed.
entries.rootCause: The successor test conflated the design-system rail token with the final child render extent after scaffold/exported-semantics host layout.
entries.prevention: Tests assert the shared destination rail token separately and require rendered plus semantic edge controls to be at least 44 logical pixels. Exact child height is asserted only where the host contract guarantees it independently of exported inset layout.

entries.mistake: The next C29N cycle was rejected before formatting or analysis because the source gate required the exact syntax Key('social-create-moolsocial-quiz'), while the passing protected test stores that literal in a list and constructs Key(key) in its assertion loop.
entries.rootCause: The gate asserted one equivalent Dart construction shape instead of the stable key literal plus the executed behavioral test owner.
entries.prevention: Ticket source gates assert stable customer-contract literals and required behavioral test ownership, not an interchangeable local syntax form. Widget tests remain the authority for constructed key behavior.

entries.mistake: The C29N protected batch passed 117 tests and then the connected-chooser Create journey laid out the new header FilledButton with an inherited infinite width, causing RenderPhysicalShape to reject BoxConstraints(w=Infinity, 48<=h<=58).
entries.rootCause: The composer header relied on the button's ambient style for horizontal sizing. One valid connected-chooser host provides an unbounded horizontal constraint path, so the CTA needed its own finite compact boundary.
entries.prevention: The composer header constrains its publish CTA to an explicit finite width and minimum 44-pixel height before applying FilledButton styling. Both normal keyboard and connected-chooser hosts remain in the protected C29N suite and reject layout exceptions.

entries.mistake: After the publish CTA constraint was fixed, the targeted Screen 04 Create test attempted to tap mool-compact-launcher while the composer was active. C29N intentionally hides the entire dock during composition, so the obsolete finder was absent.
entries.rootCause: The test title and final interaction still modeled the pre-C29N connected chooser beneath the composer instead of the approved full-height, keyboard-safe composer lifecycle.
entries.prevention: Protected Create journeys assert that Mool, Chat and the local dock are absent while composing, use the explicit Close action, then assert the gateway and global edges are restored before testing the connected chooser and Back lifecycle.

entries.mistake: A pre-mutation audit command guessed two delivery-checker filenames and therefore failed after reading only the regression checker.
entries.rootCause: Descriptive policy names were treated as if they implied repository script filenames instead of resolving exact owners from a bounded script inventory.
entries.prevention: Before reading or invoking delivery and scope gates, resolve exact filenames with a completed rg --files scripts inventory and use only returned literal owners. A compound read containing one absent path is rejected in full.

entries.mistake: A read-only API inventory requested six large mobile and backend owners in one output, which was truncated and therefore could not establish complete evidence for the audit.
entries.rootCause: The inventory was bounded by filenames but not by total output or explicit line ranges, so unrelated large owners competed for the same tool-response budget.
entries.prevention: Read API owners one exact file at a time and split large owners into explicit non-overlapping line ranges. Reject every truncated combined result as evidence before ticket selection or implementation.

entries.mistake: Immediately after registering the broad API-read truncation, a symbol-only search still named three large owners together and was also truncated.
entries.rootCause: The retry reduced content density but did not enforce the newly required one-owner boundary or a bounded line interval.
entries.prevention: Each API evidence command names one exact owner and either one small symbol family or one explicit line interval. A no-truncation result is required before the evidence is admitted, and a retry after truncation may not broaden its target set.

entries.mistake: A bounded API-owner inventory printed a line count and then ended with an rg symbol search whose valid empty result returned exit 1, causing the compound command to be reported as failed.
entries.rootCause: An absence-capable search was used as the terminal step of a compound evidence command without explicitly admitting rg exit 1 as an empty result.
entries.prevention: Line counts and absence-capable searches run separately. Empty-search assertions explicitly admit rg exit 1 and reject greater exit codes; small owners are read literally instead of inferred from symbol names.

entries.mistake: A read-only audit command guessed apps/mobile/lib/shared/shared_session.dart, but no such path exists.
entries.rootCause: The remembered SharedSession class name was treated as if it implied its declaring filename and directory.
entries.prevention: Resolve declaring files from a completed rg --files inventory plus an exact class-symbol search, then open only the returned literal owner path.

entries.mistake: The OPPO inventory returned no connected device, but the compound command continued to package and window identity reads without an exact qualified serial.
entries.rootCause: Device inventory and serial-bound evidence reads were sequenced in one unconditional command rather than separated by an exact-one-device qualification gate.
entries.prevention: Run device inventory alone. Begin package, activity, screenshot, semantic or input calls only after exactly one authorized serial is present and host-qualified, and pass that literal serial to every adb command.

entries.mistake: One product patch attempted many distant Social consumer edits and was rejected atomically when a copy anchor did not match the exact current file.
entries.rootCause: State cleanup, copy changes, action rewiring, method insertion and class removal were combined despite belonging to separate local source regions.
entries.prevention: Each product patch edits one freshly re-read local region or one exact repeated mechanical symbol family. Distant UI, state, method and class edits remain separate.

entries.mistake: At 320x568 with the actual descendant text scale set to 1.4, the YouTube watch journey overflowed a horizontal RenderFlex by 12 pixels.
entries.rootCause: The previous Social root clamp masked a narrow-screen row that was never required to lay out at the user's real 140 percent text scale.
entries.prevention: Supported-viewport tests assert the descendant MediaQuery scale before fitment. Narrow rows adapt or wrap and never repair overflow by lowering the user's requested scale.

entries.mistake: The new C29O source-absence test initially used String.fromEnvironment with an empty default, so it could not inspect the actual production source owner.
entries.rootCause: A compile-time fixture mechanism was introduced without a non-empty value or provenance assertion instead of reusing the repository's literal package-local file-read pattern.
entries.prevention: Source-shape tests read the exact package-local owner with File(...).readAsStringSync(), or assert the explicit non-empty provenance of an injected fixture. Empty environment defaults are never source evidence.

entries.mistake: The new 320x568/140 percent sequential Social destination test consumed a horizontal RenderFlex overflow of 8.1 pixels at the Shorts checkpoint.
entries.rootCause: The test initially consumed layout exceptions only after each destination tap, so the exception still required isolation to the exact preceding render state.
entries.prevention: Sequential viewport tests consume and assert a clean exception state immediately after initial pump and after every individual transition, then adapt the exact failing row without lowering text scale.

entries.mistake: The canonical-share proof scrolled the lower action row into view before the existing Details journey, leaving the later Details trigger above the viewport so its tap missed.
entries.rootCause: A newly added scroll-mutating assertion was inserted before navigation assertions that relied on the original watch scroll position.
entries.prevention: Scroll-mutating proofs run after earlier position-sensitive journeys, or explicitly restore and verify the required scroll position before the next tap.

entries.mistake: The new C29O Social edge test searched for the reusable Chat widget's default mool-global-chat key even though the Social dock injects social-global-chat.
entries.rootCause: The test assumed a reusable widget default instead of reading the concrete host call site's controlKey.
entries.prevention: Navigation tests use the exact key supplied by the tested host owner and never assume a reusable widget default survives explicit host injection.

entries.mistake: Repository-root policy gates were invoked as ./scripts from apps/mobile. They were not found, while later Flutter analysis and tests passed and left the compound shell exit code at zero.
entries.rootCause: Repository gates and package-local Flutter commands were mixed in one working directory despite the permanent coordinate-frame rule.
entries.prevention: Run repository policy/source gates from the repository root and Flutter format/analyze/test from apps/mobile in separate commands. Reject a compound result if any earlier command emitted a discovery error even when the final command exits zero.

entries.mistake: The C29O source gate required inline Key('screen04-rail-shorts') even though the executed widget test constructs the same key from its literal shorts journey map.
entries.rootCause: The gate asserted one equivalent Dart construction syntax instead of the stable journey literal, dynamic key expression and behavioral test owner.
entries.prevention: Source gates assert stable contract literals plus the executed behavior owner and do not require one interchangeable inline key construction.

entries.mistake: After the C29O PowerShell source gate passed, a LASTEXITCODE check caused an early zero exit before the delivery, scope and regression gates ran.
entries.rootCause: LASTEXITCODE was treated as the success authority for .ps1 invocation even though it is a native-process exit variable and can be null or stale in this path.
entries.prevention: Set parent ErrorActionPreference to Stop and invoke PowerShell gate scripts directly. Let thrown gate failures terminate; never sequence .ps1 gates with LASTEXITCODE.

entries.mistake: The first full C29O cycle exposed two 2px bottom RenderFlex overflows in the 46px Create one-tap tool button interior at 320x568 and actual 140 percent text.
entries.rootCause: The prior Social text clamp hid that fixed tool-row height did not accommodate its icon, gap and scaled label after vertical padding.
entries.prevention: Create tool controls own a text-scale-aware vertical extent with at least 44px semantics. They never clip or scale down text and never add taps or hide a format to repair fitment.

entries.mistake: A generic build-method patch anchor inserted Create tool scale locals in the preceding widget while _ToolAction referenced them out of scope, causing analysis and compilation rejection.
entries.rootCause: The repeated Widget build(BuildContext context) signature was used without the exact declaring class as part of the patch anchor.
entries.prevention: Repeated method signatures are never mutation anchors by themselves. Include the exact declaring class and method in the local patch, then run focused analysis before tests.

entries.mistake: The broad C29O protected suite found that the Screen 04 customer-copy audit still expected the MoolSocial composer immediately at the default Create route even though the accepted C29N journey now opens the two-owner creation gateway first.
entries.rootCause: The static customer-copy audit was not migrated with the accepted Create gateway navigation contract and therefore rejected the correct runtime destination.
entries.prevention: Default Create-route audits first prove the Social creator gateway, then tap the explicit MoolSocial posting action and audit the composer. They never bypass or erase the distinct YouTube-hosted and MoolSocial-hosted ownership choice.

entries.mistake: A combined read of the C29O source gate and broad recursive quality/config search exceeded the bounded command timeout before either result could be admitted as qualification evidence.
entries.rootCause: An exact small owner read was coupled to a repository-wide content search instead of being executed independently with a narrowly resolved target set.
entries.prevention: Qualification owner reads remain one exact file per command. Evidence discovery first resolves candidate filenames, then searches only those bounded files and never shares a command with a required gate-owner read.

entries.mistake: The 1,818-line shared model owner was read as one complete file during C29P reuse analysis, repeating the already-forbidden large-owner pattern and producing truncated output.
entries.rootCause: The file was treated as a small model owner without checking its line count and bounding the already-resolved Social model region first.
entries.prevention: Every source owner is line-counted before full read. Owners above the bounded threshold are read only through explicit non-overlapping ranges, and truncated output is never admitted even when the required declarations appeared before truncation.

entries.mistake: The first C29P backend typecheck rejected explicitly undefined optional properties, unchecked array access and Firestore getAll result assumptions under the repository's strict TypeScript contract.
entries.rootCause: New Social owners were written against permissive JavaScript intuitions before the exactOptionalPropertyTypes and noUncheckedIndexedAccess compiler contract was replayed.
entries.prevention: New backend contracts omit absent optional properties, narrow every indexed value and guard every Firestore result before use; focused typecheck runs before any compiled test.

entries.mistake: A transient backend patch inserted Dart nullable-pattern syntax into a TypeScript owner and was rejected before admission.
entries.rootCause: A syntax fragment was transferred between adjacent Dart and TypeScript implementation work without language-local validation.
entries.prevention: Each cross-language patch is syntax-reviewed in its declaring language and immediately checked with that package's focused analyzer or compiler before further edits.

entries.mistake: The first C29P focused Flutter run retained a hard-coded review post ID and retried a named unavailable fixture whose state was intentionally still unavailable.
entries.rootCause: Tests encoded the former process-local gateway implementation detail instead of the durable gateway response and explicit fixture-state contract.
entries.prevention: Social tests inject their gateway, derive server-owned identifiers from the acknowledged result and separate named static-state proofs from runtime retry journeys.

entries.mistake: The first full C29P npm test invocation emitted the entire suite and exceeded the available output context, so its result could not be admitted.
entries.rootCause: A known large suite was invoked without capturing and bounding its terminal output.
entries.prevention: Large native suites capture combined output, preserve the immediate native exit status and print only a bounded tail containing totals and status; truncated output is never qualification evidence.

entries.mistake: The first targeted C29P Flutter analysis reported five strict lint findings for constructor parameter style and nullable collection construction.
entries.rootCause: The new authenticated gateway was functionally written before matching the repository's preferred initializing-formal and null-aware collection syntax.
entries.prevention: New Dart owners run targeted analysis immediately; constructors and conditional collections are conformed before focused behavior tests or full qualification.

entries.mistake: A repository-wide search for one known regression ID timed out after the exact registry hit had already identified its bounded evidence owner.
entries.rootCause: The bounded evidence-discovery rule was not applied and a content search was run across the whole dirty repository.
entries.prevention: Once the registry names an evidence path, read that literal owner only. Repository-wide evidence searches are prohibited when the target is already resolved.

entries.mistake: Two bounded rg commands passed a shell-style backend/functions/src/social/*.ts operand on Windows, where the literal wildcard path was rejected after other matches printed.
entries.rootCause: A Unix shell-expansion assumption was used in PowerShell instead of rg's own glob filter.
entries.prevention: Windows rg searches name a directory and use --glob for file patterns; any nonzero search result is rejected even when preceding matches look useful.

entries.mistake: Firebase CLI and Java availability were probed in one compound command; the expected missing Java executable made the otherwise useful Firebase CLI result a failed command.
entries.rootCause: Independent dependency inventories with different absence semantics were coupled into one native exit path.
entries.prevention: Host dependencies are probed independently with Get-Command and explicit found/not-found output. An absent optional executable is recorded as a gate dependency, not emitted as an unhandled shell error.

entries.mistake: After the review gateway moved from lib to test support, two tests retained the now-unused production gateway import and targeted analysis rejected both warnings.
entries.rootCause: The symbol move updated construction imports but did not remove the former transitive type-owner import in the same atomic patch.
entries.prevention: A production-to-test owner move includes an import-use inventory for every consumer, followed immediately by targeted strict analysis.

entries.mistake: The first C29P source-gate passes guessed authentication copy and variable names, required a formatter-sensitive one-line media message and attributed the Reply gate to the content card instead of its consumer callback owner.
entries.rootCause: The gate was authored from remembered equivalent behavior without re-reading each exact declaring region after formatting and ownership wiring.
entries.prevention: A new source gate asserts exact freshly-read stable literals in their real declaring owner, avoids formatter-dependent full lines and proves delegated callbacks at both the host and leaf boundary where needed.

entries.mistake: Prequalification review found that candidate uploads shared an idempotency path, conflicting recovered commits could leave an orphan, declared image MIME was trusted, missing local media escaped the domain error contract, and the decoded media ceiling could not fit safely inside its base64 request ceiling.
entries.rootCause: The initial happy-path implementation treated transport bytes, concurrent transaction outcomes and local file lifetime as separate concerns instead of one end-to-end publish boundary.
entries.prevention: Publish candidates use unique post paths, clean only their own losing media for every transaction outcome, verify image signatures, map local file loss to a domain error and keep decoded/base64 ceilings jointly bounded with focused race and conflict tests.

entries.mistake: The first C29P source version left the review-only in-memory Social gateway in lib and did not explicitly bind a deny-all Storage rules owner in firebase.json.
entries.rootCause: Test support and future deployment security configuration were treated as secondary after production runtime wiring.
entries.prevention: Review gateways live only under test, production fails closed when the endpoint define is absent, and both Firestore and Storage direct-client rules are explicit deny-all owners required by the source gate.

entries.mistake: A recursive ui_v2 file inventory included thousands of capture and golden assets, exceeded the output bound and was truncated while trying to identify a small Social test set.
entries.rootCause: The inventory was sorted before applying an exact Social Dart-test filename filter.
entries.prevention: Test discovery filters to .dart and the exact Social or Screen 04 filename family before sorting or output; image and failure artifact trees are excluded at discovery time.

entries.mistake: The first emulator-test owner used import.meta.url even though the backend compiles to CommonJS, and strict typecheck rejected it.
entries.rootCause: The path resolver was written with ESM assumptions before replaying the package module target.
entries.prevention: Backend test helpers derive repository paths from CommonJS __dirname and run package typecheck before any emulator startup.

entries.mistake: The first emulator invocation left the comma-separated --only value unquoted in PowerShell and found no emulator; the second set JAVA_HOME but did not expose the bundled java executable on the child PATH.
entries.rootCause: Firebase CLI argument parsing and Java discovery were not proven with a local host preflight before the full emulator command.
entries.prevention: Quote comma-separated Firebase --only values and expose the exact bundled JDK bin only for the child command, restoring the prior PATH in finally. The command must use the synthetic local project ID.

entries.mistake: Adding the official Firebase rules test dependencies surfaced one high brace-expansion advisory and seven moderate Firebase Admin Storage lineage advisories in the production audit.
entries.rootCause: The lockfile inherited a vulnerable brace-expansion patch through the existing Firebase Admin dependency tree, while the remaining moderate advisories have no safe non-major npm audit resolution in the current official versions.
entries.prevention: Pin the safe brace-expansion patch override, require zero high or critical audit findings before source qualification, record remaining upstream moderate lineage explicitly and block deploy if its contextual review changes or a safe vendor update becomes available.

entries.mistake: The C29Q promotion inventory repeated a shell-style apps/mobile/test/social_v2_* operand on Windows; rg printed bounded source matches but rejected the wildcard path.
entries.rootCause: The C29P Windows rg-glob rule was not replayed when the ticket changed.
entries.prevention: Every Windows rg command uses directories plus --glob filters, including ticket-transition searches; partial matches from a nonzero command are never evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C29Q reuse manifest and source-copy test named a nonexistent social_v2_youtube_player.dart owner, causing the focused test to fail after four policy tests passed.
entries.rootCause: The embedded-player owner was inferred from widget responsibility instead of resolved from the consumer imports and filesystem before ticket selection.
entries.prevention: Every manifest owner must exist before selection. Resolve embedded-player ownership from exact imports and rg --files, then keep the manifest, scope assessment, tests and source gate on the same literal owners.

entries.mistake: The first C29R request-contract audit combined a complete source-owner read with an index range, exceeded the response bound and was truncated before the owner could be accepted as evidence.
entries.rootCause: The existing line-count and bounded-range rule was not replayed when two related backend owners were inspected together.
entries.prevention: C29R counts each source owner first and reads one explicit non-overlapping range per command; combined full-file plus range reads are rejected even when the command exits successfully.

entries.mistake: The first C29R line-count inventory guessed backend/functions/src/youtube/service.ts even though that owner does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The ProviderService declaration was remembered semantically and converted into an inferred filename instead of being resolved from the TypeScript source inventory.
entries.prevention: C29R resolves every backend owner with an exact declaration search over existing TypeScript files before it is read, tested or written into a ticket manifest.

entries.mistake: The C29R preflight encountered a pre-existing 126-line Social customer-copy expansion in ui_v2_customer_copy_machine_gate_test.dart whose checksum no longer matches the Screen 03 lock expected by check-approved-ui-locks.ps1.
entries.rootCause: A shared customer-copy test was expanded for later Social qualification while the older immutable lock still treats the entire shared test file as Screen 03-owned.
entries.prevention: C29R preserves that dirty owner byte-for-byte, excludes it from all patches, records the inherited mismatch and requires the C29R source gate to prove its observed preflight checksum is unchanged. The immutable lock must be reconciled only under separate reference authority.

entries.mistake: The first shared-catalogue client test imported nonexistent HttpRequest and HttpResponse names instead of the repository-owned HttpTransportRequest and HttpTransportResponse types.
entries.rootCause: Generic HTTP type names were written from memory instead of copied from the exact HttpTransport contract or an existing client test.
entries.prevention: New YouTube transport tests resolve and reuse the literal HttpTransport, HttpTransportRequest and HttpTransportResponse exports from types.ts before the first compile.

entries.mistake: Two C29R regression entries referenced the planned C29R source-gate script before that file existed, so the mandatory regression-memory gate failed closed.
entries.rootCause: A future acceptance owner was recorded as a current executable gate before its implementation and validation step.
entries.prevention: Regression entries reference only existing evidence and gate owners. A new source gate is added to registry coverage only after the script exists and has passed independently.

entries.mistake: A composite PowerShell qualification command allowed dart format --set-exit-if-changed to modify one test, then reported the later successful Flutter test exit code as the command result.
entries.rootCause: Formatter, analyzer and test commands were placed in one shell invocation without preserving each immediate exit status.
entries.prevention: Apply Dart formatting as an explicit mechanical step, then run the no-change formatter check, analyzer and test in separate invocations or fail immediately on each nonzero status. A later test result can never mask a formatter delta.

entries.mistake: The first combined C29R gate replay invoked the archived C29O source gate, which correctly rejected because it requires C29O rather than C29R to be the active MVP scope ticket.
entries.rootCause: A predecessor ticket's selection-time gate was treated as a timeless regression gate even though its contract intentionally hard-binds the active ticket identity.
entries.prevention: After a successor is selected, predecessor behavior is protected by its focused tests and successor containment assertions. Do not invoke an older active-scope gate unless it explicitly supports an archival mode.

entries.mistake: Prequalification review found the first durable quota-measurement implementation read its measurement document after queuing the quota usage write in the same Firestore transaction.
entries.rootCause: The existing in-memory document seam did not enforce Firestore's all-reads-before-writes transaction rule, so focused tests could not detect the invalid production ordering.
entries.prevention: Quota and measurement documents are both read before any transaction write. The C29R in-memory transaction seam rejects every get after create, set or delete, and the quota measurement test exercises accepted and rejected decisions.
