entries.mistake: Prequalification review found invalid persisted quota or catalogue counters would be treated as zero, allowing corrupted evidence to be silently understated.
entries.rootCause: Counter helpers used a permissive default for both absent fields and malformed existing values instead of distinguishing schema absence from corruption.
entries.prevention: Absent counters initialize to zero; present counters must be non-negative safe integers or the measurement write fails. Focused tests inject corrupt quota and catalogue counters and require rejection.

entries.mistake: The first post-connection audit printed an empty adb device list but continued with protected serial 2b3e0f71, producing two avoidable device-not-found errors.
entries.rootCause: Device discovery and serial-scoped identity reads were combined without a fail-closed online-serial branch.
entries.prevention: Every device action runs adb devices -l alone first. Serial-scoped reads, launches, tests, builds or installs remain blocked unless the exact protected or candidate serial appears once with state device; empty, offline or unauthorized output stops the attempt.

entries.mistake: The first C29U scope assessment used the invented implementation disposition deployment_only, which the founder-locked delivery gate rejected.
entries.rootCause: The deployment nature of the ticket was encoded as a new machine vocabulary value instead of the supported configuration disposition.
entries.prevention: Every new ticket resolves implementationDisposition against the delivery-lock allowlist before selection. Dev deployment reuses sealed owners and is represented by reuse, configuration and test_only_acceptance.

entries.mistake: The first C29U scope state encoded the founder's exact Dev authorization as an invented authorization.state value, which the MVP scope gate correctly rejected.
entries.rootCause: Human-readable authorization detail was placed in a machine-enumerated field instead of the existing founderAcceptance and evidence fields.
entries.prevention: MVP tickets use only founder_acknowledged_mvp_scope or existing_ticket_authority_confirmed in authorization.state. Exact authorized actions and exclusions remain explicit in founderAcceptance, execution flags, ticket authority and retained evidence.

entries.mistake: A C29U diagnostic combined two reads and guessed a nonexistent regression-memory JSON path; the second gate-owner read completed but the composite command exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The registry filename was recalled instead of resolved from AGENTS.md, and unrelated owner reads were combined into one shell invocation.
entries.prevention: Read one exact owner per shell invocation, resolve permanent-regression paths literally from repository instructions, and reject every composite diagnostic when any child read fails.

entries.mistake: The first C29U regression-memory replay passed unsupported phase external and PowerShell rejected it before the gate body ran.
entries.rootCause: The ticket's external-service capability was mistaken for a supported regression-gate phase.
entries.prevention: Resolve Phase against the gate's ValidateSet before invocation. Dev backend deployment and rules qualification use implementation; APK build and OPPO replay later use build and device separately.

entries.mistake: The first C29U source gate used backslash-escaped double quotes inside a PowerShell string, so the literal assertion searched for a backslash and falsely rejected the correct project constant.
entries.rootCause: JavaScript and shell escaping conventions were applied to PowerShell, where backslash does not escape a double quote.
entries.prevention: PowerShell source-literal assertions that contain double quotes use single-quoted PowerShell strings; the gate must pass independently before it protects deployment.

entries.mistake: The C29U emulator preflight called Get-Command java without absence handling, repeating the registered host-dependency-probe failure even though the repository uses a bundled JDK.
entries.rootCause: The global PATH was probed as a required owner instead of resolving the already-qualified bundled JDK from the existing emulator workflow.
entries.prevention: Optional global dependency probes use Get-Command with explicit absence handling. Firebase emulator runs bind the exact existing bundled JDK only for the child command and use a synthetic local project ID.

entries.mistake: After opening the visible founder-controlled gcloud login, a project-describe retry ran before the founder confirmed authentication completion and repeated the non-interactive reauthentication failure.
entries.rootCause: The interactive security prompt and the non-interactive metadata probe were not separated by an explicit founder-completion checkpoint.
entries.prevention: After launching a founder-controlled authentication window, do not poll a secured gcloud command. Wait for explicit founder confirmation that authentication finished, then replay regression and scope gates before the next cloud request.

entries.mistake: The first bounded Functions metadata list used --gen2, but the installed gcloud surface accepts --v2 and rejected the command before reading metadata.
entries.rootCause: The generation flag was recalled from another gcloud command surface instead of resolved from the installed command syntax.
entries.prevention: For this installed SDK, gcloud functions list uses --v2. Function generation remains verified from returned environment metadata, and a rejected list command is never treated as absence evidence.

entries.mistake: A five-way nested parallel shell probe rendered empty wrapper objects for every Secret Manager metadata result, so none of its output could prove secret presence.
entries.rootCause: Shell result objects were composed through the orchestration wrapper without first proving that the wrapper preserved stdout for this tool surface.
entries.prevention: Secret metadata is read with one bounded direct gcloud invocation at a time. Empty wrapper output is rejected, and no secret value or version payload command is used.

entries.mistake: A cross-tree search for the Social runtime account and candidate IAM roles traversed broad docs, config and backend scopes and timed out without admissible output.
entries.rootCause: The exact C29P/C29U ticket and evidence filename family was not resolved before searching for a small IAM-owner decision.
entries.prevention: Resolve bounded ticket/evidence filenames first, then read or search one exact owner. Broad documentation trees never support a cloud mutation decision after timeout or truncation.

entries.mistake: The first screenshot-coordinate attempt to expand Databases and storage expanded Hosting and serverless instead; no cloud resource or setting changed.
entries.rootCause: The coordinate was inferred from the rendered screenshot without accounting for the Computer Use window-coordinate mapping after Chrome layout scaling.
entries.prevention: After any coordinate result, inspect the refreshed tree and visible outcome. Firebase sidebar navigation uses the current accessibility element when available; a wrong expansion is closed or superseded before continuing and never treated as the intended product selection.

entries.mistake: Clicking the accessibility index labelled Firebase product search focused Chrome's address bar instead; the focus check stopped before any text was typed.
entries.rootCause: The browser and web-document accessibility trees exposed overlapping element indexes whose action mapping did not match the labelled document element.
entries.prevention: Always reobserve focused_element before typing. When Chrome's address bar is explicitly confirmed, navigate only to an exact authorized Dev Firebase URL; never type a product query into an ambiguously focused field.

entries.mistake: Computer Use set_value reported an unknown outcome for Chrome's verified address-bar element; reobservation proved the original Firebase URL remained unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The generic accessibility value setter is not reliable for Chrome's omnibox on this host.
entries.prevention: Chrome URL replacement uses the browser-owned Ctrl+L selection chord, a refreshed focus check, literal typing and Enter as separate observed actions. set_value is not retried for the omnibox.

entries.mistake: The accessibility action on the labelled Firebase Storage Get started button completed without error but left the same page and setup state unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The Chrome web-document accessibility action mapping did not dispatch the visible Angular button control on this host.
entries.prevention: A successful input call is not a successful UI outcome. If the refreshed URL, tree and screenshot remain unchanged, record a no-op and use one screenshot-backed coordinate from that exact observation, then verify the modal before continuing.

entries.mistake: Clicking the accessibility option labelled ASIA-SOUTH1 closed the location list but left the selected value at US.
entries.rootCause: The off-viewport Angular option was present in the accessibility tree but its action mapping did not select the underlying list row.
entries.prevention: Off-viewport Firebase location options are not clicked from accessibility alone. Open the exact dropdown, scroll within its screenshot-bounded list, click the visibly rendered ASIA-SOUTH1 row and require the closed combo to display ASIA-SOUTH1 before Continue.

entries.mistake: The first visible regional-row coordinate selected ASIA-NORTHEAST3 instead of ASIA-SOUTH1; the closed combo exposed the mismatch before Continue.
entries.rootCause: The coordinate offset changed after scrolling the Angular overlay, so the earlier window-to-screenshot calibration was no longer valid for the moved row list.
entries.prevention: Never continue from an inferred row click. Reopen and scroll the same list, calibrate from the visibly selected adjacent row, target the exact ASIA-SOUTH1 row and require the closed combo literal ASIA-SOUTH1 before advancing. Any other region remains a rejected pre-submit state.

entries.mistake: After maximizing Chrome, the screenshot coordinate intended for Continue mapped far above the visible button and left the bucket-options step unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The prior windowed screenshot-to-input coordinate calibration was reused after the window size and DPI mapping changed.
entries.prevention: Maximize invalidates all prior coordinates. Reobserve and prefer the current semantic button owner for Continue; accept progress only when the refreshed dialog exposes Security rules Step 2. Do not infer a new coordinate from the displayed maximized bitmap.

entries.mistake: The project IAM binding mutation for the Social runtime App Check verifier role emitted the complete project policy and exceeded the available output context, so its result was not admissible deployment evidence.
entries.rootCause: The mutation command was allowed to print the broad updated policy instead of suppressing mutation output and following it with a member-scoped read.
entries.prevention: IAM mutations use quiet/no-output formatting where supported and are never accepted from mutation stdout. Every role addition is proven afterwards by an exact member-filtered get-iam-policy read with only the role column returned.

entries.mistake: The resumed repository inspection combined a full dirty-tree listing with a guessed registry path, producing truncated output before failing on the nonexistent filename; a follow-up also guessed the registry collection property and returned no entries.
entries.rootCause: Known repository owners were not addressed directly and unrelated high-volume inspection was composed into the same command.
entries.prevention: C29U continuation uses the durable registry owner config/codex-development-regression-registry.json, its entries collection, and separately bounded reads. Full git status is never combined with registry or evidence inspection; branch and HEAD use dedicated scalar commands when needed.

entries.mistake: The bucket IAM verification used an unsupported gcloud storage get-iam-policy --filter flag, and the composite PowerShell command continued to a bucket-description read after the native process failed.
entries.rootCause: Project IAM filter capabilities were assumed to exist on the separate gcloud storage surface, while PowerShell ErrorActionPreference was incorrectly treated as native-process exit propagation.
entries.prevention: Bucket IAM verification requests JSON without --filter, checks LASTEXITCODE immediately, parses the exact member locally, and emits only its roles. Native cloud reads are isolated or followed by an explicit exit-code guard before any later command runs.

entries.mistake: A composite predeployment source read included the complete large backend/functions/src/index.ts and exceeded the available output context.
entries.rootCause: A small configuration audit and a large function owner were read with the same whole-file strategy instead of using exact symbol and bounded line extracts.
entries.prevention: Large source owners are never printed whole during C29U. Use ripgrep for exact exports/config symbols, then bounded Get-Content slices around only those matches; keep small manifest reads separate.

entries.mistake: The exact C29U Firebase dry run reached its passed predeploy build but then failed before rules or function validation because the Firebase CLI credential was no longer valid.
entries.rootCause: Successful gcloud reauthentication was incorrectly treated as sufficient for the separately cached Firebase CLI session.
entries.prevention: Before a Firebase deployment window, validate Firebase CLI identity independently. On an explicit stale-session response, stop without retry, record the gate, and run one founder-visible firebase login --reauth flow; never copy or print its credential material.

entries.mistake: The first unauthenticated Storage list probe used a non-empty prefix without a trailing slash and received HTTP 400, which could not prove the deny-all rule.
entries.rootCause: The Firebase Storage REST list-prefix syntax was not validated before interpreting the response as a rules outcome.
entries.prevention: Cloud Storage rules probes use an empty prefix or a synthetic folder prefix ending in exactly one slash. Only an authorization response such as 401/403 is accepted as deny-all evidence; request-shape 400 responses are rejected and registered.

entries.mistake: The exact three-function deployment updated both existing YouTube functions but returned nonzero after creating moolSocialContent because Firebase CLI could not set its HTTPS invoker policy.
entries.rootCause: A newly created Gen2 HTTPS function needs an explicit Cloud Run invoker binding, while the sealed function declaration relied on Firebase's implicit public-invoker step and the CLI could not complete that IAM mutation.
entries.prevention: A new HTTPS function is never treated as deployed from source-upload or function-state output alone. After any partial result, independently describe all intended revisions and compare bounded Cloud Run IAM. Add only the exact missing roles/run.invoker binding when founder authority and organization policy permit, then re-read the policy and endpoint behavior before closing the deploy gate.

entries.mistake: A metadata lookup searched config, deployment, all quality documents and the complete artifact evidence tree together and timed out without a result.
entries.rootCause: The known C29L provider audit and deployment manifest owners were not queried directly before expanding into a large historical artifact corpus.
entries.prevention: C29M metadata resolution starts from the exact sourceDependency/currentProviderState paths in its ticket and the deployment manifest. Ripgrep is scoped to those named files or their immediate directory; the full artifacts tree is never a first-pass search target.

entries.mistake: The legacy verify-youtube-private-dev-deployment wrapper was invoked after the C29U deployment, but its nested preflight aborted on an unrelated login-account-handoff approved-UI production lock before checking provider metadata.
entries.rootCause: The older provider verifier composes repository-wide approved-UI locks that predate and are not scoped to the current accepted Social dirty tree, while C29U has a newer exact sealed-source gate for this deployment.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or bypass the stale UI lock and do not mutate accepted navigation/UI owners from a backend ticket. C29U acceptance uses its exact source/rules/functions gate, direct revision/service-account/secret/environment reads, rules denials and endpoint security probes. The legacy verifier remains evidence of an incompatible composite gate until separately reconciled by its owner.

entries.mistake: Completion state and revision fields were added to the C29U ticket manifest even though its exact SHA-256 is a sealed predeployment input enforced by the C29U gate.
entries.rootCause: Durable completion evidence was incorrectly placed inside an immutable selected-ticket manifest instead of a separate completion owner and successor state.
entries.prevention: Once a ticket manifest hash is sealed by a deployment gate, completion never mutates that manifest. Record outcomes in a separate completion document and transition only the successor ticket/scope machine owners. If an accidental edit occurs, register it and restore only the agent-authored delta with apply_patch before any gate or deployment continues.

entries.mistake: The C29M selection assessment used descriptive disposition values temporary_configuration and supervised_test_only_acceptance, which the delivery lock rejected as noncanonical.
entries.rootCause: Narrative qualifiers were encoded in the machine enum instead of the assessment text, repeating the known unsupported-disposition class.
entries.prevention: Machine implementationDisposition values are selected only from the delivery-lock canonical set. C29M uses configuration and test_only_acceptance; temporary/supervised semantics remain in the narrative, robustness coverage and implementation state fields.

entries.mistake: The bounded apps/web reuse search produced no matches, but ripgrep exit code 1 was allowed to surface as a shell-command failure instead of an expected negative result.
entries.rootCause: The command did not explicitly distinguish ripgrep's no-match status from execution errors during a negative reuse audit.
entries.prevention: Negative ripgrep audits capture output and accept exit code 1 as no matches; only exit codes above 1 are errors. The resulting no-match disposition is recorded without retrying the same search.

entries.mistake: The C29L source gate was invoked after the machine state had correctly transitioned to C29M, so it rejected the active ticket mismatch before the later static proof check ran.
entries.rootCause: A predecessor ticket-bound gate was treated as reusable after successor activation instead of relying on its sealed host-qualification evidence captured while C29L was active.
entries.prevention: Ticket-bound predecessor gates run before successor transition or are reused only through their durable sealed evidence. Once C29M is active, do not rerun the C29L gate; run C29M-safe proof controls and current scope/delivery/regression gates only.

entries.mistake: A useful bounded source slice proving the YouTube creator route was composed with a follow-up ripgrep over incomplete component-owner paths; the no-match exit marked the whole command as failed despite the valid first result.
entries.rootCause: A negative follow-up search was composed with an independent positive evidence read and again lacked explicit exit-code 1 handling.
entries.prevention: Positive source slices and negative owner searches are separate commands. Any bounded ripgrep lookup that may legitimately return no matches explicitly accepts exit code 1; proven route evidence is never coupled to that search status.

entries.mistake: A composite PowerShell command embedded the HTTPS creator route, capture path interpolation and several ADB operations in one quoted string; the shell safety parser rejected it before execution.
entries.rootCause: Route launch and evidence capture were over-composed with mixed quoting instead of passing the Android intent URI as a simple literal in an isolated command.
entries.prevention: ADB deep-link launch is isolated from capture and cleanup. Use one literal am-start command with explicit package/component semantics, verify its exit, then capture in a separate command. Never combine URL quoting and interpolated evidence paths in one shell string.

entries.mistake: Even after isolating the ADB intent, the literal HTTPS creator route was blocked by the local shell safety policy before ADB execution.
entries.rootCause: The host command policy treats the raw HTTPS token in this shell command as unsafe; isolation alone does not make that literal invocable.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the HTTPS deep link through shell quoting or encoded variants. Use the verified in-app navigation owner and on-device taps; the custom moolsocial callback activity is reserved for OAuth return and is not used as a generic route launcher.

entries.mistake: The protected r60.34 client cannot reach the sealed C29L YouTube creator gateway: its global plus opens only the MoolSocial workbench and route intents return to YouTube Home.
entries.rootCause: The installed protected candidate predates the current sealed creator-gateway behavior, so a real App Check/Auth/OAuth upload proof cannot be performed on it before a qualified successor client is installed.
entries.prevention: C29M private-upload proof requires a device client whose sealed C29L route is present. Reorder the dependency safely: restore PublicData review, qualify/build/install C29V without enabling upload, verify the creator gateway on the fresh identity, then open a new expiring C29M proof window. Never simulate the missing route or use user media.

entries.mistake: The expiring PrivateUpload profile was activated after server/static qualification but before proving that the protected installed client contained a reachable creator gateway.
entries.rootCause: Server readiness was treated as sufficient to start the bounded window; client route readiness had only source evidence, not installed-binary evidence.
entries.prevention: Before any future PrivateUpload activation, first prove the exact installed package identity and creator-gateway route under the all-safe PublicData profile. Only then materialize and deploy the expiring profile. If client qualification fails, restore PublicData immediately and record no-consent/no-upload outcome.

entries.mistake: A broad build-script inventory used an alternation that effectively selected nearly every PowerShell file; the output exceeded the model context and was truncated before the approved wrapper could be identified.
entries.rootCause: The second alternation matched the generic .ps1 suffix independently of the intended Android/build terms, so the command was not bounded by the actual wrapper owner.
entries.prevention: Discover APK build ownership only from exact durable handoff/build references or a narrowly scoped scripts-directory content search with an explicit result limit. Never enumerate all PowerShell files to infer the wrapper.

entries.mistake: A read-only machine-state size probe piped directly from a foreach statement without grouping; PowerShell rejected the command before reading either file.
entries.rootCause: The foreach statement was used as a pipeline expression without an enclosing expression or intermediate result variable.
entries.prevention: For bounded multi-file PowerShell probes, assign foreach output to a task-specific variable and pipe that variable afterward. Never append a pipeline directly to a foreach statement.

entries.mistake: A structured ticket probe assumed several C29N-C29R filenames. Missing paths produced nonterminating Get-Content errors while the command still returned partial JSON with exit code zero.
entries.rootCause: Ticket identifiers were converted into guessed filenames instead of first resolving exact repository paths, and ErrorAction Stop was not applied to the read.
entries.prevention: Resolve ticket files with a narrow exact-id content search before reading them. Every multi-ticket read validates path existence and uses terminating error handling; partial rows are never accepted as evidence.

entries.mistake: A fixed-string lookup for a known C29T qualification hash searched the repository root and timed out despite excluding two large paths.
entries.rootCause: The evidence lookup was broader than its known config/docs ownership and traversed unrelated repository content.
entries.prevention: Qualification-hash and evidence-reference lookups are limited to their exact config and docs owners with a hard result bound. Repository-root evidence searches are forbidden for C29W qualification.

entries.mistake: The durable C29N-C29T ticket-bound source gates were invoked after C29W became the active scope ticket; C29N correctly rejected the active-ticket mismatch before any later gate ran.
entries.rootCause: Durable predecessor qualifications were confused with current-source test evidence even though their gate contracts require their own ticket to be active.
entries.prevention: Under C29W, never rerun C29N-C29T ticket-bound gates or mutate the active ticket to satisfy them. Reuse their durable host evidence and run only C29W-scoped format, analysis, focused tests, delivery, scope and regression gates.

entries.mistake: C29W source cycle 1 used Flutter's expanded default reporter for 149 passing assertions; the transcript was truncated even though the final pass result remained visible.
entries.rootCause: The assertion scope was appropriately broad, but the reporter emitted a status line for nearly every assertion and exceeded the tool-output budget.
entries.prevention: Retain the identical protected test set but use Flutter's compact reporter for repeat qualification cycles and build evidence. Record only the decisive assertion total, exit status and source fingerprint.

entries.mistake: Cycle 2 used Flutter's compact reporter as planned, but the host expanded carriage-return progress frames and again truncated the transcript despite the final 149/149 pass remaining visible.
entries.rootCause: Compact terminal refreshes reduce visible lines interactively but are serialized as many lines by the tool transport.
entries.prevention: For future broad Flutter suites, bound transported output with a task-specific rolling tail while preserving the external process exit code and final assertion result. Reporter selection alone is not an output bound.

entries.mistake: The delivery-lock script printed its explicit pass result, but a follow-up LASTEXITCODE check read a stale native-process value and falsely threw before the remaining gates ran.
entries.rootCause: LASTEXITCODE is not a reliable success signal for a PowerShell script that completes by output/exception and does not invoke a final native command.
entries.prevention: Invoke PowerShell gates under ErrorAction Stop and accept normal return as success; do not inspect LASTEXITCODE afterward. Use LASTEXITCODE only immediately after the native process that owns it.

entries.mistake: The successful r60.35 profile build reported that several third-party plugins still apply the Kotlin Gradle Plugin and a future Flutter version will require Built-in Kotlin migration.
entries.rootCause: The sealed dependency set includes plugins that have not yet migrated to Flutter's future Built-in Kotlin requirement.
entries.prevention: Keep successful sealed candidates unchanged, but block every future APK/AAB wrapper before Gradle while any resolved release plugin explicitly applies the legacy Kotlin Gradle Plugin. Upgrade or override dependencies only under a separate dependency ticket, never patch Pub cache, and rerun both full Android qualification cycles after migration.

entries.mistake: A coordinate intended for the Shorts dock target was reused without refreshing the semantic tree after several route transitions; it reached the image-post media action and opened Android Photo Picker.
entries.rootCause: The device route stack changed between the last captured semantics and the tap, so a previously valid coordinate was no longer evidence-bound to the intended control.
entries.prevention: Before every consequential device tap, capture a fresh UI hierarchy and bind the coordinate to its current content description and bounds. If the visible route differs, stop and recover with Back; never select media or continue from an unintended picker.

entries.mistake: A fresh UI hierarchy was captured, but the probe assumed the menu target's exact content description was 'Social, current domain' and rejected when that literal was absent.
entries.rootCause: The target label varies with current-domain/navigation state, so an exact literal was treated as stable before inspecting the fresh hierarchy.
entries.prevention: Inspect the bounded fresh clickable-node inventory first, then bind the tap to the actually exported Social description and bounds. Do not guess state-dependent semantic labels.

entries.mistake: A bounded Shorts-owner search assumed the backend source lived at functions/src; ripgrep rejected because that path does not exist in this repository layout.
entries.rootCause: A conventional Firebase directory was guessed instead of resolving the exact deployed backend owner from firebase.json or the existing C29U evidence.
entries.prevention: Resolve the backend source directory from the repository's firebase.json and C29U ticket before searching. Never guess conventional source paths in this dirty production tree.

entries.mistake: A 326-line Social feed owner slice exceeded the available model context and was truncated before the complete class boundary could be inspected.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic range was too broad for a large, densely implemented Dart owner.
entries.prevention: Resolve the exact class and method boundaries first, then inspect one literal owner in non-overlapping 60-to-100-line ranges. No range above 120 lines is accepted for Social feed implementation evidence.

entries.mistake: The resumed branch reconciliation printed the full very large dirty tree, and the transported status output was truncated.
entries.rootCause: A full human-readable status render was requested even though this repository is known to contain thousands of preserved evidence paths.
entries.prevention: Establish branch and HEAD as scalar values, count status records without rendering them, and inspect only ticket-owned paths plus exact unexpected-path projections. A truncated status render is never dirty-tree evidence.

entries.mistake: The complete regression-memory document and registry tail were emitted in one tool result; the document render exceeded the output budget and was truncated.
entries.rootCause: A required complete read was combined with a second projection instead of paging the large document through verified non-overlapping ranges.
entries.prevention: Line-count large required documents first, page one literal owner through non-overlapping bounded ranges, and confirm total coverage. Registry projections run separately and remain bounded.

entries.mistake: A PowerShell projection counted null-delimited git status output as one pipeline object and reported status_records=1, which did not represent the dirty-tree record count.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell captured the native null-delimited stream as one string instead of splitting its NUL separators or using line-delimited porcelain output for counting.
entries.prevention: Count dirty records with line-delimited git status --porcelain=v1 output captured as an array, and emit only the scalar count. Null-delimited output is reserved for a parser that explicitly splits NUL bytes.

entries.mistake: A fixed protected-lock hash lookup searched all quality documents and timed out before confirming the already-known inherited checksum mismatch evidence.
entries.rootCause: The content search traversed the large append-only quality evidence tree instead of using the already-pinned durable C29R qualification owner from current project memory.
entries.prevention: Use the exact existing C29R completion/qualification path recorded by the active handoff or a bounded filename inventory before any content read. Never search the complete quality tree for a known protected-lock hash.

entries.mistake: The compact Chat rail used defaultTargetPlatform without directly importing package:flutter/foundation.dart, and focused analysis rejected the owner.
entries.rootCause: The new platform symbol was assumed to be reachable through Material or the imported navigation owner; Dart imports are not transitive.
entries.prevention: Every production owner directly imports the declaring library for each new public symbol. Run focused strict analysis immediately after formatting before writing behavior tests.

entries.mistake: The direct Flutter analysis command was stored in a registry gates array, but the checker treats every gate entry as a repository path and rejected it as missing evidence.
entries.rootCause: A command invocation was confused with the registry schema's existing-path gate contract despite the durable lesson that entries may reference only materialized owners.
entries.prevention: Registry gates list only existing repository scripts or files. Direct commands stay in evidence prose until a separately authored and passing source-gate script exists.

entries.mistake: A required bounded test-file read was combined with an optional import-token search; zero optional matches made the compound command exit one despite the successful read.
entries.rootCause: The absence-capable ripgrep result was not isolated or explicitly admitted before it shared the required inspection command.
entries.prevention: Required file reads run alone. Optional absence searches run separately, explicitly accept ripgrep exit one as zero matches and reject only codes above one.

entries.mistake: Immediately after registering the compound-search rule, a required local-navigation token lookup was again combined with an optional navy-token lookup whose zero matches made the command exit one.
entries.rootCause: Two logically independent source-token questions were still placed in one shell invocation instead of applying the newly active isolation rule.
entries.prevention: Each ripgrep token question is a separate invocation. Required symbols must match; optional symbols explicitly map exit one to zero results. No compound multi-symbol diagnostic is accepted for C29X.

entries.mistake: The new edge test and two existing Chat journeys still searched for the non-compact mool-home-launcher key after Chat intentionally moved to the shared compact rail.
entries.rootCause: The source used the correct shared compact launcher identity, but the Chat test migration did not atomically replace its three old non-compact key references with the exact production mool-compact-launcher key.
entries.prevention: When a founder-approved navigation successor changes the shared control variant, inspect the declaring production key and migrate every affected test reference atomically. Never add a duplicate compatibility key that would diverge from the uniform rail contract.

entries.mistake: After the key migration, one Chat journey tapped the compact Mool launcher but still expected the old immediate personal-mool-root-v2 visible owner; the focused suite rejected that post-tap state.
entries.rootCause: Only the control key was migrated. The assertion following the action was not reconciled with the shared compact launcher's connected-switcher interaction contract.
entries.prevention: A navigation variant migration audits the complete action-to-visible-owner sequence, including overlay or hub state and Back recovery. Update tests only after inspecting the exact shared production callback and stable visible-owner key.

entries.mistake: Three independent Create test-token inventories were combined; the third optional token had zero matches and made the command exit one after two useful result sets printed.
entries.rootCause: The active one-token-per-invocation rule was not applied when transitioning from C29X to C29Y test discovery.
entries.prevention: Every C29Y test token inventory is its own ripgrep invocation with explicit required or optional semantics. Printed matches from a failed compound command are leads only and are re-established separately before use.

entries.mistake: The creator ownership header patch closed the TextStyle/Text/children nesting with mismatched parentheses, and dart format rejected the file at lines 450-452.
entries.rootCause: A nested const Row/Column/Text replacement was not syntax-reviewed in its freshly patched local region before running the formatter.
entries.prevention: After a nested Dart widget-tree patch, re-read the exact changed region and count list versus constructor closures before formatting. Formatter success is required before analysis or tests.

entries.mistake: The bracket-fix patch used an ambiguous two-line closure anchor and changed a different matching widget closure near line 369 while leaving the ownership header invalid.
entries.rootCause: A repeated generic `),` sequence was used as a mutation anchor instead of including the exact declaring widget and nearby unique text.
entries.prevention: Closure repairs include the unique local widget declaration and surrounding literal text in the patch hunk. Re-read every formatter-reported region before the next attempt and never patch a repeated closure signature alone.

entries.mistake: After removing the reachable intermediate creator gateway, focused analysis found the gateway upload import and _youtubeCreatorReady field were no longer used.
entries.rootCause: The behavior branch was removed without a complete import-and-field consumer inventory in the same atomic patch.
entries.prevention: A removed Create owner branch includes an exact remaining-use search for every branch-only import, field and helper. Unused dependencies are removed in the same ticket before focused analysis is rerun.

entries.mistake: The full Create publication suite kept a helper that generated two-choice poll and quiz fixtures; production correctly rejected them under the new four-choice contract, then the test failed while searching for an item that was never published.
entries.rootCause: The main test cases were migrated to four choices, but a shared fixture helper later in the same file was missed.
entries.prevention: Choice-count contract changes inventory every SocialPublishedChoice construction in the exact focused test owner. All accepted poll/quiz fixtures use four complete choices, while a named negative test retains the two-choice rejection case.

entries.mistake: The Screen 04 conformance test migrated its main Create case but retained three later expectations for the removed social-creator-gateway owner; 25 cases passed and 3 failed.
entries.rootCause: Only the initially inspected local test region was updated even though the exact former-gateway key inventory already proved additional references elsewhere in the same file.
entries.prevention: A removed visible owner is migrated from the complete exact-key reference inventory for every affected test file, not one local range. Re-run the whole owner suite after all references map to the direct composer or Feed recovery state.

entries.mistake: The compact Feed header intentionally changed the badge from MOOL OWNED to PUBLIC FEED, but the continuous Social suite retained the old copy expectation; 43 cases passed and 1 failed.
entries.rootCause: The Feed presentation patch removed the oversized ownership hierarchy without migrating the exact copy assertion in its owning focused test.
entries.prevention: Founder-visible Feed copy changes include an exact test-token inventory and migrate stable ownership assertions in the same patch. The new test also asserts the compact brand key and truthful empty CTA rather than the removed hierarchy.

entries.mistake: The combined C30A ticket and preselection-evidence Add File patch returned a truncated tool result, leaving both mutation outcomes unknown.
entries.rootCause: Two durable files with long ticket prose were submitted in one mutation call, and the resulting tool response exceeded the available context.
entries.prevention: After recording this rejection, verify only the two exact target paths and parse any materialized JSON before reuse. Future durable ticket files are added one per patch, followed by a bounded existence, parse and hash check; an unknown tool result is never treated as success.

entries.mistake: The bounded two-path existence inspection piped directly from a foreach statement without grouping it, and PowerShell rejected the command with an empty-pipe parser error.
entries.rootCause: The foreach output expression was not assigned or enclosed before ConvertTo-Json.
entries.prevention: Bounded multi-path PowerShell inspections first assign foreach results to a task-specific variable and pipe that variable to serialization. Parser-failed output is discarded and the check is rerun only after the rejection is registered and the memory gate passes.

entries.mistake: The maxResults source inventory included the guessed path backend/functions/test, which does not exist; ripgrep returned exit one despite printing valid owner matches.
entries.rootCause: The backend test directory was assumed instead of being established through a bounded filename inventory.
entries.prevention: Discard matches from a command containing an invalid path. Establish exact backend test owner paths with rg --files and a filename filter, then run each required token search only against verified files or verified directories.

entries.mistake: The complete Social suite found that C29O still attempted to select Feed from the global rail after selecting direct Create, even though the accepted composer contract intentionally hides that rail until the composer closes.
entries.rootCause: The test's sequential destination loop was not migrated atomically when Create became a direct posting-ready surface with composer-open rail containment.
entries.prevention: Social destination tests treat direct Create as a terminal step in a rail sequence or close the composer through its real owner before selecting another rail destination. They never require a hidden rail while composition is active.

entries.mistake: The complete Social suite found that the Feed ownership test still expected no post CTA when a real public item was loaded, contradicting the founder-approved timeline-first then posting-ready CTA composition.
entries.rootCause: C29Z migrated the publication-order tests but missed the independent Feed ownership owner's obsolete absence assertion.
entries.prevention: Every Feed owner test asserts real public content appears before the single posting CTA. Loaded-state tests no longer interpret the founder-required after-timeline CTA as filler.

entries.mistake: After correctly closing the OPPO composer, the hierarchy parser assigned the selected Home node to PowerShell's read-only $HOME variable and the inspection command was rejected.
entries.rootCause: A common system variable name was reused instead of a task-specific device hierarchy variable, directly violating the workspace command-variable rule.
entries.prevention: Every shell variable uses a task-specific name such as $socialHomeNode. Never assign $HOME, $home or $CODEX_HOME. The rejected parse output is discarded and the next semantic action occurs only after regression memory passes.

entries.mistake: A combined registry-and-evidence patch returned truncated tool output, so its mutation result could not be treated as known.
entries.rootCause: The patch operation bundled more output than the available result context could reliably report.
entries.prevention: Register the truncation first, then verify each prior target by exact ID and exact path in bounded checks; never infer success from a truncated mutation result.

entries.mistake: The OPPO positioning check required a Feed semantic action to coexist on the YouTube Home hierarchy even though the accepted native YouTube bottom surface exposes the Mool edge rather than the nested MoolSocial Feed action.
entries.rootCause: The verification mixed the global Home-surface contract with a nested MoolSocial destination contract.
entries.prevention: Founder-review positioning verifies the selected YouTube Home state and its native Home/Shorts/Create plus global Mool/Chat actions. Nested Feed semantics are checked only after opening MoolSocial.

entries.mistake: The OPPO Home tap center calculation added regex capture strings before numeric conversion, producing an out-of-bounds coordinate and leaving Feed selected.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell string concatenation occurred before the enclosing integer cast.
entries.prevention: Convert every captured bounds coordinate to an integer before addition, validate the calculated point lies within the reported bounds and device display, then issue exactly one semantic tap and verify the selected destination in a fresh hierarchy.

entries.mistake: A final read-only summary queried build, install and acceptance properties at the C30B machine-state root without first respecting their actual nested schema, yielding misleading default zero and false values.
entries.rootCause: The state shape was assumed from semantic field names instead of reading the exact sealed JSON structure.
entries.prevention: Inspect the bounded machine-state schema first, then select values only from proven paths; missing PowerShell properties are never cast into reportable zero, false or empty defaults.

entries.mistake: The mandatory full dirty-tree reconciliation serialized every status line in one tool result and the output was truncated.
entries.rootCause: The very large preserved worktree was emitted directly instead of being reconciled through a retained full inventory plus bounded category counts and hashes.
entries.prevention: For this repository, preserve a complete status inventory inside the authorized evidence directory, report bounded tracked/untracked/category counts and a SHA-256, and inspect only exact ticket-owner paths needed for the selected scope. Never treat truncated status output as complete.

entries.mistake: The bounded dirty-state inventory used ordinary Windows Git traversal; retained browser-profile evidence produced many filename-too-long warnings, truncated the result, and made the untracked inventory incomplete.
entries.rootCause: The command did not enable Git's per-invocation long-path support before traversing the preserved evidence tree.
entries.prevention: Repeat reconciliation only with per-command core.longpaths=true, capture standard output and standard error separately, require zero exit and zero warning records, then seal the full inventory hash. The rejected inventory is retained but never used as authoritative evidence.

entries.mistake: The Shorts diagnostic assumed one Android Back from active embedded playback must expose the YouTube Home bottom action, then failed when the fresh hierarchy did not contain that action.
entries.rootCause: The command asserted a destination before identifying whether Back first exited player controls, the watch surface, or the Social surface.
entries.prevention: After every provider-player Back, inspect the fresh hierarchy and foreground state first. Navigate through only the semantics actually present, and never infer the next Social destination from a fixed Back count.

entries.mistake: A semantic coordinate tap on the visible YouTube filter sheet Close action returned success but the fresh hierarchy still exposed the same sheet and actions.
entries.rootCause: ADB input success was treated as sufficient without requiring a destination-state change; the sheet may have intercepted or ignored the coordinate action.
entries.prevention: Every device dismissal must assert the target sheet semantics disappear. If a semantic tap produces no state change, register it and use the platform Back dismissal contract only after the regression gate passes.

entries.mistake: Platform Back also left the current YouTube filter sheet visible, proving it is a persistent app-state defect rather than a one-off coordinate miss.
entries.rootCause: The existing filter owner lacks a reliable dismissal/route restoration contract while the keyboard/search state is active.
entries.prevention: Replace the internal filter sheet with a route-owned YouTube search surface whose Close/Back and IME transitions are widget-tested and OPPO-replayed; do not retry dismissal on the defective owner as if it were production-ready.

entries.mistake: The required preimplementation approved-UI lock gate rejected because the already-dirty shared ui_v2_customer_copy_machine_gate_test.dart hash differs from the immutable login checkpoint manifest.
entries.rootCause: Prior preserved Social work modified a cross-screen shared test that the old Screens 01-03 lock also hashes; C30C did not create the mismatch, but a broad parallel gate call obscured the otherwise passing ticket gates.
entries.prevention: Preserve and do not edit the pre-existing shared test or any locked Screen 01-03 file. Record its exact pre-ticket hash, add C30C tests in a new focused owner, run ticket gates separately, and report the pre-existing lock rejection without rewriting the immutable manifest.

entries.mistake: Both focused Search widget cases called TestTextInput.receiveAction without awaiting its Future, then immediately called pump or pumpAndSettle and triggered guarded-function conflicts.
entries.rootCause: The test treated keyboard action delivery as synchronous even though Flutter test guards it as asynchronous.
entries.prevention: Every TestTextInput.receiveAction call is awaited before any subsequent tester API. Focused IME tests must pass the guarded-operation check before behavioral failures are interpreted.

entries.mistake: The first full Social regression-suite wait emitted more Flutter progress output than the available model context, so the completion state and result were not usable evidence.
entries.rootCause: The long suite streamed its complete progress through the interactive wait channel instead of retaining the full output in a file and returning only a bounded exit summary.
entries.prevention: Long Flutter suites write complete output to a new retained evidence log and return only exit code, bounded final lines, byte count and SHA-256. A truncated tool result is rejected and never inferred to be a pass.

entries.mistake: The regression-memory gate was invoked with an unsupported -Mode parameter and PowerShell rejected the command before the gate ran.
entries.rootCause: A parameter shape was assumed from another gate instead of reading the current script's declared parameter block.
entries.prevention: Read the bounded parameter block of a repository gate before invoking optional arguments. Use only parameters declared by that exact script, and never interpret parameter-binding failure as a gate result.

entries.mistake: The rejected full-suite exec cell was queried after its truncated wait, but the cell had already closed and was no longer available, so no bounded completion result could be recovered.
entries.rootCause: The first run did not persist its authoritative output independently of the transient exec-cell lifecycle.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or infer the unavailable cell. Rerun the exact suite with output persisted atomically to a new repository evidence log and retain a bounded exit/hash summary outside the cell lifecycle.

entries.mistake: The first C30D MVP-state patch assumed several JSON arrays were single-line, so apply_patch rejected the unmatched context before changing the state file.
entries.rootCause: The patch was composed from a semantically accurate read but did not preserve the file's exact live whitespace and multi-line array formatting.
entries.prevention: Use exact bounded live sections for state-file patches, keep hunks small, and validate the resulting JSON plus ticket manifest hash before running the MVP gates. Never infer a partial update from an apply_patch context rejection.

entries.mistake: The C30D gate batch invoked a guessed scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate.ps1 path that does not exist; the surrounding delivery and regression gates passed, but the missing command itself is rejected.
entries.rootCause: The scope-gate filename was recalled generically instead of resolved from the repository's exact live scripts inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve gate filenames with a bounded rg --files query before invocation, run the exact existing scope gate separately, and treat any missing command in a multi-command batch as a rejection even if the shell's final exit code is zero.

entries.mistake: The first C30D focused widget test deferred its SemanticsHandle disposal to addTearDown, but Flutter's end-of-test verification still observed the handle as active and rejected the case after all behavioral assertions passed.
entries.rootCause: The new test used teardown timing instead of the proven focused-test pattern that disposes the semantics handle explicitly before the test body returns.
entries.prevention: Dispose a focused test's SemanticsHandle explicitly after its final semantics assertion and before the test body exits; reserve addTearDown for owners and view resets. Rerun the focused test only after the regression is registered.

entries.mistake: The historical C28E host-remediation gate was invoked under the active C30D founder-authorized build/install scope and rejected because that old ticket permanently requires build and install authority to be closed.
entries.rootCause: A completed historical source gate was reused as if it were a current successor-qualification gate, even though it reads the mutable active MVP scope and asserts C28E-era authority values.
entries.prevention: Do not weaken or rewrite C28E. Under a later build-authorized ticket, prove its immutable 58/44/27 geometry with the current C28B/C30D Flutter tests and fresh native OPPO bounds gate; report the historical script as not context-compatible rather than retrying it.

entries.mistake: The historical C26D source-literal gate was invoked after the accepted Social ownership redesign and rejected because it still requires the old direct bottomNavigationBar: MoolDestinationNavigationV2 literal.
entries.rootCause: The gate predates the accepted conditional SocialOwnershipDock successor and validates a removed implementation string instead of the current customer navigation contract.
entries.prevention: Do not restore the obsolete generic Social projection or weaken C26D. Use current C29E/C29N/C30D widget contracts for Mool-left, Chat-right, Home/Shorts/Create/Feed order, tap reach and exported semantics; run the customer-copy gate separately.

entries.mistake: The full user-facing-copy gate rejected the pre-existing shared social_content_gateway.dart owner at line 441 for the prohibited word endpoint; C30D did not edit that owner and its prior gate batch had not reached the copy gate.
entries.rootCause: A broad copy gate contains an already-dirty Social backend-recovery copy owner outside the footer ticket; running it only after the navigation gates exposed the inherited rejection.
entries.prevention: Prove the exact owner and current copy context before disposition. Do not silently waive the broad gate or fold unrelated backend recovery copy into C30D; register a sequential bounded copy correction if the phrase is customer-visible, otherwise retain the pre-existing rejection with focused C30C/C30D copy tests.

entries.mistake: The post-build read-only Android tool discovery repeated the registered PowerShell parser error by piping directly after a foreach statement, so it failed before locating apksigner or manifest tools.
entries.rootCause: The formatter used a control statement directly on the pipeline instead of first assigning its emitted objects to a bounded collection.
entries.prevention: Assign foreach output to a task-specific array, then pipe that array to ConvertTo-Json. Run the build-regression memory gate before retrying; the successful one-build artifact remains untouched and no second build is allowed.

entries.mistake: The first-launch evidence queried mCurrentFocus and mFocusedApp from dumpsys window windows, but this OPPO build emitted neither field and the bounded foreground value was null.
entries.rootCause: The command assumed legacy window-service focus fields instead of using the OPPO-proven resumed-activity field from ActivityTaskManager.
entries.prevention: Retain the first untapped hierarchy and screenshot, register the empty field, then read mResumedActivity from dumpsys activity activities without relaunching or tapping. Foreground identity must be non-empty before accepting the native bounds record.

entries.mistake: The corrected foreground query required the literal mResumedActivity: form, but the OPPO activity service did not return a matching line and the bounds formatter rejected before parsing the preserved hierarchy.
entries.rootCause: The field-name correction remained too specific about punctuation and did not first inventory the bounded resumed/top-resumed activity lines emitted by this OS build.
entries.prevention: Read only bounded activity lines matching ResumedActivity or topResumedActivity without assuming punctuation, select a non-empty com.moolsocial.app owner, and reuse the original untapped hierarchy. Do not relaunch or interact to repair evidence formatting.

entries.mistake: The first Watch-from-Search assertion counted every clickable node whose description equals YouTube as a prohibited top-header logo, conflating required content-card attribution with the removed header owner and rejecting the combined state.
entries.rootCause: The native selector used label equality without constraining the node to the header region or excluding content-level attribution descendants.
entries.prevention: Inspect the retained Watch screenshot and bounded node coordinates, assert Back and Search independently, and classify a YouTube attribution as a top-logo regression only when its bounds lie in the header region. Required clickable content attribution remains allowed and must not fail the gate.

entries.mistake: A real Search result opened the Watch surface with a native Back action labelled Back to YouTube Home even though C30C intentionally returns that action to the preserved Search results.
entries.rootCause: The Watch header owns a fixed Home-oriented tooltip and was not given the runtime return destination selected by the Search-to-Watch continuity state.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.37 for founder acceptance, confirm the Back action returns to Search, then add a bounded source successor whose visible/native label is Back to YouTube Search results only for Search-origin Watch and remains Back to YouTube Home for Home-origin Watch. Cover both semantics before another separately qualified build.

entries.mistake: The apply_patch result for the C30H prebuild machine-state file exceeded the available model context and was truncated, leaving the target's creation state unknown.
entries.rootCause: A large one-shot patch did not preserve a bounded mutation result that could be verified inside the remaining context.
entries.prevention: Before retrying, inspect only the exact target's existence, JSON parseability and bounded seal fields. Reapply only when absence or incompleteness is proved, using smaller patches, and run the permanent regression gate before resuming the build sequence.

entries.mistake: The first coordinate-driven Search replay used a previously captured Home hierarchy, but the post-action native capture showed Feed was active before text input, so the resulting artifacts could not prove Search.
entries.rootCause: The replay did not re-read and assert the live device state immediately before and immediately after the coordinate action.
entries.prevention: Before every device interaction, capture and parse the live hierarchy, derive the action bounds from that exact capture, perform only that action, and assert the expected destination in a new hierarchy before the next interaction. Preserve the rejected artifacts and never claim them as Search evidence.

entries.mistake: PowerShell concatenated captured XML bound strings before division and produced an impossible device tap midpoint.
entries.rootCause: The calculation cast only after adding string-valued regex captures instead of converting each capture to an integer first.
entries.prevention: Convert every captured bound component to an integer before addition, range-check the midpoint against the live physical display, then perform the action and assert the destination in a new hierarchy.

entries.mistake: The guarded replay expected an Open Home, YouTube action in the fresh hierarchy, but the current surface contained no such node and the action correctly stopped before tapping.
entries.rootCause: The replay still selected an intended action from an assumed prior Feed surface instead of first classifying the newly captured live surface.
entries.prevention: Classify the current surface from a bounded inventory of live native labels before selecting any action. Derive and range-check the next action only from that classified hierarchy, and assert the destination before continuing.

entries.mistake: The Open Social action succeeded, but a fixed wait asserted stable Home readiness while the real provider was still in its explicit loading state.
entries.rootCause: The replay treated elapsed time as provider readiness instead of polling native state until the stable required action set appeared.
entries.prevention: After a successful route action, use bounded no-touch hierarchy polling that accepts the explicit loading state and stops only on stable required actions or a captured timeout/error state. Never repeat the route action merely to repair timing.

entries.mistake: A read-only label lookup included a remembered YouTube Search test filename that does not exist and made rg exit non-zero.
entries.rootCause: The command used an inferred test path instead of discovering the exact current path from the repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files to discover the exact test path before including it in a lookup, and never append a remembered or inferred filename to a gate or search command.

entries.mistake: Green vertical edge lines became visible on both sides of the stable YouTube Home surface after keyboard-event replay and persisted across Social navigation.
entries.rootCause: A raw hardware-key event focused the Android Flutter root View, whose API-26 default focus fallback drew the device's green highlight around the full surface because NormalTheme did not disable that native fallback.
entries.prevention: API-26 day and night NormalTheme owners must set android:defaultFocusHighlightEnabled=false while Flutter retains control-level focus visuals and semantics. Keep the focused C30I resource contract active and require native raw-key replay on a separately qualified successor.

entries.mistake: A bounded reuse search found no existing Android focus-highlight resource test, but rg exit code 1 was surfaced as a command failure instead of an explicit no-match result.
entries.rootCause: The command did not distinguish rg's valid no-match exit code from execution failure.
entries.prevention: For duplicate-audit searches where zero matches is valid, classify exit code 0 as matches, 1 as no matches, and any other code as failure.

entries.mistake: The C30I machine ticket used the invented implementation disposition shared_owner_extension, which the locked MVP delivery checkpoint does not support.
entries.rootCause: The ticket vocabulary was authored from intent instead of the exact allowed-value set in the locked checkpoint.
entries.prevention: Read the locked allowed-value set before authoring or updating a machine ticket and use the narrowest exact supported token; never invent a semantically similar disposition label.

entries.mistake: The checkpoint vocabulary lookup guessed a root property named allowedImplementationDispositions that does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The command inferred a JSON property path from a validation message instead of discovering the actual bounded schema first.
entries.prevention: Inventory the checkpoint's bounded root and nested property names first, then read only an actually discovered property path; never infer schema paths from validation messages.

entries.mistake: A full Social test command inferred from two visible loading paths in an old 164-test log executed only 17 tests.
entries.rootCause: The prior log's carriage-return rendering was treated as a complete input inventory instead of recovering an explicit suite command or enumerating the intended tests.
entries.prevention: Recover the complete suite definition from an explicit prior command or enumerate the exact intended test inventory before execution, and assert the expected final test count for every claimed full cycle.

entries.mistake: A test log path used ../../../ from apps/mobile and resolved to the workspace-level artifacts directory instead of the production repository artifacts directory.
entries.rootCause: The evidence path was not resolved and boundary-checked before the test command wrote its log.
entries.prevention: Resolve and print the absolute evidence directory before execution, require it to start with the production repository artifacts/quality boundary, and pass that absolute path to the log writer.

entries.mistake: The historical 164-test count was treated as reproducible from nine recoverable test paths, but the recovered-path matrix plus two C30I tests passed only 87 tests.
entries.rootCause: The historical machine evidence stored a count and log hash but no explicit complete test input inventory, and carriage-return output could not reconstruct every invoked path.
entries.prevention: Every full-cycle contract must store an explicit current test inventory, final count and log hash; both cycles must use the identical sealed inventory and count.

entries.mistake: The current Social qualification inventory included historical C17c clear-glass and C20d four-action conformance tests whose shell assertions were superseded by the founder-accepted Social redesign.
entries.rootCause: Filename-based inventory selection included protected historical reference owners without checking their active/superseded disposition.
entries.prevention: Do not edit or weaken the historical tests; version the current suite inventory, explicitly disposition C17c and C20d as protected historical references, and qualify current Social owners plus active global navigation and accessibility gates.

entries.mistake: The YouTube account-state owner audit appended the nonexistent shorthand functions/src even though repository discovery identified backend/functions/src.
entries.rootCause: A discovered repository path was shortened from memory in the follow-up search command.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files discovery results as the only backend-owner inputs and never shorten or infer a repository path for follow-up searches.

entries.mistake: A material zero-match search proving no YouTube connection-status gateway exists in the consumer/router was allowed to surface as an unclassified rg failure.
entries.rootCause: The REG1388 exit-code classifier was not reused for a duplicate-audit search where zero matches was valid.
entries.prevention: Classify rg exit code 0 as matches, 1 as a valid no-match finding, and any other code as failure for every duplicate-audit search.

entries.mistake: The active continuous Social batch still expected the YouTube Home account action to open the old MoolSocial account sheet after C30J moved it to the authoritative YouTube channel-status route.
entries.rootCause: The adjacent current-owner test was not included in the focused navigation matrix before the first complete cycle.
entries.prevention: Assert the neutral YouTube channel-status route in the active batch and independently retain MoolSocial account coverage through its global owner; never restore a MoolSocial account avatar inside YouTube Home.

entries.mistake: A combined multi-file source-hash command emitted more output than the available model context after the C30J qualification cycles, so the result could not be used as bounded evidence.
entries.rootCause: The read-only evidence command requested unnecessary per-file output instead of returning only the exact hash needed for the next state transition.
entries.prevention: Request one required hash per bounded command, cap direct output, and never combine an open-ended source inventory with a state-transition hash operation.

entries.mistake: The Dev social-content owner inventory appended a root firebase path that does not exist in the repository and made rg surface a path error.
entries.rootCause: The discovery command mixed verified roots with an inferred conventional Firebase directory name.
entries.prevention: Discover repository roots and exact files with rg --files first, then search only verified paths; never append a conventional service directory name without confirming it exists.

entries.mistake: A single symbol search spanned mobile gateway, large Flutter presentation files and all social backend owners, producing truncated output that could not be treated as a complete audit.
entries.rootCause: The audit combined independent owner questions and broad high-frequency terms in one command instead of inspecting each bounded contract owner separately.
entries.prevention: Inspect mobile gateway, backend contract/service/store, and presentation owners in separate bounded commands using narrow symbols or line ranges; never claim completeness from truncated search output.

entries.mistake: The Dev Auth provisioning audit guessed a gcloud identity platforms command group that is not installed in the current CLI and surfaced an invalid-choice failure.
entries.rootCause: A remembered Identity Platform CLI namespace was invoked without first discovering the exact installed gcloud command surface.
entries.prevention: Use bounded gcloud help search or documented installed commands before invoking an identity-management namespace; never infer a CLI group from product naming.

entries.mistake: The complete 498-test backend suite was streamed directly into the tool response, which truncated intermediate output even though the final summary reported a pass.
entries.rootCause: The large suite was not redirected to a repository evidence log before execution.
entries.prevention: Run complete backend suites into a pre-resolved repository evidence file, then return only the bounded final summary, exit code and SHA-256; never accept a directly truncated run as qualifying evidence.

entries.mistake: A combined Firebase CLI and Java availability check invoked java directly even though no Java executable is on the current PATH, surfacing a command-not-found failure.
entries.rootCause: The dependency probe did not classify Get-Command java before attempting execution.
entries.prevention: Resolve each host dependency with Get-Command first and execute a version probe only when an exact executable is present; record a missing runtime as a bounded qualification gate instead of invoking it.

entries.mistake: The first deny-all rules emulator attempt invoked emulators:exec before verifying how the installed Firebase CLI resolves the configured Firestore and Storage emulator targets, and the CLI reported no emulators to start.
entries.rootCause: The exact installed CLI version, parsed target argument and effective firebase.json selection were not preflighted after supplying the Android Studio Java runtime.
entries.prevention: Before retrying, record the installed Firebase CLI version, use an explicit config path and a quoted comma-delimited --only value, then confirm the CLI recognizes the exact configured targets without changing firebase.json.

entries.mistake: The Flutter corpus-coverage audit appended a remembered C29Z feed timeline test path that was not verified and made the multi-file rg command exit non-zero.
entries.rootCause: An inferred ticket-derived filename was mixed with two existing test paths instead of using the repository file inventory as the only input.
entries.prevention: Discover exact Flutter test paths with rg --files before multi-file searches and never derive a path from a ticket identifier or test description.

entries.mistake: After C30K transitioned to the exact external Dev apply state, the focused gate correctly validated the authority but still printed a hard-coded externalWrites=false summary.
entries.rootCause: The gate output string was not derived from the same state predicate used by its authorization assertion.
entries.prevention: Derive the reported external-write state from the validated exact apply-state predicate and reject any mismatch before an external mutation.

entries.mistake: The first exact Dev corpus apply exited after secure ADC authentication with only the generic runner_failed code, so the completed stage and possible partial writes could not be classified from the bounded evidence.
entries.rootCause: The runner redacted unknown Firebase and Google Cloud failures without retaining a safe operation-stage code, and it did not preflight required Auth, Firestore and Storage authority before the first mutation.
entries.prevention: Before any retry, perform bounded non-sensitive readback, add stage-specific safe error classification and preflight exact Dev services; rely on deterministic persona identities and post idempotency to reconcile any partial state without overwrite or duplication.

entries.mistake: C30K created all three personas and persisted the first four Asha records, then stopped when the first Quick Poll reached Firestore with an image property explicitly set to undefined on every text choice.
entries.rootCause: FirestoreSocialContentRepository always emitted the choice image field, using undefined when a choice had no media slot. Firestore rejects undefined document fields, while prior repository tests covered posts with no choices and Image Polls with defined choice images but not text-choice persistence.
entries.prevention: Omit the image property entirely for text choices, add a repository regression test that rejects any undefined value in a four-choice Quick Poll document, and retain deterministic idempotency reconciliation for the three users, four posts and eight media objects already written.

entries.mistake: The post-fix reconciliation stopped before mutation because the new Firestore read preflight used the reserved double-underscore document identifier __c30k_read_probe__ and returned grpc_3.
entries.rootCause: The preflight identifier was selected for visual namespacing without applying Firestore's reserved __.*__ identifier constraint.
entries.prevention: Use a stable ordinary identifier such as c30k-read-probe for bounded Firestore reads and retain stage-specific error classification so preflight failures cannot be confused with mutations.

entries.mistake: The first deployment-readiness summary piped a PowerShell foreach statement directly into ConvertTo-Json and was rejected by the parser before any audit result was produced.
entries.rootCause: The command assumed a foreach statement could be used directly as a pipeline expression without first grouping or assigning its output.
entries.prevention: Assign bounded loop output to an array or wrap it in an array expression before conversion, and keep independent deployment audit questions in separate commands.

entries.mistake: While preparing the deployment audit regression entries, a read-only command requested scripts/check-codex-development-regressions.ps1, which is not an existing repository path.
entries.rootCause: The command used a shortened remembered gate name instead of the verified scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 path already recorded in the registry.
entries.prevention: Use exact gate paths from the registry or discover candidates with rg --files before reading or invoking a script; never shorten a known script name from memory.

entries.mistake: The regression registration verification passed a wildcard-bearing Windows filename argument directly to rg, which reported an invalid filename syntax for the documentation path.
entries.rootCause: The command treated a shell-style filename glob as if rg on Windows would expand it before opening the path.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files with a -g filter or Get-ChildItem -Filter for wildcard discovery on Windows, then pass only resolved literal paths to rg.

entries.mistake: A repository-wide deployment evidence search included JSON artifact trees and matched a large Flutter timeline payload, truncating the output before the relevant App Check and invoker history could be fully evaluated.
entries.rootCause: The search combined independent App Check, IAM and revision questions across broad docs, artifacts and config roots without excluding generated timeline evidence.
entries.prevention: Read exact known deployment records and bounded registry line windows separately; exclude generated performance payloads and never infer completeness from a truncated broad search.

entries.mistake: The C30K-FIX1 machine-gate discovery repeated the Windows rg wildcard-path class by passing two wildcard-bearing script filename arguments directly to rg.
entries.rootCause: The known REG-1412 prevention was not applied when narrowing delivery-gate owners after the ticket hash check.
entries.prevention: All Windows wildcard file discovery must start with rg --files plus -g filters or Get-ChildItem -Filter; resolved literal paths are the only file arguments passed to content searches.

entries.mistake: The first successful 499-test C30K-FIX1 backend verification used a repository-relative evidence path while running from backend/functions, so the log was written under backend/functions/artifacts instead of the repository evidence root.
entries.rootCause: The command changed working directory for npm but did not resolve the evidence directory to an absolute repository-root path first.
entries.prevention: Resolve every evidence directory to an absolute path from the repository root before changing a command workdir; retain the first valid run but repeat qualification into the canonical evidence root.

entries.mistake: The first exact Firebase dry run used functions:moolSocialContent, completed the local predeploy build, and then stopped because no function matched that filter in the named provider codebase.
entries.rootCause: The deployment audit preserved the human target name but did not include the Firebase CLI codebase segment required by this firebase.json functions configuration.
entries.prevention: Discover the installed Firebase CLI's codebase-qualified filter syntax and use only functions:provider:moolSocialContent for both dry run and the authorized Dev redeployment; treat a no-match filter as fail-closed and never broaden to all functions.
