entries.mistake: The successful firebase-functions 7.3.2 patch update was followed by a PowerShell ConvertFrom-Json check that could not represent package-lock.json's empty-string root package property as a PSCustomObject.
entries.rootCause: The verification assumed every JSON property name could be converted to a normal PowerShell object property instead of using the hashtable mode required for the package-lock root key.
entries.prevention: Verify package-lock root dependencies with ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable or npm pkg commands; keep npm's exit code and generated hashes separate from follow-up parsing so a successful dependency mutation cannot be misclassified.

entries.mistake: After all C30K-FIX1 machine gates passed, the bounded npm residual-risk summary used the JavaScript-style literal false, which PowerShell attempted to invoke as a command.
entries.rootCause: A cross-language boolean literal was inserted into a PowerShell PSCustomObject instead of using $false.
entries.prevention: Use only PowerShell $true and $false literals in shell audit objects and keep completed gate results distinct from a later reporting-format rejection.

entries.mistake: The first parallel postdeployment verification repeated REG-1418 by using the JavaScript-style literal false in the bounded Cloud Run IAM summary, so the orchestrated result was rejected even though the cloud reads were non-mutating.
entries.rootCause: The just-registered PowerShell boolean prevention was not applied to every prepared parallel command before execution.
entries.prevention: Audit every PowerShell object literal for $true/$false before execution, keep each postdeployment proof independently bounded, and rerun all postdeployment reads after this registration rather than relying on partially returned parallel results.

entries.mistake: The C30L qualification audit correctly listed the C30J inventory directory, then appended a guessed source-manifest.txt filename even though the listing showed only inventory-seal.md and test-inventory.txt.
entries.rootCause: A prior C30H manifest naming convention was projected onto the distinct C30J Social inventory owner after exact filenames were already available.
entries.prevention: Read only filenames returned by the bounded directory inventory; do not append a conventional manifest name from another ticket, even with error suppression.

entries.mistake: The first C30L host summary redirected java -version stderr inside PowerShell and serialized the resulting ErrorRecord object, triggering JSON depth truncation instead of a bounded version string.
entries.rootCause: Native stderr was captured as a PowerShell error object without coercing each line to text before selecting the first version line.
entries.prevention: Capture native version output through cmd /c or explicitly stringify bounded lines before JSON serialization; never serialize a PowerShell ErrorRecord as host qualification evidence.

entries.mistake: After APK qualification, a bounded script-name search for install, device-qualification or apk-qualification returned no matches and exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The audit assumed a dedicated install wrapper naming convention even though prior accepted device tickets record the single in-place adb install directly in machine state and evidence.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat speculative wrapper-name searches; use the accepted bounded adb -s SERIAL install -r procedure only after exact identity, checksum, machine-state and one-install checks pass.

entries.mistake: The one authorized adb install -r completed with Success, then its reporting object repeated the JavaScript-style true/false literal class and failed after the device mutation had already succeeded.
entries.rootCause: The install result object used bare true and false values instead of PowerShell $true and $false despite the registered boolean-literal prevention.
entries.prevention: Never repeat the install. Treat the single Success log as the consumed mutation, register the reporting failure, and reconstruct postinstall evidence read-only with PowerShell-native booleans and exact installed identity checks.

entries.mistake: The C30L prebuild audit reconciled the post-r60.38 C30I/C30J/C30K work and current content deployment but did not fail on C30A's older active source_complete_real_shorts_provider_deployment_held dependency before consuming the one build.
entries.rootCause: The dependency audit treated post-r60.38 tickets as the candidate delta instead of enumerating every active Social ticket whose machine state contains a runtime or deployment hold.
entries.prevention: Before any future device build, enumerate all Social ticket states for deployment_held, runtime_required or provider proof, map each to the exact live revision, and fail closed if any mandatory journey depends on an undeployed source fix.

entries.mistake: C30L Home loaded real YouTube videos, but the first Shorts journey and one bounded Retry both settled on the truthful unavailable state instead of playable YouTube-hosted Shorts.
entries.rootCause: Live revision youtubeprovider-00035-jis predates the C30A source fix and supplies maxResults 50 to the Shorts public-catalogue client contract capped at 25, producing provider bad_request.
entries.prevention: Do not accept C30L or create a second APK. Obtain separate exact Dev youtubeProvider redeployment authority for the already implemented pageSize 25 source, qualify and deploy only that function, prove live Shorts on the installed checksum-matched r60.39 client, then resume the same founder-review candidate without rebuild or reinstall.

entries.mistake: After semantically returning from Shorts to Home, the Watch replay attempted to assign the parsed UI document to $home, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's read-only $HOME variable and aborting before any Watch tap.
entries.rootCause: A short screen-state variable name violated the workspace rule that $HOME/$home must never be repurposed.
entries.prevention: Use task-specific names such as $homeUiDocument for every screen-state object; preserve the successful Home return capture and resume from that exact current state without repeating the prior tap.

entries.mistake: The first C30L Feed client-path audit combined SharedSession and multiple Social consumer windows in one read, causing the output to exceed the available context and truncate before the exact gateway decision could be proven.
entries.rootCause: Multiple code owners and oversized source windows were read together instead of tracing one bounded owner and call site at a time.
entries.prevention: Inspect the Feed path in separate exact line windows for gateway construction, SharedSession availability/load, and Social consumer invocation; do not rely on any truncated output or repeat the combined read.

entries.mistake: The Feed runtime-define audit tried to inspect a guessed 05-single-build.log filename that does not exist in the exact C30L artifact directory.
entries.rootCause: The logical one-build evidence label was projected onto a filename instead of listing the already-sealed artifact directory and using its returned exact name.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the guessed path. Use the exact C30L machine-state requiredRuntimeDefines as the authoritative omission proof, and list bounded artifact filenames before reading any additional build evidence.

entries.mistake: The first semantic Create-navigation attempt added regex capture strings before division, concatenating each coordinate pair and producing an off-screen tap that left Feed unchanged.
entries.rootCause: Bounds captures were coerced to integers only after addition rather than before calculating the semantic-node center.
entries.prevention: Convert each of the four bounds captures to a task-specific integer variable before midpoint arithmetic, verify the point remains within the captured node, and only then issue the next bounded tap.

entries.mistake: The multi-format Create replay assumed the shared YouTube Short action would remain semantically present after switching into Carousel, so its final chained lookup failed after the valid Image Poll, Quiz and Carousel captures completed.
entries.rootCause: The replay chained heterogeneous composer states without re-auditing Carousel's current hierarchy before requesting the next action.
entries.prevention: Preserve the three completed captures, inspect Carousel independently, then leave or reopen Create through its current semantic controls before exercising YouTube Short; never assume bottom-action continuity across format-specific composer states.

entries.mistake: The first C30L disposition write combined registry, ticket, APK state, MVP state and four new evidence files in one patch; an over-broad MVP authorization context failed verification, so the entire patch was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Independent durable owners were mutated in one composite patch with context that was not re-read as an exact small window immediately before application.
entries.prevention: Confirm no partial mutation, then patch each owner independently using exact bounded context: registry first, new files second, C30L ticket, APK state, and MVP state last with JSON validation after every owner.

entries.mistake: C30L deployed and verified the real Dev MoolSocial content runtime, but its exact APK runtime-define allowlist omitted MOOLSOCIAL_SOCIAL_CONTENT_URL, so the installed client selected UnavailableSocialContentGateway and rendered an empty Feed without calling the function.
entries.rootCause: The prebuild dependency audit treated the live content function as sufficient and did not map C29P's required mobile endpoint define through the machine-state allowlist and the global APK gate, whose allowed define names also omit the Social content endpoint.
entries.prevention: Reject every future Feed/Create device candidate unless the current Dev content endpoint is an exact non-secret machine-state define, the global APK gate explicitly allows and validates it, focused controls reject omission or non-Dev endpoints, and prebuild proof observes an authenticated client call before consuming a build.

entries.mistake: The final C30L disposition validation invoked the historical C30K-FIX1 execution gate after the MVP scope machine had correctly closed, so that gate rejected the absence of its former active ticket.
entries.rootCause: A completed deployment's active-execution gate was treated as a timeless integrity gate even though it intentionally binds to the currently authorized MVP ticket.
entries.prevention: Do not reopen or alter closed MVP scope to manufacture a historical pass. Preserve the prior C30K-FIX1 passed seal and deployment evidence, and run only scope-closed, delivery-lock, registry, JSON and evidence-integrity checks after C30L disposition.

entries.mistake: The first C30M repository reconciliation printed full git status for the very large preserved dirty tree, producing filename-length warnings and truncated output before branch, HEAD and the complete count could be admitted.
entries.rootCause: The required status check was executed without separating exact branch/HEAD from a bounded dirty-state count and small path sample, despite the known multi-thousand-entry tree.
entries.prevention: Retry branch and HEAD as exact scalar reads; redirect porcelain status to a temporary repository-local evidence file or count it without printing; return only category counts, bounded first/last samples and warning count. Never print the full dirty tree during C30M.

entries.mistake: The first bounded C30M required-reading inventory repeated the PowerShell foreach-pipe parser class by piping directly after the foreach statement, producing an empty-pipe-element parser rejection.
entries.rootCause: The known PowerShell requirement to materialize foreach output before a downstream pipeline was not applied to the newly composed documentation metadata command.
entries.prevention: Wrap foreach output in @(...), assign it to a task-specific array, and only then pipe or serialize it. Re-run both the regression gate and the complete bounded inventory after registration.

entries.mistake: The first bounded C30M provider-deploy script inventory supplied youtubeProvider|functions:provider|firebase deploy as one fixed string, returning a false zero-match result.
entries.rootCause: Regex alternation syntax was combined with Select-String -SimpleMatch instead of passing three explicit fixed patterns.
entries.prevention: Repeat the already-bounded path inventory with a literal pattern array under -SimpleMatch, require nonzero owners, and use only the returned exact paths for subsequent reads.

entries.mistake: The first C30N reconciliation enumerated every untracked path, producing thousands of Windows long-path warnings and truncated output.
entries.rootCause: The dirty-tree check used --untracked-files=all instead of separating tracked changes from bounded top-level untracked-owner counts.
entries.prevention: Never enumerate the preserved untracked tree; read branch and HEAD as scalars, count tracked changes with --untracked-files=no, and count only top-level owners with --untracked-files=normal.

entries.mistake: C30N wrote the descriptive top-level MVP state ticket_disclosed_authority_pending without first resolving the gate-owned state vocabulary.
entries.rootCause: Authorization nuance was placed in a machine-state field whose accepted literals are owned by the gate.
entries.prevention: Read the exact gate transition literals before changing the top-level state and retain disclosure and authority nuance only in the ticket and nested authorization fields.

entries.mistake: The first C30N gate-source inspection requested one dense 75-line range and the output truncated before the exact state vocabulary could be admitted.
entries.rootCause: The source read was not split into context-sized exact non-overlapping windows.
entries.prevention: Read the rejected source range through smaller exact non-overlapping windows and confirm complete coverage before changing machine state.

entries.mistake: The resumed C30N audit guessed a nonexistent docs/quality/permanent-regression-memory.json path, causing the combined read to exit nonzero.
entries.rootCause: A generic memory filename was assumed instead of resolving the exact repository-owned files from AGENTS.md.
entries.prevention: Use config/codex-development-regression-registry.json and docs/quality/CODEX-DEVELOPMENT-REGRESSION-MEMORY.md exactly; never retry or substitute the guessed path.

entries.mistake: C30N requested a HEAD template for config/mvp-scope-gate-state.json even though that current local machine-state owner is not tracked at HEAD.
entries.rootCause: Historical ownership was assumed without first distinguishing the preserved untracked local state from Git-owned files.
entries.prevention: Reject the null summary, do not repeat Git history lookup for this owner, and correct the current local JSON only from exact gate-source vocabulary and validation.

entries.mistake: C30N invoked the delivery lock's active selection requirement after correctly moving the authority-pending MVP scope to its closed state with no active ticket ID.
entries.rootCause: An active-execution switch was treated as a general pending-scope integrity check despite its exact active-ticket ID invariant.
entries.prevention: Validate pending scope with the delivery lock without RequireTicketSelectionAssessment and the closed MVP scope gate; use the active selection switch only after exact authority creates a disclosed-and-authorized active ticket.

entries.mistake: The first C30N source cycle used Tee-Object -LiteralPath with -Append, which PowerShell rejected after only the copy gate had run.
entries.rootCause: The append switch was combined with the wrong Tee-Object path parameter set.
entries.prevention: Preserve the partial log, restart the entire cycle under a new filename, and use the resolved absolute path through Tee-Object -FilePath when appending subsequent gate output.

entries.mistake: The C30M endpoint negative-control suite used its historical default APK machine candidate while MVP scope was correctly active for C30N, so candidate mismatch masked the intended endpoint rejection.
entries.rootCause: The test control hard-bound a historical state path instead of accepting the exact active successor state as its variant source.
entries.prevention: Parameterize the control with an explicit machine-state path and generate every negative endpoint variant from the active C30N candidate; preserve and reject the partial cycle before restarting all gates.

entries.mistake: The successful C30N 168-test cycle forwarded Flutter compact reporter status through Tee-Object, causing the tool transcript to truncate despite complete durable logs.
entries.rootCause: The compact reporter's carriage-return progress was treated as bounded terminal output instead of being suppressed after evidence capture.
entries.prevention: Preserve but do not seal the truncated cycle; rerun every cycle under new filenames with Tee-Object output piped to Out-Null and return only immediate exit status, hashes and bounded log tails.

entries.mistake: The first C30N host summary treated an absent global java command as a fatal host failure despite the registered optional-runtime rule.
entries.rootCause: The combined audit called global java before resolving Flutter's configured Android toolchain runtime.
entries.prevention: Reject the combined summary, obtain Java ownership from Flutter doctor/configuration, invoke that exact binary, and do not mutate PATH or install a duplicate runtime.

entries.mistake: C30N prematurely described the first r60.40 semantic-height result as rejected even though its hierarchy showed Shop Home and its sequential screenshot showed a restored product-detail route.
entries.rootCause: Sequential UIAutomator and screenshot captures were treated as one stable frame without confirming route and semantic-state consistency during retained-state restoration.
entries.prevention: Preserve the mismatched pair, withdraw its disposition, capture two new no-tap hierarchy/screenshot pairs after settling, and decide C28D only from matching stable-state evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C30N Feed runtime diagnosis combined many gateway patterns and contexts, truncating the source output before error ownership could be established.
entries.rootCause: Credential, transport, response mapping and unrelated model code were requested in one diagnostic read.
entries.prevention: Reject the partial output and read separate exact small windows for credential acquisition, HTTP/error decoding and Feed exception-state mapping.

entries.mistake: The exact lookup for the rendered Feed error heading returned no source match.
entries.rootCause: The accessibility-rendered heading was assumed to be stored as one exact source literal.
entries.prevention: Treat the no-match as absent, retry with a shorter exact fragment already present in device evidence, and inspect only the returned literal owner path.

entries.mistake: A broad C30N Android logcat filter captured a complete Play Core integrity request line containing a one-time request nonce.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic included the integrity request-construction marker instead of limiting output to bounded completion, callback and redacted error markers.
entries.prevention: Never read or retain a complete Play Integrity request line; exclude nonce and request-payload fields, query only bounded completion/callback/error markers, and redact any request-like field before output or evidence retention.

entries.mistake: C30N consumed one profile build and one ADB install without first proving that the off-Play review distribution could satisfy the Dev Firebase App Check Play Integrity policy.
entries.rootCause: Package, signature and provider registration were qualified, but the intended installer channel was not bound to the exact App Check acceptance policy before the build/install authority was consumed.
entries.prevention: Before a successor build, qualify the intended distribution channel against the exact Dev App Check policy; use a Play-recognized internal-test artifact/install for a production-grade candidate, and require a successful signed-in live Feed read before any Create write.

entries.mistake: A read-only C30N evidence-summary command piped directly from a statement-form foreach block and failed at parse time with an empty-pipe-element error.
entries.rootCause: Statement-form loop output was not materialized before the formatter pipeline.
entries.prevention: Materialize loop output in an explicit @() collection or use pipeline-form ForEach-Object before formatting; reject parser-failed commands as no evidence.

entries.mistake: The August 12 release-sequencing audit repeated the statement-form foreach direct-pipe parser error already prohibited by REG-20260812-1479.
entries.rootCause: The active materialize-before-format memory rule was not applied while composing the bounded repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell collection loop is first assigned with $rows = @(foreach (...) { ... }); only the materialized variable may enter a formatter pipeline, and the regression-memory gate must pass before retry.

entries.mistake: The C30O Play Internal Testing and YouTube compliance reconciliation again placed a statement-form foreach block directly before a formatter pipeline and failed at PowerShell parse time.
entries.rootCause: The active materialize-before-format rule was acknowledged in durable memory but was not applied to the first bounded file-inventory command of the resumed task.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell collection loop is constructed as $rows = @(foreach (...) { ... }) before any formatter or selector pipeline; the regression-memory gate must pass for local, implementation, build and device phases before successor progression.

entries.mistake: The first C30O OPPO package-identity preflight invoked cmd package get-install-source, which is unsupported on the connected Android 13 command surface and returned exit 255.
entries.rootCause: A package-manager subcommand was assumed available without first binding installer-source discovery to the exact OPPO command surface.
entries.prevention: Use only a supported bounded installer owner such as dumpsys package installer metadata or one exact pm list packages -i row, capture its native exit immediately, and never infer Play recognition from an unsupported command or package identity alone.

entries.mistake: The Firebase Console account-menu audit used a fresh Chrome accessibility index whose control had no input geometry, and the Windows-control bridge rejected the click before dispatch.
entries.rootCause: A text-accessibility observation was treated as sufficient click geometry for this Chrome-rendered control.
entries.prevention: Discard the accessibility index, reacquire the exact Chrome window with a fresh screenshot-backed state, use at most one coordinate from that state, refresh immediately, and stop visibly for any password, MFA or authentication prompt.

entries.mistake: The one screenshot-backed coordinate click on the visible Firebase Google Account avatar produced no account menu, modal, focus change or navigation result.
entries.rootCause: The screenshot-backed coordinate did not resolve to an actionable account-menu control in the exact Chrome window state.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the avatar input or guess another signed-in account slot; proceed only through a separately verified account/window surface or a founder-visible account-switch checkpoint, with password and MFA interaction left to the founder.

entries.mistake: A read-only firebase help appcheck query assumed an App Check command family that the installed Firebase CLI reports as invalid.
entries.rootCause: The installed CLI command surface was not verified before treating it as a possible App Check inventory owner.
entries.prevention: Do not invent or retry Firebase CLI App Check commands; use only the supported Firebase Console or documented Firebase App Check management API after verifying the exact hello@moolsocial.com account context, without reading tokens or private verdicts.

entries.mistake: A C30O Dart symbol-inventory diagnostic placed a colon immediately after the interpolated PowerShell variable $name and failed at parse time before ripgrep ran.
entries.rootCause: The permanent delimited-variable rule was not applied while composing a bounded error message.
entries.prevention: Use the PowerShell format operator for diagnostic text or explicitly delimit every interpolated variable before punctuation; parser-failed inventories remain no evidence until the regression-memory gate passes and the corrected query completes.

entries.mistake: The first C30O privacy, deletion and revocation URL lookup combined known live web owners with the complete docs tree and returned 309 mixed historical and product matches.
entries.rootCause: An exact current public-page question was sent to an unnecessarily broad secondary documentation root.
entries.prevention: Read only the exact current privacy, disconnect, delete-account and youtube-api public owners one file at a time, or separately verify their live URLs; the broad result is never compliance evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C30O release-player audit combined four Android plugin owners in one read and the transcript truncated before release ownership could be established.
entries.rootCause: Multiple build and registrar owners were requested in one tool result instead of reading each exact release-sensitive file separately.
entries.prevention: Reject the combined output, pass the regression-memory gate, and read one exact player owner per command before deciding any release source-set or registrar correction.

entries.mistake: The first C30O release-player source-gate correction required one exact multi-line whitespace layout for the build-time feature flag and rejected the valid formatted Dart owner.
entries.rootCause: A semantic source assertion was implemented as a whitespace-sensitive multi-line substring.
entries.prevention: Assert bool.fromEnvironment and the exact feature-flag name as independent required tokens while retaining the separate kReleaseMode prohibition, then rerun the same gate only after regression memory passes.

entries.mistake: The first focused C30O player test cycle ran while youtube_embedded_player_android_test.dart still asserted the superseded debug/profile-only kReleaseMode boundary.
entries.rootCause: The exact release-boundary test owner was discovered but was not updated before the focused suite executed.
entries.prevention: Update the existing test to require build-flag control, release registrar registration and exact native player reuse while prohibiting kReleaseMode, then rerun the same focused files only after regression memory passes.

entries.mistake: The C30O signing-environment presence audit again piped directly from a statement-form foreach block and failed at parse time before reading any value.
entries.rootCause: The permanent materialize-before-format rule was not applied when a scalar version read and a small boolean presence table were composed together.
entries.prevention: Assign every statement-form loop to an explicit @() collection before formatting, return boolean presence only, and never read or print signing or Firebase environment values.

entries.mistake: A combined C30O command ran from apps/mobile but passed an apps/mobile-prefixed test path to dart format; the later successful Flutter test masked the formatter's path failure with an overall exit zero.
entries.rootCause: Repository-root paths were reused after changing the working directory and two native exits were not kept independent.
entries.prevention: Use mobile-relative paths from apps/mobile and execute formatting and tests separately so each native exit remains authoritative.

entries.mistake: The resumed C30O Windows preflight invoked title() on the saved Chrome window even though that object does not expose title as a function.
entries.rootCause: The saved computer-use object was reused without binding the query to the documented property or snapshot surface.
entries.prevention: Use the existing screenshot-backed state or documented window property/snapshot API, and dispatch no input until a fresh Play Console control is identified.

entries.mistake: The fresh C30O Chrome inspection passed a list-windows result directly to get_window_state instead of wrapping it in the documented options object.
entries.rootCause: The correct window identity was not adapted to the get-window-state argument shape.
entries.prevention: Call get_window_state({ window: exactWindow }), emit the fresh screenshot, and inspect it before any navigation or input.

entries.mistake: The minimized-window recovery called get_window({ window: existingWindow }), which is not the documented refresh argument shape.
entries.rootCause: The get-window-state and get-window methods were incorrectly assumed to share one options shape.
entries.prevention: Re-read the exact computer-use API owner and use only the documented get_window identifier arguments before any further UI method call.

entries.mistake: The C30O API refresh looked for api.md directly under the installed computer-use skill directory, but the referenced owner is not at that recalled path.
entries.rootCause: A previously read relative reference location was recalled from memory instead of rediscovered from the exact skill directory.
entries.prevention: Inventory only the exact installed computer-use skill directory and read the precise referenced API owner before another Windows-control call.

entries.mistake: The first C30O Gmail read requested the complete long-running compliance thread with full MIME payloads and the connector transcript truncated.
entries.rootCause: Historical messages and transport headers were retrieved when only the exact 2026-08-06 request and immediately preceding founder response were needed.
entries.prevention: Read only the exact shortlisted messages in the smallest representation that preserves essential headers and text body; never use the truncated full-thread result as evidence.

entries.mistake: The bounded C30O scripts filename search for source, aggregate or manifest returned no match and exit 1.
entries.rootCause: The historical manifest generation owner was assumed to be named after its output rather than discovered from the sealed C30N evidence.
entries.prevention: Search the exact C30N artifact or provenance owner for its manifest-generation command and do not broaden to the complete repository.

entries.mistake: The first C30O qualifier read LASTEXITCODE after a PowerShell gate script under strict mode, and the undefined native-process variable rejected cycle 1 before format, analysis or tests.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell script success was checked through the native-process exit variable instead of terminating-error propagation.
entries.prevention: Let PowerShell gate scripts propagate terminating errors directly, reserve LASTEXITCODE for explicit native dart and flutter calls, and restart cycle 1 under new durable log names.

entries.mistake: The complete C30O cycle retained a C30J source assertion requiring the Create-to-YouTube callback that C30O intentionally removes to keep MoolSocial Create distinct and upload unreachable.
entries.rootCause: The historical account-state source test encoded the previous Create entry point rather than the durable channel-status route owner.
entries.prevention: Update only the exact C30J assertion to require the account-status route while prohibiting the Create-to-YouTube binding, preserve the rejected logs, and restart the complete cycle under new filenames.

entries.mistake: C30O cycle 1r passed 193 Flutter tests and source gates but post-processed the compact carriage-return log with Get-Content -Tail, continued consuming CPU, missed its cycle JSON and outlived the 124-second tool timeout.
entries.rootCause: A compact reporter log was treated as a normal newline-delimited tail owner, repeating the known compact-output hazard in post-processing.
entries.prevention: Stop only the verified orphan qualifier process, replace tail extraction with one exact All tests passed match and boolean summary, preserve 1r logs, and restart cycle 1 as 1rr with a longer outer timeout.

entries.mistake: The C30O build-hold gate correctly rejected absent founder inputs, but its parent harness treated nested powershell nonzero exit as a catchable in-process exception and then incorrectly claimed the negative control passed unexpectedly.
entries.rootCause: Native-process exit semantics were confused with in-process PowerShell exception propagation.
entries.prevention: Capture nested PowerShell output and immediate LASTEXITCODE, require a nonzero exit and exact expected rejection text, and never use try/catch alone for a native-process negative control.

entries.mistake: The first Play Create app form input used set_value on Chrome edit controls whose cached UIA value/read-only property was unavailable, and the bridge rejected the attempt before submission.
entries.rootCause: The accessible edit indexes did not expose the property set required by set_value in the current Chrome form state.
entries.prevention: Refresh and inspect both fields, then for any unchanged field use one indexed click followed by Ctrl+A and type_text, refreshing after each field; never submit until every identity and declaration is visibly exact.

entries.mistake: One Play Create app call attempted five sequential category, pricing and declaration inputs spanning below the current viewport, and the first offscreen declaration click was rejected at y=906 against a height-798 window.
entries.rootCause: Accessibility indexes were treated as directly clickable without ensuring each control was visible in the current screenshot-backed viewport.
entries.prevention: Refresh selection state, handle visible radios separately, scroll once to declarations, reacquire indexes, click only visible controls, and submit only after a final full form audit.

entries.mistake: The fresh screenshot showed the programme-policy checkbox inside the lower viewport, but its accessibility-index click resolved to y=843 outside the height-798 window and was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Chrome UIA geometry for the lower declaration control did not match the screenshot-backed visible position.
entries.prevention: Refresh and verify pricing, use the fresh screenshot ID with one exact in-bounds checkbox coordinate, refresh immediately, and do not reuse the mismatched accessibility geometry.

entries.mistake: A fresh Play declaration state request attempted to emit screenshot images and the full accessibility payload in one result, and the outer transcript exceeded its context budget and truncated.
entries.rootCause: Visual and semantic evidence were combined even though only one bounded view was needed to place the next declaration input.
entries.prevention: Reuse the successfully refreshed state, emit only its screenshot or only narrowly filtered declaration lines in a single call, and never combine full accessibility output with images.

entries.mistake: The continuation attempted to read config/permanent-regression-memory.json, which does not exist, instead of the repository-owned codex development regression registry.
entries.rootCause: A generic remembered registry label was converted into a guessed filename instead of using the durable repository path from the existing gate owner.
entries.prevention: Use config/codex-development-regression-registry.json and its exact checker; never guess a permanent-memory filename.

entries.mistake: The fallback rg filename inventory matched repository-wide historical regression artifacts and produced a truncated 1009-line result when only the registry path was needed.
entries.rootCause: The fallback search used broad regression globs rather than the known config directory and checker reference.
entries.prevention: Restrict any registry discovery to config and scripts, cap output before execution, and use the now-confirmed exact registry path directly.

entries.mistake: A screenshot-coordinate click intended for the visible Play app signing declaration did not change its unchecked state.
entries.rootCause: The captured coordinate did not resolve to the checkbox hit target even though the square was visible, so the post-action screenshot remained unchecked.
entries.prevention: Treat the unchanged screenshot as authoritative, reacquire only the exact visible signing checkbox accessibility match, and click that refreshed element once before verifying again.

entries.mistake: The accessibility click on the non-visible Create app button completed without an API error but did not navigate or create the app container.
entries.rootCause: The accessibility element existed in the tree while its action target was not visibly rendered in the current bottom viewport, so the generated click landed outside the effective control.
entries.prevention: Keep the unchanged form as authoritative, use bounded keyboard focus inspection from the last visible declaration to reach the explicit Create app button, verify the focused element, and press Enter only on that exact focus.

entries.mistake: The export-checkbox focus maneuver attempted a click and compensating space toggle, but its follow-up state capture failed because the window crop was outside the captured monitor.
entries.rootCause: The Chrome window was not re-activated and rehydrated immediately before the screenshot-backed verification sequence after keyboard focus had moved to browser chrome.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the toggle sequence; rehydrate and activate the exact Chrome window, capture a fresh state, and visibly verify every declaration before any further form action.

entries.mistake: Rehydrating and activating the previously exact Chrome window id still produced an off-monitor crop capture failure.
entries.rootCause: The prior Chrome window binding was no longer sufficient after desktop focus and window state changed, even though get_window returned without error.
entries.prevention: List current windows without screenshots, select the live Chrome window whose title matches the Play form, activate that returned binding, and only then request a fresh screenshot.

entries.mistake: A bounded 25-Tab keyboard trace remained on Chrome's address bar for every step and did not reach any Play page control.
entries.rootCause: Keyboard events were sent while the Chrome window remained in the stale off-monitor/capture-failing state, so toolbar focus could not transition into page content.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat tab tracing; first use the exact window's system menu to maximize it onto the captured monitor, then acquire a visible fresh state before any page input.

entries.mistake: Alt+Space opened Chrome's system menu, but the following x keystroke did not activate Maximize and left the menu open while an adjacent Google Play information tab was active.
entries.rootCause: The single-letter system-menu accelerator was not accepted by the Windows/Chrome menu state in this environment.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the accelerator; close only the open system menu with Escape, return to the already-open Create app tab by its fresh screenshot coordinate, and continue with the now-visible window.

entries.mistake: After reducing the Play page to 90 percent zoom, the refreshed Create app accessibility action remained non-rendered and another click still produced no navigation or app container.
entries.rootCause: The repeated no-op after a material viewport change shows that geometry was not the complete cause and an unresolved form validation or account eligibility condition must be identified.
entries.prevention: Do not click Create app again until exact visible or accessibility error/required text and all field selection states are audited; correct only the disclosed condition and then perform one verified submission.

entries.mistake: The intentionally reversible export-checkbox click likely toggled the declaration off but did not establish page focus; accessibility still reported Chrome's address bar.
entries.rootCause: In this Chrome bridge state, indexed page clicks dispatch pointer input but the reported keyboard focus remains captured by browser chrome.
entries.prevention: Abandon checkbox-based focus routing, restore the export declaration with one direct refreshed click, verify it visibly, and use a different path to diagnose or invoke the enabled action.

entries.mistake: The fresh screenshot-coordinate click on Chrome's visible maximize button was rejected before dispatch because the foreground window did not report a process id.
entries.rootCause: The computer-use bridge could not validate foreground ownership for the title-bar input despite the Play window's saved binding.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat title-bar geometry attempts; preserve the visible form, continue with read-only account/form diagnosis, and use a founder-visible manual action only if the UI bridge remains unable to invoke the exact enabled control.

entries.mistake: A read-only screenshot-coordinate switch to the adjacent Google Play information tab was rejected before dispatch because the foreground window again lacked a process id.
entries.rootCause: The Chrome binding was being asked to activate and click in one operation while another desktop window held foreground ownership that the bridge could not validate.
entries.prevention: Perform exact Chrome activation as a separate operation, refresh its state, and only then issue one bounded read-only tab switch; do not combine activation recovery with the target input.

entries.mistake: A standalone activate_window call for the exact Chrome binding was rejected because the current foreground window did not report a process id.
entries.rootCause: The bridge's current desktop-ownership state prevents even the supported activation escape hatch, independent of the requested Play action.
entries.prevention: Stop UI retries while the ownership condition persists, continue independent local/read-only qualification, and resume only after Chrome is visibly foregrounded or the bridge reports a valid process owner.

entries.mistake: The Test and release sidebar click may have dispatched, but its combined follow-up screenshot failed because the window crop was outside the captured monitor.
entries.rootCause: Navigation input and screenshot verification were combined while desktop/window ownership remained sensitive to foreground changes.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the click blindly; run the permanent gate, refresh semantic state without a screenshot, determine whether Internal testing is already exposed, and only then capture or navigate once.

entries.mistake: The Internal testing Get started semantic click returned success but the page remained on the Test and release overview while Codex visibly occluded most Chrome content.
entries.rootCause: The indexed click was dispatched against an underlying page whose effective hit target was obscured by the foreground Codex window.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the occluded semantic click; ask the founder to foreground Chrome and click only the visible Internal testing Get started action, then refresh and verify the resulting title before any track mutation.

entries.mistake: After entering the tester-list name and refreshing semantic state, the email step reused the former edit index 775 and the bridge rejected it as unavailable before typing.
entries.rootCause: Dialog accessibility indexes were assumed stable across a value change and state refresh.
entries.prevention: Preserve the entered list name, reacquire the exact Add email addresses edit index from the current dialog state, type the founder email once, press Return, and verify the added row before saving.

entries.mistake: With the founder tester list fully populated, a fresh title-bar maximize click was again rejected before dispatch because the foreground window did not report a process id.
entries.rootCause: The bridge still cannot validate foreground ownership for Chrome title-bar input even though page-level inputs and captures work.
entries.prevention: Do not retry title-bar automation; preserve the populated unsaved dialog and ask the founder to click only Chrome's maximize square, then reacquire the dialog and invoke Save changes once visibly reachable.

entries.mistake: A screenshot refresh was attempted before the founder confirmed the requested maximize action and failed because the foreground window did not report a process id.
entries.rootCause: The task resumed UI inspection while the explicit founder desktop handoff was still outstanding.
entries.prevention: Do not poll the UI during a founder desktop handoff; wait for the founder's exact confirmation, then re-list the live Play window and acquire one fresh state.

entries.mistake: The selected computer-use skill was requested as one full raw shell output and the retained output was truncated before a complete read could be proven.
entries.rootCause: The instruction file was streamed as a single unbounded response instead of being read in bounded sequential line ranges through end of file.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat full raw output for the skill or its required references; determine line counts, read every line in bounded sequential chunks through EOF, and take no computer-use action until the complete read is confirmed.

entries.mistake: The refreshed Test and release accessibility control was invoked through the Windows bridge, but the combined input-and-refresh operation returned an unknown-outcome exception; a separate fresh observation proved the dashboard remained unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The Windows bridge did not expose a lower-level cause and could not verify dispatch of the semantic click; the unchanged page proves this specific invocation was non-operative.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat this semantic click; reacquire state and use a distinct bounded route to the authorized Internal-testing surface, then verify the resulting page title before any mutation.

entries.mistake: The previously observed app-scoped Internal-testing track URL was reused after the Play Console session returned to the dashboard, and Play Console rejected it with unexpected error 72E46BF7.
entries.rootCause: The saved opaque track route was treated as durable across the changed Console session without first re-resolving the current Internal-testing route from the live dashboard.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the saved opaque track URL; return through the live dashboard's exact Release your app early for internal testing without review task and verify the resulting page before any write.

entries.mistake: The exact View tasks for Release your app early for internal testing without review accessibility button was invoked through the same page-level semantic-click mechanism that had already failed in the current Chrome bridge state; a fresh observation proved the dashboard remained unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The same non-operative semantic-click mechanism was reused on a different dashboard control after the preceding Test and release semantic click had already disclosed the bridge limitation.
entries.prevention: Do not issue another page-level semantic click in this Chrome session; use a distinct keyboard-focus path from a fresh maximized observation, or pause for a single founder-visible click if keyboard focus cannot reach the exact Internal-testing task.

entries.mistake: With Chrome focus verified on the address bar, F6 and then Shift+F6 were tried as forward and reverse focus-transfer paths, but fresh observations remained on the same address bar after both inputs.
entries.rootCause: The current Chrome/Windows bridge does not move focus from browser chrome into the Play page using the normal F6 focus-cycle commands.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat F6, Shift+F6, page-level semantic clicks, or the rejected opaque track URL in this session; request one founder-visible click on only the exact Internal-testing dashboard task, then reacquire state.

entries.mistake: Four packaged browser diagnostics were launched with Promise.all, and the expected nonzero extension-installed status rejected the aggregate before the other results were retained.
entries.rootCause: Expected diagnostic exit statuses were treated as exceptional inside a fail-fast aggregate instead of being isolated per command.
entries.prevention: Do not rerun the conclusive extension check; execute any remaining diagnostics independently with per-command error isolation so one expected nonzero result cannot discard the others.

entries.mistake: On the correctly resolved Internal testing Testers page, the refreshed Create email list accessibility control was invoked through the known-unreliable semantic-click path; a separate observation proved the dialog did not open.
entries.rootCause: The current Chrome bridge's page-level semantic-click limitation persisted after navigation, but the same mechanism was tried once on the newly resolved control.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat this semantic click; use at most one fresh screenshot-bound coordinate action on the visibly rendered Create email list control, then stop for one exact founder click if that distinct path is non-operative.

entries.mistake: A screenshot-only observation for the Chrome target showed the Codex application visibly covering the Play page, so the rendered Create email list control was not safely available for coordinate input.
entries.rootCause: The Codex application regained foreground ownership after the founder returned control while the target Chrome page remained behind it.
entries.prevention: Do not use the occluded screenshot or its coordinates; raise only the selected Chrome target as a standalone action, refresh, and proceed only if the target is unobscured, while never automating the Codex app.

entries.mistake: After the founder opened the correct Create email list dialog, the refreshed List name edit control was invoked through the same Chrome semantic-click path; the operation returned unknown and focus remained on the address bar.
entries.rootCause: The modal was present in the accessibility tree, but Chrome foreground and focus ownership remained with browser chrome rather than the page surface.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the edit click while this focus state persists; activate only the selected Chrome window once, reacquire state, and retry only if Chrome is raised, otherwise request founder entry of the two approved non-secret values.

entries.mistake: After founder confirmation, Computer Use was asked to open a new Chrome tab for the official extension, but the safety layer stopped because it could not determine the current browser URL with sufficient confidence.
entries.rootCause: The Windows-control surface could not establish URL provenance for the target Chrome window at the point of navigation.
entries.prevention: Do not retry store navigation through Computer Use; after the founder's manual official-extension installation, resume only through the Browser skill Chrome connection and verify the existing Play tab before action.

entries.mistake: C30O machine state and evidence recorded Play app ID 474778280777295872, while the fresh authoritative signed-in Play tab URL identified app ID 4974778280277295872.
entries.rootCause: The opaque app ID was manually transcribed from the early Console session and lost digits instead of being qualified against the exact live app URL.
entries.prevention: Treat the current signed-in Play app URL and exact 19-digit path segment as authoritative; correct every bounded C30O occurrence and pass gates before further Play action, and never infer or abbreviate an opaque Play app ID.

entries.mistake: An exact-string rg search for the rejected and authoritative Play app IDs was run from the repository root without bounding large artifact and evidence surfaces, and timed out.
entries.rootCause: An otherwise narrow fixed-string query was applied to the full large dirty tree instead of the known C30O configuration, quality-document, and script surfaces.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the repository-root search; search only bounded config, docs/quality, and scripts text authorities with generated artifacts and build trees excluded.

entries.mistake: The fixed-string follow-up was limited to config, docs/quality, and scripts, but docs/quality remained large enough that the search still timed out after returning the exact live facts needing correction.
entries.rootCause: The prevention narrowed top-level folders but did not narrow to the already-known C30O live-authority filenames; folder-level scope was still excessive.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat folder-level app-ID searches; patch only the exact disclosed machine-state and two live evidence files, preserving historical regression text that records the rejected value.

entries.mistake: A single web request combined the official Domain Restricted Sharing page with two searches and requested a long response, causing the result to exceed retained context and be truncated.
entries.rootCause: The official-source lookup bundled too many overlapping retrieval operations instead of opening one primary Google Cloud page and one narrowly scoped official reference at a time.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the combined request; use only focused Google Cloud primary sources, one page or narrow query at a time with short or medium output, and never mutate organization policy from partial documentation.

entries.mistake: The mandatory Git reconciliation used unbounded git status --short --branch in a repository whose founder-owned dirty tree contains thousands of paths, and the output was truncated.
entries.rootCause: The required status command was run without routing its full output to an in-memory summary or applying the repository's existing large-dirty-tree output-bounding prevention.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat an unbounded status display in this tree; retain the command semantics while reporting only branch, counts, and a bounded sample, and preserve the entire dirty tree.

entries.mistake: Four read-only gcloud diagnostics were launched in one fail-fast aggregate; the disabled Organization Policy API caused an expected nonzero result to reject the aggregate and discard the other independent outputs.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostics repeated the registered pattern of treating an expected per-command diagnostic failure as exceptional inside Promise.all.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the Organization Policy API command or enable the API for diagnosis; run remaining project, account, and legacy-policy diagnostics independently with per-command error isolation.

entries.mistake: After opening the existing-project selector, a generic Close button locator matched both the nested project-list dialog and the parent Cloud-project link dialog, so strict mode rejected the click.
entries.rootCause: The close action was not scoped to the exact nested Existing Google Cloud dialog opened by the preceding action.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat an unscoped Close locator while nested dialogs are present; close the exact nested dialog first, then act on the parent only after a fresh snapshot proves one target.

entries.mistake: The Close button scoped to the Existing Google Cloud dialog returned without an exception, but a fresh snapshot still showed the same nested dialog open and active.
entries.rootCause: The Play Console nested project picker did not commit the scoped Close interaction even though the browser action completed without an API error.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the same Close interaction; use the already-open dialog's bounded search control with the exact Dev project number and require a fresh snapshot before treating any dialog action as effective.

entries.mistake: The exact Dev project-number search was scoped to the dialog name shown in the preceding snapshot, but the live accessibility tree no longer exposed that name and the textbox fill timed out with zero matches.
entries.rootCause: The locator treated a transient Play Console overlay label as stable across dialog transitions.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the stale parent-dialog locator; reacquire a fresh snapshot and, only if unique, target the exact search textbox without depending on a transient dialog label.

entries.mistake: After navigating to the exact Play Integrity settings URL, a heading readiness check called Browser locator waitFor with a timeout but without the required explicit state, so the API rejected the check.
entries.rootCause: The action assumed an implicit default wait state that this Browser wrapper does not provide.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the incomplete wait call; inspect URL and snapshot directly, and specify state visible explicitly if a later wait is necessary.

entries.mistake: The evidence-backed roles/browser prerequisite made MoolSocial Dev Trial visible and enabled Link project, but the authorized submission failed server-side asking that the Play account be made a project owner.
entries.rootCause: Project discovery permissions were incorrectly treated as the complete Play Integrity link authorization instead of being qualified against Play's server-side requirement.
entries.prevention: Do not retry with roles/browser alone and do not grant Cloud Owner blindly; qualify the current official requirement and prefer a Cloud-authorized identity in Play Console when it avoids an unnecessary broad grant.

entries.mistake: The read-only IAM verification for user:supermanditech@gmail.com timed out without returning policy data.
entries.rootCause: The Cloud IAM read stalled at the external CLI or service boundary, while project-dashboard visibility alone cannot distinguish Browser access from accepted Owner access.
entries.prevention: Do not treat dashboard visibility as Owner proof; retry only one narrower read-only IAM query with a bounded longer timeout, and do not retry Play until roles/owner is observed.

entries.mistake: A bounded repository keystore search returned no matches using ripgrep exit code 1, but the compound diagnostic failed because that expected result was not normalized.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic treated ripgrep's documented no-match result as an exceptional command failure.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the unhandled search; run the same bounded search once with exit 1 mapped to NO_MATCHES while preserving all other nonzero failures, and never broaden outside the workspace.

entries.mistake: The founder upload-key helper selected Android Studio keytool using Get-Item, then invoked the FileInfo through a nonexistent Source property and failed before keytool ran.
entries.rootCause: The helper used one variable for CommandInfo and FileInfo objects and assumed both exposed the executable path through Source.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the failed version; normalize discovery into one validated keytoolPath string, invoke only that string, and revalidate syntax, tool existence, and target absence before retry.

entries.mistake: The C30O founder release launcher allowed Windows PowerShell 5.1 to consume its one AAB build authority, then a benign Flutter Kotlin plugin warning on native stderr became a terminating NativeCommandError before an artifact was produced.
entries.rootCause: The new launcher and wrapper failed to enforce the already registered PowerShell 7 Android-build requirement before credential prompts and authority consumption, while the wrapper merged native stderr under ErrorActionPreference Stop.
entries.prevention: Never rerun C30O; every successor launcher and wrapper must fail closed on PowerShell major below 7 before prompts or machine-state mutation, and must capture native output without converting informational stderr into a terminating host error.

entries.mistake: Post-failure dirty-state reconciliation first produced no usable summary from scalar NUL-delimited status capture, then repeated full untracked enumeration alongside a broad search, causing truncation, long-path warnings and an invalid count of the aggregation wrapper.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic ignored the existing founder-owned large-dirty-tree bounding rule and failed to validate the selected numeric Measure-Object property before reporting it.
entries.prevention: Never enumerate the full untracked set or combine status with content search; read branch and HEAD separately, summarize bounded tracked and top-level untracked owners independently, and validate the exact numeric aggregation property.

entries.mistake: The first C30P MVP-state patch used a recalled C30O approvalState literal instead of the exact current dirty-file value, so apply_patch rejected the complete update.
entries.rootCause: A mutable machine-state checkpoint value was inferred from prior context rather than re-read from its exact current owner immediately before patching.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the broad patch; read the exact live ticket, authorization, checkpoint and selected-assessment windows and apply smaller context-verified updates without recalled mutable literals.

entries.mistake: The qualified C30P release AAB attempt compiled a generated Android registrant that referenced the dev-only integration_test plugin after release Gradle intentionally removed that plugin from the release classpath.
entries.rootCause: The prebuild gates did not exercise or statically reject a release registrant containing a dev_dependency plugin, so a debug/test-only Android registration escaped into release javac.
entries.prevention: Never rerun C30P, never add integration_test to the production release classpath and never hand-edit the ignored generated registrant; prove repository usage and correct only the unused dev dependency or its generation boundary under a new exact successor with release-specific static and source gates.

entries.mistake: A read-only Flutter SDK search included a recalled flutter_plugins_test.dart path that does not exist, causing ripgrep to exit nonzero despite matches in other owners.
entries.rootCause: The search owner was guessed from memory rather than enumerated from the installed SDK before content search.
entries.prevention: Enumerate exact matching SDK test filenames first, search only existing owners and normalize a legitimate no-match exit without treating partial matches as a complete audit.

entries.mistake: The C30Q wrapper gate demanded a direct releaseConfigExitCode assignment from LASTEXITCODE even though the wrapper correctly obtains the immediate native exit code through its bounded capture helper.
entries.rootCause: The static gate encoded an implementation detail that contradicted the selected helper abstraction instead of asserting the helper return and caller assignment independently.
entries.prevention: Require the helper to return immediate LASTEXITCODE and require releaseConfigExitCode to be assigned from Invoke-NativeCaptured; do not force a false direct-assignment literal.

entries.mistake: C30Q usage qualification piped enumerated filenames into ripgrep stdin, so it searched filename text instead of file contents and falsely reported no integration_test imports.
entries.rootCause: File enumeration and content search were composed through the pipeline without supplying the enumerated files or their bounded directory as ripgrep path arguments.
entries.prevention: Search the exact integration_test directory as ripgrep's path owner, normalize only no-match exit 1, and require at least one matching real import before continuing.

entries.mistake: C30Q carried --no-pub onto the release config-only workaround, so the installed Flutter bug continued suppressing platform-tooling regeneration and the stale IntegrationTestPlugin registration remained.
entries.rootCause: The subsequent AAB's dependency-sealing flag was incorrectly copied onto the distinct official config-only regeneration step whose purpose is to run the regeneration path gated by pub handling.
entries.prevention: Run release apk config-only without --no-pub, seal pubspec and lockfile hashes plus the APK sentinel before/after, require the release registrant to exclude IntegrationTestPlugin, and keep --no-pub only on the one AAB invocation.

entries.mistake: A successful zero-output release config-only command produced no Tee-Object pipeline items, so its expected evidence log was never created and the qualifier failed while hashing it after writing a partial manifest.
entries.rootCause: The native evidence helper assumed Tee-Object creates a file even when the upstream command emits zero objects.
entries.prevention: Precreate every native log as empty UTF-8 before invocation, preserve rejected logs and partial manifests, and use new retry filenames plus a distinct accepted manifest.

entries.mistake: The first independent C30Q post-build verifier invocation assumed a conventional PowerShell 7 executable path that is not present on this Microsoft Store installation, so the verifier did not run.
entries.rootCause: The executable owner was inferred from a common installation layout instead of resolved from the current machine before invocation.
entries.prevention: Resolve pwsh with Get-Command and invoke its exact Source; never infer a conventional PowerShell 7 installation path on this machine.

entries.mistake: A read-only attempt to locate the regression registry used a broad recursive content search across config, scripts and docs and timed out before returning a usable result.
entries.rootCause: Content search was used across an unnecessarily large owner set when bounded filename enumeration was sufficient.
entries.prevention: Enumerate bounded filenames with rg --files, filter expected registry or memory names and inspect only the exact selected owner.

entries.mistake: A read-only Play Console file-input inspection used instanceof HTMLElement inside the browser evaluation sandbox, where HTMLElement was not exposed as a constructor, so the inspection rejected.
entries.rootCause: The verifier depended on a page-realm DOM constructor instead of supported locator methods and direct attribute reads.
entries.prevention: Use supported locator methods and direct attribute reads for browser form inspection; do not depend on page-realm DOM constructors in the isolated evaluation sandbox.

entries.mistake: The first Play Console upload attempt waited for a chooser and clicked the visible Upload button, but the Chrome bridge did not surface a chooser within its effective window and the unhandled asynchronous timeout reset the browser session before file selection.
entries.rootCause: The chooser wait was not recovered inside the browser execution call, and the visible button path did not surface a file chooser within the bridge's effective timeout.
entries.prevention: Read and follow Chrome file-upload troubleshooting, handle chooser waits so timeout cannot escape unhandled, re-inspect visible state and verify that no upload occurred before using the supported recovery flow.

entries.mistake: A read-only full DOM snapshot of the reclaimed Play draft release page exceeded the browser-control execution window and reset the control session before returning state.
entries.rootCause: A full-page state read was requested while the Play release surface was unresponsive instead of starting with the cheapest bounded title, URL and targeted locator checks.
entries.prevention: Require Chrome extension file-URL access before retry, then inspect title and URL followed by targeted locator counts; do not begin recovery with a full-page DOM snapshot.

entries.mistake: A read-only required-reading inventory piped directly after a statement-form foreach closing brace, so PowerShell rejected it with an empty-pipe-element parser error.
entries.rootCause: The command did not assign foreach output to a bounded array before serialization.
entries.prevention: Assign foreach output to a named bounded array and serialize that array; never append a pipeline directly to a statement-form foreach closing brace.

entries.mistake: The first post-reconnect Play tab selector required both the exact app URL owner and a current title containing MoolSocial, so it rejected when no current tab metadata matched both predicates.
entries.rootCause: A mutable page title was promoted to a required identity predicate instead of supporting evidence after enumerating current tabs.
entries.prevention: Enumerate bounded current open-tab metadata, select by the exact Play developer/app URL owner and use mutable title only as supporting evidence.

entries.mistake: After identifying Play's hidden .aab file input, the upload recovery tried to force-click it, but Chrome's locator bridge still required a visible match and rejected before opening a chooser.
entries.rootCause: The implementation treated force-click as a supported bypass for an intentionally hidden file input instead of activating its visible Upload control.
entries.prevention: Do not force-click Play's hidden file input; arm a handled chooser wait and activate the visible Upload button after file-URL access is enabled, handling both click and chooser failures in-call.

entries.mistake: A read-only C30Q upload-state search passed an unexpanded docs/quality/UAW-C30Q* wildcard as a Windows path owner, so ripgrep returned a nonzero invalid-filename result after valid matches.
entries.rootCause: A Unix-style path-owner expansion assumption was used on Windows instead of bounded file enumeration or a ripgrep --glob filter.
entries.prevention: Enumerate matching evidence owners with rg --files and filter names, or search the exact directory with --glob; never pass an unexpanded wildcard as a Windows path owner.

entries.mistake: After the C30Q Internal Testing release became active, Chrome found the exact visible Testers tab but its page-control command timed out before the click completed.
entries.rootCause: The dynamic Play tab control did not complete a Chrome page-control click within the bridge window even though locator diagnostics proved it visible and enabled.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the stalled click; navigate once from the authoritative current track URL to its tab=testers form and verify the visible tester list and opt-in link there.

entries.mistake: The first OPPO Play-link attempt combined an Android intent write, wait, activity inspection and UIAutomator capture in one nested shell command, which local command policy rejected before execution.
entries.rootCause: A device mutation and its evidence reads were unnecessarily composed into one complex command boundary.
entries.prevention: Run the authorized Android intent as one minimal command and perform activity and visible-UI inspections in separate read-only commands.

entries.mistake: The separated minimal adb shell am start request for the authorized Internal Testing opt-in link was still rejected by local command policy before execution.
entries.rootCause: ADB intent navigation itself is unavailable through the current command policy, not merely the earlier combined orchestration.
entries.prevention: Do not retry ADB intent navigation; use Google Play web tester enrollment and Play-mediated device installation, bringing any password, MFA or device confirmation visibly to the founder.

entries.mistake: The first Add account interaction used a top-document role locator even though the current DOM proved the Google account switcher control was inside an active iframe.
entries.rootCause: The interaction did not preserve the iframe ownership shown by the immediately preceding DOM snapshot.
entries.prevention: Use a frame-scoped locator for the proven account-switcher iframe and stop at any password or MFA page for founder entry.

entries.mistake: The iframe-scoped locator found Google's exact visible Add account link, but the account-card overlay intercepted the semantic pointer event and the click rejected.
entries.rootCause: The dynamic account-card overlay retained the pointer hit target even though the underlying link was visible to the locator.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the intercepted click; navigate once to the exact visible AddSession URL exposed by the current DOM and stop at any password or MFA prompt for founder entry.

entries.mistake: After read-only verification of the attached tester email, the first dialog-close attempt inferred an exact accessible name close that the dynamic Play dialog did not expose, so the locator rejected.
entries.rootCause: An icon's visual text was treated as its exact accessible role name without inspecting current button labels.
entries.prevention: Do not retry an inferred icon label; leave the unchanged dialog and use a separate tab, or inspect exact current button labels before closing it.

entries.mistake: The first Windows-control click on Download test app returned an unknown input/refresh outcome; a fresh observation proved that the page had not navigated.
entries.rootCause: The Windows input or its immediate refresh failed without an authoritative action result even though the element was present in the prior accessibility observation.
entries.prevention: Discard the failed observation and indexes, re-observe and activate the current window, then use one fresh input; if semantic input fails again, stop and hand the visible click to the founder instead of looping.

entries.mistake: After registration and a fresh observation, the one permitted recovery click on Download test app again failed at the Windows-control input layer; a new observation proved no navigation.
entries.rootCause: The Supermandi Chrome page exposes the link to accessibility, but the current Windows-control input path cannot activate it reliably.
entries.prevention: Do not automate this link again through Windows control; hand the single visible link click to the founder and resume from the resulting Play listing with a new observation.

entries.mistake: C30Q prequalification allowed an in-place Google Play install flow without first comparing the preserved sideloaded r60.40 signer to the distinct Play App Signing certificate; readback proved r60.40 remained installed after the founder-reported install completion.
entries.rootCause: The distribution plan correctly qualified the upload and Play signing identities but omitted the predecessor-to-Play signing-lineage compatibility gate. The installed predecessor is Android-debug-signed, while Google Play distributes C30Q under a different Play-managed signing certificate.
entries.prevention: Before any in-place Play transition from a sideloaded predecessor, pull or otherwise verify the installed APK certificate and require equality or a qualified signing lineage with the Play App Signing certificate. A mismatch blocks the install flow before founder handoff; never retry, uninstall or clear data without a new exact founder decision and machine-authorized scope.

entries.mistake: The C30Q install-rejection seal changed the already pinned ticket state, so the MVP delivery discipline lock rejected the selected-ticket manifest hash before journey execution.
entries.rootCause: A runtime distribution outcome was incorrectly written into the immutable selected-ticket manifest instead of being confined to separate evidence and the mutable machine-result state.
entries.prevention: After a ticket assessment hash is pinned, preserve the ticket file byte-for-byte. Record build, upload, install and journey outcomes only in separate evidence and the designated mutable machine-result owner; restore the pinned ticket before any gate retry.

entries.mistake: Codex recommended a secondary Android user on the same OPPO as a non-destructive way to install the Play-signed C30Q package alongside the debug-signed predecessor.
entries.rootCause: Per-user app-data isolation was incorrectly generalized to APK and signing-identity isolation. Android manages package code and signing compatibility device-wide, so another user cannot install a differently signed APK for the same package while the predecessor remains installed.
entries.prevention: Never use secondary users, guests, work profiles or cloned-app features as a signer-mismatch workaround. Require a compatible signing lineage, complete package removal followed by Play installation, or a separate physical device with the package absent; keep removal and data loss explicitly founder-gated.

entries.mistake: The first C30R MVP scope-state transition attempted one large contextual patch, and an inexact expected exclusion string caused apply_patch to reject the entire patch before modification.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined many distant JSON edits and relied on a manually reconstructed context line instead of first reading and patching each exact bounded section.
entries.prevention: For large durable machine-state JSON transitions, patch small exact-context sections, parse JSON after each bounded group, recompute the pinned manifest hash and run delivery/MVP gates before any external action.

entries.mistake: The second C30R MVP scope-state patch repeated the context-mismatch failure because one exclusion line was reconstructed inaccurately instead of copied from the literal raw file.
entries.rootCause: The attempted recovery still used whole-object replacement and preserved the same manual-context risk that the first registration was meant to eliminate.
entries.prevention: Do not retry whole-object replacement. Patch only single properties or arrays with old text copied from bounded raw-file reads, parse after every group, and run manifest, delivery, scope and C30R gates before any external action.

entries.mistake: The C30Q release AAB passed source and static release checks but the Play-installed r60.43 app never rendered its first Flutter frame because Firebase initialization threw an uncaught missing-Crashlytics-build-ID PlatformException.
entries.rootCause: Release qualification proved Dart defines, package, signing and plugin registration but did not verify the release variant's generated Crashlytics build identifier or execute a release-mode Firebase initialization smoke test. The release packaging also omitted the expected google_app_id resource identity.
entries.prevention: Before any successor release build or upload, require a nonblank release Crashlytics build ID, verify the expected Firebase Android resource identity without exposing the API key, and pass a release-mode Firebase.initializeApp first-frame smoke test. Debug/profile startup and static plugin checks cannot substitute for this gate.

entries.mistake: A C30R ticket-exclusions array patch repeated the context mismatch because two raw underscore-delimited values were manually retyped with spaces.
entries.rootCause: The edit again attempted multi-line array context instead of enforcing the registered literal single-line replacement rule.
entries.prevention: For the remainder of this transition, do not patch array blocks. Replace only one exact raw line per patch, parse after every bounded set, and run regression, manifest, delivery, scope and ticket gates before runtime or external action.

entries.mistake: The first promised literal single-line C30R scope patch still retyped one underscore as a space and was rejected before modification.
entries.rootCause: The old line was not copied from a fresh bounded raw-file read before composing the patch.
