entries.prevention: Use rg -n to read each remaining exact raw line, copy it without reconstruction, replace it alone and parse before the next line.

entries.mistake: The C30R checker printed a journey-phase pass after validating only the Play-installed identity even though journeyResult was explicitly rejected before the first frame.
entries.rootCause: The postinstall identity assertions were reused for journey phase without an independent runtime-testing authorization assertion.
entries.prevention: Require the journey phase to assert an exact non-rejected runtime-testing authorization state in addition to installed identity. An install pass alone must never authorize device journeys.

entries.mistake: A combined C30R diagnosis ended with an optional rg filename filter that correctly found no Firebase config file but returned exit code 1, making the whole useful read appear failed.
entries.rootCause: An optional zero-match search was left as the final status owner of a multi-finding command instead of being normalized to an explicit boolean.
entries.prevention: Run optional inventories separately and print an explicit boolean for expected no-match results; never let optional rg status own a combined diagnostic command exit code.

entries.mistake: The C30S preflight attempted to hash a full untracked git-status inventory; Git still traversed retained browser-profile evidence with overlong paths and flooded stderr, truncating the otherwise bounded command output.
entries.rootCause: The command bounded stdout after traversal but did not apply the existing long-path-safe retained-evidence exclusion strategy before asking Git to enumerate every untracked descendant.
entries.prevention: Treat the already captured 55,211-entry status hash as the C30S ownership snapshot. Do not repeat full untracked enumeration. Use path-bounded status and exact-file fingerprints for C30S-owned files, while preserving every pre-existing tracked and untracked path.

entries.mistake: The first C30S registration patch assumed expanded multi-line arrays for the compact registry tail and apply_patch rejected it before modification.
entries.rootCause: The registry tail was inferred from deserialized output rather than copied from a fresh literal raw-file read.
entries.prevention: Read the literal registry tail before each append and patch only its final evidence line and closing object. Keep existing compact formatting intact and parse the complete JSON immediately afterward.

entries.mistake: The first C30S comprehensive-audit scope patch left the checker build-phase hunk under the JSON state-file update header, so apply_patch rejected the atomic patch before modification.
entries.rootCause: Several file edits were composed in one patch without a separate update header immediately before the checker hunk.
entries.prevention: Apply the audit expansion one exact file at a time: ticket, state, checker, then findings. Parse JSON and run PowerShell syntax checks after the corresponding file changes before continuing.

entries.mistake: The first C30S MVP scope-state transition repeated the known context rejection by reconstructing inherited C30R exclusion strings with incorrect underscore and space separators.
entries.rootCause: A multi-property patch was composed from displayed prose instead of literal raw lines even though REG-1581 and REG-1582 require single-line replacements copied from a fresh read.
entries.prevention: For the C30S scope transition, use rg -n to read every exact target line and apply one literal single-line replacement per patch. Do not patch array blocks or reconstruct their contents. Parse the JSON after every bounded group.

entries.mistake: A context-free single-line replacement for implementationDisposition matched the first identical line and changed the historical C30K assessment instead of the active C30S assessment.
entries.rootCause: The single-line rule was applied without a unique neighboring anchor even though the target property occurs in four assessment objects.
entries.prevention: Single-line replacements must include a unique adjacent ticketId, manifest hash or object-specific line whenever the raw target text is duplicated. Immediately verify the exact line number after every ambiguous property edit and restore historical assessments before continuing.

entries.mistake: The bounded C30S single-line transition stopped when the expected exclusion used 'no_build upload' but the literal file contains 'no_build_upload'.
entries.rootCause: The target value was copied from a visually wrapped earlier output instead of the latest exact rg line, repeating the separator error despite the single-line strategy.
entries.prevention: Use the latest rg output as the only source for each remaining line, including every underscore. Stop on the first rejection, preserve already parsed changes, register it, then resume only from a new exact read.

entries.mistake: The next bounded C30S ticket transition stopped when the expected exclusion used a space after no_new_build but the literal value is no_new_build_upload.
entries.rootCause: The inherited value was again transcribed from formatted output rather than copied from the immediately preceding exact rg result.
entries.prevention: Copy every remaining raw value directly from a fresh rg line, including contiguous underscore-delimited tokens. Do not infer separators from prose or earlier rendered blocks.

entries.mistake: The first C30S unused-plugin source inventory piped a foreach statement directly to ConvertTo-Json without grouping, producing an empty-pipe parser rejection before execution.
entries.rootCause: The PowerShell command composed loop output and pipeline syntax in one inline expression instead of assigning an explicit result array.
entries.prevention: Assign inventory rows to an explicit array, normalize each optional ripgrep zero-match to an empty array, then serialize the completed array. Parse the command structure before execution.

entries.mistake: The first C30S releaseRuntimeClasspath dependency audit failed during Gradle configuration and emitted an unsupported Kotlin plugin warning before dependency proof could complete.
entries.rootCause: The release signing guard used a broad case-insensitive substring check across Gradle start-parameter task names, so the read-only releaseRuntimeClasspath configuration name was misclassified as an artifact-packaging task.
entries.prevention: Require signing only for exact release packaging/install/signing task families. Keep release dependency reporting executable without secrets, allow only Flutter 3.44's documented AGP 9 legacy-KGP warning, and block AAB authority until the dependency audit exits zero without forbidden unused Firebase SDKs.

entries.mistake: After the signing-guard correction, the second releaseRuntimeClasspath audit still exited one before dependency resolution and exposed an AGP 9 legacy android-DSL deprecation warning.
entries.rootCause: AGP 9 disables custom resValue generation unless buildFeatures.resValues is explicitly enabled; the new non-secret Firebase resource identities therefore failed project configuration.
entries.prevention: Enable only buildFeatures.resValues, statically pin the three exact non-secret Firebase resources, and explicitly classify only Flutter 3.44's documented legacy-KGP and legacy-DSL warnings. Dependency resolution must exit zero before source qualification.

entries.mistake: The first successful Gradle dependency resolution was correctly rejected by the stricter C30S audit because one forbidden-name line remained and AGP 9 deprecations included four repository-owned YouTube plugin lines plus upstream compatibility warnings.
entries.rootCause: The forbidden matcher used the broad firebase-config substring and falsely matched required firebase-config-interop; the repository-owned YouTube plugin also used deprecated srcDirs APIs. Remaining Kotlin/legacy-DSL warnings are upstream Flutter 3.44 AGP 9 compatibility output.
entries.prevention: Match exact forbidden Maven artifacts rather than substrings, keep firebase-config-interop allowed, use non-deprecated repository-owned Gradle APIs, and require the shared release resource-link preflight with --warning-mode=fail before every APK/AAB build. Current upstream or third-party deprecations must be removed through dependency upgrades or overrides before packaging; never patch machine caches or silently allowlist a future-failing warning.

entries.mistake: The first repository-owned srcDirs migration called MutableSet.addAll with two string arguments instead of one collection.
entries.rootCause: The deprecated vararg srcDirs call shape was transferred directly to the collection-based directories API without adapting its signature.
entries.prevention: Use java.directories.addAll(listOf(...)) for multiple source directories and run Gradle configuration before accepting the migration. Register pre-test API-shape defects as soon as they are noticed.

entries.mistake: A parallel read-only C30S audit batch treated ripgrep's expected no-match exit code as a tool failure, so the batch rejected before returning the other independent results.
entries.rootCause: One absence-proof search intentionally had no matches but its exit code was not normalized before Promise.all combined it with other read-only commands.
entries.prevention: For absence-proof ripgrep checks, explicitly accept exit codes zero and one, reject only greater values, and return a structured empty result. Keep independent audit outputs available even when one check rejects.

entries.mistake: The first read-only Gradle properties filter nested a PowerShell command inside a double-quoted outer PowerShell command, so the outer shell consumed the scriptblock variable and the filter reported that .Line was not a command.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic unnecessarily launched a second PowerShell parser and failed to preserve the inner $_ token across quoting layers.
entries.prevention: Invoke Gradle directly from the existing PowerShell host and parse returned output in the same shell. Avoid nested PowerShell command strings for structured filters.

entries.mistake: The first combined release manifest and Gradle task audit exited one because the Crashlytics plugin could not create uploadCrashlyticsMappingFileRelease.
entries.rootCause: Crashlytics Gradle plugin 3.0.7 requires Google Services Gradle plugin 4.4.1 or newer. The app had only manual resource values, so Crashlytics AppIdFetcher rejected task creation with Google-Services plugin not found.
entries.prevention: Apply the official Google Services 4.5.0 and Crashlytics 3.0.7 plugin pair, disable mapping upload only for the un-obfuscated release variant, and require processReleaseGoogleServices plus injectCrashlyticsMappingFileIdRelease task registration before qualification. Supply the founder-controlled configuration only transiently during the single build.

entries.mistake: The first artifact resource-dump probe attempted to execute Gradle's cached bundletool library artifact with java -jar and exited one before reading the existing predecessor AAB.
entries.rootCause: The cached Maven artifact is not guaranteed to be a standalone executable JAR with its runtime dependencies and entrypoint packaged for java -jar use.
entries.prevention: Qualify a standalone bundletool executable before postbuild use or use Android's supported compiled-resource inspection path. Test the inspector against the preserved predecessor without exposing unrelated resources, and pin its identity in provenance.

entries.mistake: A read-only test inventory command embedded a regex literal as an invalid PowerShell .Split method argument and rejected during parsing before execution.
entries.rootCause: JavaScript/regex-style delimiter syntax was used inside a PowerShell method call instead of System.IO path handling.
entries.prevention: Use repository-relative path normalization plus the platform DirectorySeparatorChar, or a PowerShell -split expression, and parse commands before execution. The qualifier enumerates exact Dart test files without ad hoc grouping syntax.

entries.mistake: Release manifest processing was invoked after the official Google Services plugin was applied but before its founder-controlled transient configuration existed, so the task exited one and the previous merged manifest remained stale.
entries.rootCause: processReleaseMainManifest participates in the configured release graph and cannot be accepted as current evidence when the required Google Services input is absent. The old output predated the C30S dependency cleanup.
entries.prevention: Before founder input, prove only fail-closed task registration and source/static contracts. During the single founder launcher, create the transient release google-services.json, run release config processing, assert fresh output and delete the file afterward. Never accept a merged manifest whose task exited nonzero or whose timestamp/hash was not sealed in the current attempt.

entries.mistake: The first C30S readiness run invoked regression memory while earlier registered C30S entries already referenced the planned qualifier path, but that qualifier file had not yet been created.
entries.rootCause: Regression prevention paths were registered before the concrete gate owner existed, temporarily making the global memory gate fail closed.
entries.prevention: Create every referenced gate owner in the same patch as its first registry reference, or order implementation so the gate exists before invoking global regression memory. The missing C30S qualifier is created before this check is retried.

entries.mistake: The first complete C30S static-readiness execution exited nonzero but the shell integration returned no exception text, leaving the failed assertion unidentified from that invocation.
entries.rootCause: The direct pwsh process relied on default error-stream propagation instead of wrapping the gate with an explicit exception-to-output envelope.
entries.prevention: During gate development, wrap the top-level invocation in try/catch that returns only exception type and message while preserving a nonzero exit. Once stable, the permanent qualifier captures every gate stream to evidence logs.

entries.mistake: The static readiness gate invoked the Android Gradle wrapper by absolute path while remaining at the repository root, so release task registration exited one despite passing from the Android project directory.
entries.rootCause: Gradle wrapper location and Gradle project working directory were incorrectly treated as interchangeable.
entries.prevention: Push the Android project directory before invoking gradlew and restore location in finally. Require exit zero plus the exact Google Services and Crashlytics release task names.

entries.mistake: The first C30S wrapper self-audit rejected because the build wrapper ran release manifest preflight but did not explicitly assert that its log contained the Crashlytics build-ID and Google Services tasks.
entries.rootCause: Task registration was proved by the static gate, but execution proof was initially inferred from Gradle success instead of being independently pinned in the manifest-preflight log.
entries.prevention: After successful release manifest preflight, require the log to name processReleaseGoogleServices and injectCrashlyticsMappingFileIdRelease before consuming AAB authority. Keep postbuild compiled-resource proof as a separate final gate.

entries.mistake: The wrapper self-audit rejected because bundletool path and SHA-256 were machine-state pinned, but the wrapper did not independently require the exact standalone filename.
entries.rootCause: Inspector identity relied on state data and hash comparison without a second code-level filename invariant.
entries.prevention: Require the resolved inspector leaf to equal bundletool-all-1.18.3.jar and its SHA-256 to equal the pinned state value before preflight or artifact inspection.

entries.mistake: The first C30S cycle-1 invocation set a one-second shell timeout expecting a yielded process, so the shell terminated qualification instead of returning a persistent cell.
entries.rootCause: The shell tool timeout was confused with the orchestration yield interval. This tool terminates at timeout rather than automatically returning a resumable cell for ordinary shell commands.
entries.prevention: Launch long qualification through Start-Process with hidden window and explicit stdout, stderr, exit-code and PID evidence files, then poll those files at intervals under 60 seconds. Preserve terminated-attempt logs and never count them as a successful cycle.

entries.mistake: A read-only qualification process snapshot requested dart, flutter and pwsh together; it returned the active dart/pwsh rows but exited one because no process named flutter existed.
entries.rootCause: Get-Process reports a non-terminating not-found error for any absent requested name, and the combined invocation did not normalize expected absence.
entries.prevention: Enumerate the process table once and filter names in memory, or query each optional process with ErrorAction SilentlyContinue and explicitly return success. Never treat an absent optional process as qualification failure.

entries.mistake: The first complete C30S cycle stopped at flutter analyze because main.dart imported dart:ui even though Flutter foundation already provided every used element, including PlatformDispatcher.
entries.rootCause: The Crashlytics asynchronous-error handler added an explicit SDK import without checking Flutter foundation's exports under the pinned Flutter 3.44 toolchain.
entries.prevention: Use PlatformDispatcher through the existing Flutter foundation import and require clean full-project flutter analyze in both qualification cycles before any AAB authority is consumed.

entries.mistake: After the failed cycle's analysis phase, readiness found 16 registered Android plugins because Flutter had regenerated IntegrationTestPlugin into the dev registrant; the initial C30S qualifier omitted the known post-test release config-only restoration.
entries.rootCause: The C30Q permanent regression was understood but not carried into C30S's new comprehensive qualifier implementation before the first cycle attempt.
entries.prevention: After every analyze/test phase, run flutter build apk --release --config-only with r60.44 identity, prove pubspec/lock and APK/AAB sentinels unchanged, and require the exact 15-plugin registrant with IntegrationTestPlugin absent before repository gates and source sealing.

entries.mistake: The first comprehensive C30S test attempt ran every test owner in the large dirty repository and finished with 1254 passes, 36 skips and 323 failures across pre-existing frozen golden/design areas unrelated to Firebase startup recovery.
entries.rootCause: Repository-wide coverage was substituted for bounded complete affected coverage despite C30S explicitly freezing broad Shop, Care, Work and global redesign owners. The current dirty baseline does not claim every unrelated historical test is green.
entries.prevention: Preserve the full-suite rejection as baseline evidence, do not modify frozen product owners, and construct a deterministic affected-test manifest from every C30Q-owned test plus all Social, YouTube, Firebase/App Check/Auth, startup, platform, session, retained-state, offline/retry and Android adapter tests. Require that exact manifest to pass twice and seal its hash.

entries.mistake: The first combined affected-suite qualifier and findings patch was atomically rejected because a documentation context phrase wrapped differently from the patch hunk.
entries.rootCause: A long multi-file patch used an approximate prose anchor instead of the exact existing tail lines.
entries.prevention: Verify exact anchors immediately before patching and separate executable and prose changes when their contexts are independent. Confirm atomic rejection left all target files unchanged before retry.

entries.mistake: The first affected-suite implementation would have copied the fixed accepted test manifest before the cycle-1 test command passed.
entries.rootCause: Manifest identity construction and manifest acceptance were combined before the test result boundary.
entries.prevention: Before testing, calculate and log the candidate manifest only. For cycle 1, write the fixed accepted manifest only after tests, release config, dependencies, repository gates, artifact sentinels and source fingerprint all pass. For cycle 2, require the existing accepted hash before execution and never overwrite it.

entries.mistake: The first 52-file affected suite found platform_configuration_test still expected releaseTaskRequested even though C30S intentionally narrowed the production guard to releasePackagingTaskRequested.
entries.rootCause: The focused signing implementation was strengthened but its source-contract test was not updated in the same patch.
entries.prevention: Assert the exact releasePackagingTaskRequested guard, the bounded packaging-task regex and founder environment names. Require the affected suite to pass twice.

entries.mistake: The first 52-file affected suite found the Android private-Dev adapter source gate observed registerViewFactory where the release registrar must remain a no-op.
entries.rootCause: The test still encoded the obsolete pre-review rule that profile/release registrars were no-ops and Dart required kDebugMode. Current founder-authorized reviewer scope explicitly requires official embedded playback in the Play release, while the build flag remains disabled by default.
entries.prevention: Require debug, profile and release registrars to use the same closed PlatformView factory, keep the feature flag default false, require the C30S build define to enable it, preserve the Android-only and forbidden-JavaScript bridge checks, and run both the focused test and Android player gate twice.

entries.mistake: A follow-up source diagnostic searched only the plugin main Kotlin directory for debug-only view-registration symbols and returned the expected no-match exit code as a failed tool call.
entries.rootCause: The absence search did not normalize ripgrep exit one and did not include the variant registrar directories needed for comparison.
entries.prevention: Read the three exact registrar files and source-set mapping directly; for future absence searches, accept ripgrep exits zero and one and reject only execution errors.

entries.mistake: The corrected YouTube adapter source-contract test was patched without running Dart formatting before the next full cycle, so format rejected one file.
entries.rootCause: The focused tests were executed immediately after the semantic patch, but formatting was deferred to the cycle instead of being a local post-edit check.
entries.prevention: Run dart format on every edited Dart file immediately after the patch, then require non-mutating format checks in both full cycles.

entries.mistake: The qualifier passed packages/youtube_embedded_player_private_dev/test to dart format even though that package has no test directory, contributing to a nonzero format phase.
entries.rootCause: The format path list assumed every local package has both lib and test owners without checking the actual bounded inventory.
entries.prevention: Format only existing lib, test and integration owners. Inventory local package paths before encoding them and require all path arguments to exist.

entries.mistake: The first follow-up lookup for the Data Connect dependency rejection guessed an incorrect generated attempt timestamp and Select-String could not find that log.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic reconstructed a path manually instead of selecting the newest exact cycle attempt directory from the preserved evidence tree.
entries.prevention: Resolve the attempt directory from the actual file inventory sorted by LastWriteTime and verify the target exists before reading it. Never infer generated timestamps.

entries.mistake: The otherwise successful release dependency audit rejected because it required a Maven artifact named firebase-dataconnect, which the Flutter Data Connect package does not add to the Android runtime graph.
entries.rootCause: A direct Dart dependency name was incorrectly assumed to map one-to-one to a native Maven artifact family.
entries.prevention: Prove firebase_data_connect as a direct pubspec/lock dependency and through its affected Flutter tests, while requiring only the Android-native App Check, Auth, Common and Crashlytics families in releaseRuntimeClasspath. Keep exact forbidden unused native SDK assertions.

entries.mistake: A second diagnostic again typed an approximate generated qualification-attempt timestamp for repository-gates.log after REG-1620 had already required resolving actual directories.
entries.rootCause: The command combined a direct script read with a manually typed log path instead of first resolving and storing the newest attempt directory.
entries.prevention: Never type qualification-attempt timestamps. Resolve the directory with Get-ChildItem sorted by LastWriteTime, verify the exact log exists, and then read it in a separate operation.

entries.mistake: The otherwise passing cycle reached the legacy protected Social baseline gate, which expected 178 files but the founder-owned current dirty tree contains 201 and requires a separately approved baseline replacement.
entries.rootCause: C30S added a global founder-baseline seal to its new qualifier even though the authorized successor cannot rewrite that historical C25F baseline and the current C30Q accepted source already postdates it.
entries.prevention: Do not mutate or replace the founder-approved C25F baseline inside C30S. Preserve the rejection evidence, require the accepted C30Q source baseline, exact C30S source fingerprint, 52-file affected suite, Android player gate and action projection twice. Any future global baseline replacement needs separate founder authority.

entries.mistake: The C30S state checker passed BuildMode release to the permanent regression-memory gate after both qualifying cycles, but that gate accepts only none, debug or profile and therefore rejected the otherwise complete qualification.
entries.rootCause: The new release-AAB checker invented an unsupported regression-memory BuildMode value instead of preserving the established exact enum. The release identity already belongs to the C30S state contract and does not require expanding the global enum.
entries.prevention: For C30S release phases, call regression memory in implementation mode with BuildMode none, then let the exact C30S state checker, wrapper, signing and AAB artifact gates enforce release semantics. Preserve failed cycle evidence and require a new immutable evidence generation with two identical cycles after this correction.

entries.mistake: The founder launcher validated the google-services.json leaf path but attempted to write it without first proving or creating the exact release source-set parent directory, so it rejected after secret entry but before wrapper invocation.
entries.rootCause: The launcher treated a missing transient leaf as sufficient write readiness and did not model the parent-directory lifecycle for a release-only source set that had never existed in the repository.
entries.prevention: Before founder prompts, validate every transient output parent against its exact bounded root, require the private signing parent to exist, create only the exact Android release source-set directory when absent, and prove every transient leaf is absent. Keep finally cleanup and rerun two immutable identical qualification cycles after launcher changes.

entries.mistake: The fresh release-manifest preflight rejected READ_GSERVICES as an unexpected unused permission even though manifest-merger blame proves it is contributed by the retained com.google.android.recaptcha:recaptcha:18.7.1 runtime dependency used by Firebase Authentication.
entries.rootCause: The initial merged-manifest denylist grouped a retained Firebase Auth reCAPTCHA permission with permissions from removed messaging, notification and advertising SDKs without dependency-level provenance classification.
entries.prevention: Keep notification, messaging and advertising permissions forbidden. Require READ_GSERVICES exactly once, require fresh manifest-merger blame to attribute it to com.google.android.recaptcha:recaptcha:18.7.1, seal that blame evidence, and rerun both immutable complete qualification cycles before build. Any dependency-origin change must fail closed for reclassification.

entries.mistake: The wrapper self-gate required an unescaped com.google.android prefix followed by an escaped version, while the implementation correctly encoded the entire artifact coordinate inside a regex, so the self-gate rejected the present provenance guard.
entries.rootCause: The static substring assertion duplicated a partial representation of the runtime regex instead of selecting a stable literal fragment shared by the checked implementation.
entries.prevention: Assert the stable exact literal fragment recaptcha:18\.7\.1 together with the independent READ_GSERVICES and merger-blame markers. Parse both scripts before qualification and preserve the runtime manifest/blame proof as the authoritative semantic gate.

entries.mistake: A launcher attempt received a Firebase value that did not match the full Android API-key shape, then an earlier terminal transcript was pasted into the returned PowerShell prompt and interpreted as commands.
entries.rootCause: The launcher named the credential but did not state its non-secret identifying shape or keep the founder inside a bounded re-prompt loop after a shape error, leaving the normal shell prompt exposed to accidental transcript paste.
entries.prevention: Before the secure prompt, identify the correct console row as Android key (auto created by Firebase), state that the full value is 39 characters beginning AIza, warn to paste only that value, and allow at most three hidden shape-validation attempts before rejection. Never echo or persist the value and keep authority untouched until all preflights pass.

entries.mistake: After a fail-closed manifest rejection preserved its config and manifest logs, the next qualified launcher run rejected immediately because the wrapper used the same fixed preflight evidence filenames and correctly refused to overwrite them.
entries.rootCause: The single-AAB model distinguished build authority from preflight, but its evidence model allocated only one filename set for potentially multiple non-consuming preflight attempts.
entries.prevention: Keep the final sealed AAB path unique and fixed, but select the first unused bounded immutable preflight-attempt suffix across every log, prebuild state, merged manifest, merger blame and provenance output. Preserve all prior attempts, cap selection fail-closed, record the chosen attempt in provenance, and never consume build authority until the selected preflight succeeds.

entries.mistake: The fresh merged-manifest gate required exactly two app-owned exported activities and rejected four additional exported components contributed by retained Firebase Auth, Google Play services Auth and AndroidX ProfileInstaller dependencies.
entries.rootCause: The initial attack-surface assertion counted dependency-owned components but did not classify their exact functions, protecting permissions and merger-blame origins before deciding whether they were legitimate.
entries.prevention: Require an exact six-component release surface: two app-owned activities, two Firebase Auth callback activities, the permission-protected Google Sign-In revocation service, and the DUMP-protected ProfileInstaller receiver. Prove exact node types, permissions, relevant callback actions and merger-blame artifact versions; reject any addition, removal, permission change or origin drift.

entries.mistake: A read-only exported-component detail diagnostic piped directly after a foreach block with a malformed closing expression and PowerShell rejected it before execution.
entries.rootCause: The one-line command combined nested XML projections, a foreach statement and a terminal pipeline without first materializing the result array.
entries.prevention: For structured PowerShell diagnostics, assign foreach results to a named array, end the statement, and format the array separately. Parse complex diagnostic scriptblocks before execution when practical.

entries.mistake: The single authorized r60.44 AAB completed and was sealed, but post-build verification aborted because a PowerShell command bound LiteralPath more than once.
entries.rootCause: The post-build verifier reached an unexercised command-shape defect after the artifact build; static token-presence gates did not execute the offline verifier against an existing AAB before authority consumption.
entries.prevention: Locate the exact duplicate parameter with AST inspection, correct it, and add a build-forbidden post-build recovery verifier that accepts only the already sealed r60.44 AAB. It must prove signer, package/version, Google app ID, Crashlytics build ID, base/arm64 payload, sealed manifest/blame evidence, credential-free logs and original accepted source fingerprint without invoking Flutter or Gradle. Upload remains blocked until this existing artifact passes.

entries.mistake: The first AST diagnostic for the post-build parameter-binding failure again piped directly after a structured foreach block and failed to parse, recurring after REG-1631.
entries.rootCause: The command repeated the same compact one-line construction instead of materializing its result array as required by the newly registered prevention rule.
entries.prevention: Never append a pipeline directly to a complex foreach diagnostic. Assign the full result to a named array, terminate the statement, then format the array separately; parse the diagnostic scriptblock before running it.

entries.mistake: The build-forbidden offline verifier passed signer, package, version and Google app ID proofs but rejected the sealed AAB because its exact Crashlytics build-ID resource proof did not pass.
entries.rootCause: The verifier queried the nonexistent legacy-style name com_crashlytics_build_id. Exact AAB inventory proves the Crashlytics Gradle plugin generated the modern string/com.google.firebase.crashlytics.mapping_file_id and version_control_info resources.
entries.prevention: Inspect bundletool output using non-secret structural booleans and exact resource inventory, compare it with generated release resources and Crashlytics task outputs, and never waive or synthesize the resource after build. If it is absent, reject the single AAB and require separate founder authority for any successor; if proof syntax is wrong, correct only the build-forbidden verifier and rerun against the identical sealed hash.

entries.mistake: C30S preflight recognized the injectCrashlyticsMappingFileIdRelease task but its post-build verifier queried string/com_crashlytics_build_id instead of the resource actually generated by Crashlytics Gradle plugin 3.0.7.
entries.rootCause: The resource-name assertion was inferred from a runtime error phrase rather than derived from the exact generated resource inventory. The actual AAB contains string/com.google.firebase.crashlytics.mapping_file_id and string/com.google.firebase.crashlytics.version_control_info.
entries.prevention: For Crashlytics Gradle plugin 3.0.7, require bundletool inventory to contain com.google.firebase.crashlytics.mapping_file_id exactly once, select that exact resource with values, and require a nonempty canonical UUID. Keep Google app ID as a separate exact resource proof and reject any resource-name drift.

entries.mistake: After correcting the Crashlytics resource name, the verifier still rejected because it assumed the mapping-file build ID was a canonical hyphenated UUID.
entries.rootCause: The value-shape assertion was guessed rather than derived from the generated plugin 3.0.7 resource. Structural inspection proves the sealed AAB carries a quoted nonempty default string containing exactly 32 hexadecimal characters.
entries.prevention: Require the exact mapping_file_id resource name, one quoted nonempty default string value and an exact 32-hex build ID. Do not print the identifier and do not infer UUID formatting without artifact evidence.

entries.mistake: The first browser upload attempt armed a file-chooser wait and clicked the first .aab file input, but Chrome did not emit the chooser event before the control timeout. No file was selected or transmitted.
entries.rootCause: The hidden/native upload input did not surface a chooser through the initial direct input click in the extension-controlled Play Console tab; the attempt relied on the generic file-upload path without first applying the Chrome-specific recovery guidance.
entries.prevention: Before retrying, read the Chrome file-upload troubleshooting guidance, re-establish the exact Internal Testing draft, prove the draft contains no uploaded bundle and the sealed AAB hash is unchanged, then use the documented Chrome-compatible visible upload control or input flow. Fail closed on any ambiguous chooser or duplicate upload and never rebuild the AAB.

entries.mistake: The first C30S release-note value placed the en-GB opening tag, note text and closing tag on one line. Play Console rejected it as an unclosed locale tag and kept Next disabled.
entries.rootCause: The value followed the visible placeholder semantically but did not preserve the newline-delimited locale-tag layout required by Play Console's release-note parser.
entries.prevention: Use an exact three-line value with <en-GB> alone on the first line, bounded truthful note text on the second line and </en-GB> alone on the third line. Require Play to report one language and enable Next before leaving the create-release step.

entries.mistake: The first OPPO Play Store UI inspection requested uiautomator to dump to /dev/tty, but this device returned only the dump-location message and no XML hierarchy, so no Update/Open state could be classified.
entries.rootCause: The OPPO Android 13 uiautomator implementation does not stream the hierarchy through the adb shell output for /dev/tty even though the command exits successfully.
entries.prevention: Use one exact agent-owned file under /data/local/tmp, verify the path literally, dump the hierarchy there, read only sanitized relevant nodes, and remove only that exact temporary file after inspection. Never infer an update button from coordinates without parsed text, description and bounds.

entries.mistake: A narrow read-only search for apksigner/build-tools references under scripts returned no matches, and ripgrep's expected exit code 1 was allowed to surface as a shell-command failure.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic omitted the registered no-match handling even though absence of a repository-packaged tool path was a valid result and the SDK path could be resolved from scoped Android configuration.
entries.prevention: For optional ripgrep searches, explicitly treat exit code 1 as no matches and reject only exit codes above 1. For Android build-tool resolution, prefer the exact sdk.dir from apps/mobile/android/local.properties and select a known build-tools directory without scanning unrelated folders.

entries.mistake: An ADB tap used the centre of a previously captured YouTube Try again node, but the resulting screen was the MoolSocial composer instead of the expected retry state.
entries.rootCause: The coordinate was separated from its hierarchy capture by evidence collection and inspection steps, so the action relied on stale bounds without an immediate same-state revalidation.
entries.prevention: For every OPPO tap, capture a fresh hierarchy immediately before the action, require exact package focus and one exact semantic node, derive the centre from that same node, perform one tap, then recapture and classify the result. Never reuse bounds across intervening steps or screens.

entries.mistake: The recovery step expected a fresh Close composer node, but the immediate hierarchy contained zero such nodes because the device screen had changed since the prior capture.
entries.rootCause: The proposed recovery target was based on the last observed screen while device UI state remained live; by action time that semantic target no longer existed.
entries.prevention: Treat a zero-or-multiple fresh semantic match as a successful fail-closed stop, never as permission to reuse the earlier coordinate. Register the state change, inspect the new hierarchy read-only, and choose the next action only from that new authoritative state.

entries.mistake: A screenshot destination was named as Feed-read rejection evidence after an earlier Feed hierarchy, but the live OPPO was manually navigated before the screenshot and the image actually shows Work with the Mool menu open.
entries.rootCause: The hierarchy classification and screenshot capture were not one atomic state-locked evidence operation, while the founder was also exercising the device.
entries.prevention: Never infer screenshot content from an earlier hierarchy or its planned filename. Visually inspect every screenshot before citing it, preserve misclassified artifacts as invalid evidence, and use only an atomic fresh hierarchy-plus-screenshot pair when the device is not concurrently operated.

entries.mistake: The first atomic Quiz-format selection required a single-line content description equal to Quiz with an ellipsis, but the fresh OPPO hierarchy exposed one clickable selector with the two-line content description Quiz newline Quiz. The assertion found zero targets and stopped before any tap.
entries.rootCause: The test gate matched the terminal table's visual truncation instead of normalizing and evaluating the complete accessibility description returned by uiautomator.
entries.prevention: For format selectors, normalize CR/LF-separated accessibility descriptions into trimmed nonempty tokens, require all tokens to equal the requested exact label, and still require exactly one enabled clickable node from the immediately fresh hierarchy before deriving its centre. Never match the console's truncated rendering.

entries.mistake: The normalized Quiz selector retry found one semantic XML element but stored the filtered pipeline as a scalar and then indexed it as if it were an explicit array. The subsequent bounds assertion rejected before any tap.
entries.rootCause: The PowerShell pipeline result was not wrapped at the outermost assignment boundary, so the single XmlElement retained scalar XML adapter/indexing behavior instead of deterministic array semantics.
entries.prevention: Wrap the entire filtered XML-node pipeline in an explicit array before checking Count or indexing, cast the chosen bounds property to string, validate the exact coordinate shape, cast each capture group to integer independently, and derive the centre only after all assertions pass.

entries.mistake: The atomic Carousel-format inspection omitted whitespace between the PowerShell return keyword and $false inside the semantic-node filter. PowerShell emitted non-terminating command-not-found errors for rejected nodes, while the unique enabled clickable Carousel selector still passed and was tapped once, opening the Android photo picker.
entries.rootCause: A compressed one-line diagnostic sacrificed token separation and did not set ErrorActionPreference to Stop, allowing a scripting error to coexist with a successful final process exit.
entries.prevention: Use readable token separation in all device scripts, set ErrorActionPreference to Stop at the start, avoid return inside Where-Object when a single boolean expression is sufficient, and reject any stderr/error-record emission before performing a device action. Preserve the picker evidence but perform no further UI action until this recurrence is registered and the current focus is re-proven.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to select Image from the Carousel composer correctly found zero Image selectors because that state exposes only Carousel and Text, but its fail-closed branch omitted whitespace between the PowerShell throw keyword and the error string. ErrorActionPreference was Stop, so no tap occurred.
entries.rootCause: The immediately preceding tokenization prevention was applied to return but not generalized to all PowerShell language keywords in another compressed one-line device command. The action also assumed the six-format selector remained present after Carousel changed the composer mode.
entries.prevention: Do not compress device-control PowerShell. Put spaces after every language keyword, express fail-closed assertions as readable multiline statements, set ErrorActionPreference to Stop, and inspect the current semantic selector set before choosing a transition. From Carousel, use the one visible Text selector to return to the six-format grid before seeking Image.

entries.mistake: After the Image selector correctly opened the Android photo picker and one Back action cancelled it, the verifier expected the composer title New image. The fresh hierarchy instead exposed the correct full title New image post, so evidence capture stopped after the intended picker cancellation.
entries.rootCause: The postcondition used an inferred shorthand title instead of first deriving the exact accessibility title from the current released app semantics.
entries.prevention: For each composer mode, assert the exact title observed from a fresh hierarchy or a source-backed contract. For this released Image mode require exactly one New image post node, retain the no-selection postcondition, and only then capture evidence. Do not reuse shorthand labels from other modes.

entries.mistake: The Image-composer screenshot showed a text cursor but no on-screen keyboard. The next step incorrectly treated it as keyboard-open and sent Back, which returned from MoolSocial to the Google Play Store. Its postcondition then found no Close composer node, and the error branch again omitted whitespace after the PowerShell throw keyword.
entries.rootCause: Keyboard state was inferred from focus/cursor styling rather than proven from the screenshot or window insets, and the command reused compressed keyword syntax after two registered tokenization mistakes.
entries.prevention: Never send Back to dismiss input unless the on-screen keyboard is positively proven from the current atomic evidence. If Close composer is already semantically available, tap that exact node instead. Ban compressed PowerShell device commands for the remainder of C30T: every assertion and keyword must use readable spacing and ErrorActionPreference Stop. To recover, prove the exact Play Store app-detail focus and one enabled Open node, tap it once, then recapture MoolSocial before any journey action.

entries.mistake: The first recovery attempt required one directly clickable Google Play Open text node. The current Play hierarchy instead exposes two non-clickable Open label nodes with identical bounds inside one enabled clickable ancestor, so the assertion stopped before any tap.
entries.rootCause: The recovery gate assumed Flutter-style label/click target co-location instead of accommodating Google Play's nested Android view semantics.
entries.prevention: On the exact MoolSocial Play app-detail activity, require the unique app title, require the text and content-description Open labels to share the same label bounds, walk each label to its nearest enabled clickable ancestor, require those ancestors to resolve to one identical bounds rectangle, and tap only that ancestor centre from the same fresh hierarchy.

entries.mistake: After the five-domain navigation pass, the helper for returning to Social used the compressed invalid token return$d. ErrorActionPreference Stop terminated the helper during the initial read-only hierarchy load, before any tap.
entries.rootCause: The ban on compressed device-control PowerShell was stated but not operationalized in the very next ad hoc command; brevity was again favored over explicit token separation.
entries.prevention: For the rest of C30T, do not define compressed inline functions or place control-flow keywords adjacent to expressions. Use fully expanded multiline commands with one statement per line, visible whitespace after every keyword, and a separate fresh hierarchy capture for each action. Any command containing patterns such as return$, throw quote adjacency, or -and$ must not be executed.

entries.mistake: After opening the main menu from Chat, the return assertion expected Open Social. Chat is already classified inside the Social domain, so the exact clickable menu label is Social, current domain and the assertion stopped before a second tap.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic conflated domain selection state with the currently displayed route. The domain can be Social while the nested Chat route remains visible; selecting the current-domain control still routes to the Social root.
entries.prevention: When returning from a nested route, derive the exact fresh family label instead of assuming it has the Open prefix. From Chat require exactly one enabled clickable Social, current domain node and tap its same-hierarchy centre, then require Social Home semantics before continuing.

entries.mistake: The exact Social current-domain target was tapped successfully, but the post-action verifier assigned its matching nodes to $home. PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive, so this attempted to overwrite the protected read-only $HOME variable and stopped verification.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic used a generic variable name explicitly prohibited by workspace command discipline instead of a task-specific name.
entries.prevention: Never declare or assign HOME, home, CODEX_HOME or other common system-option names. Use task-specific names such as $socialHomeNodes. After any post-action verifier failure, do not repeat the tap; recapture the current state read-only and verify whether the intended transition already occurred.

entries.mistake: The Feed navigation command embedded the exact UI copy We couldn’t refresh your Feed inside a single-quoted PowerShell literal. The curly apostrophe was parsed as a quote boundary in this command path, producing a parser error before the script or any device action began.
entries.rootCause: User-visible typographic copy was interpolated directly into shell syntax instead of using an ASCII-safe structural predicate.
entries.prevention: Do not embed typographic apostrophes or copied rich text in PowerShell single-quoted predicates. Use an ASCII-safe anchored regex or match stable neighboring semantics, require exactly one result, and keep the full Unicode copy only in evidence files written with apply_patch.

entries.mistake: The exact Feed navigation target was tapped successfully, but the postcondition required the Feed error description to end immediately after its heading. The released accessibility node combines the heading twice and the explanatory detail in one multiline description, so the anchored match found zero and stopped verification.
entries.rootCause: The assertion assumed one semantic node per visual text element instead of inspecting the composite semantics emitted by the Feed error card.
entries.prevention: After a successful navigation action, do not repeat it. From a fresh hierarchy require one Feed-current node, require one composite description whose first normalized token is the expected error heading, and independently resolve the Create a post label to its unique clickable ancestor before testing that CTA.

entries.mistake: The first status-only Cloud Run log query escaped the timestamp quotes with backslashes inside PowerShell. gcloud received the timestamp as a separate malformed argument and rejected both provider queries before returning any log entry.
entries.rootCause: Bash-style backslash quote escaping was used in PowerShell argument construction instead of building one literal filter string variable.
entries.prevention: Construct each Cloud Logging filter as a single PowerShell string variable using doubled double quotes or single-quoted interpolation-safe components, pass that variable as one positional argument, and retain the safe output projection limited to timestamp, revision, request method, status and severity. Never request payload, URL, headers or private verdict fields.

entries.mistake: A bounded backend source search passed functions and services as repository roots even though those directories do not exist. ripgrep returned useful mobile matches but exited with path errors for both missing roots.
entries.rootCause: The search guessed conventional backend directory names instead of first enumerating repository-owned candidate paths with rg --files.
entries.prevention: Before a multi-root ripgrep search, derive exact existing repository paths from rg --files or Test-Path. Search only confirmed roots, and explicitly handle optional no-match exit code 1 without masking path or I/O errors.

entries.mistake: The first Chat filter helper wrapped the source node list before piping it to Where-Object, but PowerShell unwrapped the single matching result during pipeline assignment. Indexing that scalar as targets[0] did not return the intended XML element, so the bounds value was empty and the assertion stopped before any tap.
entries.rootCause: The helper assumed @() around the pipeline input also guaranteed an array result after the pipeline, and used dynamic XML property access instead of explicit attribute access.
entries.prevention: Cast the complete filtered pipeline result to [array], require Count exactly one, retrieve the node with GetValue(0), and read bounds with GetAttribute('bounds'). Keep the bounds regex and numeric-coordinate assertions before every tap.

entries.mistake: While preparing the XML-helper regression entry, the diagnostic guessed that the prior evidence filename contained the numeric registry ID. The actual discovered evidence filename did not, so Get-Content failed on a nonexistent path.
entries.rootCause: A repository evidence path was inferred from an ID instead of discovered from rg --files, repeating the path-guessing class registered immediately before it.
entries.prevention: For every repository evidence reference, first discover the exact path with rg --files and a stable filename fragment, then read only the returned path. Never synthesize documentation paths from registry IDs.

entries.mistake: The Chat attachment-sheet sequence tapped the exact enabled Dismiss semantic node and then immediately tried to locate Back to conversations without first proving that the sheet had closed. The next assertion found no Back target and stopped.
entries.rootCause: The helper treated a successful input event as proof of a UI transition instead of recapturing and validating the post-action state before continuing to a different control.
entries.prevention: After every sheet or dialog dismissal action, recapture the hierarchy and screenshot, prove whether the overlay remains, and do not issue another action until the state is classified. If Dismiss is inert, register a product defect and use only a separately evidenced safe closure mechanism.

entries.mistake: A read-only Identity Platform configuration probe invoked the gcloud alpha command group without first checking whether the alpha component was installed. The Cloud SDK rejected the command and reported that its installation directory could not be modified.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic assumed optional gcloud component availability instead of discovering installed stable or beta command surfaces first.
entries.prevention: Do not install or modify the Cloud SDK. Discover available command groups with existing gcloud help or component-list metadata, and use an installed read-only surface. Never obtain or print an access token to work around missing commands.

entries.mistake: After the connected browser reported an empty tab list, the diagnostic guessed a browser.tabs.open method. The browser runtime rejected it because that method does not exist, and no tab was created.
entries.rootCause: The tab-creation API was inferred rather than discovered from the connected browser binding after the compacted context no longer contained the previously read method details.
entries.prevention: Before retrying browser navigation, inspect the callable tab-manager method names from the already connected binding without invoking them, then use exactly one discovered creation method. Do not cycle through guessed methods.

entries.mistake: After the alpha Identity Platform command was proven unavailable, the diagnostic also invoked the beta command group without first confirming that the beta component was installed. It failed for the same immutable Cloud SDK installation reason.
entries.rootCause: The alternative route repeated an optional-component availability assumption instead of treating the component listing as authoritative.
entries.prevention: Stop all alpha and beta command probes on this machine. Use only installed stable gcloud surfaces, repository source, and already authorized read-only console evidence; do not install components or use access-token workarounds.

entries.mistake: The first YouTube error-state refactor patch spanned several control-flow branches and included an expected context fragment that did not exactly match the current dirty source. apply_patch rejected the entire edit before changing any file.
entries.rootCause: The edit attempted one broad replacement from a previously inspected conceptual flow instead of anchoring each change to a small exact source range in the current dirty tree.
entries.prevention: Before retrying a rejected edit, re-read the exact bounded source ranges and use multiple small apply_patch hunks with current literal anchors. Never widen or approximate patch context to force a dirty-tree edit.

entries.mistake: A read-only backend source search used one broad regular expression and did not explicitly normalize ripgrep exit code 1. The shell call stopped with no output before the bounded source display could run.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic again treated an optional search match as guaranteed and omitted the repository-mandated distinction between no-match exit 1 and actual path or I/O failures.
entries.prevention: Use small fixed-string ripgrep queries against confirmed paths. Immediately capture LASTEXITCODE, accept only 0 or 1, reset it before subsequent bounded reads, and fail only for values greater than 1.

entries.mistake: The new Chat service boundary test passed a validation call directly to assert.rejects. The method validates synchronously before returning its repository promise, so the expected ChatError escaped the asynchronous assertion and failed the test harness.
entries.rootCause: The test assumed every Promise-returning service signature deferred all failures asynchronously, even though request-shape validation intentionally fails before I/O.
entries.prevention: Use assert.throws for synchronous request validation, or pass an async function to assert.rejects only when the contract deliberately rejects after an await. Keep the service's fail-fast validation unchanged.

entries.mistake: The public Feed credential test added an assertion against a variable named transport while still constructing the fake transport inline in the gateway constructor. The test file did not compile, although the other focused tests passed.
entries.rootCause: The assertion was added without first refactoring the inline test double into a local binding visible to the assertion.
entries.prevention: When a new assertion needs state from an inline test double, create the named local before constructing the subject and pass that exact instance. Run dart format and compile the single changed test before rerunning the broader focused suite.

entries.mistake: The single Flutter-test retry used apps/mobile as its working directory while the same command referenced the regression registry and gate script with repository-root-relative paths. Get-Content failed before the gate, formatter, or test ran.
entries.rootCause: Two commands with different path roots were combined without converting every repository path to an absolute path or splitting the commands by working directory.
entries.prevention: Run repository machine gates from the repository root. Run Flutter format and tests in a separate command rooted at apps/mobile. Do not mix relative paths from different roots in one shell call.

entries.mistake: After conversation compaction, the retained summary identified a previously yielded test cell, but attempting to resume that cell failed because the execution runtime no longer contained the cell identifier.
entries.rootCause: The continuation treated a compacted summary's asynchronous tool handle as durable across execution-runtime boundaries.
entries.prevention: After compaction, treat yielded execution-cell identifiers as provisional. First query an attached terminal or other read-only runtime status; when no durable session exists, record the lost result and restart only the bounded verification command from its documented working directory.

entries.mistake: The regression-memory verification invoked check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 with a guessed TicketPath parameter that the script does not declare. JSON validation completed, but the gate did not run.
entries.rootCause: The command reused a parameter shape from a different repository gate instead of reading the target script's param block after compaction.
entries.prevention: Before invoking any repository gate whose exact command surface is not present in current context, read its bounded param block and pass only declared parameters. Do not transfer ticket or state parameters between gate scripts by convention.

entries.mistake: Static analysis and a bounded Flutter regression suite were launched through one Promise.all aggregation. The analyzer exited nonzero for four warnings, causing the orchestration script to fail without returning the sibling test process result.
entries.rootCause: Independent verification jobs with useful failure evidence were coupled through fail-fast promise aggregation without per-job error capture.
entries.prevention: Run analyzer and regression suites independently when either may legitimately expose new findings, or wrap every parallel job in its own result capture so one nonzero exit cannot suppress sibling evidence. Rerun only the result that was not durably captured.

entries.mistake: A bounded multi-file display assigned one nested two-value range using @(@(start,end)). PowerShell unwrapped the single nested range, so the loop iterated scalar integers and Math.Min received mismatched argument types.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic repeated the PowerShell singleton-unwrapping class already registered for XML query results, this time for a one-item collection of numeric ranges.
entries.prevention: Do not use a polymorphic one-or-many nested range container in PowerShell diagnostics. Display each file with explicit scalar start/end bounds, or force the outer collection with the unary comma and validate each item is a two-element array before indexing.

entries.mistake: Two rewritten Chat tests used exact single-widget text expectations for copy rendered as a longer sentence and for a participant name that legitimately appeared in both the app bar and a message sender label.
entries.rootCause: The tests asserted incidental Text widget cardinality instead of the intended behavioral state and stable control identities.
entries.prevention: Use stable keys for behavior and route ownership. When copy is deliberately part of a longer sentence, use textContaining; when the same truthful identity may appear in multiple semantic locations, require at least one match and pair it with the exact screen key or subtitle assertion.

entries.mistake: After correcting the duplicated Mahadev Fresh Mart identity expectation, the same test still required exactly one Order Support text widget. The support identity also appeared in both the app bar and the message sender label, causing the bounded retry to fail for the same reason.
entries.rootCause: The first correction was applied to only the failure reported in the prior run instead of auditing the entire rewritten test for identical exact-cardinality assertions before retry.
entries.prevention: When a test failure establishes a repeated assertion-pattern defect, search the complete bounded test for every equivalent matcher and correct the full class before rerunning. Do not patch only the first reported instance.

entries.mistake: The updated Chat navigation test tapped the connected navigator's Social family destination but then expected the separate Personal Mool home screen key. The product correctly opened the Social destination.
entries.rootCause: The test conflated the left-edge Mool launcher control with the destination selected inside its connected family menu.
entries.prevention: Assert the route owner associated with the exact selected family action. The launcher opens the family menu; selecting Social must assert the Social screen, while a dedicated Mool-home action must be used to assert the Personal Mool root.

entries.mistake: A combined focused Flutter verification command guessed the C29N creator ergonomics test filename. That path did not exist, so the test runner reported one load failure even though the other 26 tests passed.
entries.rootCause: The command relied on a shortened name retained in continuation context instead of discovering the exact current dirty-tree path with rg --files.
entries.prevention: Discover every focused test path with rg --files before constructing a multi-file Flutter command. If one guessed path causes only a load failure while sibling tests pass, preserve those results and run only the exact discovered missing test after registration.

entries.mistake: The complete Flutter inventory was used as if it were a single C30T release gate even though the repository contains hundreds of broad Shop, Care, Work, motion, and golden tests intentionally frozen outside the Social/YouTube/Chat successor scope. The run produced 699 passes, 31 skips, and 193 failures, dominated by stale golden baselines and legacy prototype assumptions unrelated to C30T.
entries.rootCause: The verification command did not partition release-critical C30T tests from the repository's historical design-review inventory before execution.
entries.prevention: Before a bounded successor release, classify tests into exact scope-critical, shared navigation/startup, and frozen historical design/golden inventories. Require the first two partitions to pass. Run the broad inventory only as evidence, record unrelated failures as deferred tickets, and never update unrelated goldens or redesign frozen domains under the successor ticket.

entries.mistake: The product entrypoint was changed to construct ChatSession.production(), but the same patch did not add the chat_session.dart import. A bounded source-header review caught the omission before analyzer execution.
entries.rootCause: The compatibility correction focused on ownership and disposal at the runApp call site without verifying that the newly referenced type was already imported.
entries.prevention: Whenever a new concrete type is introduced at a Dart call site, inspect the file header in the same edit cycle and add its exact package-relative import before formatting or compiling. Keep the pre-compile source check as a mandatory step.

entries.mistake: The post-compatibility verification grouped four Chat-dependent vertical slices with the full Retailer Business Services suite. The Chat-dependent paths passed, but an existing compact-accessibility test in Business Services reported a 16-pixel overflow unrelated to Chat or C30T.
entries.rootCause: The bounded compatibility command included an entire neighboring-domain test file instead of selecting only the exact Chat continuity test within that file.
entries.prevention: Use plain-name selection or exact focused files for cross-domain compatibility checks. Record unrelated neighboring-domain failures as deferred domain tickets and do not rerun or repair them under a Social/YouTube/Chat successor.

entries.mistake: The authorized Firebase Android API key update succeeded and preserved the visible API target list, but the post-write assertion incorrectly expected 25 targets. The existing list actually contains 27, so the wrapper exited nonzero after the external change had completed.
entries.rootCause: The target count was manually miscounted from the read-only JSON instead of being captured mechanically before mutation and compared afterward.
entries.prevention: For configuration updates, mechanically seal the exact pre-write normalized restriction set before mutation and compare the full post-write set, not a hand-entered cardinality. When the write has already succeeded, never repeat it solely because a later verification assertion was wrong; perform a read-only re-verification after registration.

entries.mistake: The exact two-function Dev deployment successfully updated moolSocialContent and created moolSocialChat, then Firebase CLI returned exit 2 because it could not set the new Chat service's implicit public invoker IAM policy under the organization policy. This repeats the known new-HTTPS-function partial-deployment class from C29U.
entries.rootCause: Firebase CLI attempts an IAM policy write when creating a second-generation HTTPS function, while this project's accepted application-security model uses Cloud Run's invoker IAM check disabled and enforces App Check plus Firebase Auth inside the function.
entries.prevention: For a newly created HTTPS function in this project, treat Firebase's IAM failure as a classified partial state, never broadly redeploy, and recover only the exact created Cloud Run service with --no-invoker-iam-check. Then prove the service is ready, uses the sealed runtime identity, reaches application-level 401 without credentials, and that excluded revisions did not change.

entries.mistake: A read-only C30T child-ticket inventory piped directly from a foreach statement to Format-Table. PowerShell rejected the empty pipe element before reading any ticket state.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic used statement-to-pipeline syntax that is not valid in the active PowerShell parser instead of collecting foreach output in an explicit array.
entries.prevention: For PowerShell inventories, assign foreach output to an explicitly initialized array, then pipe the completed array to formatting. Never place a pipe immediately after the closing brace of a foreach statement.

entries.mistake: A read-only rg command passed config/uaw-c30t-*-ticket.json as a positional path. On Windows the wildcard was not expanded, so rg rejected the literal invalid path.
entries.rootCause: The command relied on shell glob expansion for a positional rg path even though PowerShell did not expand it for this native executable invocation.
entries.prevention: Run rg against an existing directory and use --glob for filename selection, or discover exact paths with rg --files first. Never pass an unresolved wildcard as a positional Windows path to rg.

entries.mistake: A combined C30T state-and-evidence patch assumed the existing Chat deployment note contained a section headed Prevention. The file instead ended with Bounded recovery, so apply_patch rejected the complete patch before making changes.
entries.rootCause: The patch used remembered semantic structure rather than the exact current text of every target in a large multi-file mutation.
entries.prevention: Before a multi-file evidence update, inspect the exact anchor text of every existing target. Split machine-state, ticket-state and documentation append operations into bounded patches so one documentation anchor cannot reject unrelated state changes.

entries.mistake: After source and provider completion, the aggregate C30T ticket state string was changed to describe progress. The robust-delivery gate rejected the ticket because its immutable SHA-256 no longer matched the selected-ticket assessment.
entries.rootCause: Lifecycle progress was written into the sealed authorization ticket instead of only into the separate mutable machine-state and evidence records.
entries.prevention: Once a ticket hash is sealed in mvp-scope-gate-state.json, never mutate that ticket. Record implementation, provider, build, upload, install and journey progress only in the designated machine-state and evidence files.

entries.mistake: The new C30T readiness gate copied C30S's exact 15-plugin release registrant count without first reconciling the current dirty-tree generated registrant. The gate failed because the current registrant contains 16 plugins.
entries.rootCause: A predecessor release invariant was reused as current truth instead of mechanically inventorying the successor's dependency-derived plugin surface before sealing the allowlist.
entries.prevention: Before sealing a successor registrant count, enumerate every generated plugin, map it to an intentional current pubspec dependency, reject debug/integration or unused plugins, and then pin the exact audited list in both readiness and build gates.

entries.mistake: Pre-execution review found that the C30T wrapper gate placed $ErrorActionPreference inside a double-quoted required-pattern string, so the gate would expand the variable instead of matching the literal wrapper source.
entries.rootCause: A source-code pattern was expressed as an interpolating PowerShell string without escaping the leading dollar sign.
entries.prevention: All wrapper self-audit patterns containing PowerShell variable names must use single-quoted literals or an escaped dollar sign. Review the complete pattern array before first execution.

entries.mistake: C30T qualification cycle 1 failed before tests because release readiness scanned gate scripts containing the credential detector's own AIza regular expression and reported seven credential-shaped source files.
entries.rootCause: The credential absence scan included its own detection-pattern definitions without distinguishing literal scanner code from actual credential-bearing content.
entries.prevention: Audit all product, Android and backend source normally. For gate scripts, exclude only lines that define the detector regex itself, then scan the remaining content. Continue to fail on every other credential-shaped match and never print matching values.

entries.mistake: A registry correction patch attempted to update REG-1688's status and also match the same entry again as the insertion anchor for REG-1689. The overlapping contexts caused apply_patch to reject the entire patch.
entries.rootCause: One patch addressed the same JSON object through separate hunks instead of replacing one exact contiguous entry block or separating the operations.
entries.prevention: When updating an existing registry entry and appending a successor entry, use one exact contiguous hunk for the existing entry through its closing brace, then append the new entry in that same hunk. Keep documentation edits separate.

entries.mistake: The first explanation of the seven credential-shaped filename hits blamed scanner self-matches before running the bounded filename-only inventory. That inventory proved all seven hits were existing backend security/redaction test fixture files.
entries.rootCause: The failure cause was stated from pattern design intuition rather than first collecting the safe filename-only evidence already available from rg -l.
entries.prevention: For credential-scan failures, report no cause until a filename-only inventory is captured. Require zero matches in production source and allow credential-shaped test fixtures only through an exact filename allowlist; never print or read the matching values.

entries.mistake: Qualification cycle 1 reached the exact credential-fixture filename comparison, but readiness accessed .Count directly on Compare-Object's zero-result value. Under strict mode the null result has no Count property.
entries.rootCause: The set comparison did not force the possibly empty pipeline result into an array before reading cardinality.
entries.prevention: Wrap every possibly empty PowerShell pipeline result in @() before accessing Count, including Compare-Object, Select-String and filtered inventory results.

entries.mistake: C30T qualification cycle 1 stopped at the no-write formatter gate because apps/mobile/lib/features/shared/social_content_gateway.dart was not formatter-clean after the Social auth-boundary implementation.
entries.rootCause: The earlier focused source verification ran analyzer and tests but did not retain a final formatter-clean check after the last Social gateway edit.
entries.prevention: After the last source edit in a release ticket, run dart format in check-only mode over the complete release source inventory. If exactly one C30T-owned file fails, register it, format only that file, and restart the full qualification cycle.

entries.mistake: C30T qualification cycle 1 focused tests produced three failures: a Feed ownership test retained the removed _choiceByWorld source-string expectation, Videos overflowed by 14 pixels at 140% text in C29O, and the C27D six-family helper found no expected widget.
entries.rootCause: The pre-qualification focused runs did not include this exact combined accessibility/navigation partition after the final Feed, YouTube header and production Chat changes.
entries.prevention: Audit each failure separately: replace obsolete source-string ownership assertions with stable behavior, correct the real Videos 140% overflow without broad redesign, and reconcile C27D against the exact current family control. Rerun the three exact tests before restarting the full cycle.

entries.mistake: The targeted C27D Social-navigation correction asserted selected state with SemanticsData.hasFlag(SemanticsFlag.isSelected). The current Flutter SDK deprecates hasFlag and no longer exposes SemanticsFlag through this test surface, so analyzer stopped with one info and one error before focused tests ran.
entries.rootCause: The new assertion used a remembered legacy semantics API instead of the repository's already-established current flagsCollection.isSelected Tristate pattern.
entries.prevention: Before adding Flutter semantics assertions, search current repository tests for the accepted SDK pattern. Assert flagsCollection.isSelected against Tristate.isTrue or Tristate.isFalse, then run analyzer before any test or release qualification retry.

entries.mistake: The first correction for REG-1694 changed the selected-state assertion to flagsCollection.isSelected and Tristate but did not add the dart:ui import that exposes Tristate in this test file. Analyzer therefore stopped with two undefined-name errors.
entries.rootCause: The correction copied the expression pattern from established tests without also reconciling the source file's imports.
entries.prevention: When adopting an established Flutter test API pattern, compare both the expression and its explicit imports before retrying analyzer. Add only the narrow dart:ui symbol import required by the assertion.

entries.mistake: The exact three-test rerun passed Feed ownership and the 140-percent Videos layout, then C29O expected the Create workbench from an unstarted unauthenticated JourneySession and C27D expected the Social dock to remain visible while the full-screen Create composer was open.
