entries.rootCause: The tests did not model the current production contracts: Create is Firebase-authenticated, and the full-screen composer intentionally hides the destination dock until Close returns to Feed.
entries.prevention: Create journey tests that assert composer contents must start a deliberately authenticated JourneySession. Global-navigation tests must treat Create as a full-screen branch, assert the composer and hidden dock, close it through the real control, prove the Feed return state, and only then continue dock navigation.

entries.mistake: A combined registry-and-four-document resolution patch used 'prove the Feed return state' as an anchor, while the actual C30T evidence file says 'prove the Feed dock state'. apply_patch rejected the whole patch before making changes.
entries.rootCause: The combined patch paraphrased one previously written evidence line instead of matching its exact current text.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact tail of every evidence target before updating it. Keep registry status changes in one bounded patch and append resolution sections to documents with exact local anchors so one wording mismatch cannot reject all updates.

entries.mistake: The new REG-1694 through REG-1696 entries used human-readable commands such as 'flutter analyze' in their gates arrays. The regression-memory checker requires each gate value to resolve to an existing repository path and rejected the first invalid value.
entries.rootCause: Execution evidence labels were confused with the registry's repository-path-only gate metadata contract.
entries.prevention: Registry gates must contain only exact existing repository-relative file paths. Record command outcomes in evidence documents, and use the actual C30T qualifier and machine-state paths in the gates array.

entries.mistake: C30T qualification cycle 1 ran the complete focused Flutter partition with exit code zero, 140 passing tests and one intentional skip, but rejected the log because it required the exact text 'All tests passed!' while Flutter emits 'All other tests passed!' when skips are present.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier's redundant success-marker assertion did not account for Flutter's documented skip-aware terminal wording even though the native command exit code had already proved success.
entries.prevention: Retain the mandatory zero exit-code check and accept only Flutter's two exact success forms: 'All tests passed!' or 'All other tests passed!'. Continue to reject every nonzero test command before marker evaluation.

entries.mistake: C30T qualification cycle 1 completed backend verification with exit code zero, 503 passed and 0 failed, but rejected the log because it required the legacy '# pass 503' reporter line while the active Node reporter emits 'ℹ pass 503'.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier pinned a reporter decoration instead of the exact semantic pass and fail summary values.
entries.prevention: Keep the mandatory zero process exit code, then require an anchored summary line ending in 'pass 503' and a separate anchored summary line ending in 'fail 0', allowing only non-alphanumeric reporter decoration before each label.

entries.mistake: The bounded backend marker diagnostic passed backend/functions/test to rg even though this repository stores backend tests under backend/functions/src. rg returned exit 2 after the useful log and qualifier lines had already been printed.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic guessed a conventional test directory without first confirming it exists in this repository.
entries.prevention: Inventory backend paths with rg --files or Test-Path first and pass only existing exact paths to rg. Treat rg exit 1 as no matches and exit 2 as a command/path mistake requiring registration.

entries.mistake: C30T qualification cycle 1 began with the exact 15-plugin release registrant, then the focused Flutter test command regenerated the 16-plugin test registrant. The later repository release-readiness gate correctly rejected that post-test generated state.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier restored release-generated Android state only before tests, even though Flutter tests are allowed to regenerate the shared plugin registrant for the test dependency graph.
entries.prevention: After all Flutter tests and before final release gates or source sealing, rerun release config-only, prove pubspec and lock are unchanged, prove no APK/AAB changed, and assert the exact 15-plugin release registrant again. Never weaken the release registrant invariant to accept the test plugin.

entries.mistake: Review of the next unexecuted qualifier phase found Get-RelativeFiles would search nonexistent backend/functions/test after already inventorying all TypeScript under backend/functions/src, where this repository's backend tests actually live.
entries.rootCause: The source-manifest inventory assumed a conventional separate backend test directory that does not exist in this repository.
entries.prevention: Build source manifests only from confirmed existing directories. The recursive backend/functions/src TypeScript inventory already includes production and .test.ts files, so remove the nonexistent redundant directory instead of suppressing rg exit 2.

entries.mistake: A read-only C30T child-ticket status inventory again piped directly from a foreach statement into Format-Table. PowerShell rejected the empty pipe element, repeating REG-1682, and the parallel orchestration discarded the other read-only outputs.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic was composed from a familiar pipeline shape without applying the already-registered explicit-array prevention rule.
entries.prevention: For every PowerShell foreach inventory, initialize an array, append each object inside the loop, and pipe only the completed array. Never place a pipe immediately after a foreach closing brace, including in read-only diagnostics.

entries.mistake: A successful PowerShell regression-memory script invocation printed its pass result, but the wrapper then compared an unset LASTEXITCODE to zero. PowerShell evaluated null -ne 0 as true and falsely threw a gate failure.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic applied a native-process exit-code contract to a PowerShell script invocation, which does not guarantee that LASTEXITCODE is assigned.
entries.prevention: Invoke repository PowerShell gates under ErrorActionPreference Stop and rely on terminating errors or the returned success record. Inspect LASTEXITCODE only immediately after native executables that explicitly set it; never use an unset or stale LASTEXITCODE to classify a PowerShell script.

entries.mistake: The first 49-file expanded C30T audit run reported 303 passes, one skip and six failures, but the diagnostic emitted only the last 120 compact-reporter lines. The actual six failure blocks occurred earlier and were lost from the retained tool output.
entries.rootCause: The audit optimized output volume before proving that all failure blocks would remain visible, and compact reporter progress lines displaced the actionable context.
entries.prevention: For a newly widened Flutter partition, persist or filter complete failure blocks and the failing file names before truncating output. If the first aggregate run fails, isolate candidate files without changing source, classify each failure, and only then retry an affected test after the failure is durably registered.

entries.mistake: C30T replaced fabricated runtime Chat threads with authenticated real-provider states, but the four Chat phone golden tests still compare the new product against screenshots of the removed inbox, order-support, business and people fixtures. All four comparisons fail by design-sized pixel differences.
entries.rootCause: The functional Chat implementation and focused gateway tests were updated without updating or retiring the visual baselines whose content contract depended on the forbidden fixtures.
entries.prevention: Every removal of runtime fixture data must inventory visual baselines that render the fixture. Rebaseline only after inspecting the truthful signed-out, empty, loading or unavailable replacement at the exact accepted viewport; never approve pixels solely because update-goldens makes a test green.

entries.mistake: The C29E Social hosting-separation test constructs a ReviewOtpGateway marked signed in but never starts JourneySession before tapping Create, then expects the authenticated Create workbench. The current truthful auth boundary correctly does not render that postcondition.
entries.rootCause: The older test relied on constructor configuration as if it were an established session and escaped the earlier authenticated-lifecycle test correction inventory.
entries.prevention: Every widget test expecting an authenticated Social mutation surface must call JourneySession.start and assert isAuthenticated before pumping or tapping the mutation route. Constructor arguments alone are not an authenticated lifecycle.

entries.mistake: The C10B global-navigation regression still requires screen04-feed-thumb-composer before and after a Work round trip, but C30T removed that key and now exposes the public Feed through screen04-moolsocial-feed-brand plus truthful loading, empty, error or content owners.
entries.rootCause: A navigation test asserted a retired internal child widget instead of the durable Feed route/root owner that its journey actually needed to prove.
entries.prevention: Global-navigation tests must assert the canonical route/root and a durable current surface owner, not a mutable composer child. When a C30T view owner is removed, inventory every key reference before source qualification.

entries.mistake: After correcting C10B's retired Feed child key, the focused rerun reached a second stale assertion that requires moolsocial-single-home-launcher-shell on the Social Feed root. The current Social root exposes the durable mool-compact-launcher directly, but does not render that conditional wrapper shell in this projection.
entries.rootCause: The older navigation test asserted both the public launcher control and an internal conditional wrapper, although only the public compact launcher is required to prove the journey and remains stable across root projections.
entries.prevention: Global-navigation journey tests must assert and operate the durable mool-compact-launcher plus destination owners. Do not require conditional layout wrappers unless the wrapper itself is the acceptance subject and the tested projection is proven to render it.

entries.mistake: The original C30T source manifest inventoried Dart test files but not the PNG golden assets those tests compare. A golden could therefore change without changing the sealed source fingerprint.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier treated test source as code-only even though visual baselines are executable acceptance inputs.
entries.prevention: Every release qualifier that runs golden tests must inventory the exact golden asset directory alongside test source. Preserve historical assets, include new candidate-named baselines, and seal their checksums into both qualification cycles.

entries.mistake: The historical C30T qualifier still targeted the invalidated -01 evidence root and, after cycle 2, expected available-once build authority and transitioned directly to the founder secret prompt state. That no longer matches the founder-directed deeper pre-AAB audit and separate AAB authorization boundary.
entries.rootCause: The audit hold updated machine state but the qualifier's evidence epoch and terminal transition were not simultaneously revised.
entries.prevention: A founder-directed audit invalidation must allocate a new immutable evidence epoch and update the qualifier terminal state in the same change. Pre-AAB success may record qualification and fingerprint only; it must leave build, upload and install authorization false until a later explicit founder authorization updates the gate.

entries.mistake: The first comprehensive -02 attempt included six historical C03/C05/C07/C09/R15/C25F suites alongside their later replacement owners. Forty assertions failed because those files require the removed mool-root-selected route, retired Mool Home copy and grid, review Chat attachments/replies, and the pre-C27 54px compact-cell width.
entries.rootCause: The expanded manifest was reconstructed by filename breadth rather than by the repository's chronological contract succession. Superseded ticket tests were treated as simultaneous current acceptance owners.
entries.prevention: For cumulative release qualification, map each journey to its latest accepted owner and record an explicit disposition for superseded suites. Preserve historical tests unchanged, but select current C24-C30 connected-navigation, exact-return, fitment and accessibility owners so the release gate does not demand mutually exclusive UI contracts.

entries.mistake: Two current-contract replacement suites still treated Social as a generic MoolDestinationNavigationV2 family and required moolsocial-local-shorts-selection. C30T Social intentionally owns its four destinations through screen04-rail-* while the other five families retain generic local-selection keys.
entries.rootCause: The shared six-family journey helper erased the accepted specialized Social rail-key boundary when checking all families uniformly.
entries.prevention: Cross-family navigation tests must share behavior and sizing assertions but resolve each family's canonical owner keys. Use screen04-rail-* for Social and moolsocial-local-*-selection for the generic Shop, Food, Travel, Care and Work rails.

entries.mistake: The continuous Social audit comparison attempted to normalize Windows separators with a two-backslash literal, so mixed-separator candidate paths remained unequal and all 61 files were falsely reported missing. The following registry read also guessed config/codex-regression-memory.json instead of discovering the durable config/codex-development-regression-registry.json path.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic used shell-language path and catalog-name assumptions without first proving the normalized representation and exact durable filename.
entries.prevention: Normalize both path sets with PowerShell regex replacement (`-replace '\\','/'`), assert representative normalized values before set comparison, and discover durable registry paths with `rg --files config` before reading. Treat impossible all-missing results or a missing guessed catalog path as diagnostic defects, not product findings.

entries.mistake: The bounded Social/YouTube release-surface search passed apps/mobile/lib/app.dart to rg even though that optional conventional entrypoint does not exist in this repository. rg returned exit 2 after emitting useful matches from the valid paths.
entries.rootCause: The search mixed proven repository paths with a guessed conventional Flutter filename instead of inventorying exact existing entrypoints first.
entries.prevention: Use `rg --files apps/mobile/lib` or Test-Path to resolve exact entrypoints before a bounded source search, and pass only existing paths. Never treat partial rg output from exit 2 as a completed audit result.

entries.mistake: The YouTube capability audit explicitly passed backend/functions/src/index.test.ts to rg even though backend tests are distributed under discovered *.test.ts paths and that guessed file does not exist. This repeated the already registered nonexistent-path diagnostic class and produced rg exit 2 after partial useful output.
entries.rootCause: The command was expanded with a conventional colocated test filename without applying the mandatory rg --files discovery rule from REG-1701, REG-1703 and REG-1716.
entries.prevention: Before every multi-path backend search, obtain the exact path set from `rg --files backend/functions/src`, filter that discovered set, and pass only those results. Do not hand-type optional test filenames. Exit 2 invalidates the diagnostic regardless of partial matches.

entries.mistake: The accepted Dev public-review profile enables public YouTube discovery but structurally requires ownerConnect=false. The release UI truthfully requests minimum youtube.readonly, yet live revision youtubeprovider-00036-qer must reject its connection start, status and disconnect operations as capability_disabled.
entries.rootCause: The long-lived accepted reviewer mode inherited the single-capability supervised-proof invariant even though the declared reviewer use case contains two compatible read-only capabilities: public discovery and separately user-initiated channel connection.
entries.prevention: Define one exact Dev-only accepted reviewer capability set containing publicData plus ownerConnect and no mutation, upload, Analytics, Reporting, Live, creator-asset or owner-action capability. Keep the mode incompatible with proof profile/expiry controls, gate its materialization and verification scripts, and prove every non-readonly capability remains false before any deployment authorization.

entries.mistake: The continuous expanded audit added four older C23/C24/FIX1 files whose five assertions require Social Home to select families in place and expose the retired Shorts/Videos/Feed/Create wording and mool-home-social-videos key. Current C29/C30 Social intentionally exposes Home/Shorts/Create/Feed and routes top-level families directly; later C25/C26/FIX2 owners already test the accepted navigation contract.
entries.rootCause: The breadth inventory again treated historical ticket filenames as cumulative current acceptance owners without checking their UI-contract succession against the C29/C30 specialized Social surface.
entries.prevention: Preserve C23/C24/FIX1 suites as history but exclude mutually exclusive Social Home expectations from C30T release qualification. Select the passing current C25 main-only, C26 service/care/work, FIX2 exact-owner, and C29/C30 specialized Social owners; retain the iOS player containment source gate.

entries.mistake: The first qualifier hardening patch expected the YouTube revision assertion twice even though it appears once in the current script. apply_patch rejected the context atomically and changed no file.
entries.rootCause: The patch was composed from an intended replacement shape instead of the exact just-read current block.
entries.prevention: Before retrying a multi-file qualifier patch, locate every target line with rg, inspect the exact bounded block, and patch only unique current context. Verify the failed atomic patch made no partial state change before retrying.

entries.mistake: The 55-file local audit shell command used timeout_ms=1000 as if it were an early-yield control. The shell tool correctly terminated the command before the evidence root was created. The follow-up process check then returned exit 1 when no dart/flutter process existed because Get-Process absence was not converted into an explicit successful empty inventory.
entries.rootCause: Command execution timeout was confused with orchestration yield behavior, and an expected empty process lookup inherited a nonzero PowerShell command status.
entries.prevention: Give long Flutter audit commands a realistic execution timeout and rely on the tool's normal yielded-cell behavior for progress. For optional process inventories, assign the result under ErrorAction SilentlyContinue and emit an explicit success record; do not allow expected absence to determine the shell exit code.

entries.mistake: The public Feed author line renders the literal text 'Just now' for every provider-returned post, ignoring SocialPublishedItem.publishedAt. Preserved C30K posts therefore appear newly published regardless of their authoritative timestamp.
entries.rootCause: The prototype author-line copy was retained when the Feed switched from local review items to real provider DTOs.
entries.prevention: Render one deterministic bounded age/date label from the server timestamp, test future/just-now/minute/hour/day/older boundaries, and never substitute a static recency claim for provider metadata.

entries.mistake: The focused Feed timestamp verification was launched before task compaction, but its yielded execution-cell identifier was no longer available afterward. The final exit code and complete output therefore could not be recovered and cannot be used as test evidence.
entries.rootCause: A transient tool-process handle was treated as durable across context compaction even though only completed filesystem evidence is durable.
entries.prevention: Reject every unrecoverable yielded-cell result as unknown, register it before retry, run one fresh bounded command with a durable log file, and record the exit code and checksum before relying on the result.

entries.mistake: The Social interaction backend audit passed `backend/functions/src/socialContent*` as an rg path on Windows. The filesystem rejected the wildcard path and rg exited 2 after producing partial matches from other valid paths.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style wildcard was used in a positional Windows path instead of an rg `-g` filter over a proven directory.
entries.prevention: Search only proven directory roots and apply filename filters with `-g`, or discover exact files first with `rg --files`. Exit 2 invalidates the entire diagnostic even when partial matches are useful.

entries.mistake: The public-share route audit searched broad apps, backend, deployment, docs and config roots in one parallel orchestration step. One search exceeded its ten-second budget, causing the whole orchestration result to fail while emitting only partial output.
entries.rootCause: The search scope included generated backend output and unrelated documentation instead of first limiting the question to current mobile routing, Android app-link declarations and public web route owners.
entries.prevention: Run small independent searches over exact current source roots, exclude generated output, and preserve each command's exit result separately. A timed-out parallel aggregate cannot establish absence or presence for the audit question.

entries.mistake: The bounded share-route retry launched several shell searches from one orchestration script but did not normalize ripgrep exit 1 for an expected no-match result. The first absence aborted the script before the remaining searches and suppressed their outputs.
entries.rootCause: A semantic absence query was executed under a tool wrapper that treats every nonzero shell result as an exception, without an explicit exit-1 contract.
entries.prevention: For searches where no match is a valid audit result, capture ripgrep output and exit code inside PowerShell, emit an explicit `matches=0` record for exit 1, and fail only on exit greater than 1. Keep each audit question independently observable.

entries.mistake: The second bounded share-route retry dynamically concatenated JavaScript and PowerShell quote fragments for four searches. The resulting tool script had invalid JavaScript syntax and no nested shell command ran.
entries.rootCause: Unnecessary dynamic command construction mixed three quoting languages for fixed audit queries.
entries.prevention: Use literal, separately awaited shell-tool calls for fixed queries. Keep PowerShell exit normalization inside each literal command and avoid constructing command strings from embedded quote fragments.

entries.mistake: A later four-way audit normalized the optional asset-link file search but left the optional documentation-contract search unnormalized. Its valid no-match exit 1 again caused the parallel orchestration to fail and hid otherwise valid outputs.
entries.rootCause: The REG-1726 exit-normalization rule was applied to only the query expected to be empty, not to every audit query whose absence is semantically valid.
entries.prevention: Every optional rg query in a parallel batch must use the same explicit 0/1/>1 exit wrapper, regardless of whether matches are expected. Prefer direct file reads for proven files and independently observable outputs.

entries.mistake: The live Android App Links audit tried to open two exact moolsocial.com URLs directly through the web tool before establishing the domain through search. The tool rejected both as unsafe-to-open and returned no HTTP evidence.
entries.rootCause: The external read assumed direct URL opening was allowed for an unestablished domain in the current web-tool session.
entries.prevention: Establish the exact official domain with a bounded search first, then open a returned domain reference or its same-origin URLs. Treat an unsafe-open rejection as no evidence and register it before retry.

entries.mistake: The Android App Links source-owner audit searched for the live stale certificate fingerprint in a parallel batch without normalizing the legitimate no-match exit 1. This repeated the optional-search orchestration failure class and suppressed the other results.
entries.rootCause: An exact-presence check was treated as if a match were guaranteed even though proving the value absent from current source was one expected outcome.
entries.prevention: Every exact presence/absence query must explicitly normalize ripgrep exit 1 before entering a parallel tool batch. After repeated recurrence, run optional searches sequentially unless each wrapper has already been proven.

entries.mistake: The Feed Share sheet presents `Copy MoolSocial link` and then reports `MoolSocial link copied`, but the action never calls Clipboard.setData and is not bound to the selected post. The adjacent `Share in MoolSocial Chat` option only opens Chat and does not attach or send the post.
entries.rootCause: Prototype share-sheet copy was retained after real provider posts were introduced, without a stable public post-link contract or a verifiable share operation.
entries.prevention: Bind Share to the exact post, expose only an implemented action, write the stable HTTPS post URL to the clipboard before showing success, resolve the item query in Feed, test clipboard payload and deep-link pagination, and never report a share/copy success without an authoritative side effect.

entries.mistake: The live `https://moolsocial.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json` returns a certificate SHA-256 that does not match the Google Play app-signing certificate for com.moolsocial.app, and `https://moolsocial.com/app/social?...` returns HTTP 404. Android therefore cannot establish the intended verified Social App Link or provide a browser fallback for a shared post URL.
entries.rootCause: The public association file belongs to an earlier signing identity and its source is absent from the repository; Firebase Hosting also excludes dot-prefixed paths and has no Social-link fallback page.
entries.prevention: Version-control an exact assetlinks.json for package com.moolsocial.app and the Play signing SHA-256, permit the `.well-known` source in Hosting inventory, add a noindex Social-link fallback, test all three contracts, and require live HTTP plus on-device verified-link proof after separate Hosting deployment authority.

entries.mistake: Guest Feed readers can tap Like, Save or a poll/quiz choice, but the UI calls the authenticated content gateway directly. Firebase token acquisition then returns `Sign in to continue` as an inline error instead of starting the real sign-in journey and preserving the exact Feed post return location.
entries.rootCause: Create and author-message actions gained explicit JourneySession authentication gates during C30T, while card-level mutation actions remained coupled only to SharedSession and had no route-aware authentication callback.
entries.prevention: Gate Like, Save and Vote at the Social presentation owner with JourneySession.isAuthenticated; guests must begin sign-in with the exact Feed item return URI and no interaction write, while authenticated users continue to the same server-acknowledged SharedSession operation. Cover all three actions and the consumer return route.

entries.mistake: The post-interaction-test release restoration helper wrote `return'absent'` without required PowerShell token spacing. Because the release APK was legitimately absent, PowerShell tried to invoke a nonexistent `returnabsent` command and then emitted Get-Item/Get-FileHash errors. The outer command still exited zero and printed an untrustworthy artifact comparison.
entries.rootCause: The compact one-line helper sacrificed PowerShell syntax clarity and did not set ErrorActionPreference Stop, allowing non-terminating snapshot errors to coexist with a successful final condition.
entries.prevention: Use a multiline proven snapshot helper with `return 'absent'`, set ErrorActionPreference Stop, capture pre/post values only after successful helper calls, and reject the entire prior comparison even if plugin counts were correct.

entries.mistake: Like, Save and Vote controls remain enabled while their authenticated provider mutation is pending. Rapid taps can send concurrent toggles or votes for the same post, allowing response ordering or a vote conflict to overwrite truthful UI state.
entries.rootCause: Publish has an explicit busy/idempotency owner, but `_runSocialInteraction` has no per-post in-flight ownership and the card controls do not project pending state.
entries.prevention: Own one in-flight interaction per post in SharedSession, reject a second programmatic request without transport, notify listeners before and after the operation, disable Like/Save/all choices while pending, and test one transport call plus server-acknowledged final state.

entries.mistake: The first bounded Chat audit referenced the nonexistent path apps/mobile/lib/navigation/journey_router.dart. Ripgrep reported a path error after returning partial Chat results, so the combined query could not establish the release route owner.
entries.rootCause: The Journey router location was reconstructed from a conventional navigation directory instead of discovered from the current repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Discover route-owner files with rg --files before bounded content queries, use the exact returned path, and reject every combined ripgrep result that contains a path error even if other files produced matches.

entries.mistake: The path-rejection registration step attempted to read config/codex-regression-memory.json, which does not exist. This repeated the permanent class of guessing the regression registry filename.
entries.rootCause: The canonical filename was shortened from memory instead of located through repository file inventory despite prior registry-path regression entries.
entries.prevention: Never reconstruct the registry filename. Locate it with rg --files, use config/codex-development-regression-registry.json exactly, and run scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 before the next mutation.

entries.mistake: ChatSession.retry removed a failed message and its stored retry key before calling send. When Chat was already busy, send returned false without transport, so the failed message disappeared and its retry state was lost.
entries.rootCause: The retry transition performed destructive local-state preparation before checking the session-wide write lock, while the failed-message Retry control remained enabled during a pending write.
entries.prevention: Reject retry before any local mutation when Chat is busy, disable the message Retry control for the same interval, preserve the failed message and idempotency identity, and test that a busy retry makes no additional gateway call.

entries.mistake: The Chat retry focused verification command was launched with timeout_ms=1000. It completed formatting and was then terminated before the regression-memory check or Flutter tests could complete, repeating the REG-1721 command-timeout class.
entries.rootCause: Shell command runtime was again confused with an early-yield control despite the permanent rule requiring a realistic timeout for Flutter work.
entries.prevention: Assign Flutter test commands a realistic execution timeout, use normal tool yielding for progress, reject the timed-out run completely, confirm an explicit empty orphan-process inventory, and perform only one fresh durable logged retry.

entries.mistake: The post-test release registrant verifier counted `.registerWith(` occurrences and reported zero plugins after config-only generation. Current GeneratedPluginRegistrant.java contains one registerWith method and one `flutterEngine.getPlugins().add(new ...)` statement for each plugin.
entries.rootCause: The plugin-count regex was reconstructed without inspecting the current generated Java call shape.
entries.prevention: Count exact `flutterEngine.getPlugins().add(new` statements for the 15 release plugins, separately prove IntegrationTestPlugin absent, and do not repeat config generation when only the readback predicate was wrong.

entries.mistake: The corrected plugin readback guessed the preserved C30S AAB filename as moolsocial-r60.44-c30s.aab. The actual artifact path stored in the C30S machine state is MoolSocial-1.0.0-r60.44-2026081244-release.aab, so the combined verification failed after the plugin checks passed.
entries.rootCause: A release artifact filename was inferred from the ticket/evidence name instead of read from the durable predecessor buildResult.artifactPath field.
entries.prevention: Resolve preserved artifacts only from the predecessor machine state, compare the exact stored byte length and SHA-256, and reject any combined readback that includes a missing guessed path.

entries.mistake: The Create poll-expiry audit filtered backend filenames for social.*content or content.*social. No filename matched, ripgrep exit 1 aborted the command, and only partial mobile-model output was returned.
entries.rootCause: Provider ownership was inferred from filename conventions rather than discovered through exact operation and schema symbols in the proven backend source root.
entries.prevention: Locate backend owners by exact operation/schema symbols, normalize optional filename-filter exit 1, read only returned exact files, and reject the partial combined result.

entries.mistake: The operation-based backend-owner retry embedded a mixed-quote regular expression in a PowerShell double-quoted command. PowerShell interpreted an intended regex alternation bar as an empty shell pipe and rejected the command before any search ran.
entries.rootCause: Known fixed operation names were unnecessarily composed into one cross-language regex containing quote literals and shell-significant characters.
entries.prevention: Run separate simple fixed-string ripgrep searches for known backend operations, avoid mixed quote-literal regexes inside PowerShell command strings, and register parser rejection before retry.

entries.mistake: The backend discovery passed a quote-containing `case feed` pattern using backslash as if it escaped a PowerShell double quote. Ripgrep received a malformed argument, treated feed\ as a filesystem path, and exited 2.
entries.rootCause: Shell escaping rules from another language were applied to PowerShell despite the audit not requiring a quote-literal pattern.
entries.prevention: Search simple exact symbols without embedded quotes, never use backslash as a PowerShell quote escape, and reject all ripgrep exit-2 output before retry.

entries.mistake: The Social tab-key lookup included the nonexistent conventional filename social_v2_widgets.dart. Ripgrep emitted a path error after other files returned useful partial matches.
entries.rootCause: A supporting widget filename was guessed instead of using the exact component import already present in social_v2_consumer.dart.
entries.prevention: Use imported exact component paths or rg --files inventory before querying supporting widgets, and reject combined results containing any path error.

entries.mistake: SocialCreateWorkbenchV2 owns every unfinished Create field only inside its conditionally mounted widget State. Switching to Feed, Home or Shorts disposes that State and returning to Create silently loses the caption, format, media, choices and Quiz answer.
entries.rootCause: The real Create workbench replaced prototype routes without moving draft ownership above the consumer's tab switch boundary.
entries.prevention: Own one complete in-memory draft at the Social consumer lifetime, bind every workbench mount to it, preserve all five approved MoolSocial-hosted formats and their fields, clear only after authoritative publish success, and test navigation away and back.

entries.mistake: The first Create draft-controller implementation used one broad apply_patch across distant regions. A recovered-media context block did not exactly match the current user-owned dirty file, and the patch was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: A multi-region change relied on recalled rather than freshly bounded exact context for every hunk.
entries.prevention: Patch the dirty file in small independently verifiable exact-context regions, inspect after each group, and preserve the atomic rejection as no implementation progress.

entries.mistake: The first draft-retention widget test tried to tap screen04-rail-feed while the full-screen Create composer was open. The composer intentionally hides the local rail and exposes screen04-create-close, so the test failed with zero matching rail widgets.
entries.rootCause: The test used the underlying Social tab model instead of the controls actually visible in the full-screen composer presentation.
entries.prevention: Test the visible journey through Create close, Feed state and Feed Create-a-post action; never assume controls outside a full-screen composer remain mounted or visible.

entries.mistake: The visible-path draft-retention test closed to Feed and tapped the authenticated Create-a-post CTA using an Owners fixture whose JourneySession had not been started signed in. The app correctly entered sign-in, so the workbench did not immediately remount.
entries.rootCause: The test inferred authentication from a populated email field and a direct initial Create subaction rather than an explicit ready authenticated JourneySession.
entries.prevention: Any Create-author test crossing an authentication-owned CTA must start a ready JourneySession with ReviewOtpGateway signedIn true and a completed setup snapshot before mounting the consumer.

entries.mistake: The authenticated draft-test fixture passed a guessed nonexistent completedSetupExperienceVersion parameter to JourneySnapshot and then accessed a nullable constructor argument shadowing the initialized non-null journey field.
entries.rootCause: The fixture API and initializer scope were edited from memory instead of copying the proven minimal C30T snapshot shape and explicitly referring to this.journey.
entries.prevention: Use the proven JourneySnapshot parameters from c30t_social_auth_and_feed_gateway_test.dart, use this.journey after nullable-field initialization, and require targeted static analysis before the widget retry.

entries.mistake: The Feed Create CTA and creation gateway authenticate guests, but the Social local Create rail calls _selectChoice directly and mounts the Create workbench without sign-in. Authentication is discovered only later through a failed publish.
entries.rootCause: Authentication ownership was added to explicit Create CTAs but not centralized at the shared local-action selection boundary.
entries.prevention: Gate the local Create choice before changing tabs, start real sign-in with exact /app/social?sub=create return, keep the workbench unmounted for guests, and test signed-in navigation remains direct.

entries.mistake: The first YouTube inventory queried the nonexistent apps/mobile/lib/features/youtube directory. Ripgrep emitted a path error after partial Social UI matches, and the combined output was truncated.
entries.rootCause: The YouTube runtime location was reconstructed from a conventional feature directory instead of discovered from current repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Discover YouTube owners with rg --files apps/mobile/lib, use the exact core/youtube and Social UI paths returned, reject partial path-error output, and prove active router ownership before classifying similarly named screens.

entries.mistake: A bounded YouTube source inventory supplied apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/social/social_v2_youtube* as a literal path to ripgrep on Windows. Ripgrep returned OS error 123 after producing partial, truncated matches.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style wildcard was placed in the path operand instead of using discovered explicit paths or ripgrep include globs.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files to discover exact files, pass explicit LiteralPath-safe operands, or use --glob only for filename filtering; reject all partial output from a command that exits nonzero.

entries.mistake: A source-read command combined seven YouTube line ranges and exceeded the tool output budget, leaving middle ranges truncated even though the command exited successfully.
entries.rootCause: The individual ranges were bounded, but their aggregate output was not budgeted as one tool response.
entries.prevention: Read one behavioral owner or one compact line range per command and do not classify any omitted middle range from a truncated response.

entries.mistake: A combined format-and-test command ran from apps/mobile but passed apps/mobile-prefixed paths to dart format. Formatting rejected both paths while the later Flutter test succeeded and made the compound command exit zero.
entries.rootCause: The working directory and path operands were composed independently, and sequential command exit status masked the earlier format failure.
entries.prevention: When the working directory is apps/mobile, pass lib/... and test/... paths; run formatting as a separately checked command before accepting test evidence.

entries.mistake: The first post-format catalogue-continuity test invocation used personal-mvp in the filename instead of the repository's personal_mvp spelling, so Flutter rejected the nonexistent path before loading tests.
entries.rootCause: The known test path was retyped instead of reused verbatim from the successful inventory and format command.
entries.prevention: Copy the exact rg-discovered test path without normalizing separators in filenames and require Flutter to report named test execution before accepting evidence.

entries.mistake: A multi-file YouTube ticket patch expected conventional trailing-comma formatting in the C30T gate defect list, while the current dirty-tree owner used leading commas. Apply-patch rejected the entire operation atomically.
entries.rootCause: The patch context was reconstructed from parsed JSON output instead of copied from the exact current file text.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current text immediately before editing dirty shared state, preserve its existing formatting, and split machine-state, registry, ticket and documentation updates into atomic file-specific patches.

entries.mistake: Overlapping YouTube catalogue refreshes had no request-generation ownership, so an older Videos/Shorts response could complete last and overwrite a newer successful retry and its snapshot cache.
entries.rootCause: Search already used request generations, but the paired public Videos/Shorts catalogue loader applied every completion unconditionally.
entries.prevention: Assign each paired catalogue load a monotonically increasing request generation, ignore stale completions before cache or widget mutation, and prove newer results survive older late completions.

entries.mistake: A valid video-watch route with a fresh cached provider record initialized with no active video and waited for the network refresh; a slow or failed refresh left the user on YouTube Home despite the usable cached item.
entries.rootCause: The catalogue cache was mapped before initial rendering, but active-video resolution occurred only in the asynchronous refresh completion path and used that request's mapped response rather than the retained catalogue.
entries.prevention: Resolve the initial video-watch item from the fresh cache synchronously and resolve refresh results from the retained authoritative catalogue so an offline refresh cannot discard a valid watch route.

entries.mistake: A preserved-C30S-AAB integrity check guessed candidate.aabPath in the prior machine state. The missing property became null, Join-Path resolved it to the repository directory, and Get-FileHash rejected that directory path.
entries.rootCause: The machine-state schema was accessed from memory instead of enumerating its exact current properties before path resolution.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact C30S candidate/artifact property names, require a nonempty file path and Test-Path -PathType Leaf, then compare bytes and SHA-256 to the sealed expected values.

entries.mistake: Multiple lifecycle-driven YouTube connection refreshes could complete out of order, allowing an older disconnected or error result to replace a newer connected channel status.
entries.rootCause: The connection screen refreshed on init, app resume, disconnect and callback state without a request-generation owner.
entries.prevention: Assign each connection refresh a monotonically increasing generation and reject stale success or error completions before mutating connection state.

entries.mistake: The connection screen derived its error from an immutable failed callback query on every refresh, so the old failure could reappear after the user explicitly retried or the lifecycle resumed.
entries.rootCause: A route input representing one callback event was treated as durable provider state rather than a one-time notice owned by the current widget State.
entries.prevention: Consume the failure once after the authoritative refresh, clear it when connection begins, and re-arm it only when didUpdateWidget receives a newly changed failed callback result.

entries.mistake: SharedSession cleared its active Feed cursor before a refresh request completed. If refresh failed while cached posts and hasMore remained, the next Load more request used a null cursor and silently requested page one again.
entries.rootCause: Refresh request input and committed successful pagination state shared the same mutable cursor field.
entries.prevention: Pass null as the refresh request cursor without changing committed state; update cursor and hasMore only from a successful authoritative page, and prove pagination resumes from the preserved cursor after failure.

entries.mistake: Like, Save and Vote stored an offline/provider failure only in SharedSession.errorMessage, but the active Feed surface did not render that shared field, so the control merely re-enabled with no user-visible outcome.
entries.rootCause: The Social interaction state machine was shared with generic app flows, while the published-content card had no per-post failure ownership or completion feedback.
entries.prevention: Retain exact interaction errors by post, await the authoritative boolean result in the card, show the per-post failure when false, and leave all provider-owned post state unchanged.

entries.mistake: Repost was rendered as an enabled Feed action but only wrote an internal unsupported-action error that the Feed never displayed, making the tap appear inert.
entries.rootCause: Unsupported state was recorded below the UI without a visible local response at the action owner.
entries.prevention: Keep Repost non-mutating and display an exact not-available/nothing-changed message from the visible action until a separately authorized backend journey exists.

entries.mistake: A multi-file Feed retry patch accidentally placed a test-context line under the social_v2_consumer.dart patch section. Apply-patch could not find that line and rejected the operation atomically.
entries.rootCause: Session, UI and test edits were composed in one patch without closing the UI hunk before introducing the test context.
entries.prevention: Apply one owner file per patch for cross-layer Feed changes, verify each succeeds, then add tests in a separate patch with exact current context.

entries.mistake: The visible cached Feed retry always called loadSocialFeed(refresh: true). After a Load more failure, retry discarded the failed operation and restarted at page one instead of resuming the preserved later-page cursor.
entries.rootCause: The session retained cursor and error but not the request mode that produced the error; the UI guessed refresh for every cached failure.
entries.prevention: Retain refresh-versus-load-more for the last failed request, expose retrySocialFeed to repeat it exactly, disable visible retry while loading, and prove cursor reuse after a later-page failure.

entries.mistake: A bounded qualifier-test discovery command passed unverified root-level test and tests directories to rg, so the inventory command exited without useful output.
entries.rootCause: The search roots were guessed instead of being derived from the repository's existing directory inventory.
entries.prevention: Inventory repository paths first and search only verified roots or the exact scripts directory; treat an empty rg result separately from an invalid-path failure.

entries.mistake: A multi-file qualifier coverage patch expected the final consolidated finding paragraph as one physical line even though the current file wraps it across two lines, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: Patch context was copied from rendered prose rather than the exact current file tail, and too many owner files were grouped in one operation.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current tail and patch each ticket, finding, gate, consolidated evidence and registry owner separately with tight literal context.

entries.mistake: The C30T pre-AAB qualifier omitted the read-only YouTube connection regression, Hosting/App Links static tests, Hosting public source and most newly created C30T defect tickets from its comprehensive two-cycle ownership.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier's focused test and source manifests were created before later continuous-audit corrections and relied on a partial hardcoded ticket list.
entries.prevention: Run the connection and Hosting static suites, dynamically inventory all C30T defect tickets, fingerprint all Hosting public source and record exact Hosting pass markers and evidence hashes before pre-AAB qualification can pass.

entries.mistake: A second shared Feed item route arriving while the first item was paginating returned behind a boolean resolving guard; the older completion could promote its card and finish without resolving the newest route.
entries.rootCause: Shared-link resolution had mutual exclusion but no request generation or deferred restart owner for route updates.
entries.prevention: Assign a generation to every requested shared item, reject stale completion before UI state changes, restart the newest request when a superseded owner releases the resolver, and prove it with delayed-page route replacement.

entries.mistake: A successful YouTube Shorts refresh could reduce the catalogue below the current page index; every remaining Short then rendered inactive and the official player disappeared from the visible page.
entries.rootCause: Catalogue replacement updated the list but did not reconcile the active page or PageController against the new bounds.
entries.prevention: Clamp the active Shorts page whenever a successful catalogue replaces the list, restore the controller after render, and test a later-page three-to-one refresh.

entries.mistake: A read-only Create audit passed apps/mobile/test/*create*test.dart as a literal rg path on Windows; that search leg failed because the wildcard was not expanded.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style path wildcard was used instead of rg's --glob option from an exact verified directory.
entries.prevention: Use the verified apps/mobile/test directory with --glob '*create*test.dart', or enumerate exact files before searching; never pass a wildcard as a Windows literal path.

entries.mistake: A read-only Create/backend audit included the guessed file backend/functions/src/socialContent.ts alongside the valid source directory; the nonexistent exact file made rg exit non-clean.
entries.rootCause: A likely historical filename was supplied without first proving it existed in the current backend tree.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files on backend/functions/src first and search only verified files or the exact backend/functions/src/social directory.

entries.mistake: SharedSession caught only SocialContentGatewayException, allowing unexpected Firebase plugin, platform or decoding exceptions to escape Feed, publish and interaction futures without a retained-state customer recovery.
entries.rootCause: The typed gateway contract was treated as exhaustive even though SDK and platform boundaries can still throw untyped exceptions.
entries.prevention: Contain untyped exceptions at the Shared Social UI boundary, preserve cached Feed/draft/post state, emit fixed non-sensitive retry copy, and test Feed, publish and interaction failures together.

entries.mistake: ChatThreadScreen loaded only in initState, so a router-reused State with a new thread ID omitted the new message load while the old asynchronous callback still owned mark-read timing.
entries.rootCause: The screen had no didUpdateWidget path or request/thread/session generation checks across its asynchronous load sequence.
entries.prevention: Reload on thread or session change, validate request/session/thread after each await, mark read only after current successful loading, and test a late old response after route replacement.

entries.mistake: A late message-load failure from an old Chat thread wrote the global session error and could display its banner on a newer successfully loaded conversation.
entries.rootCause: Message-list errors used the same global owner as inbox and send errors despite concurrent per-thread loading.
entries.prevention: Store and clear message-load errors by thread ID, render only the current thread's error, keep private exception details sanitized, and test a late old-thread failure after route replacement.

entries.mistake: A Create picker-failure test patch guessed the fake picker's exact tail formatting, so apply_patch could not find the expected typed const line and rejected the whole patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: The test insertion and helper class were grouped before reading the current formatted tail of the file.
entries.prevention: Read the exact test insertion point and helper tail, then patch the widget test and fake picker as separate owner hunks with current literal context.

entries.mistake: The Create picker-failure widget test mounted SocialCreateWorkbenchV2 directly under MaterialApp, so its ScaffoldMessenger message helper asserted because the production Scaffold owner was absent.
entries.rootCause: The isolated harness omitted the Scaffold that always surrounds the workbench in the real Social screen.
entries.prevention: Wrap the isolated workbench in a production-equivalent Scaffold before testing SnackBar recovery copy, and restore the release registrant immediately after any failed Flutter test.

entries.mistake: Create's native image, carousel, image-poll, reel and lost-data recovery calls had busy-state cleanup but no exception containment, allowing plugin/platform failures to escape the UI future.
entries.rootCause: Picker cancellation was handled as a null or empty result, but exceptional native completion was treated as impossible.
entries.prevention: Catch unexpected failures at every media-picker boundary, retain the complete draft, always release selection busy state, show fixed retry copy without private detail, and test caption retention after a failing native call.

entries.mistake: The first explicit Create tool-route test assumed SocialCreateWorkbenchV2 would receive didUpdateWidget, but the parent's content key included _createView and remounted the child before that lifecycle method could run.
entries.rootCause: The lifecycle audit inspected the workbench but did not first trace the keyed parent boundary that owns child State identity.
entries.prevention: Trace ancestor keys before choosing a child lifecycle correction, keep the Create workbench key stable across in-place tool intents, retain a distinct key across actual tab changes, and restore release configuration after any failed Flutter run.

entries.mistake: An explicit mounted Create tool route changed the parent's keyed subtree, remounted the workbench and then ignored the new intent because the retained draft was already initialized.
entries.rootCause: The parent key conflated in-place Create tool state with actual Social tab identity, while the child consumed route intent only during fresh initialization.
entries.prevention: Keep the workbench key stable across tool routes, consume changed explicit intents in didUpdateWidget, preserve all draft fields, retain distinct tab keys, and test Text-to-Quiz route replacement plus Feed round-trip retention.

entries.mistake: The first combined C30T release-readiness audit invocation used a one-second shell timeout even though its Gradle task registration check requires longer, so the parent command timed out after JSON validation before reporting the gate result.
entries.rootCause: The orchestration timeout was sized for a quick static parser rather than the readiness script's bounded Gradle configuration work.
entries.prevention: Inspect and reconcile any surviving child process, preserve the partial log as rejected evidence, and run release readiness with a bounded timeout of at least two minutes while continuing concise progress updates.

entries.mistake: The first controlled readiness retry still passed a one-second timeout to the shell tool despite the prevention rule requiring at least two minutes, so it repeated the parent timeout before the gate could report.
entries.rootCause: The intended timeout change was described in reasoning but not reflected in the actual shell tool parameter.
entries.prevention: Before another readiness invocation, explicitly set and review timeout_ms at 180000, use a fresh log path, confirm no orphaned check process remains, and reject both short-timeout logs as evidence.

entries.mistake: The first Chat inbox route-continuity patch grouped source, test, ticket and aggregate edits while guessing the aggregate defect-ticket tail, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: The aggregate JSON had changed after the earlier inspection and its exact current insertion context was not reread immediately before patching.
entries.prevention: Read each current owner immediately before mutation and apply source, test, ticket/document and aggregate-list changes as separate patches with exact literal contexts.

entries.mistake: The production Chat inbox applied filter and start-recipient route inputs only during initState, allowing a reused inbox to ignore the newest recipient or navigate from an older late direct-thread completion.
entries.rootCause: The route-owned load/create/navigation chain had neither didUpdateWidget handling nor request-generation ownership across its asynchronous boundaries.
entries.prevention: Reapply changed session, filter, recipient and return inputs; serialize overlapping route work; drain to the newest request; validate route identity after every await; and prove a late old recipient cannot navigate.

entries.mistake: A read-only Chat test search passed wildcard path components directly to rg on Windows, which rejected the paths before searching.
entries.rootCause: Shell wildcard syntax was used where rg requires a concrete root plus --glob filters on Windows.
entries.prevention: Search from the concrete apps/mobile/test root and express filename selection only through rg --glob options.

entries.mistake: The first per-thread Chat feedback clear helper combined two map removals with short-circuit OR, so an existing error could prevent the notice removal expression from running.
entries.rootCause: A boolean change-detection expression was allowed to control side-effect execution order.
entries.prevention: Perform each state-removal side effect in its own statement, then combine the captured booleans only for notification control and cover clear behavior in the focused suite.

entries.mistake: A reused Chat thread screen shared one text controller and global send feedback across recipients, so an old send completion could expose or clear the current recipient's draft and show the wrong result banner.
entries.rootCause: Composer text and send completion state were owned at the shared screen/session level rather than by the exact thread and submitted text identity.
entries.prevention: Retain text drafts by thread, clear only the exact submitted draft for its owning thread, own send success/error feedback by thread, render only current-thread feedback, and test a delayed old completion after route reuse.

entries.mistake: A late media-picker result could attach to a different active Create tool, and the shared publish mapping could include that hidden media with a text post, poll or quiz.
entries.rootCause: Picker futures had no request generation or visible format/tool owner, while publication treated the shared media draft as valid for nearly every content type.
entries.prevention: Give every picker request generation and visible-owner checks, invalidate pending work on route/tool changes, disable publish while current selection is pending, and derive publish media only from the active visible media owner.

entries.mistake: The Social Account sheet exposed an in-memory Creator workspace and legacy locally simulated YouTube connection path that could imply distribution or upload capability outside the declared reviewer use case.
entries.rootCause: A broad prototype Creator entry remained reachable from the production Social account surface after the read-only YouTube connection received its own real provider-backed route.
entries.prevention: Expose only the provider-backed minimum-read-only connection, disconnect and Google-permissions route from Social; keep upload false on every production route; and test that the Social account contains no Creator workspace claim.

entries.mistake: An aggregate evidence patch guessed a wrapped consolidated-findings paragraph as exact context and was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: Rendered line wrapping from a prior tail read was reconstructed instead of using an exact append anchor from the file.
entries.prevention: Patch ticket, finding, consolidated evidence and registry as independent owners; use an exact disk-read final line for append-only consolidated findings.

entries.mistake: Feed and YouTube link actions awaited the platform clipboard directly, so an unavailable clipboard escaped the asynchronous UI callback without reviewer recovery guidance.
entries.rootCause: Only successful clipboard delivery was modeled and tested at the public Feed and official YouTube link boundaries.
entries.prevention: Contain clipboard failures at both UI boundaries, retain the owning journey, show only fixed sanitized retry copy, prohibit false success, and test exact success plus injected failure for each link surface.

entries.mistake: A read-only player audit command found the real core/youtube files but tried to open a guessed integrations/youtube path.
entries.rootCause: The follow-up read path was reconstructed from memory instead of copied from the search result.
entries.prevention: Open only exact paths returned by rg and split discovery from content reads when component placement is uncertain.

entries.mistake: A Chat audit repeated the known Windows mistake of embedding chat_* in the path passed to rg.
entries.rootCause: The prior permanent regression rule was not applied when expanding the read-only search command.
entries.prevention: Always pass the concrete apps/mobile/test root to rg and express file selection only with -g 'chat_*.dart'.

entries.mistake: An aggregate Chat patch applied a chat_flow_test context block under the global-navigation test owner and was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: Two test-file edits were composed in one patch without preserving their distinct file anchors.
entries.prevention: Patch ChatSession, ChatThreadScreen, navigation tests and flow tests independently using exact neighborhoods read from each file.

entries.mistake: Three stateful Flutter test files were passed together and the navigation suite lost its Mool finder across corrected and unrelated cases under concurrent scheduling.
entries.rootCause: A combined invocation was treated as serial even though Flutter schedules test files concurrently by default.
entries.prevention: Run the exact corrected contract first and run the complete navigation, production Chat and Chat flow suites with --concurrency=1 before accepting evidence.

entries.mistake: The C05 failures were initially attributed to parallel test-file interference before inspecting the first failure and the helper key.
entries.rootCause: A plausible harness explanation was accepted before a serial rerun and exact source inspection established the stale mool-root-selected key.
entries.prevention: Inspect the first failure and exact helper implementation before assigning root cause, and use the smallest serial reproduction to confirm or falsify harness hypotheses.

entries.mistake: The retired launcher key was blanket-replaced with the compact key even though Shared routes render the standalone home launcher.
entries.rootCause: Two valid Mool navigation variants were treated as one uniform widget key.
entries.prevention: Use mool-compact-launcher for compact Chat and mool-home-launcher for standalone Shared routes, based on exact source ownership.

entries.mistake: The first C05 contract correction updated launcher keys but retained the retired expectation that Mool navigates to personal-mool-root-v2.
entries.rootCause: Only the failed finder line was updated before tracing the current launcher's complete connected-navigator behavior.
entries.prevention: Test the full current contract: owner-specific launcher opens mool-connected-action-navigator, system Back closes it, and the exact owner remains.

entries.mistake: A negative rg assertion correctly found no dormant Chat symbols but its exit code 1 was allowed to mark the entire verification command failed.
entries.rootCause: The shell command treated all nonzero rg statuses alike instead of distinguishing no match from a search error.
entries.prevention: For negative searches, explicitly accept rg exit 1 as pass, preserve exit 0 as a defect match, and reject only search errors above 1.

entries.mistake: A permanent navigation test still required retired reply and attachment previews while ChatSession retained dormant global composer state and a legacy attachment label falsely behaved as if provider content could open.
entries.rootCause: The production Chat surface was reduced to text-only without reconciling its permanent continuity contract and all underlying prototype state and label behavior.
entries.prevention: Retain only real per-thread text drafts, keep retired controls absent, render unbacked legacy labels as non-interactive references, and run current Mool overlay/Back plus production Chat suites serially.

entries.mistake: The official-player Try again action reselected the failed video instead of consuming the one permitted provider retry, appeared for terminal failures, and lifecycle pause delivery could escape asynchronously.
entries.rootCause: Presentation reduced all failed snapshots to one boolean and bypassed the controller's explicit retryability and retry-budget contract; lifecycle pause assumed an infallible native channel.
entries.prevention: Derive retry visibility from snapshot.failure.retryable, invoke retryPlayerFailureFromUser exactly, keep terminal states on provider recovery only, and detach/release the shared lease if lifecycle pause delivery fails.

entries.mistake: A successful Create request unconditionally cleared the workbench even when the creator had entered newer text or changed format while the older upload was pending.
entries.rootCause: Publication completion owned the mutable current composer rather than the exact submitted draft and session identity.
entries.prevention: Fingerprint the exact visible submitted draft, clear only an unchanged match, persist newer state, reject completion UI ownership after a session change, and prove durability after remount with a delayed gateway.

entries.mistake: A dense PowerShell evidence command combined restoration, nested interpolation, hashes and artifact reads and exited without diagnostic output.
entries.rootCause: Too many verification boundaries were composed into one interpolated command, obscuring the parse or runtime failure point.
entries.prevention: Run release restoration, registrar checks, evidence hashes and preserved artifact reads as separate simple commands and accept only explicit output.

entries.mistake: Poll and quiz UI invented a constant seven-day closing claim and remained interactive after expiry, while the Firestore transaction accepted late votes.
entries.rootCause: The provider closesAt field was decoded but not used as an interaction boundary in either presentation or transactional enforcement.
entries.prevention: Derive UI closure state from closesAt, invent no deadline when absent, disable expired choices, and check the authoritative instant inside the vote transaction before update or set.

entries.mistake: A reconciliation command printed the full unbounded git status of the known huge dirty production tree.
entries.rootCause: Branch and HEAD checks were composed with an unnecessary full path listing despite permanent regression memory requiring bounded output.
entries.prevention: Use scoped status for exact owners or transform full status directly into a count/hash without emitting individual paths.

entries.mistake: The first async-lifecycle registration patch assumed trailing-comma formatting and rejected against the machine state's valid leading-comma array style.
entries.rootCause: A multi-file patch was composed from parsed values and partial search output instead of inspecting the exact raw patch context first.
entries.prevention: Inspect exact raw lines before patching preserved machine JSON and split registration patches so an unrelated context mismatch cannot reject every new evidence file.

entries.mistake: One Chat start-route continuation and four Create picker failure continuations referenced BuildContext after an async gap without a direct mounted guard.
entries.rootCause: Mounted state was hidden inside owner-validation helpers, leaving lifecycle safety implicit at context-using call sites and failing static verification.
entries.prevention: After every asynchronous boundary, guard context use directly with mounted in addition to request, session, format and tool ownership checks; require a clean analyzer before release readiness.

entries.mistake: REG-1810 used a PowerShell command label in its gates array, causing the regression-memory checker to treat it as missing repository evidence.
entries.rootCause: The registry's gates field was treated as descriptive metadata instead of its enforced repository-path contract.
entries.prevention: Use only existing repository-relative files in registry gates and evidence arrays, then run the regression-memory checker immediately after every new entry.

entries.mistake: The first evidence-path schema repair corrected REG-1810 but missed the same command-label error in newly added REG-1809.
entries.rootCause: The repair was scoped only to the first reported failing entry rather than auditing every registry entry added in the same change set.
entries.prevention: After a schema-class failure, inspect and validate the complete newly added registry set before rerunning the machine gate.

entries.mistake: A registry-path preflight used an interpolated variable immediately followed by a colon and failed PowerShell parsing.
entries.rootCause: The command used an ambiguous interpolated string instead of a delimiter-safe format expression.
entries.prevention: Use the PowerShell format operator for composite diagnostic values containing colons after variables.

entries.mistake: Explicit Feed loading and unavailable wrappers could lose their progress or retry controls when independently loaded content made the status card conditional.
entries.rootCause: The status owner keyed the outer route state independently but decided whether to build the inner state card solely from content emptiness.
entries.prevention: Explicit loading, error and unavailable states must own their complete fail-closed status UI; cached-content refresh recovery remains a separate runtime state with focused and expanded regression coverage.

entries.mistake: A successful silent TypeScript compile left no Tee-Object pipeline item, so the expected compile log was absent when evidence hashing ran.
entries.rootCause: The evidence command assumed Tee-Object always creates its destination even when the upstream tool emits zero output.
entries.prevention: Pre-create evidence logs for commands that may succeed silently, then tee output into that file and hash it only after exit and existence checks.

entries.mistake: The C30T post-implementation lock check reproduced the pre-existing shared customer-copy test hash mismatch already documented by C29R and C30C.
entries.rootCause: Later Social customer-copy coverage shares a file that the older immutable Screen 03 lock hashes in full; C30T neither created nor owns the mismatch.
entries.prevention: Preserve the observed shared-test hash byte-for-byte, do not edit immutable Screens 01-03 or their lock, run C30T gates separately, and require separate founder reference authority for reconciliation.

entries.mistake: A registry search again passed wildcard path arguments directly to rg on Windows and those targets were rejected.
entries.rootCause: The permanent Windows rule to search literal directories with --glob filters was not applied to a multi-owner evidence lookup.
entries.prevention: Use only literal existing directory arguments with rg on Windows and express filename selection through --glob; never pass shell-style wildcard paths.

entries.mistake: A supplemental GeneratedPluginRegistrant count reported zero because Java call parentheses were not escaped in the Select-String regular expression.
entries.rootCause: A source literal containing regex metacharacters was passed as a regex without escaping even though the result was being used as an exact release count.
entries.prevention: Escape punctuation for exact source-call regexes or use SimpleMatch; require the supplemental count to agree with the authoritative release-readiness gate.

entries.mistake: The Android package-list name filter returned both com.moolsocial.app and com.moolsocial.app.test, making the unfiltered installer result ambiguous.
entries.rootCause: The cmd package list argument was treated as an exact package lookup even though it performs substring filtering.
entries.prevention: Filter package-list output to the exact literal package record before accepting installer identity; never infer from the first or combined result.

entries.mistake: The optional complete mobile suite exposed 301 failures after 1,314 passes and 36 skips; treating the aggregate as one defect or rerunning it without grouping would be invalid.
entries.rootCause: The repository-wide inventory contains many owners beyond the focused C30T release set, including legacy, golden, environment and unrelated domain contracts with different prerequisites.
entries.prevention: Group failures by exact file and failure class, isolate only in-scope Social groups, require reproducibility before source changes, and preserve unrelated failures without silently expanding C30T scope.

entries.mistake: The first exhaustive-failure grouping command used invalid comma placement with Sort-Object -Descending and failed parsing.
entries.rootCause: A multi-key mixed-direction sort was written using shorthand that PowerShell does not support.
entries.prevention: Use explicit calculated Sort-Object properties whenever sort keys require different directions.

entries.mistake: A supplemental test-file classifier treated repository-relative rg --files output as absolute and repeatedly failed Substring prefix removal.
entries.rootCause: The path shape returned by rg was assumed instead of inspected before normalization.
entries.prevention: Retain repository-relative rg --files results unchanged, or resolve each path explicitly before absolute-prefix operations; reject partial classifier output after any exception.

entries.mistake: A corrected classifier repeated REG-1813 by interpolating a variable immediately before a colon inside a wildcard string.
entries.rootCause: The permanent format-operator prevention was not replayed while composing the new -like pattern.
entries.prevention: Use the format operator for every composite PowerShell pattern containing punctuation adjacent to a variable; never use variable-colon interpolation.

entries.mistake: The first upload-reachability source test selected an end marker that occurs before the start marker and would have thrown a range error.
entries.rootCause: The end marker was chosen semantically without checking its literal order in the current large Social source file.
entries.prevention: Inspect source order and use the immediate next owner declaration as the end marker before running any substring-based source gate.

entries.mistake: A reviewer-control audit combined a source-file read with a broad multi-directory search and exceeded the available output context, repeating the earlier multirange-output truncation class.
entries.rootCause: The permanent bounded-output prevention from REG-1754 was not replayed before composing the combined privacy, deletion, revocation and permissions audit command.
entries.prevention: Inspect one small source range or one exact symbol set per command, scope searches to one owner at a time, and reject every truncated result instead of inferring values from it.

entries.mistake: The first bounded reviewer-control source read used an abbreviated presentation path from working notes that does not exist in the current repository.
entries.rootCause: The exact current owner path was assumed rather than resolved from the workspace before the read.
entries.prevention: Resolve the exact repository-relative owner with rg --files and an exact filename filter before every bounded source read whose full path is not already evidenced.

entries.mistake: The first local Hosting lookup assumed root-level firebase.json, .firebaserc and hosting paths and suppressed the diagnostic stream, producing no auditable result.
entries.rootCause: Hosting ownership paths were guessed and missing-path diagnostics were discarded before the repository layout was resolved.
entries.prevention: Resolve Firebase configuration files with rg --files first, inspect their declared public directories, and never suppress lookup diagnostics used as release evidence.

entries.mistake: A supplemental official-Google search query containing nested quoted phrases was rejected by the orchestration parser before execution.
entries.rootCause: The query text used unnecessary nested quote syntax in a JavaScript tool call.
entries.prevention: Use plain unquoted search phrases in tool-call strings, and exclude every parser-rejected query from evidence instead of retrying when accepted authoritative guidance is already sufficient.
