entries.mistake: A YouTube attribution search passed Unix-style social_v2* and youtube* path wildcards to rg on Windows, repeating the registered invalid-wildcard class and rejecting two test scopes.
entries.rootCause: The permanent resolved-file-list prevention from REG-1817 was not replayed when adding test owners to the search.
entries.prevention: Resolve candidate test files with rg --files and filter their paths before content search; never pass wildcard path operands to rg on Windows.

entries.mistake: A pre-AAB machine-state summary selected ticketId/buildConsumed/uploadConsumed/installConsumed and related top-level properties that are not present in the current C30T state schema, yielding only nulls.
entries.rootCause: Property names from an earlier gate shape were assumed instead of inspecting the current JSON schema before summarizing authority.
entries.prevention: Parse the current state and inspect its exact top-level and nested property names before selecting counters or authority flags; reject all-null summaries.

entries.mistake: The C30T static release-readiness gate found 16 generated Android registrants where the qualified release contract requires exactly 15.
entries.rootCause: Flutter test/analyze tooling regenerated the dev-only IntegrationTestPlugin after an earlier release config-only restore; the final workflow did not independently verify the registrant after every Flutter tooling phase.
entries.prevention: End source qualification with release config-only plus restore-release-generated-plugin-registrant-c30t.ps1, require the same verifier after build-wrapper config-only and before authority consumption, and prove exactly 15 allowed classes with IntegrationTestPlugin absent.

entries.mistake: The registrant-classification command mixed the real apps/mobile/.flutter-plugins-dependencies path with a nonexistent repository-root metadata path and suppressed the missing-path diagnostic, causing a nonzero exit despite useful partial matches.
entries.rootCause: An unverified alternate metadata location was added to the exact owner query and diagnostics were redirected away.
entries.prevention: Resolve the single existing Flutter plugin metadata path first, query only that literal file, retain diagnostics, and reject the combined command status as qualification evidence.

entries.mistake: The first registrant-resolution consolidation patch used root-cause and prevention sentences that did not exactly match the current registry entry, so apply_patch rejected the entire multi-file patch.
entries.rootCause: The update was composed from working-memory paraphrase instead of re-reading the exact stored REG-1831 text.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current registry slice before patching existing long string fields; confirm the prior multi-file patch applied nothing before retrying with exact context.

entries.mistake: The first attribution exact-destination source test forbade the generic YouTube Home URI across the entire Social consumer file, rejecting the legitimate separate Home launcher.
entries.rootCause: The assertion was applied to the whole source owner rather than the bounded _YouTubeAttribution class whose fallback was removed.
entries.prevention: Extract the exact _YouTubeAttribution class between verified adjacent declarations and assert generic-home absence only inside that class while retaining separate Home-launch coverage.

entries.mistake: After the focused test failed and analyzer execution was intentionally skipped, the combined command still tried to tail the nonexistent analyzer log and produced a secondary missing-path diagnostic.
entries.rootCause: Execution was conditional but the human-readable log-tail step was not guarded by Test-Path.
entries.prevention: Guard every conditionally created evidence log with Test-Path before reading it and report the skipped phase explicitly.

entries.mistake: The first local extractor for the qualifier-owned focused-test array guessed a following variable name and failed to find the manifest block before any tests ran.
entries.rootCause: A fragile trailing assignment marker was invented rather than resolving the PowerShell array AST or exact current closing boundary.
entries.prevention: Parse the PowerShell AST and select the focusedTests assignment expression, or inspect the exact current line boundary before a bounded textual extraction; reject empty manifests.

entries.mistake: The first AST-based focused-manifest extractor omitted the closing parenthesis in its inline Test-Path if guard and was rejected by the PowerShell parser.
entries.rootCause: A dense one-line nested condition was composed without a parser precheck.
entries.prevention: Use a multiline resolved-path guard with balanced parentheses and parse or visually verify the command before execution; treat parser rejection as no manifest evidence.

entries.mistake: The combined pre-AAB handoff patch produced tool output that exceeded the available model context, leaving the mutation result indeterminate.
entries.rootCause: Two substantial new files were submitted in one patch without first bounding the expected tool response and without an immediate per-file postcondition check.
entries.prevention: Reject a truncated patch result as evidence, inspect each exact target read-only, use one small file patch at a time for any repair, and validate JSON or bounded content after every mutation.

entries.mistake: The first REG-1838 insertion patch used an incorrect end-of-array context and apply_patch rejected it without changing the registry.
entries.rootCause: The JSON object terminator and array terminator were represented as two adjacent object braces instead of the exact stored closing boundary.
entries.prevention: Read the exact final registry slice immediately before appending and anchor the insertion to the unique prior evidence line plus the verified object terminator.

entries.mistake: The executable authority-precedence search included a guessed check-play-internal-aab-gate-c30t.ps1 path that does not exist, causing a nonzero command exit despite valid matches in the other exact files.
entries.rootCause: The gate filename was inferred from naming convention instead of being resolved from the repository script inventory.
entries.prevention: Enumerate the exact C30T script paths with rg --files before a multi-owner bounded search and pass only verified literal paths to rg.

entries.mistake: A YouTube player source search passed wildcard filenames as Windows path arguments, so rg returned invalid-path diagnostics and a nonzero exit after printing partial matches.
entries.rootCause: The already registered Windows rg wildcard prohibition was not applied to the test-file owner arguments.
entries.prevention: Pass existing directory roots only and express filename selection with rg --glob; reject partial output from a command that reports invalid path syntax.

entries.mistake: The fixture-fallback audit included an assumed apps/mobile/lib/features/shared/social_content_models.dart owner that does not exist, making the otherwise useful search exit nonzero.
entries.rootCause: A model filename was inferred instead of being resolved from the shared-feature file inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve exact owners with rg --files before a multi-file audit; search verified directories when the specific model filename is not known.

entries.mistake: The first declared-use-case reachability search combined broad mobile and backend mutation/analytics terms and produced truncated output, so the result could not prove complete reachability boundaries.
entries.rootCause: Multiple large owner trees and high-frequency analytics terms were queried in one command without per-owner output bounds.
entries.prevention: Audit the router, candidate feature flags, mobile client and deployed provider dispatcher in separate exact-owner queries; reject truncated search output as completeness evidence.

entries.mistake: The bounded YouTube upload-route audit included assumed youtube_private_dev_contract.dart and journey_routes.dart filenames that do not exist, causing a nonzero exit after valid router and screen matches.
entries.rootCause: Contract and route owners were inferred from class naming instead of resolved from the exact mobile file inventory.
entries.prevention: List exact core/youtube and journey01 owner paths first, then query only verified files; retain the verified route/screen evidence but reject the command as complete cross-owner proof.

entries.mistake: The first internal Creator-route reachability query used a mixed quote-class regex inside PowerShell and returned no output with exit code 1, including for known Creator copy.
entries.rootCause: Shell and regex quote semantics were combined unnecessarily in one expression, making the intended literal search ambiguous.
entries.prevention: Use separate rg -F fixed-string searches for each route and customer-copy marker and verify expected known markers are found before drawing a reachability conclusion.

entries.mistake: The fixed-string Creator-route test search chained required and optional rg queries; positive route evidence printed, but a later no-match query made the overall command exit 1.
entries.rootCause: Required-presence searches and optional-absence searches shared one unguarded command status.
entries.prevention: Run required and optional queries separately, assert required results, and explicitly interpret exit 1 as no matches only for a bounded optional query with no diagnostics.

entries.mistake: The required/optional sequential rg exit-status mistake recurred while searching for Creator containment tests; known matches printed, then a later no-match returned exit 1.
entries.rootCause: The newly registered per-query status rule was not applied before composing the next related search.
entries.prevention: Stop chaining optional searches; resolve one exact test owner and add or inspect one bounded source-level contract there.

entries.mistake: After the exact Creator-entry source test passed, a broad shared_vertical_slice_test.dart suite was appended as focused evidence and failed on its unrelated historical mool-root-chat expectation.
entries.rootCause: The selected suite mixed the changed shared-model owner with older universal-dock contracts rather than isolating the exact shared route behavior.
entries.prevention: Use the qualifier-owned exact source contract plus a test selected by precise plain-name ownership; classify unrelated historical navigation failures separately before retrying or changing runtime.

entries.mistake: A third related diagnostic again chained an optional fixed-string query; valid mool-root-chat and mool-global-chat ownership printed, then the absent mool-compact-chat query returned exit 1.
entries.rootCause: The no-chained-optional-query prevention was not followed during immediate failure classification.
entries.prevention: Do not append optional rg queries at all; use one command per required marker and omit unneeded synonym searches once exact current and retired owners are established.

entries.mistake: The retired mool-root-chat key in the shared account journey was directly replaced with mool-global-chat, but that current global control is not mounted on the final shared account screen and the exact retry failed.
entries.rootCause: Current ownership was inferred from the global navigation component without proving that the shared account route embeds that component at the test's final state.
entries.prevention: Revert the unproven edit, inspect the exact shared screen and router owner at the final route, and migrate the journey only to a control actually mounted there or remove the obsolete cross-owner assertion with explicit contract evidence.

entries.mistake: The qualifier-coverage audit again chained fixed-string queries; present screen04 and Chat owners printed, while absent shared owners made the combined command exit 1.
entries.rootCause: Individual optional membership checks were used after repeated no-chain prevention records instead of reading the qualifier array and source inventory structurally once.
entries.prevention: Parse the PowerShell AST for the focusedTests array and inspect the source relativePaths assembly in one verified owner read; report membership from that structured result only.

entries.mistake: The successful 57-file focused regression command tailed 45 verbose expanded-reporter lines, and the tool presentation truncated that tail even though the full evidence log persisted and exit code was 0.
entries.rootCause: A verbose test reporter and oversized tail were returned through the direct tool output channel.
entries.prevention: Persist the complete log, return only the final summary line plus hash and byte count, and inspect any failure by exact test name rather than a large tail.

entries.mistake: The final reconciliation combined nested JSON gates, device state, preserved artifact identity and provider revision reads in one command, causing the tool response to exceed its output budget and truncate.
entries.rootCause: Several individually bounded checks were composed into one oversized result instead of persisting verbose gates and reporting only compact phase summaries.
entries.prevention: Run each reconciliation phase separately; redirect verbose gate output to immutable evidence logs and return only pass state, hash and count; return only regex-derived device fields and one compact line per provider revision; reject the truncated combined result in full.

entries.mistake: The new reconciliation regression entry named a guessed C30T readiness-script path that did not exist, so the regression-memory checker correctly rejected the registry before verification could continue.
entries.rootCause: The gate owner was inferred from descriptive wording instead of enumerating the exact C30T script filenames before writing the registry entry.
entries.prevention: Enumerate exact repository-owned C30T script filenames before adding any registry gate path, validate every new evidence and gate path structurally, and retain the failed memory-gate log.

entries.mistake: After correcting the readiness script, the memory checker exposed a second guessed path in the same reconciliation entry: config/apk-regression-gate-state-c30t.json does not exist.
entries.rootCause: A historical APK-state naming convention was inferred instead of inventorying the exact C30T gate-state files before the registry mutation.
entries.prevention: Inventory exact C30T config filenames before recording machine-state evidence, validate all new registry paths as one bounded structural check, and preserve every failed memory-gate log.

entries.mistake: The bounded OPPO reconciliation attempted cmd package get-install-source, but this device build does not implement that package-manager command and returned Unknown command.
entries.rootCause: Command availability was assumed from newer Android package-manager shells instead of using the already compatible installer query for the connected CPH2375.
entries.prevention: Use adb shell pm list packages -i with the exact package on this OPPO, parse only the bounded installer field, and never treat an unsupported read-only command as device evidence.

entries.mistake: The OPPO-compatible pm list packages -i query returned installer=null for com.moolsocial.app even though the exact dumpsys package record reports installerPackageName=com.android.vending.
entries.rootCause: The compact package-list installer projection is lossy on this device build and cannot be treated as the authoritative install-source field.
entries.prevention: Derive the installer only from the exact installerPackageName field in the package-specific dumpsys record, return only that matched line, and reject pm list packages -i null as non-authoritative.

entries.mistake: The bounded Cloud Run reconciliation attempted to describe all four exact revisions in an assumed asia-south1 region and suppressed the native diagnostic; the first revision read failed.
entries.rootCause: The current deployment region was inferred rather than derived from durable repository evidence or a bounded project revision inventory before the exact describe calls.
entries.prevention: Derive the exact region first, retain command diagnostics on failure, then describe one exact revision at a time and return only revision, service, region and Ready status.

entries.mistake: The first Cloud Run describe failure was attributed to an assumed region while stderr was suppressed; the bounded retry with diagnostics showed the actual immediate blocker was expired gcloud authentication requiring interactive reauthentication.
entries.rootCause: The native diagnostic was hidden on the first read, allowing an unproven region explanation to be stated before the exact error was retained.
entries.prevention: Never suppress provider-read stderr on a failed command; classify the exact diagnostic before assigning cause; never attempt interactive login, password or MFA without the founder visibly present.

entries.mistake: After the Cloud CLI reauthentication blocker, the read-only browser fallback assumed browser.tabs.open existed; the connected browser API rejected that method.
entries.rootCause: A tab-opening method was inferred without consulting the exact connected browser documentation in the current runtime.
entries.prevention: Read and follow the complete connected-browser documentation before any further browser method call, reuse existing tab bindings when possible, and never guess browser-client APIs.

entries.mistake: The Chrome browser fallback listed open tabs before assigning the required task-specific browser session name.
entries.rootCause: The existing browser binding was reused before its complete current documentation had been read and applied.
entries.prevention: For every Chrome browser task, call browser.nameSession with a bounded task name before opening, claiming, navigating or inspecting tabs, then follow only documented methods.

entries.mistake: The read-only browser fallback navigated to an inferred /run/revisions Cloud Console route, which rendered URL not found; the selected Chrome account was also supermanditech@gmail.com and had no selected Dev project.
entries.rootCause: A console route was guessed instead of using the visible Cloud Run Services navigation, and authentication identity was verified only after navigation.
entries.prevention: Verify the visible signed-in account and project access first, use the console's visible Services navigation rather than guessed route variants, and never restore IAM solely to bypass a read-only reconciliation blocker.

entries.mistake: The in-app browser open-tab inventory was printed verbatim and exposed a transient Cloud Console reauthentication query value in tool output.
entries.rootCause: The raw BrowserUserTabInfo object was emitted instead of matching it internally and returning only a redacted host/path summary.
entries.prevention: Never emit full authenticated console URLs or query strings; match tab metadata internally, redact all query components before any output, do not copy or persist transient values, and use the claimed tab without reading cookies or session storage.

entries.mistake: The in-app browser reconciliation assumed a button aria-label beginning Account would be available on the claimed Cloud Credentials page; the exact selector timed out.
entries.rootCause: A Chrome Console header selector was assumed to be identical on the in-app browser page without first obtaining safe redacted locator ground truth.
entries.prevention: Do not fall back to broad authenticated DOM capture after an account selector fails; retain only the visible project signal, defer the provider revision read to founder-visible CLI reauthentication, and emit no authenticated query strings.

entries.mistake: After successful gcloud reauthentication, the deployment preflight attempted a Firebase CLI app inventory before proving the separate Firebase CLI session was current; Firebase rejected its expired credentials.
entries.rootCause: The local gcloud and Firebase CLI authentication stores were treated as if one successful Google account reauthentication refreshed both tools.
entries.prevention: Before any Firebase preflight or deployment, independently run a bounded Firebase read and, when it reports expired credentials, require founder-visible firebase login --reauth; never infer Firebase readiness from gcloud auth state.

entries.mistake: The provider-only control validation was invoked before fingerprinting the ignored Firebase runtime file; it failed because the preserved file enables public data only and is not the accepted public-data-plus-readonly-connect review profile.
entries.rootCause: The older C30M helper's existing-runtime contract was assumed to match the current C30T accepted review profile without first comparing its exact safe capability flags.
entries.prevention: Before any provider validation or deployment, fingerprint the ignored runtime, prove it contains no forbidden secret names, preserve its exact bytes in memory, temporarily materialize the accepted review profile only for Firebase deployment, and restore the original bytes and hash in a finally block.

entries.mistake: The combined deployment-authorization patch expected an older aggregate-state line shape and was rejected in full by apply_patch verification.
entries.rootCause: The current JSON used a leading-comma property style that was not re-read immediately before composing a multi-file patch.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current target line immediately before state mutation, apply registry/evidence additions separately from aggregate-state updates, and verify that a rejected patch made no partial changes.

entries.mistake: The compact Cloud Run service read did not execute because a diagnostic string used $s: and PowerShell parsed the colon as part of an invalid variable reference.
entries.rootCause: A loop variable adjacent to punctuation was interpolated without braces in an inline PowerShell command.
entries.prevention: Use ${s} or format-string arguments whenever a PowerShell variable is adjacent to a colon, and retain parser failures as no-execution evidence before retrying.

entries.mistake: The Cloud preflight exposed that apps/mobile/test/ui_v2_customer_copy_machine_gate_test.dart no longer matches the immutable login-account-handoff approved-lock checksum, so the deployment gate cannot pass yet.
entries.rootCause: The shared customer-copy test changed somewhere in the bounded dirty tree without the immutable approved-lock relationship being reconciled before the environment deployment preflight.
entries.prevention: Classify the exact diff and ownership before any deployment retry; do not edit an immutable accepted manifest, do not revert user-owned work, and require the approved UI lock to pass through an authorized non-presentational correction or a separately founder-approved immutable checkpoint cycle.

entries.mistake: The moved Social customer-copy test passed a size named argument copied from the protected test, but the destination Social test's existing _mount helper has no named parameters and already fixes the viewport to 390 by 844.
entries.rootCause: The test body was moved before the destination helper signature was inspected.
entries.prevention: Read the exact destination helper contract before moving test cases, reuse its existing fixed viewport without extra arguments, and preserve the failed compile log before retrying.

entries.mistake: After restoring the first protected test, check-approved-ui-locks exposed a second checksum mismatch in apps/mobile/test/platform_configuration_test.dart.
entries.rootCause: Release-platform assertions were added to another test file shared with the immutable Screens 01–03 checkpoint without isolating successor coverage before deployment preflight.
entries.prevention: Classify and move only the successor platform assertions into a C30T-owned test, restore the protected file to its exact accepted checksum, and repeat the approved UI lock until every protected owner passes without modifying its manifest.

entries.mistake: The immutable checksum lookup searched the entire large dirty repository and timed out before returning a result.
entries.rootCause: The search scope included artifacts and thousands of unrelated tracked/untracked files instead of the approved-reference manifest and lock-script owners.
entries.prevention: Inspect approved-references/manifest.json and scripts/check-approved-ui-locks.ps1 first, then search only the exact referenced immutable evidence directory if needed.

entries.mistake: After authentication and protected locks passed, the YouTube Cloud preflight rejected the current Firebase Functions ignore list as different from its exact sealed inventory.
entries.rootCause: The Functions deployment ignore list evolved during later release/provider work while the older private-Dev preflight retained its prior exact set.
entries.prevention: Compare the current and expected arrays structurally, prove every added exclusion is test-only or review-corpus-only and no required runtime file is hidden, then update only the preflight expectation and its focused control test under C30T authority.

entries.mistake: After the ignore-list reconciliation, the older YouTube preflight rejected the current Functions source because it assumes both and only the provider exports occupy the inspected option set, while the shared provider codebase now also owns separately gated Social and Chat functions.
entries.rootCause: A preflight written before the shared codebase gained Social/Chat exports still reasons about the current index as a two-function package instead of validating the YouTube exports by exact names and deploy target.
entries.prevention: Inventory all current exported functions structurally, assert youtubeProvider and youtubeOAuthCallback independently remain in asia-south1, and keep the authorized Firebase deploy target exactly functions:provider:youtubeProvider.

entries.mistake: A requested preflight source excerpt unexpectedly produced an oversized, truncated tool result, so the returned text could not be treated as complete evidence.
entries.rootCause: The formatted source-range command was not bounded tightly enough for the unusually large dirty-workspace output environment.
entries.prevention: Inspect only exact Select-String matches or source windows of at most 20 lines, reject every truncated result, and use structural assertions instead of broad source dumps.

entries.mistake: The mandatory full git status command emitted thousands of dirty paths and the tool truncated the displayed result.
entries.rootCause: The repository has a very large founder-owned dirty tree, and the branch reconciliation command combined the required status with an unbounded path listing.
entries.prevention: Run the mandatory branch/status reconciliation once, preserve its exit and branch evidence, then use porcelain counts and exact C30T path filters for subsequent checks without reprinting or rescanning the full list.

entries.mistake: The older YouTube preflight rejected the shared Functions source because separately gated Social media code legitimately references Cloud Storage.
entries.rootCause: The no-YouTube-media-proxy assertion scanned every non-test TypeScript file after the Functions codebase gained independent Social and Chat owners.
entries.prevention: Apply the storage-proxy prohibition to the exact YouTube provider/callback export blocks and the YouTube runtime module tree, while leaving Social and Chat outside both the assertion and the authorized deploy target.

entries.mistake: A follow-up search for the Firebase Storage service owner timed out after scanning broad config, docs, deployment, scripts and backend trees.
entries.rootCause: Although narrower than the whole repository, the search still included very large evidence and policy trees despite the exact deployment manifest and preflight already being known owners.
entries.prevention: Inspect only the exact deployment manifest, preflight, current C30T authorization and active backend gate state first; do not broaden to docs or backend trees unless an exact owner remains unresolved.

entries.mistake: The read-only cloud preflight rejected the Dev project because the sealed allowed-service inventory lacked the already enabled Firebase Storage API.
entries.rootCause: The YouTube deployment manifest predated the separately gated Social media backend, which enabled firebasestorage.googleapis.com in the same Dev project.
entries.prevention: Compare live and manifest service names exactly, classify every delta against a separately authorized owner, and add only the confirmed Firebase Storage service without enabling, disabling or otherwise changing any service.

entries.mistake: A bounded source-inspection command placed arithmetic expressions directly inside a PowerShell array expression and failed with an op_Subtraction error.
entries.rootCause: The command constructed @($hit-1,$hit+19,$hit+39), which PowerShell parsed as array operations instead of three scalar offset values.
entries.prevention: Compute each integer offset in its own scalar assignment before building the array, or inspect one fixed source window per command.

entries.mistake: After adding Firebase Storage to allowedEnabledServices, the manifest self-check still failed because preExistingPlatformServices is the second exact owner used to construct the reviewed inventory.
entries.rootCause: The first reconciliation updated only the derived allowed list and missed the source classification list that the preflight independently joins with required provider services.
entries.prevention: When an exact manifest inventory is derived from classified component lists, reconcile the classified source list and the exact aggregate in the same review, then parse and compare both before retrying Cloud preflight.

entries.mistake: A Firebase CLI identity check used login:list with JSON output, which unexpectedly included live OAuth access, refresh and ID token material in the tool output.
entries.rootCause: The command was assumed to return only account identity metadata; Firebase CLI 15.5.1 serializes its stored token object in JSON mode.
entries.prevention: Never invoke firebase login:list with JSON output or any Firebase command that serializes credential state. Verify identity only through redacted human output or authenticated project reads, reject all commands capable of emitting token fields, and require revocation plus fresh interactive authentication after any exposure.

entries.mistake: A combined command ran the full backend, Hosting, deployment-control and cloud preflight gates successfully, but the 551-line console transcript was truncated in its middle.
entries.rootCause: The full 505-test TAP stream and every subsequent gate were emitted through one tool result instead of separate immutable evidence logs with bounded summaries.
entries.prevention: Run each full suite into its own immutable evidence log, verify exit code and SHA-256 independently, and print only bounded final summaries to the interactive console.

entries.mistake: The new provider wrapper falsely reported that the accepted review-mode line was missing even though the common materializer appended it.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper used a multiline end-of-line regex against CRLF content without permitting or normalizing the carriage return before the line anchor.
entries.prevention: Normalize a validation-only copy of generated runtime content from CRLF to LF before exact-line assertions, while preserving the original generated bytes and checksum for deployment materialization.

entries.mistake: The first CRLF correction patch was rejected because a new file-update delimiter appeared inside an unfinished update hunk.
entries.rootCause: The multi-file patch did not close the provider-script hunk with sufficient context before starting the authorization-file hunk.
entries.prevention: Use independently complete hunks with exact surrounding context for each file and treat any patch-parser rejection as zero mutation before retrying.

entries.mistake: The first provider deployment attempt failed before Firebase dry-run because the delegated package gate rejected the current four compiled exports as unexpected.
entries.rootCause: The package gate retained the historic two-export YouTube-only inventory after the shared Functions codebase added separately gated Social and Chat exports; the C30T Validate wrapper did not execute this deeper delegated package path.
entries.prevention: Validate the exact four compiled exports in the package gate, retain the exact provider-only Firebase deploy target, and make the C30T local Validate mode exercise the delegated package gate against a non-writing accepted-runtime validation path before deployment readiness can be sealed.

entries.mistake: A bounded package-gate inspection derived its line window from a missing exact search hit and printed negative line labels instead of the relevant source.
entries.rootCause: The command did not assert that Select-String returned exactly one line number before subtracting the context offset.
entries.prevention: Require exactly one non-null search hit before deriving offsets, or use the already reported fixed failure line with a fixed bounded window.

entries.mistake: The authorized provider deployment succeeded and was verified by its delegated owner, but the outer C30T wrapper then falsely failed because it read the no-invoker-IAM-check annotation from the revision template instead of the Cloud Run service metadata.
entries.rootCause: gcloud run services update --no-invoker-iam-check stores run.googleapis.com/invoker-iam-disabled on service metadata; the wrapper queried spec.template.metadata.annotations.
entries.prevention: Read the exact service-level annotation, require it to equal true, retain the safe capability and revision readbacks, and do not roll back a correctly deployed authorized revision merely because the verifier used the wrong metadata path.

entries.mistake: The final Hosting readback recorded a blank optional version fileCount because the current channel-list response did not expose that field for the new release.
entries.rootCause: The readback treated fileCount as a consistently present channel-list field even though Firebase CLI response enrichment can omit optional version metadata.
entries.prevention: Require the finalized version name, new live release identity, exact local source manifest, successful deployed-route markers and security/App Links checks; record fileCount only when the CLI exposes it and never substitute it for authoritative content verification.

entries.mistake: The first C30T qualification-cycle launch used a short command-host timeout. The host terminated the qualifier before it emitted output, leaving an immutable zero-byte console log and no running qualifier process.
entries.rootCause: A long-running qualification script was launched through a command call whose effective timeout was only a few seconds instead of a durable background process with an explicit PID and completion marker.
entries.prevention: Launch long-running qualification cycles as hidden durable PowerShell processes, capture the exact PID and exit-code marker, poll read-only progress at bounded intervals, and never infer completion from the initiating command host.

entries.mistake: Two bounded read-only audit commands attempted to place a PowerShell if statement directly inside a parenthesized expression, producing command errors instead of the intended inventory output.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc command composition incorrectly treated PowerShell if as an expression in a context where it was parsed as a command name.
entries.prevention: Assign conditional values with a preceding if statement, use a switch or ternary operator only where the active PowerShell version supports it, and prefer simple format strings for audit output.

entries.mistake: After the authorized bounded Dev YouTube provider deployment advanced the qualified revision to youtubeprovider-00038-cic, two C30T pre-AAB gates still required predecessor revision youtubeprovider-00036-qer and rejected qualification before any build.
entries.rootCause: The deployment completion updated both C30T machine-state files and the dynamic qualifier, but did not update the two static provider-revision assertions in the AAB reconcile gate and release-readiness gate.
entries.prevention: All C30T provider-revision assertions must require the exact deployed qualified revision youtubeprovider-00038-cic, while the live qualifier continues to compare Cloud Run readback against machine state. Search every C30T pre-AAB gate for stale predecessor revision literals before retry.

entries.mistake: C30T qualification cycle 1 reached the comprehensive static release-readiness pass but the no-write Dart formatter gate found two C30T source files that were not canonical: the YouTube creator-upload owner and public-runtime test.
entries.rootCause: The final C30T implementation edits were not followed by an exact canonical formatter pass before the sealed qualification cycle began.
entries.prevention: Run Dart formatter only on the two reported files, then rerun the no-write whole-scope formatter gate before restarting qualification. Do not weaken or remove the set-exit-if-changed gate.

entries.mistake: C30T cycle 1 passed focused Flutter, backend, Hosting and provider-control tests but the live safe-flag verifier directly accessed valueFrom on a Cloud Run environment entry whose JSON legitimately contained only a direct value property. StrictMode raised a missing-property error.
entries.rootCause: The verifier assumed ConvertFrom-Json materializes absent optional JSON fields as null-valued PowerShell properties. It does not under StrictMode.
entries.prevention: Inspect PSObject.Properties explicitly. Require exactly one environment entry, require a direct value property, reject any valueFrom property, and compare only the expected non-secret capability value.

entries.mistake: A bounded source audit passed scripts/*c30t*.ps1 as a literal ripgrep path on Windows, producing an invalid-filename error after the useful exact-file search completed.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell did not expand the wildcard path in the ripgrep argument as assumed.
entries.prevention: Pass the directory as the search root and use ripgrep --glob for filename filtering, or enumerate exact literal files before invocation.

entries.mistake: While classifying pending C30T tickets after qualification, a read-only hash command guessed a nested path for the Social customer-copy test that does not exist. The same command still confirmed that the accepted focused manifest contains the actual Social customer-copy gate and C30T release-signing/provenance test.
entries.rootCause: The audit inferred a directory from the test's conceptual owner instead of using the exact filename already sealed in the focused-test manifest.
entries.prevention: Use the accepted focused-test manifest as the exact test-name authority and never guess protected-test paths. Because the permanent regression registry is source-sealed, invalidate and repeat both no-AAB qualification cycles after registering this mistake.

entries.mistake: The new protected-test path-assumption entry cited the future cycle-1 focused-test manifest as a gate before that immutable artifact existed, so regression-memory validation correctly rejected the pre-cycle reconcile.
entries.rootCause: The entry conflated a future result artifact with an already existing executable prevention gate.
entries.prevention: Registry gates must exist when the entry is registered. Cite the existing qualifier as the gate; add the generated manifest only to later completion evidence after it exists, without making current regression-memory validation depend on a future file.

entries.mistake: A resumed read-only reconciliation captured complete NUL-delimited Git status and enumerated all untracked paths internally before printing only scalar counts.
entries.rootCause: The restart audit optimized for counts instead of applying the permanent evidence-heavy-workspace boundary that forbids full untracked inventory.
entries.prevention: Use branch and HEAD scalar reads, tracked-only status, named C30T owner reads and the accepted source manifest; never capture NUL-delimited full status or enumerate the complete untracked evidence tree.

entries.mistake: A read-only dirty-owner summary used a question-mark wildcard with PowerShell like matching, matched tracked and untracked rows, and emitted a truncated listing.
entries.rootCause: The status prefix was treated as literal while using a wildcard operator, and the resulting row set was emitted without a bounded scalar projection.
entries.prevention: Avoid full untracked enumeration; where a bounded classification is necessary, use an anchored literal-safe expression and emit only verified scalar results. Truncated status output is rejected.

entries.mistake: After authoritative C30T release gates passed, an additional read-only regression-memory probe invoked phase build with the nonexistent BuildMode release and was rejected before execution.
entries.rootCause: The auxiliary probe inferred an enum from the release AAB artifact instead of copying the checker's declared none, debug and profile ValidateSet.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the invented enum. Use the existing C30T AAB gate and its declared implementation regression boundary; before any direct checker call, read and copy both exact ValidateSet declarations.

entries.mistake: The first wrapper intended to create three regression evidence files failed JavaScript parsing because Markdown delimiters were embedded unescaped in a template literal, so the patch tool was never called.
entries.rootCause: The composed wrapper was not mechanically checked for language-delimiter collisions before execution.
entries.prevention: Use one independently complete file-local patch per evidence owner through ordinary quoted strings that contain no conflicting template delimiters, and treat wrapper syntax failure as zero mutation.

entries.mistake: After the first restarted C30T qualification cycle passed, a bounded read-only evidence check guessed two artifact filenames that were not the canonical names written by the qualifier.
entries.rootCause: The follow-up inspection relied on summarized labels instead of resolving the qualifier's exact literal output names before issuing the read.
entries.prevention: Before reading C30T qualification evidence, resolve and copy the exact literal artifact names from scripts/qualify-play-internal-live-read-recovery-c30t.ps1; do not infer names from descriptive labels. Because the registry is source-sealed, repeat both no-AAB cycles after registration.

entries.mistake: The next bounded read-only check guessed config/codex-regression-memory.json instead of the repository's canonical config/codex-development-regression-registry.json owner.
entries.rootCause: A summarized concept name was treated as a filesystem path without first resolving the already known prior registry ID.
entries.prevention: Resolve the registry owner with an exact known REG ID and then reuse the returned literal path; never convert conceptual regression-memory labels into guessed filenames.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to append the two new registry entries failed verification and made zero mutation because its patch context did not exactly match the registry tail.
entries.rootCause: The patch used a generic closing-brace anchor instead of the unique final evidence path from the last registered entry.
entries.prevention: For registry-tail changes, anchor the patch on the exact unique evidence path of the current final entry and include the complete closing structure in the reviewed patch.

entries.mistake: A pre-authorization read-only exact-value search included an inferred build wrapper filename that does not exist, causing the search command to return a nonzero status after the canonical gate and launcher had already produced the required matches.
entries.rootCause: The search mixed two known literal owners with a third conceptually named path that had not been resolved from an existing owner.
entries.prevention: Search only canonical named owners already resolved from repository instructions or executable references. Resolve any additional wrapper path from the canonical launcher before including it in a command; never infer a script filename.

entries.mistake: After a new source-sealed regression entry invalidated the prior qualification, the next cycle pair was started without first resetting the non-source-sealed AAB and aggregate owners from the previous pre-AAB-passed state to the continuous-audit build hold. Cycle 2 rejected the state before granting authority or building.
entries.rootCause: The evidence root was advanced for requalification, but the required machine-state reset step was not repeated as part of the same invalidation transaction.
entries.prevention: Whenever a new source-sealed entry invalidates a completed cycle pair, atomically advance the immutable evidence root and reset the AAB owner to founder_authorized_continuous_social_audit_in_progress_build_held plus the aggregate owner to prebuildQualificationPassed false and sourceFingerprint null before cycle 1 starts.

entries.mistake: The first non-source authorization update advanced the source-manifest and cycle evidence paths to the current qualification root but left the focused-test manifest path on the older root. The inconsistency was detected before any build gate or build consumed the record.
entries.rootCause: The authorization evidence bundle was patched field-by-field without an atomic checklist covering source manifest, focused manifest, both cycle files, hashes, counts, and machine state.
entries.prevention: Treat the qualificationResult evidence bundle as one atomic update. Verify all four canonical paths, all four hashes, source and focused counts, and the machine state in one bounded post-patch assertion before activating build authority.

entries.mistake: The first atomic postqualification authorization patch failed verification and made zero mutation because it expected the AAB owner to remain on the pre-cycle continuous-audit hold even though successful cycle 2 had correctly transitioned it to the pre-AAB-passed state.
entries.rootCause: Patch context was prepared from the pre-cycle reset value rather than the qualifier's declared successful cycle-2 transition.
entries.prevention: Postqualification authority patches must anchor the AAB and aggregate owners to pre_aab_audit_passed_founder_aab_authorization_required, while prequalification invalidation patches anchor to the continuous-audit hold. Verify the transition immediately before composing the patch.

entries.mistake: The first visible founder-launcher start attempt was safely stopped by a duplicate-process guard that matched its own current PowerShell command line because the launcher path appeared inside the guard command itself. No launcher, prompt, authority consumption, or build occurred.
entries.rootCause: The process query searched command-line text without excluding the current shell process that was executing the search.
entries.prevention: Founder-launcher duplicate detection must exclude the current process ID before testing command-line containment. Only a distinct existing process may block a new visible launcher start.

entries.mistake: A post-build search for prior release-note evidence used a repository-wide dot scope without excluding tmp and matched an unrelated temporary Chrome Secure Preferences file, causing session-setting metadata to appear in tool output. No credential value was used, copied, persisted or acted upon.
entries.rootCause: The search excluded large build and artifact trees but failed to apply the permanent session-specific-settings boundary to repository-local temporary browser profiles.
entries.prevention: All remaining C30T release reads use exact named durable owners only. Never search repository-local browser profile or session directories; broad dot-scope searches must exclude tmp, browser profiles, Preferences and Secure Preferences. The sealed AAB remains tied to its build-time source manifest and no second build or upload is authorized by this post-build operational entry.

entries.mistake: The first C30T OPPO Play Update tap command parsed the verified Update bounds but added regex capture strings before division, producing concatenated out-of-range coordinates in the tap log. The subsequent Play UI showed Cancel, so no second tap was attempted while an update was in progress.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell regex captures were used directly in arithmetic without casting each capture to an integer before addition, and the center was not asserted against the physical display bounds before input injection.
entries.prevention: For any future bounded device tap, assign left, top, right and bottom to distinct integer variables before arithmetic, calculate the center only from those integers, read the device display size, assert the center lies within both the parsed node and display, then perform at most one tap. Never retry an update tap when Play shows Cancel, Pending or progress.

entries.mistake: The first C30T installed-base signer check used keytool -printcert -jarfile and then required one SHA256 certificate line. The installed Play-delivered APK did not expose a matching line through that JAR-certificate path, so the parser produced a false failure before any signer claim was made.
entries.rootCause: A JAR-oriented certificate inspection command was treated as an authoritative APK v2/v3 signing-certificate verifier without first proving that its output contract applied to the Play-generated split APK.
entries.prevention: Installed Play APK signer qualification must use Android apksigner verify --print-certs from an exact installed build-tools dependency, capture only the signer certificate SHA-256 digest, normalize it, and compare it to the founder-pinned Play app-signing certificate. Never retry the keytool JAR parser for this evidence.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to resolve the exact apksigner dependency assumed android/local.properties existed at the repository root. This repository's Flutter Android owner is nested, so the read failed before apksigner ran.
entries.rootCause: The command used a conventional root-relative Android path without first resolving the app's exact tracked Android owner from named repository files.
entries.prevention: Resolve Android toolchain configuration only from the exact nested MoolSocial Flutter app owner named by repository scripts or bounded tracked-file discovery. Assert the owner exists before reading it, then select an existing apksigner binary. Do not repeat the repository-root android/local.properties assumption.

entries.mistake: After exiting the provider-owned YouTube playback surface with Android Back, the next semantic-tap attempt assumed the Social Shorts rail was present. The fresh pre-tap helper found zero exact Shorts nodes and stopped without tapping.
entries.rootCause: Foreground MainActivity identity was treated as proof of a specific nested Flutter route after a provider WebView/fullscreen Back transition; no fresh post-Back hierarchy had proved the current screen.
entries.prevention: After every provider WebView, system picker, dialog, fullscreen player or system-Back transition, capture and inspect a fresh current UI hierarchy before selecting the next semantic. Activity identity alone never proves the nested route. Retain the zero-match pre-tap XML and do not retry from stale evidence.

entries.mistake: The Play-installed r60.45 YouTube Shorts surface renders its title and channel header through the Android status-bar region, visibly colliding with the clock and status icons on OPPO CPH2375.
entries.rootCause: The release acceptance set did not detect the real-device system-inset collision on the immersive Shorts route before the single authorized AAB was built and published. Exact layout ownership requires successor diagnosis; no source correction is inferred from the screenshot alone.
entries.prevention: A successor candidate must render the Shorts header below the effective top system inset on OPPO 720x1612 at 320 dpi, preserve provider video composition, and add a current-owner real-device or deterministic inset regression before any separately authorized build. r60.45 remains rejected and no second C30T build is authorized.

entries.mistake: A two-gate PowerShell wrapper invoked the regression-memory script and then tested $LASTEXITCODE before invoking the journey gate. Because a PowerShell script does not reliably set a native-process exit code, the condition skipped the second gate while the host command still exited zero.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper repeated a registered native-versus-PowerShell status-channel confusion instead of relying on terminating errors and direct sequential script calls.
entries.prevention: Invoke repository PowerShell gates directly under ErrorActionPreference Stop and let terminating errors stop orchestration. Never inspect $LASTEXITCODE after a PowerShell script; reserve it for the immediately preceding native executable only.

entries.mistake: After one successful exact YouTube channel-status tap, the generic stable-device helper was invoked with its default Open MoolSocial main menu requirement. The intended full-page account route does not expose that rail, so evidence capture false-rejected after its first readiness dump.
entries.rootCause: A helper whose default contract is a global-navigation surface was reused for a nested full-page route without first proving and supplying a route-specific required semantic.
entries.prevention: For nested account, search, picker, dialog and provider routes, use a route-specific capture that proves package, foreground activity and an exact semantic already observed on that route. Never invoke the global-rail capture default merely because MainActivity remains foreground, and never repeat the successful navigation tap after capture-only failure.

entries.mistake: The Play-installed r60.45 YouTube channel surface tells a signed-out user to sign in to MoolSocial again but exposes only Try again. One exact retry returns to the same unavailable state, leaving a content creator with no direct authentication recovery action on the connection route.
entries.rootCause: The release acceptance set proved truthful signed-out copy and retry containment but did not require the channel route itself to offer a reachable MoolSocial authentication handoff before the single AAB was published. Exact source ownership remains to be diagnosed during the authorized successor implementation.
entries.prevention: The successor must provide one explicit MoolSocial sign-in action from the signed-out YouTube channel state, return to the same optional read-only connection route after successful user authentication, preserve privacy/revocation controls before consent, and prove cancel/error/retry/connected/disconnect continuity. No secret input may be automated and no second build is implied.

entries.mistake: A Google sign-in handoff attempt selected its exact semantic from an earlier captured MoolSocial auth hierarchy. The semantic helper's new pre-tap hierarchy found zero matches and stopped, so no account chooser opened.
entries.rootCause: The secure action target was derived from a prior route snapshot rather than first proving the immediately current MoolSocial-owned screen and then acting without an intervening state change.
entries.prevention: Before every authentication or external-consent handoff, inspect a fresh current MoolSocial hierarchy, prove the exact single semantic, and perform the one tap immediately from that same capture. Never inspect or capture the account chooser, password, MFA or consent account identity after handoff; pause for the founder instead.

entries.mistake: The zero-match Google sign-in tap was initially diagnosed as a stale auth screen. Reinspection of the retained pre-tap hierarchy proved the screen and node were current; the raw content-desc contains a line break between the two Google labels, while a diagnostic display had normalized it to a space before that normalized string was supplied to an exact-match helper.
entries.rootCause: Human-readable whitespace-normalized diagnostic output was reused as machine-exact accessibility input, and the resulting exact mismatch was misclassified before the retained raw XML was checked.
entries.prevention: Never derive an exact tap semantic from whitespace-normalized display output. For multiline accessibility labels, retain and pass the exact raw content-desc or select exactly one current node and compute asserted integer bounds from that same hierarchy. Diagnose a zero match from the retained raw XML before assigning route-state cause.

entries.mistake: On Play-installed r60.45, the exact Google sign-in gate returns a YouTube-branded bottom sheet saying sign-in was not completed because the package certificate hash could not be obtained. Try again loops to the same failure, Choose another method only returns to the grid, and the founder reports the YouTube, X, Instagram and Facebook gates also do not proceed.
entries.rootCause: The release authentication owner did not successfully qualify its runtime Android package-certificate hash path under the Google Play app-signing identity, and the error presentation does not preserve the provider selected by the user. Exact shared and provider-specific source causes require bounded diagnosis before implementation.
entries.prevention: The successor must use the installed Play signing identity through a tested Android certificate-hash owner, preserve the exact selected provider in loading/error/retry state, prove Google and every exposed provider gate separately on Play-installed OPPO, and keep email OTP and mobile OTP independently qualified. No account identity, password, MFA, token or OAuth payload may be inspected or automated.

entries.mistake: The r60.45 social sign-in failure sheet visibly renders Choose another method, but its clickable accessibility node exports empty bounds [0,0][0,0]. The recovery can be targeted only visually and has no valid semantic touch geometry.
entries.rootCause: The release auth error-sheet layout did not preserve non-empty semantics bounds for its secondary recovery control, and current release tests did not assert the exported geometry on the real device.
entries.prevention: The successor must export one non-empty clickable Choose another method node of at least 48 logical pixels, preserve reading and focus order after Try again, prove visual and semantic recovery to the provider grid on OPPO, and add a current-owner bounds regression. No second build is implied.

entries.mistake: The founder reports that the Play-installed r60.45 Email OTP gate does not complete authentication from the Social sign-in screen.
entries.rootCause: The release acceptance set did not complete and independently qualify the Email OTP path on the Play-installed candidate before publication. Exact route, request and return ownership requires bounded successor diagnosis.
entries.prevention: The successor must independently prove Email OTP request, invalid input, resend timing, wrong/expired code, success, cancellation and exact requested-route return without inferring success from any social-provider or Mobile OTP path.

entries.mistake: The founder reports that the Play-installed r60.45 Mobile OTP gate does not complete authentication from the Social sign-in screen.
entries.rootCause: The release acceptance set did not complete and independently qualify the Mobile OTP path on the Play-installed candidate before publication. Exact route, request and return ownership requires bounded successor diagnosis.
entries.prevention: The successor must independently prove country/mobile input, OTP request, invalid input, resend timing, wrong/expired code, success, cancellation and exact requested-route return without inferring success from Email OTP or any social-provider path.

entries.mistake: The r60.45 recovery path moves a creator from YouTube channel status into a generic MoolSocial social-provider grid without clearly distinguishing MoolSocial authentication from the later selection of the existing Google account that owns the YouTube channel.
entries.rootCause: The release flow did not preserve the authentication purpose and return destination in customer copy across the YouTube-channel-to-MoolSocial-auth handoff.
entries.prevention: The successor must label the first boundary as MoolSocial sign-in, retain the YouTube channel return destination, then on the connection route explicitly ask the user to choose the existing Google account containing the channel and state the youtube.readonly/no-upload boundary before consent.

entries.mistake: After the founder dismissed the social-provider failure sheet to the MoolSocial provider grid, one Android Back exited MoolSocial and exposed the previously foreground Play Store task instead of returning to the requested Create or originating Social route.
entries.rootCause: The release authentication handoff does not retain a back-stack or explicit cancellation return contract for an auth screen entered from a protected Social destination.
entries.prevention: The successor must preserve the requested post-auth route and origin, handle Android Back as an in-app authentication cancellation, return to the originating Social surface without exiting the app, and add current-owner Google/provider/OTP cancellation continuity tests.

entries.mistake: C30T's two-cycle pre-AAB qualification truthfully proved source, backend, configuration and release-build readiness, but its strong qualification language could be read as comprehensive Social production readiness even though signed-in Play-installed journeys were explicitly still pending. Current-owner tests also failed to pre-detect Shorts system-inset, Play-signer authentication, provider-identity, OTP independence and auth-return defects later exposed on OPPO.
entries.rootCause: Release readiness vocabulary did not sharply separate pre-AAB build readiness, Internal Testing candidate activation, post-install real-user acceptance and final go-live qualification, while automated coverage was treated as deeper assurance than the unexecuted live exploratory matrix could support.
entries.prevention: For every remaining MoolSocial capability through go-live, label each gate by its exact phase; treat tests as necessary but never sufficient; conduct adversarial exploratory real-user testing on the exact Play-installed candidate across signed-out/signed-in, cancel, error, retry, offline, relaunch, system Back, provider/system surfaces and accessibility geometry; register every unexpected issue before continuing; implement only exact authorized tickets; and never claim complete, production-grade, reviewer-ready or go-live-ready until every required live journey passes with zero unresolved blocker.

entries.mistake: After relaunching r60.45 and opening public Feed from the normal Social rail, the screen rendered This shared post is not available even though no shared link was opened during the current session.
entries.rootCause: A retained unavailable shared-post state is not cleared or scoped away from ordinary Feed entry. Exact route/session owner requires successor diagnosis.
entries.prevention: The successor must scope shared-post lookup/error state to the explicit shared-link route, clear it when returning to ordinary Feed, preserve pagination and posts, and prove retained-data relaunch plus normal rail entry contains no stale shared-post banner.

entries.mistake: A read-only foreground diagnostic safely proved topResumedActivity was MoolSocial, then an optional mCurrentFocus search returned no line and the command called Trim on null, producing an avoidable diagnostic exception.
entries.rootCause: An optional Select-String result was dereferenced as though the line were mandatory without materializing and count-checking the match first.
entries.prevention: Materialize every optional dumpsys match as an array, branch on count, and report absent explicitly. Never call a string method on an optional search result. Preserve independently proved foreground output when a secondary optional diagnostic is absent.

entries.mistake: The first multi-action Feed guest-auth harness assigned a saved hierarchy path to $home. PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive, so this attempted to overwrite the protected HOME variable and stopped before opening Feed or tapping any Feed action.
entries.rootCause: A generic route-state variable reused a permanently forbidden system variable name despite the workspace rule requiring task-specific names.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell harness uses task-specific names such as $feedHomeXml and never declares or assigns $HOME, $home or $CODEX_HOME in any case. Preserve the already created pre-action evidence and restart under unused evidence stems.

entries.mistake: The guest Feed action harness classified Save, Message and a quiz choice as not opening the auth grid because it regex-searched raw UIAutomator XML for whitespace between multiline labels. The raw file encodes the line break as an XML entity; parsed clickable nodes prove all eight auth methods were present.
entries.rootCause: An outcome assertion searched serialization syntax rather than parsing the accessibility document and comparing semantic values.
entries.prevention: Every UIAutomator outcome assertion parses XML and compares node text/content-desc values. Never infer multiline semantic absence from a raw serialized whitespace regex. Correct earlier harness booleans from the retained parsed evidence without repeating product taps.

entries.mistake: A read-only evidence inventory emitted existing-file rows with Length and missing-file rows with Missing, then the default mixed-property table visually retained only the Length-oriented columns. The missing page-2 capture names were incorrectly described as 1-byte placeholders even though the files did not exist.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic relied on PowerShell's implicit table projection across heterogeneous objects instead of emitting an explicit uniform Exists, Length and SHA256 schema and validating existence before byte reads.
entries.prevention: Every evidence inventory materializes uniform rows with explicit Exists, Length and SHA256 properties, reports missing files as Exists=false, and reads bytes or hashes only after a positive Test-Path result. Never infer a placeholder from blank cells in an implicit mixed-property table.

entries.mistake: A Feed share-copy harness stopped before action because it required parsed content-desc to equal Share exactly. The current Flutter accessibility nodes were clickable and exposed two semantic lines, Share followed by Share; two visible cards also contributed separate Share nodes.
entries.rootCause: The harness parsed XML correctly but still compared an unnormalized composite semantics value and assumed one page-wide occurrence instead of selecting the intended visible card by exact bounds.
entries.prevention: Normalize parsed semantic values into trimmed lines, match the intended action token as a complete line, retain clickable and enabled requirements, and select the intended visible card using retained bounds and card context. Never relax to a blind coordinate or assume one occurrence across a virtualized Feed viewport.

entries.mistake: A second Feed share-copy harness normalized the Share action but searched for the carousel card context from the previous viewport. Its own preflight scroll had moved the carousel off-screen and exposed two different Asha cards, so the contextual assertion stopped before tapping.
entries.rootCause: The action selector carried forward a product-card identity from an earlier screenshot instead of deriving the current visible card context from the exact hierarchy captured immediately before action.
entries.prevention: After every scroll, parse the new hierarchy and choose an intended current card from that same capture. Bind the action to its current public author and card description, exact enabled/clickable bounds and current foreground before tapping. Never carry a prior viewport's card context across a scroll.

entries.mistake: A grouped pre-implementation read concatenated nine required UI, release, traceability, copy, state, plan and backlog owners. The tool output truncated mid-group, so the group could not prove that every required owner was read completely.
entries.rootCause: The read was bounded by file count but not by aggregate bytes or lines, despite the permanent dense-owner rule requiring small non-overlapping windows whose output cannot truncate.
entries.prevention: Read required owners one file at a time when small and in explicit line-numbered non-overlapping windows when large. Record exact line totals first, reject any truncated window in full, and complete every window through EOF before mutation.

entries.mistake: A single-file 700-line read of ACTIVE-CODEX-HANDOFF.md exceeded the available output context and was truncated, so none of that window could prove the required handoff owner was read.
entries.rootCause: The window was sized from average line density instead of the dense local lines and current output-context limit.
entries.prevention: Read ACTIVE-CODEX-HANDOFF.md in explicit numbered non-overlapping windows of at most 200 lines through its exact measured EOF. Reject any truncated window in full and register a recurrence before reducing the window again.

entries.mistake: A read-only diagnostic guessed three regression-owner paths; the regression memory, registry and preceding incident document guesses were wrong and the read failed without mutation.
entries.rootCause: Durable filenames were reconstructed from memory instead of being resolved from a narrow repository filename inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve required regression-owner paths using a narrow rg --files pattern before reading, then use the exact returned durable paths. Never guess quality-document or registry locations.

entries.mistake: The first Email OTP owner diagnostic included a guessed apps/mobile/lib/features/journey01/review_journey_contracts.dart path that does not exist. The compound read still found the real gateway, session and screen owners, but emitted an inadmissible path error.
entries.rootCause: A plausible contract filename was inferred from neighboring owner names instead of resolving the EmailOtpGateway declaration through a symbol search and reading only returned files.
entries.prevention: For authentication contracts, first run a bounded rg symbol search across an existing verified root, then read only exact returned paths. Do not append a convention-derived contract filename to a grouped read, and treat any missing-path diagnostic as rejected evidence even when the compound command exits zero.

entries.mistake: The first resumed YouTube creator handoff diagnostic used the stale path apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/screens/social_v2/social_v2_youtube_creator_upload.dart. That file does not exist, so the grouped read failed before producing admissible owner evidence.
entries.rootCause: A path retained in compacted conversational context was treated as repository evidence instead of being re-resolved from the current dirty tree.
entries.prevention: After any resume or compaction, resolve UI owner paths with a narrow rg --files filename search before reading. Never treat a summarized or remembered path as verified current-tree evidence, and register any missing-path failure before retrying.

entries.mistake: The first YouTube handoff focused suite omitted ui_v2_social_continuous_batch_test.dart. The authoritative 59-file manifest then found its channel-status test constructed a signed-in gateway but never started JourneySession, leaving the UI actor signed out while asserting the old direct-route behavior.
entries.rootCause: The narrow suite covered the dedicated channel-state owner but did not include the accepted focused manifest's second channel-status consumer. The older test relied on a gateway fixture as though it were already reconciled session state.
entries.prevention: For a changed Social action contract, intersect exact symbol matches with the accepted focused-test manifest before declaring the narrow suite complete. Every test claiming a signed-in actor must explicitly start and assert JourneySession authentication before the action; a signed-in gateway fixture alone is not authenticated UI state.

entries.mistake: A post-focused qualification lookup guessed hosting/package.json while trying to recover the existing Hosting test command. That path does not exist, so the grouped diagnostic was rejected before any test retry.
entries.rootCause: The Hosting test owner was inferred from a conventional package layout instead of being resolved from the current repository file and script inventory, recurring after the path-guess prevention rule was already active.
entries.prevention: Never infer package roots for qualification. Resolve package.json and Hosting gate files with narrow rg --files queries, then read or invoke only exact returned paths. A prior successful qualification summary is not a substitute for current-tree path evidence.

entries.mistake: The final no-change format audit invoked dart format on the entire apps/mobile directory. Dart traversed a stale generated build/firebase_remote_config transform path that disappeared during listing and aborted before a valid format result.
entries.rootCause: The format scope included generated build and tool directories even though only owned Dart source and test roots were required.
entries.prevention: Run the no-change Dart format audit only against exact owned roots such as lib, test and explicitly verified local package Dart directories. Never aim dart format at an application root containing volatile build output.

entries.mistake: The first search for the founder-reported Feed Like-to-Play defect ran optional ripgrep queries in a grouped diagnostic. A normal no-match exit code of 1 rejected the whole group and discarded otherwise independent search output.
entries.rootCause: The harness treated ripgrep's distinct no-match status as a command failure and did not emit an explicit zero-match result per query.
entries.prevention: Every optional ripgrep discovery query captures output and exit code independently, accepts only 0 or 1, emits an explicit zero-match marker for 1, and fails only for exit codes above 1. Never place unclassified optional rg calls in a fail-fast grouped diagnostic.

entries.mistake: The first Shorts sealing patch correctly began with the ticket JSON update but then placed the findings-document appendix before declaring a docs file update section. apply_patch rejected the entire patch before writing.
entries.rootCause: Two file mutations were composed in one patch without an explicit file-boundary header between the JSON and Markdown hunks.
entries.prevention: For sealing state and narrative evidence, use separate apply_patch calls per file or verify that every hunk is preceded by its exact file header. Treat a rejected patch as zero mutation and register it before retrying.

entries.mistake: After the laptop restart, the first reconciliation command grouped the root AGENTS owner, repository AGENTS owner, Git identity and the full dirty-tree status. Its output exceeded the tool context and was truncated, so none of the grouped output was admissible proof of the required owner reads or exact repository state.
entries.rootCause: The resume diagnostic repeated a known aggregate-output mistake by combining dense policy owners and an intentionally huge dirty-tree inventory instead of bounding each output independently.
entries.prevention: After every restart or compaction, read each required AGENTS owner separately. Measure dense owners first and read them in numbered non-overlapping windows of at most 200 lines through EOF. Reconcile branch, HEAD and dirty ownership with separate bounded commands and persist a full machine-readable status artifact only when its owner authorizes that evidence write.

entries.mistake: The first bounded dirty-tree reconciliation captured `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` in a PowerShell variable and treated the result as an array of NUL-separated records. PowerShell exposed the captured stream as one string, producing the false count of one dirty entry.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic assumed native NUL delimiters survive PowerShell command capture as enumerable record boundaries without an explicit raw-byte parser.
entries.prevention: For bounded dirty-tree reconciliation in PowerShell, use line-delimited porcelain output when filenames are not printed, validate every status line with the two-column porcelain prefix, and compute the evidence hash over a deterministic UTF-8 line join. Use a dedicated raw-stream byte owner before relying on `-z`; never infer record count from PowerShell's captured object count.

entries.mistake: The line-delimited dirty-tree retry parsed the status records correctly but allowed Git's large set of long-path scan warnings to share the tool output. The warning stream exceeded the output limit and truncated the command, so its displayed counts and hash were rejected in full.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic bounded stdout content but did not enable Git long-path handling or capture and classify stderr independently before reporting the compact summary.
entries.prevention: Run dirty-tree reconciliation with per-command `core.longpaths=true`, capture stderr to a workspace-local temporary file, and admit the result only when the Git exit code is zero and the captured warning/error file is empty. Print only compact validated counts and the deterministic hash, then remove the temporary diagnostic file after its exact workspace path is verified.

entries.mistake: The next Git status retry planned to redirect stdout and stderr to repository-local temporary files and remove them in a validated finally block. The shell command was rejected by policy before execution because it contained a destructive cleanup operation.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic introduced avoidable temporary filesystem state and cleanup even though the compact reconciliation can capture native process stdout and stderr separately in memory.
entries.prevention: Use `System.Diagnostics.Process` with redirected standard output and standard error, read both streams asynchronously in memory, and create no temporary files. Admit the summary only when the process exits zero, stderr is empty, porcelain records validate and output remains bounded to the compact summary.

entries.mistake: The first required-owner metric inventory attempted to pipe directly from a PowerShell `foreach` statement to `Format-Table` without wrapping the statement as an expression. PowerShell rejected the command with an empty-pipe-element parser error before reading the owners.
entries.rootCause: The compact diagnostic was written with pipeline syntax valid for cmdlet output but invalid for that statement form in the current PowerShell parser.
