entries.prevention: Collect bounded metric rows into an explicit `$results` array inside `foreach`, then pipe only that array to formatting. Treat parser errors as zero evidence and register them before any corrected owner inventory.

entries.mistake: The Feed action audit treated the manifest's relative `screens/04-universal-social-feed-create/v2` root as though it were located directly under the screenbook repository root. The resulting read-only existence check returned false.
entries.rootCause: A manifest-relative approved-reference root was joined to an inferred repository layout instead of resolving the exact file from the authorized screenbook filename inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve approved HTML interaction contracts with a narrow `rg --files` search inside the exact authorized screenbook root, then read only the returned path. Never convert a manifest-relative root into a filesystem path by convention.

entries.mistake: The prior-repair replay invoked the regression-memory gate and then placed `flutter test` later in the same PowerShell command. The gate script terminates its host with `exit`, so the process ended after the gate pass and none of the requested Flutter tests ran.
entries.rootCause: A machine-gate script that owns process exit was treated as a normal returning function in a compound command.
entries.prevention: Run each potentially exiting PowerShell gate in its own shell command. Start tests and any later gates in separate tool processes, and admit a test result only when the output contains the test runner's own completion line and exit code.

entries.mistake: The first Repost/Share Chat-context search included guessed paths `apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/chat/chat_v2.dart` and `apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/universal/universal_v2.dart`. Neither exists, so the grouped search and all otherwise returned matches were rejected.
entries.rootCause: Likely Chat and Universal filenames were inferred from feature naming instead of resolving exact current-tree owners before the symbol search.
entries.prevention: Run a narrow `rg --files apps/mobile/lib` inventory for Chat and Universal filenames first, then search symbols only in exact returned paths plus an independently verified router path. Treat any rg path error as rejection even if a pipeline masks its native exit status.

entries.mistake: A verification read requested roughly 190 dense lines from `social_v2_public_content.dart`. The tool output was truncated, so the result could not prove that the partially inserted quoted-post widget remained at a valid top-level Dart location.
entries.rootCause: The source window followed the general 200-line upper bound even though dense Flutter widget code and the compacted task context required a smaller output budget.
entries.prevention: Inspect dense Dart source only through exact, non-overlapping windows of at most 100 lines. Treat any truncated read as zero verification evidence and register it before retrying with smaller windows.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to register regression 1953 combined registry, memory and incident-document edits. Its memory hunk expected the phrase `its native exit code`, while the current owner says `the native exit code`, so the entire patch was rejected with zero changes.
entries.rootCause: A compound multi-owner patch reused a nearly matching remembered sentence instead of the exact current local context already visible in the owner tail.
entries.prevention: Patch each regression owner independently using exact freshly read context. Treat a rejected patch as zero mutation, confirm owner state, register the rejection, and only then retry.

entries.mistake: A grouped implementation-owner search included the guessed path `apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/social/social_v2_screen.dart`, which does not exist. The grouped search exited nonzero, so all otherwise displayed matches were rejected.
entries.rootCause: The Social consumer filename was inferred from the feature name instead of resolving it from the authorized current-tree filename inventory.
entries.prevention: Resolve every Social implementation owner through a narrow `rg --files apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/social` inventory before symbol search. Search only verified returned paths and reject any grouped result containing a path error.

entries.mistake: The first focused Flutter run was started after the search had already revealed an assertion requiring `Repost is not available yet`. That retired expectation predictably failed once Repost used the shared server-backed interaction path.
entries.rootCause: The known obsolete assertion was inspected but not updated before executing the focused suite, producing an avoidable red run.
entries.prevention: When an implementation intentionally replaces a retired behavior, update the exact authoritative focused assertion and add the successor positive/negative contract before the first test run. Never run a suite with a known stale expectation.

entries.mistake: The first backend Social test symbol search passed `backend/functions/src/social/*.test.ts` as a literal Windows path. Ripgrep rejected the path with OS error 123, so the grouped output was discarded.
entries.rootCause: A shell-expanded Unix wildcard convention was used in PowerShell where the native tool received the wildcard as an invalid literal path.
entries.prevention: Pass the verified directory as the ripgrep path and express filename selection with ripgrep `--glob '*.test.ts'`. Reject every grouped search containing a path error before retry.

entries.mistake: The first Repost/Undo and Add-thoughts positive widget tests used `_Owners`, which assigns an email string but does not establish authenticated Journey state. Both actions correctly entered the sign-in gate, so the tests falsely expected a mutation and composer transition.
entries.rootCause: A display identity field was treated as proof of runtime authentication instead of using a started Journey snapshot whose authenticated identity is authoritative.
entries.prevention: Positive authenticated Social tests construct and start an explicit authenticated Journey snapshot, assert `isAuthenticated` before pumping the action, and separately preserve guest gate tests. Never infer authentication from an email field alone.

entries.mistake: The new Chat draft test asserted that the thread message list was empty even though the selected production test gateway intentionally seeds a received message during load. The draft remained unsent and the gateway send-call list was correctly empty.
entries.rootCause: No-send truth was inferred from total thread history instead of the authoritative outbound gateway call record.
entries.prevention: Prove a prefilled Chat draft is unsent with the exact draft field value, zero outbound send calls and no additional optimistic message. Do not require a seeded conversation history to be empty.

entries.mistake: Backend verification showed that an empty quoted publish was safely rejected by the generic `Write something or add an image` validator before reaching the intended quote-specific `Add your thoughts` recovery contract. One of 508 backend tests failed.
entries.rootCause: Quoted-post identity was parsed and checked only after generic content-format validation, making the more actionable quote-specific validation unreachable for the exact invalid input it owned.
entries.prevention: Parse and validate the optional quoted-post identity before generic format validation, reject empty quoted thoughts with the exact bounded recovery message, then run the standard format validator. Preserve both rejection layers in tests.

entries.mistake: A test-only multi-file patch placed an extra `@@` hunk marker immediately before the second `Update File` header. Patch parsing rejected the entire operation with zero changes.
entries.rootCause: Two otherwise independent test edits were manually combined without validating the patch boundary syntax.
entries.prevention: Apply each test owner in an independent patch using exact current context. Treat any parser rejection as zero mutation and register it before retry.

entries.mistake: A compound scope-state selection patch expected the classification sentence without its current word `Feed`. Exact patch verification rejected the whole operation with zero changes.
entries.rootCause: Several independent selection fields were combined and one sentence was reconstructed from memory rather than copied from the current owner.
entries.prevention: Patch scope-state selection fields in small independent hunks using exact freshly read context. A rejected scope patch is zero mutation and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The first Comment/Reply cross-owner search combined alternations and an escaped quoted `case` pattern inside a PowerShell double-quoted argument. The resulting ripgrep expression had an unclosed group and returned no evidence.
entries.rootCause: Shell quoting transformed the intended regular expression before ripgrep parsed it.
entries.prevention: Use separate simple literal `rg -F -e` patterns or a single-quoted verified expression for cross-owner discovery. A regex parse error is zero evidence and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: Dart analysis reported two undefined-method errors because SharedSession called `comments` and `reply` on a local still statically typed as `SocialContentGateway`, despite a runtime check for the separate `SocialCommentGateway` interface.
entries.rootCause: The implementation assumed flow analysis would expose members from an unrelated optional interface on a variable declared with the base gateway type.
entries.prevention: Resolve the optional capability once through an explicit nullable `SocialCommentGateway` adapter or cast, branch on null, and call capability methods only on that typed adapter. Run focused analyzer before tests.

entries.mistake: A compound command ran from `apps/mobile` but passed `apps/mobile/lib/...` to `dart format`, producing `No file or directory found`. A later analyzer command in the same process exited zero and masked the formatter failure, so the combined result was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Repository-relative and app-relative paths were mixed, and two qualification tools were chained in one shell process.
entries.prevention: Run formatter and analyzer in separate tool processes. Resolve every path relative to the explicit workdir, admit each command only from its own exit code and completion output, and never let a later tool mask an earlier failure.

entries.mistake: The first corrected Comment/Reply focused analyzer invocation grouped five owners and its tool result was reported as exceeding the available model context. No explicit analyzer completion or exit evidence was admissible.
entries.rootCause: The qualification group was still too broad for the evidence channel even though the analyzer target set was focused.
entries.prevention: Run Comment/Reply analysis in small independent owner groups, admit only an explicit analyzer completion line and exit code for each group, and treat any truncated result as no qualification evidence.

entries.mistake: A regression-memory lookup searched the entire repository dot root. Ripgrep entered large artifact JSON and the tool output was truncated, so the broad result was inadmissible.
entries.rootCause: The lookup used `.` despite the memory owner already being constrained to config and docs, and file globs did not exclude artifacts.
entries.prevention: Search regression-memory owners only in exact config/docs paths or resolve filenames first with `rg --files`. Never use a dot-root content search when artifact trees can match.

entries.mistake: Backend typecheck found that the Social service FakeRepository was not expanded with the new comments and reply methods when the production repository interface was expanded.
entries.rootCause: The production contract and Firestore implementation were updated before compiling every interface implementer, leaving the authoritative service test double structurally incomplete.
entries.prevention: When a repository interface gains methods, inventory and update every production and test implementation in the same ticket before the first typecheck. Add method-specific test storage and assertions rather than empty stubs.

entries.mistake: The new reply boundary test exposed that a 501-character reply returned the generic `body is invalid` error instead of an actionable 500-character recovery contract.
entries.rootCause: Reply body validation reused the generic required-text helper, whose field-level error does not explain the ticket's explicit bounded reply rule.
entries.prevention: Validate the trimmed reply body with a reply-specific 1-to-500-character contract before repository work, preserve an actionable message in backend and client tests, and do not rely on generic field errors for user recovery boundaries.

entries.mistake: The Comment/Reply client decoder accepted comment rows and an acknowledged post without proving their postId/id matched the exact requested Feed item. A stale or malformed response could therefore be placed under the wrong post.
entries.rootCause: The initial Dart SocialComment model discarded backend postId and the gateway decoded response objects independently without cross-checking them against the request owner.
entries.prevention: Preserve comment postId in the shared model and reject public comment pages or reply acknowledgements unless every comment postId and the acknowledged post id equal the exact requested post. Add negative gateway tests before ticket qualification.

entries.mistake: A compound gateway-test patch used the pre-format one-line reply test declaration as context after dart format had wrapped it. Patch verification rejected the entire operation with zero changes.
entries.rootCause: The patch context was not refreshed after a formatter mutation and combined new tests with a helper signature edit.
entries.prevention: After formatting, reread the exact insertion boundaries and patch the negative tests and helper edit independently. A rejected patch is zero mutation and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The first independent retry patch for gateway negative tests contained only an unchanged context hunk and therefore made no source mutation.
entries.rootCause: The intended insertion body was omitted while reducing the previously rejected compound patch.
entries.prevention: Before applying an insertion patch, verify that the hunk contains explicit added lines and a stable anchor. Treat an accepted no-op as zero mutation and register it before retry.

entries.mistake: The corrected negative-test insertion copied the complete existing SharedSession test body and renamed the original anchor as a duplicate, creating redundant coverage instead of a clean insertion.
entries.rootCause: The insertion hunk treated the test declaration as a replacement boundary and supplied a replacement body rather than inserting only the new tests before the untouched declaration.
entries.prevention: For insert-before patches, add only new blocks before the exact untouched anchor declaration. Never reproduce or rename the anchored test body; inspect the resulting narrow region before formatting or running tests.

entries.mistake: The timeout-test insertion repeated the context-only no-op from REG-1972: the patch named the endpoint-test anchor but contained no added timeout test lines.
entries.rootCause: The tool call was issued after choosing an anchor but before composing the insertion body, despite the newly registered prevention rule.
entries.prevention: Compose and visually verify the entire added block, including leading plus signs and unchanged anchor, before invoking apply_patch. Never send a placeholder patch call.

entries.mistake: The first post-qualification MVP scope gate failed because the Comment/Reply ticket state and evidence were updated without resealing the selected-ticket manifest hash in the scope assessment.
entries.rootCause: Ticket qualification was treated as documentation-only even though the scope gate deliberately binds the selected assessment to the exact ticket manifest bytes.
entries.prevention: After any selected ticket JSON mutation, recompute its exact SHA-256, update only the authoritative selected-assessment manifest hash, validate both JSON owners, then rerun the scope gate.

entries.mistake: A no-build reconciliation projected buildCount, uploadCount and installCount as top-level fields from both C30T gate owners and returned nulls, providing no admissible count evidence.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic assumed a flat schema instead of first locating the exact nested count owners in the current JSON files.
entries.prevention: Locate exact count field paths with a narrow search or schema read before projecting release state. Reject null projections and report only verified nested values without exposing credential material.

entries.mistake: An index dispatch search passed escaped double-quoted `case` literals through PowerShell. Ripgrep split parts of the intended patterns into paths and returned file-not-found errors, so the search was incomplete.
entries.rootCause: JavaScript-string escaping and PowerShell argument parsing were combined for literal quoted source text instead of using PowerShell single-quoted arguments.
entries.prevention: Use PowerShell single-quoted `rg -F -e` arguments for source literals containing double quotes. Treat any ripgrep path error as zero evidence and retry only after registration.

entries.mistake: The author-return routing search included a guessed `lib/core/review_app_router.dart` path that does not exist. Ripgrep returned an error and the combined result was incomplete.
entries.rootCause: A likely router filename was supplied from memory instead of resolving the current repository router owner first.
entries.prevention: Resolve router owners with a narrow filename inventory before symbol search, then query only verified paths. Any nonexistent-path error invalidates the combined search evidence.

entries.mistake: The first author-card consumer patch expected a reconstructed indentation/context sequence and was rejected with zero changes.
entries.rootCause: The card call site was patched from a remembered earlier excerpt instead of a freshly read exact narrow region after other Social changes.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current card-construction region immediately before patching and use its literal indentation and adjacent callbacks. A rejected patch is zero mutation and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The first author profile sheet placed avatar, multi-line identity metrics and the long guest `Sign in to follow` button in one horizontal row. At the production 390px viewport it overflowed by 18 pixels.
entries.rootCause: The relationship action was treated as a compact trailing control despite its authentication-state copy and dynamic metrics consuming bounded sheet width.
entries.prevention: Keep the avatar and identity summary in one flexible row, then place Follow/Unfollow as a full-width control below it. Preserve compact and large-text no-overflow widget coverage.

entries.mistake: The author-query audit assumed `firestore.indexes.json` existed at repository root. Ripgrep returned a nonexistent-path error and no index evidence.
entries.rootCause: The standard Firebase filename was treated as the exact repository owner without first reading firebase.json or inventorying index files.
entries.prevention: Resolve the configured Firestore index owner from firebase.json or a narrow filename inventory before content search. A nonexistent-path error is zero evidence and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The author response-containment test patch expected the pre-format one-line Follow test declaration. Dart format had wrapped it, so patch verification rejected the edit with zero changes.
entries.rootCause: The insertion anchor was taken from the earlier unformatted patch rather than current source after formatting.
entries.prevention: After every formatter run, reread the exact formatted test boundary before inserting adjacent coverage. A rejected patch remains zero mutation and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The author negative-test retry again sent a context-only apply-patch with no added lines, repeating the placeholder no-op class already recorded in REG-1972 and REG-1974.
entries.rootCause: The exact anchor was found, but the edit tool was invoked before the insertion body was composed, violating the existing permanent prevention rule.
entries.prevention: Do not invoke apply_patch for an insertion until the full new block is present in the patch text. Explicitly verify at least one plus-prefixed semantic line beyond the header before execution.

entries.mistake: The 320px, 140-percent author-sheet journey exposed a 3.6-pixel horizontal overflow in the originating Feed author header when a real authorId made the trailing text `Message` action visible.
entries.rootCause: The public author header always used a labeled trailing button regardless of available width and text scaling; earlier compact coverage used an item without authorId and never rendered the action.
entries.prevention: At compact width or enlarged text, render the same keyed Message action as a tooltip-backed icon button while preserving semantics and behavior. Cover compact cards with real authorId values.

entries.mistake: A diagnostic replacement used the generic `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)` line as its only patch context. Apply-patch changed the first occurrence in an unrelated guest-Create test instead of the compact author test.
entries.rootCause: A repeated assertion was treated as a unique anchor without including the surrounding compact-test-specific lines.
entries.prevention: Patch repeated test assertions only with a unique nearby test name, finder key or adjacent compact-specific statement. Inspect the resulting line location immediately and restore any mis-targeted zero-purpose mutation before continuing.

entries.mistake: The compact Feed overflow diagnostic printed full widget descriptions for an unbounded number of RenderFlex rows. The focused Flutter run exceeded the evidence channel and returned only a truncation result, so it provided no admissible root-cause evidence.
entries.rootCause: Diagnostic instrumentation was added without an explicit record limit or compact output schema before replaying the failing widget test.
entries.prevention: Bound diagnostic records before execution, print only stable compact numeric fields, and cap shell output. Treat any truncated run as zero evidence and register it before a bounded retry.

entries.mistake: A post-compaction read used inaccurate summarized paths for the regression registry, permanent memory and Social source owner. The command returned missing-path errors and its combined evidence was invalid.
entries.rootCause: Compacted handoff path labels were treated as exact repository owners instead of being reconciled through a narrow current-tree filename inventory.
entries.prevention: After compaction or restart, resolve exact current owner paths with a bounded filename inventory before reading or patching them. Never promote summarized path recollection into a direct multi-owner command.

entries.mistake: A follow-up search traversed config, docs and the accumulated artifacts tree for a prior regression identifier and timed out before returning bounded evidence.
entries.rootCause: The lookup repeated a repository-scale evidence search even though the exact registry and quality-memory owners could be read directly.
entries.prevention: Read exact registry and quality-memory owners directly; use capped filename enumeration for incident documents and never include accumulated artifact roots in a routine regression-memory lookup.

entries.mistake: The complete backend verification used the default verbose Node test reporter. Its 516 passing test lines exceeded the evidence channel and the tool marked the output truncated, so the run is rejected as qualification evidence despite a visible final summary.
entries.rootCause: The full suite was replayed without selecting a bounded reporter even though the backend test inventory is known to exceed the tool output budget.
entries.prevention: Run typecheck and build explicitly, then execute the full compiled Node suite with the dot reporter or another bounded reporter. Admit the result only when exit, totals and summary are returned without truncation.

entries.mistake: The bounded Node dot-reporter replay returned only success dots and exit zero, without an explicit test total. That output did not independently satisfy the newly registered qualification requirement for a visible total.
entries.rootCause: The dot reporter was selected for bounded output without first accounting for its summary-free output contract in the installed Node version.
entries.prevention: Capture the bounded dot stream in process memory, count only reporter dots, and emit the exact dot count with the preserved Node process exit. Reject a count that differs from the expected discovered suite total.

entries.mistake: The author-ticket sealing audit piped a raw multi-kilobyte scope JSON string into Select-String. A match caused the complete one-record document and wide context to be rendered, truncating the combined inspection output.
entries.rootCause: Structured JSON was searched as one raw text record instead of being parsed and projected to the exact selected-assessment and checkpoint nodes.
entries.prevention: Parse large JSON owners with ConvertFrom-Json and serialize only the exact bounded nodes needed for the decision. Never use Select-String against a raw whole-document JSON string for qualification.

entries.mistake: Author-ticket sealing replaced the canonical top-level scope state with a descriptive source-qualified value. The scope checker rejected it because execution authorization requires the exact disclosed-and-authorized state.
entries.rootCause: The implementationState field and evidence manifest were correctly advanced, but the top-level gate state was incorrectly treated as a free-form progress label rather than a checker-enforced enum.
entries.prevention: Preserve the canonical top-level `ticket_disclosed_and_authorized` state while advancing implementation evidence in the selected assessment, ticket manifest and checkpoint wording. Inspect checker-enforced state enums before changing them.

entries.mistake: The OTP pending-ticket lookup passed `config/uaw-*ticket.json` as a ripgrep path on Windows. The wildcard was not resolved as an exact file set, the second search exited nonzero, and the combined lookup was invalid.
entries.rootCause: A shell wildcard path was used after the first bounded filename inventory had already returned the two exact ticket owners.
entries.prevention: Use the exact paths returned by `rg --files` for all follow-up ticket reads or content searches. Never pass a Windows wildcard as a ripgrep path argument in qualification work.

entries.mistake: The authentication recovery preselection introduced `accessibility_geometry_correction` as an implementation disposition. The MVP delivery lock rejected it because dispositions are a checker-enforced canonical enum.
entries.rootCause: A descriptive adjustment label was placed in the policy disposition field without reading the delivery lock's accepted vocabulary first.
entries.prevention: Read the delivery lock's exact allowed dispositions before introducing a selected assessment. Put ticket-specific descriptions under adjustments and use only canonical disposition values in implementationDisposition.

entries.mistake: The new Screen 03 accessibility test referenced `SemanticsAction.tap` without importing the `dart:ui` owner. Focused analysis rejected the test before execution.
entries.rootCause: The semantic-node API was added from memory without checking whether the existing test imports exposed the engine semantics enum.
entries.prevention: When a widget test asserts `SemanticsAction`, add or verify the explicit `dart:ui` show import before analysis. Focused analyzer failure is registered before any retry.

entries.mistake: The new accessibility test registered `SemanticsHandle.dispose` with `addTearDown`. Flutter's widget-test end verification ran first and rejected the still-active handle even though all semantic assertions passed.
entries.rootCause: The semantics handle was treated like a general test resource, but WidgetTester requires it to be disposed before the test body returns.
entries.prevention: Wrap semantics-enabled widget-test bodies in `try/finally` and dispose the handle inside the test body. Do not defer SemanticsHandle disposal to addTearDown.

entries.mistake: The quote-validation follow-up found `_validateSocialContent` at line 803 but read a stale 940-1045 range, then combined an optional zero-match test search whose ripgrep exit made the whole command nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The exact symbol line returned by the first search was not used to bound the source read, and an optional absence query was mixed with required evidence.
entries.prevention: Read the narrow range around the exact current symbol line returned by ripgrep. Run optional absence searches separately and explicitly normalize a zero-match result instead of invalidating required source evidence.

entries.mistake: Immediately after registering REG-1997, the duplicate-ticket filename check again ran an optional ripgrep query without normalizing exit 1 for no matches. The command returned nonzero and supplied no admissible duplicate-search evidence.
entries.rootCause: The new permanent rule was documented but not applied to the very next optional absence command.
entries.prevention: Every optional ripgrep absence check includes an explicit branch that converts only exit 1 into a labeled `no_match` success while preserving any other nonzero exit. Never issue an optional raw ripgrep pipeline.

entries.mistake: The Social empty-handler audit ran a raw optional ripgrep regex and exited 1 when no handler matched, repeating the optional no-match class after REG-1997 and REG-1998.
entries.rootCause: A zero-match result was expected, but the command was still issued without the mandatory labeled absence wrapper.
entries.prevention: Raw ripgrep is forbidden for optional absence audits. Enumerate exact source files and use PowerShell Select-String with an explicit match count, or wrap ripgrep exit 1 before the tool call is issued.

entries.mistake: The 58-file authoritative Flutter manifest used the compact reporter directly in the evidence channel. Carriage-return progress still expanded to a truncated tool result, so the visible 401-pass/3-skip ending is rejected as cumulative qualification evidence.
entries.rootCause: Compact reporter was assumed to be bounded in this host, but the tool normalized its progress updates into a large output stream.
entries.prevention: Run large Flutter manifests with the JSON reporter captured in process memory, parse testDone and error events, and emit only exact pass/skip/fail counts with the preserved process exit. Never stream compact progress directly for authoritative manifests.

entries.mistake: The bounded JSON wrapper counted every successful testDone event as a user test. Flutter emitted one synthetic load test for each of the 58 manifest files, producing 459 instead of the expected 401 and causing the wrapper to exit nonzero despite zero test failures and process exit zero.
entries.rootCause: The reporter parser ignored testStart metadata and assumed all testDone events represented visible authored tests.
entries.prevention: Join testDone events to testStart metadata by test ID and exclude only reporter-hidden or synthetic `loading` tests before asserting authored pass/skip totals. Emit raw and filtered totals for auditability.

entries.mistake: A read-only r60.45 reconciliation projected upload/install counts and aggregate authority flags from guessed nested fields. Several values returned null, repeating the schema-assumption class already recorded in REG-1976.
entries.rootCause: The current state objects were projected before enumerating the exact property names in buildResult, uploadResult, installResult and aggregate authority owners.
entries.prevention: Enumerate exact relevant object properties with PSObject.Properties before any release-state projection. Reject every null and report only exact non-null paths; never reuse a prior release schema from memory.

entries.mistake: The source-fingerprint reconciliation combined broad ripgrep results with a fixed 95-line read from the large C30T qualifier. The tool result exceeded the evidence channel and was truncated, so none of that output is admissible qualification evidence.
entries.rootCause: A broad symbol search and a large source range were bundled into one diagnostic call instead of locating one exact definition and then reading a narrow surrounding region.
entries.prevention: Search one exact symbol at a time, cap returned matches, and read only a 20-30 line region around the verified line. Never combine broad qualifier matches and a fixed large range in one evidence call.

entries.mistake: The first current-source fingerprint calculation was issued as one oversized inline PowerShell command. The shell host rejected process launch with `Access is denied` before producing any result.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier's multi-owner manifest algorithm and comparison logic were compressed into the command argument instead of placed in a reviewable bounded script owner.
entries.prevention: Complex multi-owner qualification calculations are added with apply_patch as a bounded repository audit script, executed read-only, and kept or removed only through an explicitly reviewed patch. Do not issue them as oversized shell command arguments.

entries.mistake: The ticket reconciliation enumerated exact top-level properties but then guessed fields inside verification, resolutionEvidence, founderDecision and authority. Those guessed nested projections returned null and are rejected.
entries.rootCause: The REG-2002 enumeration rule was applied only at the outer object boundary instead of at every nested owner used by the projection.
entries.prevention: Before projecting any nested ticket field, enumerate that exact nested object's properties and reject absent owners. Top-level schema enumeration does not authorize nested field guesses.

entries.mistake: The reply-test inventory assigned search results to `$matches`, which is case-insensitively the PowerShell automatic `$Matches` variable, and then executed regex matches in the same command. The collection was clobbered and the command failed without evidence.
entries.rootCause: A reserved automatic PowerShell variable name was reused for ordinary collection state.
entries.prevention: Never use automatic variable names such as `$Matches` for task collections in PowerShell, regardless of casing. Use explicit names such as `$foundLines` and calculate filtered results once before reporting them.

entries.mistake: The bounded authoritative Flutter JSON parser ran under strict mode and accessed `test.hidden` directly. Valid testStart events without that optional property caused the parser to fail after the test process completed, so the run is rejected as cumulative evidence.
entries.rootCause: The parser treated optional Flutter protocol properties as universally present instead of checking each event object's property collection.
entries.prevention: JSON reporter parsers access optional protocol fields only through explicit property-existence helpers with documented defaults. Strict mode remains enabled, and a parser exception invalidates the entire run before retry.

entries.mistake: A final Git reconciliation requested `status --untracked-files=all` in the founder's enormous evidence tree. Git streamed long-path warnings from historical browser artifacts and the tool result was truncated, so its dirty counts are rejected.
entries.rootCause: A full untracked inventory was requested even though the task only required bounded branch, HEAD and tracked-change reconciliation and the huge user-owned untracked tree was already established.
entries.prevention: Use exact branch and HEAD commands plus `git status --untracked-files=no` for bounded reconciliation. Never enumerate the entire untracked evidence tree merely to count it; preserve it as an established owner set.

entries.mistake: Deployment reconciliation recursively searched config, scripts, deployment and the entire large docs/quality tree for runtime service names. The command timed out and produced no admissible owner evidence.
entries.rootCause: A service-owner lookup included the large historical quality-document corpus instead of first constraining the search to executable config, scripts and deployment manifests.
entries.prevention: Search executable config, scripts and deployment manifests first with exact terms and bounded output. Consult only specifically named evidence documents returned by those owners; never include the entire quality-document tree in an initial service lookup.

entries.mistake: An official YouTube audit-policy follow-up query embedded unescaped quotation marks inside a JavaScript string. The orchestration script failed to parse before any web request was made.
entries.rootCause: Quoted search terms were copied into a double-quoted JavaScript string without escaping or simplifying the query.
entries.prevention: Use plain unquoted search terms or correctly escaped string literals in web orchestration calls. A parse failure is registered before retry and never treated as research evidence.

entries.mistake: The new C30U selected-ticket assessment used `release_gate` as an implementation disposition without first reading the delivery lock's exact allowed enum. The scope gate failed closed before any build or deployment.
entries.rootCause: A descriptive phrase was treated as a machine enum instead of reusing the exact repository-supported vocabulary.
entries.prevention: Before writing any scope-state enum, read the exact allowed set from the current machine gate and use only those values. A rejected enum is registered before correction and retry.

entries.mistake: The C30U selected-ticket assessment referenced its intended source-audit summary path before that evidence file was created. The delivery lock failed closed before any build or deployment.
entries.rootCause: Scope state and evidence creation were sequenced in the wrong order even though the gate requires the selected evidence path to exist.
entries.prevention: Create and parse the selected-ticket evidence owner before writing its path into MVP scope state. Verify existence and checksum first, then run the delivery and scope gates.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to generalize the existing single-AAB wrapper bundled many replacements, including two version-verification lines whose exact current text differed. apply_patch rejected the entire patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-hunk patch was composed from partial line evidence instead of verifying every exact target region.
entries.prevention: Patch release wrappers in small, independently verified hunks. Read the exact current region immediately before each patch; never bundle unverified distant contexts into one release-control edit.

entries.mistake: The founder-only C30U launcher was submitted as one very large add-file patch. The tool output exceeded the evidence channel and was truncated, leaving the patch result ambiguous until the exact file and parser state are verified.
entries.rootCause: A release-control file was added in one oversized patch instead of bounded sections with an immediate path, checksum and PowerShell-parser verification.
entries.prevention: Add or amend large release launchers in small verified sections. After any truncated apply_patch result, perform read-only exact path, size, SHA-256 and PowerShell parser checks before relying on or retrying the mutation.

entries.mistake: A read-only required-document inventory piped directly from a PowerShell foreach statement. The shell parser rejected the empty pipeline position, so the command produced no admissible inventory evidence.
entries.rootCause: The foreach statement was treated as a parenthesized pipeline expression without assigning its output to an explicit collection first.
entries.prevention: Assign foreach output to a task-specific collection variable, then pipe that collection to formatting. Keep the retry bounded and verify its exit code before using the result.

entries.mistake: The immediately following batched reconciliation repeated the invalid direct pipeline from a PowerShell foreach statement in the machine-state projection subcommand. The batch is rejected as evidence.
entries.rootCause: The documented prevention was applied to the first retry but not carried into a separately composed parallel subcommand in the same release reconciliation.
entries.prevention: No release diagnostic may contain the textual statement pattern `} |`. Every foreach result is assigned to an explicit collection, and commands are parser-checked or visually audited before batching. A batch containing one parser failure is rejected in full.

entries.mistake: The C30U state command correctly enumerated candidate.id, a string buildAuthorization, candidateInstallCount and aggregate candidate counters, but its following projection still used older field names. The resulting nulls are rejected.
entries.rootCause: The current schema enumeration and the projection were composed together, so stale field expressions were not corrected after the actual property list became known.
entries.prevention: Schema enumeration and value projection are separate tool calls. The projection is authored only from returned exact property names, asserts every required value is non-null, and fails closed on any absent field.

entries.mistake: The first REG-2017 registration patch omitted the required plus prefix on one added Markdown line. apply_patch rejected the patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: A multiline add-file block was composed without verifying that every semantic line had the patch addition prefix.
entries.prevention: Register incidents in small patches and visually verify every add-file content line begins with plus. A rejected patch is zero mutation and is itself registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The exact C30U projection returned required numeric zero counters, but a generic comparison against an empty string coerced zero and falsely classified the counters as missing.
entries.rootCause: Required-value validation did not distinguish numeric counters from strings before applying an empty-string test.
entries.prevention: Validate null with ReferenceEquals. Apply IsNullOrWhiteSpace only to string values and preserve numeric zero as a present required value. Release counters are additionally asserted against exact integer limits.

entries.mistake: The new build-wrapper checker required a literal secondBuildPerformed false assignment that the wrapper does not contain. The false value is sealed in machine state and the wrapper preserves it, so the checker produced a false failure.
entries.rootCause: A desired invariant was translated into an assumed source literal without first verifying the exact wrapper implementation.
entries.prevention: Release-control source gates assert exact current implementation patterns. For preserved boolean state, forbid any assignment to true and rely on the state gate's false invariant instead of requiring a nonexistent reset literal.

entries.mistake: The wrapper checker required the full version-name literal inside the founder launcher. The launcher owns candidate id, version code and the r60.46 label, while the machine gate owns the exact full version name, so the check failed falsely.
entries.rootCause: The checker conflated responsibilities between the secure-input launcher and the authoritative release-state gate.
entries.prevention: Check each release invariant in its actual owner: launcher for secure prompts and selected state/version code, machine gate for exact versionName, package, branch and HEAD, and build wrapper for dynamic propagation.

entries.mistake: C30U cycle 1 backend verification exited zero with 516 tests, but the qualifier required TAP summary lines beginning with hash. Node 22 emitted the spec reporter summary with the information-symbol prefix, so the qualifier failed before source sealing.
entries.rootCause: The bounded parser reused an older TAP prefix assumption without reading the exact current Node 22 captured summary syntax.
entries.prevention: The counted backend and Hosting parser accepts only the exact hash or information-symbol pass/fail prefixes, still requires explicit integer totals, preserved process exit zero and the exact expected counts.

entries.mistake: The first qualifier version used only cycle-number log names. After a failed pre-seal cycle, a direct retry would have overwritten founder-owned failure logs.
entries.rootCause: Qualification cycle identity and attempt identity were conflated in log paths even though a failed attempt must remain immutable evidence.
entries.prevention: Qualifier retries require an explicit positive Attempt. Attempts after one receive an attempt suffix, Invoke-Captured rejects an existing log path, and the accepted cycle JSON remains written only once after a full pass.

entries.mistake: C30U qualifying cycle 1 reached the immutable approved UI gate and found apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/screens/screen03_login/login_screen_v2.dart at SHA-256 1F0DEA832A8E7A264E1A7BA7FFA1C0C7F2D9ABE63A6407E21C15611499103E14 instead of the approved 9F8F8A72ACED405332920BC8F46B71B9907A14F6B440AD851ABFD2A96BFCD28B.
entries.rootCause: Post-r60.45 authentication and provider-handoff repairs were source-qualified without replaying the immutable Screen 03 checksum gate early enough, allowing a locked presentation owner to enter the candidate tree.
entries.prevention: Run check-approved-ui-locks before editing or qualifying any dependency touching login/account handoff and again as the first candidate gate. Never update the approved hash or bypass the gate without a separate founder acceptance workflow. Restore the locked owner by a reviewed minimal patch or stop for founder acceptance if the requested outcome truly requires a presentation change.

entries.mistake: The Screen 03 recovery investigation combined six owners and up to 120 matches in one formatted search. The evidence channel truncated the result, so it is rejected for implementation decisions.
entries.rootCause: A bounded match count was still too broad when formatted wrapped paths and long Dart lines multiplied the output size.
entries.prevention: After the exact owners and symbol lines are known, read only one 20-40 line region per owner. Do not combine formatted cross-owner results during locked-screen recovery.

entries.mistake: After the locked Screen 03 production owner was restored, the approved UI gate exposed a changed apps/mobile/test/ui_v2_screen03_login_test.dart hash: 504BF15DBD2495B3EE57690BBD8318674A1CEB2002004ACE50227CA805895EC6 instead of A36A4FD2B6BDBA9F0DA4262EB360BB7885FB9E7270BEC37CC50D5B75181A6C5A.
entries.rootCause: Provider-handoff coverage was added directly to the immutable accepted Screen 03 test owner rather than a new non-locked Social integration test owner.
entries.prevention: Immutable accepted test owners are checked before patching. Successor journey coverage belongs in a new or existing non-locked ticket-specific test file unless a separate founder acceptance workflow versions the locked test.

entries.mistake: After the two direct Screen 03 owners were restored, the approved UI gate exposed apps/mobile/test/platform_configuration_test.dart at DD60E2C7D91CD6A804A5069E330FA3C23FA56949717BFEDEDD1D16BE1ACCFCA3 instead of its approved DEFFE5CFD7CD7C1432D6057E5C045A1569DC3F71FBD5F9D8EF26251E984A68CA.
entries.rootCause: Successor platform and release configuration assertions were added to a test owner included in the immutable Screen 03 checkpoint.
entries.prevention: Read the approved reference file list before extending shared platform tests. Put successor release/Firebase/plugin assertions into candidate-specific non-locked gate scripts or a separately versioned test owner.

entries.mistake: The first REG-2027 text manually transcribed the current platform-test SHA-256 with an inserted space near the final bytes.
entries.rootCause: A machine-returned checksum was retyped manually inside a long registry sentence.
entries.prevention: Copy exact checksums directly and validate every recorded SHA-256 against the 64-hex pattern before admitting a registry entry. Do not add visual grouping spaces.

entries.mistake: The first correction of REG-2027 still left one grouping space in the platform-test SHA-256, and the progress update repeated the malformed display.
entries.rootCause: The correction was patched and narrated before validating the final literal against the exact machine-returned checksum.
entries.prevention: Before a checksum correction, compare the final literal directly with Get-FileHash output and assert it matches the 64-hex regular expression. Only then patch or report it.

entries.mistake: The first reverse patch removed the platform-test semantic additions but did not restore the approved byte hash, leaving a whitespace-only difference and hash 490721029D88301E42DC593526618B4F94198AB586C1E55D709CAE12776123BC.
entries.rootCause: The reverse patch deleted adjacent blank lines together with added blocks instead of verifying the post-patch Git diff and exact approved checksum.
entries.prevention: After restoring a locked owner, require both zero Git diff lines and the exact approved SHA-256. If either differs, inspect only the remaining post-patch diff before another patch.

entries.mistake: The first platform-test byte-variant diagnostic nested two foreach statements inside an array expression with an unmatched closing brace. PowerShell rejected it before producing evidence.
entries.rootCause: An unnecessarily compressed inline loop obscured block closure while testing a small fixed set of encoding variants.
entries.prevention: For a small fixed encoding matrix, calculate explicit named byte arrays and rows without nested inline loops. Parser failures are zero evidence and are registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The acceptance-owner lookup filtered only by Screen 03 id, returning v2 and v3. PowerShell concatenated both productionAcceptance paths and Get-Content failed.
entries.rootCause: The query did not add the required status=production-accepted predicate before treating the result as a scalar.
entries.prevention: Acceptance lookups require screenId plus status=production-accepted, assert exactly one result, and only then resolve the path.

entries.mistake: After the authoritative approved UI lock passed, a manual follow-up invoked the historical C19 acceptance script. That script correctly rejected C30U because it permits only its old C19/C18D active ticket ids.
entries.rootCause: A historical acceptance workflow gate was mistaken for a timeless checksum gate even though its source contains ticket-specific scope assertions.
entries.prevention: Use check-approved-ui-locks.ps1 for current immutable checksum enforcement. Invoke a historical ticket acceptance script only when its exact ticket is active or when reading it as evidence, never as a successor qualification gate.

entries.mistake: A combined format, analyze and Flutter-test command ran inside try/finally. The test failed, but the final Pop-Location statement became the shell command result and the tool reported exit zero.
entries.rootCause: Several native tools were chained inside one PowerShell command and the last cleanup statement masked the authoritative native exit code.
entries.prevention: Run formatter, analyzer and test as separate shell processes, or capture and explicitly exit with each native result after cleanup. A later cleanup command may never determine the reported status.

entries.mistake: The focused Social test file was streamed with Flutter's compact reporter. Carriage-return progress expanded and the failure details were truncated, so the output is rejected as diagnostic evidence.
entries.rootCause: The permanent JSON-capture rule for Flutter was not applied to a focused file because its size was underestimated.
entries.prevention: Use a single named test with the expanded reporter for bounded diagnosis, then use the captured JSON counted wrapper for file or manifest qualification. Never stream compact reporter progress into the evidence channel.

entries.mistake: The new bounded guest continuation test began on Social Videos but JourneySession.authenticationCancelFallback became /app/social rather than /app/social?sub=videos.
entries.rootCause: The YouTube account action derived its cancellation location from mutable _tab state, which was not authoritative for the requested initial Videos sub-action at the interaction boundary.
entries.prevention: YouTube channel entry records the exact stable Videos origin explicitly. A non-locked Social test asserts return location, cancel fallback and YouTube authentication purpose together before AAB qualification.

entries.mistake: Capturing _tab before awaiting the explanation dialog did not fix the cancellation path. At the YouTube account action boundary, _tab was already home and the test still received /app/social.
entries.rootCause: The action's account control can be rendered from a home-owned composition even when its authoritative recovery workspace is Videos, so widget tab state is not the route contract.
entries.prevention: The YouTube channel-status action owns an explicit /app/social?sub=videos recovery location. Do not derive this provider workflow's return route from presentation composition state.

entries.mistake: Immediately after documenting separate tool processes, the regression-memory gate and Dart formatter were still issued in one shell command. Both passed, but the structure could mask the first exit in a failing run.
entries.rootCause: The separation rule was interpreted narrowly as format/analyze/test only rather than every authoritative gate or native action.
entries.prevention: Use one authoritative gate or native action per shell tool call during release work. Do not sequence a memory gate with formatting, analysis, tests or builds in the same command.

entries.mistake: The Social action passed the explicit /app/social?sub=videos cancellation value, but JourneySession.authenticationCancelFallback still exposed /app/social and the named test failed again.
entries.rootCause: The prior repair targeted the caller without first proving how JourneySession stores or canonicalizes cancelLocation.
entries.prevention: When an explicit caller value is lost, inspect the exact session getter and canonicalization method before another patch. Assert both the private-owner contract through its public getter and end-to-end Social behavior.

entries.mistake: The guest YouTube continuation test asserted authenticationCancelFallback, which intentionally returns the last ready route for router interception. The active sign-in cancellation destination is exposed by readyRoute(), which preserves _authenticationCancelTo.
entries.rootCause: Two distinct session navigation getters were treated as synonyms without reading their exact current implementations.
entries.prevention: Assert authenticationCancelFallback only for router interception fallback and readyRoute() for the active sign-in cancellation destination. Read both owner implementations before navigation assertions.

entries.mistake: The direct C30U implementation-phase regression-memory gate output exceeded the task output boundary and was truncated, so it could not be admitted as a pass.
entries.rootCause: The gate output was streamed directly instead of being captured under a unique immutable attempt log with only a bounded final summary returned.
entries.prevention: Run the regression-memory gate as the sole authoritative action, capture complete stdout and stderr in a new immutable C30U evidence log, preserve its immediate process exit, and emit only bounded final lines.

entries.mistake: The post-restart reconciliation grouped git status --short --branch with branch and HEAD reads. The huge founder-owned dirty status body was truncated and is rejected as complete ownership evidence.
entries.rootCause: The resume check repeated an unbounded full-status display instead of following the durable tracked-only, independently bounded reconciliation rule.
entries.prevention: Read branch and HEAD independently. Reconcile tracked ownership using an in-memory Git process with long-path support, --untracked-files=no, separate stdout/stderr, zero exit and empty stderr, then report only deterministic record count and SHA-256. Never enumerate the full preserved untracked tree.

entries.mistake: A successful bounded rg --files inventory returned 2,710 paths, but exact membership returned zero because Windows emitted backslashes and the expected C30U owner list used forward slashes.
entries.rootCause: Current inventory paths were not normalized to one repository-relative separator convention before exact comparison.
entries.prevention: Capture and validate rg --files first, normalize every returned path to forward slashes, compare with the exact two C30U Social owner paths, and require a count of two before formatting, analysis or tests.

entries.mistake: The first focused test-name lookup assumed a guest YouTube prefix and returned an unclassified zero-match nonzero result, so it proved no executable test name.
entries.rootCause: The formatted current test owner was not used to derive the exact complete test names before composing a named Flutter invocation.
entries.prevention: Use a no-match-safe literal YouTube projection over the exact current test owner, emit only matched line numbers and text, copy complete names from the file, and never guess a named-test prefix.

entries.mistake: The C30U qualifier filtered adb devices through a PowerShell pipeline before checking LASTEXITCODE, allowing a stale or obscured native result to influence exact OPPO readiness.
entries.rootCause: Native output capture, native exit preservation and row filtering were combined instead of validating ADB immediately before any PowerShell pipeline.
entries.prevention: Capture raw adb devices output, assign its native exit immediately, reject nonzero, then filter header and blank lines and require exactly one anchored 2b3e0f71 device row. Statistically forbid the prior piped invocation before final cycles.

entries.mistake: The first post-cycle-failure projection placed statement-form if directly in a PSCustomObject property value, which PowerShell treated as an unknown command and rejected.
entries.rootCause: The conditional value was not calculated into a named scalar or wrapped in a valid subexpression before object construction.
entries.prevention: Calculate every conditional artifact-state value into an explicit ticket-named scalar before constructing the bounded projection. A parser-rejected diagnostic is zero evidence.

entries.mistake: C30U cycle 1 attempt 3 stopped at the authoritative 58-file Flutter audit with 403 passed, 3 skipped, 2 failed, 2 error events and exit 1; no source seal was created.
entries.rootCause: The product/test causes remain unknown because the current captured JSON wrapper emits only counts and does not join failing authored test IDs to bounded names and URLs.
entries.prevention: Strengthen the authoritative wrapper to emit only a bounded exact failing-name and URL projection on failure, diagnose and register each cause, then reconcile expected pass count from the current manifest without weakening tests or blindly changing 401.

entries.mistake: The authoritative manifest reproducibly reports an error in C30J signed-out viewer starts the distinct MoolSocial auth handoff after C30U introduced explanation-first account entry.
entries.rootCause: Pending exact current assertion and expanded named-test diagnosis; a stale direct-first-tap expectation and a runtime distinct-account regression must not be conflated.
entries.prevention: Resolve and read the exact current C30J assertion owner, run only the exact name with expanded output, retain the distinct MoolSocial-versus-YouTube account invariant, and migrate only a proven superseded first-tap expectation with positive and negative coverage.

entries.mistake: The authoritative manifest reproducibly fails C30J source never infers YouTube authorization from an avatar after the C30U Social account-entry change.
entries.rootCause: Pending exact assertion and production-source inspection; the failure may be a lexical false match or a real authorization-state inference and cannot be inferred from the test title.
entries.prevention: Read the exact bounded C30J source assertion and matched production owner, run the named test independently, preserve the semantic ban on avatar-derived authorization, and repair without weakening that invariant.

entries.mistake: The expanded C30J source-shape failure serialized the complete Social consumer source through Matcher's Actual value, overflowing and truncating the task transcript.
entries.rootCause: A whole-source contains matcher was allowed to report its entire large actual string when the expected synchronous method signature became async.
entries.prevention: Retain semantic negative assertions, but express method-shape checks as bounded-region or boolean contains assertions so failures cannot print the complete source. Replay the named test in a bounded passing run.

entries.mistake: The migrated C30J signed-out test started an empty default JourneySession and expected ready, but startup truthfully entered setup because setup snapshot/version was absent.
entries.rootCause: The fixture did not model its intended signed-out viewer who already completed onboarding; calling start exposed the missing journey-store state.
entries.prevention: Reuse an exact passing signed-out-ready in-memory store pattern, seed completed setup/version, call start, assert ready and unauthenticated, then test the explanation and exact continuation. Never bypass startup.

entries.mistake: The C30J signed-out-ready fixture used MemoryJourneyStore and JourneySnapshot without their direct declaring import, and focused analysis rejected both names.
entries.rootCause: The fixture body was copied without the passing owner's exact import; journey_session.dart was incorrectly assumed to re-export the types.
entries.prevention: Read the passing test import block, add only the exact declaring library import, format, and rerun focused analysis before behavior tests. Never assume Dart transitive imports.

entries.mistake: A read-only C30U scope-state validation assumed selectedTicketAssessment was top-level, produced a null manifest path, and failed before proving the resealed ticket binding.
entries.rootCause: The current MVP scope owner's exact nested schema was not enumerated before using an older remembered projection.
entries.prevention: Enumerate current root properties, then candidate nested owner names, require a non-null manifest path, and compare its stored 64-hex hash to a fresh literal digest before the scope gate.

entries.mistake: C30U cycle 1 attempt 4 passed through the authoritative Flutter/backend/Hosting/config checks and then failed closed when check-social-protected-baseline.ps1 returned exit 1.
entries.rootCause: Pending exact 289-byte gate-log diagnosis; a genuine protected mismatch and an authorized successor checksum change must not be conflated.
entries.prevention: Read the retained exact gate log and only its named gate owner/checksum assertion. Never bypass or reseal a genuine mismatch; use a separate passing C30U successor containment gate only if the predecessor hard-binds an intentionally superseded owner.

entries.mistake: The first C30U successor-seal gate run failed under strict mode because the candidate baseline recorded AAB fields but omitted the generic retainedApk compatibility properties.
entries.rootCause: The generic protected gate selects its candidate schema whenever candidate exists and reads retainedApk and retainedApkSha256 even while both values are intentionally blank.
entries.prevention: Candidate successor baselines include empty generic retained-APK compatibility fields plus their ticket-specific AAB fields. Never modify the historical gate or invent an artifact value to bypass schema compatibility.

entries.mistake: The first final C30U AAB machine-state projection exceeded the available transcript context and was truncated, so it proved none of the intended state, successor-seal or zero-count assertions.
entries.rootCause: A structured projection was rendered when the required facts fit in a single bounded scalar record; the host expansion risk was not eliminated before the final pre-cycle reconciliation.
entries.prevention: Project only the exact required AAB state facts into one semicolon-delimited line, calculate comparisons before rendering, reject missing values, and require the literal zero build/upload/install counts. A truncated state projection is zero evidence.

entries.mistake: C30U cycle 1 attempt 5 passed the preceding qualification stages and then failed closed when scripts/check-user-facing-copy.ps1 returned exit 1; no source seal was created.
entries.rootCause: The Chat URI validator used ArgumentError.value with the developer-only quoted parameter label endpoint and a Dev endpoint instruction, allowing internal configuration vocabulary into a potentially surfaced exception and violating the production copy gate.
entries.prevention: Chat configuration validation throws only a generic user-safe configuration-unavailable error. Preserve and hash the exact failed gate log, replay focused analysis and Chat tests plus the unchanged copy gate, and independently replay the unchanged protected Social successor gate.

entries.mistake: A read-only C30U successor-seal owner lookup passed config/play-internal-*c30u.json as a literal Windows path to rg, which rejected the invalid filename and returned exit 1 after other useful matches.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style wildcard was placed in rg's positional path list instead of using explicit existing files or an rg --glob selector rooted at an existing directory.
entries.prevention: On Windows, pass each known JSON owner as an explicit literal path, or search an existing directory with an rg --glob filter. Any mixed-output nonzero lookup is registered and not treated as complete inventory evidence.

entries.mistake: A read-only protected-inventory lookup added a guessed C24F baseline directory that does not exist at that path, causing rg to return exit 1 and invalidating the combined lookup.
entries.rootCause: A historical baseline path was reconstructed from memory instead of being resolved from the current successor audit or enumerated with a bounded exact-directory search.
entries.prevention: Use only already verified baseline owner paths. If a historical owner is required, resolve it with a bounded exact-name inventory first and require one match before reading it. Never append a remembered path to an otherwise valid command.

entries.mistake: After repairing Chat copy, the incident record incorrectly stated that chat_services.dart belonged to the protected Social successor and therefore required a reseal before exact baseline membership was checked.
entries.rootCause: The audit's narrative phrase Chat-adjacent was treated as file-level membership instead of querying the exact C30U and C29E baseline manifests.
entries.prevention: Before declaring that a repair changes a protected tree, perform a no-match-safe exact path query against the current and predecessor baseline manifests. Reseal only a proven member; zero exact matches require replaying the unchanged gate without rewriting the seal.

entries.mistake: C30U cycle 1 attempt 6 passed all captured software gates and the exact OPPO/version checks, then failed closed because the live installer-source assertion did not find com.android.vending; no source seal was created.
entries.rootCause: The qualifier invoked cmd package get-install-source, but this OPPO package-service implementation does not support that subcommand and returns Unknown command with native exit 255. The unsupported command was incorrectly used as universal Play-installer evidence.
entries.prevention: Preserve attempt-6 evidence and require the supported exact-package installer listing with native exit captured immediately and one exact com.moolsocial.app installer=com.android.vending row. Never weaken the Play predecessor invariant or mutate the device to make the gate pass.

entries.mistake: The first bounded post-attempt-6 installer-source read returned native ADB exit 255 before any installer fields could be observed.
entries.rootCause: ADB devices returned the exact ready 2b3e0f71 device row; the retried bounded command then returned Unknown command: get-install-source, proving an unsupported OPPO package-service subcommand rather than USB disconnection.
entries.prevention: After native exit 255, prove the exact device row once, preserve the unsupported-command output, and switch only to a documented supported read-only package-manager identity query. Never loop the unsupported command or mutate the app/device.

entries.mistake: A get-install-source owner search included scripts, tmp, the full regression registry and the quality archive, then timed out with exit 124 after partial matches.
entries.rootCause: The search scope was broader than the repair required and included very large durable-memory owners despite the current qualifier path already being known.
entries.prevention: Search only the exact current script directories for executable owners, then read the already located prior registry line regions separately. Treat timeout 124 and its partial output as incomplete evidence.

entries.mistake: C30U cycle 1 attempt 7 passed the preceding software, runtime and OPPO gates, generated its source manifest, then failed closed because the qualifier asserted that protected source owners were unexpectedly missing; no cycle seal was created.
entries.rootCause: The manifest builder's extension/root inventory omitted 46 exact members of the passing 206-file protected Social tree: one asset, five iOS/package files, one test-driver owner and 39 protected PNG goldens. The qualifier detected this only through an invalid hard-coded >1109 total-row proxy and had already written the accepted-looking path before the postcondition.
entries.prevention: Union the exact 206-owner protected inventory into the source manifest, assert 206 protected owners and zero missing owners, validate the counted summary and manifest hash, write attempt-specific provisional evidence, and promote a distinct accepted-v2 path only after all postconditions pass. Preserve the failed attempt-7 manifest unchanged.

entries.mistake: A post-attempt-7 lookup repeated the registered Windows error by passing docs/quality/UAW-C30U* as a positional rg path, producing a nonzero mixed-output result.
entries.rootCause: The already recorded REG-20260814-2058 prevention was not applied when composing a later search command; the wildcard belonged in an rg --glob selector rooted at docs/quality.
entries.prevention: Escalate the rule: every Windows rg call with multiple paths is composed only from verified literal owners or existing directories. Filename patterns are permitted only through --glob, and the command is visually checked for positional asterisks before execution.

entries.mistake: The first exact ComparePath self-test of the repaired C30U source manifest failed because PowerShell attempted to invoke AsSpan as an instance method on enumerated System.Byte values.
entries.rootCause: The script used $existing.AsSpan().SequenceEqual($bytes), but AsSpan is not a callable byte-array instance method on this PowerShell/.NET binding surface.
entries.prevention: Compare the retained manifest with the freshly composed payload using exact byte length plus SHA-256 equality, both calculated before the comparison. Exercise OutputPath and ComparePath modes independently before either final cycle.

entries.mistake: After a passing C30U cycle 1, a read-only combined seal projection used an unverified cycle JSON property name and rejected its own assertion without identifying the mismatched scalar.
entries.rootCause: The cycle-evidence schema was not enumerated before joining state, cycle, manifest and count checks into one opaque boolean assertion.
entries.prevention: Enumerate exact root property names first, then validate each scalar separately with a named bounded result. Because registering this diagnostic changes sealed regression memory, preserve the prior passing cycle as superseded and run two fresh cycles under versioned manifest/cycle owners before build authority can activate.

entries.mistake: After two passing source cycles, the agent directly invoked the C30U AAB gate with Phase build before the founder launcher qualified its transient upload password and Firebase Android API key inputs; the gate rejected single-build readiness.
entries.rootCause: Source-qualified build authority availability was conflated with the later launcher-owned build-phase precondition that can only become true after founder-only secure input validation.
entries.prevention: After two source cycles, validate only the source-qualified machine state and zero counts. Never invoke Phase build directly. Launch the exact founder-only wrapper visibly; it alone collects hidden inputs, qualifies transient configuration, invokes the build gate at the correct boundary and consumes the one authority.

entries.mistake: After final cycle 1 passed, cycle 2 was invoked with Attempt 1, whose cycle2-flutter-format.log already belonged to a preserved prior cycle-2 run; the qualifier rejected the immutable log collision before its first test.
entries.rootCause: Manifest and cycle JSON owners were versioned after prior superseded cycles, but the log stem still derives from the attempt number and Attempt 1 was reused without an explicit preflight for every cycle-2 log path.
entries.prevention: Before every cycle invocation, enumerate the exact full log set for that cycle and attempt and require all absent. Use the first unused attempt number; for the final pair use a new cycle-1 attempt and cycle-2 Attempt 2, with another versioned manifest/cycle/summary owner set. Never overwrite preserved logs.

entries.mistake: The post-qualification launcher read passed a guessed scripts/build-play-internal-aab-c30u.ps1 owner to rg even though that file does not exist, causing a nonzero mixed-output result after valid launcher matches.
entries.rootCause: A build implementation owner was inferred from naming convention instead of reading the already verified founder launcher and its existing static wrapper gate only.
entries.prevention: Before final cycles, inspect only exact known existing owner paths. Never add an inferred release-script filename. After the final pair, perform no exploratory owner search; launch the exact known founder wrapper directly and let its already-passing static gate own its implementation graph.

entries.mistake: The founder-only C30U launcher validated both hidden inputs and passed the C30U build phase, but the underlying C30T wrapper failed closed before the AAB build because its exported dependency-component merger-blame origin assertion changed.
entries.rootCause: The current generated merger-blame preserves all expected exported components, but RevocationBoundService now comes from com.google.android.gms:play-services-auth:21.6.0 while the historical C30T wrapper still required 20.7.0. Firebase Auth 24.1.0 and Profile Installer 1.4.0 origins remain unchanged.
entries.prevention: Bind RevocationBoundService to exact current play-services-auth 21.6.0 provenance, statically forbid the obsolete 20.7.0 literal in the C30U wrapper gate, replay all four generated merger-blame origins, and run two fresh source cycles. Never retry hidden inputs until those gates pass.

entries.mistake: After the one authorized r60.46 AAB succeeded, a read-only rg query searched config, docs, artifacts and scripts together for upload-state evidence and exceeded its bounded execution time.
entries.rootCause: A broad historical evidence search was used even though the exact C30U state owner and gate script were already known and sufficient for the current pre-upload transition.
entries.prevention: After a sealed release build, query only the exact C30U machine-state owner and the exact C30U gate script. Never sweep historical artifacts or unrelated ticket generations for a current upload transition; use bounded exact-owner reads.

entries.mistake: The required permanent record for the postbuild search timeout was added to the regression registry before the pre-upload gate, but the registry is part of the qualified C30U source manifest, so the gate rejected the source fingerprint before any Play upload.
entries.rootCause: The postbuild instruction to register every new mistake was followed without first proving whether the regression registry was excluded from the immutable source seal or whether an exact postbuild recovery owner existed.
entries.prevention: After a single-build authority is consumed, never mutate the regression registry until the exact release gate's sealed-source ownership and documented postbuild recovery path have been read. If the registry is sealed, stop before mutation or use only an existing founder-approved recovery owner that proves product inputs and the built artifact unchanged; never bypass the gate or build again without new authority.

entries.mistake: The first r60.47 post-authorization read-only Git reconciliation grouped branch, HEAD and bounded dirty status into one wrapper that threw a generic exception when any component produced a diagnostic, hiding the component result.
entries.rootCause: Three independently admissible Git facts were coupled behind one fail-fast exception instead of being captured and validated separately with their own exit, stdout and stderr ownership.
entries.prevention: Run branch, HEAD and dirty ownership as independent bounded process reads. Capture each exit, stdout and stderr separately, emit only deterministic scalar summaries, and never let one component diagnostic hide the other reconciliation facts.

entries.mistake: A read-only r60.47 owner-metrics command failed at parse time because its materialized foreach expression lacked the closing statement-block brace.
entries.rootCause: The loop, conditional row construction and formatter were compressed into one inline expression without verifying the brace pairing before execution.
entries.prevention: Use a simple statement-form foreach that appends rows to a ticket-specific collection, close the loop before formatting, and visually verify every block delimiter before the command runs.

entries.mistake: A bounded C30U owner filename inventory used PowerShell -replace with a lone backslash regex, causing repeated invalid-pattern errors and zero admissible results.
entries.rootCause: Literal Windows separator normalization was incorrectly implemented as a regular-expression replacement despite permanent memory requiring literal normalization.
