entries.prevention: Normalize repository-relative paths only with `.Replace([char]92, [char]47)` or omit normalization for a case-insensitive token filter. Capture rg output and its immediate native exit before filtering, cap the accepted rows, and reject every diagnostic stream.

entries.mistake: A bounded Select-String context projection was rejected at parse time because the pipeline variable member access was written as `$_ .Line` with an invalid separating space.
entries.rootCause: A custom context-rendering pipeline was composed for one already-located token instead of using a simpler numeric range read, and the member-access token was not syntax-checked.
entries.prevention: For one located token, read its scalar line number and then one bounded Get-Content numeric range. If pipeline member access is unavoidable, keep `$_.Member` contiguous and parser-check the command before execution.

entries.mistake: After two identical C30V qualification cycles passed, a direct build-phase gate invocation rejected the candidate because the single-build readiness or final source/preserved-service proof differed, before any founder prompt or AAB build.
entries.rootCause: The direct diagnostic invoked the build-phase gate too early. Its two founder-qualified runtime flags are intentionally false after qualification and are set true only inside the visible founder launcher after both hidden inputs validate and immediately before the launcher invokes the build wrapper.
entries.prevention: After two identical cycles, do not invoke the build phase directly while founder-qualified runtime flags are false. Launch only the already-qualified visible founder wrapper; it owns hidden-input validation, transient runtime qualification, the build-phase gate, and cleanup. Direct reconcile reads remain admissible before the prompt.

entries.mistake: The first visible C30V founder launcher process exited immediately before presenting or consuming its prompts because the `-File` launcher path containing spaces was supplied to Start-Process as an unquoted argument-list element.
entries.rootCause: Start-Process joined the argument list for the child command line without preserving the spaced launcher path as one explicitly quoted `-File` value.
entries.prevention: For a visible PowerShell launcher under a spaced workspace path, pass one deliberately constructed argument string whose `-File` value is wrapped in literal double quotes. After any immediate exit, prove machine state and all action counts before retrying; never infer prompt or build progress from process creation alone.

entries.mistake: The first browser file-selection call was rejected at JavaScript parse time because the nested tool-call object wrote the `timeout_ms` property name with template-literal delimiters.
entries.rootCause: The outer code-mode JavaScript object and the nested browser-tool argument object were composed without a syntax check, and a plain property name was accidentally written as a template string.
entries.prevention: Before a Play upload browser call, keep the nested tool arguments on a minimal plain JavaScript object and verify every property delimiter. A parse-time rejection must be treated as no upload; confirm the page still shows no candidate before one corrected retry.

entries.mistake: The corrected Play file-selection attempt called standard Playwright `setInputFiles` on the browser-client locator, but that locator API does not expose the method, so the call failed before file selection.
entries.rootCause: The browser-client locator surface was assumed to match raw Playwright file-input methods instead of using the plugin's documented supported upload mechanism.
entries.prevention: Before retrying a browser file upload, read the exact browser-client upload API or its local implementation contract, confirm r60.47 remains absent on the page, and use only the supported file chooser or upload method with the exact sealed AAB path.

entries.mistake: A bounded browser-client upload-API search matched a single minified bundle line, causing the tool output to be truncated even though only the file-chooser interface was needed.
entries.rootCause: Line-count bounding does not bound byte size when a generated JavaScript bundle is minified onto one very large line.
entries.prevention: For minified browser-client code, never emit matching source lines. Read the exact known file once and extract only the narrowly bounded API-manifest substring for the named interface, with an explicit maximum length, before composing the browser call.

entries.mistake: The sealed r60.47 AAB was attached once to the Internal Testing draft after the postbuild gate but before an explicit invocation of the C30V `preupload` phase gate.
entries.rootCause: The postbuild proof was incorrectly treated as the immediate upload-readiness transition even though the C30V gate has a distinct `preupload` phase.
entries.prevention: For every future Play release, invoke and preserve the exact preupload phase immediately before opening or using the file chooser. For this already attached one-file draft, run the still-valid preupload gate before final activation, prohibit any second file selection, and consume upload count only after Play proves the Internal release active.

entries.mistake: After the founder confirmed final Internal activation in a new turn, the first Save-and-publish click targeted the prior browser-client tab handle, but that agent tab had been cleaned up between turns and the action failed with `Tab not found`.
entries.rootCause: A tab binding was assumed to survive the confirmation boundary even though browser bindings and tab bindings have different lifetimes and the tab list was empty after cleanup.
entries.prevention: At every post-confirmation continuation, list agent tabs first. If the prior tab is absent, discard the stale handle, create a fresh tab from the existing browser binding, navigate to the exact Internal track, recover the existing draft without selecting another file, and only then perform the confirmed publish action.

entries.mistake: The final Google Play publish modal was visible and the nested confirmation action returned a locator-deadline error during the transition, creating ambiguity about whether the representational action completed.
entries.rootCause: The browser-client response observed the modal locator after Google Play had already navigated back to the track, so the tool reported no remaining match even though the confirmation side effect completed.
entries.prevention: Any browser error around a state-changing confirmation is outcome-unknown, never a safe retry signal. Immediately read the exact target track. If it proves the candidate active, record the completed single action and do not click again; retry only when durable external readback proves no mutation.

entries.mistake: The preinstall OPPO identity read invoked `cmd package get-install-source`, but this device's package shell does not support that subcommand and returned exit 255.
entries.rootCause: A package-manager diagnostic available on some Android builds was assumed to exist on the OPPO firmware instead of reusing the previously proven supported installer query.
entries.prevention: On OPPO CPH2375, prove installer identity with the exact supported `pm list packages -i com.moolsocial.app` row and require `installer=com.android.vending`. Treat unsupported diagnostics as no evidence and never substitute an install action.

entries.mistake: The first post-cold-launch device diagnostic assigned app process output to PowerShell's reserved `$PID` variable, causing a read-only-variable error and making that emitted process scalar inadmissible.
entries.rootCause: A common shell automatic variable name was reused instead of a ticket-specific diagnostic variable.
entries.prevention: Never assign to `$PID`, `$HOME`, or other automatic/system variables. Use a ticket-specific name such as `$c30vAppProcessId`, capture every native exit separately, and discard all scalar conclusions from a command that emitted a PowerShell error.

entries.mistake: The Play-installed r60.47 app resumes and receives focus but renders no usable UI because `main` throws an unhandled release-configuration exception before `runApp` when the Google server client ID define is absent from the AAB.
entries.rootCause: The r60.47 build path and two-cycle qualification proved manifest/resources/static validation but did not prove that every required Dart release define was embedded and that the resulting release runtime reached a rendered first frame. The existing configured Play predecessor masked this missing candidate-specific runtime proof.
entries.prevention: Every future Android release candidate must fail closed unless a secret-safe release-define key-name gate proves the complete required key set, a release-configured runtime smoke test reaches `runApp`, and the Play-installed candidate cold-launches to a named interactive screen with no app-process Flutter/AndroidRuntime error or ANR. Static manifest/config-only checks alone can never qualify an AAB.

entries.mistake: The new cold-start regression entry listed the planned C30W gate script and test file in its executable `gates` array before those files existed, so the regression-memory gate failed on missing repository evidence.
entries.rootCause: Mandatory future controls were confused with current executable gate owners during registration order.
entries.prevention: A registry entry's `gates` array may contain only paths that already exist and are executable/readable at registration time. Planned owners belong in findings/prevention text until created and verified; add them to the registry only afterward.

entries.mistake: A secret-safe launcher key-name inventory command failed at parse time because a character class containing both quote forms was embedded incorrectly in a double-quoted PowerShell regex literal.
entries.rootCause: The inventory only needed `MOOLSOCIAL_` token names, but an unnecessary surrounding-quote matcher introduced avoidable PowerShell escaping complexity.
entries.prevention: For secret-safe key-name inventories, match only the simple token pattern `MOOLSOCIAL_[A-Z0-9_]+`, emit unique token names, and never compose mixed-quote regex character classes inline. Parser-check any nontrivial diagnostic before execution.

entries.mistake: The C30W scope transition diagnostic emitted the entire large MVP scope-state JSON, causing tool-output truncation even though only the current selection, ticket, authorization, execution, protected-candidate and provider tail owners were needed.
entries.rootCause: A full-owner read was used after the exact mutable tail sections and selected assessment were already known.
entries.prevention: For large governance owners, locate exact unique section keys and read only bounded numeric ranges or scalar projections. Never emit historical assessment collections when transitioning one current ticket.

entries.mistake: The first C30W MVP scope transition patch failed verification because it expected a stale C30V selected-assessment sentence that did not exactly match the current owner.
entries.rootCause: The patch was composed from an earlier summarized/truncated representation rather than a fresh bounded serialization of the exact current selected assessment and tail owners.
entries.prevention: Before patching a large living governance owner, serialize only the exact current subobjects, copy their current literals verbatim, and split the transition into small independently verified patches. A failed verification means no mutation and must not be retried from the same stale context.

entries.mistake: The interrupted C30W wrapper inspection used one broad multi-token ripgrep query against a PowerShell gate containing large embedded source assertions, and the resulting tool output was truncated before the required launcher checks could be established.
entries.rootCause: The exact wrapper owner was known, but the inspection still emitted every matching line for several generic terms rather than first locating one exact token and then reading a bounded numeric range.
entries.prevention: Inspect release wrappers only through exact token line-number discovery followed by small numeric Get-Content ranges. Never emit broad multi-token matches or embedded here-string bodies when one gate clause is required.

entries.mistake: The resumed C30W reconciliation invoked the repository-mandated full short status literally and rendered the established huge dirty tree, causing output truncation instead of a complete admissible ownership summary.
entries.rootCause: The repository instruction to run status was followed without applying the many active workspace-specific memories that require capturing the command in memory and emitting only scalar counts and digests.
entries.prevention: For this repository, read branch and HEAD as scalars, capture tracked status with untracked traversal disabled and separate stderr, and emit only record count plus SHA-256. Inspect only exact C30W owners afterward; never render the complete dirty path list.

entries.mistake: The first exact-file Dart formatting command ran from apps/mobile but passed `main.dart` instead of the repository-relative mobile path `lib/main.dart`. Dart reported the missing target while formatting the three valid files.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed a filename copied from the repository root context with paths relative to the apps/mobile working directory.
entries.prevention: Before every exact-file mobile formatting command, resolve each argument relative to apps/mobile and require `lib/main.dart` for the bootstrap owner. Treat any missing-target diagnostic as a rejected formatting attempt even if Dart exits zero.

entries.mistake: The first C30W source gate rejected the safe fallback because it searched for one complete customer sentence while Dart represented the sentence as adjacent wrapped string literals.
entries.rootCause: The static gate asserted rendered-copy contiguity against source text instead of checking stable literal fragments and relying on the widget test for the fully rendered sentence.
entries.prevention: Static Dart copy checks must assert stable source-literal fragments only. Rendered sentence composition belongs to the widget test; source formatting and adjacent literals may not create a false release rejection.

entries.mistake: The first C30W focused test load failed because the new secret-leak copy assertion referenced Flutter's `Text` type without importing package:flutter/material.dart.
entries.rootCause: flutter_test was incorrectly assumed to re-export the Material widget types used explicitly by the test's generic widget inspection.
entries.prevention: Every widget test that names Material types directly must import package:flutter/material.dart. Run the exact test load before admitting any new focused-manifest result.

entries.mistake: The first C30W analyzer command ran from the repository root, causing Flutter to inspect preserved historical artifact trees and report 15,999 irrelevant issues with truncated output instead of analyzing the mobile package.
entries.rootCause: The source gate and Flutter analyzer were combined under one repository-root working directory even though Flutter's authoritative package root is apps/mobile.
entries.prevention: Run repository PowerShell gates from the repository root and Flutter analyze only from apps/mobile as separate commands. Never analyze preserved artifact/evidence trees or treat their intentional rejected fixtures as current source.

entries.mistake: The pre-cycle-two regression-memory invocation supplied the unsupported phase value `qualification`; the ValidateSet rejected before the second Flutter cycle started.
entries.rootCause: A conceptual workflow phase was passed without checking the gate's executable phase set of general, implementation, build and device.
entries.prevention: Use the supported `implementation` phase for source/test qualification cycles. Validate gate parameter sets before composing a new invocation; a parameter rejection means the intended cycle did not start.

entries.mistake: The C30W qualification update replaced the MVP scope owner's exact top-level `ticket_disclosed_and_authorized` sentinel with a source-progress label, so the final scope replay failed closed.
entries.rootCause: An authorization contract field was mistaken for a mutable implementation-progress field even though dedicated assessment, checkpoint and provider fields already own progress.
entries.prevention: Preserve the exact top-level scope authorization sentinel for the lifetime of an authorized ticket. Record implementation and qualification progress only in dedicated implementationState, checkpoint, provider and ticket machine-state owners.

entries.mistake: A read-only C30W owner-metrics command placed statement-form if expressions directly inside pscustomobject property values, so PowerShell rejected the command before producing an inventory.
entries.rootCause: Conditional property values were composed inline instead of being calculated into ticket-specific scalars before object construction, repeating an existing statement-expression boundary lesson.
entries.prevention: Compute existence, line-count and byte-length values into explicit scalars before constructing a PowerShell object. Diagnostic projections contain scalar assignments only; statement-form if and foreach blocks stay outside object literals and formatter pipelines.

entries.mistake: A deliberate read-only replay of the failed r60.47 state asserted the later not-founder-qualified exception, but the historical state correctly rejected earlier because the successor-only googleServerClientIdQualifiedByFounder property is absent.
entries.rootCause: The current failed candidate runtimeConfiguration property names were not enumerated before composing an exact expected exception, so a successor schema was assumed for a historical state.
entries.prevention: Enumerate the exact current nested state schema before every negative release replay and derive the first fail-closed condition from that state plus the current gate. Historical candidates may lawfully reject earlier than successor states; exact-message qualification requires the current boundary.

entries.mistake: Two dense 200-line ACTIVE-CODEX-HANDOFF owner windows were requested in one tool call, and the combined returned output exceeded the available context and was truncated, so the attempted range provided zero admissible read evidence.
entries.rootCause: The command respected the per-window line limit but failed to budget the aggregate result volume of multiple dense windows in one tool response.
entries.prevention: Request one dense owner-document window per tool call, keep it at 200 lines or fewer, and verify both requested boundary line numbers before advancing the read cursor. Any truncation marker or missing final line is zero evidence.

entries.mistake: A bounded read-only reviewer-package metrics command piped directly from a statement-form foreach block into ConvertTo-Json, so PowerShell rejected the command before producing evidence.
entries.rootCause: The result-producing loop was placed at the pipeline boundary instead of being assigned to an explicit array before formatting.
entries.prevention: Assign foreach output to a task-specific array, then pipe only that completed array to ConvertTo-Json. Keep the path list explicit and treat any parser rejection as zero evidence.

entries.mistake: A read-only reviewer-package test-owner search included guessed apps/web/test and test directories alongside the real apps/web/tests owner, causing a nonzero result that could not be admitted as clean evidence.
entries.rootCause: Likely test-directory conventions were supplied before enumerating the exact bounded web directory structure.
entries.prevention: Enumerate exact owners with rg --files first, search only proved paths, and reject mixed-success nonzero discovery output rather than using its partial match to choose a gate.

entries.mistake: A read-only post-YouTube planning search supplied a remembered descriptive filename for the Universal preauthorized backlog instead of an enumerated exact path, so rg rejected the nonexistent owner before reading content.
entries.rootCause: A document title from the required owner read was converted into a guessed filesystem name.
entries.prevention: Enumerate exact delivery filenames with rg --files, copy the returned path literally, and never synthesize repository owner filenames from remembered titles.

entries.mistake: A read-only final C30W seal check requested a guessed focused-source-manifest-c30w.txt filename instead of enumerating the exact bounded evidence-directory owner, so the path failed before content was read.
entries.rootCause: The remembered concept of a focused source manifest was converted into a filename despite an available exact directory inventory.
entries.prevention: Enumerate the bounded C30W evidence directory, copy the returned basename literally, and never infer filename segments from a document description.

entries.mistake: The final overnight report total update used an expected sentence that did not match the report's exact regression-memory wording, so apply_patch rejected without changing the file.
entries.rootCause: The semantic content was recalled correctly but the exact target line was not enumerated immediately before constructing the patch.
entries.prevention: Use rg to enumerate the exact bounded report line immediately before a precision patch, copy that line literally into the patch context, and treat any apply_patch verification failure as zero mutation and a registered retry boundary.

entries.mistake: The first autonomous Buy discovery command requested remembered PRE-TICKET-REUSE-CHECKPOINT and delivery/ACTIVE-CODEX-HANDOFF paths that do not exist at those locations, so the combined command exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: Owner document titles were converted into likely filesystem paths instead of copying exact paths from a bounded repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files with exact filename fragments before each new owner read, copy the returned paths literally, and reject every mixed-success nonzero command as zero admissible evidence.

entries.mistake: The first autonomous Buy discovery command combined AGENTS, a large machine-state owner and broad Buy/backend search output, exceeding the tool result budget and producing truncated output.
entries.rootCause: Several individually relevant reads were composed into one response without budgeting their aggregate density and output size.
entries.prevention: Read one dense owner per tool call, constrain searches by exact enumerated path and narrow patterns, and require the requested final boundary to be visible before accepting the result as evidence.

entries.mistake: A metrics-only owner inventory piped directly from a statement-form foreach block into ConvertTo-Json, repeating the registered PowerShell parser boundary and producing no evidence.
entries.rootCause: The applicable regression lesson was not applied when composing a new diagnostic command after the preceding path-discovery retry.
entries.prevention: Before every PowerShell owner inventory, assign foreach output to a task-specific result array and pipe only that completed array to formatting. Run the implementation regression-memory gate before any product write.

entries.mistake: The Buy mobile-owner search included retained candidate captures, golden images and failure images, producing thousands of matching paths and a truncated result.
entries.rootCause: The inventory filtered by Buy-related names but did not first restrict the result to executable Dart source and test owners.
entries.prevention: For mobile implementation inventory, enumerate only *.dart under exact lib and test roots and explicitly exclude candidate_captures, failures, goldens and retained artifact directories before applying domain-name filters.

entries.mistake: The implementation regression-memory gate was invoked with a repository-relative scripts path while the process working directory was backend/functions, so pwsh could not resolve the script.
entries.rootCause: A repository-root gate and a package-local typecheck were combined under the package working directory without resolving their different path owners.
entries.prevention: Run repository machine gates from the repository root in their own tool call. Run package commands separately from the exact package directory only after the repository gate passes.

entries.mistake: A failed regression-gate invocation was followed by npm typecheck in one shell command, and the later successful command yielded an overall zero exit despite the earlier failure.
entries.rootCause: Two independent qualification boundaries were sequenced without fail-fast handling, allowing the shell's final-command exit code to mask the first failure.
entries.prevention: Run each qualification gate in its own tool call, or use explicit fail-fast exit handling. Never accept a combined result when any constituent command prints an error even if the overall exit is zero.

entries.mistake: The repository-global Buy backend absence-boundary gate was invoked even though durable evidence already records that the preserved acceptance_policy_governance_contract.test.ts owner is outside its historical allowlist; the gate correctly rejected that owner.
entries.rootCause: The current domain-state audit was reconciled, but the older gate's known dirty-tree incompatibility was not checked against the applicable regression record before invocation.
entries.prevention: Before invoking any repository-global Buy boundary, search durable regression and handoff evidence for its current dirty-tree compatibility. Do not weaken the gate or mutate the separately ticketed owner; report the known rejection and use exact per-ticket hash/typecheck/test evidence until a separately authorized additive boundary replacement exists.

entries.mistake: The read-only full compiled backend test corpus used Node's verbose default reporter, producing more than five hundred result lines and a truncated tool response even though the final process exit was zero.
entries.rootCause: Test runtime and count were budgeted, but reporter output volume was not bounded before the whole-corpus invocation.
entries.prevention: Capture whole-corpus test output in memory, emit only exit status and exact test/pass/fail/cancelled/skipped/todo/duration summary lines, and emit bounded diagnostic tails only on failure. A truncated response is zero accepted evidence.

entries.mistake: The first full-Chat reference discovery searched every Markdown file under the large docs tree with a broad multi-alternative regex and exceeded the bounded command timeout.
entries.rootCause: The search scope included the complete retained evidence corpus before exact Chat ticket, manifest and handoff owners were enumerated.
entries.prevention: Search approved-references/manifest.json and exact filename inventories first, then query only enumerated Chat handoff, ticket, delivery and design-memory owners. A timed-out search is zero evidence and must not be retried broadly.

entries.mistake: The first Chat Dart-owner inventory supplied a guessed apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/chat directory even though the current Chat presentation owners live under apps/mobile/lib/features/chat, causing rg to exit nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The general V2 presentation convention was applied before enumerating the exact current Chat source roots.
entries.prevention: Enumerate Dart files from the existing apps/mobile/lib and apps/mobile/test roots, filter the returned paths for Chat, and never infer a feature subdirectory from naming conventions.

entries.mistake: The first backend Chat symbol inventory included guessed backend/functions/test and backend/functions/tests directories even though Chat tests are colocated under backend/functions/src/chat, causing the combined command to exit nonzero.
entries.rootCause: Common package test-directory conventions were supplied before the bounded backend Chat file inventory had proved the repository's colocated test owner.
entries.prevention: Enumerate exact backend/functions/src Chat files first and search only paths returned by that inventory. Never add conventional test roots unless the repository inventory proves they exist.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to register the backend Chat path mistake requested config/development-regression-memory.json instead of the authoritative config/codex-development-regression-registry.json owner, causing the lookup to exit nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The regression-memory document title was converted into a guessed config filename instead of enumerating the bounded config root.
entries.prevention: Enumerate config filenames with rg --files before every registry lookup and copy the exact codex-development-regression-registry.json path literally.

entries.mistake: The first full-Chat implementation regression gate invocation used an unsupported -Mode parameter, so PowerShell rejected the command before the gate executed.
entries.rootCause: The intended implementation phase was mapped to a remembered generic parameter name instead of reading the gate's declared param block, which defines -Phase.
entries.prevention: Read the exact gate param block before first invocation in a task and use -Phase implementation exactly. A PowerShell parameter-binding rejection is zero gate evidence.

entries.mistake: The first full-Chat baseline invoked Flutter's compact reporter directly; carriage-return progress expanded into thousands of captured tokens and the tool response was truncated despite a zero process exit.
entries.rootCause: The compact terminal reporter was treated as compact captured output even though the execution bridge preserves repeated carriage-return progress frames.
entries.prevention: Capture Flutter test output to a task-local in-memory variable, emit only the final pass/fail summary on success, and emit a bounded diagnostic tail on failure. A truncated direct reporter response is zero accepted evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C31A backend typecheck rejected a fake-repository tuple because its optional final string element was populated explicitly with string or undefined under exact optional typing.
entries.rootCause: The test double modeled an always-present captured call slot as an optional tuple position instead of an explicit string-or-undefined position.
entries.prevention: When a test double records every argument position, declare the tuple slot as string | undefined rather than using optional tuple syntax. Run backend typecheck before compiled tests.

entries.mistake: The first C31A focused Flutter analyzer rejected an if-guarded optional replyToMessageId map entry under the enabled use_null_aware_elements lint.
entries.rootCause: The additive gateway request used the older conditional collection-element form instead of the repository's current Dart null-aware map-value element syntax.
entries.prevention: Represent optional request values with the Dart null-aware map-value form key: ?value and run the focused analyzer before tests.

entries.mistake: The first null-aware syntax correction patch used the pre-format two-line conditional map-entry shape after dart format had condensed it to one line, so apply_patch rejected with zero changes.
entries.rootCause: The exact target line was not enumerated after the formatting command and before constructing the precision patch.
entries.prevention: After any formatter changes a file, enumerate the exact bounded target lines immediately before every follow-up precision patch and copy the current context literally.

entries.mistake: The first compiled C31A backend test process exited zero, but its success summarizer required count lines to begin exactly with # and emitted no test, pass or fail counts in the captured environment.
entries.rootCause: The summary parser assumed an exact Node test reporter line anchor without first preserving a bounded sample of the environment's captured output shape.
entries.prevention: For a focused Node test file, emit the bounded final output tail on success and failure; accept qualification only when exact tests, pass and fail lines are visible.

entries.mistake: The first draft of the C31A Firestore test fake used Dart constructor shorthand and initializer-list syntax inside a TypeScript file; review caught it before typecheck or test execution.
entries.rootCause: The fake was authored immediately after Flutter model work and constructor syntax from Dart crossed into the TypeScript test owner.
entries.prevention: For cross-language implementation waves, review every newly added class constructor against the target language before first typecheck; TypeScript fakes must declare fields and assign them in explicit constructor bodies.

entries.mistake: The first C31B Firestore test additions used Dart's .single collection accessor in three TypeScript assertions; source review caught the recurrence before typecheck.
entries.rootCause: The registered cross-language prevention checked new class constructors but did not require a whole-added-block scan for Dart collection APIs before compiling TypeScript tests.
entries.prevention: Before first TypeScript typecheck after Flutter work, scan every added TypeScript test block for Dart-only constructor, final, Future, .single, map and collection syntax; use indexed access or exact JavaScript methods and let no known cross-language pattern remain.

entries.mistake: The first C31B read-state addition left reply and reaction eligibility checking exact delivered equality, which would hide those actions once a message advanced to read; review caught it before tests.
entries.rootCause: A new terminal success state was added without auditing every feature guard that treated delivered as the only settled message state.
entries.prevention: Whenever ChatDeliveryState expands, enumerate every equality guard and switch; define settled eligibility as delivered or read, while sending and failed remain ineligible, and retain a regression for actions on a read message.

entries.mistake: The first expanded TypeScript language-boundary scan classified valid JavaScript String(...) conversion as Dart syntax and exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic regex included ambiguous cross-language tokens instead of only constructs that are invalid in TypeScript test code.
entries.prevention: Language-boundary scans must target only unambiguous Dart-only patterns such as .single, Future<, final declarations, StateError(, .addAll( and .containsKey(; do not reject shared identifiers or valid JavaScript constructors.

entries.mistake: The first C31B repository test run reached the real listMessages flow, but the bounded Firestore fake lacked DocumentReference.get(), causing two TypeError failures.
entries.rootCause: The C31A fake covered transaction reads and collection queries but was not expanded through the non-transaction threadForParticipant document-read contract before C31B tests ran.
entries.prevention: Before exercising a new Firestore repository path, trace every runtime method on collection, query, document, snapshot and transaction references and implement the bounded fake surface before compiling tests.

entries.mistake: The first C31B service test expected the new mutation to reject as a promise, but markThreadRead was not declared async and invalid identifier validation threw synchronously before assert.rejects could own it.
entries.rootCause: The new operation returned a repository promise on success but did not match the explicit async contract used by sibling Chat mutation service methods.
entries.prevention: Declare every Chat mutation service method async so validation and repository failures share one promise-rejection contract, then cover invalid input with assert.rejects.

entries.mistake: The first C31C MVP scope-state update used one oversized multi-hunk patch whose tool response exceeded the available context and was truncated, leaving the mutation result inadmissible until separately verified.
entries.rootCause: The machine-state change bundled distant nested owners into one tool call instead of using bounded patches followed by exact schema-aware projections.
entries.prevention: Split large machine-state changes into bounded exact blocks, parse JSON after every block, enumerate the current nested schema before projecting values, and accept only a compact projection of required non-null authority fields.

entries.mistake: The first C31C compile checkpoint combined repository-relative backend paths with an apps/mobile working directory, so Select-String resolved the backend owners under apps/mobile and failed before format or compilation.
entries.rootCause: One shell call crossed backend and Flutter owner roots without making every path absolute or choosing the repository root.
entries.prevention: Run backend source audits from the repository root and Flutter formatter/analyzer commands from apps/mobile in separate calls; never mix relative owners from different roots in one working directory.

entries.mistake: The first focused C31C Flutter run passed and printed all 15 authored tests, but an auxiliary regex expected pass lines to begin with +N and incorrectly emitted expandedPassLines=0 because Flutter prefixes elapsed time.
entries.rootCause: The custom counter parsed presentation text instead of the Flutter machine-readable event stream.
entries.prevention: Use Flutter's JSON reporter for counted qualification, join testDone events to testStart metadata, exclude only loading or synthetic tests, preserve the native exit, and print failed test names before any retry.

entries.mistake: The first C31C Flutter JSON join returned 16 passes for a visibly 15-test file because the synthetic event name was path-qualified as loading plus the file URL instead of exactly loading.
entries.rootCause: The parser excluded only an exact loading name and did not apply the repository rule to loading-prefixed synthetic testStart metadata.
entries.prevention: Exclude a Flutter JSON test only when hidden is true, its name equals loading, or its name begins with loading followed by a space; preserve raw testDone separately and assert the authored count against current source names.

entries.mistake: C31C strengthened the C31B read-message action test but renamed it from the exact historical phrase expected by the sealed C31B static gate; source review caught the drift before running that gate.
entries.rootCause: The successor assertion was added by replacing the existing test description instead of preserving the historical description as a stable prefix.
entries.prevention: Successor tests may append scope to a historical test name but must preserve every predecessor static-gate literal exactly; replay predecessor gates before C31C qualification.

entries.mistake: The first patch intended to register and repair the historical test-name drift was rejected atomically because it used the pre-format one-line declaration while Dart format had split the owner across lines.
entries.rootCause: The source correction reused remembered patch context after a formatter mutation instead of rereading the exact bounded owner.
entries.prevention: After any formatter runs, reread the exact 10-line target region immediately before a source patch; a rejected multi-file patch is verified as zero mutation before retry.

entries.mistake: The first predecessor replay under active C31C failed because the C31A gate recognized only active C31B as its recorded direct successor and did not verify C31B's recorded C31C successor chain.
entries.rootCause: The historical gate implemented one-hop successor continuity while the full Chat program now has a second separately registered child sharing the same owners.
entries.prevention: A historical Chat gate may accept a later active child only by verifying each explicit machine-state hop and every predecessor-preservation boolean; narrative ancestry or an unregistered descendant never passes.

entries.mistake: The first combined C31C Chat run compared the newly visible Forward action against three sealed C31A/C31B golden paths, so all three predecessor visual cases failed.
entries.rootCause: The successor UI changed a shared message-bubble action row without first versioning each affected visual expectation to a new C31C path.
entries.prevention: Never overwrite predecessor Chat goldens; preserve their bytes, version every affected shared-owner visual case to a new C31C filename, generate only absent successor PNGs and replay both historical static gates.

entries.mistake: The first combined C31C Chat run asserted 39 authored tests by adding new tests to a remembered prior total, while the current three-file JSON join identified 28 authored tests before repair.
entries.rootCause: The expected total was inferred from historical handoff prose rather than the exact current selected file inventory and joined testStart metadata.
entries.prevention: Derive each qualification expectation from the exact current manifest and a bounded JSON name inventory; never arithmetically extend a remembered pass count across a changed file set.

entries.mistake: The post-C31C global approved-UI-lock audit rejected the pre-existing apps/mobile/test/platform_configuration_test.dart checksum for the login-account-handoff accepted production file.
entries.rootCause: The founder-owned dirty tree already contains protected platform-configuration test drift outside the C31C Chat owner set; C31C neither selected nor modified that file.
entries.prevention: Do not reseal, restore or edit a protected unrelated owner under a Chat ticket. Keep the global lock result failed, qualify only exact C31C owners, and require separate founder-authorized protected-lock reconciliation before any release claim.

entries.mistake: A read-only recursive C31B evidence inventory included the entire compiled backend-lib tree and truncated the output before a useful bounded artifact list could be accepted.
entries.rootCause: The lookup targeted an evidence directory with hundreds of generated compiler outputs when only the already known source manifest and state owners were relevant.
entries.prevention: Qualification reconciliation reads exact known manifest, state, assessment and log paths; never recursively enumerate a compiled evidence subtree to discover already registered owners.

entries.mistake: The first AAB-preparation audit printed the complete C30W gate, the large single-AAB wrapper and the wrapper static gate in one call; the tool output truncated before the wrapper could be reviewed completely.
entries.rootCause: Three large release-control owners were bundled into a broad read instead of locating exact symbols and reading bounded regions independently.
entries.prevention: Release-control audits first locate exact symbols, then read one bounded 20-40 line region per owner. A truncated combined read is zero audit evidence and is never used to approve or modify a build gate.

entries.mistake: The single-AAB wrapper verifies that the release GeneratedPluginRegistrant contains exactly 16 plugins but writes releaseRegistrantPluginCount = 15 into the post-build provenance record.
entries.rootCause: The provenance literal was not updated when the exact qualified release plugin set increased to 16, and the wrapper static gate does not compare the assertion count with the provenance count.
entries.prevention: Before any successor AAB, derive one exact release-plugin count once, use it for both the prebuild registrant assertion and provenance, and make the static gate require those two owners to be identical. A mismatch blocks build authority.

entries.mistake: The current C30V postupload, postinstall and journey phases require versionCode 2026081347 and versionName 1.0.0-r60.47, while the single-AAB wrapper contract switch does not recognize any successor gate contract.
entries.rootCause: Historical r60.47 acceptance owners were reused as the apparent future entry point even though their version identity and launcher remain intentionally sealed to the failed candidate.
entries.prevention: Never mutate or reuse the failed r60.47 state for a successor. Create a new exact successor candidate contract whose version comparisons derive from its own candidate object, add it explicitly to the wrapper allowlist, and statically prove the historical r60.47 owners remain unchanged.

entries.mistake: The C30V postbuild gate resolves the sealed AAB and provenance paths but does not compare current AAB SHA-256, byte length, signer, package/version or provenance bindings; preupload checks only buildCount and uploadCount.
entries.rootCause: Artifact proofs are calculated inside the build wrapper, but the later state gate trusts boolean fields and file existence instead of independently rebinding the bytes immediately before upload.
entries.prevention: The successor postbuild and preupload phases must parse non-secret provenance, recompute AAB SHA-256 and byte length, require exact candidate/package/version/signer bindings, re-run bundle structure/resource proofs or verify their immutable evidence, and reject any mismatch before upload authority can be used.

entries.mistake: A read-only repository search combined broad release, scope, Chat and regression terms; long matching JSON lines exceeded the output budget and truncated the result.
entries.rootCause: The audit searched several known owners and broad directories in one command even though the exact wrapper, state gate, scope state and Chat gate paths were already known.
entries.prevention: Release preparation must query one exact known owner and one exact symbol set at a time, bound every line region, and treat truncated output as zero audit evidence.

entries.mistake: The C30V AAB wrapper static gate passes in PowerShell 7 but throws a MethodException in Windows PowerShell because it calls String.Contains with a StringComparison argument that is unavailable on Windows PowerShell's .NET Framework runtime.
entries.rootCause: The static gate used a modern .NET overload without a cross-host compatibility owner even though release qualification requires both PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell.
entries.prevention: Use an explicit ordinal IndexOf comparison for case-sensitive and case-insensitive literal checks, then require the same static gate to pass in both PowerShell hosts before successor build authority can become available.

entries.mistake: The first resolution-status patch guessed the final sentence of the plugin-count evidence document and apply_patch rejected the entire multi-file patch.
entries.rootCause: The patch reused remembered wording instead of reading the exact current document tail before appending the resolution evidence.
entries.prevention: Read the exact bounded tail of every documentation target before a multi-file resolution patch; patch status and evidence in small independently verifiable units.

entries.mistake: A bounded symbol lookup for the C30W release gate passed an incorrectly escaped alternation to rg and the regex parser rejected it before returning any lines.
entries.rootCause: A PowerShell variable expression and regex grouping were mixed in one shell-escaped query even though fixed-string searches were sufficient.
entries.prevention: Use separate fixed-string rg queries or direct bounded line reads for known PowerShell phase labels; a regex parser error is zero evidence and must not be retried unchanged.

entries.mistake: The first current authoritative Flutter-manifest audit was launched with a one-second command timeout; the shell wrapper terminated it before a verdict could be produced.
entries.rootCause: An interactive-yield assumption was applied to a shell command tool that enforces its timeout by terminating the process rather than returning a resumable execution cell.
entries.prevention: Run the bounded 59-file authoritative audit with a build-appropriate terminal timeout and capture one immutable complete log; never infer a test result from a terminated partial run.

entries.mistake: The current 59-file C30W Flutter manifest produced 417 authored passes, 3 declared skips and zero failures/errors, but the reusable audit runner exited one because its default expected-pass count remains the historical C30T value 405.
entries.rootCause: The runner has a stale default manifest and expected count, and the audit invocation selected the current manifest without explicitly binding its current authored-test count.
entries.prevention: The successor gate must provide an explicit count pinned to the exact current focused-manifest file and hash, and the reusable runner must not silently apply a historical default to a different manifest.

entries.mistake: The new stale-Flutter-count regression entry named the planned C30X gate before that file existed, so the regression-memory validator correctly rejected the registry.
entries.rootCause: A future prevention owner was placed in the machine-validated gates array, whose contract requires every referenced path to exist at registration time.
entries.prevention: Regression entries list only existing gate files. Add a successor gate reference only in a later registered strengthening after the file exists; never use the gates field as a future-work placeholder.

entries.mistake: The complete 53-file backend test run was streamed through Tee-Object to the tool console, and the 528 passing test names exceeded the output budget even though the retained log completed successfully.
entries.rootCause: The command combined immutable full-log capture with unbounded console emission instead of writing the full runner output to evidence and printing only the final bounded summary.
entries.prevention: Full backend regressions write all output directly to a unique evidence log, check the native exit code, and emit only the final tests/pass/fail/skipped/duration summary to the console.

entries.mistake: The combined negative release-phase test reached postupload with an empty artifact path, but PowerShell's mandatory-string binder rejected the argument before the C30X gate could emit its exact fail-closed evidence message.
entries.rootCause: The repository path and JSON readers asserted empty paths inside their bodies but did not allow an empty string through parameter binding, and postupload attempted artifact rebinding before validating its state transition.
entries.prevention: Allow empty strings at helper binding solely so the gate can reject them with its own exact message, and validate each phase state/count transition before resolving artifact or evidence paths. Negative tests must assert the exact C30X rejection owner.

entries.mistake: The failed r60.47 candidate state records sourceQualification.analyzerPassed=true while its aggregate records sourceQualification.wholeMobileAnalyzerClean=false, so the historical aggregate cannot be reused as truthful successor readiness evidence.
entries.rootCause: Two release-state owners recorded conflicting analyzer truth and the historical phase gate did not require equality between them before the candidate advanced.
entries.prevention: Preserve the failed r60.47 records unchanged, never reuse their qualification, and require one fresh successor state whose analyzer result, evidence log and two-cycle aggregate agree before build authority becomes available.

entries.mistake: A second multi-document resolution patch failed because it split one existing sentence at a non-existent line boundary in the preupload evidence file; the whole patch was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Although the exact document tail had been read, the patch still used a manually reflowed two-line context and combined four documentation updates with four registry status changes.
entries.prevention: Update registry statuses separately from documentation, then append to each evidence document using one exact final line as context. Never manually reflow remembered Markdown in patch anchors.

entries.mistake: The first Screen03 v4 manifest patch anchored only on a generic production-accepted status and closing array, so it changed Screen01 v3 to superseded and inserted the new Screen03 object outside the intended Screen03 lineage block.
entries.rootCause: Repeated JSON field names in the protected approved-reference manifest were patched without including the exact screenId, version and adjacent root as one unique context block.
entries.prevention: Protected manifest patches must anchor on the full exact screenId/version/status/root block, immediately parse the complete JSON and assert exactly one production-accepted version per locked screen before any gate retry.

entries.mistake: The first correction to the ambiguous manifest patch assumed Screen01 v3 was the previously active production version; the global gate then proved v3's locked splash source hash does not match the current accepted owner.
entries.rootCause: The correction used version ordering and the post-error status table instead of comparing each preserved Screen01 acceptance package against the current twelve locked owner bytes to identify the exact pre-existing active version.
entries.prevention: Before changing any unrelated protected status, compare the complete locked-file set for every candidate version against current bytes and select only the unique exact match. Never infer active status from version numbers or a state already affected by a failed patch.

entries.mistake: The Screen01 recovery resolution append used only the remembered second half of the document's wrapped final sentence, so apply_patch rejected the append.
entries.rootCause: The patch anchor omitted the exact preceding wrapped line even after the document tail had been printed.
entries.prevention: For a wrapped Markdown sentence, anchor on both exact physical lines or append after a unique heading block; never anchor on a reconstructed suffix.

entries.mistake: The C30X build phase and founder launcher require sourceQualification.releasePreflightPassed before invoking the single-AAB wrapper, but that wrapper is the owner that runs the release config-only and merged-manifest preflights after the build phase and before consuming build authority.
entries.rootCause: A historical mutable preflight result was copied into the successor's pre-build qualification condition without separating source/static release-control qualification from current-invocation generated configuration and manifest evidence.
entries.prevention: The source gate and launcher must require qualified source/static release controls and a sealed manifest, while the wrapper alone must run and verify current-invocation config-only and manifest preflights before consuming the one build authority. Never require a wrapper-produced result as a prerequisite to enter that wrapper.

entries.mistake: The first FIX2 order-contract run could not find the build-authority consumption source because its double-quoted needle interpolated $state; the postbuild needle also risked interpolating $_.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell source-code fragments containing dollar-prefixed tokens were represented as expandable strings instead of literal single-quoted strings or escaped dollar characters.
entries.prevention: Every static PowerShell source needle containing a dollar sign must use a literal single-quoted string with embedded quotes doubled where needed. Inspect all sibling needles in the same new checker before retrying it.

entries.mistake: The generic wrapper static gate passed while emitting 'one dynamic r60.47 appbundle authority', even though C30X prohibits r60.47 reuse and the wrapper now accepts a distinct successor contract.
entries.rootCause: The static gate's final human-readable success message was not migrated when the executable assertions were generalized from the historical C30V candidate to the C30X successor contract.
entries.prevention: Success output for a generalized release gate must name the dynamic successor contract without a historical version. A static assertion must reject the stale r60.47 success label while retaining historical failure checks where they are semantically required.

entries.mistake: A cycle-preparation read assumed hosting/package.json and failed because that path does not exist in the repository.
entries.rootCause: The command inferred a conventional package location instead of reusing the exact previously passing Hosting test owner or resolving it from a bounded package inventory.
entries.prevention: Before the next Hosting cycle command, resolve package.json candidates with rg --files inside the repository, select the unique Hosting owner from its scripts/content, and use that exact path for both cycles.

entries.mistake: The Screen03 v4 production-acceptance gate validates only the completed FIX1 ticket and requires FIX1 reference-write authority, so it cannot replay under the active C30X source-qualification scope.
entries.rootCause: The gate coupled immutable acceptance-content validation to the temporary mutation authority used to create v4 and did not define a read-only successor replay context.
entries.prevention: Historical protected-reference gates must separately validate immutable acceptance bytes and the active scope. Permit only the exact completed creation ticket with write authority or an explicitly named successor qualification ticket with reference writes false, while all runtime/build/external/secret authorities remain false.

entries.mistake: The current exact apps/web Hosting suite passed 8 tests while C30X state and aggregate still record hostingPassed=7.
entries.rootCause: C30X copied a historical Hosting count without reconciling the current two-file suite, and the build gate checked only the hostingVerifyPassed boolean rather than binding the exact current count in both state files.
entries.prevention: Ticket and qualify the current eight-test Hosting contract, bind hostingPassed=8 in state and aggregate, and require exact state/aggregate count equality in the C30X build phase before source qualification can authorize a candidate.

entries.mistake: The first fresh-cycle backend run printed all 528 test cases directly, so the tool truncated the output even though the final 528/528 summary remained visible.
entries.rootCause: The run repeated REG-20260814-2155 instead of capturing complete backend output to a unique immutable log and rendering only a bounded tail.
entries.prevention: Escalate the existing rule: every full backend node --test invocation in AAB qualification must redirect complete stdout/stderr to a prevalidated new in-repository log, then parse and print only compiled-file and TAP summary scalars plus a short tail. Direct full-suite console rendering is prohibited.

entries.mistake: The backend cycle output used ..\..\.. from backend/functions and resolved to C:\GUARANTEED OUTCOME\artifacts instead of the production repository's artifacts directory.
entries.rootCause: The relative parent-depth was not resolved and asserted against the exact production repository root before TypeScript wrote the new evidence directory.
entries.prevention: Construct backend evidence paths from the already known absolute production repository root, require the resolved path to start with that root plus a separator, require the target to be absent, and preserve the escaped failed-attempt directory without deletion or reuse.

entries.mistake: A combined backend-incident resolution patch used a non-existent final sentence in the escaped-output document, so apply_patch rejected the registry and both documentation updates.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined status and two document changes without first reading the exact physical tail of each target, repeating the registered multidocument context pattern.
entries.prevention: Resolve registry statuses in one exact ID-anchored patch, read each document tail, then append to each document in separate patches using its exact physical final lines. Never combine unrelated resolution appends.

entries.mistake: After two identical cycles were recorded, C30X reconcile rejected the truthful source_qualified_exact_successor_candidate_selection_pending state because it accepts only prebuild_audit_blocked_no_candidate_no_authority.
entries.rootCause: The reconcile phase modeled only the initial audit state and did not define the legitimate source-qualified, no-candidate, no-authority transition that occurs before exact candidate ticket selection.
entries.prevention: Ticket an explicit two-state reconcile contract: accept the initial blocked state only with unqualified source facts, or the exact source-qualified candidate-selection-pending state only with a current sealed manifest, two cycles, all regression counts and source controls true. Both contexts must retain empty candidate identity, zero counts and no release authority.

entries.mistake: The C30Y cycle 2 authoritative Flutter suite lost its running execution cell when laptop power failed, so no completion summary or qualifying Flutter result exists for that interrupted attempt.
entries.rootCause: External power loss terminated the process and its execution-cell state before the authoritative runner could emit a complete exit result.
entries.prevention: Preserve the already passing cycle 2 static-gate evidence, treat the interrupted Flutter attempt as non-qualifying, rerun the authoritative Flutter manifest with a fresh attempt boundary, and then run only the remaining cycle 2 analyzer, Hosting and backend stages with unique evidence paths. Never infer success from a missing execution cell.

entries.mistake: The C30X build phase invokes regression memory with Phase=build and BuildMode=none, while the regression-memory contract rejects none for every build phase and has no release build-mode value.
entries.rootCause: The successor release-AAB gate reused a non-build qualification mode without reconciling the regression-memory parameter contract with the actual release build type.
entries.prevention: Regression memory must expose an exact release build mode, C30X must invoke that release mode, and a static cross-owner contract must reject BuildMode=none in the C30X build phase before any founder prompt or build retry.

entries.mistake: The combined prebuild replay launched the regression-memory checker through a child pwsh process but did not test its native exit code, so later read-only gates ran and the outer command returned zero despite the first child failure.
entries.rootCause: ErrorActionPreference does not automatically promote a native child-process exit code to a terminating PowerShell error in this command shape.
entries.prevention: Each child pwsh or powershell.exe replay must be followed immediately by an exact LASTEXITCODE assertion, or the script must be invoked in-process so terminating errors propagate. Never treat a combined command's final exit as proof of every child stage.

entries.mistake: The C31C gate passed the exact C30Y scope with buildAuthorized=true but emitted a hard-coded build=false success label.
entries.rootCause: The historical chat gate's executable scope predicate was expanded for the successor candidate, but its human-readable evidence label remained fixed to the original no-build ticket context.
entries.prevention: C31C success evidence must render the validated current build-authority boolean dynamically, and a cross-owner static gate must reject the stale hard-coded build=false label while preserving all chat authority boundaries.

entries.mistake: The first founder-authorized C30Y launcher attempt completed release config-only and merged-manifest preflight but changed sealed source owners GeneratedPluginRegistrant.java and android/local.properties; the final current-source check rejected the attempt before authority consumption.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper runs source-mutating Flutter and Gradle configuration tasks after source qualification, restores only a non-exact registrant form, does not restore local.properties, and then requires the entire sealed source manifest to remain byte-identical.
entries.prevention: Before any retry, ticket a mutation-safe preflight transaction that snapshots the exact qualified bytes of every permitted generated source owner, restores them in a finally path before the current-source assertion or exit, proves all other owners unchanged, preserves every attempt artifact, and never consumes the one build authority until exact restoration passes.

entries.mistake: A bounded candidate-file search piped rg --files through a generated-file-name filter and returned exit 1 because ignored generated owners were absent from rg's inventory; the command treated ordinary no-match as an execution failure.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic used the repository file index for ignored/generated path recovery and did not explicitly handle rg's no-match exit contract.
entries.prevention: For exact generated-owner recovery, use an explicit workspace-bounded filesystem enumeration or intentionally handle rg exit 1 as zero matches. Never infer absence from a gitignore-aware inventory and never let a no-match status obscure the hashes already collected.

entries.mistake: The FIX2 recovery update combined one regression-status change and two Markdown resolution appends in a single successful patch despite the permanent rule requiring status and documentation operations to be separate.
entries.rootCause: The recovery facts were grouped for convenience instead of applying the already registered exact-tail and single-purpose patch discipline.
entries.prevention: Escalate the rule: every future registry status update is one patch containing registry JSON only; each Markdown resolution append is a separate patch after reading that document's exact tail. No combined resolution patch is permitted even when its contexts are known and it would succeed.

entries.mistake: The first C30Y FIX2 checker run evaluated a double-quoted wrapper needle containing $state, so strict mode attempted to read an unset checker variable before any behavioral probe ran.
entries.rootCause: A new static source needle repeated the already registered dollar-interpolation failure class instead of using a literal single-quoted representation.
entries.prevention: Escalate REG-2163: every new or edited static PowerShell checker must inventory all needle strings containing dollar signs before its first run and represent each as a literal single-quoted string with embedded quotes doubled. The FIX2 checker must include no expandable source needles.

entries.mistake: The first C30Y FIX2 checker replay under Windows PowerShell failed because the behavioral probe used [IO.Path]::GetRelativePath, an API unavailable in Windows PowerShell 5.1's .NET runtime.
entries.rootCause: The new checker was first validated only under PowerShell 7 and was not passed through the repository's existing Windows PowerShell compatibility rule before the explicit legacy-host replay.
entries.prevention: New dual-host release gates must avoid the repository compatibility checker's forbidden modern path/hash APIs from their first implementation. Repository-contained probe paths must derive relative names with an ordinal root-prefix assertion and substring conversion, then pass PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell before qualification.

entries.mistake: Both post-FIX1 C30Y cycle summaries name backend compile-log paths that do not exist, so their typecheckPassed=true claim is not bound to the referenced retained files.
entries.rootCause: The summaries were written from observed command success without asserting that each named compile evidence file was newly created, repository-contained, present and referenced exactly before the cycle was accepted.
entries.prevention: Every successor qualification cycle must write backend typecheck output to a unique prevalidated in-repository file, retain the file even when output is empty, and use a gate that rejects any cycle summary whose referenced compile/test evidence path is missing, escaped, reused or not bound to the current cycle.

entries.mistake: Both post-FIX1 C30Y cycle summaries claim eight Hosting tests passed but name no Hosting evidence file, while the only retained Hosting log in the evidence root reports the obsolete seven-test suite.
entries.rootCause: The cycle summaries recorded a console-observed count without requiring one unique retained Hosting log whose parsed tests/pass/fail scalars exactly match the summary and current eight-test contract.
entries.prevention: Every successor qualification cycle must capture the complete current Hosting test output in a unique repository-contained log and a gate must require exactly tests=8, pass=8, fail=0 in both the log and summary before accepting the cycle.

entries.mistake: The first post-FIX3 cycle-1 static run correctly reached the C30X fail-closed build owner with exit 1, but the orchestration classified it as failure because it searched for 'C30X successor AAB gate rejected' instead of the exact emitted 'C30X successor AAB hard gate rejected'.
entries.rootCause: The negative classifier reconstructed the rejection prefix from memory instead of binding to the exact Assert-C30X owner text and expected incomplete-qualification message before the first cycle run.
entries.prevention: Successor qualification must use a repository-owned negative classifier that requires nonzero exit and the exact C30X hard-gate rejection prefix plus the expected incomplete candidate/authority/qualification message. Failed orchestration evidence remains non-qualifying and every retry uses a new cycle-attempt evidence name.

entries.mistake: The first FIX4 checker run rejected the child C30X output as not matching its exact incomplete-qualification contract, but the checker did not retain or emit the normalized child text needed to identify whether the mismatch came from scope, ANSI/native error formatting or the expected-reason expression.
entries.rootCause: The new negative classifier combined child execution and final classification without an attempt-specific diagnostic output path, so its own fail-closed message obscured the child rejection evidence on first failure.
entries.prevention: Every child-process negative classifier must accept a unique repository-contained diagnostic evidence path, refuse overwrite, retain the native exit and normalized bounded child text before classification, and use that preserved evidence to correct the exact owner/reason contract before retry.

entries.mistake: The first retained FIX4 diagnostic expected C30X's incomplete candidate/authority/qualification rejection while FIX4 was still the active MVP ticket, but C30X correctly rejected the non-C30Y scope earlier with 'C30X preparation or exact C30Y candidate scope changed'.
entries.rootCause: The negative classifier treated the eventual candidate-qualification context as available during the child repair's own selected-ticket context and did not model the C30X common-scope assertion that precedes phase-specific build checks.
entries.prevention: Negative release classifiers must name the exact active state context and expected gate-order owner. FIX4 uses two stages: classify the exact scope rejection while FIX4 is selected, then classify the exact incomplete-qualification rejection only after the scope returns to C30Y; both stages must prove unchanged state, aggregate, manifest, authority and counts.

entries.mistake: The candidate-context diagnostic contains the exact C30X incomplete-qualification reason, but PowerShell rendered the wrapped continuation with a leading error-record '|' gutter, so the classifier's whitespace-only expression did not match 'is | incomplete'.
entries.rootCause: The classifier removed ANSI control sequences but treated PowerShell's presentation gutter as semantic child text and did not create a second gutter-stripped classification form.
entries.prevention: PowerShell child-error classifiers must retain the ANSI-normalized record for evidence, derive a separate semantic form by removing only line-leading ErrorRecord gutters, and apply exact owner/reason assertions to that semantic form. Each retry uses a new diagnostic evidence path.

entries.mistake: The first post-FIX4 cycle-2 analyzer attempt launched the authoritative whole-mobile analyzer through a shell tool timeout of ten seconds, so orchestration terminated before the analyzer could complete or write a trustworthy native exit record.
entries.rootCause: The long-running analyzer command used the shell timeout as a yield mechanism instead of giving the command a sufficient execution timeout and relying on the asynchronous cell wait mechanism for progress collection.
entries.prevention: Long-running qualification commands must use a sufficient command timeout, unique attempt evidence paths and asynchronous cell waits no longer than sixty seconds. A timed-out attempt is preserved as non-qualifying evidence and the retry must use a new attempt stem without overwriting any partial file.

entries.mistake: A post-cycle release-state lookup passed a guessed invoke-play-internal-aab-build-c30v.ps1 positional path to rg even though that file does not exist, producing exit 1 and invalidating the combined lookup output.
entries.rootCause: The lookup inferred an executable owner name from the C30V contract suffix instead of first enumerating exact existing files in the bounded scripts and tmp directories, repeating the missing-path diagnostic class after it was already documented in regression memory.
entries.prevention: Before every multi-path rg lookup, enumerate or Test-Path every literal positional owner. Release-wrapper discovery must use bounded filename inventory first, select only exact existing paths, and then perform content lookup. Any command containing one absent positional path is incomplete evidence and cannot support a state promotion.

entries.mistake: The first final pre-prompt replay declared a helper parameter named Host, which collides case-insensitively with PowerShell's read-only automatic $Host variable, so the wrapper failed before invoking its first child gate.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc replay helper was not checked against PowerShell automatic and reserved variable names before execution.
entries.prevention: Qualification orchestration helpers must use task-specific parameter names such as RunnerExecutable, never Host, HOME or other automatic/system variable names. A replay that fails before its first child remains non-qualifying and must be retried only after regression registration with a new wrapper invocation.

entries.mistake: The corrected final replay reached the FIX4 classifier but invoked it without ExpectedContext and DiagnosticEvidencePath, so PowerShell rejected the call before the classifier ran.
entries.rootCause: The composite replay treated the FIX4 checker like parameterless static gates instead of preserving its exact candidate_incomplete context and unique diagnostic-evidence contract from qualification cycles.
entries.prevention: Every FIX4 replay must pass ExpectedContext candidate_incomplete and a new repository-contained diagnostic path for each PowerShell host. Composite gate lists must encode required arguments per gate rather than assuming a parameterless common shape.

entries.mistake: Authority withdrawal after the replay failure wrote a new temporary C30X machine-state and source-state label that the exact release gate had never qualified.
entries.rootCause: The recovery mutation described the current condition with newly invented state strings instead of restoring the already-qualified post-FIX4 requalification labels.
entries.prevention: Release recovery may use only exact state labels already accepted by the qualified C30X gate. Narrative detail belongs in blockers and evidence, never in a new machine-state enum value without its own authorized gate change and qualification.

entries.mistake: The first final available-authority replay invoked the FIX4 negative classifier after one-build authority had been made available, and FIX4 correctly rejected because its negative probe requires no build authority and zero release actions.
entries.rootCause: The final replay treated every pre-authority qualification gate as reusable after authority promotion instead of respecting FIX4's explicit negative-context phase boundary.
entries.prevention: FIX4 runs only while build authority is withheld and is bound through the final qualifying cycle evidence. After authority promotion, final replay must omit FIX4, rebind both already-passed cycle summaries, validate source/current state and run only gates applicable to the available-authority pre-prompt phase.

entries.mistake: The first final launcher-precondition audit combined dozens of state, aggregate and scope booleans into one array and threw only a generic scalar-preconditions failure, so it did not identify the mismatched property.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc audit optimized for compact execution instead of following the registered rule to enumerate the exact current JSON schema and validate each named scalar separately.
entries.prevention: Final launcher audits must emit or throw the exact property label for every scalar comparison, validate state, aggregate and scope fields separately, and stop at the first named mismatch. Opaque combined assertions cannot authorize or block a release transition.

entries.mistake: The attempt-06 cycle-1 authoritative Flutter audit exited 1 because its strict-mode parser accessed event.type directly on a successfully decoded JSON object that did not expose a type property.
entries.rootCause: The runner safely handled optional booleans but assumed every JSON reporter line was a typed event, so one untyped JSON object crashed classification before the authoritative result summary could be produced.
entries.prevention: The authoritative Flutter JSON parser must read event type through an optional-property helper, classify absent or blank type as an explicit non-event JSON count, require that count to be zero or an exact separately qualified allowance, and retain enough bounded evidence to distinguish reporter metadata from test failures without crashing.

entries.mistake: The first post-restart reconciliation probe tried to read config/release-action-counts-c30y.json even though no such owner exists, causing the otherwise read-only compound probe to exit 1.
entries.rootCause: The probe inferred a standalone action-count filename from the handoff description instead of resolving the already-qualified machine-state and aggregate owners and enumerating their exact current schemas before reading named count fields.
entries.prevention: Post-restart release reconciliation must discover only exact existing state owners from the bounded C30X/C30Y ticket references, enumerate each current JSON schema, and validate separately labeled build/upload/install scalars. A guessed standalone count path invalidates the compound probe and is never retried.

entries.mistake: The first exact-owner projection enumerated only each JSON root schema and then read unverified nested paths such as releaseActions.build.count; because those paths were absent, PowerShell's null-chain Count behavior rendered misleading numeric zeroes instead of exposing the schema mismatch.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic treated root-schema enumeration as sufficient for nested projections and did not require each intermediate property owner and scalar type to exist before reading the release-action counts.
