entries.prevention: Release-state diagnostics must enumerate every intermediate nested object's property names and runtime types first, then read only exact present scalar paths with reference-null and numeric-type checks. Chained property access on an unverified or null owner is prohibited because null Count can masquerade as zero.

entries.mistake: The first post-FIX5 evidence-binder contract run failed because its positive self-test reused a historical post-FIX2 source manifest whose runner hash is legitimately superseded by FIX5.
entries.rootCause: The generic evidence-binder self-test made current-source validation depend on an old real qualification manifest rather than generating a minimal current probe manifest inside its isolated temporary probe directory.
entries.prevention: The binder contract self-test must generate a unique one-row probe manifest from an exact current stable owner, bind and validate that manifest inside the isolated probe, and delete only the generated probe directory afterward. Historical real manifests remain immutable evidence and are never required to stay current for a later generic self-test.

entries.mistake: After a Promise.all gate batch rejected on the first failed child, the follow-up diagnostic assumed every sibling gate had completed and required all four planned log paths, then exited on the absent Windows-PowerShell binder log.
entries.rootCause: The orchestration conflated requested sibling tasks with completed durable evidence and used an all-required compound inventory before discovering which exact outputs actually existed.
entries.prevention: Qualification gates run sequentially unless their orchestrator returns an explicit settled result for every child. After any parallel rejection, inventory each planned exact path as a labeled present-or-absent scalar first; read only proven-present files and never require unproven sibling evidence.

entries.mistake: The first post-FIX5 reseal preflight correctly verified the immutable 1132-file manifest hash and count, then incorrectly required the regression registry to be an existing manifest member; the exact membership check rejected that assumption before writing a provisional manifest.
entries.rootCause: The preflight inferred source-manifest membership from a control owner's release importance instead of first projecting the old manifest's exact path set and classifying each candidate owner as present or absent.
entries.prevention: Source reseals start from the exact sealed path list. Every candidate owner receives a labeled exact-membership result before any required-member assertion. Existing members get current hashes, explicitly approved new source owners are added, and narrative/control importance never implies manifest membership.

entries.mistake: The first post-FIX5 cycle-1 analyzer wrapper failed PowerShell parsing before Flutter analyze started because its inline nested GetFullPath/Join-Path expression had unbalanced parentheses.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper attempted to resolve the evidence log path inside the Tee-Object argument after Push-Location instead of calculating simple exact absolute log and exit scalars before changing directories.
entries.prevention: Analyzer wrappers must resolve and validate exact repository-contained absolute log and exit paths in separate named scalars before Push-Location, pass the already-resolved log scalar directly to Tee-Object, capture the native exit immediately, and use a new immutable attempt stem after any parser failure.

entries.mistake: Post-FIX5 cycle-1 attempt-02 backend typecheck exited 0 with an empty output stream, but Tee-Object did not create the required compile log, so the evidence binder correctly rejected the summary as missing backend compile evidence.
entries.rootCause: The native wrapper assumed Tee-Object always materializes its target even when the pipeline produces zero objects and did not precreate the exact retained log before invoking the silent typecheck.
entries.prevention: Every qualification stage whose successful output may be empty must precreate a unique zero-byte UTF-8 log before native invocation, capture the native exit separately, and require both files to exist afterward. An exit-only typecheck is not bindable evidence, and the failed binder attempt forces a fresh versioned complete cycle.

entries.mistake: The first final available-authority replay invoked the Screen03 v4 successor lock after scope build and device-install authority were true; the gate correctly rejected because its exact successor replay context is read-only and requires both authorities false.
entries.rootCause: The final replay list did not classify the Screen03 lock as a pre-authority-only gate and redundantly replayed it instead of relying on its dual-host passes already bound into both qualifying cycle summaries.
entries.prevention: The available-authority phase matrix must omit both FIX4 and the Screen03 read-only successor lock. Their dual-host pre-authority passes are rebound through both final cycle summaries. After authority is available, replay only gates whose contracts explicitly accept build/device scope true.

entries.mistake: The post-REG-2202 two-cycle comparison wrapper failed while validating distinct evidence paths because a compacted Test-Path call omitted whitespace before -PathType, so PowerShell treated the expression as an invalid positional argument sequence.
entries.rootCause: The already-proven uncompressed named-scalar comparison form was shortened into dense inline syntax, merging the path variable and named parameter boundary.
entries.prevention: Qualification comparisons must reuse the proven uncompressed form. Every Test-Path result is calculated in a separate explicitly named boolean with whitespace-delimited named parameters before the comparison; dense inline path-validation expressions are prohibited.

entries.mistake: The post-REG-2203 cycle-1 attempt-05 static wrapper shortened its record helper to R; PowerShell command precedence resolved R to the built-in Invoke-History alias, so the wrapper failed before its first child gate ran.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper replaced the previously proven task-specific helper names with an unverified one-letter command name and did not account for alias precedence over functions.
entries.prevention: Release orchestration reuses the proven full helper names Write-Record and Invoke-Gate verbatim. One-letter or generic helper commands are prohibited, and no qualification wrapper is compacted after a prior form has passed.

entries.mistake: The second available-authority replay failed C31C because MVP scope deviceInstallAuthorized was promoted true alongside build authority, while C31C's exact C30Y successor phase permits build true but requires device install false until the later postupload/preinstall transition.
entries.rootCause: State promotion conflated founder-approved machine one-time install/device authority with the current MVP execution phase and did not preserve the C31C contract's separate build-now/device-later boundary.
entries.prevention: At pre-prompt/build availability, MVP scope sets buildAuthorized true and deviceInstallAuthorized false. Machine upload/install/device authorities may remain available_once under their later gates. Scope device-install authority changes only at the separately qualified postupload/preinstall transition.

entries.mistake: The post-resume reconciliation probe guessed config/mvp-scope-state.json and produced a path-not-found error instead of reading the repository's exact MVP scope owner config/mvp-scope-gate-state.json.
entries.rootCause: The probe used a shortened inferred filename from the handoff description rather than first resolving the bounded config inventory and confirming the exact durable owner path.
entries.prevention: Every resumed release diagnostic must resolve exact existing owner paths from repository references or a bounded rg --files inventory before Get-Content. A missing inferred path invalidates only that probe, is registered before retry, and is never silently substituted.

entries.mistake: The first postbuild owner-discovery command combined a parameter read, a filename inventory and a broad multi-tree content search; it exceeded the command timeout before returning usable output.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic grouped independently bounded questions into one search across scripts, config and quality documentation instead of reading the exact C30X gate header first and inventorying candidate filenames separately.
entries.prevention: Postbuild discovery uses separate bounded commands: read the exact gate parameter block, inventory only scripts/tmp filenames, then search only the selected exact owners. A timeout is preserved as a failed read-only probe and is never retried in the same compound form.

entries.mistake: Postbuild regression audit attempt 01 invoked the C30W build-phase gate with RepositoryRoot but omitted its required candidate StatePath, so the gate rejected before executable postbuild tests.
entries.rootCause: The audit copied the source-phase invocation shape into a build-phase replay and did not preserve the exact C30X-owned call contract that passes the current C30X state path.
entries.prevention: Every C30W build-phase replay passes the exact repository-contained config/successor-aab-regression-hard-gate-state-c30x.json through -StatePath. Phase-specific parameters are copied from the proven C30X owner and checked before execution.

entries.mistake: When postbuild regression audit attempt 01 caught the C30W rejection, its catch path used Tee-Object with an unsupported append parameter combination; the secondary error prevented creation of the planned exit-code evidence file.
entries.rootCause: The failure path was not copied from a proven evidence writer and assumed Tee-Object supported append semantics instead of writing the caught message with Add-Content and always emitting the exit file afterward.
entries.prevention: Audit wrappers write normal output through Tee-Object, but catch paths use Add-Content -LiteralPath for the bounded error line. Exit evidence is written in a finally-equivalent step and its existence is verified even when the child gate fails.

entries.mistake: The first Internal Testing browser upload attempt clicked the hidden file input directly; no chooser was emitted within the browser-control timeout, and the uncaught chooser rejection reset the browser-control session before any file transfer.
entries.rootCause: The attempt preferred a technically present hidden input over the visible Play Console Upload control and did not catch the chooser promise rejection inside the browser execution call.
entries.prevention: The retry reconnects to the existing Internal Testing draft, starts a caught filechooser wait, clicks the visible Upload button, and sets exactly the sealed r60.48 AAB only after a chooser is returned. Afterward it verifies the visible version code before any Save, Next or rollout action.

entries.mistake: The visible Play Upload control returned a multi-capable file chooser, but the retry guard treated isMultiple=true as an error and stopped before selecting the sealed AAB.
entries.rootCause: The guard conflated chooser capability with intended selection cardinality. A multi-capable chooser can safely receive a one-element file list.
entries.prevention: Accept either single- or multi-capable Play choosers, pass exactly one absolute path in a one-element list, and verify the resulting visible artifact row is exactly version code 2026081348 before Save or Next.

entries.mistake: The first upload-selection evidence/status patch assumed a documentation tail sentence that was not present verbatim, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch before changing any file.
entries.rootCause: The combined multi-file patch used a remembered prose anchor instead of reading the exact short document tail before constructing the resolution hunk.
entries.prevention: Before updating a narrative status, read that exact document tail and anchor on its real lines. Keep new evidence creation and registry status changes in exact bounded hunks, and verify atomic patch failure left all targets unchanged before retry.

entries.mistake: The first OPPO Chrome Internal Testing link navigation typed the URL and pressed Return in one Windows-control action without an intervening observation, so the resulting screen could not prove whether navigation dispatched.
entries.rootCause: The device-browser sequence combined text entry and submission even though the Windows-control contract requires a refreshed focus and value observation between them.
entries.prevention: Use separate observed actions for address focus, URL typing, URL-value verification, submission and tester-page verification. An ambiguous combined type-and-submit outcome is zero navigation evidence and must not be repeated in the same form.

entries.mistake: The C30Z auth/navigation inventory passed apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/social/*.dart as a positional Windows path, so ripgrep returned an invalid-filename error after partial output.
entries.rootCause: The command did not apply the already-registered Windows rule that filename wildcards belong behind --glob while positional arguments must be exact existing files or directories.
entries.prevention: Use the literal existing apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/social directory with --glob '*.dart', require every positional path to exist, and discard the failed command's partial output as an incomplete inventory.

entries.mistake: The first reconciliation command guessed docs/quality/CODEX-REGRESSION-MEMORY.md, which does not exist, and a follow-up assumed the prevention-prose memory file contained each REG identifier inline, so both reads produced zero registry evidence.
entries.rootCause: The commands used remembered naming and schema assumptions instead of resolving the exact memory owner and reading the machine registry structure first.
entries.prevention: Resolve the memory owner with a bounded exact filename inventory, then read config/codex-development-regression-registry.json for identifiers and status while treating docs/quality/CODEX-DEVELOPMENT-REGRESSION-MEMORY.md as prevention prose. Never require an incident ID to occur in the prose owner.

entries.mistake: A literal first-install timestamp search was aimed at the whole artifacts/quality archive and timed out before returning any usable evidence.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic widened from the exact C30Y evidence root to the historical artifact archive even though the current package fields and sealed predecessor install state were already sufficient for scoped reconciliation.
entries.prevention: Never scan the full quality archive for an OPPO timestamp. Read the exact current package fields, the exact candidate state and only a previously located predecessor evidence owner; treat timeout 124 and partial output as zero evidence and do not retry the broad search.

entries.mistake: A single bounded C30X checker excerpt wrapped one integer pair in a nested PowerShell array and iterated it, so automatic unrolling supplied scalar integers instead of the expected pair and emitted no source lines.
entries.rootCause: The command repeated the registered nested-array-unrolling mistake even though only one direct line range was required.
entries.prevention: For one source range, use direct scalar start/end variables and a direct for loop. For multiple ranges, use strongly typed objects with named Start and End fields; never iterate @(@(start,end)). Zero emitted lines are zero inspection evidence.

entries.mistake: The source-qualified and Play-installed r60.48 candidate allowed Google and YouTube account choice but founder testing could not establish a MoolSocial authenticated session afterward.
entries.rootCause: Prebuild tests covered gateway contracts with fakes but no hard gate proved the Play-signing SHA, enabled Firebase Google provider and exact Android/web OAuth relationship as one live release readiness boundary; Android configuration failures can also surface as a cancellation after account choice.
entries.prevention: A successor must preserve structured Google failure truth, never label an account-selected configuration failure as a successful or user-cancelled sign-in, roll back partial Firebase identity state when downstream account bootstrap fails, and require non-secret live provider-readiness plus Play-installed success evidence before acceptance.

entries.mistake: r60.48 presented Email OTP as an operable production method even though its sealed runtime definition set contained no MOOLSOCIAL_AUTH_API_BASE_URL and the gateway deterministically rejects a missing base URI.
entries.rootCause: Screen 03 did not consume runtime method availability, and the release gate validated Firebase/Google startup inputs without validating or explicitly disabling the email OTP dependency.
entries.prevention: Email OTP is disabled and labelled unavailable unless an exact qualified HTTPS endpoint is present. Its backend request/verify/custom-token contract, abuse controls and tests must qualify before any deployment or release enables the method.

entries.mistake: r60.48 presented Mobile OTP as an operable production method, but founder real-device testing found it non-operative and no release gate proved enabled Phone auth, SMS region policy, signing fingerprints and Play Integrity app verification together.
entries.rootCause: The client gateway existed and was unit-tested, but presentation did not depend on an explicitly qualified live-provider readiness flag.
entries.prevention: Mobile OTP remains disabled and truthfully labelled until a non-secret readiness record proves the enabled provider, permitted SMS region, Play signing fingerprint/app-verification prerequisites and a separately authorized real-device send/verify journey.

entries.mistake: Screen 03 rendered all six social-provider controls with active tap and Continue semantics even when JourneySession production availability contained only Google and YouTube.
entries.rootCause: The screen iterated SocialAuthProvider.values and enabled each control whenever the session was not busy, leaving availability enforcement only inside the post-tap session method.
entries.prevention: Provider presentation consumes the same JourneySession availability set as dispatch. Unavailable providers cannot invoke a gateway, expose enabled semantics or promise Continue behavior, while layout and approved visual ownership remain stable.

entries.mistake: Founder testing reported that selecting guest Feed could redirect to sign-in, while the intended contract permits public Feed reads and gates only create and write interactions.
entries.rootCause: The report has not yet been separated into the Feed tab entry versus a protected action within Feed, and source qualification lacks one release-specific guest Feed entry assertion bound to r60.48 behavior.
entries.prevention: Prove guest Feed tab entry and refresh remain public, then separately prove create, like, comment, repost/share, save and message sign-in gates with exact return continuity. Do not classify expected protected-write authentication as a Feed-read defect.

entries.mistake: The unchanged historical C30X FIX1 Screen03 v4 acceptance gate was invoked after the MVP state transitioned to C30Z, and it rejected because its exact creation/read-only replay scope does not include the new repair ticket.
entries.rootCause: The preimplementation check treated a historically scoped gate as directly reusable under a successor ticket instead of first adding a separate containment gate that preserves every substantive v4 lock.
entries.prevention: Do not weaken or append C30Z to the historical C30X FIX1 gate. Add one C30Z-owned successor containment gate that verifies the historical gate owner remains unchanged, replays its substantive manifest/layout/source/test locks, and adds the new authentication-method truth invariants.

entries.mistake: A combined registry, assessment and documentation status patch assumed the C30Z qualification document ended with the sentence 'service state changed.', so apply_patch rejected the complete multi-file patch before changing any target.
entries.rootCause: The patch reused closing context from the separate Screen03 gate incident document instead of reading the exact tail of the C30Z qualification document.
entries.prevention: After an atomic multi-file patch rejection, verify the targets remain unchanged, read each exact short tail, and retry in bounded independently anchored hunks. Never share a remembered narrative anchor between different quality documents.

entries.mistake: The authoritative 59-file Flutter JSON audit was started with a 60-second parent shell timeout, so exit 124 terminated the process before its bounded counted summary was emitted.
entries.rootCause: The command timeout was sized like a focused test even though the full manifest historically requires multiple minutes; the wait tool was available to preserve frequent progress updates without killing the process.
entries.prevention: Full-manifest Flutter runs use a non-killing long process timeout and 10-second wait yields. Only the wrapper's final bounded counts and native exit are qualification evidence; timeout 124 with no summary is preserved as zero evidence and is never reinterpreted.

entries.mistake: The corrected 59-file Flutter audit was invoked with ExpectedPassed=420 by adding three authored tests to a remembered prior count, but the wrapper observed 418 passed and 3 skipped with zero failures/errors and native Flutter exit zero, then correctly rejected the count mismatch.
entries.rootCause: The expected count was derived arithmetically from a remembered broader qualification total instead of proving the exact focused manifest membership for every changed test owner and its prior authored baseline.
entries.prevention: Before retrying an expected-count mismatch, require exact normalized membership for each changed test file, identify which newly authored tests are inside the selected manifest, and bind the next expected count to that manifest-specific delta. A clean native run does not authorize changing the expectation by observation alone.

entries.mistake: The newly authored cycle-02 summary copied focusedAuthAndFeed passed=36 from cycle 1 even though only the full 59-file wrapper and analyzer had been rerun for cycle 2 at that point.
entries.rootCause: The summary template treated focused evidence as part of the full cycle without separately checking whether the exact three-file focused command had a second native execution.
entries.prevention: Every cycle summary binds each named suite to an execution in that cycle. A copied focused result is marked invalid before promotion and is retained only after the exact named focused suite reruns with native exit zero; otherwise the field explicitly says not rerun.

entries.mistake: A read-only Chat capability audit passed apps/mobile/test/chat* as a positional ripgrep path on Windows, so ripgrep returned an invalid filename diagnostic after printing partial matches from valid directories.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed resolved source directories with a shell-style test filename wildcard even though repeated repository memory requires all Windows filename selection to use --glob or exact discovered paths.
entries.prevention: Treat the mixed-output command as rejected. Resolve Chat test files with rg --files apps/mobile/test and a name filter first, then pass only literal returned paths or search the existing directory with --glob 'chat*.dart'. No positional path containing an asterisk is permitted.

entries.mistake: A combined backend source read and optional installed-type lookup ended with ripgrep exit 1 because no getSignedUrl declaration matched the selected dependency path, causing the shell to report the whole audit as failed after the required source reads had printed.
entries.rootCause: The optional discovery leg was left under ErrorActionPreference Stop without explicitly accepting ripgrep's no-match exit as a valid inventory result or separating it from authoritative source reads.
entries.prevention: Run optional negative symbol searches as their own bounded command, capture LASTEXITCODE, accept only 0 or 1, and treat 2+ as failure. Required source reads and optional dependency discovery must not share one unnormalized exit contract.

entries.mistake: The first C31E ticket draft required the complete photo-message response to hide owner and thread IDs, although the existing participant-scoped Chat message contract legitimately includes senderId and the current target threadId.
entries.rootCause: A private Storage metadata requirement was written as a whole-message response requirement instead of being scoped to the attachment object path and upload-binding fields.
entries.prevention: Preserve established participant-scoped sender and target-thread semantics. C31E redaction applies only to the internal Storage object path, generation, signed-header binding digests and upload owner/thread metadata; signed read URLs remain short lived and participant gated.

entries.mistake: REG-2230 listed the planned C31E static gate in its gates array before that script existed, so the regression-memory gate rejected the registry entry as referencing missing repository evidence.
entries.rootCause: A future implementation owner was treated as current retained evidence during incident registration instead of waiting until apply_patch creation and successful execution.
entries.prevention: A registry entry references only files that exist at registration time. Planned gates stay in the ticket manifest; add them to regression evidence only after the exact file exists and has passed. Replay memory immediately after every registry patch.

entries.mistake: The first C31E backend typecheck failed because photoFromDocument's validated content type widened to string in its returned object and FakeChatRepository had not yet implemented preparePhotoUpload and sendPhotoMessage after ChatRepository was extended.
entries.rootCause: The runtime narrowing was not pinned with an explicit result type, and the production interface expansion was applied before the same atomic patch extended its structural test double.
entries.prevention: Annotate the normalized photo record with ChatPhotoContentType after validation, and extend every ChatRepository fake in the same contract wave with exact captured inputs and outputs. Typecheck must pass before any backend test execution or client implementation.

entries.mistake: The corrected C31E wording still claimed an internal object path never appears in a participant message response, although a direct Cloud Storage signed read URL necessarily contains its opaque object name in the URL path.
entries.rootCause: Separate response fields and the serialized signed URL itself were treated as the same disclosure surface instead of documenting the minimum unavoidable opaque locator inside a time-limited capability URL.
entries.prevention: Use a random UUID-only object name with no user, thread, filename or business identifier. Do not return raw objectPath, generation or binding metadata as separate fields. Document that the short-lived signed URL necessarily contains the opaque object locator and remains participant gated.

entries.mistake: The first attachment-store test typecheck assigned a value read back from a string map index directly to another string index, but noUncheckedIndexedAccess correctly typed the read as string or undefined.
entries.rootCause: The negative test corrupted and then reconstructed the owner binding by a second unchecked map lookup instead of retaining the already proven original header value.
entries.prevention: Capture required signed header values with an explicit existence assertion before mutating test metadata, then restore from that definite local value. No unchecked map read may be assigned to a required string field.

entries.mistake: The photo-reply contract patch added replyToMessageId twice to FakeChatRepository.sendMessage and did not extend sendPhotoInput's tuple at the intended position, producing duplicate identifiers, tuple length errors and shifted type assignments.
entries.rootCause: A broad repeated parameter anchor matched the earlier text-message fake instead of the later photo fake, and the tuple declaration was not reread before typecheck.
entries.prevention: Read the exact bounded fake fields and both method signatures before patching repeated parameter lists. Patch each owner with a unique method-name anchor, then verify tuple arity and index mapping before rerunning typecheck.

entries.mistake: The first correction to REG-2235 removed the duplicate method parameter but adjusted repeated string slots incrementally, leaving sendPhotoInput with a misplaced slot and three shifted assignment type errors.
entries.rootCause: A positional tuple with several adjacent string fields was repaired by local insert/remove hunks rather than replacing and verifying the complete named arity as one block.
entries.prevention: For heterogeneous tuples with adjacent same-type fields, replace the full declaration from its unique field name through closing bracket and list every semantic position in order. Verify the method assignment count against that block before typecheck.

entries.mistake: The resumed C31E source check invoked check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 with Phase=source, but the gate accepts only general, implementation, build or device and rejected the invocation before emitting evidence.
entries.rootCause: The intended source-work meaning was translated into an unverified phase name instead of reading the script parameter contract or using the repository's implementation phase.
entries.prevention: Use Phase=implementation for source and source-test work. Before invoking a parameterized repository gate after a resume, verify its ValidateSet or use an already proven exact command; an argument-validation rejection is zero evidence and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The first C31E mobile analyzer run reported prefer_initializing_formals for the optional picker and rejected an unconditional sendPhoto call because the local ChatGateway nullable value was not promoted to the separate ChatPhotoGateway interface strongly enough at the invocation.
entries.rootCause: The review constructor redundantly assigned its optional private field in the initializer list, and the send path relied on an implicit nullable intersection-type promotion across two unrelated interfaces.
entries.prevention: Use an initializing formal for the review picker. Resolve the production photo capability once into an explicitly typed nullable ChatPhotoGateway local, fail closed when it is absent, and invoke only the proven non-null capability owner. Targeted analysis must pass before adding tests or UI qualification.

entries.mistake: The first C31E photo test run ended 3 passed and 2 failed: the session's third exact-caption send returned false after a deliberately rejected changed-caption attempt, and the widget never displayed Photo delivered after tapping its send control. The assertions did not project busy, thread error, pending identity, request count and hit-test/action completion at each failing boundary.
entries.rootCause: The first assertions omitted bounded state. The registered diagnostic retry then proved both sends reached the gateway and isolated an UnsupportedError while appending to the fixed-length message list returned by the fake, matching AuthenticatedChatGateway's growable:false production list contract.
entries.prevention: Before any source correction or qualification retry, capture the exact session busy/error/notice/pending/request state around the failed third send and use ensureVisible plus an awaited pump boundary for the widget send control. Update this entry with the proven cause; do not guess from the shared symptom.

entries.mistake: ChatSession.loadMessages stored the gateway result directly, while AuthenticatedChatGateway deliberately returns a fixed-length list. Subsequent text optimistic append or authoritative photo append can throw UnsupportedError after a real production message load; the C31E const fake exposed the same contract mismatch.
entries.rootCause: The session treated a read-only gateway collection as its mutable local state owner instead of taking a defensive growable copy at the ownership boundary.
entries.prevention: Every gateway message result is copied into a new growable session-owned list before storage. Tests retain a fixed-length source-list case and prove text/photo append continuity after load; do not weaken the gateway's immutable response contract to hide the ownership defect.

entries.mistake: A combined C31E state and predecessor-gate read guessed check-uaw-c31c-chat-forwarding-contract.ps1 and a C31B analogue before resolving their literal repository names. Get-Content rejected the missing path and invalidated the complete combined lookup.
entries.rootCause: Narrative gate labels from earlier evidence were converted into assumed script naming conventions despite active memory requiring an exact bounded inventory before historical owner reads.
entries.prevention: Resolve predecessor Chat gate owners with rg --files scripts and a bounded c31/chat filter, require literal existing paths, then read each exact result in a separate no-guess call. Mixed successful and missing-path output from the rejected command is zero evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C31E static gate required the Firestore forward method to contain sourceMessageData.photo, but the existing method names the record sourceData and excludes every non-text message through the stronger messageType !== text discriminant. All other projected backend invariants were true.
entries.rootCause: The new gate encoded an assumed implementation detail instead of reading and binding the existing C31C text-only forward owner before writing its C31E assertion.
entries.prevention: Gate the actual messageType extraction, the messageType !== text rejection and the retained customer error together. Do not require an additional photo-field branch when the authoritative discriminated message type already excludes photo, and project every combined condition before retry.

entries.mistake: The first post-YouTube backlog inventory combined three independent ripgrep shell calls under Promise.all. One optional route/screen/copy search returned exit 1, causing the complete tool call to reject with no retained per-leg output.
entries.rootCause: Despite REG-2229, optional discovery searches were again treated as one all-success contract and their valid no-match exit was not normalized independently before aggregation.
entries.prevention: Run every optional backlog inventory as a separate command, capture LASTEXITCODE, accept only 0 or 1, and print an explicit no-match result for 1. Never use Promise.all over unnormalized optional ripgrep calls; the rejected combined call is zero inventory evidence.

entries.mistake: The first final backlog status/hash verification placed a pipeline directly after a foreach statement, producing an empty-pipe-element parser error before any requested status or checksum evidence was emitted.
entries.rootCause: A statement-form foreach loop was treated like the pipeline-capable ForEach-Object cmdlet without wrapping or collecting its output first.
entries.prevention: For bounded PowerShell evidence, assign foreach output to a named task-specific array and pipe that array to formatting, or use ForEach-Object explicitly. A parser-rejected verification is zero evidence and is registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The follow-up registry inspection guessed a REG-2243 evidence filename with an extra C31E prefix. Get-Content could not resolve it and the combined command exited nonzero even though the registry metadata read succeeded.
entries.rootCause: The exact evidence path already existed in the registry entry, but a narrative-derived filename was attempted before reading that authoritative property.
entries.prevention: Read the last registry entry and its evidence array first, validate each returned literal path, then access the file in a separate command. Never append inferred ticket prefixes to evidence filenames, and do not combine an authoritative metadata read with an unverified path read.

entries.mistake: The post-YouTube independent navigation audit found that check-personal-uniform-navigation-six-family-conformance-c27d.ps1 rejects the current canonical six-family projection after the videos item, despite the bounded 216-test Flutter smoke run passing.
entries.rootCause: C29E intentionally replaced the predecessor Social default with the accepted Home-first order videos, shorts, create, feed, but the still-invoked C27D gate retained the older shorts, videos, feed, create literal sequence and Videos label. The runtime owner and later focused tests were correct; the historical static assertion was stale.
entries.prevention: C32I binds C27D to the C29E Home-first ticket, runtime owner and focused test, rejects the superseded literal order, and retains every non-Social C27D family assertion. A future accepted successor must update the bound gate contract through an exact ticket and two fresh cycles rather than leaving an older qualification owner contradictory.

entries.mistake: The C32I audit-result insertion used the existing YouTube hold heading as both retained context and a repeated trailing heading, leaving an empty duplicate YouTube section before the new source-smoke section.
entries.rootCause: The add-before-heading patch did not remove the original anchor line from the replacement hunk before re-emitting it after the inserted block.
entries.prevention: When inserting a Markdown section before an existing heading, replace the single anchor with new-section content followed by exactly one copy of the anchor. Immediately project heading counts before broader document validation; duplicate structural headings are corrected only after registration.

entries.mistake: The post-C32I C28E gate-only preflight stopped at check-personal-android-navigation-host-qualification-c28e.ps1 because its r60.27 machine-state hash assertion rejected the current bytes. None of the remaining C28E preflight gates ran.
entries.rootCause: Unresolved at registration. The exact expected path/hash, current file hash, repository history and any later authorized successor binding must be compared before classifying protected-state mutation versus a stale historical hash assertion.
entries.prevention: Treat the C28E preflight as failed with zero downstream gate evidence. Do not change the protected r60.27 state, its C28E contract or host gate and do not retry until exact literal paths and hashes are read, current bytes are compared to authoritative retained evidence, and any repair is converted into an exact ticket.

entries.mistake: After C32J repaired the C28E historical evidence binding, the gate-only preflight progressed through the host, exported semantics, C27B, C27C, C27D and C26B gates, then C26C rejected the current switcher because targetAnchor Alignment.topLeft was absent.
entries.rootCause: Unresolved at registration. The C26C predecessor contract must be compared to the later C27C uniform embedded-switcher owner and any newer end-aligned Social amendment before deciding whether runtime alignment regressed or the old top-left literal is superseded.
entries.prevention: Treat the C28E preflight as incomplete after six passed gates and one C26C rejection. Do not edit or retry C26C until the exact predecessor and successor gate, runtime owner, ticket evidence and focused tests are read and a separate exact ticket is selected if reconciliation is required.

entries.mistake: The first bounded search for compactOverlayAlignEnd and right-edge switcher evidence combined broad roots with restrictive C29E/navigation globs and returned no matches, but the valid optional ripgrep exit 1 was not normalized, so the shell call failed with no evidence.
entries.rootCause: The search relied on filename globs that excluded the actual current runtime owner and repeated the REG-2243 mistake of treating an optional no-match as a command failure.
entries.prevention: Search the exact already-resolved runtime, C29E focused test and completion evidence paths separately. Capture LASTEXITCODE, accept only 0 or 1, print an explicit no-match result for 1 and never use the rejected broad-glob call as evidence.

entries.mistake: The next compactOverlayAlignEnd evidence search scanned the full large regression registry and all docs/quality under a 10-second bound. It timed out with exit 124 before returning a complete match set.
entries.rootCause: The search scope was not projected from exact known C29E/C29N evidence owners even though broad quality-tree searches are known to exceed bounded command limits in this dirty repository.
entries.prevention: Resolve exact ticket and completion filenames first, inspect the known REG-1154/1155 entries by id through parsed registry objects, and search only those literal files. A timed-out search is zero evidence and cannot support an alignment conclusion.

entries.mistake: After the C32K correction, the C28E preflight passed seven gates and then C26D rejected current Social because it no longer contains bottomNavigationBar MoolDestinationNavigationV2.
entries.rootCause: Unresolved at registration. C26D's original shared Social projection must be compared to later C29E/C29N provider-aware dock authority, current exact edge/middle order and focused tests before deciding whether Social regressed or the predecessor gate is stale.
entries.prevention: Treat the C28E preflight as incomplete after seven passed gates and one C26D rejection. Do not edit or retry C26D until its exact literals, later Social authority, current runtime owner and tests are read and a separate exact ticket is selected if reconciliation is required.

entries.mistake: The first C32L scope transition wrote no_runtime_UI_route_screen_copy_reference_order_or behavior_change with a space inside the machine-style exclusion identifier.
entries.rootCause: A prose conjunction was pasted into an underscore-delimited machine-state string without a final separator check.
entries.prevention: Project every newly patched machine-state array value before gate validation and require consistent underscore-delimited identifiers. Register and correct copy defects before treating the state as executable evidence.

entries.mistake: The post-C32L C28E gate-only preflight passed every navigation, copy, interaction, route, scope and memory gate through the Personal action projection, then check-buy-protected-baseline rejected current Buy tree hash 12a9880a... against historical expected 6e2c18af....
entries.rootCause: The C28E preflight correctly invokes the founder-approved Buy protected-tree gate. The latest existing Buy baseline remains the 43-file FSC06 seal with hash 6e2c18af..., while the current dirty Buy tree hashes to 12a9880a.... No existing protected baseline records the current hash, so later Buy source work has not received a founder-approved successor baseline and cannot be silently accepted by this historical audit.
entries.prevention: Keep C32J/C32K/C32L source implementation separate from full qualification. Do not replace, rewrite, bypass or weaken the Buy baseline; require exact founder review of the Buy delta and a separately authorized immutable successor baseline before retrying the complete C28E preflight. Report every preceding gate only as individually passed, not as aggregate qualification.

entries.mistake: The first 18-file C32J-L focused cycle passed memory, MVP scope/delivery and UI locks, then the new C32J checker rejected scope ticket differs because it required C32J to remain the active ticket after the lawful C32K and C32L child transitions.
entries.rootCause: The C32J checker encoded current active-ticket equality rather than accepting either active ownership during implementation or the exact preserved priorC32JBlockedTicketAssessment after a child ticket becomes active. The same lifecycle risk exists in C32K.
entries.prevention: A chained successor checker must validate active scope only while its ticket is current, then validate its exact immutable prior assessment id, manifest hash and implementation state after transition. Convert this to a separate exact source-gate ticket, repair C32J and C32K together, and restart focused cycles with a fresh fingerprint.

entries.mistake: The first C32M scope transition compound patch was rejected atomically because it expected a copied C32L exclusion line with alignment change wording that did not match the current state.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined assessment preservation, new selection, ticket disclosure and authority updates while one lower ticket-array context was reconstructed from memory instead of copied from the exact current file.
entries.prevention: Re-read the exact current selected assessment and lower ticket/disclosure blocks. Apply the currentTicketId, assessment rename/addition, checkpoint, ticket arrays and evidence paths as separate short hunks, validating JSON and hash binding after each logical group. The rejected patch changed zero bytes.

entries.mistake: The first post-transition C32M validation invocation passed -CandidateId to check-mvp-delivery-discipline-lock.ps1, but that gate has no CandidateId parameter, so the parallel validation group stopped before its results could be accepted.
entries.rootCause: The invocation shape was inferred from the neighbouring MVP scope gate instead of being copied from the delivery-lock script's declared parameter block.
entries.prevention: Read each gate parameter block before composing a grouped validation. Invoke the delivery lock with -RequireTicketSelectionAssessment and its default state paths, and treat the aborted parallel group as producing no accepted validation result.

entries.mistake: The C32M prior-cycle fingerprint lookup searched config, docs, artifacts, scripts and mobile tests together and timed out while traversing the large retained artifacts tree.
entries.rootCause: The lookup repeated the already-registered broad-evidence-search pattern instead of first targeting the two known C32J/C32M evidence documents named by the active scope and regression entries.
entries.prevention: Do not include artifacts or repository-wide quality evidence in a discovery search when exact evidence paths are already registered. Read the named C32J chained-scope evidence and C32M state directly, then search only those files if a literal lookup remains necessary.

entries.mistake: The first protected Buy delta audit correctly read check-buy-protected-baseline.ps1 but also attempted to read a guessed config/buy-protected-baseline.json path that does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The baseline location was inferred from a generic naming convention instead of being taken from the gate's declared default BaselinePath, which points to the retained FSC06 artifact directory.
entries.prevention: When auditing a protected baseline, read the gate first, extract its exact default path, and then read only that path. Do not pair a known gate read with a speculative state filename.

entries.mistake: The Buy delta audit attempted to read RUNTIME-MANIFEST.txt beside the C25F BASELINE.json even though C25F explicitly records its predecessor manifest in the C24F artifact directory.
entries.rootCause: The manifest filename was taken from the baseline but its exact repository-relative predecessorManifest value was not; directory co-location was assumed.
entries.prevention: Resolve protected evidence only from the full exact path recorded in the parsed baseline property. Never combine a declared filename with an inferred sibling directory.

entries.mistake: The retained C24F RUNTIME-MANIFEST line for buy_v2_saved_products_store.dart contains a 62-character value, 044da1e0...b7ed94, instead of a complete 64-character SHA-256; the current file computes to 044da1e0...e9e1e563...b7ed94.
entries.rootCause: Unresolved at registration. The malformed line appears to have dropped two hexadecimal characters inside the digest. The immutable evidence must not be edited, and no current Buy drift may be inferred from this line until its generation history and surrounding tree evidence are reconciled.
entries.prevention: Require every retained runtime-manifest digest to match exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters before using it for per-file delta classification. Preserve the defective C24F file byte-for-byte, register a separate exact evidence-reconciliation ticket, and distinguish malformed evidence from genuine current-source changes.

entries.mistake: An optional exact-hash lookup for the current Buy screen returned ripgrep exit code 1 because no existing config or quality document records that hash, and the command treated normal no-match as failure.
entries.rootCause: The optional discovery command did not explicitly accept ripgrep exit code 1, repeating the known PowerShell optional-search handling defect.
entries.prevention: For optional ripgrep discovery, explicitly accept exit codes 0 and 1 or avoid the search when direct source and declared baseline evidence are sufficient. Do not retry this no-match lookup.

entries.mistake: After the C32N transition, C32M correctly validated priorC32MFocusedTicketAssessment on both hosts but its static success message still printed active=C32M.
entries.rootCause: The lifecycle assertions were made conditional, but the pre-existing pass-output literal was not updated to describe active-or-preserved-prior binding.
entries.prevention: Whenever a gate gains a historical lifecycle path, update its success identity in the same ticket and assert that the output does not make an active-scope claim. Register misleading green evidence before retrying the gate.

entries.mistake: C32N initial focused cycle 1 passed all source gates and 43 Flutter cases, then three buy_v2_router_test cases failed because key mool-home-launcher was absent.
entries.rootCause: Unresolved at registration. The test may retain a predecessor launcher key after the accepted compact Mool navigation migration, or the runtime may have lost a required connected action. Current navigation owners and later focused acceptance must be compared before any edit or retry.
entries.prevention: Stop the C32N cycle after 43 passed and 3 failed cases. Read the failing test, current shared navigation owner, C29N/C27 acceptance and direct route behavior. Select a separate exact ticket before changing a stale test or runtime, and restart with a fresh manifest fingerprint.

entries.mistake: After the exact compact-launcher replacement, buy_v2_router_test still failed three cases because it expected buy-local-destination-tabs to be absent and tried obsolete mool-navigator-buy-orders/shop keys after selecting the Buy family.
entries.rootCause: C32O assumed the launcher key was the complete stale-test surface. The predecessor test also predates the accepted C26D split between the compact family chooser and the persistent Buy local destination rail.
entries.prevention: Stop after 6 passed and 3 failed Buy router cases. Read the accepted C26D helper and current Buy local keys, then create a separate exact test-topology successor. Preserve every content, route, Back and no-legacy assertion and restart with a fresh fingerprint.

entries.mistake: The first additional read-only backend regression audit attempted to read backend/package.json, but the repository has no package manifest at that root.
entries.rootCause: A conventional Node backend layout was assumed instead of discovering exact package.json owners inside the bounded backend directory.
entries.prevention: Before invoking backend tests, use rg --files backend -g package.json, read the exact discovered package scripts and then run only repository-declared read-only test commands. Do not guess a backend root manifest.

entries.mistake: The post-C32P 17-file cross-vertical Flutter audit completed 183 cases and then failed the Retailer Business Services compact-accessibility case because a RenderFlex overflowed by 16 pixels on the right at 320x700 with text scale 1.3.
entries.rootCause: MoolOutcomeDock's three-action center Row had 216 pixels available at 320 width but required three fixed 72-pixel capsules plus two 8-pixel gaps, totaling 232 pixels and overflowing by exactly 16.
entries.prevention: Keep three-action capsules flexible up to the 72-pixel design maximum so compact layouts absorb the two fixed gaps without reducing the 44-point minimum target. Require phase-specific 320x700 text-scale-1.3 assertions, direct dock tests, analyzer and the original 17-file cross-vertical audit.

entries.mistake: The first post-failure evidence probe attempted to read config/mvp-scope-state.json, which does not exist.
entries.rootCause: A generic scope-state filename was guessed even though the active handoff and repository inventory must remain the only path authorities.
entries.prevention: Discover scope and ticket state files with bounded rg --files config filtering before reading them. Do not retry the guessed path or infer a conventional state filename.

entries.mistake: The registered post-C32P diagnostic invoked the PowerShell regression-memory gate, received its explicit pass output, and then falsely threw because it compared the unset native-process LASTEXITCODE variable with zero.
entries.rootCause: LASTEXITCODE was used for an in-process PowerShell script even though it is not the script-success authority and may remain null when no native executable set it.
entries.prevention: For repository PowerShell gates, rely on terminating errors and the PowerShell success indicator after invocation; reserve LASTEXITCODE checks for native commands that actually set it. Do not convert a printed gate pass into a wrapper failure.

entries.mistake: The first C32Q scope-gate invocation was rejected before source mutation because selectedTicketAssessment used the invented implementationDisposition value runtime_source_repair.
entries.rootCause: The ticket selection used a descriptive phrase without first constraining it to the delivery lock's exact implementation-disposition enum.
entries.prevention: Read the delivery lock's allowed disposition values and use only an existing exact enum. Keep the gate failure as evidence and do not touch runtime source until scope and delivery gates pass.

entries.mistake: C32Q inferred that the unconstrained protected empty-state action caused the 16-pixel overflow and bounded its button, but the exact compact focused test still failed by the same 16 pixels in the access-denied phase.
entries.rootCause: The app bar, empty state and dock were compared statically, but the exact overflowing RenderFlex creator was not captured before selecting the shared empty-state owner.
entries.prevention: Remove the non-causal shared-widget edit, preserve the phase-specific test assertions, capture the overflowing RenderFlex creator and ancestor path from the exact failing frame, and repair only the evidenced production owner before retrying acceptance.

entries.mistake: The first C32Q RenderFlex creator diagnostic failed to compile because the test referenced RenderFlex while importing material.dart but not flutter/rendering.dart.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic assumed the Material library exported the concrete rendering type used for render-tree traversal.
entries.prevention: Import package:flutter/rendering.dart explicitly for RenderFlex diagnostics, run the exact one-case diagnostic before any production edit, and remove diagnostic-only code after the creator is captured.

entries.mistake: After the exact C32Q case, domain file and analyzer passed, an eight-file shared-navigation batch was selected by broad source-symbol search without checking successor applicability. It mixed current tests with superseded predecessor expectations and ended 15 passed and 30 failed.
entries.rootCause: Textual references to MoolOutcomeDock and minimumTapTarget were treated as acceptance applicability. The batch included known-obsolete mool-home-launcher topology and unrelated historical geometry/copy-fit suites.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the eight-file batch. Reconcile each failure-bearing filename against regression memory and later accepted C26D/C27D/C29N/C32P authorities, then run only current applicable shared-dock navigation tests plus the original cross-vertical suite.

entries.mistake: An optional lookup for state or qualification rows in the C32N-C32P manifest returned ripgrep exit code 1 and the command treated normal no-match as failure, repeating the known optional-search handling defect.
entries.rootCause: The lookup did not explicitly accept ripgrep no-match even though it was exploratory and direct manifest reads had already established the required format.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the lookup. Use the directly read ordered relative-path and SHA-256 row format; future optional ripgrep searches must explicitly accept exit codes 0 and 1.

entries.mistake: The first C32Q 32-file manifest calculation used a single-quoted PowerShell format string, preserving backtick-t as literal characters instead of inserting the required tab separator.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell escape expansion was incorrectly expected inside a single-quoted format string.
entries.prevention: Discard the invalid 2AD3C0... aggregate, recompute the unchanged ordered rows with a double-quoted format string that inserts a real tab, visually verify tab-separated output and only then create the manifest.

entries.mistake: The first C32R later-authority comparison command correctly inventoried the matching test files, but its following content search still used guessed universal-directory paths for the C29N Social test and a nonexistent C32P test filename, causing ripgrep to exit 1 after returning partial evidence.
entries.rootCause: The command combined path discovery and content inspection instead of consuming the exact inventory output before constructing the second bounded read.
entries.prevention: Separate repository path discovery from content inspection. Reuse only exact rg --files results in later commands, and do not infer a directory or filename from a ticket ID when no matching file was inventoried.

entries.mistake: The historical C22F file produced one pass and eight failures: six family cases expected the removed 72x48 local-cell geometry but received the accepted 72x58 destination rail cell, and two motion cases searched for local inner-chroma widgets that the later flat local-destination system no longer owns.
entries.rootCause: C22F predates the C27B/C27D fixed destination-rail system. It still equates local destination cells with legacy glass dock capsules even though current source intentionally retains inner chroma only in the historical dock primitive and uses fixed icon-label cells for local navigation.
entries.prevention: Migrate C22F under a separate test-only successor to assert the current differentiated owners: 58-pixel local rail cells, 48-pixel legacy dock capsules, local selected indicator and press scale, and retained dock-only chroma. Require C27B and C27D to remain green.

entries.mistake: The historical C23C file produced one pass and one failure because it required the removed full-width mool-home-launcher and rejected destination-local navigation, while current destination shells intentionally expose the compact Mool launcher, local rail and Chat anchor.
entries.rootCause: C23C froze the pre-C25/C26 destination shell before the accepted compact connected-navigation topology was introduced and later qualified by C26D, C27B and C27D.
entries.prevention: Migrate C23C under a separate test-only successor to the compact launcher and local-navigation contract without restoring compatibility keys or weakening current topology assertions.

entries.mistake: The historical C07 file produced one pass and four failures because it requires removed mool-home-area, mool-home-primary-actions, mool-root-selected and horizontal root-rail overflow owners instead of the accepted fixed Mool Home dashboard and six-family domain menu.
entries.rootCause: C07 is a predecessor of the C23-C27 home and connected-navigation redesign but remained executable with assertions for its superseded topology.
entries.prevention: Migrate C07 under a separate test-only successor to the exact mool-home-dashboard and mool-home-family-* owners, direct family routing and current platform-back behavior. Keep R03, C24B2, C26D and C27D green.

entries.mistake: The historical C20F aggregate file produced two passes and two failures because it requires the state marker c20f after the machine contract advanced to C20H and requires an exact C10E test title that later changed from local/global wording to contextual/connected wording.
entries.rootCause: The aggregate test treated transient phase labels and a human-readable test title as permanent source contracts instead of following the accepted C20H lifecycle and current C10E behavior owner.
entries.prevention: Migrate C20F under a separate test-only successor to exact C20H state and current C10E behavior tokens, preserving all family counts, route owners and closed build/install authority checks.

entries.mistake: The historical R15 file produced one pass and fifteen failures because every fitment case and the compact operability case calls scrollUntilVisible on the removed mool-root-main-actions rail before reaching the remaining Personal exposure matrix.
entries.rootCause: R15 retained the predecessor horizontally scrolling root-action owner after Mool Home moved to a fixed six-family domain menu with mool-home-family-* targets.
entries.prevention: Migrate only the root portion under a separate test-only successor to fixed dashboard family targets and current semantics, then run the entire R15 matrix so later phases cannot remain hidden behind the first stale owner. Keep R03 and C24B2 compact 140-percent coverage green.

entries.mistake: The first C32S focused run did not load because the migrated C22F assertion referenced MoolColors.navy while the test imported mool_design_system.dart but not the mool_theme.dart owner that declares MoolColors.
entries.rootCause: The migration reused a production theme constant without checking its defining library against the test's imports before the first compile.
entries.prevention: Import the exact mool_theme.dart owner in the test, rebind the C32S source hash, run the dual-host gate and analyzer, and only then retry the focused Flutter test.

entries.mistake: The C32S pre-retry command ran repository-root scripts through relative paths while its working directory was apps/mobile. All three gate launches failed path resolution, but the trailing successful Flutter analyzer left the composite shell command with exit code 0.
entries.rootCause: Repository gates and the mobile analyzer were combined in one command despite requiring different working directories, and the sequence did not fail closed on an earlier native-process error.
entries.prevention: Run repository PowerShell gates from repository root in a dedicated fail-closed command. Run Flutter analyzer and tests separately from apps/mobile, and never use the final command's exit code as proof that every earlier native command succeeded.

entries.mistake: The initial C32U ticket said the successor would assert Social-to-Home, carrying forward C07's obsolete assumption that tapping Mool from Social navigates directly to /app/mool.
entries.rootCause: The ticket was drafted from the historical test title before reading the current MoolGlobalNavigationV2 launcher handler, which toggles the connected six-family navigator and never invokes a direct Home callback.
entries.prevention: Correct the ticket before test mutation to assert Social-to-connected-menu and direct-route Mool Home as separate journeys. Rehash the ticket, rebind scope and dual-host gate, and do not restore the removed direct-home behavior.

entries.mistake: After the two known Mool Home root portions were migrated, R15 completed fifteen cases and then failed the compact operability case at the first nonroot MvpActionChoiceRoot assertion because it still searched for the removed mool-action-<family> selected-main key.
entries.rootCause: The original fifteen failures all stopped at the earlier root-rail owner, hiding a second historical navigation contract inside the same test file. The action-choice shell now uses its standalone Mool launcher topology rather than the removed global root rail keys.
entries.prevention: Preserve C32W's 15-pass/1-fail evidence, select a separate C32X test-only successor, compare against the exact current MvpActionChoiceRoot and its dedicated tests, then migrate only the hidden action-choice navigation assertions before retrying the full R15 matrix.

entries.mistake: A C32W evidence search appended the Windows-incompatible path apps/mobile/test/uaw_personal_mvp_* after exact directory owners, so ripgrep returned useful partial matches but exited 1 on the wildcard path.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style filename wildcard was passed as a literal Windows path despite the existing regression rule requiring rg --files inventory or directory roots on Windows.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the wildcard. Read only exact paths already returned by the partial inventory, and use rg --files with a regex filter for any further discovery.

entries.mistake: The first C32X migration assumed system Back would close the connected navigator before invoking the standalone MvpActionChoiceRootV2 callback. The full R15 run again reached 15 passes, then found the menu still visible after Back.
entries.rootCause: The MaterialApp no-op harness has no Router back-button dispatcher, so the root PopScope owns Back and invokes onBack while the overlay stays mounted. The dedicated current FIX2 authority verifies launcher toggle and root survival but never claims standalone Back closes the menu; production routes do not use this legacy presentation unless the tests-only flag is enabled.
entries.prevention: Correct C32X to use the explicit outside-dismiss owner for menu closure, then verify one root Back callback separately. Rehash the ticket and test gate before retry; do not treat the no-op harness overlay as a production runtime defect or change runtime source.

entries.mistake: The corrected C32X R15 run reported 16 passes but emitted four hit-test warnings because each attempted launcher close tap was obscured by the open overlay. The pointer actually reached the overlay outside-dismiss layer, so the assertions passed for the wrong interaction owner.
entries.rootCause: The connected navigator overlay is intentionally modal and covers the launcher hit point. The test assumed the underlying toggle remained directly tappable instead of using the explicit mool-switcher-outside-dismiss owner.
entries.prevention: Reject the warning-bearing run as qualification evidence. Correct the ticket and test to assert the outside-dismiss key and tap an unobscured coordinate within it, require zero warnings, then rerun the full matrix and current FIX2 authority.

entries.mistake: After C32X produced a clean 16-pass R15 successor, the C32W predecessor gate still pinned the intermediate 15-pass/1-hidden-failure R15 file hash even though C32X was authorized to change the remaining assertion block in that same test owner.
entries.rootCause: C32W made its scope-ticket binding lifecycle-safe, but its shared test-file hash assertion remained unconditional. The gate preserved ticket history while overlooking that a later authorized successor would legitimately advance the same file bytes.
entries.prevention: Preserve the C32W intermediate hash in its machine evidence. Require that hash only while C32W is active; otherwise accept the exact C32X final hash only through the active C32X ticket binding or a preserved qualified C32X assessment, then replay both predecessor and successor gates on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: The first intended C32P-C32X gate-chain replay used remembered C32P and C32Q script filenames. The initial literal existence check rejected the nonexistent C32P name before any gate ran.
entries.rootCause: Ticket labels and remembered qualification wording were treated as executable script filenames instead of resolving exact owners from the repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the guessed names. Resolve the exact C32P-C32X script paths with rg --files, require one intended gate per ticket, and execute only the returned literal paths in fail-closed host-specific loops.

entries.mistake: The first new-manifest validator correctly split the header and every data row on real tabs, but then used a single-quoted regex containing backtick-t and falsely reported all 61 rows as malformed.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell does not expand backtick escapes inside single-quoted strings. The validator combined a correct field split with a contradictory regex that searched for the literal backtick and letter t.
entries.prevention: Reject the contradictory validation output. Split each row on an actual tab, validate the two fields independently, verify every listed file hash, and reseal because registering this mistake changes a manifest member and adds a new evidence owner.

entries.mistake: The first final manifest reseal patch supplied replacement hunks out of file order: registry and later C32X documents preceded the alphabetically earlier ACTIVE-CODEX-HANDOFF row, so apply_patch rejected the whole patch.
entries.rootCause: Independent manifest-row replacements were composed in semantic update order rather than their actual order in the target file, while relying on one sequential multi-hunk patch.
entries.prevention: Verify atomic rejection, register the failure, then use separate or strictly target-file-ordered hunks. Recompute the now-changed registry and new evidence hashes before reseal and revalidate every manifest member afterward.

entries.mistake: The first post-seal backlog reconciliation placed required document reads and an optional C32Y/C33 filename search in one Promise.all. The optional no-match exited 1 and hid the successful sibling outputs.
entries.rootCause: A raw ripgrep optional inventory was allowed to control aggregate orchestration status despite the permanent rule requiring exit-1 no-match normalization before aggregation.
entries.prevention: Run required document reads independently. Normalize optional rg exit 1 to an explicit no-match result before any aggregation, and retain the C32R-C32X manifest as historical because registering this recurrence changes a listed registry member.

entries.mistake: A backlog search passed the nonexistent remembered path config/mvp-delivery-discipline-lock.json alongside real owners, producing an OS path error after partial matches.
entries.rootCause: The delivery gate's presumed config filename was guessed instead of reading the gate parameter defaults or resolving exact paths from the repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the guessed path or use its partial search output as evidence. Read the exact owner from scripts/check-mvp-delivery-discipline-lock.ps1 or use a normalized rg --files inventory before any related check.

entries.mistake: An Eat inventory guessed apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/eat from the real test/ui_v2/eat directory. The nonexistent runtime path caused an OS error after exact test-title and features/eat partial output.
entries.rootCause: Test-directory structure was assumed to mirror production runtime structure without an rg --files inventory or import resolution.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the guessed directory or qualify the partial command. Resolve runtime owners from the exact tests' imports and literal existing paths returned by rg --files before any focused execution.

entries.mistake: The first successful whole-lib Eat regex used the unbounded substring eat, so it also matched create and mixed unrelated Creator, Social Create and YouTube files into the output.
entries.rootCause: A domain-name substring was treated as a path component without delimiter boundaries.
entries.prevention: Reject the noisy inventory. Require the literal features/eat path segment and enumerate imported shared app, journey and universal owners separately from exact test imports.

entries.mistake: The historical C20E focused run produced one pass and five failures: four family cases require compact clusters centered at the 160-pixel rail center although current left-anchored clusters center at 76 or 116 pixels, and the reduced-motion case casts a keyed SizedBox to AnimatedContainer.
entries.rootCause: C20E predates the accepted C27B compact-leading destination rail and still binds centered glass-capsule geometry and removed per-cell animation owners.
entries.prevention: Preserve the 1-pass/5-fail run, do not retry or mutate runtime, and compare C20E's exact geometry/type assertions with current accepted source and later focused tests. Convert the attributed finding into one exact successor ticket before any test or source change.

entries.mistake: The first C21E authority lookup repeated the raw optional-rg-in-Promise.all pattern, so a no-match test-filename search suppressed three successful required document reads.
entries.rootCause: The already-registered optional inventory rule was not applied when composing a new parallel read batch.
entries.prevention: Do not reuse the suppressed output. Read required C21E and C22G owners independently and normalize optional filename search exit 1 to an explicit no-match before any aggregation.

entries.mistake: The first C20E failure summary called expected 160 versus actual 76/116 panel heights, but line 222 compares horizontal center coordinates: rail center x=160 versus left-anchored cluster centers x=76/116.
entries.rootCause: Numeric failure output was interpreted before binding the stack line to the exact assertion expression.
entries.prevention: Read the exact failing source line before naming a geometric quantity. Correct REG-2297 and its evidence to center alignment while preserving the separate SizedBox/AnimatedContainer type failure and native 1-pass/5-fail result.

entries.mistake: The C21E C17D matrix owner produced zero passes and ten failures: nine cases require centered clusters at x=206 instead of current left-anchored centers x=76/116, and the inventory requires 200/268 widths instead of current 152/232.
entries.rootCause: C17D/C21E predates the accepted C27B compact-leading destination rail and still binds centered 200/268-pixel optical-glass geometry and removed glass/specular owners.
entries.prevention: Preserve the 0-pass/10-fail run, do not retry or alter production geometry, and compare exact C17D/C21E assertions with current C27-era local navigation tests and tokens. Select a separate exact successor ticket before any historical-test migration.

entries.mistake: The first C33A migration read indicator.width and indicator.height from AnimatedContainer, but that widget exposes no such public getters, so analyzer reported two undefined_getter errors.
entries.rootCause: Constructor width/height parameters were assumed to remain public widget properties instead of being represented through internal constraints.
entries.prevention: Measure rendered indicator geometry with tester.getSize(finder); use widget<AnimatedContainer> only for public properties such as duration. Rehash the test and gate before analyzer retry.

entries.mistake: Both C33A host gates and the Flutter analyzer were launched in one aggregate call. The analyzer failure suppressed any successful gate outputs, leaving no usable host-gate evidence.
entries.rootCause: Independent repository-gate and mobile-analysis evidence owners were coupled under one failing aggregate result.
entries.prevention: Run repository gates separately from apps/mobile analyzer and tests. Treat the suppressed host calls as no evidence and replay them only after registration and source rehash.

entries.mistake: The first C33A Flutter run measured unselected indicator widths after only one pump while remounting the same keys across selected indices. Four families observed the previous 14-pixel selected width instead of the settled zero width.
entries.rootCause: The migrated steady-state matrix retained the historical one-frame pump even though current selected-indicator geometry animates between selected indices.
entries.prevention: Use pumpAndSettle in the steady-state mount helper before geometry measurement. Keep reduced-motion duration and one-tap behavior in their independent case, rehash the test/gate, and only then retry C20E.

entries.mistake: The first final C33B chain stopped because C33A unconditionally pinned C17D's preserved pre-C33B failure hash even though C33B is authorized to migrate that same separately held owner.
entries.rootCause: C33A preserved its own lifecycle assessment but treated the excluded future C17D owner as permanently immutable in its executable gate rather than binding later bytes through the authorized successor.
entries.prevention: Keep C33A machine evidence pinned to the original 0/10 hash. Require that hash only while C33A is active; otherwise require the exact C33B final hash through active C33B or preserved qualified C33B scope binding, then replay C33A and C33B on both hosts.

entries.mistake: The combined REG-2304 status/result patch used an unwrapped document sentence as its anchor even though the file stores the sentence across two lines, causing atomic rejection.
entries.rootCause: The registry and document updates were composed from one remembered phrase rather than independently read exact anchors.
entries.prevention: Verify atomic rejection, register the failure, then patch registry status and document result separately using exact current anchors read from each target.

entries.mistake: The first focused Ride C16E Flutter test command completed through the shell tool, but its output was truncated at the model boundary, leaving the exact pass/fail result unknown and unusable as qualification evidence.
entries.rootCause: The focused test was run without a bounded durable log and exit-code sidecar, so output truncation removed the only visible result.
entries.prevention: Never infer the C16E result. After registration, rerun that one suite independently with output redirected to a retained bounded log and a separate exit-code sidecar, then read only the summary tail and preserve the full log.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to inspect the current regression-memory tail guessed config/codex-regression-memory.json, which does not exist, and caused the aggregate read call to fail.
entries.rootCause: A descriptive memory label was converted into a presumed filename instead of resolving the exact repository owner first.
entries.prevention: Resolve memory owners with rg --files before reading. Use config/codex-development-regression-registry.json and run required reads independently from any optional inventory.

entries.mistake: The current Ride booking journey throws the shared local-navigation minimum-width assertion at a 320x568 logical surface with 1.4 text scale. Both C16E cases fail before Ride's four local actions render, including the reduced-motion case.
