entries.rootCause: MoolDestinationNavigationV2 reserves compact global Mool, Ride-family-root and Chat controls in the same row, while MoolLocalNavigationRail still requires four 44-pixel actions plus gaps and internal insets. The remaining bounded width is smaller than the rail's asserted 182-pixel minimum.
entries.prevention: Preserve the 0-pass/2-fail log. Before changing source, select one exact MVP Ride compact-navigation successor. The repair must keep every local action at least 44 logical pixels, preserve Mool/family/Chat controls and reduced-motion behavior, avoid provider or route expansion, and pass C16E plus current shared navigation regressions and analyzer.

entries.mistake: The C33C scope transition preserved C33B under completedC33BTicketAssessment, but the qualified C33A and C33B gates require the established priorC33BQualifiedAssessment property.
entries.rootCause: A new descriptive property name was introduced without first reading the predecessor gates' exact lifecycle contract.
entries.prevention: Correct only the property name to priorC33BQualifiedAssessment, preserve the assessment bytes, and require the C33A/C33B/C33C gate chain to pass on both PowerShell hosts before qualification.

entries.mistake: The qualified C33A and C33B gates unconditionally require the pre-C33C mool_design_system.dart hash and a scope with runtimeWriteAuthorized=false, so the authorized C33C runtime successor cannot replay its predecessor chain.
entries.rootCause: Both test-only predecessor gates treated a shared runtime owner and the then-current execution flags as permanently immutable instead of lifecycle-binding a later exact runtime successor.
entries.prevention: Preserve the old hash and runtime=false checks when C33C is absent. Accept the exact C33C design hash and runtime=true only through the active C33C assessment or a preserved qualified C33C assessment; keep backend, build, device, external and secret authorities false and replay all three gates on both hosts.

entries.mistake: The first Book test-owner regex matched the ui_v2/book directory path without constraining the extension, so four candidate-capture PNGs were counted among twelve reported tests.
entries.rootCause: The alternate directory-match branch bypassed the .dart suffix constraint that applied only to the filename branch.
entries.prevention: Reject the twelve-test count. Re-run rg --files with a *.dart glob first, then apply the Book path/name filter and report capture assets separately if needed.

entries.mistake: After C33C, C16F passes its reduced-motion chooser case but the 320dp direct Bus journey misses ride-local-bus because the fourth action is off-screen in the new horizontal viewport; bus-booking-home never opens.
entries.rootCause: The 320dp destination row gives the local rail exactly 182 logical pixels, enough for four 44-pixel actions and three 2-pixel gaps. C33C nevertheless tests the minimum against an inset-reduced 166 pixels, creating overflow even though the rail applies no visible 8-pixel leading/trailing padding to the cluster.
entries.prevention: Preserve the 1-pass/1-fail C16F log. Select an exact successor before mutation. Use edge-to-edge minimum geometry when the physical rail width is at least 182 pixels, retain 44-pixel hit targets, and reserve horizontal overflow only for widths below the real cluster minimum; replay C16E, C16F and shared-family gates.

entries.mistake: The qualified C33C gate unconditionally requires runtimeWriteAuthorized=false, so a later exact runtime successor cannot replay C33C while its own bounded source mutation is active.
entries.rootCause: C33C closes its runtime authority correctly at qualification but does not distinguish its own completed scope from a future active or preserved runtime successor assessment.
entries.prevention: Preserve runtime=false for active/completed C33C. Permit runtime=true only through the exact active C33D ticket and source hash, then require runtime=false again after C33D qualification; keep all backend, build, device, external and secret authorities closed and replay the chain on both hosts.

entries.mistake: The first C33D attempt assumed the real 320dp Ride local rail received exactly 182 pixels and changed the fit decision accordingly. C16E still rendered the overflow owner, while the independent 181-pixel below-minimum case passed.
entries.rootCause: Destination-row arithmetic was inferred from nominal child tokens and gaps without measuring the actual LayoutBuilder width in the mounted production shell.
entries.prevention: Preserve the failed first C33D run. Before another source attempt, add a bounded diagnostic assertion/output for the actual adaptive-layout width, run only that focused diagnostic, remove diagnostic-only output, and base the correction on measured constraints rather than remembered token arithmetic.

entries.mistake: C16E and C16F call binding.setSurfaceSize(320x568) but do not set the test view physical size or device-pixel ratio. The rendered scaffold is constrained while MediaQuery remains wide, selecting 54-pixel fixed destination controls and leaving only 152 pixels for the local rail.
entries.rootCause: The historical harness assumed setSurfaceSize also changed View/MediaQuery responsive input in the current Flutter test environment.
entries.prevention: Remove the diagnostic print. Set tester.view.physicalSize to 320x568 and devicePixelRatio to 1, reset both after each test, and retain text scale 1.4. Re-run C16E and C16F independently and require real 44-pixel fixed controls plus direct Bus hit testing.

entries.mistake: C33A and C33B accept only the pre-C33C or C33C design hash, while C33C pins both its own design and C16E hashes. The authorized C33D successor legitimately advances those shared owners, so the predecessor chain cannot replay without exact successor binding.
entries.rootCause: The C33C lifecycle extension covered the first runtime successor but did not reserve a generic exact later-successor binding for the same shared design and acceptance owner.
entries.prevention: Preserve every historical hash in its state. Accept C33D design and C16E bytes only through the exact active C33D assessment or a preserved qualified C33D assessment, enforce the corresponding runtime-authority lifecycle, and replay C33A through C33D on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: The first C33C lifecycle patch wrote the final status subexpression as if ($c33dBound) with the dollar sign escaped by a backtick inside the script, risking literal rather than variable evaluation.
entries.rootCause: JavaScript patch-string escaping was carried into the target PowerShell source even though the target line itself required an ordinary variable token.
entries.prevention: Register before execution, replace only the escaped target token with $c33dBound, inspect the exact line, and then run the gate independently on both hosts.

entries.mistake: The C33D state, contract, qualification and gate were added in one large apply_patch whose returned result exceeded the model context and was truncated, leaving the mutation result unknown at the interruption point.
entries.rootCause: Four sizeable file additions were combined into one tool response instead of using bounded patches and immediate per-file verification.
entries.prevention: Treat truncated mutation output as unknown, register it before proceeding, verify every intended path with existence, size, SHA-256 and bounded head/tail reads, and never retry until verification proves whether the original mutation landed. Keep future patches small enough for an unambiguous result.

entries.mistake: The resumed C33D inspection searched the full repository root for REG2317 and timed out with exit 124 before producing complete evidence.
entries.rootCause: A required known-registry lookup used a broad dot-root search instead of the exact registry owner and already known quality path.
entries.prevention: Reject the timed-out search completely. Read the exact config/codex-development-regression-registry.json owner with a parsed bounded tail projection and search only verified literal directories when discovery is genuinely required.

entries.mistake: The resumed identity check emitted the huge full dirty-tree status together with registry data, and the successful result was truncated before the complete status could be inspected.
entries.rootCause: A preservation check combined an unbounded git status listing with unrelated JSON output even though branch, HEAD and a bounded change count were sufficient for the resumed gate.
entries.prevention: Reject the combined result as a complete tree inventory. Re-run branch and HEAD as exact scalars, count status rows without printing filenames, and inspect only task-owned paths with literal filters; preserve every other path without enumeration.

entries.mistake: The resumed C33D check printed the complete append-only regression-memory document in one command and the rendered result was truncated, so it was not a complete read.
entries.rootCause: The document was treated as a small policy file even though the permanent memory already requires large append-only documents to be read in bounded verified ranges.
entries.prevention: Reject the unpaged read. Count exact lines, read non-overlapping bounded ranges whose union covers line 1 through EOF, confirm each range boundaries and total coverage, then run the implementation memory gate with captured bounded output.

entries.mistake: C33D runtime and test/gate execution flags were closed while the scope owner still retained ticket_disclosed_and_authorized and the active ticket id, so the base MVP scope gate rejected the completed lifecycle.
entries.rootCause: The close transition changed execution and assessment fields but did not first re-read the scope checker's complete closed-state tuple: awaiting_next_ticket_classification, blank ticket id and successorRegistered=false.
entries.prevention: Preserve the rejected gate result. Copy the exact closed-state tuple from the checker, retain the qualified C33D assessment under priorC33DQualifiedAssessment, clear only active-ticket identity, and rerun the closed scope gate plus C33A through C33D on both hosts before qualification.

entries.mistake: After C33D moved to a preserved qualified assessment and all execution flags closed, the Windows PowerShell C33A predecessor gate rejected the correct closed scope as scope live authority differs.
entries.rootCause: C33A lifecycle-bound the C33D design bytes and active runtime flag, but its later generic scope assertion still retained the historical C33A test-only execution expectation when C33D was no longer active.
entries.prevention: Preserve this first stopped-chain failure. Read the exact C33A authority block, distinguish active C33A, active C33D and preserved-qualified C33D, require all execution flags false in the preserved closed branch, then replay C33A through C33D independently on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: After the C33A closed-scope rejection, bounded inspection found C33B and C33C contain the same unconditional testOrGateWriteAuthorized=true assertion and would reject the preserved-qualified C33D closed lifecycle.
entries.rootCause: The predecessor-chain extension modeled C33D runtime authority transitions but left test/gate authority pinned to an earlier active ticket instead of binding it to active versus preserved successor state.
entries.prevention: Register the static finding before executing either doomed replay. In C33A, C33B and C33C require test/gate authority only while their exact active or active-successor implementation remains open; require false when C33D is preserved qualified and the MVP scope is closed, while keeping all live authorities false.

entries.mistake: Bounded inspection before the first preserved C33D self-gate replay found that its non-active branch verifies qualified assessment and live-service holds but does not explicitly require runtimeWriteAuthorized and testOrGateWriteAuthorized to be false.
entries.rootCause: The new lifecycle branch guarded active authority equality but omitted the complementary preserved-qualified closed-authority assertion.
entries.prevention: Add one preserved branch that requires runtime and test/gate authority false, retain all existing backend/build/device/external/secret holds, and only then execute the first preserved C33D gate on each host.

entries.mistake: The C33D assessment was moved to priorC33DQualifiedAssessment with a qualified implementation state, but its evidencePath still named the original ticket manifest instead of the completed qualification document.
entries.rootCause: The close transition renamed and qualified the assessment without separately advancing its selected-ticket evidence pointer to the final qualification owner.
entries.prevention: Bind the qualified assessment evidencePath to the existing C33D qualification document, make the C33D self-gate assert that exact repository-relative owner, and replay closed scope plus dual-host predecessor/self gates before sealing.

entries.mistake: The first C33D evidence-path gate patch asserted the qualification document unconditionally before computing whether the assessment was selected or qualified, which would invalidate its legitimate prequalification branch.
entries.rootCause: The new evidence invariant was inserted beside ticket identity rather than after the existing assessment lifecycle discriminant.
entries.prevention: Register before execution, derive the expected evidence path from the already validated lifecycle state, require the ticket path for selected prequalification and qualification path for the qualified branch, then parser-check and replay both current qualified hosts.

entries.mistake: The new completed-audit backlog record recalled C33A as REG2293, but the exact parsed registry identifies the C20E finding as REG-20260815-2297-POST-SEAL-C20E-ADAPTIVE-FAMILY-CONTRACT-FAILURE.
entries.rootCause: The backlog patch used a summarized sequence assumption instead of copying the full identifier from the exact registry owner immediately before mutation.
entries.prevention: Register before correcting the backlog. Resolve every cited ID through a bounded parsed registry query, require each full exact ID to exist once, patch only the incorrect literal, and parse/cross-check the backlog before source-manifest creation.

entries.mistake: The restarted backlog cross-check found the C33B item used a reconstructed REG2300 suffix and matched zero registry entries; the exact ID ends in POST-SEAL-C17D-C21E-REMAINING-FAMILY-GLASS-CONTRACT-FAILURE.
entries.rootCause: Although the numeric entry had been found, the backlog patch still expanded its full name from ticket meaning instead of copying the exact complete ID returned by the registry.
entries.prevention: Patch the exact returned ID verbatim, then restart the full findings and ticket cross-check from its first item. A numeric prefix is never sufficient traceability and no manifest is created until every complete ID exists exactly once.

entries.mistake: The first C33D morning-checklist patch assumed the sentence beginning This is source qualification started on a new context line, but the current owner keeps This at the end of the preceding line, so apply_patch rejected the complete mutation.
entries.rootCause: The patch anchor was reconstructed from visual prose instead of copied from an immediate literal bounded read of the checklist owner.
entries.prevention: Confirm zero C33D checklist matches after the atomic rejection, copy the exact current wrapped lines, and apply the audit update and risk bullet as two independent bounded hunks before rereading the complete small document.

entries.mistake: The C33D handoff section embedded a 2,300-entry registry count before all qualification documentation was sealed; REG2330 immediately made that sentence stale.
entries.rootCause: A volatile append-only count was written into a living handoff before the no-more-mutations boundary instead of reporting the stable machine-gate result.
entries.prevention: Replace the count with a stable statement that the implementation-phase regression-memory gate passes. Exact counts belong only in final bounded command output after all registry mutations, never in pre-seal living prose.

entries.mistake: The post-C33D shared-shell audit ran current C09 independently and preserved 2 passes with 3 failures: no Mool Home current semantic, no Your area recovery text and no More MoolSocial options horizontal-overflow semantic.
entries.rootCause: The audit selection repeated REG-20260813-1713 by invoking preserved historical C09 without first applying its explicit superseded-suite disposition. C09 requires the retired area/copy/action-grid Home and old overflow rail; C24B2/C24B3 own the accepted fixed six-domain menu and connected chooser.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or edit C09 and do not restore its retired runtime. Apply the chronological suite disposition before every broad navigation audit; current C24B2 and C24B3 must pass independently, while C27B/C27D and the migrated C07/R15/FIX2 owners retain their separate current invariants.

entries.mistake: The first post-C33D Buy source-audit inventory printed an unbounded combined runtime and test path set, exceeded the available model context and returned truncated output.
entries.rootCause: The read-only discovery command did not separate counts from path disclosure or cap each filename batch, despite the repository's large retained Buy surface and dirty evidence tree.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the broad printed inventory. Count runtime and test candidates first, then inspect exact non-golden filenames in small capped groups and inventory visual or golden evidence separately. Preserve each bounded result before selecting current tests.

entries.mistake: A follow-up Buy boundary read combined five complete JSON owners, including the large MVP scope state, and the tool returned truncated output.
entries.rootCause: The bounded filename inventory recovery was not carried through to content inspection; a known large append-only scope owner was printed raw beside four smaller files.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the combined raw read. Parse and print only named scope/state fields from large JSON owners, read small ticket files separately, and cap every multi-file content batch before execution.

entries.mistake: The first C33E local replay invoked the repository-relative C30Z gate from apps/mobile, so PowerShell could not find the script; the following Flutter command passed 31 tests and left the combined shell cell with exit code zero despite the earlier gate error.
entries.rootCause: Two commands with different required working directories were combined without fail-fast error handling, allowing the later native-process exit code to mask the first PowerShell command-resolution failure.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Run the C30Z gate alone from the repository root with ErrorActionPreference Stop, verify its exit code, then run mobile Flutter tests as a separate cell from apps/mobile. Never infer a combined pass from the final process exit code when prior error records exist.

entries.mistake: The fail-fast C33E replay proved the C30Z gate rejects the legitimate C33E authentication device-evidence successor solely because it requires C30Z to remain the active scope ticket with runtime-write authority.
entries.rootCause: The C30Z source-containment gate encoded only its original active implementation lifecycle and has no preserved-qualified successor branch, so normal ticket closure and auth acceptance succession produce a false failure even when every C30Z source and failed-r60.48 invariant remains intact.
entries.prevention: Before retry, select an exact test/gate-only child ticket and make the C30Z scope assertion lifecycle-aware: retain the original active-source branch, add only the exact preserved-qualified C30Z plus C33E successor branch, require current C33E test-only and existing-client authority boundaries, and continue rejecting runtime, build, install, provider, external and secret authority drift.

entries.mistake: A read-only lifecycle-pattern search passed scripts/check-uaw-c33*.ps1 as a Windows path argument, and ripgrep rejected the wildcard path syntax before producing useful results.
entries.rootCause: The command used a shell-style filename wildcard where ripgrep on Windows required a literal directory plus --glob filtering.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Search the literal scripts directory with --glob 'check-uaw-c33*.ps1', cap the matches and keep the exact C30Z path as a separate literal input.

entries.mistake: The first three-manifest hash read used Format-Table with long absolute paths, and the rendered output showed only the Path column while suppressing the required Hash values.
entries.rootCause: Width-dependent table formatting was used for exact integrity evidence instead of explicit scalar output.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Emit each repository-relative filename and SHA-256 as an explicit name=hash line; never use width-dependent tables for required digest evidence.

entries.mistake: The C33E FIX1 behavioral checker passed in PowerShell 7 but failed in Windows PowerShell 5.1 because System.IO.Path.GetRelativePath is unavailable in .NET Framework.
entries.rootCause: The new dual-host checker used a modern .NET path API without first verifying availability on the repository-required Windows PowerShell host.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Replace GetRelativePath with a validated repository-prefix substring conversion, parser-check the script, confirm no temporary fixture residue and restart the complete checker on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: An auth diagnosis read combined the complete small C30T provider-configuration record with the very large C30T findings document, and the tool truncated the combined output.
entries.rootCause: File size was not counted before combining two complete documents, so an append-heavy historical findings owner exceeded the output budget.
entries.prevention: Discard the partial large-document output, preserve only independently complete small-file evidence, and use bounded exact line ranges or parsed targeted searches for the findings owner. Never combine an unmeasured living handoff/findings file with another complete read.

entries.mistake: The bounded read-only Firebase Android SHA list command failed because the existing Firebase CLI credentials were no longer valid and reauthentication was required.
entries.rootCause: The audit assumed an existing non-secret metadata session remained usable without first accounting for session expiry; the CLI emitted firebase-debug.log before the command returned no SHA list.
entries.prevention: Do not retry, reauthenticate, run firebase login:list --json or inspect the debug log. Preserve firebase-debug.log unmodified and obtain only the Play SHA-1 presence yes/no through founder-visible Firebase Console state or a later separately authorized non-secret read session.

entries.mistake: The C33E FIX2 implementation preflight printed the complete 166,077-byte regression-memory document and the memory gate in one tool result, which truncated before complete document coverage could be established.
entries.rootCause: The existing bounded-read rule was not applied to the known append-only regression-memory owner, and an independent gate invocation was unnecessarily combined with the large document read.
entries.prevention: Discard the partial document rendering. Read the regression-memory document in verified non-overlapping line pages, confirm total line coverage, and execute its machine gate in a separate bounded call before implementation continues.

entries.mistake: A bounded authentication source-symbol lookup formatted a file and line prefix as $f:$line, causing PowerShell to reject the command before any source evidence was returned.
entries.rootCause: The audit command repeated the registered interpolation rule that a colon cannot immediately follow an undelimited PowerShell variable name.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the format operator or delimit the variable explicitly as ${f}: before a colon, and accept only a parser-clean bounded result.

entries.mistake: The source-qualified Social-auth rollback still delegates to a sequential Firebase-then-Google sign-out; a Firebase cleanup exception prevents the Google account-cache cleanup from being attempted after account-bootstrap failure.
entries.rootCause: The shared gateway modeled sign-out as one success-only sequence, and existing tests covered successful order and successful rollback but omitted first-leg and second-leg cleanup failures plus JourneySession origin/error continuity.
entries.prevention: Before another release qualification, select an exact authentication recovery ticket, attempt both cleanup owners independently, never report cleanup success when either leg fails, retain the original account-bootstrap recovery and signed-out local state, preserve the exact return route, and add a ticket-specific negative regression owner without editing locked Screen 03 presentation or accepted tests.

entries.mistake: The first FIX3 JourneySession rollback test expected a signed-out ready start but omitted allowGuestReady: true, so production correctly started at mandatory sign-in and the test failed before exercising rollback.
entries.rootCause: The new fixture copied completed setup state but did not copy the established signed-out-ready constructor precondition from the qualified authentication tests.
entries.prevention: Before retry, set allowGuestReady: true on the exact fixture, assert ready plus unauthenticated after start, explicitly begin sign-in from the protected origin, and rerun all four focused cases. Booting or mandatory sign-in is never accepted as signed-out-ready setup.

entries.mistake: A read-only Social action-continuity audit requested lines 1 through 135 of the dense social_v2_public_content.dart owner in one result, and the tool truncated the source output.
entries.rootCause: The audit used a broad source range instead of small symbol-centered windows despite the file's dense widget structure.
entries.prevention: Discard the partial rendering. Retry only with verified non-overlapping source windows of at most 60 lines around exact symbols and accept no truncated range as source evidence.

entries.mistake: The resumed mandatory repository identity check printed the complete short-status listing for the huge founder-owned dirty tree, and the tool truncated the path inventory.
entries.rootCause: The check combined required branch and HEAD verification with an unbounded rendering of thousands of preserved dirty paths.
entries.prevention: Retain the separately completed branch and HEAD evidence, discard the partial path inventory, and use only a porcelain count plus explicitly scoped ticket-owned paths for future dirty-tree checks. Never rewrite, clean or infer ownership from a truncated listing.

entries.mistake: A read-only scope audit serialized multiple nested sections of the append-heavy MVP scope state together, and historical assessment content caused the tool result to truncate.
entries.rootCause: The projection selected whole nested objects even though only exact current ticket, execution, authorization, disclosure and provider scalars were needed.
entries.prevention: Discard the broad partial rendering. Query only exact named current scalar paths and the selected ticket assessment; read any required historical owner separately with a bounded named projection.

entries.mistake: Signed-out Like, Save, Repost, Reply and Poll vote requests all collapse to one item-only authentication return URI, so a successful provider sign-in cannot recover which exact protected action the customer requested.
entries.rootCause: The public Social card exposes one untyped authentication callback, the poll and action-row callers discard action metadata, the consumer records only the Feed item, and existing C30T tests assert that lossy item-only behavior.
entries.prevention: Before another release qualification, select an exact MVP authentication-continuity ticket; carry typed action metadata and poll choice through the existing route; never automatically replay toggle or vote mutations from a persistent URI; consume a valid intent once into the exact existing UI recovery; reject malformed or stale intent safely; and add ticket-specific route, cancellation, success and negative regressions without changing locked Screen 03 or adding provider scope.

entries.mistake: An exact-action contract search passed Windows wildcard paths directly to ripgrep and named a stale guessed C30Z state path, so the command failed before returning complete evidence.
entries.rootCause: The audit repeated the registered Windows wildcard-path rule and guessed a historical path instead of discovering existing candidates first.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Discover candidate files with rg --files, search literal existing files, and apply --glob only against a literal directory. Never mix guessed missing paths with required evidence searches.

entries.mistake: The first FIX4 analyzer run referenced readySnapshot from a separate C30T test library, where the private top-level constant is not visible.
entries.rootCause: The test fixture copied a private identifier by name without checking Dart library ownership and visibility.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Define a ticket-local immutable JourneySnapshot with the exact ready setup preconditions, format the complete test owner, and rerun the same full analyzer and focused tests from the start.

entries.mistake: The FIX4 retry command ran from apps/mobile while registry and memory-gate paths were repository-root relative; those preflights failed, but PowerShell continued to analyzer and tests and returned a later combined failure.
entries.rootCause: Repository-root and mobile-root commands were combined without explicit working-directory-safe paths or fail-fast error handling.
entries.prevention: Discard the combined run as qualification evidence. Validate the registry and run the memory gate in a separate fail-fast repository-root command, then invoke mobile commands separately from apps/mobile only after preflight success.

entries.mistake: The strengthened guest Like regression found that authenticationCancelFallback remained /app/social instead of the explicit Feed item cancellation route passed by the Social consumer.
entries.rootCause: The test confused authenticationCancelFallback, which exposes the pre-authentication last-ready fallback, with readyRoute(), which correctly prioritizes the explicit _authenticationCancelTo route stored by beginSignIn.
entries.prevention: Assert action-bearing success with returnTo and explicit action-free cancellation with readyRoute(). Use authenticationCancelFallback only when testing the caller's fallback selection before beginSignIn. Rerun the full guest Like and FIX4 suites without changing production session behavior.

entries.mistake: The first cancellation-resolution patch tried to match registry JSON fields inside the evidence Markdown target, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch before changing any file.
entries.rootCause: Several logical file updates were composed without a new explicit update header before the registry anchors.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use a separate explicit update header and file-local anchor for every evidence, registry and source owner, then validate each resulting file independently.

entries.mistake: The second cancellation-resolution patch left an empty update hunk before a new file header, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch as invalid syntax.
entries.rootCause: The multi-file patch retained an unused hunk marker after the intended Markdown insertion.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Separate registration from evidence and test corrections, omit empty hunks, and validate each patch target independently.

entries.mistake: Two FIX4 regression entries referenced the planned FIX4 source gate before that file existed, causing the mandatory memory gate to fail closed.
entries.rootCause: Planned completion evidence was recorded as a current gate dependency instead of being added only after the gate owner was created.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Every registry gate/evidence path must exist at write time. Retain only the existing memory gate until the FIX4 gate is created and qualified, then add it through the completion update.

entries.mistake: The FIX4 gate used Split-Path on PSScriptRoot as a parameter default; PowerShell 7 passed, but Windows PowerShell 5.1 evaluated the default while PSScriptRoot was empty and rejected the gate before execution.
entries.rootCause: The dual-host script assumed PSScriptRoot availability during parameter default binding instead of resolving it after the param block.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Leave RepositoryRoot empty by default, resolve it from PSScriptRoot inside the script body, and rerun the complete gate under both PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.

entries.mistake: The first FIX4 source cycle whole-mobile analyzer found that social_v2_create_publication_test.dart still supplied the old zero-argument authentication callback to the new typed public-card contract.
entries.rootCause: The focused analyzer covered the changed runtime and C30T/FIX4 tests but omitted an independent SocialPublishedContentCardV2 test owner that constructs the callback directly.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Update the existing test callback to accept and assert the exact typed intent, include that owner in the FIX4 gate, run whole-mobile analysis, and restart the complete source cycle from repository preflight.

entries.mistake: The first Chrome-control skill read used an unbounded raw file read and the resulting tool output was truncated, so complete instruction coverage was not established.
entries.rootCause: The skill file size and line count were not measured before selecting a read strategy.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Measure exact bytes and lines, read non-overlapping bounded pages through EOF, verify full coverage, and decline any browser inspection whose visible or returned state could expose prohibited credential or attestation values.

entries.mistake: The final checkpoint command invoked the nonexistent shorthand path scripts/check-mvp-scope.ps1 after two earlier gates had passed.
entries.rootCause: The MVP scope gate filename was inferred instead of being discovered from the repository and checked against its parameter contract.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use a bounded repository filename search, inspect the discovered script's param block, and invoke only the exact existing gate path.

entries.mistake: A read-only r60.49 preparation inspection converted the complete nested preTicketSelectionCheckpoint to JSON and truncated because it contains a long chain of historical assessments.
entries.rootCause: A whole-object projection was used after this exact broad-scope output class had already been registered, instead of applying the required named-field allowlist.
entries.prevention: Register the recurrence before continuing. Do not retry the broad projection; use only explicit scalar or short-array field allowlists, discover property names first, and access historical objects solely by one named property at a time.

entries.mistake: The r60.49 pre-ticket checkpoint invoked check-mvp-delivery-discipline-lock.ps1 with a guessed CandidateId parameter that the gate does not expose.
entries.rootCause: The gate path was known, but its parameter contract was inferred from the separate MVP scope gate instead of being inspected directly.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Inspect the exact param block for every remaining gate and invoke only supported parameters; never transfer arguments between similarly named gates by analogy.

entries.mistake: The first Windows PowerShell syntax check embedded an interpolated nested Command string, which changed the text reaching the legacy parser and produced artificial token-spacing errors after the PowerShell 7 parse had passed.
entries.rootCause: A complex parser invocation crossed two PowerShell interpolation and quoting boundaries instead of using a literal encoded command.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Send a literal UTF-16LE Base64 EncodedCommand to Windows PowerShell and keep the gate path resolution inside the legacy host; do not reuse nested interpolated Command text.

entries.mistake: A protected-manifest comparison referenced a variable created in a prior shell invocation even though each shell command runs in a fresh process, making the comparison result invalid.
entries.rootCause: Ephemeral shell state was incorrectly treated as persistent tool-session state.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Recompute both bounded path sets inside one shell invocation and never reuse shell variables across tool calls; pass durable file paths instead.

entries.mistake: The historical C30V source-manifest generator requires 206 protected owners and cannot represent the exact current 209-owner set after the qualified FIX3, FIX4 and Chat attachment-store successors.
entries.rootCause: The protected inventory was intentionally sealed before three later qualified owners existed, but its generator had no exact successor-extension contract.
entries.prevention: Under the selected C33F ticket, retain the 206-owner baseline, require the three exact qualified successor paths, require exactly 209 unique current protected paths, and reject any other addition or omission before generating a fresh manifest.

entries.mistake: The first cycle-one command set ran repository-relative gates from apps/mobile, then allowed the final successful analyzer to mask six earlier child-process path failures and return shell exit zero.
entries.rootCause: The orchestration working directory was set for the final Flutter command instead of the repository gates, and native child exit codes were not checked after each invocation.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Orchestrate from repository root, use exact repository-relative gate paths, check LASTEXITCODE immediately after every native child, enter apps/mobile only inside a bounded Push-Location block, and restart cycle 1 from manifest comparison.

entries.mistake: The first valid C33F Flutter run passed 426 authored tests and 3 declared skips with zero failures, but the command expected 425 because a formatting-sensitive source regex undercounted the added FIX4 suite by one.
entries.rootCause: Expected authored passes were inferred from line-anchored test declaration text instead of the authoritative Flutter JSON reporter's authored-test model.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the completed reporter result to set the exact 426-pass expectation, retain all zero-failure/error/non-JSON/untyped checks, and restart cycle 1 from immutable-manifest comparison.

entries.mistake: Cycle 1 npm test used Node's default per-test reporter, emitted 524 lines and truncated tool output even though typecheck and all 537 tests passed.
entries.rootCause: A high-cardinality backend suite was started without selecting a bounded reporter after earlier unbounded-output regressions were known.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Rerun the compiled suite with Node's compact dot reporter and immediate exit checking; require a bounded reporter before every future high-cardinality test command.

entries.mistake: A C33F gate-content search passed wildcard script paths to rg on Windows after exact filenames had already been discovered, causing the follow-up search to exit 1.
entries.rootCause: The registered explicit-path rule was not applied to the second content-search stage.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the exact filenames returned by rg --files and never pass wildcard path arguments to Windows rg; wildcard filtering belongs only in the file-list pipeline.

entries.mistake: The first static-gate audit combined full reads of the C30X preflight-order gate and C30V wrapper gate in one command, and the resulting output was truncated before either file had complete verified coverage.
entries.rootCause: The two files were read together without first measuring their exact line counts and selecting bounded non-overlapping pages.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Measure each file, read one file at a time in bounded non-overlapping pages through EOF, and verify complete coverage before invoking or changing either static gate.

entries.mistake: The bounded founder-launcher source read emitted hard-coded certificate and Firebase identifier-adjacent metadata that was unnecessary for proving prompt and gate ordering.
entries.rootCause: Line-bounded output was treated as sufficient even though this secret-handling owner also contains identity metadata that must not be reproduced in tool output.
entries.prevention: Register before continuing. Do not output the founder launcher raw again; inspect only redacted structural tokens, parser results and exact ordering indices, and never reproduce password, key, OAuth client-ID, token, certificate, app-ID or related identity values.

entries.mistake: A wrapper structure search placed PowerShell variable-shaped text in a double-quoted rg regular expression, so interpolation changed the pattern and rg rejected it.
entries.rootCause: A multi-token regular expression crossed the PowerShell interpolation boundary instead of using independent literal fixed-string searches.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use single-quoted PowerShell literals and rg fixed-string mode for each exact structural token; do not combine variable-shaped source text in an interpolated regular expression.

entries.mistake: A scope-state search inferred an approvedTickets property name that is not present, so the bounded search returned no match.
entries.rootCause: The current large state schema was inferred from an older convention instead of discovering its root property names first.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Parse only the current scope-state root and print its property-name list, then access the exact discovered ticket collection by name without broad nested projection.

entries.mistake: The historical C30V and C30X static gates do not prove that the retargeted r60.49 founder launcher invokes the C33F gate before hidden prompts or that the dynamic wrapper selects C33F before generated preflights, authority consumption and appbundle execution.
entries.rootCause: The founder launcher was retargeted after the first C33F source qualification, while static ownership remained bound to historical launchers and states.
entries.prevention: Register and implement UAW-C33F-FIX1 before any build. The current C33F gate must parse both owners, require exact candidate/state/gate bindings, prove one C33F invocation before all three hidden prompts, prove wrapper gate/config/manifest/preflight/consume/appbundle ordering, reject credential output or clipboard owners, pass both PowerShell hosts, and complete a new immutable manifest plus two identical full cycles.

entries.mistake: A script filename search inferred that a dedicated focused-manifest generator existed, but no matching script was present.
entries.rootCause: The focused-manifest creation mechanism was inferred from the artifact name instead of being recovered from its actual format and prior orchestration evidence.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Inspect only the existing focused manifest's bounded format and the recorded cycle summary fields, then reuse the exact authoritative file list to generate a fresh current hash inventory without inventing a generator path.

entries.mistake: The first FIX1 cycle-1 authoritative 60-file Flutter run used a 120-second shell timeout and was terminated before the suite could report an authoritative result.
entries.rootCause: The command timeout was sized like a focused test even though the known 60-file regression suite requires a long-running budget.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Verify no orphan Flutter process remains, use a long bounded command timeout, keep user-visible progress through no-longer-than-60-second waits, and restart cycle 1 from immutable-manifest comparison; never count the timed-out attempt.

entries.mistake: Cycle-1 command discovery successfully read backend scripts but then inferred apps/hosting/package.json, which does not exist, and the shell continued because the discovery command did not set stop-on-error behavior.
entries.rootCause: The Hosting workspace path was inferred from product naming instead of discovered from repository package manifests, and mixed discovery steps lacked ErrorActionPreference Stop.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Discover the exact Hosting package.json with a bounded file list, inspect only its scripts property, set ErrorActionPreference Stop for multi-step discovery, and do not count this command as a cycle gate.

entries.mistake: Cycle 1 found that the preserved C30X preflight-order gate rejects the retargeted r60.49 launcher because it requires the historical sourceReleaseControlsPassed literal even though C33F proves the exact two-cycle source facts directly before prompts.
entries.rootCause: The launcher evolved from the historical C30X state contract to the exact C33F source-cycle contract, but the preserved compatibility gate retained only the old source-proof spelling.
entries.prevention: Register and implement UAW-C33F-FIX2 before retry. Preserve the ban on downstream releasePreflightPassed in the launcher, accept only the exact historical sourceReleaseControlsPassed proof or the exact current completedIdenticalCycles/whole-analyzer proof, run the gate on both PowerShell hosts, reseal source and restart both full cycles.

entries.mistake: The first combined FIX2 patch was rejected because an inferred MVP scope approvalState context did not match the exact current file, so no part of the patch was applied.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-file patch reused a remembered state string instead of reading the exact current named scalar and local preparationFixTickets context immediately before mutation.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Confirm that the failed patch applied no files, discover the exact current scalar values and bounded local array context, then use smaller scoped patches and verify each JSON/script immediately.

entries.mistake: Play Console navigation attempted to call scrollIntoViewIfNeeded directly on the browser-client locator, but that locator surface does not expose the method.
entries.rootCause: A Playwright locator convenience method was assumed to be directly forwarded by the browser-client locator API without checking the already loaded browser contract.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the supported locator evaluate action to call the DOM element's scrollIntoView method, then continue navigation without reading or reproducing signing fingerprints, identifiers or credential-adjacent values.

entries.mistake: After locating the Play Store protection Show details button inside an evaluated DOM subtree, the navigation attempted to invoke button.click inside the evaluation surface, where click was not callable.
entries.rootCause: The DOM evaluation surface was used for interaction after it had served only for structural discovery, instead of returning to the browser-client locator action surface.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the browser-client getByRole button locator with exact accessible name Show details, disambiguate by the visible Play Store protection row if required, and do not invoke evaluated DOM methods for interaction.

entries.mistake: The first secure comparison attempt reused the prior Play Console tab binding after browser cleanup had removed that tab; only the newly opened Firebase tab remained.
entries.rootCause: A persistent browser binding was correctly reused, but its earlier tab binding was assumed to remain live across the user turn without an immediate tab-presence check.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Discard the stale Play tab, create a fresh Play Console tab from the existing browser binding, navigate directly to the already established MoolSocial app-signing page, and compare scoped SHA-1 values only in transient block variables with boolean-only output.

entries.mistake: The Play SHA-1 row-context audit attempted to call compareDocumentPosition on evaluated DOM proxies, where that method was not callable.
entries.rootCause: A native DOM position method was assumed to survive the browser-client evaluation proxy boundary after earlier evidence showed native evaluated methods may be unavailable.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the locator's stable document-order indices together with the visible App signing key, Previous app signing keys and Upload key certificate heading order; scope the first SHA-1 label to the first App signing key section and keep value comparison transient with boolean-only output.

entries.mistake: The bounded readiness-state context read attempted to call Prepend on a PowerShell string array, but that method was unavailable on the returned object.
entries.rootCause: A LINQ-style array helper was assumed instead of emitting the match line and bounded PostContext explicitly.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Emit the matched line and each bounded context line as separate output items, or patch the already known exact scalar without another projection; never retry the unsupported method.

entries.mistake: The first combined mismatch-registration patch was rejected because the readiness fact is stored in a different exact JSON layout than the inferred multi-line context, so no part of the patch applied.
entries.rootCause: A parsed fact projection was used to infer physical JSON formatting in a large multi-file patch instead of discovering the exact current scalar line before mutation.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Add the finding, ticket and sanitized evidence independently, discover the exact current readiness status line with fixed-string search, then apply a small scoped state patch and verify every JSON owner.

entries.mistake: The existing Firebase Android app SHA-1 does not match the Google Play App signing key SHA-1 for the Play-installed package, so Play-delivered Google sign-in cannot rely on the required Android certificate relationship.
entries.rootCause: Firebase currently records a different Android certificate relationship than the Google-held app-signing certificate used for Play-delivered installs.
entries.prevention: Keep the r60.49 build gate closed. Under a separate exact provider-mutation approval, add the Play App signing key SHA-1 to the existing Firebase Android app for com.moolsocial.app, preserve all existing fingerprints, then re-verify the Firebase/Play match and the Android OAuth package/Play-signer relationship with sanitized evidence before any AAB authority can become available.

entries.mistake: The first FIX3 authorization record wrote a rounded receivedAtUtc value without reading an authoritative clock at the time of persistence.
entries.rootCause: The user approval was exact, but its timestamp was inferred for convenience instead of distinguishing approval receipt from the later exact repository recording time.
entries.prevention: Register before correction. Replace receivedAtUtc with an exact recordedAtUtc obtained from the system clock, preserve the verbatim authorized action, and never infer approval timestamps.

entries.mistake: The authorized Firebase repair attempted to reuse tab 6 after browser-session cleanup had removed it.
entries.rootCause: The Firebase tab binding was not revalidated immediately before the approval-dependent mutation workflow.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Discard the stale Firebase tab, create a fresh Firebase tab from the existing browser binding, verify the exact project/package page using headings only, then perform only the authorized fingerprint addition.

entries.mistake: The first read of the newly opened Play app-signing page found neither the App signing key heading nor any SHA-1 value after only the initial DOM-content-loaded wait.
entries.rootCause: The authenticated Play Console route had not yet exposed its application controls at the first bounded readiness check; its exact current tab state was not inspected before attempting locators.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Inspect only the claimed tab title, URL and safe page headings, then either wait for the existing route to settle or request founder authentication if Play presents a login/interstitial; do not reopen tabs or emit certificate values.

entries.mistake: The Play Console tab creation passed an object containing url, but the Chrome tabs API created an about:blank tab instead of navigating to the requested route.
entries.rootCause: The in-app Browser tab-construction signature was incorrectly carried over to the Chrome tabs API without verifying its documented string URL argument.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the Chrome skill's documented string URL argument, verify the same claimed tab's title and exact allowed-domain URL before reading signing controls, and never infer cross-plugin method signatures.

entries.mistake: A second Chrome tab-creation attempt using the documented string URL argument also returned an about:blank tab with no title or headings.
entries.rootCause: This connected Chrome control surface is usable for claimed user tabs but did not navigate newly constructed tabs in the current session.
entries.prevention: Register before changing approach. Stop creating Chrome tabs; reuse the already authenticated in-app Play Console binding for a transient public-certificate read, while retaining the claimed Chrome Firebase tab solely for the founder-authorized additive mutation.

entries.mistake: The single founder-authorized Firebase fingerprint Save returned a generic processing-error dialog instead of a success acknowledgement.
entries.rootCause: The Firebase console did not expose a specific failure cause in the authenticated additive form response, so the provider commit state is not yet proven.
entries.prevention: Register before any retry. Perform a value-free backend-state comparison against the transient Play app-signing SHA-1; if it matches, treat the write as committed and do not retry. If absent, diagnose the authenticated provider request without exposing identifiers, then use at most one controlled additive retry that preserves all existing fingerprints.

entries.mistake: The one controlled retry from a freshly reopened Firebase fingerprint form validated the value as SHA-1 but again returned the same generic processing error and did not expose the new match.
entries.rootCause: The repeated provider response proves this is not a single stale-dialog condition; the underlying Firebase relationship or provider request is rejecting the additive write without a specific console explanation.
entries.prevention: Register before further diagnosis. Stop all Firebase UI writes, keep the release gate closed, and use only a captured read-only Firebase CLI SHA-state query whose output is parsed in memory and never emitted. Do not retry mutation until the exact provider conflict is identified or a method-equivalent, exact-action CLI repair is proven safe.

entries.mistake: The first captured read-only Firebase Android SHA-list CLI query exited with code 2 and returned no parsed certificate rows.
entries.rootCause: The exact CLI rejection category has not yet been classified; it may be a command-version, option, authentication, or application-resolution issue.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Read only a fingerprint-, app-ID-, token-, URL- and credential-redacted error category from the captured process failure, verify the installed CLI command help if needed, and never emit raw stdout/stderr or use firebase login:list --json.

entries.mistake: The first combined preservation patch inferred wording in the older C33E quality document, so apply_patch rejected the entire change because the expected anchor was not exact.
entries.rootCause: The registry anchor was read exactly, but the older quality-document sentence was reconstructed from memory instead of read before composing a multi-file patch.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Verify atomic rejection, read each target's exact current anchor, then split the transient-pointer migration, historical-document amendment and new evidence-loss record into independently verifiable patches.

entries.mistake: The founder-authorized interactive Firebase reauthentication was launched with the production repository as its working directory, and the successful CLI lifecycle removed the pre-existing untracked root firebase-debug.log referenced by regression 2341.
entries.rootCause: An interactive CLI success path was assumed not to affect its prior transient root debug artifact; the reauthentication process was not isolated in a temporary working directory outside the repository.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Preserve the durable sanitized 2341 quality record, remove only the now-invalid transient evidence pointer, never recreate or inspect the deleted log, and launch all future interactive Firebase authentication from a dedicated temporary directory outside the production repository while keeping the repository unchanged.

entries.mistake: The post-reauthentication Firebase SHA-list command exited zero, but the first parser recognized only colon-delimited certificate values and therefore reported zero rows despite known existing Firebase fingerprints.
entries.rootCause: The parser assumed the CLI rendered certificate hashes in the same colon-delimited format as the consoles instead of first reading the CLI's current output schema.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Redact all 40/64-hex, colon-delimited certificate, app-ID, OAuth-ID, API-key, token, email and URL values before inspecting labels; then parse only the confirmed hash field shape and emit boolean/count results.

entries.mistake: The first sanitized Firebase SHA-list schema output redacted certificate hashes and protected credential shapes but left the table's fixed-width SHA Id resource identifiers visible.
entries.rootCause: The sanitizer covered certificate values, application IDs, OAuth IDs, API keys, tokens, accounts and URLs but did not include the CLI-specific 16-hex SHA Id column discovered only after rendering the current schema.
entries.prevention: Register before parsing. Never emit this captured schema again; future Firebase SHA-list sanitization must redact the SHA Id column or every standalone 16-hex provider resource identifier before any bounded output.

entries.mistake: Firebase Console returned the same generic processing-error dialog and its stale page showed no match after the authorized additive Save flow, but the post-reauthentication authoritative Firebase CLI inventory proves the Play app-signing SHA-1 is present.
entries.rootCause: The console acknowledgement and page DOM did not reflect the committed backend certificate state, so a value-free page-text comparison produced a false-negative result.
entries.prevention: After any ambiguous provider acknowledgement, stop writes and query authoritative provider state before retry. A backend match ends the mutation path immediately; never issue a duplicate add because a stale console page still reports failure.

entries.mistake: The first 2399 registry patch referenced the sanitized qualified-evidence JSON one step before that file had been created.
entries.rootCause: The finding registration and provider-fact evidence creation were split in the wrong order even though the regression-memory contract requires every current evidence path to exist immediately.
entries.prevention: Register before running any gate. Create the sanitized qualified evidence in the same corrective patch, validate its JSON, then compute and bind its hash before replaying readiness gates.

entries.mistake: The first 2-of-4 build-gate wrapper correctly received a nonzero rejection but its ad hoc message regex did not match the gate's actual bounded wording, so the wrapper failed before reporting state equality.
entries.rootCause: The expected-rejection classifier guessed generic live-readiness words instead of first binding the C33F gate's current fail-closed reason string.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Snapshot exact state/aggregate/readiness hashes and action counts, capture only the bounded first rejection line, require nonzero plus the gate's actual 2-of-4 reason, then require byte-identical state on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: The post-provider source-manifest equality check was unnecessarily invoked on Windows PowerShell 5.1, where the C30V owner cannot call the .NET SHA256.HashData API.
entries.rootCause: Dual-host readiness-gate requirements were incorrectly generalized to the source-manifest generator even though its qualified execution owner is PowerShell 7.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Run C30V ComparePath only on PowerShell 7, retain the already-passed separate dual-host C33E/C33F gates, and do not modify the sealed source owner under a provider-evidence ticket.

entries.mistake: The read-only OAuth relationship audit passed an object URL to the in-app browser new-tab method, which created an about:blank tab instead of navigating to Google Cloud credentials.
entries.rootCause: A URL-bearing constructor signature was assumed instead of using the already-created tab's direct navigation mechanism in this connected browser surface.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Reuse the same blank tab and navigate it directly to the exact allowed Google Cloud credentials URL; verify title, project and safe headings before reading only display names and application types.

entries.mistake: The retry attempted to assign location.href inside the in-app browser's evaluated page context, but that controlled location object exposes only a getter and rejected assignment.
entries.rootCause: A normal web-page navigation primitive was assumed to be writable inside the browser-control sandbox instead of using the app-supported browser URL opening action.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use the Codex app browser-target URL action to open the exact Google Cloud credentials route, then locate and bind only the resulting allowed-domain tab; do not attempt another evaluated location mutation.

entries.mistake: The post-open browser discovery attempted to access playwright on browser.tabs.get('8') without awaiting the tab-handle promise.
entries.rootCause: A previously bound tab ID was used as an ad hoc delay owner and the asynchronous get operation was not resolved before property access.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. List tabs directly without an unrelated wait handle, and await every tabs.get call before accessing its page-control surface.

entries.mistake: After the Codex browser URL action reported queued, the next direct tab-list retry found the previously persistent browser binding undefined.
entries.rootCause: The browser-control JavaScript session reset or disconnected between the queued app action and discovery, invalidating the assumed persistent binding.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Reinitialize the mandated browser runtime, select the browser for the exact Google Cloud credentials URL, read its complete documentation once, then discover only allowed-domain tabs without relying on old IDs or bindings.

entries.mistake: The first Android OAuth detail read used getAttribute('value') and reported false/empty results even though the correct Package name and SHA-1 labels were present.
entries.rootCause: Google Cloud's form controls expose their current data through live input properties rather than serialized value attributes.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Read only the labeled Package name and SHA-1 live properties into transient memory, emit only package-match and SHA-shape booleans, and never locate or read the OAuth Client ID field.

entries.mistake: After clicking the auto-created Web OAuth link, the audit assumed a detail form and used getByLabel('Name'), but the current page remained the credential list and the locator matched three unrelated table headers.
entries.rootCause: The click's destination was not verified before applying a generic detail-form locator, and the list page contains several Name-labelled tables.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Inspect the current tab title plus safe headings and current controlled-tab inventory, then either bind the newly opened detail tab or reselect the exact Web client link. On a verified detail page, use its unique Web-application heading before reading only the display-name field.

entries.mistake: The corrected Web-client click reused list-page readiness too late; Google Cloud re-rendered the credential table and the exact link locator had zero matches at click time.
entries.rootCause: The dynamic credential table was not explicitly awaited immediately before reacquiring and clicking the display-name link.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Wait for the OAuth 2.0 Client IDs heading and the exact auto-created Web display name to be visible in the same fresh locator cycle, then click once and verify the unique Web-application detail heading before any field read.

entries.mistake: After reloading the credentials page, the final bounded audit assumed OAuth 2.0 Client IDs remained exposed with heading semantics, but the semantic heading locator had no match and timed out.
entries.rootCause: The dynamic Google Cloud console changed or withheld the table's accessibility role after reload, so the prior visible text could not be safely reused as a heading contract.
entries.prevention: Register and stop this browser path. Preserve the independently proven Android package/Play-signer fact, keep the Web server-client/mobile relationship pending, and require a separate hidden-value-safe qualification workflow rather than broad DOM reads or weakened selectors.

entries.mistake: The fourth-fact readiness update changed the active C33F ticket lifecycle wording even though preserved C30Z/C33E gates bind that ticket byte-for-byte as a sealed selection manifest.
entries.rootCause: Mutable release-state progression was incorrectly mirrored into a sealed ticket before inventorying every literal ticket hash binding.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Restore the sealed C33F ticket and selected-ticket hash, retain 4/4 truth only in the dedicated readiness/state/aggregate and scoped status owners, verify the ticket hash, then replay regression memory and all release gates from the beginning.

entries.mistake: The r60.49 founder launcher validated all three hidden inputs, persisted hiddenFounderInputsEntered=true, and then called a wrapper whose first C33F build gate requires that flag to remain false until the one build boundary is consumed.
entries.rootCause: The static order contract covered gate and command positions inside each owner but omitted the cross-owner lifecycle invariant for the hidden-input marker between launcher validation, wrapper entry and authority consumption.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Keep the marker false through wrapper entry and the C33F build gate, set it only in the wrapper's existing post-preflight authority-consumption transaction, add exact static and behavioral transition coverage, reseal source, and complete two fresh full cycles before another founder prompt.

entries.mistake: REG-2412 listed the planned FIX4 behavioral test in its gates array before the test file existed, so regression memory correctly rejected the entry.
entries.rootCause: A future ticket deliverable was incorrectly represented as present machine-detectable prevention evidence at registration time.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Active regression entries reference only existing files; keep future gates in the selected ticket plan, create and pass them during implementation, and add them to a later status update only after existence is proven.

entries.mistake: A repeated gates-array patch hunk attached the new FIX4 test path to historical REG-2374 instead of active REG-2412.
entries.rootCause: The patch used a non-unique repeated field as its primary context rather than anchoring the edit to the exact regression identifier.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Every registry update hunk includes the unique REG identifier and is immediately verified by a bounded search of both the intended entry and any displaced path occurrence before running memory or release gates.

entries.mistake: A compound command attempted to read guessed scripts/check-c30v-single-aab-wrapper-contract.ps1 even though the immediately preceding bounded inventory did not return that path.
entries.rootCause: A remembered gate label was converted into a filename and left in the same compound command after literal discovery had already disproved it.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Cycle reconstruction uses only literal paths returned by rg --files; discovery is completed and inspected before a separate read, and the exact existing C30V owner is scripts/check-play-internal-aab-build-wrapper-c30v.ps1.

entries.mistake: The first cycle-1 analyzer command redirected to a repository-relative artifact path after Push-Location apps/mobile, so PowerShell rejected the nonexistent apps/mobile/artifacts path before starting Flutter.
entries.rootCause: The command separated tool working-directory ownership from neither evidence-path resolution nor failure-tail resolution.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Resolve every cycle log to an absolute repository-contained path before Push-Location, require the exact new path absent, run Flutter from apps/mobile, and read the same absolute path for failure or success evidence.

entries.mistake: An unchanged in-progress state, absent transient release files and a zero-byte buffered build log initially appeared consistent with an early build exit even though a Gradle worker outside the direct launcher descendant tree was actively compiling.
entries.rootCause: The initial liveness view was limited to the direct launcher process tree and file flush state; the active Gradle daemon worker was a separate long-lived Java process and the redirected log had not flushed.
entries.prevention: When single-build authority is consumed, never restart from state age, transient absence or log size alone. Inspect sanitized terminal state, artifact metadata, full Dart/Java process names and bounded CPU deltas; preserve the process until wrapper exit and register any terminal failure before new authority.

entries.mistake: After the one authorized wrapper wrote the truthful r60.49 success state and complete artifact provenance, its mandatory C33F postbuild gate rejected that state because the gate still required the prerelease founder-prompt state.
entries.rootCause: The C33F gate computed one readiness-derived machine state before branching on Phase, making the prerelease state universal across postbuild and later lifecycle phases.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Make machine-state expectations phase-aware, require the exact wrapper-produced success state for postbuild and preupload, add wrong-phase negative fixtures on both PowerShell hosts, and do not upload until the repaired postbuild and preupload gates pass.

entries.mistake: Read-only continuation proved that the C33F postbuild gate would next reject the wrapper's correct aggregate candidate build count of one because a universal prerelease assertion requires it to remain zero.
entries.rootCause: Prerelease zero-action invariants were placed before the phase branch, and the gate output reports a baseline actionCounts field instead of the authoritative buildResult counter.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Move candidate counter expectations into exact phase branches, require buildResult and aggregate build counts of one at postbuild/preupload, keep upload/install counts zero there, and report the authoritative result counters.

entries.mistake: The C33F gate declares four postbuild Play/install phases but supplies no dedicated positive state, count, authority or evidence contract for them; they fall through prerelease assertions.
entries.rootCause: The gate was extended with phase names and a postbuild block without completing the lifecycle state switch promised by the parent r60.49 ticket.
entries.prevention: Register before any Play action. Implement explicit Internal Testing upload/activation and in-place Play-update phase contracts with exact one-action counts, artifact binding, retained-data and cold-start evidence, forbidden-track and forbidden-ADB mutations, plus dual-host positive and negative fixtures.

entries.mistake: The successful r60.49 wrapper advanced buildResult.buildCount and aggregate.candidate.buildCount to one but left state.actionCounts.build at zero, and the gate printed the stale mirror as the build count.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper authority-consumption transaction updated only two of three declared count owners, while the release gate neither enforced mirror equality nor reported the authoritative result counter.
entries.prevention: Register before correction. Advance all declared build-count mirrors atomically, correct the current mutable state only from preserved wrapper/provenance evidence, require exact mirror equality in phase fixtures, and report buildResult/playResult/installResult counters.

entries.mistake: The resolved REG-2420 gates array spelled the C33F successor gate filename with successOR instead of the exact lowercase successor path.
entries.rootCause: A long inline registry patch retyped an existing path instead of copying the literal path returned by repository inventory and validating it before insertion.
entries.prevention: Register before correction. Copy gate paths only from rg --files output, verify exact ordinal spelling and Test-Path existence for every newly added gates entry, then run regression memory.

entries.mistake: After the live upload authority advanced to available_once, the embedded FIX5 suite cloned that live value into its synthetic postbuild fixture, whose exact authority must remain held_postbuild_qualification.
entries.rootCause: The postbuild fixture treated the current mutable lifecycle state as a stable template instead of explicitly assigning every phase-owned authority and counter like the other synthetic phases.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Explicitly normalize the complete postbuild synthetic state, statically bind its phase-owned assignments, replay the dedicated suite and full preupload gate on both PowerShell hosts, and perform no external action until all pass.

entries.mistake: The first FIX6 main-gate patch placed dollar-prefixed PowerShell source needles in double-quoted strings, which would interpolate variables instead of searching exact literal source text.
entries.rootCause: Runtime message-string syntax was reused for source-code contract needles without applying PowerShell interpolation rules under strict mode.
entries.prevention: Register before correction. Use single-quoted literals or explicit dollar escaping for every PowerShell source needle, review interpolation semantics before executing the parser or gate, and retain bounded exact-source assertions.

entries.mistake: The first FIX6 parser batch embedded comma-separated Join-Path invocations directly in an array and PowerShell concatenated both intended targets into one invalid path.
entries.rootCause: Command invocation syntax was used where already-resolved scalar array elements were required.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Resolve each path into a scalar variable, verify every target with Test-Path -PathType Leaf, then create the parser input array from those scalars.

entries.mistake: The first final Internal Testing confirmation scoped through an exact dialog name that omitted Play Console's descendant Close text, so no dialog or confirmation button matched and no publish action executed.
entries.rootCause: The locator assumed the heading text was the complete accessible dialog name instead of reacquiring the modal's rendered accessible name after it opened.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Reacquire a fresh modal DOM snapshot, require exactly one visible active Save and publish confirmation in the modal state, click once, and verify the Internal Testing page and exact version before updating release state.

entries.mistake: The first r60.49 OPPO cold-start diagnostic assigned the Android app process ID to PowerShell's read-only automatic PID variable, making its processRunning boolean invalid.
entries.rootCause: A short generic variable name collided case-insensitively with a PowerShell automatic variable, and the command did not enable Stop semantics for write errors.
entries.prevention: Register before retry. Use an explicit moolSocialAppPid variable, set ErrorActionPreference to Stop, suppress launcher diagnostic streams, and require independent process, focus and interactive-hierarchy agreement before sealing evidence.

entries.mistake: The Play-installed r60.49 candidate still returns from Google account selection without completing sign-in and shows an error, despite being built as the Google-auth successor.
entries.rootCause: The exact runtime cause is not yet established. The release qualification proved source contracts and sanitized configuration readiness but did not prove a successful real-account credential exchange and Firebase session on the installed Play artifact before upload.
entries.prevention: Block every future AAB until the exact Google account-selection return, Firebase authenticated session, retained relaunch and sanitized failure/retry paths pass on a release-equivalent artifact; source-only mocks and provider-readiness facts cannot satisfy this journey.

entries.mistake: Tapping Social Create on the Play-installed r60.49 candidate crashes the application.
entries.rootCause: The exact crash site is not yet established. The qualifying suite did not exercise the signed-out retained-data Create tap through the release-mode navigation and process-liveness boundary used by the installed Play artifact.
entries.prevention: Require a focused signed-out and authenticated Create tap matrix, process survival, destination semantics, Android exit-reason checks and two affected regressions before a future AAB can be authorized.

entries.mistake: Signed-out Social Feed entry on r60.49 redirects to login instead of preserving the approved public guest-feed read journey.
entries.rootCause: The exact routing branch is not yet established. Existing source checks did not prove the real shell-to-Feed tap with retained device state on the installed Play build.
entries.prevention: Add a fail-closed release prerequisite for the exact signed-out Main-to-Social-to-Feed journey, asserting public-feed ownership and absence of login routing while protected Feed mutations continue to request authentication.

entries.mistake: The visible social-media identity choices on r60.49 do not produce a usable supported sign-in outcome, leaving the real user with repeated errors.
