entries.rootCause: The exact behavior per visible method is not yet reconciled. The release did not prove that supported Google sign-in succeeds while unintegrated providers are non-interactive or truthfully identified without launching a misleading account-selection flow.
entries.prevention: Inventory every visible authentication method on the installed journey, keep only truly supported methods actionable, require truthful non-operational treatment for unintegrated providers, and gate copy, semantics and navigation per method before release.

entries.mistake: r60.49 was built, uploaded and installed even though the predecessor acceptance defects had not been closed by real-device journey evidence; source-only checks and a narrow cold-start pass allowed the same customer blockers to escape again.
entries.rootCause: The successor gate referenced prior repair tickets and source cycles but had no machine-readable unresolved-defect carry-forward matrix requiring every founder-reported blocker to be resolved by an exact test and release-equivalent journey before AAB authority consumption.
entries.prevention: Create a durable acceptance-blocker ledger keyed by regression and ticket, reject candidate selection and AAB authority while any applicable blocker is unresolved or lacks focused plus device evidence, and never let cold-start-only evidence satisfy complete journey acceptance.

entries.mistake: The first sanitized OPPO hierarchy reader passed Android's XML plus its trailing dump-status line to XmlDocument, causing a metadata parse failure and printing the app-owned hierarchy in the command error.
entries.rootCause: The reader searched only for the XML start marker and assumed the remainder of `/dev/tty` was valid XML instead of bounding the payload at the closing hierarchy tag.
entries.prevention: Before retry, extract exactly one payload from the XML declaration through `</hierarchy>`, fail on missing or multiple boundaries, restrict parsed nodes to the MoolSocial package and redact identifier-like text before any output.

entries.mistake: A context-light evidence patch updated the first repeated pending-status value, falsely marking the Feed defect confirmed instead of the Google sign-in defect.
entries.rootCause: The patch hunk targeted a non-unique repeated JSON value without including the stable defect ID and journey fields in its match context.
entries.prevention: Every repeated-field evidence patch must include the immutable record ID and adjacent semantic field, then immediately verify an ID/status projection before any dependent action.

entries.mistake: The first ID-bound correction attempt omitted the registry Update File header, so apply_patch searched for a registry record in the evidence JSON and rejected the entire patch.
entries.rootCause: Two target-file hunks were composed as one file section instead of giving each target an explicit patch header.
entries.prevention: Use one explicit Add or Update File section per target, verify context belongs to that target before execution, and confirm that a rejected patch changed no intended file before retry.

entries.mistake: A related-evidence rg command supplied Windows wildcard strings as input paths, so rg rejected them as invalid literal paths and the composite read-only diagnostic exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: Shell-glob assumptions from another platform were used instead of rg directory roots plus its own -g file filters.
entries.prevention: On Windows, pass verified directory roots to rg and express filename selection with -g; treat any nonzero composite command as failed even when preceding sections printed valid output.

entries.mistake: The first C33G FIX1 selection assessment used thin_adapter, which the MVP delivery machine gate rejected before source mutation.
entries.rootCause: The human checkpoint's thin-adapter wording was shortened instead of copying the machine gate's exact allowed thin_policy_adapter enumeration value.
entries.prevention: Copy implementation-disposition values from the live machine allowlist, validate the selected ticket through the MVP gate before any product edit, and refresh the ticket hash after correcting a ticket field.

entries.mistake: A launcher-owner rg search included the nonexistent scripts/templates directory, causing a nonzero composite diagnostic after valid matches from other targets.
entries.rootCause: The search path was assumed from a generic repository layout instead of copied from the current file inventory or verified with Test-Path.
entries.prevention: Use only paths returned by rg --files or verified by Test-Path, and never classify partial output from a nonzero composite command as a passing inventory.

entries.mistake: Pre-execution review found a double-quoted PowerShell source needle containing the Dart ${_socialProviderLabel(provider)} expression, which PowerShell would interpolate instead of matching literally.
entries.rootCause: A Dart source fragment with a dollar-prefixed interpolation expression was placed in a PowerShell interpolating string despite the existing literal-needle regression rule.
entries.prevention: Use single-quoted literal strings or single-quoted regular expressions for every cross-language dollar-prefixed source needle, and review those semantics before the first parser or gate run.

entries.mistake: A read-only C33G inventory requested two stale gate filenames and two nonexistent source directories, so the composite diagnostic returned partial output and exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: Paths were inferred from generic names instead of copied from the current repository inventory, repeating the path-resolution class already captured by REG-2438.
entries.prevention: Resolve every non-ticket path from the current scripts or mobile-lib file inventory, verify every explicit path with Test-Path, and reject all partial output from a nonzero composite command.

entries.mistake: A composite read-only inventory combined broad file enumeration, repository documentation search and source reads and exceeded its execution timeout before producing usable output.
entries.rootCause: Independent diagnostic questions were combined under one timeout instead of using explicit file targets and bounded single-purpose searches.
entries.prevention: Use one bounded diagnostic purpose per command, prefer explicit files and top-level directories already proven to exist, and register a timeout before retrying with narrower scope.

entries.mistake: Pre-execution review found the new C33G FIX2 gate had a double-quoted PowerShell needle containing the Dart ${provider.name} interpolation expression.
entries.rootCause: The existing REG-2439 prevention was not applied while composing a second cross-language provider-key needle.
entries.prevention: All Dart source needles containing a dollar sign must use PowerShell single-quoted literals with doubled embedded apostrophes, and every new gate must be searched for double-quoted dollar expressions before its first run.

entries.mistake: Pre-execution review found the C33G FIX2 shared-provider assertion used two exact strings whose newline representations did not robustly cover repository CRLF and LF materialization.
entries.rootCause: A multiline Dart relationship was modeled with hand-authored newline strings instead of the repository's established whitespace-tolerant static-contract pattern.
entries.prevention: Use a single-quoted whitespace-tolerant regex for multiline source relationships and validate the gate on PowerShell 7 plus Windows PowerShell before accepting evidence.

entries.mistake: Pre-execution review found the C33G FIX3 cancel-origin regex was double-quoted while containing the Dart ${_tab.name} expression.
entries.rootCause: The cross-language literal-dollar prevention from REG-2439 and REG-2442 was not applied while composing the second ticket gate.
entries.prevention: Represent every Dart interpolation fragment as a PowerShell single-quoted literal or literal regex with doubled embedded apostrophes, and scan each new gate before first execution.

entries.mistake: The first C33G FIX3 gate run falsely rejected the two valid Create cancellation-origin owners because the hand-written regular expression did not match the Dart interpolation literal.
entries.rootCause: Regex metacharacters in a fixed cross-language source fragment were escaped manually instead of passing the exact single-quoted needle through Regex.Escape.
entries.prevention: For an exact fixed source count, define one PowerShell single-quoted literal, use Regex.Escape programmatically, assert the expected count, and reserve handwritten regex for relationships that truly need flexible whitespace.

entries.mistake: The second C33G FIX3 gate run repeated the cancellation-origin rejection after a matcher rewrite because the corrected needle count was not independently projected before retry.
entries.rootCause: The correction was reasoned from displayed source context but was not validated with a single-purpose exact count against the raw source before re-running the complete gate.
entries.prevention: After any matcher failure, independently print the sanitized needle length and exact raw-source occurrence count, prove the expected projection, and only then retry the full gate.

entries.mistake: The FIX3 gate expected two global occurrences of the Social cancellation-origin fragment, but a third legitimate occurrence belongs to the message-author authentication path.
entries.rootCause: A shared source fragment was counted across the entire consumer instead of within the two Create ownership methods named by the ticket.
entries.prevention: Static checks for repeated shared fragments must first inventory every occurrence, then assert within explicit method boundaries so unrelated valid owners cannot cause false rejection or satisfy the wrong contract.

entries.mistake: The first FIX3 widget matrix expected a Social home-origin Create cancellation route of sub=home, but the existing Social home surface canonically owns the Videos tab and returned sub=videos.
entries.rootCause: The test inferred the cancellation route from the constructor input instead of projecting the consumer's canonical active tab after initialization.
entries.prevention: For stateful tab surfaces, assert cancellation against the canonical active tab exposed by the accepted implementation and existing navigation tests, not an unnormalized input alias.

entries.mistake: The first FIX3 restart test assumed a bare beginSignIn plus one microtask would persist the shared-post pending intent, but the reconstructed session resumed ready.
entries.rootCause: The new test copied a timing pattern without first verifying which JourneySession method owns durable pending-route persistence for this exact guest Create intent.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact JourneySession persistence owner, use its deterministic completion contract in tests, and prove the stored snapshot projection before reconstructing the session.

entries.mistake: A persistence-coverage diagnostic passed an unsupported -Recurse parameter to Select-String, causing the composite command to exit nonzero after valid explicit-file output.
entries.rootCause: Recursive-search syntax from another command was assumed instead of using rg or piping an explicit file inventory into Select-String.
entries.prevention: Use rg for recursive text search, or use Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File piped to Select-String; never pass -Recurse directly to Select-String and never treat partial composite output as a pass.

entries.mistake: A signed-out production session with a persisted protected Create, Feed action or Chat intent could restart in guest-ready state instead of resuming sign-in and preserving its exact cancellation origin.
entries.rootCause: JourneySession startup special-cased only the YouTube connection path, while JourneySnapshot persisted only the return route and not the exact authentication cancel route or purpose.
entries.prevention: Persist the bounded local cancel route and authentication purpose with each pending intent, classify exact authentication-required routes at startup, resume only those routes in sign-in, and gate public Feed plus cancel/retry/success restart behavior.

entries.mistake: A combined FIX3 correction patch used the pre-format test loop layout, so apply_patch rejected the patch when the formatted source no longer matched the expected context.
entries.rootCause: The target file was formatted after initial composition, but the next patch was built from the earlier layout instead of re-reading the current formatted section.
entries.prevention: After any formatter changes a target, re-read the exact current section before patching and separate unrelated target-file corrections into explicit file sections with independently verified context.

entries.mistake: The C33G FIX4 continuation attempted to read scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate.ps1, which does not exist; the canonical repository owner is scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate-state.ps1.
entries.rootCause: The gate filename was recalled from a generic label instead of being resolved from the repository file inventory before invocation.
entries.prevention: Resolve every gate path with rg --files before first use after an interrupted continuation, then invoke only the exact repository-owned path and keep the resolved path in the ticket evidence.

entries.mistake: The first FIX4 qualification patch targeted an expanded multi-line representation of REG-2432 gates and evidence, while the current registry stores those arrays on compact single lines, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch.
entries.rootCause: The patch was built from parsed JSON output instead of the exact current serialized file context.
entries.prevention: Before patching a registry entry, read the exact serialized lines from the current file and target that representation; confirm the rejected atomic patch changed no ticket or evidence file before retrying.

entries.mistake: The first C33G FIX4 release-ready mode required future Play-installed OPPO evidence before allowing the AAB that must exist and be uploaded to produce that evidence, creating an impossible circular dependency.
entries.rootCause: Prebuild source qualification and post-install device acceptance were collapsed into one boolean release-ready phase instead of being modeled as ordered, separately fail-closed lifecycle phases.
entries.prevention: Use explicit prebuild and postinstall phases: prebuild requires every blocker to have an exact ticket plus passed source gate, tests and qualification with device acceptance pending; postinstall requires the exact newer candidate's retained Play-installed OPPO evidence and resolved-complete state. Never allow final acceptance or reviewer-ready claims from prebuild evidence.

entries.mistake: An authentication inventory command passed apps/mobile/test/*auth* as a positional Windows path to rg, producing an invalid filename error after otherwise valid results.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style wildcard was used as a Windows path instead of an rg --glob filter or a repository directory plus regex.
entries.prevention: On Windows, pass repository directories as positional paths and express file selection with rg --glob; treat any diagnostic stderr as a failed composite even when a downstream pipeline masks the exit code.

entries.mistake: After Firebase Phone Auth accepted an automatic or manual credential, a subsequent MoolSocial account-bootstrap failure could return a visible verification error while leaving the Firebase user signed in.
entries.rootCause: The Social authentication path explicitly rolled back partial provider authentication around _completeAuthentication, but the Phone OTP automatic and manual completion paths called _completeAuthentication without an equivalent OtpGateway sign-out rollback.
entries.prevention: Wrap both automatic and manual Phone OTP account completion with a bounded OTP rollback, prove Firebase sign-out on bootstrap failure, retain the protected return intent, and require independent Phone OTP regression coverage before enabling the live runtime flag.

entries.mistake: After toggling the Firebase Phone provider switch, the same composite browser action attempted to open the test-number expansion panel using a click point invalidated by the resulting layout update.
entries.rootCause: Two UI mutations were chained without collecting a fresh DOM state after the provider switch changed the dialog layout.
entries.prevention: After every Firebase console switch or expansion mutation, read a fresh DOM snapshot and current checked state before the next click; never reuse a locator action point across a dynamic panel update.

entries.mistake: A read-only Firebase dialog inspection called ariaSnapshot on the browser skill locator wrapper, which does not expose that Playwright helper.
entries.rootCause: A standard Playwright locator API was assumed to be available through the browser skill's constrained locator wrapper without checking the documented supported surface.
entries.prevention: Use the browser tab's supported playwright.domSnapshot method after every dynamic Firebase action, and use semantic locators only for supported click and form operations; never infer unsupported locator helpers.

entries.mistake: After adding the fictional Phone Auth test row, the first Save attempt used a click point invalidated by the row-driven dialog layout change, and the in-app browser rejected the action.
entries.rootCause: The Save locator was resolved against the post-entry layout without a browser action boundary that refreshed its translated click point after the table row was inserted.
entries.prevention: After adding or deleting any Firebase inline table row, collect a fresh DOM snapshot and reacquire the visible enabled Save control in a later browser action before clicking it; verify the provider table afterward.

entries.mistake: The Firebase Phone provider Save click reproduced the same in-app-browser mouse translation failure even after a fresh DOM snapshot and newly acquired visible enabled locator.
entries.rootCause: The failure is not merely a stale semantic locator: the in-app browser's translated mouse point remains detached from the rendered dialog position for this control after the inline table expands.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the same mouse action. Use a supported keyboard submit on the semantically located enabled Save control or a viewport-safe browser operation, then verify the provider table before declaring success.

entries.mistake: Pressing Enter through the semantically located Firebase Save button returned without error but did not submit the dialog; the provider table remained Phone Disabled.
entries.rootCause: The locator press operation did not establish an activation state that dispatched the button's submit behavior in this in-app browser dialog.
entries.prevention: Never treat a no-error input action as an external-service success. Verify the authoritative provider table and dialog closure; when mouse translation and locator press are ineffective, use the enabled button element's DOM click through the supported locator evaluate operation and re-verify.

entries.mistake: The attempted Firebase Save fallback called el.click inside the browser locator evaluate operation, but this constrained wrapper did not provide a native DOM element and rejected the call.
entries.rootCause: The supported evaluate method was assumed to share standard Playwright's native element-handle callback contract without verifying the wrapper's actual behavior.
entries.prevention: Do not use locator evaluate as a DOM-click substitute in this browser surface. Inspect the already initialized tab and locator method surface, use only a demonstrably supported input or viewport operation, and retain provider-table verification as the success authority.

entries.mistake: Browser recovery used rg against the installed plugin scripts directory outside C:\GUARANTEED OUTCOME after the required skill and browser documentation had already been loaded.
entries.rootCause: A troubleshooting attempt treated a referenced runtime implementation as repository diagnostic scope instead of respecting the explicit workspace boundary and the already-loaded public browser surface.
entries.prevention: Do not scan, inspect or mutate plugin implementation directories during MoolSocial work. Use only the loaded browser API and files inside the authorized workspace; if those cannot complete the action, report or request the smallest user interaction.

entries.mistake: Dispatching Space to the enabled Firebase Save button also returned without error but did not submit; authoritative verification continued to show Phone Disabled with the dialog open.
entries.rootCause: Keyboard dispatch through the in-app browser locator does not activate this dynamic Material dialog submit control, just as Enter did not.
entries.prevention: Stop automated retries on this control after authoritative verification. Preserve the staged values and request exactly one founder click on the visible Save button; resume only after re-reading the provider table.

entries.mistake: The first affected-auth-test inventory filtered rg --files output with a forward-slash-only directory expression, producing a false zero on Windows backslash paths.
entries.rootCause: The output path separator was not normalized and the regex unnecessarily depended on a directory separator although only exact filenames were needed.
entries.prevention: For Windows test inventory, filter on exact basenames or a [\\/] separator-neutral expression, declare zero-match semantics and require at least one exact current file before running tests.

entries.mistake: The first Phone OTP ledger wording could be read to require Play Integrity or reCAPTCHA return qualification before building the candidate that must be Play-installed to produce that evidence.
entries.rootCause: Prebuild-configurable provider prerequisites and post-install candidate-specific Android app-verification evidence were grouped under one broad live-provider label.
entries.prevention: Prebuild may require only Phone provider and SMS-region-policy prerequisites plus source qualification. Once those pass, use candidate-device-pending status; Play Integrity/reCAPTCHA return and OPPO send/verify remain mandatory post-install evidence and can never be required to create the candidate.

entries.mistake: The first required-UI-document size inventory placed a statement-form PowerShell foreach directly before a pipeline and failed parsing with an empty pipe element.
entries.rootCause: The command repeated the already registered PowerShell rule that statement-form loop output must be assigned or wrapped before piping.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell document inventory assigns foreach output to an explicit ticket-named array, then pipes that array for formatting; never place a bare foreach statement directly before a pipe.

entries.mistake: A 605-line design-memory read exceeded the available output/context budget and was truncated before complete review could be established.
entries.rootCause: The read was bounded by a large line count without also accounting for byte and token density.
entries.prevention: Read large required documents in independently verified chunks of no more than 200 lines, reduce further for dense sections, and require each requested range to return without truncation before advancing.

entries.mistake: A resumed read guessed APPLE-HUMAN-INTERFACE-GUIDELINES-MEMORY.md although the repository owner is APPLE-INSPIRED-PRODUCT-DESIGN-MEMORY.md.
entries.rootCause: A summarized descriptive name was treated as a literal repository path instead of re-resolving the exact current owner.
entries.prevention: Resolve every retained documentation owner with a bounded rg --files inventory and use only the returned literal path before a resumed read.

entries.mistake: A combined command printed the complete MVP state, multiple recent ticket manifests and broad handoff search results, exceeding the output budget and truncating the evidence.
entries.rootCause: Several individually bounded questions were aggregated without a total output cap, so one large state owner consumed the shared output budget.
entries.prevention: Read one exact state or ticket owner per command; for handoff refreshes use narrowly targeted match ranges with an explicit small maximum and then read only the required line windows.

entries.mistake: Browser tool discovery printed complete matching tool descriptions, causing a large truncated result instead of a bounded callable-name inventory.
entries.rootCause: The discovery projection returned full metadata objects when only exact tool names were required.
entries.prevention: Tool discovery maps bounded matches to exact names only; read a single selected description/schema afterward if needed and never print the full matching metadata collection.

entries.mistake: The first in-app browser runtime attempt used a bare Playwright dynamic import that failed because the available module entrypoint requested an unavailable default export.
entries.rootCause: The browser connection surface was assumed from a generic Node REPL example instead of being confirmed from the currently callable plugin tools.
entries.prevention: Do not retry a blind Playwright bare import. Inventory exact callable browser surfaces by name; if no valid in-app browser control surface is exposed, use repository-contained static/render verification and open the finished page through the Codex browser panel without claiming automated interaction evidence.

entries.mistake: The first successful Screen 03 rendered audit allowed ThreadingTCPServer to print connection-reset tracebacks while Edge connections closed during server shutdown.
entries.rootCause: The local audit handler suppressed request logs but the server did not override handle_error for expected browser disconnects at teardown.
entries.prevention: Every local threaded browser-audit server overrides handle_error to suppress teardown-only connection resets, while Selenium exceptions, console errors and assertion failures remain fail-closed.

entries.mistake: The first Screen 03 evidence screenshots captured only the phone element's visible viewport intersection because the review header left most of the phone below the current viewport.
entries.rootCause: Element screenshot capture was invoked without first scrolling the exact phone target to the viewport origin and verifying captured dimensions.
entries.prevention: Before every element screenshot, scroll the target to block start, verify its top is at the viewport origin, capture, and assert the PNG dimensions against the intended viewport before accepting evidence.

entries.mistake: C33I final local verification directly invoked the historical C30X FIX1 Screen03 v4 gate, which correctly rejected the unrelated active C33I ticket after all current scope and approved-UI gates had passed.
entries.rootCause: The immutable-content gate filename was mistaken for a generally replayable current UI lock despite permanent regression memory documenting its exact historical scope boundary.
entries.prevention: Never invoke check-screen03-v4-production-acceptance-c30x-fix1.ps1 under a later active ticket. Use check-approved-ui-locks.ps1 for the current immutable reference set and only a registered current-ticket successor containment owner when one exists; direct hash comparison remains read-only evidence, not historical-scope replay.

entries.mistake: The attempt to launch a hidden persistent Python HTTP server for founder review was rejected by the shell policy before execution.
entries.rootCause: A background process launch was chosen even though the standalone proposal can be presented through a local file URL without a persistent helper.
entries.prevention: For standalone founder-review HTML with local relative assets, use the Codex browser panel file URL first. Do not retry a policy-rejected background server; use a bounded foreground test server only inside an active verification command.

entries.mistake: The first Screen 03 v5 email-link proposal collapsed the accepted six-icon social account grid into one full-width Google row, even though the authorized successor was limited to replacing the Email OTP interaction.
entries.rootCause: Provider-truth concerns were incorrectly expressed as a broader method-selection redesign instead of preserving the accepted Screen 03 presentation and changing only the email path.
entries.prevention: A versioned single-method Screen 03 amendment starts from an exact accepted-state inventory and preserves every unrelated visible provider, label, order and layout. The v5 diff and rendered audit must prove the six social icons and Mobile OTP remain present before founder re-review.

entries.mistake: A read-only search was launched from the screenbook while also naming production-repository-relative owners, so the screenbook match emitted but the production paths were unresolved and the command exited 1.
entries.rootCause: Two repository-relative searches with different owning roots were combined under one working directory.
entries.prevention: Run each repository-relative search from the repository that owns the path, or use an already verified absolute path; never aggregate production and screenbook relative paths under one working directory.

entries.mistake: The first local-browser navigation retry invoked browser.tabs.open even though the connected browser binding does not expose that method, so the call failed before navigation.
entries.rootCause: The tab API name was guessed after a persistent browser binding was reused without the method surface being present in the compacted task context.
entries.prevention: When a persistent browser binding is reused but its callable surface is not available in current context, inspect supported method names first and invoke only a verified method; never guess a tab-open API.

entries.mistake: The connected in-app browser rejected automated navigation to the local Screen 03 file URL under its URL safety policy; no navigation or mutation occurred.
entries.rootCause: The browser-control surface does not permit model-driven navigation to this local-file URL.
entries.prevention: Do not retry, bypass or substitute another browser-control surface after this policy block; use immutable-source comparison and repository-contained static assertions, then provide the exact local path for founder-controlled review.

entries.mistake: The first post-correction static audit aggregated source slicing, fourteen assertions and two hashes into one long inline shell command, which the shell host rejected with Access is denied before any assertion result.
entries.rootCause: Too many independently bounded checks were composed into one inline shell invocation, increasing host-policy and diagnostic ambiguity.
entries.prevention: Run source/hash verification and structural assertions as small independent read-only commands; a host-level rejection is zero audit evidence and no assertion result may be inferred.

entries.mistake: After splitting the static audit, three read-only shell checks were launched concurrently and the Windows host rejected the aggregate launch with Access is denied before any result was returned.
entries.rootCause: The correction removed command monolith size but retained concurrent Windows process launches, leaving a second host-level rejection surface.
entries.prevention: Run C33I post-correction shell checks strictly one process at a time; accept evidence only from an individually completed exit-zero command.

entries.mistake: A serial PowerShell check loaded the full proposal, sliced the choose-state substring and evaluated several regex assertions, but the host rejected it with Access is denied before any result.
entries.rootCause: The audit retained an inline full-file substring and regex execution shape that the shell host rejected despite removing concurrency.
entries.prevention: For this proposal use serial bounded rg exact-anchor checks and direct hashes only; normalize an expected no-match explicitly and never retry inline full-file substring execution.

entries.mistake: A handoff lookup found the C33I active-handoff section but also supplied two reconstructed qualification and handoff filenames that do not exist, so rg emitted partial matches and exited 1.
entries.rootCause: Descriptive ticket wording was converted into literal filenames instead of resolving the repository's exact current owners first.
entries.prevention: Resolve C33I documentation owners with rg --files and a bounded C33I filter before any content search; partial matches followed by missing positional paths are zero evidence.

entries.mistake: The first post-FINAL repository identity check included the entire apps/mobile/test directory in targeted git status, causing the large dirty evidence listing to be truncated even though branch and HEAD were confirmed.
entries.rootCause: A broad directory was treated as a bounded status target in a repository with extensive user-owned test evidence.
entries.prevention: Post-FINAL status checks name only exact active-ticket files; directory-level apps/mobile/test status is prohibited and exact test owners are resolved with rg --files first.

entries.mistake: The first founder-screenshot dimension and hash inventory placed a statement-form PowerShell foreach directly before Format-Table, producing an empty-pipe parser failure before any image was read or copied.
entries.rootCause: The command repeated REG-20260815-2468 instead of applying its required named-array pattern.
entries.prevention: Every PowerShell inventory assigns loop output to an explicit ticket-named array and only then pipes the array for formatting; the C33I retry must use c33iScreenshotFacts as that owner.

entries.mistake: A bounded source-inventory command supplied scripts/check-mvp-scope*.ps1 as a positional ripgrep path on Windows; ripgrep rejected the invalid filename syntax after returning other requested matches.
entries.rootCause: A PowerShell-style wildcard was passed as a literal ripgrep path instead of resolving matching files first.
entries.prevention: Resolve wildcard script inventories with rg --files and a bounded filename filter, then pass only verified exact paths to content search; mixed partial output plus a path error is zero evidence for the rejected lookup.

entries.mistake: An email-link dependency inventory included a guessed repository-root pubspec.yaml path that does not exist, causing ripgrep to return a path error after printing the separately requested Screen03 frame source.
entries.rootCause: A conventional dependency-manifest location was assumed without resolving the repository's actual pubspec owners.
entries.prevention: Resolve dependency manifests and every optional search root with rg --files before content search; pass only verified owners and normalize a clean no-match independently from path errors.

entries.mistake: The first C33J ticket and assessment patch bundled new files with two historical documentation appends and guessed one wrapped sentence as exact patch context; apply_patch rejected the entire patch before mutation.
entries.rootCause: A broad atomic patch mixed independent additions with an unverified prose context anchor.
entries.prevention: Create new C33J owners in a dedicated patch, inspect exact documentation tails, and append chronological corrections in separate patches using verified terminal anchors.

entries.mistake: The first native v5 layout wrapped a shrink-wrapped provider GridView in IntrinsicHeight, which Flutter rejects because a RenderShrinkWrappingViewport cannot provide intrinsic dimensions.
entries.rootCause: Bottom legal-copy alignment used an intrinsic-height pattern without accounting for the chooser's embedded viewport widget.
entries.prevention: Screen03 v5 uses a non-intrinsic scroll column with explicit minimum-height spacing; focused chooser and 320x568 at 140 percent tests must pass before any broader gate.

entries.mistake: A command changed working directory to apps/mobile but still passed apps/mobile-prefixed formatter paths, and a semicolon allowed the focused test to run after the formatter reported missing paths.
entries.rootCause: Repository-relative paths were reused after changing the command working directory, and the multi-step command lacked explicit fail-fast control.
entries.prevention: From apps/mobile, use lib/... and test/... paths only; run formatting and tests as separate commands or explicitly stop on nonzero exit before continuing.

entries.mistake: The first focused widget-test failure emitted the full repeated intrinsic-layout stack and exceeded the tool output bound, so the combined result was truncated.
entries.rootCause: The failure replay used the default expanded reporter without bounded retained log evidence after a render assertion generated repeated frames.
entries.prevention: Use the compact Flutter test reporter for retries, retain bounded failure evidence, and never treat a truncated combined output as complete test evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C33J static-gate replay read founderDecision from acceptance.approval, but the frozen v5 acceptance schema stores that field under acceptance.verification; strict mode stopped the gate.
entries.rootCause: The gate assertion reconstructed a plausible nested path instead of binding the exact already-inspected acceptance schema.
entries.prevention: Static gates bind JSON fields only from an exact parsed owner inventory; C33J uses acceptance.verification.founderDecision and never guesses sibling object placement.

entries.mistake: The second C33J gate replay searched all JourneySession source for the token emailLink:, so the legitimate in-memory named argument passed to Firebase was misclassified as persistence.
entries.rootCause: A security assertion targeted a lexical token across the whole state owner instead of the exact persistence schema boundary.
entries.prevention: Extract the JourneySnapshot declaration through the JourneyStore boundary and assert that exact persisted schema contains neither emailLink nor emailAddress; allow the opaque in-memory adapter call required for completion.

entries.mistake: The first nine-file affected regression batch passed 59 tests, but repeated MOOLSOCIAL_STARTUP diagnostics caused the displayed transcript to be partially truncated despite the compact reporter.
entries.rootCause: Compact reporting did not bound application debug output emitted by many session starts.
entries.prevention: Replay the identical exact-file batch through a streaming summary filter that emits only the terminal pass/fail line while preserving the native Flutter exit code; retain the unfiltered pass only as preliminary evidence.

entries.mistake: C33J qualification directly replayed the historical C33E FIX4 static gate, which correctly rejected because it byte-binds the prior C33F successor release context rather than the current C33J ticket selection.
entries.rootCause: A predecessor lifecycle gate was treated as an unconditional current semantic regression gate after the active MVP ticket changed.
entries.prevention: Do not replay byte-bound predecessor gates under unrelated active tickets. Preserve their qualified evidence and run their source-level Flutter matrix plus the current successor composition gate instead.

entries.mistake: C33J initially wired an email-link return only through platformDispatcher.defaultRouteName at cold launch; no active-process route-information observer forwarded a link opened while MoolSocial remained running.
entries.rootCause: Cold-start completion was treated as covering all App Link delivery modes without inventorying the existing WidgetsBindingObserver lifecycle surface.
entries.prevention: Every external-return journey proves both cold-start and already-running delivery. C33J FIX1 adds one route-information handoff that reuses JourneySession and rejects unrelated routes.

entries.mistake: The open REG2498 finding listed its planned FIX1 test and checker under gates before either file existed, so the regression-memory gate correctly rejected the missing repository paths.
entries.rootCause: Planned evidence owners were recorded as existing executable gates during preselection rather than added only after creation.
entries.prevention: Open findings reference only existing evidence and memory gates. Add a planned test or checker to registry gate paths only after the file exists and is validated.

entries.mistake: The first FIX1 test used tester.binding.handlePushRouteInformation, but TestWidgetsFlutterBinding in the pinned Flutter SDK does not define that method, so the focused file failed compilation with four errors.
entries.rootCause: A production binding method name was assumed to be directly exposed by the widget-test binding without verifying the pinned public testing API.
entries.prevention: Verify the route-information test injection surface from current official Flutter API documentation, then use only the documented public messenger/binding contract and retain a compile-pass focused test.

entries.mistake: The first compiling FIX1 run asserted JourneySession.readyRoute after GoRouter had already opened and confirmed the protected destination, so the test treated intentional one-shot pending-route consumption as query loss and failed 1 of 3 despite the Create destination being reached.
entries.rootCause: A transient authentication return intent was used as a post-navigation route oracle instead of asserting the query-selected destination in the rendered router owner.
entries.prevention: Foreground authentication return tests assert the destination through its exact selected UI semantics before separately proving that the pending return intent was consumed; readyRoute is not used as the current-location oracle after GoRouter confirmation.

entries.mistake: The second FIX1 run proved authentication completion but found no screen04-rail-create semantics after the foreground link, so exact post-authentication destination rendering remains unqualified while 2 of 3 tests pass.
entries.rootCause: JourneySession completion notified GoRouter, which automatically opened and confirmed the exact return route; before didPushRouteInformation resumed, confirmation consumed returnTo, so its second router.go called readyRoute and overwrote the exact destination with the generic Social fallback.
entries.prevention: Email-link completion captures a canonical, non-persisted one-shot destination before notifying the router. The foreground callback consumes that destination after await and never recomputes an already-consumed return intent.

entries.mistake: A read-only C33J FIX1 lookup passed apps/mobile/test/uaw_c33j* as a Windows ripgrep root, repeating the invalid wildcard-path class and emitting OS error 123 after the useful exact-root search.
entries.rootCause: A filename wildcard was placed in a positional Windows path instead of using an existing directory root with an rg -g filter.
entries.prevention: Ripgrep searches use verified literal roots; filename selection uses -g patterns only. Mixed successful matches plus any invalid-root error are not a clean lookup transcript.

entries.mistake: The first REG2502 repair retained and consumed a one-shot completion destination, but the focused replay still rendered no screen04-rail-create owner and remained 2 passed, 1 failed.
entries.rootCause: Pending diagnosis: retaining the destination prevented no proven overwrite, so the actual post-authentication router owner and redirect sequence must be observed before another repair.
entries.prevention: Do not retry a plausible asynchronous navigation repair until the rendered owner or router destination is observed through a bounded test diagnostic; source-level reasoning alone is insufficient for this race.

entries.mistake: A bounded key lookup included the guessed directory apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/screens/screen02_setup, which does not exist, so the otherwise useful output ended with a missing-path error.
entries.rootCause: A plausible feature directory was passed to ripgrep without first resolving its owner through rg --files.
entries.prevention: Content searches use only verified literal files or directories returned by rg --files; a guessed optional path is never added alongside known roots.

entries.mistake: The bounded post-authentication diagnostic found zero Sign-in, Splash, Setup, legacy-containment and Social Create owners after foreground completion, leaving the app with no qualified rendered route owner while 2 of 3 focused tests pass.
entries.rootCause: Pending diagnosis: inspect the public GoRouter routeInformationProvider URI and any framework exception before another source change.
entries.prevention: Every authentication return must prove both a canonical router URI and one rendered destination owner; a state-ready session with zero known owners is a blocking blank-route regression.

entries.mistake: After foreground completion the public GoRouter routeInformationProvider URI was exactly /app/social?sub=create and no framework exception existed, but zero known route owners rendered.
entries.rootCause: Pending diagnosis: compare the router delegate's current configuration with the exact provider URI and bounded widget types.
entries.prevention: Authentication return qualification binds route-provider state, router-delegate state and rendered destination ownership; a correct provider URI alone cannot qualify the journey.

entries.mistake: The first REG2507 registry append patch used a mismatched compound context and apply_patch rejected it without changing files.
entries.rootCause: The patch coupled a status replacement and an append around an assumed neighboring id rather than the inspected exact tail anchor.
entries.prevention: Registry append retries first inspect the exact tail, then use the existing final evidence line and array close as the narrow append anchor; a rejected patch counts as no mutation and no evidence.

entries.mistake: The focused test used screen04-rail-create as the exact Create destination oracle even though the provider and delegate were exact and the rendered tree already contained SocialUniversalV2 and SocialCreateWorkbenchV2.
entries.rootCause: A navigation control was mistaken for the destination content owner in a responsive rendered state where the exact Create workbench exists without that compact-rail key.
entries.prevention: Authentication return tests assert the canonical provider URI, delegate URI and the exact destination-content owner. A responsive navigation control is not used as the destination oracle.

entries.mistake: A combined exact-file lookup found creator keys but its optional class-name search returned zero matches, causing the shell command to exit 1 even though zero was an admissible discovery result.
entries.rootCause: The optional second ripgrep search did not normalize exit 1 before being combined with the required first lookup.
entries.prevention: Required and optional searches run separately. Optional ripgrep zero-match exits are explicitly normalized and never invalidate a successful required lookup.

entries.mistake: The first test-oracle correction patch inserted a second Update File header before closing the preceding hunk, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch without changing files.
entries.rootCause: Two verified file edits were composed into one malformed patch envelope instead of separate complete hunks.
entries.prevention: Each file update uses a complete independently valid apply_patch hunk; after a malformed multi-file patch, retry files separately against freshly inspected context.

entries.mistake: The first same-device App Link inventory read the verified build.gradle.kts and then also requested a guessed optional build.gradle path, leaving an otherwise useful read command nonzero.
entries.rootCause: Alternative Android Gradle owner names were requested together instead of resolving the single repository owner through rg --files first.
entries.prevention: Android configuration inventory discovers the exact Gradle owner with rg --files and reads only that literal path; optional alternative filenames are not appended to evidence commands.

entries.mistake: The first exact release-wrapper search for MOOLSOCIAL_EMAIL_LINK returned the admissible finding of zero matches but was not normalized, so the combined read command exited 1.
entries.rootCause: A negative dependency inventory was executed as a required ripgrep match instead of an optional absence check.
entries.prevention: Release-wrapper presence audits normalize optional ripgrep exit 1 and record zero matches as a finding; absence cannot be claimed from an unclassified nonzero command.

entries.mistake: The first FIX2 focused run expected Uri.hasPort to reject an explicitly written :443, but Dart normalizes the default HTTPS port and the case correctly qualified; the matrix passed 2 and failed 1.
entries.rootCause: The test asserted lexical URL spelling through a semantic Uri API that treats the default HTTPS port as the same origin.
entries.prevention: Runtime URL tests distinguish security-relevant origin changes, using a genuinely non-default port such as 444; default HTTPS port spelling is not treated as a different origin.

entries.mistake: The first FIX2 static gate invocation stopped before assertions because its helper declared parameter $Host, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's read-only automatic $Host variable.
entries.rootCause: A concise domain parameter name was chosen without checking PowerShell automatic-variable ownership.
entries.prevention: PowerShell helpers use task-specific parameter names such as DomainHost and never declare names that collide case-insensitively with automatic or preference variables; both hosts must compile and run the gate.

entries.mistake: The first composed predecessor replay rejected the stricter FIX2 source because the C33J parent gate still required the superseded isQualifiedHttpsRuntimeEndpoint call spelling; the fail-fast command therefore did not execute or count the following FIX1 gate.
entries.rootCause: The successor implementation replaced a protected runtime invariant without updating the predecessor gate's static composition anchor before replay, and two independently countable gates were invoked in one fail-fast shell command.
entries.prevention: Successor hardening updates predecessor static anchors in the same scoped change, then replays parent, FIX1 and FIX2 gates separately on both PowerShell hosts; only an explicitly observed exit-zero result is counted.

entries.mistake: A read-only affected-test inventory filtered rg --files output with a regular expression that required POSIX slash separators, so Windows backslash paths produced zero matches and exit 1.
entries.rootCause: The filename filter encoded one platform's separator instead of validating already-known paths literally or accepting both slash forms.
entries.prevention: Known affected files are validated with literal Test-Path checks; cross-platform rg file filters use [\\/] and an unclassified zero match cannot prove absence.

entries.mistake: The first C33K execution-authority replay used a descriptive authorization.state value not accepted by the existing MVP gate, so the gate rejected before any external write.
entries.rootCause: A machine-enumerated field was populated from prose meaning instead of the exact accepted values in its checker; the exact founder wording already had a separate evidence field.
entries.prevention: Before writing machine state, inspect and use only the checker's enumerated values; preserve exact founder language in the ticket and founderAcceptance evidence rather than inventing a new enum.

entries.mistake: The first Firebase provider-form attempt selected the first unsaved switch but the in-app browser could not dispatch the second Email Link switch click at its translated coordinate; Save was not pressed.
entries.rootCause: A semantic setChecked action still depended on a browser-coordinate translation that failed for the second visible switch in Firebase's inline editor.
entries.prevention: After a browser action has no effect, inspect the fresh visible DOM, retarget the exact node through DOM interaction, verify both checked states and enabled Save state, then submit once and count only a successful provider-table readback.

entries.mistake: The one authorized Firebase provider Save submission returned the visible error Error updating Email/Password; no successful post-submit provider-table readback existed and the write was not counted.
entries.rootCause: The pre-refresh Firebase console session rejected the write even though the source and form inputs were valid; the founder's explicit page refresh restored the accepted write path.
entries.prevention: External form submissions count only after authoritative post-submit readback. After rejection, preserve zero counts and wait for an explicit session change; after refresh, rerun gates, submit once, then verify the provider row plus both switch states without exposing tokens.

entries.mistake: A read-only capability check invoked gcloud identity-platform --help, but the installed Cloud SDK has no identity-platform command group and exited nonzero.
entries.rootCause: A REST Identity Platform resource name was incorrectly assumed to map to a locally available gcloud command group.
entries.prevention: Use only documented locally available CLI commands with proven semantics; do not infer gcloud groups from REST resources and never obtain or print an OAuth access token to bypass a missing command.

entries.mistake: The one authorized attempt to add exactly moolsocial.com returned Error updating authorised domain list; the authoritative table remained unchanged and the action was not counted.
entries.rootCause: Two distinct Firebase Authentication writes were rejected in the same pre-refresh console session; after the founder refreshed that session, the exact domain write succeeded with all three domains visible.
entries.prevention: After distinct Firebase configuration writes fail in the same session, stop retries until an explicit session change, rerun gates, then attempt the exact write once and count it only after the requested domain and all preserved domains are authoritatively visible.

entries.mistake: A dry-run-only firebase deploy --only auth invocation was rejected because the installed Firebase CLI does not recognize Auth as a deploy target; no deployment started.
entries.rootCause: Current official Firebase documentation and schema support the Auth deploy target, but the installed local CLI surface is older or otherwise lacks that capability.
entries.prevention: Do not retry an unsupported local target, update tooling or obtain access tokens as a bypass; preserve the official source declaration and resume through a founder-refreshed signed-in console with authoritative table readback.

entries.mistake: After provider success was authoritatively re-read, the semantic Cancel action for the unchanged Firebase provider dialog failed at coordinate translation; the dialog stayed open and the domain flow did not start.
entries.rootCause: The Firebase inline editor remained positioned where the in-app browser's semantic click translated to a missing point, repeating the interaction-layer failure already seen on its second switch.
entries.prevention: For this Firebase inline editor, use fresh visible-DOM node actions after any coordinate-backed failure, verify the dialog closed, and preserve separately proven provider success.

entries.mistake: The first sanitized dual-origin assetlinks readback command piped directly from a foreach statement into Format-Table, which PowerShell rejected at parse time before any network request ran.
entries.rootCause: The one-line command omitted an explicit collection assignment or pipeline-producing grouping around the foreach statement.
entries.prevention: Assign foreach output to a task-specific collection first, then pipe that collection to formatting; register parser failures before retry and keep readback output limited to public origin, HTTP status, package-match count and fingerprint presence.

entries.mistake: The C33J FIX2 static gate was replayed after C33K became the active MVP ticket, so its intentional active-ticket assertion rejected even though the sealed C33J FIX2 qualification remains recorded as the exact predecessor.
entries.rootCause: The final C33K command list treated an active-ticket gate as a successor-safe source replay without first inspecting its state-selection contract.
entries.prevention: Before replaying any predecessor gate after ticket selection advances, inspect whether it is active-ticket-only. Preserve its sealed dual-host qualification and use current focused source tests or a separately authorized successor-aware gate instead of retrying against false state.

entries.mistake: The first next-action repository inventory repeated REG-20260815-2525 by piping directly from a foreach statement to Format-Table, so PowerShell rejected the command at parse time.
entries.rootCause: The applicable same-day regression prevention was not applied before composing the first compound read-only command of the new turn; the loop was written from habit instead of the required collection-first pattern.
entries.prevention: For every PowerShell foreach that feeds later formatting, always assign the complete loop output to a task-specific collection and only then pipe the collection. Before the first compound command of a continuation, run the regression-memory gate or manually apply every matching latest entry; a registered recurrence blocks retry until this evidence exists.

entries.mistake: The recovery gate was invoked with Phase planning even though the regression-memory checker accepts only general, implementation, build or device.
entries.rootCause: The registry appliesTo vocabulary was incorrectly assumed to be identical to the checker's Phase ValidateSet instead of using the documented general phase for cross-phase planning checks.
entries.prevention: Inspect a gate's parameter contract before selecting a value; use Phase general for continuation-wide planning and apply appliesTo tags only inside registry entries.

entries.mistake: The first C33L MVP execution-state patch bundled several distant hunks and assumed an exact current C33K ticket block; apply_patch rejected the entire patch when one context did not match the dirty tree.
entries.rootCause: The patch was composed from a partially projected section rather than re-reading and matching each narrow current block immediately before editing.
entries.prevention: After a broad patch context rejection, preserve the zero-write result, inspect the exact narrow current blocks and apply independently verifiable hunks; never retry the same broad context.

entries.mistake: The C33L file-hash reconciliation command again piped directly from a foreach statement into Format-Table, repeating REG-2525 and REG-2527 and failing at parse time before reading or changing any target.
entries.rootCause: The prevention existed only as narrative memory and was not enforced as a reusable command-construction invariant before composing another PowerShell loop.
entries.prevention: C33L release work prohibits direct foreach-to-pipeline syntax. Every loop result must be assigned to a task-specific collection before any formatting, and the implementation memory gate must pass before the corrected readback or any release-state mutation.

entries.mistake: REG-2530 named the planned C33L release-readiness checker in its gates list before that checker existed, so the regression-memory gate correctly rejected the missing repository owner.
entries.rootCause: A future enforcement owner was recorded as present evidence instead of keeping the current entry bound only to existing owners and adding the successor checker after creation.
entries.prevention: Regression entries may reference only repository paths that exist at registration time. Planned gates remain in ticket prose until created and verified, then can be added through a separately validated registry update.

entries.mistake: The combined REG-2530/REG-2531 resolution patch used an underscore in the expected REG-2531 status where the current registry used a hyphen, so apply_patch rejected the entire patch.
entries.rootCause: A multi-file resolution patch was composed without copying the exact current status token from the just-read registry.
entries.prevention: Resolution updates use narrow one-owner hunks copied from the immediate current read. A context rejection is treated as zero-write and the broad patch is not repeated.

entries.mistake: A C33L read-only gate inventory passed scripts/qualify* as a positional rg path on Windows, repeating the known invalid wildcard-path class and causing the combined command to exit nonzero after an earlier useful match.
entries.rootCause: The repository-wide prohibition on positional Windows wildcard paths was not applied while composing a second search clause.
entries.prevention: C33L diagnostics use exact verified paths or directory roots with rg --glob filters. Partial output from a combined command with any path error is not accepted as complete evidence.

entries.mistake: The first C33L source-gate replay invoked the C33E FIX2 gate, which still pins an old SHA-256 for the mutable failed C33F ticket and rejected before C33L qualification despite four preserved sanitized Google readiness facts.
entries.rootCause: A predecessor gate that composes the earlier candidate ticket lifecycle was reused as a successor-safe live-fact gate without first removing its stale C33F ticket coupling.
entries.prevention: C33L validates the immutable sanitized Google readiness state and all four evidence hashes directly, while the generic wrapper skips the predecessor C33E composition only for the C33L contract. Older contracts retain their existing behavior.

entries.mistake: The first C33L source-manifest seal used the older C30V protected-successor allowlist, which omitted the already-qualified C33G Social identity provider-truth test and rejected one unexpected protected owner.
entries.rootCause: The manifest generator's exact protected inventory was not advanced when the C33G repair added one new Social-named test after the C33F seal.
entries.prevention: Add exactly apps/mobile/test/uaw_c33g_fix2_social_identity_provider_truth_test.dart to the qualified successor protected-owner list, preserve the 206 historical owners and require exact current count 210 with zero unexpected successors.

entries.mistake: The first successful C33L manifest was sealed while REG-2535 still had a registered-pending status, so the mandatory status resolution would immediately change a manifest-bound source owner.
entries.rootCause: Manifest generation occurred before finalizing the regression entry that the same generation attempt was intended to resolve.
entries.prevention: Preserve the first manifest as immutable non-candidate attempt evidence, finalize all current registry entries and pass memory, then create a new uniquely named candidate manifest. No registry or source change is allowed after that new seal without rejecting and resealing the candidate before build.

entries.mistake: The first C33L Flutter attempt completed and preserved JSONL, but the inline summarizer accessed test.hidden directly under strict mode and failed when that optional property was absent.
entries.rootCause: The inline summarizer did not reuse the repository authoritative runner's Get-OptionalBool helper for optional Flutter JSON event properties.
entries.prevention: Parse preserved JSONL with an explicit optional-property helper, do not rerun before registration, and use the repository authoritative manifest runner with the discovered exact pass/skip counts for both final sealed cycles.

entries.mistake: The first C33L 72-file Flutter attempt produced one authored failure and one error event in private-Dev public review restores Screen 04 after safe boot.
entries.rootCause: The production bootstrap intentionally added passwordless email-link return between the existing YouTube return and /boot fallback, but the older public-review static test still required the superseded one-line initialLocation expression.
entries.prevention: The test and dual-host focused gate now require the exact YouTube-return then email-link-return then boot-fallback order. The rejected seal remains evidence; parent C33L requires a new registry-bound manifest and two fresh identical zero-failure cycles.

entries.mistake: The exact C33L FIX1 repair child was added after the failed test but before its required robustness/reuse assessment was embedded and pinned in the MVP scope machine state.
entries.rootCause: Failure registration and executable child selection were treated as one action even though repository policy requires the child checkpoint before implementation.
entries.prevention: Add the zero-duplication assessment to the child ticket, select and pin the exact child in mvp-scope-gate-state.json, disable build/device/external authorities during FIX1 and pass delivery plus MVP execution gates before editing the test or adding its prevention gate.

entries.mistake: The first C33L FIX1 prevention-gate parser check failed because one expected Dart string used backslash-escaped double quotes, which PowerShell does not recognize as string escaping.
entries.rootCause: Dart/JSON escaping syntax was carried into a PowerShell double-quoted literal instead of using PowerShell backticks or a safe single-quoted representation.
entries.prevention: Use a PowerShell single-quoted literal with doubled embedded apostrophes for the exact Dart assertion, then parse the gate before any execution or test retry.

entries.mistake: The first parsed FIX1 gate expected two literal backslashes before n in the Dart source assertions, while the repaired Dart test correctly contains one backslash-n escape.
entries.rootCause: JSON-style double-backslash transport escaping was retained in the resulting PowerShell source even though PowerShell treats backslash literally.
entries.prevention: Use one literal backslash in each PowerShell expected Dart source token, reparse, pass regression memory and then replay both PowerShell hosts before any Flutter retry.

entries.mistake: The post-restart continuation guessed config/codex-regression-memory.json for the permanent registry, so the read-only interrupted-patch verification stopped on a missing path before returning evidence.
entries.rootCause: The compacted handoff used a summarized label rather than the repository-owned literal path and the continuation failed to apply the already-registered rule that registry paths must be discovered before use.
entries.prevention: Use bounded rg --files discovery and the verified literal config/codex-development-regression-registry.json for every registry read or patch. Never guess a shortened memory filename; any recurrence invalidates the pending source seal and must be registered before retry.

entries.mistake: The first post-FIX1 C33L cycle passed the parent source gates, then the FIX1 prevention gate rejected because it invoked the MVP scope gate with the child FIX1 candidate ID after parent C33L had been correctly reselected.
entries.rootCause: The FIX1 gate proved only the child-active implementation phase and did not define a parent-replay mode that validates the immutable qualified FIX1 assessment after control returns to the parent release ticket.
entries.prevention: Add an exact C33L FIX2 gate-composition repair: accept active FIX1 only during child qualification, or active parent C33L only when priorC33LFix1SelectedTicketAssessment pins the exact qualified child ticket hash and evidence. Reject all other active tickets. Reselect the parent, create a new registry-bound seal, and restart both complete cycles from zero.

entries.mistake: REG-2543 referenced the expected FIX1 PowerShell 7 rejection log, but Tee-Object retained only success output and the terminating error was not written to that file, so regression memory rejected the missing evidence path.
entries.rootCause: The registry entry assumed a pipeline evidence file existed without verifying Test-Path after the failure-bearing command and before adding the evidence reference.
entries.prevention: Verify every evidence path as an existing repository file before registry reference. When a terminating error was not retained, reconstruct only the bounded sanitized command, exit and rejection text with apply_patch before retrying regression memory.

entries.mistake: The FIX2 checkpoint command invoked regression memory as an external pwsh process but did not immediately test LASTEXITCODE, so delivery and MVP scope checks ran after the memory child had already failed.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell ErrorActionPreference does not convert a native or child-process nonzero exit into a terminating error; the command block relied on an in-process exception behavior that does not cross the process boundary.
entries.prevention: After every pwsh, powershell.exe, Flutter or npm invocation, immediately assert LASTEXITCODE before running the next stage. Never batch a qualification sequence without per-stage exit enforcement.

entries.mistake: The second post-FIX2 Flutter cycle completed its test process but the authoritative PowerShell summarizer crashed when ConvertFrom-Json yielded null and the mandatory Event parameter rejected it before a bounded result summary could be produced.
entries.rootCause: The runner did not distinguish blank raw lines, the JSON literal null, and typed JSON objects before invoking the event-shape helper; it assumed every non-throwing ConvertFrom-Json result was an object.
entries.prevention: Add explicit pre-classification for blank lines and null JSON results, count them in bounded sanitized failure categories without reading values, and add behavioral fixtures for blank, JSON null, typed and untyped objects. Preserve cycle evidence, reseal after repair, and restart two complete cycles from zero.

entries.mistake: The generic single-AAB wrapper built and sealed r60.50 successfully, advanced the detailed build count and authority plus the aggregate candidate build count, but left aggregate actionCounts.build at zero and aggregate releaseAuthorities.build available_once; the C33L postbuild gate rejected before Play upload.
entries.rootCause: The generic wrapper's build-consumption and success transitions did not treat every detailed and aggregate lifecycle mirror as one required state contract, while its static wrapper checker asserted only aggregate.candidate.buildCount.
entries.prevention: Reject and preserve r60.50 at 1/0/0/0. Before any successor build, repair the generic wrapper to update detailed and aggregate build counts and authority together, strengthen static and behavioral dual-host gates, seal an exact candidate-specific interrupted-postbuild recovery owner, and require both postbuild mirrors plus exact AAB provenance before upload authority can become available.

entries.mistake: Two read-only postbuild inspection commands repeated the already-registered PowerShell parser failure by piping directly from a foreach statement; both exited one before reading or changing target files.
entries.rootCause: The collection-first prevention from prior C33L regressions was not applied consistently during urgent postbuild diagnosis.
entries.prevention: Every multi-item PowerShell projection must initialize a task-specific results array, append inside the loop, and pipe only the completed array. The corrected pattern and regression-memory gate must pass before the next release repair check.

entries.mistake: A recursive postbuild search across quality documents, all quality artifacts, config and scripts exceeded its command timeout and returned no complete result.
entries.rootCause: The search scope included the very large retained evidence tree even though exact known transition owners were already available.
entries.prevention: After a build, inspect only verified literal gate, wrapper, state, manifest and incident owners. Never retry repository-wide or artifacts-wide authority searches; a timeout is zero evidence.

entries.mistake: The visible founder launcher exited automatically after the AAB succeeded but the postbuild gate failed, so the founder could not distinguish build success from full release success without a separate repository audit.
entries.rootCause: The launcher requested that the terminal remain open but did not own a sanitized post-cleanup success or failure hold and relied on the external host invocation to preserve the window.
entries.prevention: The successor launcher must erase transient files, process values and secure strings first, then retain a bounded status that distinguishes AAB success, postbuild qualification and later release stages without printing private values. Launcher disappearance is never accepted as release evidence.

entries.mistake: A literal-path duplicate search expected the missing aggregate assignments and launcher pause to produce no matches, but did not normalize ripgrep exit one and therefore ended as a failed combined command.
entries.rootCause: Expected absence was expressed as a raw search rather than an explicit assertion that distinguishes no-match exit one from real execution failure.
entries.prevention: Use exact already-read source lines as the retained evidence for this finding. Future expected-no-match checks explicitly accept exit zero or one according to the assertion and fail on every other exit; do not repeat this command.

entries.mistake: A read-only historical aggregate compatibility inventory failed at parse time because the nested aggregate-path expression was missing a closing parenthesis.
entries.rootCause: Several path resolution and JSON-read operations were composed into one nested expression instead of using independently verifiable named statements.
entries.prevention: Resolve repository root, aggregate relative path and aggregate absolute path in separate statements, then read JSON and append to the named results array. Parse and memory gates must pass before wrapper implementation.

entries.mistake: The corrected compatibility inventory attempted to read a repository directory for the historical C30V row because that state has a blank aggregateStatePath; Get-Content emitted a nonterminating error while the combined command still exited zero.
entries.rootCause: The ad-hoc inventory did not enable fail-fast error handling or validate that each aggregate path was nonblank and a leaf before reading it.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the irrelevant blank C30V row. Use the valid literal C30T/C30U/C30X/C33F/C33L results and guard actionCounts.build and releaseAuthorities.build independently in the generic wrapper. Every future inventory validates nonblank leaf paths and treats any emitted error as failure.

entries.mistake: The first strengthened generic wrapper checker run rejected under strict mode because the expected aggregate release-authority source token was double quoted and PowerShell attempted to resolve an unset checker-local Aggregate variable.
entries.rootCause: A source-code token containing a dollar-prefixed variable was represented as an interpolating string instead of a literal PowerShell string.
entries.prevention: Represent the exact source token with one single-quoted PowerShell literal and doubled embedded apostrophes, parse the checker, pass regression memory and then rerun the checker on both required hosts.

entries.mistake: The generic wrapper checker rejected the current candidate-dynamic wrapper because it still required hard-coded r60.45 build-name and build-number source tokens.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper evolved into a shared successor owner, but the older static checker retained one historical candidate's exact version arguments.
entries.prevention: The generic checker requires the exact dynamic versionName and versionCode argument tokens. Each candidate-specific release gate continues to own exact version identity. Reparse, pass memory and rerun on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: The generic wrapper checker passed on PowerShell 7 but Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejected because its existing two-argument String.Contains overload is unavailable on .NET Framework.
entries.rootCause: The checker had not been qualified on both mandated PowerShell hosts after adopting StringComparison-aware Contains calls.
entries.prevention: Use IndexOf with Ordinal or OrdinalIgnoreCase for every wrapper and launcher source comparison, preserving semantics on PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. Parse, pass memory and replay both hosts.

entries.mistake: The generic wrapper checker passed on Windows PowerShell 5.1 but emitted a success line that called the host PowerShell-7.
entries.rootCause: The checker success text was inherited from its original PowerShell-7-only launch boundary and was not made host-aware when dual-host qualification was required.
entries.prevention: Report the actual PSVersionTable major in checker evidence and require the new FIX4 gate to use only PowerShell-5.1-compatible ordinal IndexOf comparisons before its first run.

entries.mistake: The first FIX4 gate run rejected the generic wrapper as credential-shaped because the gate's source scanner matched the wrapper's own required AIza leak-detection regex sentinel.
entries.rootCause: A value-oriented credential regex was applied to security-tool source that necessarily contains the same detection pattern.
entries.prevention: Do not treat detector source as a detected value. Preserve the existing leak scanner and assert exact forbidden secret-file reads, value assignments and environment-value literals in the wrapper/checker. Pass memory before retrying fixtures.

entries.mistake: The narrowed FIX4 privacy assertion still scanned the generic checker's own forbidden-token sentinel list and rejected the expected secret-file read token there.
entries.rootCause: The correction distinguished credential-shape detector source from values but did not distinguish executable wrapper source from the static checker that intentionally names forbidden constructs.
entries.prevention: Apply forbidden private-value-use assertions only to the executable wrapper, and separately require the checker to retain its sentinel enforcement. Pass memory before the next fixture retry.

entries.mistake: The FIX5 registered ticket differed from its assessed proposal by one word in an explicit exclusion, so the selected machine state's proposal hash did not match the ticket manifest.
entries.rootCause: The ticket was manually duplicated from the proposal and one semantically similar word was changed during the copy.
entries.prevention: Restore the registered ticket to the byte-identical assessed proposal, prove equal SHA-256 before the scope gate, and never manually retype a checkpointed manifest copy without immediate hash equality readback.

entries.mistake: The first FIX5 gate run found the helper function but attempted to project parameter names from FunctionDefinitionAst.Parameters, whose returned nodes did not expose the expected Name property under strict mode.
entries.rootCause: The gate assumed a convenient AST property instead of using the exact function body param-block owner for declared parameters.
