entries.prevention: Read FunctionDefinitionAst.Body.ParamBlock.Parameters, require exactly Result and NoWait, parse, pass regression memory and then retry the behavioral gate on both hosts.

entries.mistake: A pre-parent audit found that the qualified FIX4 prevention gate always calls the MVP scope gate with the FIX4 candidate ID, so it would reject after any valid successor ticket is selected.
entries.rootCause: The FIX4 gate proved only its child-active implementation lifecycle and did not define a generic qualified-successor replay binding.
entries.prevention: Add a pure selection-binding function that accepts direct FIX4 mode or successor mode only when current and selected tickets match and the prior FIX4 assessment pins the exact qualified ticket hash, state and evidence. Add dual-host active, successor and negative fixtures before parent selection.

entries.mistake: The first combined C33M ticket-selection apply-patch call returned truncated tool output, so its write result could not be inferred from the call transcript.
entries.rootCause: The attempted patch bundled a complete successor manifest with a broad machine-state edit, exceeding the available tool-output context at a release-selection boundary.
entries.prevention: Treat truncated mutation output as unknown, perform exact readback before retry, register the occurrence, and split the retry into bounded apply-patch operations. Require the registered ticket to be byte-identical to the assessed proposal and verify every selected-state field before running the scope gate.

entries.mistake: The first bounded post-registration readback constructed an ordered object but did not assign it to the variable later sent to ConvertTo-Json, producing a formatted table followed by null instead of one JSON object.
entries.rootCause: The verification command omitted the explicit assignment while shortening a previously larger PowerShell projection.
entries.prevention: Assign every verification projection to one ticket-named variable before serialization, set fail-fast behavior, and consume only that serialized object as gate evidence. The displayed direct property values remain valid but are not reused as the final structured readback.

entries.mistake: The first C33M founder-launcher result-retention patch failed verification because it assumed an empty line and closing-parenthesis context immediately before the existing try block.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined several distant launcher edits and used a generic array-closing anchor without first reading the exact adjacent source lines.
entries.prevention: Treat failed patch verification as zero writes, inspect exact bounded line ranges, and apply each launcher edit against a unique nearby owner token before structured parse and order checks.

entries.mistake: The first dual-host syntax check printed a pass with files=0 because the file array supplied after a PowerShell -Command string did not bind to the inline param block; the four paths were echoed as trailing arguments.
entries.rootCause: The invocation assumed script-file parameter binding semantics for a command-string execution boundary.
entries.prevention: Reject any parser result whose executed file count differs from the explicit expected count. Construct the exact literal file array inside each host command, parse every resolved path, and report host major plus count=4 before any gate retry.

entries.mistake: The qualified FIX5 launcher-retention prevention gate invoked the MVP scope gate with the historical FIX5 ticket ID and rejected when replayed under the valid selected C33M successor.
entries.rootCause: FIX5 was qualified only in its child-active lifecycle and did not implement the exact qualified-successor selection binding already required for FIX4.
entries.prevention: Create the exact C33M FIX1 repair ticket, preserve direct FIX5 mode, and accept successor replay only when current and selected ticket IDs agree and priorC33LFix5SelectedTicketAssessment pins the exact qualified FIX5 manifest hash, implementation state and evidence. Add dual-host active, successor and negative fixtures before C33M reselection.

entries.mistake: The dynamically generated apply-patch copy of the assessed C33M FIX1 proposal appended one extra trailing newline to the registered ticket, so the otherwise identical files had different SHA-256 hashes.
entries.rootCause: The shell-output extraction retained the proposal terminator while the Add File patch builder also appended its own terminal newline.
entries.prevention: Never infer byte identity from a generated patch copy. Compare SHA-256 immediately, inspect an exact no-index diff on mismatch, and make the registered ticket byte-identical before selection. Future copy helpers normalize exactly one terminal newline instead of blindly appending another.

entries.mistake: The first C33M FIX1 implementation patch combined function, lifecycle and output edits but failed verification because its assumed final FIX5 success-output line did not match the current qualified script.
entries.rootCause: The distant final hunk was drafted from remembered wording instead of a freshly read exact tail, causing the entire otherwise-bounded patch to reject atomically.
entries.prevention: Confirm zero write, read the exact tail and nearby unique anchors, then split the repair into function insertion, lifecycle replacement and output-only patches. Parse before running any behavioral fixture.

entries.mistake: A read-only C33M cycle-command inventory guessed scripts/check-uaw-c33l-fix2-fix1-gate-parent-replay-compatibility.ps1, which does not exist, and the bounded command failed before returning the remaining package-script inventory.
entries.rootCause: The query inferred a gate filename from the FIX2 ticket ID instead of resolving the exact qualified owner with rg --files as required by permanent memory.
entries.prevention: Register the failed lookup, retain and supersede the now-stale 2540-entry source manifest without deletion, resolve every cycle gate owner with rg --files, then seal a fresh registry generation before cycle one. Never reuse any result from the failed combined inventory.

entries.mistake: C33M cycle-one static stage passed seven gates, then the qualified C33L FIX1 Screen 04 safe-boot gate rejected because its lifecycle accepts only FIX1, the C33L parent or FIX2—not the valid selected C33M successor.
entries.rootCause: The earlier FIX2 compatibility repair encoded one historical parent ID instead of a generic exact qualified-successor binding, so the product-safety prevention was not reusable by later release parents.
entries.prevention: Create and select the exact C33M FIX2 ticket, preserve FIX1/FIX2/C33L modes, and add generic successor replay only when current and selected identities agree and the prior qualified FIX1/FIX2 assessments pin exact hashes, states and evidence. Add dual-host active, C33L, FIX2, C33M-successor and negative fixtures before resealing.

entries.mistake: The pre-cycle lifecycle audit of the qualified C33L FIX3 authoritative-Flutter gate used a broad Select-String context projection whose output exceeded the tool result boundary and was truncated, so the gate's C33M successor compatibility was not established.
entries.rootCause: The read-only audit requested every lifecycle-related match with surrounding context instead of first resolving exact line numbers and then reading only the bounded decision block.
entries.prevention: Treat the truncated result as unknown, retain and supersede the 2542-entry source manifest, then query only line number and exact text before reading one bounded literal line slice. Do not invoke FIX3 under C33M or start a fresh cycle until successor compatibility is proven or repaired under an exact ticket.

entries.mistake: The bounded pre-cycle audit proved the qualified C33L FIX3 authoritative-Flutter classification gate accepts only its child ticket or the rejected C33L r60.50 parent, so it cannot replay for the valid selected C33M r60.51 successor.
entries.rootCause: FIX3 qualification encoded one historical parent ID instead of an exact generic qualified-successor binding, repeating the lifecycle design defect already found in other reusable prevention gates.
entries.prevention: Create and select C33M FIX3, preserve direct child and C33L parent modes, and add generic successor replay only when current, top-level and selected identities agree and the prior qualified FIX3 manifest hash, state and evidence remain exact. Require dual-host historical, successor, negative and live fixtures before parent reselection and source sealing.

entries.mistake: The separately written C33M FIX3 ticket and assessed proposal differed by one exclusion token: the ticket used Play_upload while the proposal used Play upload, so their SHA-256 hashes were not equal.
entries.rootCause: The same JSON manifest was manually duplicated in two Add File hunks without deriving the registered copy from one byte-authoritative assessed proposal, allowing a one-token transcription drift.
entries.prevention: Keep the assessed proposal unchanged, repair only the registered ticket to its exact token, require no-index diff silence plus identical SHA-256 before selection, and bind the resulting exact hash in the selected assessment. Never infer byte identity from visually similar duplicated JSON.

entries.mistake: The first C33M FIX3 MVP-selection patch combined checkpoint, selected-assessment, top-level ticket, disclosure and authorization changes; verification failed on the large historical C33M parent block.
entries.rootCause: The selection edit used a long multi-region replacement whose exact parent-block context included too many independently changing lines, repeating the known distant-anchor patch fragility.
entries.prevention: Confirm the patch was atomic and the state remains on C33M, then apply current ID, selected assessment, top-level ticket and evidence fields as separate exact hunks. Parse and hash-check the state after every structural stage before invoking the MVP gate.

entries.mistake: A split C33M FIX3 minimum-scope patch still failed verification because its context typed Internal_TestING instead of the exact current Internal_Testing token.
entries.rootCause: The smaller hunk was manually transcribed instead of copied literally from the immediately preceding bounded line readback, introducing a case-only context mismatch.
entries.prevention: Treat the failed hunk as zero writes, copy every context line literally from bounded readback, and prefer minimal unique start/end anchors around unchanged arrays. Parse and identity-check before scope execution.

entries.mistake: REG2573 listed the planned C33M FIX3 fixture checker in its gates array before that repository file existed, so the permanent memory gate rejected before implementation.
entries.rootCause: The regression entry conflated a planned prevention owner named by the ticket with an already-existing executable gate required by registry integrity validation.
entries.prevention: Registry gates and evidence reference only existing repository files at registration time. Planned new owners remain in the ticket's newNecessarySharedOwners until created; after qualification, prevention may be strengthened by existing paths without breaking pre-implementation memory.

entries.mistake: The C33M FIX3 pre-implementation sequence invoked check-mvp-delivery-discipline-lock.ps1 with a guessed -TicketId parameter that the gate does not declare.
entries.rootCause: The command reused the scope gate's candidate-specific calling convention without first inspecting the delivery gate's exact parameter block.
entries.prevention: After registration, read the literal declared parameter block and invoke only supported named parameters. Do not infer one gate's interface from another gate's semantics or ticket awareness.

entries.mistake: The PS5 parser command printed a pass but also emitted a Stop=Stop command-not-found error because the outer PS7 host expanded $ErrorActionPreference inside the nested double-quoted command string.
entries.rootCause: The cross-host command boundary used an interpolating outer string for inner PowerShell source, allowing a host-local variable to be substituted before powershell.exe parsed it.
entries.prevention: Do not count the ambiguous PS5 result. Pass the inner command as a literal single-quoted outer string, set fail-fast inside that host, require exact files=2, zero parse errors and exit zero with no error stream before behavioral execution.

entries.mistake: The first candidate-binding patch used the focused manifest hash as the expected existing C33M FIX2 qualification evidence hash, so apply_patch could not verify the exact context.
entries.rootCause: Two valid 64-character hashes from the continuation summary were conflated instead of copying the existing evidenceSha literal from the bounded candidate-gate readback.
entries.prevention: Treat the failed patch as zero writes, copy the literal existing FIX2 evidence hash from the current gate, and add the new FIX3 assessment and live gate in separate hunks. Verify every bound file's hash after the patch before source execution.

entries.mistake: The visible C33M founder-launch command called Start-Process successfully, then its status projection used launcherVisible=true instead of launcherVisible=$true and failed after the process-launch boundary.
entries.rootCause: The reporting object used a JSON-style boolean literal in PowerShell and placed that fallible reporting expression after the external process mutation in the same command.
entries.prevention: Infer no launcher or build result, tell the founder not to enter values, register before inspection, locate only the exact launcher process by sanitized command-line path, terminate it if still running, and prove build state/count/transient cleanup before resealing. Future launch validates its status object before Start-Process and uses $true.

entries.mistake: The sanitized launcher-process cleanup searched pwsh.exe command lines for the launcher filename, but that literal also appeared in the cleanup shell's own command line, so Stop-Process terminated the diagnostic process and returned exit -1 with no evidence.
entries.rootCause: The process selector did not exclude the current PowerShell PID before mutation and assumed the match needle could not appear in its own invocation source.
entries.prevention: Infer no cleanup result, register before retry, exclude $PID before any Stop-Process call, compute the exact external match set first, stop only those PIDs, then use a separate read-only invocation to prove zero remaining exact launcher processes and unchanged candidate counts without printing command lines.

entries.mistake: The r60.51 public-review bootstrap constructs a newly seeded MemoryJourneyStore on every process start, so a process recreation during protected Social Create, shared-post, Chat or YouTube authentication loses the exact pending destination, cancel route and authentication purpose even though C33G FIX3 qualified those fields as restart-persistent.
entries.rootCause: The Screen 04 safe-boot branch bypassed the existing SharedPreferencesJourneyStore owner, while the qualifying restart tests reused one MemoryJourneyStore instance across sessions and therefore modeled session reconstruction rather than a genuinely fresh application process.
entries.prevention: Permanently retain the built r60.51 artifact at 1/0/0/0 without upload, reuse the existing SharedPreferences journey owner behind a seed-if-empty adapter for public review, persist only bounded non-secret JourneySnapshot fields, and require tests that construct new store and session objects over the same durable preferences before any successor source seal or build authority.

entries.mistake: A sanitized reconciliation command guessed config/uaw-c33m-r60-51-authentication-no-regression-candidate-state.json, which does not exist, after printing a truncated dirty-tree status and before reaching the intended non-secret runtime configuration projection.
entries.rootCause: The command inferred a state filename from the ticket name instead of discovering the repository's actual successor-aab-regression-hard-gate-state-c33m.json owner first.
entries.prevention: Treat the failed command as zero-write non-evidence, discover candidate state owners with rg --files before reading, then project only explicitly named non-secret fields from the exact file. Never widen a corrected read into secret, environment, terminal or command-line inspection.

entries.mistake: The r60.51 candidate compiles MOOLSOCIAL_DEVICE_REVIEW=true and MOOLSOCIAL_YOUTUBE_PUBLIC_REVIEW=true, but main.dart gives device-review mode priority when choosing the passwordless email owner, so the built public-review runtime selects ReviewEmailLinkGateway rather than the qualified FirebaseEmailLinkGateway required for the parent ticket's real passwordless email journey.
entries.rootCause: The broad device-review switch controls both presentation/runtime seeding and authentication gateway selection. The release gate proved define presence and C33J source qualification independently, but did not prove the resolved gateway for the exact combined r60.51 define matrix.
entries.prevention: Permanently retain r60.51 at 1/0/0/0 without upload, keep FIX4 and FIX5 as separately registered repairs, select the Firebase passwordless email gateway whenever its qualified runtime configuration is available in the public-review release matrix, and add exact combined-define source and behavior coverage before any successor seal or build authority.

entries.mistake: A bounded read-only bootstrap audit passed apps/mobile/lib/core/auth to rg even though that path does not exist; rg returned exit failure after also reporting matches from the explicitly listed existing main and journey service files.
entries.rootCause: The search assumed authentication gateway owners lived under a core/auth directory instead of first discovering their exact repository locations.
entries.prevention: Do not count the compound search as gate evidence. Discover owner paths with rg --files, then search only confirmed existing files; retain the direct bounded main.dart read and exact candidate-state projection as the evidence for the combined-mode audit.

entries.mistake: The first C33M FIX4 focused run expected youtubeChannelConnection to restore for the invented /app/social?sub=create&state=youtube-connect route, so the exact-purpose test failed 6 passed and 1 failed even though the durable snapshot contained the stored purpose.
entries.rootCause: The new test did not reuse the existing canonical protected YouTube handoff route /app/creator/youtube-connect. JourneySession intentionally restores the specialized purpose only for that owner and treats other protected routes as general authentication.
entries.prevention: Do not count the failed focused run. Bind the FIX4 test to the existing Screen03 and Social consumer contract: returnLocation /app/creator/youtube-connect, cancelLocation /app/social?sub=videos, then require a genuinely new SharedPreferences store and JourneySession before checking purpose and cancellation.

entries.mistake: The first combined REG2587 and YouTube test-correction apply_patch could not verify the expected formatted test context and made zero writes.
entries.rootCause: The correction patch was composed from the pre-format source shape instead of copying the exact bounded post-format readback before editing.
entries.prevention: Treat the failed patch as atomic zero-write non-evidence, register both the original failed-test error and this patch error, then apply the registry append and the minimal test substitutions as separate literal hunks copied from current bounded readback.

entries.mistake: The corrected FIX4 retry command used apps/mobile as its working directory but invoked scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 as if it were at the repository root, so pwsh exited 64 before Dart format or Flutter test ran.
entries.rootCause: One compound command mixed repository-root and mobile-package relative paths without resolving each path against its actual working directory.
entries.prevention: Count no test result from the failed command. Run repository gates from the repository root, then run format and Flutter tests from apps/mobile in a separate fail-fast command; do not mix path bases in one evidence-producing invocation.

entries.mistake: The C33J Screen03 passwordless email native-parity gate accepts only the original C33J parent, FIX1 or FIX2 as the active MVP ticket, so it rejects the lawfully selected C33M FIX4 successor even though the affected Flutter batch passes all email behavior and the source contract is unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The gate encoded a bounded three-ticket lifecycle instead of validating exact qualified C33J parent/FIX1/FIX2 evidence and then accepting the active ticket through the generic MVP scope gate.
entries.prevention: Do not count the failed C33J gate replay and do not weaken its source assertions. Select a separate gate-only FIX6 ticket, preserve the three historical branches, add exact qualified-evidence-bound generic successor replay with negative fixtures, qualify in PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell, then reselect and complete FIX4 before FIX5 or any successor release action.

entries.mistake: The bounded C33J gate trace appended rg path arguments containing config/uaw-c33m*, scripts/check-uaw-c33m* and docs/quality/UAW-C33M*, which Windows rejected as invalid filenames after the exact gate source had already been read.
entries.rootCause: The command used shell-style wildcard path arguments on Windows instead of discovering files or using rg --glob filters beneath existing directories.
entries.prevention: Treat the wildcard search as non-evidence. Use rg --files piped to rg for discovery or pass existing directories with --glob filters; retain only the exact successfully read C33J gate source when preparing the compatibility ticket.

entries.mistake: Source inspection after the C33J parent replay failure proved that the C33J FIX1 gate accepts only FIX1 or FIX2 and the FIX2 gate accepts only active FIX2, so both would reject C33M FIX4 and later lawful successors after the parent gate is repaired.
entries.rootCause: Each child prevention gate validates its source behavior inside a ticket-local selection lifecycle and lacks a generic successor branch bound to the exact qualified parent, FIX1 and FIX2 ticket hashes, states and evidence.
entries.prevention: Repair the existing C33J parent, FIX1 and FIX2 gates as one gate-only FIX6 lifecycle ticket. Preserve every historical branch and behavioral assertion, require current/ticket/selected identity plus selected manifest hash and exact prior C33J qualification evidence, add fail-closed negative fixtures, and pass both PowerShell hosts before FIX4 qualification resumes.

entries.mistake: The first C33M FIX6 ticket and selected assessment used the invented implementation disposition gate_selection_policy_repair, so the delivery discipline lock rejected before any C33J gate source mutation.
entries.rootCause: The ticket described the work semantically instead of first reading the delivery gate's closed implementationDisposition vocabulary.
entries.prevention: Preserve the rejected scope-gate result as non-qualification evidence, use only the declared reuse, configuration, thin_policy_adapter, test_only_acceptance or new_necessary_work values, recompute the changed ticket hash, update the selected assessment binding, then rerun memory, delivery and scope gates before implementation.

entries.mistake: The first combined C33J FIX2 generic-successor patch expected an outdated gate summary string, so apply_patch could not verify its final hunk and made zero writes to the FIX2 gate.
entries.rootCause: The multi-hunk edit reused an inferred output line rather than copying the exact current manifestFilters summary from bounded readback.
entries.prevention: Treat the failed patch as atomic zero-write non-evidence, preserve the already successful parent and FIX1 edits, then add the FIX2 function, live binding replacement and output mode in separate minimal hunks copied from the current file before parsing or execution.

entries.mistake: The C33K Firebase passwordless email live-readiness gate requires the active MVP ticket to equal the historical C33K ticket, so Postwrite replay rejects reselected C33M FIX4 before evaluating the already-qualified sanitized provider, domain, action-count and privacy facts.
entries.rootCause: The gate binds its immutable readiness state to an active historical selection instead of binding the exact qualified C33K ticket hash, implementation state and retained evidence for later lawful successors.
entries.prevention: Invalidate the pre-cycle FIX4 source seal, select one gate-only FIX7 ticket, preserve every Prewrite/Postwrite fact and closed action assertion, add exact qualified-C33K generic successor binding with negative fixtures, pass both PowerShell hosts, reselect FIX4, replay Postwrite, then create a fresh source seal before cycle 1.

entries.mistake: After the complete FIX4 cycle-01 evidence was read, a bookkeeping command guessed docs/quality/REGRESSION_TESTING_AND_PERMANENT_MEMORY.md as the regression registry owner; Get-FileHash reported that the file does not exist, so no registry hash was produced.
entries.rootCause: The command used a recalled descriptive filename instead of resolving the canonical registry owner from the repository before hashing it.
entries.prevention: Count the path lookup as zero hash evidence, register it before retry, discover the canonical owner with bounded rg --files output, hash config/codex-development-regression-registry.json only after readback, invalidate the 2566 source seal because this registry correction changes source, then create a fresh 2567 seal and run two independent cycles against it.

entries.mistake: The pre-cycle parameter inventory included the unverified guessed path scripts/check-approved-ui-reference-and-production-locks.ps1; Test-Path reported it missing and the checker was not invoked.
entries.rootCause: The inventory reconstructed a descriptive gate label from the retained log instead of resolving the checker filename through rg --files first.
entries.prevention: Register the missing-path lookup before any retry, discover the exact approved-reference checker only from bounded rg --files output, invalidate the 2567 pre-cycle seal, and create a fresh registry-bound seal only after every static checker path is literal and verified.

entries.mistake: The first registry-2568 Cycle 1 Flutter invocation passed an absolute focused-manifest path to a runner that joins -Manifest to RepositoryRoot, producing a duplicated root path and failing before any Flutter process started.
entries.rootCause: The runner's parameter contract was inferred from the parameter name instead of reading its manifest path resolution before invocation.
entries.prevention: Count the failed invocation as zero Flutter evidence, retain its rejection log, register it before retry, pass artifacts/quality/.../focused-test-manifest-c33m-fix4.txt as the verified repository-relative value, invalidate the 2568 seal, and run two complete cycles only after a fresh registry-bound seal.

entries.mistake: REG2598 initially referenced the intended failed Flutter Tee log before verifying that the file existed; the runner's terminating error reached the task output but the pipeline did not retain the target log, so the regression-memory gate rejected the missing evidence path.
entries.rootCause: The registration assumed Tee-Object had persisted output from a terminating upstream error instead of checking the literal evidence path before adding it to the registry.
entries.prevention: Retain the exact bounded rejection output at the intended repository evidence path, verify every new gate and evidence path literally exists before rerunning the memory gate, count no Flutter tests, and create the next source seal only after the corrected registry passes.

entries.mistake: The queued C33M FIX5 ticket uses selection_policy_repair in robustnessAndReuseAssessment.implementationDisposition even though the delivery discipline gate accepts only reuse, configuration, thin_policy_adapter, test_only_acceptance or new_necessary_work.
entries.rootCause: The queued ticket described the intended gateway-selection correction semantically instead of binding it to the delivery lock's closed disposition vocabulary before future selection.
entries.prevention: Do not select the existing ticket bytes or count their prior SHA as an executable manifest. Replace only the unsupported disposition with thin_policy_adapter, open only founder-authorized runtime and test/gate source authority, recompute the ticket SHA, preserve FIX4 as a qualified prior assessment, then require delivery and scope gates to pass before any FIX5 runtime mutation.

entries.mistake: The selected FIX5 ticket declared apps/mobile/lib/core/auth/firebase_email_link_gateway.dart as a shared implementation owner, but the literal repository path does not exist and the bounded source lookup reported that missing path.
entries.rootCause: The queued robustness inventory inferred a conventional dedicated gateway filename instead of binding the actual existing class location from the repository.
entries.prevention: Do not mutate runtime under the stale ticket hash. Resolve the FirebaseEmailLinkGateway definition from rg --files plus bounded content search, replace the nonexistent shared-owner path in the ticket and selected assessment, recompute and rebind the ticket SHA, then rerun memory, delivery and scope gates before implementation.

entries.mistake: The qualified C33M FIX4 prevention gate invokes the MVP scope gate with CandidateId fixed to the historical FIX4 ticket, so source inspection proves it cannot replay under selected FIX5 or a later lawful successor even when the exact qualified FIX4 assessment and evidence are preserved.
entries.rootCause: FIX4 source behavior was qualified inside an active-ticket-only selection lifecycle and its gate did not include the generic qualified-successor binding required after the next repair ticket is selected.
entries.prevention: Do not invoke or count the known active-ticket rejection under FIX5. Select a gate-only FIX8 ticket, preserve the FIX4-active branch, add exact current/top/selected successor identity and selected-manifest binding plus the qualified FIX4 ticket hash, assessment state and evidence, add fail-closed fixtures, qualify both PowerShell hosts, then reselect FIX5 before its affected tests and two source cycles.

entries.mistake: The scope-side owner correction for REG2601 used only the repeated nonexistent path as context, so apply_patch changed an earlier historical assessment and left the active FIX5 selected assessment's shared owner unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The patch target was not anchored to the surrounding ticketId even though the same stale path appeared in multiple retained assessments.
entries.prevention: Treat the active FIX5 owner correction as incomplete, inspect every remaining literal occurrence, preserve the semantically valid earlier correction, and replace each remaining nonexistent owner only through a hunk anchored to its exact enclosing ticketId before computing or selecting another ticket hash.

entries.mistake: The first source-only C33N composition gate invoked the inherited prevention chain as one batch before individually proving every direct predecessor invocation accepted the newly selected C33N lifecycle; the run stopped when one inherited call reached the MVP scope gate with a historical candidate identifier.
entries.rootCause: The C33N composition reused the C33M direct predecessor-call list and appended the later generic-successor gates, but did not first isolate which historical behavioral gate must be reached through its qualified compatibility owner under a new selected candidate.
entries.prevention: Count no result from the stopped run. Execute each inherited gate independently under selected C33N, identify the exact stale composition edge, then invoke only the already-qualified generic successor owner or register and qualify a separate gate-lifecycle repair before retrying the C33N source gate.

entries.mistake: The qualified C33M FIX5 prevention gate invokes the MVP scope gate with CandidateId fixed to the historical FIX5 ticket, so it cannot replay under selected C33N even when the exact qualified FIX5 assessment and evidence are preserved.
entries.rootCause: FIX5 product behavior was qualified inside an active-ticket-only selection lifecycle and its gate did not include the generic evidence-bound successor binding already required for other predecessor gates.
entries.prevention: Select gate-only C33N FIX1, preserve the FIX5-active branch, add exact current/top/selected successor identity and selected-manifest binding plus qualified FIX5 ticket hash, assessment state and evidence, add fail-closed fixtures, qualify both PowerShell hosts, then reselect C33N before any source seal or cycle.

entries.mistake: REG2605 listed the planned C33N FIX1 checker in its gates array before the checker existed, so the regression-memory gate rejected the missing repository path.
entries.rootCause: The finding entry was written as the final repair contract instead of separating durable existing evidence from a future owner that had not yet been created.
entries.prevention: Count no memory result, create the selected ticket's checker, verify every REG2605 and REG2606 repository path exists literally, and only then rerun the regression-memory gate.

entries.mistake: The first corrected C33N source-gate process completed, but orchestration emitted only the initially empty command output and did not retain the returned session identifier or final exit status, so the result cannot be counted.
entries.rootCause: The command wrapper assumed a long-running exec_command result would contain final output instead of treating its session identifier as mandatory evidence that must be polled to terminal completion.
entries.prevention: Count no result from the unretained run. On retry, retain any returned session identifier, poll that exact session until an exit code is returned, preserve sanitized terminal output and exit status, and never start a duplicate while the retained session is active.

entries.mistake: A bounded read-only C33N scope-assessment inspection piped directly after an ungrouped foreach statement, so PowerShell rejected the command at parse time with an empty-pipe error and returned no assessment data.
entries.rootCause: The one-line inspection combined a language statement and pipeline as though foreach were a pipeline expression instead of collecting its output explicitly.
entries.prevention: Count no result from the parse failure. Collect foreach output in an explicit array variable and pipe only that variable to formatting before relying on any scope-state readback.

entries.mistake: The prepared C33N focused manifest contained 73 intended test paths plus a trailing blank line, so raw evidence counted 74 records while the authoritative runner would filter and execute 73 files.
entries.rootCause: The mechanical manifest copy preserved an additional empty record without reconciling raw and nonblank file-count semantics before reporting the focused manifest count.
entries.prevention: Start and count no cycle with the ambiguous manifest. Remove the blank record before sealing and require the raw nonblank count, declared focused count and authoritative runner manifest count all equal 73.

entries.mistake: The first C33N cycle-1 static composition reused the immutable manifest writer as a comparator, passed an unsupported delivery-gate parameter, guessed a nonexistent UI-lock checker path, then returned parent exit zero because later native child successes masked the earlier nonzero exits.
entries.rootCause: The composed orchestration copied semantic steps from retained logs without first reading each current checker interface and relied on ErrorActionPreference to stop native child processes even though their nonzero exit codes require immediate explicit assertions.
entries.prevention: Count no static or cycle result. Read every checker path and parameter contract literally, use a read-only current-owner hash comparison for the immutable manifest, and assert LASTEXITCODE immediately after every native child before any later command can run or mask failure.

entries.mistake: After r60.52 postbuild qualification, a read-only Internal Testing workflow lookup passed the unproved nonexistent docs/release directory to two rg invocations; later valid-root results did not make those path failures successful.
entries.rootCause: The postbuild discovery command assumed a conventional release-document directory instead of inventorying and proving literal repository roots before composing bounded searches, and it allowed later commands to mask earlier native search errors.
entries.prevention: Register the failure before any Play action, reject r60.52 at 1/0/0/0 because the registry changed after its seal, never upload or reuse its AAB, and for a separately authorized successor inventory roots first then assert every native search exit immediately before relying on results.

entries.mistake: The first r60.52 rejection persistence attempt combined four files in one patch and used handoff context whose wrapping did not exactly match the live file, so apply_patch rejected the complete patch before applying any state transition.
entries.rootCause: The compound patch relied on remembered handoff line wrapping instead of reading and anchoring the exact live tail, unnecessarily coupling otherwise independent rejection-state files to one fragile hunk.
entries.prevention: Count no state transition from the failed patch. Read exact live anchors, then apply the rejection document, detailed state, aggregate state and handoff as separate bounded patches with readback after each before relying on the rejection state.

entries.mistake: During C33O selection, a read-only command named a nonexistent check-mvp-robust-delivery-lock.ps1 path and therefore stopped before the remaining intended gate-interface reads.
entries.rootCause: The command used a remembered semantic checker name instead of the literal repository-inventoried check-mvp-delivery-discipline-lock.ps1 owner.
entries.prevention: Count no result from the failed read. Before composing C33O gates, use only literal paths returned by a bounded pre-seal repository inventory and assert every native checker exit immediately; after the source seal, prohibit repository discovery entirely.

entries.mistake: The first C33O source-composition gate searched for a single-line Testing > Internal testing runbook marker even though the Markdown source wraps between Internal and testing, so the gate stopped before source qualification.
entries.rootCause: The new checker bound semantic prose with a literal single-line Contains call instead of allowing Markdown whitespace while preserving the exact words and order.
entries.prevention: Count no result from the failed C33O source gate. Match the exact Internal Testing navigation words with whitespace-tolerant regular expression semantics, retain the other fail-closed runbook markers, and rerun before source sealing.

entries.mistake: The C33O candidate-gate mechanical copy changed the inherited qualified C33N FIX1 checker invocation to a nonexistent C33O FIX1 path, so the second source-composition gate stopped before qualification.
entries.rootCause: The broad candidate-name substitution was only partially audited: the assessment identity was restored, but a separate qualified-prevention checker path retained the unintended C33O replacement.
entries.prevention: Count no result from the failed gate. Audit every C33O lifecycle owner for C33O FIX1, priorC33OFix1 and live_C33O_reselection forms, restore the sole inherited path to the qualified C33N FIX1 owner, parse all owners and rerun before sealing.

entries.mistake: The C33O read-only Play precheck clicked the sole generic button on an unauthenticated developer-selector page without a semantic developer-account label; it navigated to accounts.google.com rather than a proved MoolSocial app route.
entries.rootCause: A control count was treated as unique navigation evidence even though the browser had not proved a signed-in Play Console session or a semantically named developer-account control.
entries.prevention: Count no live upload-workflow qualification. Never click a Play selector control by role/count alone; require founder-visible Google sign-in and any account selection, then resume only from semantic MoolSocial and Internal testing evidence without inspecting account identifiers, credentials or session stores.

entries.mistake: After proving the signed-in MoolSocial dashboard, the C33O browser check clicked the visible Internal testing child SPAN rather than its inspected enclosing anchor control; the click timed out and navigation did not occur.
entries.rootCause: The interaction used the exact text locator after structural inspection had already shown that actionable button semantics belonged to the parent anchor, not the child span.
entries.prevention: Count no Internal Testing route proof from the timeout and never repeat the child-span click. Target the already-inspected enclosing anchor exactly once, then prove the sanitized Internal Testing route and visible heading before source sealing.

entries.mistake: After REG2617, the exact unique visible enabled parent anchor with button semantics for Internal testing also timed out under semantic locator click and the page did not navigate.
entries.rootCause: The Play Console navigation control is visible and structurally correct but is not actionable through the current semantic locator click transport, so repeating selector clicks cannot establish route proof.
entries.prevention: Count no route proof and stop locator-click retries. Derive one coordinate from the exact anchor's read-only bounding rectangle, perform one visible coordinate click, then verify sanitized route shape and heading without reading href, account ID, app ID, credentials or session data.

entries.mistake: The one CUA coordinate derived from the Internal Testing anchor's DOM rectangle expanded the nearby Testing section and left the dashboard active because external Chrome content and control coordinates were offset.
entries.rootCause: DOM viewport coordinates were assumed to map directly to the external Chrome CUA surface even though browser chrome offsets changed the effective click location.
entries.prevention: Count no route proof and prohibit further DOM-rectangle coordinate actions. Use one keyboard activation on the exact inspected Internal Testing anchor; if it fails, stop for founder navigation instead of trying another automation surface.

entries.mistake: The final permitted keyboard Enter activation on the exact unique visible Internal Testing anchor timed out and left the MoolSocial dashboard unchanged.
entries.rootCause: The current external Chrome control transport cannot activate this Play Console anchor through semantic click, parent click or keyboard press, even though the control is visible and enabled.
entries.prevention: Count no route proof and stop all Codex browser-control retries. Leave the signed-in MoolSocial dashboard open with Testing expanded; require the founder to click Internal testing, then perform read-only route and heading verification only.

entries.mistake: The first C33O cycle-2 orchestration proved the sealed source manifest unchanged, then stopped before every gate and test because its shared logger combined Tee-Object -LiteralPath with -Append, which PowerShell cannot resolve as a parameter set.
entries.rootCause: The new evidence wrapper was composed after the C33O source seal without a harmless parameter-binding preflight, and it substituted LiteralPath for the previously qualified FilePath form even though Append is not supported by that parameter set.
entries.prevention: Count no C33O cycle 2, preserve the partial log, reject C33O at 0/0/0/0, and select an exact successor. Before the successor seal, preflight its logger with non-source temporary evidence, use Tee-Object -FilePath for append semantics, retain fresh per-cycle paths and assert every child exit immediately.

entries.mistake: The first C33P selected-assessment apply-patch hunk prefixed an already prefixed first added line, leaving one literal plus character in mvp-scope-gate-state.json and causing immediate JSON parsing to fail.
entries.rootCause: The dynamic patch generator mixed a block that already contained its first diff marker with a second per-line prefix pass instead of producing exactly one marker for every added line.
entries.prevention: Count no selection result, remove only the proved extra character, parse the complete scope JSON before any gate, and require future dynamic patch blocks to add exactly one patch marker per line before C33P is sealed.

entries.mistake: The first pre-seal C33P delivery-discipline run found that the current and selected assessment named C33P while the scope state's separate top-level ticket.id still named C33O.
entries.rootCause: Successor selection updated the checkpoint current identity, assessment and provider projection but omitted the independent top-level ticket projection consumed as the active ticket by the delivery gate.
entries.prevention: Count no delivery result, replace the complete top-level ticket projection from the exact selected C33P ticket, parse and read back current top-level selected identities and manifest hash together, then rerun before source sealing.

entries.mistake: The first C33P source-composition gate expected MOOLSOCIAL-C33P-R60-53 in its generic-wrapper literal even though the selected state and wrapper correctly use R60-54.
entries.rootCause: The mechanical successor transformation replaced lowercase r60-53 forms but missed the uppercase R60-53 segment inside the wrapper contract literal.
entries.prevention: Count no source-gate result, replace the sole stale contract needle, audit every bounded C33P lifecycle owner for old candidate version and code forms, parse all PowerShell owners, then rerun before sealing.

entries.mistake: The first REG2624 correction patch supplied a contract-identity substring instead of an exact complete line, so apply-patch rejected the first file and changed nothing.
entries.rootCause: The mechanical multi-file patch assumed apply-patch performs substring replacement rather than requiring exact line context for each hunk.
entries.prevention: Count no patch result, read exact affected lines, apply one exact full-line hunk per file with readback, then parse all PowerShell owners and repeat the stale-identity audit before any source-gate retry.

entries.mistake: C33P Cycle 1 passed its opening manifest and dual-host static gates, then the authoritative Flutter runner received an absolute focused-manifest path and joined it to RepositoryRoot, producing a nonexistent doubled path before any test executed.
entries.rootCause: The cycle orchestration converted the evidence directory to an absolute path and reused that value for a runner parameter whose literal interface requires a repository-relative manifest path.
entries.prevention: Retain the partial logs, count no C33P cycle, reject C33P at 0/0/0/0, and require an exact successor to preflight the runner interface then pass the focused manifest repository-relative before completing two fresh cycles.

entries.mistake: After two clean C33Q cycles, lifecycle state exposed later founder build upload OPPO and email authorities before the required final source-phase replay, so the source gate rejected immediately.
entries.rootCause: The state transition combined cycle-result persistence and later phase-authority exposure instead of preserving the gate-required intermediate two-cycles-complete authorities-held state.
entries.prevention: Reject C33Q at 0/0/0/0. For an exact successor, first persist only two-cycle results with all later authorities held, pass final source gates in both PowerShell hosts, then expose phase-gated founder and build authorities and run build gates.

entries.mistake: Codex opened the C33R founder launcher with Start-Process from its noninteractive codex.exe host and reported processStarted=true, but the persistent pwsh child had no visible window host, so the founder could not reach the three hidden prompts.
entries.rootCause: Process creation success was treated as visible interactive-console proof even though the launched pwsh remained parented to codex.exe with MainWindowHandle zero and no user-visible terminal.
entries.prevention: Reject C33R at 0/0/0/0, preserve the proved absence of hidden inputs, transients, AAB and build children, and require an exact successor. Never open its founder launcher from Codex. After all successor gates pass, give the founder one literal pwsh command to paste into an already visible PowerShell window so the interactive console is founder-owned and directly observable before any secret entry.

entries.mistake: A read-only C33R required-file inventory attempted to pipe directly from a foreach statement and PowerShell rejected the empty pipeline element before reading any file.
entries.rootCause: The inventory repeated the already registered Windows PowerShell foreach-direct-pipeline syntax class instead of emitting objects directly or wrapping the foreach expression in parentheses.
entries.prevention: Count no inventory result. Use direct literal Get-Content reads for known required owners and use a parenthesized collection only if a later inventory pipeline is necessary; parse any composed PowerShell before execution.

entries.mistake: A read-only comparison requested a guessed C33Q rejection filename that does not exist before the repository search identified the actual retained file.
entries.rootCause: The rejection document name was inferred from a narrative label instead of selected from the repository's exact filename inventory.
entries.prevention: Count no result from a guessed path. Use rg --files with the exact candidate/version tokens before reading any retained rejection or qualification document, then open only the returned literal path.

entries.mistake: The first C33S visible-console static assertion embedded C-style backslash-escaped double quotes inside a PowerShell double-quoted string, and the PowerShell parser rejected the new gate before any gate execution.
entries.rootCause: JavaScript patch-string escaping was confused with PowerShell source escaping; PowerShell does not use a backslash to escape a double quote.
entries.prevention: Count no gate result. Replace the assertion needle with one exact single-quoted PowerShell literal containing the launcher's double quotes unchanged, then parse the gate and all bounded lifecycle owners before any source seal.

entries.mistake: The first C33S source manifest was hand-composed from the prior manifest plus two assumed new owners, and the authoritative C30V compare rejected its bytes before any source cycle.
entries.rootCause: The hand composer bypassed the authoritative C30V generator and serialized rows with LF, while the repository owner emits Environment.NewLine. A matching path/hash set is still a byte mismatch under the immutable manifest contract.
entries.prevention: Retain the invalid pre-seal manifest as failure evidence and count no source seal or cycle. After registration, use scripts/new-c30v-source-manifest.ps1 -OutputPath as the only inventory and byte-serialization owner for the new registry-bound manifest, then verify it with -ComparePath before any C33S source gate.

entries.mistake: After the C33S source manifest was sealed, a combined gate command tested LASTEXITCODE immediately after a PowerShell script. The value was null or stale, so the command exited after the regression-memory gate and never invoked the delivery, scope or C33S source gates.
entries.rootCause: Native-process LASTEXITCODE semantics were incorrectly applied to an in-process PowerShell script instead of relying on terminating errors and explicit completion markers.
entries.prevention: Count no combined-gate result, reject C33S at 0/0/0/0 because registration changes its post-seal registry, and require an exact successor. Invoke each PowerShell script in a separate command or rely on ErrorActionPreference Stop; inspect LASTEXITCODE only immediately after native executables.

entries.mistake: The founder ran the C33T launcher in the approved visible PowerShell console from C:\WINDOWS\system32. Its candidate gate passed a repository-relative MVP state path to the MVP scope gate, which resolved that path against the caller working directory and rejected it as outside the production repository before any hidden prompt.
entries.rootCause: scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate-state.ps1 normalized StatePath with GetFullPath directly. For a relative StatePath, GetFullPath uses the process current directory rather than the explicit RepositoryRoot that already owns the path boundary.
entries.prevention: Reject C33T at 0/0/0/0 and require an exact successor. Resolve relative StatePath values by joining them to the normalized RepositoryRoot before GetFullPath, retain absolute-path boundary rejection, and prove both PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell invocation from C:\WINDOWS\system32 before any successor seal or founder prompt.

entries.mistake: The pre-launch sanitized reconciliation checked mobile/build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab and returned absent, while the repository's real Flutter owner is apps/mobile and still retained the rejected C33N r60.52 AAB there.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic path was typed from an assumed repository layout instead of being taken from the candidate build owner or verified against the repository's exact apps/mobile structure.
entries.prevention: Never infer artifact absence from the shortened mobile path. Use the exact apps/mobile/build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab owner and bind any present file by SHA and bytes to retained candidate state; a historical artifact never implies a current build count or reusable authority.

entries.mistake: The first C33U wrapper mapping patch inserted a new contract exclusion into the middle of the existing first comparison and left a duplicated '[string]$state.contractId -cne' operand, producing a malformed condition before any wrapper execution.
entries.rootCause: The patch hunk matched only the prior contract literal instead of replacing the complete first comparison, so the existing comparison prefix was retained alongside the new complete comparisons.
entries.prevention: Count no wrapper result and no source seal. Read back the complete condition, replace the duplicated lines as one exact hunk, parse the wrapper in PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell, and run its static candidate binding through the C33U gate before qualification.

entries.mistake: A nested PowerShell 7 parser command emitted an interpolation error for $errors and then printed a pass marker, so the composed PowerShell 7 result was internally contradictory and cannot count as a parser pass.
entries.rootCause: The outer Windows PowerShell command and inner pwsh command mixed escaped variables and a nested subexpression inside a double-quoted throw message, allowing the wrong host to evaluate part of the expression.
entries.prevention: Count only the Windows PowerShell parser pass. Invoke PowerShell 7 with one literal single-quoted command per file and a constant failure message, require clean output and native exit zero, and never accept a pass marker accompanied by any error record.

entries.mistake: After r60.59 was activated on Internal Testing, a raw read of an older retained Play evidence JSON exposed fields containing a private account identifier and private tester link before the intended safe schema comparison.
entries.rootCause: The historical evidence comparison opened the complete prior JSON instead of projecting an explicit allowlist of non-private release fields, despite the repository privacy boundary prohibiting access to private account identifiers and private links.
entries.prevention: Never raw-read historical Play evidence. Before any comparison, inventory property names without values and project only an explicit allowlist of package, track, version, artifact, count and disposition fields; exclude all account, tester, identity, email and link properties. Reject C33U at 1/1/0/0 before OPPO and require an exact successor.

entries.mistake: The first unsealed C33V clone used a broad 2608-to-2609 replacement after changing the version code, which contaminated version and date literals from 202608 to 202609.
entries.rootCause: Registry entry-count digits were treated as a globally replaceable substring even though the same digits are embedded in version codes and dates.
entries.prevention: Count no C33V gate result. Correct exact 202609 contamination to 202608, then update registry count and SHA only through named JSON fields and exact registry assertion literals. Parse and read back every owner before source-manifest generation.

entries.mistake: The first C33V Windows PowerShell parser-validation command placed its script body in a double-quoted argument launched from PowerShell 7. The outer host expanded the inner variables, so Windows PowerShell received a malformed foreach statement and parsed none of the candidate files.
entries.rootCause: The validation repeated the cross-host interpolation class already registered in REG-20260816-2637 instead of using a literal command body owned entirely by the target host.
entries.prevention: Count no Windows PowerShell parser result. Retry only with a single-quoted literal command body passed directly to Windows PowerShell, require one clean PARSE_OK marker per bounded file and no error records, and retain the independent PowerShell 7 parser result.

entries.mistake: The first read-only attempt to inspect recent regression entries assumed config/first-attempt-regression-tests.json, which does not exist, and therefore returned no registry entries.
entries.rootCause: The registry filename was recalled from memory instead of discovered from the repository before the read.
entries.prevention: Count no registry inspection result. Discover the exact repository-owned registry path with rg --files, then read only config/codex-development-regression-registry.json and verify its parsed entry count before using any registry metadata.

entries.mistake: The first C33V source-phase gate rejected the unsealed state because authority.founderHiddenInputEntryAuthorized was true while source qualification was still incomplete.
entries.rootCause: The C33U-to-C33V state clone reset build, upload, install and founder build approval authorities but retained the later qualified-state hidden-input authorization.
entries.prevention: Count no source-gate pass and no source seal. Set founderHiddenInputEntryAuthorized false in the unqualified C33V state, bind the new registry count and SHA through named fields, then rerun the complete source gate before manifest generation. Expose hidden-input authority only after two cycles and final dual-host source replay.

entries.mistake: After correcting hidden-input authority, the C33V source gate reached the shared MVP scope gate and was rejected because config/mvp-scope-gate-state.json still selected the C33U r60.59 ticket.
entries.rootCause: The candidate-specific C33V lifecycle owners were cloned and corrected, but the shared MVP scope selection and robustness/reuse checkpoint were not reselected from C33U to C33V before the first source-gate attempt.
entries.prevention: Count no source-gate pass and no source seal. Reselect the shared MVP scope state and pre-ticket reuse checkpoint to the exact C33V ticket, ticket hash, founder disclosure and authorization evidence through named fields; retain C33U as prior qualified/rejected evidence; then validate the scope gate from C:\WINDOWS\system32 in both PowerShell hosts before source-manifest generation.

entries.mistake: After the C33V source gate exceeded the command yield window, the first sanitized Win32_Process count searched for the target script text but did not exclude the querying PowerShell process, whose own command line contained the same text.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic repeated the self-matching process-query class already prohibited by REG2582 instead of excluding the current process ID before counting exact source-gate processes.
entries.prevention: Treat the count as invalid and do not infer completion or start a duplicate. Exclude the current PowerShell PID inside the same query, output only the sanitized count, wait for zero, then rerun the source gate with a retained unified-exec session and completion marker. Count no source-gate pass from the lost session.

entries.mistake: C33V sealed its source manifest after dual-host source gates passed, but before the exact full-cycle command sequence, runner parameter contract and raw evidence-retention owners had been completely inventoried and verified.
entries.rootCause: Pre-seal review covered candidate lifecycle owners, browser workflow, source gate and manifests but deferred the retained C33U cycle-command reconstruction until after the C33V source seal, contrary to the candidate runbook's no post-seal discovery rule.
entries.prevention: Reject C33V at 0/0/0/0 before cycle 1 and require an exact successor. Before the successor source seal, read the authoritative Flutter runner parameter contract and retained prior cycle command/evidence format, create one predeclared cycle orchestration owner that writes only sanitized logs and summaries, parse and dry-validate it, and include that owner in the manifest. Never guess a parameter or discover commands after sealing.

entries.mistake: The first C33W stale-identity audit passed docs/quality/UAW-C33W-*.md as a positional rg path on Windows, where the wildcard was treated as an invalid literal path and the document portion of the audit did not run.
entries.rootCause: A shell-glob assumption was used with rg's Windows path handling instead of discovering files with rg --files or supplying explicit paths.
entries.prevention: Count no document-audit result. Use rg --files with a filename filter or pass every exact C33W document path explicitly; complete identity and historical-label readback before any source seal.

entries.mistake: The first C33W pre-seal source gate rejected the newly added cycle owner because at least one static assertion needle did not exactly match the parsed cycle-runner source text.
entries.rootCause: The gate needle set was authored from intended source spelling without an exact post-patch readback of each literal against the completed cycle owner.
entries.prevention: Count no source-gate pass. Evaluate only the boolean presence of each bounded non-secret needle, identify the missing label without dumping source, correct the exact static assertion, parse both owners in both PowerShell hosts and rerun before manifest generation.

entries.mistake: After both C33W cycles passed, the final source gate rejected the candidate because its focused manifest file hash differed from the inherited hash stored in state and aggregate.
entries.rootCause: The C33W focused manifest was recreated through apply_patch, which normalized its line-ending bytes, while the candidate state retained C33V's byte hash without an exact pre-seal file-hash readback.
entries.prevention: Reject C33W before build at 0/0/0/0. Preserve both passing cycle summaries as non-promotable evidence. For the exact successor, verify 73 nonblank repository-relative entries, bind the actual focused-manifest byte hash into state and aggregate before source-manifest generation, run the candidate source gate at cycles 0 in both hosts, and re-run two fresh cycles; never inherit an evidence-file hash after recreating its bytes.

entries.mistake: After C33X sealed its 1,273-file source manifest, one compound apply_patch attempted to bind the new manifest hash and file count into both state and aggregate, but the aggregate has no fileCount field and the patch context failed.
entries.rootCause: The post-generation lifecycle mutation assumed that state and aggregate used identical sourceQualification field layouts instead of reading back each exact JSON context before composing the patch.
entries.prevention: Reject C33X before cycle 1 and build at 0/0/0/0 even though apply_patch was atomic and changed neither file. For the exact successor, inventory state and aggregate manifest-binding schemas before sealing, include an explicit file-count field in both before pre-seal gates, and after manifest generation apply and verify one exact file at a time before any cycle starts.

entries.mistake: The first C33Y ticket correction patch expected the cloned uppercase candidate ID to contain R60-63, but the mechanical clone transformed lowercase r60-62 only and left uppercase R60-62 in ticketId and candidateId; patch verification failed before sealing.
entries.rootCause: The clone replacement set was case-sensitive and its post-clone identity audit inspected version fields but did not read back every uppercase candidate-ID occurrence before the first correction patch.
entries.prevention: Count no ticket correction or gate pass. Before retry, read every C33Y ticket and owner identity occurrence, replace uppercase R60-62 with R60-63 explicitly, then verify exact ticketId, candidateId, filenames, version name/code and zero current C33X identity leakage before computing the ticket hash or running a gate.

entries.mistake: After C33Y successfully bound its sealed source manifest into state and aggregate, exact readback showed that the sealed source gate's cycles-equals-zero branch still required manifestSha256 to be null and fileCount to be zero, while the cycle runner requires those same fields populated before cycle 1.
entries.rootCause: The pre-seal schema assertion conflated two distinct cycles-zero lifecycle stages: composition before manifest generation and sealed preparation after manifest binding but before the first cycle.
entries.prevention: Reject C33Y before cycle 1 and build at 0/0/0/0 without executing the guaranteed-failing runner. For the exact successor, model separate preseal_composition and postseal_manifest_bound_precycle states in the source gate before sealing; require null/zero manifest bindings only in composition, require exact populated bindings in the postseal precycle state, and make the cycle runner accept only the latter.

entries.mistake: After C33Z passed its build-phase candidate gate, the founder launcher rejected before any hidden prompt because the sealed state retained all three prior-candidate founder configuration-qualification flags as true while the current candidate had not received its hidden inputs.
entries.rootCause: The C33Y-to-C33Z state preparation preserved inherited runtimeConfiguration qualification flags from an earlier completed founder input cycle, and the candidate build gate did not assert the required false pre-prompt values even though the founder launcher correctly did.
entries.prevention: Reject C33Z at 0/0/0/0 without consuming hidden-input or AAB authority. For the exact successor, reset the three founder configuration-qualification flags to false before sealing, assert those false values in both source-qualified/build gates, assert static parity with the launcher's same three boolean-only pre-prompt predicates, and set them true only after the successor founder inputs validate inside the launcher.

entries.mistake: While isolating the C33Z pre-prompt failure, a diagnostic serialized the complete runtimeConfiguration object instead of limiting output to the three intended boolean qualification flags, printing non-secret runtime metadata beyond the bounded comparison scope.
entries.rootCause: The first boolean-only comparison identified the failing fields, but the follow-up command used ConvertTo-Json on their parent object rather than an explicit property-name allowlist.
entries.prevention: Do not raw-serialize runtimeConfiguration or any secret-adjacent parent object. Project only explicitly named boolean fields, output labels and boolean values only, and never inspect or print passwords, API-key values, OAuth client IDs, tokens, nonces, private keys, private account identifiers or private links.

entries.mistake: After REG2653 was registered, a numbered-line diagnostic intended to inspect C34A lifecycle and rejection fields extended into the adjacent runtimeConfiguration block and again printed non-secret runtime metadata outside the required boolean scope.
entries.rootCause: A broad fixed line range was used against a changing JSON document instead of selecting exact named properties, repeating the overbroad diagnostic-output class immediately after its first registration.
entries.prevention: Count no C34A preparation gate result. Do not use raw JSON ranges or parent-object serialization on secret-adjacent state. Read exact named non-secret lifecycle properties only; for runtime configuration, output only an explicit allowlist of boolean labels and values.

entries.mistake: The first combined C34A gate correction patch expected a parentTicketIds assertion, while the cloned gate actually uses a parentTickets containment assertion; apply_patch rejected the entire operation before changing the gate.
entries.rootCause: A multi-hunk patch was composed from the ticket JSON property name instead of the gate's exact post-clone source context, and unrelated corrections were bundled behind the unverified first hunk.
entries.prevention: Count no C34A gate result. Read back each exact non-secret gate region, apply the ticket, history, source-flag, launcher-parity and build-flag changes as separate verified hunks, then parse both PowerShell hosts before any candidate gate or source seal.

entries.mistake: After C34A sealed its source manifest and both fresh cycles passed, a broad read-only search across config, scripts and docs was used to infer the intermediate post-cycle machine-state name before persisting results.
entries.rootCause: The pre-seal runbook declared the order of cycle-result persistence, final source replay and build-authority exposure but did not bind the exact intermediate machine-state literal and complete state/aggregate patch sequence, leaving a post-seal naming decision.
entries.prevention: Reject C34A at 0/0/0/0 and retain both passing cycles as non-promotable evidence. Before the exact successor seal, declare the exact post-cycle build-authority-held machine state, every state/aggregate cycle-result field, both summary paths and the later founder-prompt transition; assert them in the gate and runbook. After seal, use only those literal owners and commands without repository search.

entries.mistake: The first combined C34B authorization, browser-qualification and runbook patch expected a browser-document context copied from another document; apply_patch rejected the entire operation without changing any document.
entries.rootCause: Three independently structured documents were bundled into one patch without exact per-document context readback, repeating the multi-hunk context-assumption class prevented by REG2655.
entries.prevention: Count no C34B preparation gate result. Read each exact document, apply and verify one document at a time, then bind the updated registry and ticket hashes before parsing or source gates.

entries.mistake: The C34B founder launcher correctly set all three founder-qualified runtime-input flags true after validating the hidden values, then invoked the generic build wrapper; the wrapper replayed the C34B build-phase gate, whose C33Z-preprompt prevention required those same three flags to be false, so every valid post-input C34B launch was rejected before wrapper or Flutter build counts could increment.
entries.rootCause: The C34B gate reused one build phase for two different lifecycle moments: the founder preprompt check, where hidden input and qualification flags must be false, and the postinput wrapper prebuild check, where founder validation has made the qualification flags true. The phase contract did not distinguish those opposite invariants and the preprompt fix was therefore incompatible with the generic wrapper call order.
entries.prevention: Reject C34B at 0/0/0/0; do not retry, upload, install or reuse it. The exact successor must declare separate preprompt and postinput-build lifecycle states and gate phases before sealing: preprompt requires hidden-input and qualification flags false; postinput build requires founder validation recorded, qualification flags true and agent-read flags false. The launcher must call the preprompt phase before Read-Host, persist the declared postinput state after validation, and the wrapper must replay the build phase against that state. Static parity checks and affected tests must prove both transitions before two fresh full cycles and one new authority can be exposed.

entries.mistake: After C34C sealed its source, completed two passing full cycles and passed preprompt in both PowerShell hosts, two non-secret postinput phase-fixture copies were created and one combined state/aggregate patch was attempted without exact generated-field context readback; apply_patch rejected the operation atomically because the assumed runtime-configuration lines were not adjacent in the fixture.
entries.rootCause: The postinput phase fixture was treated as optional evidence that could be assembled after the source seal, and its state and aggregate edits were bundled from an assumed field layout. This repeated the exact-context class prevented by REG2657 and violated the presealed runbook's rule that all fixture owners and mutations must exist before the seal.
entries.prevention: Reject C34C at 0/0/0/0 even though the failed patch changed no file and no hidden input, wrapper or Flutter build ran. Before the exact successor seal, create every positive and negative preprompt/postinput fixture, inspect each exact hunk, apply one file and field group at a time, parse both JSON owners, and execute the full dual-host transition matrix. After seal, run only the already-declared source and preprompt gates plus the founder launcher; create or patch no fixture, source, registry, ticket, runbook or gate.

entries.mistake: The first C34D MVP scope update bundled current-ticket selection, prior/current assessments and approval-state changes; its final approval-state context misspelled Internal_Testing as Internal_TestING, so apply_patch rejected the entire operation before changing the scope state.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-hunk patch was attempted despite REG2655 and REG2657 requiring exact per-owner, per-hunk readback, and the final literal was manually retyped instead of copied from the verified line.
entries.prevention: Count no C34D scope selection result from the failed patch. Read back and apply currentTicketId, assessment rename, new selected assessment, approvalState, top-level ticket, founder evidence and provider gate as separate exact hunks; parse and run the MVP scope gate after each logical group. Bind the resulting registry and final ticket hashes only after all scope updates pass.

entries.mistake: The first C34D active-handoff append used a remembered wrapped tail from an earlier output; the current file did not contain that exact three-line context, so apply_patch rejected the append atomically.
entries.rootCause: The handoff append was attempted without reading the exact current final lines immediately before the patch, repeating the context-assumption class despite the new one-hunk discipline.
entries.prevention: Count no handoff update from the failed patch. Read the exact current tail, anchor one append to those literal bytes, verify the new section once, then rebind the pre-seal registry and ticket before draft-manifest creation. No post-seal handoff mutation is permitted.

entries.mistake: After the C34D source manifest was sealed and the dual-host cycles-zero source gate passed, exact pre-cycle readback proved the sealed C34D source-cycle runner still referenced source-manifest-c34d-registry-2630.txt while the candidate state, aggregate and actual manifest were bound to registry 2632.
entries.rootCause: C34D rebinding updated the runner's summary registry count and SHA but did not update its independent manifestRelative literal. The candidate gate validated the runner parser and generic lifecycle strings but did not assert the exact runner manifest path against state, so the stale predecessor-derived path escaped the preseal transition matrix and official source gate.
entries.prevention: Reject C34D at 0/0/0/0 before any source cycle, hidden input, wrapper, Flutter build, AAB, Play or OPPO action. The exact successor must bind the cycle runner's manifestRelative to its final registry-numbered manifest before draft generation, assert that literal from the candidate gate, run the runner's prerequisite-path preflight without starting tests, then seal and execute two fresh cycles. No C34D sealed source owner may be repaired or reused.

entries.mistake: The first C34E preseal transition-matrix run used fixtures cloned before rejected C34D was appended to the real candidate history. Both positive fixture invocations failed closed because each fixture retained 19 historical candidates while the C34E gate correctly required 20.
entries.rootCause: Fixture identity, registry and manifest fields were rebound after the current state history was extended, but the historicalCandidates arrays in all four fixtures were not compared with the final real state and aggregate before invoking the matrix.
entries.prevention: Count no C34E transition result from the rejected invocations. Retain the registry-2633 draft as failed preseal evidence. Before retry, append the exact rejected C34D contract to all four fixture histories, assert state/aggregate/fixture history counts and last-entry identity are identical, rebind registry 2634 and a fresh registry-2634 draft manifest, then rerun the full dual-host positive and crossed fail-closed matrix. No build, Play or device authority is exposed.

entries.mistake: After C34E r60.69 passed its dual-host preupload gate at 1/0/0/0, the Chrome open-tab inventory was serialized in full and exposed a transient query value from an unrelated signed-in Google Cloud tab before the exact Play tab was claimed or any Play write occurred.
entries.rootCause: The browser discovery step repeated REG-20260813-1863 by emitting raw BrowserUserTabInfo objects instead of matching internally and returning only a query-free allowlisted Play host/path projection.
entries.prevention: Reject C34E at 1/0/0/0 and do not upload, install, promote or reuse it. The exact successor must use a prequalified user-mentioned Play tab or a fresh known Play route without raw tab enumeration; if discovery is unavoidable, match internally and emit only a query-free allowlisted Play host/path summary. Never read or return unrelated tab metadata, query strings, fragments, account/tester data, private links, cookies, storage or session values.
