entries.mistake: The first C34F aggregate reset patch combined identity, historical-candidate, source-qualification, authority, count, privacy and rejection changes; apply_patch rejected the operation atomically when one source-qualification context did not match the exact cloned aggregate bytes.
entries.rootCause: The aggregate was treated as layout-identical to the state and rewritten with one large remembered multi-hunk patch instead of reading and updating each exact aggregate section independently.
entries.prevention: Count no C34F aggregate update from the failed patch. Parse and read each exact aggregate section, apply one bounded hunk, parse again, and only then continue. No source seal, test, build, Play or device action is allowed until the final aggregate mirrors state and the candidate gate passes.

entries.mistake: A read-only C34F registry-binding inventory passed a wildcard inside a Windows path argument to rg, so Windows rejected that path while exact file arguments returned only a partial result.
entries.rootCause: A shell-style path wildcard was used instead of rg's explicit --glob option on Windows.
entries.prevention: Count no complete inventory result from the rejected command. Pass the directory as an exact path, use --glob for the filename pattern, require native exit zero, and only then rebind the candidate registry fields.

entries.mistake: A read-only C34E fixture inventory placed a pipeline immediately after a statement-level foreach block, so PowerShell rejected the command as an empty pipe element and returned no fixture inventory.
entries.rootCause: Statement foreach syntax was mixed with pipeline syntax instead of using ForEach-Object or wrapping the statement output.
entries.prevention: Count no fixture inventory result from the rejected command. Use Get-ChildItem piped to ForEach-Object, require parser and native exit success, and only then clone or bind fixture owners.

entries.mistake: While reconciling C34F after REG2667, a read-only combined state and fixture inventory again placed a formatter pipeline immediately after a statement-level foreach block, so PowerShell rejected the command as an empty pipe element and returned no inventory.
entries.rootCause: The verification command repeated the forbidden statement-foreach plus trailing-pipe construction instead of composing the fixture objects through Get-ChildItem or an explicit array followed by ForEach-Object.
entries.prevention: Count no reconciliation result from the rejected command. Keep scalar state reconciliation separate. For fixture output, use the exact fixture-path array piped to ForEach-Object and then to the formatter, require parser success, and bind the resulting registry only after the corrected inventory succeeds.

entries.mistake: The first C34F source-composition gate rejected the finalized pre-sealed Internal Testing runbook because four static String.Contains assertions expected phrases to remain on one physical Markdown line while the document wrapped those phrases across adjacent lines.
entries.rootCause: The candidate gate bound semantic runbook requirements with newline-sensitive literal containment even though normal Markdown wrapping preserved the exact meaning and all required words.
entries.prevention: Count no C34F source-gate result from the rejection. Before the source seal, replace only the four wrapped-phrase assertions with whitespace-tolerant regexes while retaining every exact semantic token, parse both hosts, rebind the new registry and ticket hashes, and replay source composition from zero counts.

entries.mistake: A corrected C34F source-composition gate invocation reached the 30-second orchestration yield with empty visible output, but the tool wrapper emitted only the output field and discarded any returned session id and exit metadata, so completion versus a still-running gate could not be determined.
entries.rootCause: The long-running read-only gate was invoked through a projection that did not retain the complete exec result object even though a yield was possible.
entries.prevention: Count no gate result from the unknown invocation. Exclude the current process, prove no exact C34F source-gate process remains using a sanitized PID/name-only projection, then invoke the gate with complete exec metadata retained and wait by its returned session id until an explicit exit result is available.

entries.mistake: Pre-seal readback of the C34F source-cycle runner proved its PrerequisiteOnly success message still reported registry-2634 even though manifestRelative and all current candidate bindings target the later final registry generation.
entries.rootCause: The mechanically cloned runner updated its manifest path, summary count and SHA but retained a predecessor-era human-readable registry literal that the candidate gate did not assert.
entries.prevention: Do not run or count the prerequisite preflight with the stale message. Before the official seal, bind the message to the exact final C34F registry number, add the exact message to the candidate gate static owner assertions, parse both hosts and replay source composition after registry and ticket rebinding.

entries.mistake: The first C34F preprompt positive-fixture invocation failed closed because the cloned fixture presealUploadWorkflow evidencePath still named the nonexistent C34F browser-qualification file with the predecessor date 20260816 instead of the existing C34F 20260817 evidence.
entries.rootCause: Candidate identity and registry fields were rebound across the four cloned fixtures, but the date-bearing browser evidence path was not compared with the final real C34F state before invoking the matrix.
entries.prevention: Count no matrix result from the rejected invocation. Before retry, project the exact named presealUploadWorkflow evidencePath from real state and all four fixtures, bind every fixture to the existing 20260817 C34F evidence path, rebind registry and ticket hashes, create a fresh superseding draft manifest and rerun all positive and crossed fail-closed phases.

entries.mistake: After the browser evidence path was corrected, the next C34F preprompt positive-fixture invocation failed closed because the cloned founderAuthorization evidence path still named the nonexistent C34F authorization document with predecessor date 20260816 instead of 20260817.
entries.rootCause: The first correction projected only presealUploadWorkflow evidencePath and did not perform one bounded inventory of every remaining predecessor-date literal across all four fixture JSON files before retry.
entries.prevention: Count no matrix result from the rejected invocation. Before retry, use the exact fixture directory plus an rg --glob bounded to the four C34F fixture JSON files, inventory every 20260816 literal, bind each candidate-owned evidence path to its existing 20260817 C34F owner, prove zero remaining predecessor-date literals, then rebind registry, ticket and a fresh draft manifest.

entries.mistake: A read-only C34F fixture-reference audit required every referenced repository file to exist and threw on apps/mobile/android/app/src/release/google-services.json, even though that transient founder-created release file is required to remain absent before hidden input validation and build.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic did not distinguish durable fixture evidence owners from the one exact intentionally absent transient runtime configuration path.
entries.prevention: Count no complete reference-audit result from the false failure. Rerun with only apps/mobile/android/app/src/release/google-services.json allowlisted as expected absent, require every other referenced repository file to exist, prove the transient remains absent, and do not inspect or create it.

entries.mistake: A read-only check intended to prove C34F mutable state, aggregate and fixture owners are excluded from the draft source manifest formatted long target paths and match counts as a table; console width clipped the count column, leaving the exclusion result unreadable.
entries.rootCause: Long paths were projected with Format-Table instead of explicit labeled scalar or Format-List output, repeating the truncated read-only evidence class.
entries.prevention: Count no exclusion result and do not treat the registry-2645 official file as a final seal. Rebind the successor registry, project each exact target with a labeled ManifestMatches scalar using Format-List, require all counts zero, then create and byte-compare a fresh draft and official manifest before state binding.

entries.mistake: C34F cycle 1 invoked the predeclared authoritative Flutter manifest audit, which stopped under strict mode before emitting any authoritative test result because variable $event was read on an execution path where it had not been set.
entries.rootCause: The pre-seal runner qualification proved paths, parser validity and static command bindings but did not exercise the audit's real event-processing scope. The audit therefore retained an unset-event execution path that escaped until the first sealed full cycle.
entries.prevention: Reject C34F at 0/0/0/0 and do not retry, repair or promote it. The exact successor must inspect and minimally repair the authoritative audit's event initialization or scope, add a focused executable prevention for the failing event path, bind that prevention into its gate before sealing, then use a fresh registry, source manifest and two complete cycles.

entries.mistake: The first C34F rejection-state patch combined state and aggregate lifecycle, authority and rejection-object changes and assumed rejection:null was each document's final property; apply_patch rejected the operation atomically because the real state context did not match.
entries.rootCause: The rejection transition was composed from a predecessor-shaped remembered tail instead of reading the exact current C34F rejection-property context independently in state and aggregate.
entries.prevention: Count no rejection-state write from the failed patch. Read the exact current rejection-property context, apply machine/authority and rejection objects as separate state and aggregate hunks, parse after each owner, and bind the final rejection registry generation without altering sealed source, ticket, runbook or gate owners.

entries.mistake: The first post-rejection diagnosis searched every $event reference in the authoritative Flutter manifest audit and emitted all matching source lines; the result was truncated, so no line, scope or root-cause conclusion from that output is retained as evidence.
entries.rootCause: A broad source-line projection was used where the file could contain many matches, instead of first returning only the match count and a bounded list of line numbers.
entries.prevention: Count no diagnosis from the truncated search. Before any successor selection or repair, return only the exact match count and bounded line-number batches, inspect narrow explicit line ranges around candidate references, and retain no secret-bearing or unrelated process data.

entries.mistake: A combined post-rejection reconstruction command emitted the repository's huge dirty status together with several document reads, exceeded the retained output budget, and then stopped on the nonexistent docs/quality/REGRESSION-RETEST-MEMORY.md path. Only the separately visible branch and HEAD scalars are retained; no complete status, memory, handoff or state read is counted from that command.
entries.rootCause: The command ignored the repository's known huge dirty tree and used a stale remembered memory filename instead of first resolving exact repository-owned paths with rg --files.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat or count the combined command. Resolve exact document paths with a bounded rg --files filter, summarize git status by branch plus tracked/untracked counts without listing every path, and read each exact state, memory and handoff owner separately with bounded output before reporting or patching it.

entries.mistake: The corrected handoff and memory path resolver failed closed because its rg output filter accepted only forward slashes while rg --files emitted Windows backslash paths.
entries.rootCause: The filename filter assumed POSIX separators despite running in Windows PowerShell.
entries.prevention: Count no path-resolution result from the failed command. Retry with a filter that accepts either slash or backslash, require the two exact filenames once each, and only then perform bounded reads. Do not combine path resolution with candidate or external actions.

entries.mistake: The bounded dirty-tree summary used PowerShell -like and -notlike with the pattern ??*, where each question mark is a wildcard; it therefore misclassified every status record as untracked and reported tracked dirty zero.
entries.rootCause: Git's literal two-question-mark porcelain prefix was passed to a wildcard matcher instead of a literal prefix comparison.
entries.prevention: Discard the tracked/untracked split from that command. On the one retry, use String.StartsWith('??') for literal untracked classification, require tracked plus untracked to equal the total, and emit only scalar counts.

entries.mistake: A read-only C34F parity predicate compared the complete serialized state and aggregate rejection objects and returned false because the state object carries four explicit count fields that the aggregate rejection object intentionally omits.
entries.rootCause: Parity was defined as byte-equivalent object shape instead of equality across the documented fields shared by state and aggregate plus independent equality of their actionCounts owners.
entries.prevention: Do not interpret or report the false result as a candidate-state defect. Compare only named shared rejection fields, compare actionCounts separately, and require machine state and releaseAuthorities equality before concluding parity.

entries.mistake: The first C34G scope-state inspection attempted to index a presumed top-level assessments array and stopped because that property is not present at the assumed path.
entries.rootCause: The read reused a remembered scope-state layout instead of first enumerating only the current document's top-level property names and then selecting the exact existing owner.
entries.prevention: Count no scope-state result or ticket selection from the failed read. Enumerate top-level property names only, inspect the exact existing assessment owner in a bounded follow-up, then use small parsed patches and run the MVP scope gate before any implementation mutation.

entries.mistake: The next C34G scope inspection serialized the complete preTicketSelectionCheckpoint, whose many historical assessments exceeded the retained output boundary and was truncated.
entries.rootCause: A large nested checkpoint owner was projected wholesale instead of enumerating its property names and selecting only the current assessment.
entries.prevention: Count no checkpoint assessment content from the truncated output. Enumerate checkpoint property names only, identify the exact current C34F assessment key, then read that one object and patch only the named current/prior owners for C34G.

entries.mistake: A read-only C34G ticket line inventory again placed a formatter pipeline immediately after a statement-level foreach block, causing the PowerShell empty-pipe parser error before any result was produced.
entries.rootCause: The command repeated REG2667 and REG2668 instead of assigning statement-foreach output to an explicit array and formatting that array in a separate statement.
entries.prevention: Count no inventory result from the rejected command. Build an explicit result array inside the foreach, end the statement, then format the array separately; no implementation or scope retry proceeds until this recurrence is registered.

entries.mistake: The first C34G state reset iterated state and aggregate through one shared assignment block and attempted to set allEntriesAppliedBeforeSeal on the aggregate regressionMemory object, where that state-only property does not exist. The command stopped before either JSON owner was written.
entries.rootCause: The reset assumed state and aggregate nested object shapes were identical despite the registered requirement to treat their layouts independently.
entries.prevention: Count no reset result from the failed in-memory command. Re-read both unchanged files, assign only verified shared properties in the common block, assign allEntriesAppliedBeforeSeal and other state-only fields separately, write each new C34G owner only after all mutations succeed, then parse and compare named shared fields.

entries.mistake: The second C34G reset removed the first state-only regression-memory assignment but still attempted to set qualifiedRegistryEntryCount on the aggregate presealUploadWorkflow object, where that detailed-state-only property does not exist. The command again stopped before writing either JSON owner.
entries.rootCause: The correction checked only that the nested objects existed, not that every property assigned in the shared block existed in both shapes.
entries.prevention: Count no reset from the second in-memory command. Enumerate the exact property names of state and aggregate regressionMemory, presealUploadWorkflow and sourceQualification; compute their intersections; keep only intersection fields in shared assignments and assign every other field to its explicit owner before writing.

entries.mistake: The nested state/aggregate property inventory intended to prevent REG2687 again piped directly after a statement-level foreach and failed at parse time, producing no schema evidence.
entries.rootCause: The command violated REG2667, REG2668 and REG2685 even while attempting to apply their prevention.
entries.prevention: Count no inventory. The next and all later multi-item diagnostic commands must initialize a result array, append inside foreach, terminate the foreach statement, and format the array in a separate statement. No direct trailing pipe is permitted.

entries.mistake: The next C34G in-memory reset attempted founderAuthorization.oneInPlaceOppoPlayUpdateApprovedAfterPostbuildGate, but the existing contract property is oneInPlaceOppoPlayUpdateApprovedAfterPostuploadGate. The command stopped before writing state or aggregate.
entries.rootCause: The state-only property was manually retyped instead of copied from the verified owner or asserted before assignment.
entries.prevention: Count no reset from the failed command. Assert every state-only target property exists before any mutation, use the exact oneInPlaceOppoPlayUpdateApprovedAfterPostuploadGate property, and serialize only after all assignments complete.

entries.mistake: The first dual-host C34G cycles-zero source gate rejected because the generic AAB wrapper did not yet contain the exact C34G candidate binding, gate order and single-appbundle owner strings required by the C34G candidate gate.
entries.rootCause: The mechanically cloned candidate gate was executed before the generic wrapper's explicit supported-successor branch was extended from C34F to C34G.
entries.prevention: Count neither host invocation as a pass and retain C34G at 0/0/0/0. Inspect only the exact wrapper support and postbuild mirror branch, add the smallest C34G identity/state/gate/recovery binding without changing the generic build algorithm, parse and replay the wrapper checker, then rebind the new registry and ticket hashes before retrying the candidate gate.

entries.mistake: Both corrected C34G cycles-zero source-gate invocations reached the execution yield, but the orchestration projection emitted only exit and output fields and omitted each returned session id. Neither completion result can be recovered from that output.
entries.rootCause: The dual-host parallel projection repeated REG2670 by not retaining complete exec metadata for gates that can exceed the initial yield window.
entries.prevention: Count neither invocation as a pass. Exclude the current diagnostic process, prove whether any exact C34G gate process remains through a sanitized PID/process-name-only projection, wait for absence without mutation, then invoke each host separately with the complete exec result retained and poll only its returned session id to explicit exit.

entries.mistake: The C34G fixture rebind wrote all four new fixture owners, but its verification used Format-Table and clipped manifest path, SHA and file-count columns. The write must be read back, while the clipped output cannot prove the complete binding.
entries.rootCause: A long-path fixture result used a table despite REG2675 requiring labeled scalar output.
entries.prevention: Do not count the clipped verification. The new registry generation supersedes the registry-2662 draft. Rebind state, aggregate, runner, gate, documents and fixtures to the new registry; generate a fresh draft; then verify every fixture with one labeled scalar object containing history, last candidate, registry, manifest path, SHA, count, cycles and machine state.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to register REG2692 supplied an update patch with no added or removed line and a misspelled context token, so apply_patch returned without changing the registry or creating evidence.
entries.rootCause: The registration patch was sent before verifying it contained an actual diff hunk.
entries.prevention: Count the no-op as zero change. Before every registry append, verify the patch contains an explicit added entry and evidence file, then parse the registry and confirm the new final ID before proceeding.

entries.mistake: C34G cycle 1 passed completely, but its result was persisted immediately as completedIdenticalCycles=1 before cycle 2. The predeclared sealed runner requires completedIdenticalCycles=0 at the start of each independent cycle and the lifecycle contract requires both results to be persisted together only after both cycles finish.
entries.rootCause: The post-cycle action followed an intuitive incremental counter update instead of the sealed runbook's explicit postcyclePersistenceOrder and the runner's held-authority precondition.
entries.prevention: Reject C34G at build/upload/install/device counts 0/0/0/0 without running cycle 2, repairing state or reusing cycle 1 for qualification. The exact successor must keep real state and aggregate at cycles 0/2 while both predeclared cycle commands run, verify both retained summaries independently, and only then atomically persist cycles 2/2 and both evidence paths before dual-host source replay.

entries.mistake: The C34H successor plan update returned a truncated orchestration result, so the requested plan state cannot be treated as retained or authoritative.
entries.rootCause: The planning call's returned result exceeded the orchestration projection and no complete durable readback was retained before the continuation context compacted.
entries.prevention: Do not rely on the unknown plan-tool state. Reconstruct the explicit C34H plan from durable repository evidence, register this event before selection, keep every lifecycle decision in ticket/state/aggregate/runbook evidence, and treat future plan calls as advisory rather than candidate authority.

entries.mistake: The rejected C34G aggregate's nested candidate block retained buildCount=1 and a predecessor AAB hash while authoritative actionCounts, release authorities and rejection evidence correctly say C34G had zero builds and no reusable artifact.
entries.rootCause: The candidate aggregate template inherited predecessor artifact fields and the reset/rejection verification compared shared action-count owners without independently asserting the nested candidate block.
entries.prevention: Do not repair or reinterpret rejected C34G. C34H must be initialized from explicit zero/null candidate artifact fields, and its gate must independently assert nested candidate, actionCounts, buildResult, Play result, install result and rejection/history parity before sealing and after every lifecycle transition.

entries.mistake: The first combined C34H gate, runner and wrapper patch was rejected atomically because the remembered focused-gate variable/label anchor did not exactly match the cloned gate owner.
entries.rootCause: A large multi-region patch mixed freshly inspected and remembered distant anchors instead of reading each exact local hunk immediately before applying it.
entries.prevention: Count the rejected patch as zero changes. Rebind C34H to the new registry generation, read every exact local anchor, apply bounded owner-specific hunks, and parse/read back each owner before invoking a gate.

entries.mistake: The first C34H source-gate invocation called the qualified C34G focused loop-control checker directly, but that checker is correctly bound to the selected C34G ticket and rejected the C34H scope selection before any source seal or tests.
entries.rootCause: The C34H reuse inventory treated the C34G behavior gate as directly replayable without auditing its current-ticket scope assertion.
entries.prevention: Preserve the rejected C34G checker unchanged. Add one C34H successor-replay checker that binds current/selected C34H identity, verifies the immutable C34G ticket/checker/source repair and executes the same focused cases; declare it as the only new necessary test owner, rebind the new registry generation, and pass it in both PowerShell hosts before sealing.

entries.mistake: The first poll of the yielded C34H source-composition gate used an invalid JavaScript wrapper expression, so the poll tool rejected it before contacting retained session 85589.
entries.rootCause: The polling call used a compact block form without a valid statement separator after the awaited assignment.
entries.prevention: Retain the exact session id, count the malformed poll as no process evidence, poll with a simple valid call, and treat the in-flight gate as superseded because this registration advances the pre-seal registry. Rebind and replay the gate once after the session exits.

entries.mistake: The mechanically cloned C34H browser-qualification document called the workflow C34H-qualified while retaining registry 2664 and the C34G qualification SHA, even though no new C34H browser action occurred.
entries.rootCause: Candidate-name substitution changed the evidence subject without changing or truthfully describing the underlying immutable browser-workflow qualification generation.
entries.prevention: Perform no browser retry. Preserve the C34G query-free workflow qualification as immutable behavior evidence, describe C34H only as composing that qualified workflow with zero Play writes, keep the exact C34G registry generation labeled as reused provenance, and assert the composition wording before C34H seal.

entries.mistake: The registry-2671 C34H preprompt fixture gate falsely rejected the truthful browser-composition document because a new exact Contains assertion expected 'No new' on one physical line while Markdown wrapped between those words.
entries.rootCause: The new documentation assertion repeated the known line-wrap brittleness class instead of using the repository's whitespace-tolerant semantic-marker rule.
entries.prevention: Do not edit the truthful browser evidence wording. Replace only the exact Contains assertion with a whitespace-tolerant regex, parse the gate, rebind the new registry generation and replay the full phase matrix before sealing.

entries.mistake: The pre-seal handoff update replaced the registry-2671 draft description but left a semicolon followed by a detached 'with 210 protected owners' fragment before a registry-2672 draft existed.
entries.rootCause: A partial paragraph replacement preserved a dependent clause from the superseded manifest sentence.
entries.prevention: Correct the paragraph to state only that registry-2671 is superseded and registry-2672 remains to be generated; add final counts only after readback of the new draft, then freeze documentation before sealing.

entries.mistake: The poll for yielded C34H build-phase fixture session 76488 was rejected by the orchestration JavaScript parser before tools.write_stdin contacted the retained PowerShell process.
entries.rootCause: The multi-statement polling wrapper remained vulnerable to orchestration parsing/transport failure even after the earlier syntax prevention.
entries.prevention: Retain session 76488, treat the failed poll as zero process evidence, use a minimal wrapper containing only one awaited write_stdin call and output projection, and supersede the full pre-seal phase matrix after this registry advance.

entries.mistake: A sanitized three-transient existence check placed a pipeline directly after foreach and PowerShell rejected it at parse time before reading a transient or changing candidate state.
entries.rootCause: The command compressed loop collection and JSON serialization into an invalid PowerShell statement shape.
entries.prevention: Assign foreach output to a task-specific variable and serialize it in a separate statement; a parse rejection is zero evidence and cannot be silently retried.

entries.mistake: The C34H preupload gate was invoked while upload authority was still held; it failed closed at 1/0/0/0 before any browser or Play write.
entries.rootCause: Postbuild qualification and the distinct projection of founder-authorized upload authority were treated as one implicit step.
entries.prevention: Verify postbuild, explicitly project only the one-time upload authority into mutable state and aggregate, parse both owners, then invoke preupload.

entries.mistake: The prepared Play draft exposed two raw file inputs, so a custom exact-one assertion stopped before selection or transmission after mutable authority had been marked consumed too early.
entries.rootCause: A hidden DOM file-input count was treated as stable and authority was consumed before the visible upload control shape was verified.
entries.prevention: Inspect the visible Upload control and input count before authority consumption; when Play has multiple hidden inputs, use the single visible Upload button with the documented chooser flow.

entries.mistake: A postinstall ripgrep command passed shell-style wildcard path operands on Windows and failed with invalid-filename errors.
entries.rootCause: Unix operand globbing was mixed with Windows path semantics instead of resolving the exact runtime-gate path from candidate state.
entries.prevention: Use the exact authoritative owner path; if filtering is required use ripgrep -g, never a wildcard path operand on Windows.

entries.mistake: After founder device interaction, a stale computer-control handle captured a different Windows surface instead of the OPPO mirror; no input was sent from it.
entries.rootCause: The pre-handoff window binding was reused without re-listing and rehydrating the exact live CPH2375 window.
entries.prevention: After any founder/device takeover, re-list scrcpy, require one exact CPH2375 window, rehydrate and activate it, and discard every earlier screenshot id, coordinate and element index.

entries.mistake: A C34H YouTube-provider tap opened an Android account chooser containing private account identifiers; no account was selected and the founder manually closed it.
entries.rootCause: The provider tile was treated as an unsupported-provider truth probe without classifying it as a supported authentication action capable of opening a system chooser.
entries.prevention: Treat every provider tile as an authentication boundary unless a prequalified local unavailable-state contract proves otherwise; Codex stops before any account-capable provider tap and the founder alone handles account selection.

entries.mistake: A read-only pre-ticket multifile wrapper placed a pipeline directly after a statement-level foreach block and PowerShell rejected it before any requested document content was returned.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper repeated the empty-pipe command shape instead of separating loop collection from serialization.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the wrapper; read each required document directly by literal path in bounded calls, or assign loop output to a task-specific variable before separate serialization.

entries.mistake: A JavaScript orchestration wrapper called PowerShell-style Replace on a JavaScript string and failed before launching any C34I parser or gate command.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell and JavaScript string APIs were mixed while applying unnecessary transformation to fixed literal repository paths.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the wrapper; run each dual-host parser and policy gate as one plain direct terminal command using fixed literal paths, and count the wrapper failure as zero gate evidence.

entries.mistake: The C34I mechanical release-owner generator declared both C34H and c34h in one PowerShell hashtable and was rejected during parsing before creating any owner.
entries.rootCause: Case-sensitive String.Replace inputs were represented as case-insensitive PowerShell hash keys.
entries.prevention: Keep only the uppercase substitution in the ordered map, apply lowercase c34h as a separate explicit String.Replace after the map loop, parse first, and count the rejected invocation as zero generation evidence.

entries.mistake: The generated C34I source-cycle owner retained bare registry count 2674 and referenced a nonexistent mechanically renamed C34I/C34G replay gate; readback caught both before any cycle started.
entries.rootCause: Mechanical substitution covered named strings but not a bare summary integer and renamed a predecessor-specific semantic dependency instead of selecting the C34I actor-policy gate.
entries.prevention: Before execution, audit generated owners for every registry literal, predecessor token and referenced-file existence; bind the exact current registry and invoke the selected C34I device-actor policy self-test.

entries.mistake: The first C34I registry-2684 source draft included mutable detailed and aggregate lifecycle state, so binding the manifest hash would have changed manifested files; the draft was not bound and no cycle started.
entries.rootCause: Immutable release-owner coverage was not separated from candidate state files that must change through later lifecycle transitions.
entries.prevention: Retain the rejected draft, exclude only the two mutable lifecycle state files from the fresh source manifest, and enforce their schema, registry seal, policy hash, counts, authority and phase parity through the immutable candidate gate.

entries.mistake: The one authorized C34I AAB completed and produced sealed provenance, but the generic wrapper consumed aggregate releaseAuthorities.build without consuming the matching detailed state releaseAuthorities.build; the postbuild gate failed closed and the launcher reported no success.
entries.rootCause: Prebuild qualification asserted static wrapper tokens and phase gates but did not execute the real success-transition helper against detailed and aggregate fixtures covering every mirrored lifecycle field.
entries.prevention: Permanently reject C34I at 1/0/0/0 and never rebuild or upload it. Before any successor AAB, expose one generic transition function that atomically advances detailed and aggregate machine state, authorization, release authorities, counts, disposition, artifact hash and artifact reusability; run positive and fail-closed fixtures for every release phase in both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: A combined C34J MVP-scope-state patch used a remembered long selected-assessment block and apply_patch rejected it because the live context differed; no hunk was written.
entries.rootCause: Several distant JSON sections were coupled to one large context instead of patching freshly read unique local anchors independently.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the combined patch. Read each target section immediately before mutation, patch one unique bounded section at a time, then parse the complete JSON and run the MVP scope gate.

entries.mistake: A bounded selected-assessment patch retyped the prior C34I ticket hash incorrectly in its context, so apply_patch rejected it with zero writes.
entries.rootCause: A 64-character prior hash was transcribed from memory instead of projected directly from parsed live JSON.
entries.prevention: Project the exact current selected assessment from parsed JSON, copy its literal live hash without transformation, and patch identity separately from all other sections before full JSON and MVP-gate validation.

entries.mistake: The newly inserted prior-C34I assessment transposed one SHA-256 segment even after the earlier zero-write hash-context error; readback caught it before any MVP gate or candidate authority.
entries.rootCause: The historical hash was manually retyped in the successful insertion instead of copied from the immediately retained Get-FileHash result.
entries.prevention: Correct the one field from Get-FileHash, project selected and prior manifest paths plus hashes from parsed JSON, and require both on-disk hash equalities before the MVP gate.

entries.mistake: The first C34J dual-host parser wrapper passed a relative file through a PowerShell -Command positional argument shape that produced an invalid parser path; it stopped before either fixture checker ran.
entries.rootCause: A redundant nested parser command introduced an argument boundary different from direct script-file execution.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the wrapper. Execute the checker directly with -File on each host; the checker parses the transition owner before any fixture and its exit code is the authoritative host result.

entries.mistake: The C34J mechanical owner generator repeated REG2712 by placing uppercase and lowercase authentication-privacy-safe phrase variants in one case-insensitive PowerShell hashtable; parsing stopped before either owner was created.
entries.rootCause: The prior prevention was applied to the C34I token pair but not generalized to every case-distinct replacement pair in the new generator.
entries.prevention: Keep only one case variant in the ordered hashtable, perform every lowercase variant through an explicit String.Replace after the map, parse successfully, require both target paths absent, then execute exactly once and audit all stale tokens.

entries.mistake: Generated C34J cycle and launcher owners retained hyphenated r60-73 evidence, gate and contract fragments because only dotted r60.73 was replaced; their registry-2690 literal also became stale after REG2720. Readback occurred before any cycle or launcher execution.
entries.rootCause: Mechanical substitution again treated lexical replacement as semantic qualification and did not inventory every version representation or rebind the registry after intervening memory changes.
entries.prevention: Correct the exact evidence root, gate path, contract ID and current registry literals from live owners; audit all predecessor/version/registry tokens and every referenced path for existence before prerequisite-only execution.

entries.mistake: Pre-seal verification guessed a nonexistent generic AAB wrapper checker filename, then abbreviated the exact REG2721 evidence filename; both reads stopped before the intended checker or document and caused no candidate transition, build, external write or cycle evidence.
entries.rootCause: Known naming patterns were used to reconstruct long repository paths instead of discovering exact owners with rg --files and projecting literal evidence paths from the parsed registry entry.
entries.prevention: Discover and assert the exact owner path before invocation; for regression evidence, consume the literal path from the parsed registry entry. Use scripts/check-play-internal-aab-build-wrapper-c30t.ps1 for the generic wrapper qualification.

entries.mistake: C34J pre-seal verification supplied -Phase release to the regression-memory checker, whose ValidateSet accepts only general, implementation, build or device; parameter binding stopped before the checker body ran.
entries.rootCause: The surrounding release workflow name was treated as the checker phase contract without first inspecting the declared parameter validation set.
entries.prevention: Inspect enumerated checker parameters before invocation and use the declared build phase for release-candidate preparation; do not infer phase strings from workflow prose.

entries.mistake: After correcting the regression-memory phase to build, the invocation omitted the separately required -BuildMode release, so the checker rejected its default none before completing the gate.
entries.rootCause: Only the primary phase enum was inspected; the dependent BuildMode requirement in the checker body was not supplied in the same corrected call.
entries.prevention: For C34J release preparation invoke the memory checker with the complete inspected pair -Phase build -BuildMode release and retain that exact contract in release verification.

entries.mistake: C34J's candidate gate mapped postbuild through journey phases to unsupported regression-memory phase release, which would have failed only after an AAB or later authority was consumed; consolidated pre-AAB audit caught it first.
entries.rootCause: The candidate gate invented a semantic release phase instead of preserving the called checker's declared build/device phase vocabulary across the full lifecycle.
entries.prevention: Map source through preinstall to -Phase build -BuildMode release, map postinstall and journey to -Phase device, and qualify every later phase through lifecycle fixtures before exposing founder input or build authority.

entries.mistake: C34J's postinstall candidate gate invoked the acceptance-blocker ledger's postinstall mode before device journeys were allowed to run, creating a circular dependency because that ledger mode requires the future Play-device journey evidence itself.
entries.rootCause: The candidate phase name was mapped directly to the blocker-ledger phase without accounting for the lifecycle boundary between opening device acceptance and proving completed device acceptance.
entries.prevention: Use blocker-ledger prebuild validation through the candidate postinstall phase; require blocker-ledger postinstall resolution only at final journey acceptance. Prove all eight candidate phases against an isolated resolved-ledger fixture on both PowerShell hosts before source cycles or founder input.

entries.mistake: C34K mechanical generation replaced lowercase r60-74 but retained uppercase R60-74 inside state, aggregate and generic-wrapper contract IDs; semantic readback caught it before state preparation or gate execution.
entries.rootCause: The replacement inventory again treated version spelling as one token and omitted the separate uppercase contract representation.
entries.prevention: Inventory and assert dotted, lowercase-hyphenated, uppercase-hyphenated and numeric version forms separately; require R60-75 in every C34K contract and exact generic-wrapper binding before candidate selection.

entries.mistake: A sanitized OPPO readiness diagnostic assigned to $pid, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's automatic $PID; an empty pidof result then reached Trim and made the process interpretation untrustworthy. No device or external write occurred.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic reused a PowerShell automatic variable name and did not branch on an empty native process-query result before string normalization.
entries.prevention: Use a task-specific $moolProcessId variable, handle empty pidof output before Trim, and never infer application process state from PowerShell's automatic PID. Require exact sanitized installer identity before any Play in-place update gate.

entries.mistake: Independent pre-AAB audits found ten C34K lifecycle gaps: unconstrained fixture bypass, non-crash-atomic dual files, unbound phase-gate proofs, incomplete postbuild failure catch, weak retained-evidence identity, over-trusting attempt-one recovery, cleanup-suppressed launcher result risk, unbound dual-host eight-phase fixture, mutable blocker ledger inside the immutable seal, and missing preupload browser-route proof assertions.
entries.rootCause: C34K proved transition shapes in isolation but did not model the complete release lifecycle as one durable transaction whose prerequisite proofs, evidence identities, mutable postinstall state, cleanup result, recovery verification and crash boundaries are machine-bound end to end before source cycles.
entries.prevention: Select one successor ticket covering this complete batch; confine fixtures, add crash-recoverable transaction journaling, bind exact prerequisite-gate proof hashes to transitions, catch and reject every post-Flutter failure, validate retained evidence identity/content, reverify recovery cryptographically and against current source, isolate cleanup from result retention, bind both-host eight-phase outputs before cycles, exclude/bind mutable blocker state correctly, and require exact preupload browser-route proofs.

entries.mistake: A read-only C34L checkpoint command guessed config/regression-memory.json after the MVP gate passed; the nonexistent path caused the registry count/hash portion of that command to stop. No candidate, device, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The verification command used a remembered generic filename instead of first resolving the repository-owned registry path from durable owners.
entries.prevention: Use config/codex-development-regression-registry.json for the registry count/hash and resolve owner paths with rg --files before composing combined verification commands; never silently retry a failed guessed path.

entries.mistake: A read-only multi-file PowerShell parser check placed a pipeline directly after a foreach statement, producing an empty-pipe parser error before any target script was parsed. No candidate, device, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc verification command attempted to stream a foreach statement directly into Format-Table instead of collecting its results first.
entries.prevention: Collect parser result objects into a task-specific array, then format that array in a separate statement; keep parser verification commands structurally simple and independently parseable.

entries.mistake: A read-only combined cross-host parser command passed in PowerShell 7, then outer-shell interpolation removed the Windows PowerShell $tokens assignment and caused the Windows PowerShell command itself to fail before parsing the target. No candidate, device, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The nested powershell.exe -Command payload used quoting that allowed the outer host to interpolate inner variable names.
entries.prevention: Use a retained parser script or an encoded/single-quoted command for cross-host checks; do not compose nested variable-bearing PowerShell command text inline. Preserve the agent's already-passed Windows PowerShell parser evidence and do not retry during shutdown.

entries.mistake: A read-only C34L reconstruction command parsed the current MVP scope and robustness owners, then projected candidate and assessment fields from assumed top-level names. Those values are nested in the current schemas, so the emitted blanks are rejected as scope or robustness evidence. No candidate, device, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The command reused remembered projection paths before enumerating the exact current root and nested property names.
entries.prevention: Enumerate the exact root and relevant child property names before every release-control projection; reject blank or null values, then run the owning MVP scope and delivery-discipline gates.

entries.mistake: The first patch intended to append REG2733 to the regression registry was atomically rejected because its large context retyped the existing REG2732 mistake sentence differently from the current file. The patch applied no registry mutation and changed no candidate or external state.
entries.rootCause: The append patch used a manually retyped complete prior entry instead of the smallest exact current tail anchor.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current registry tail immediately before appending, anchor only on the final unchanged evidence line and closing braces, then parse the registry and verify the exact final ID, count and SHA-256.

entries.mistake: During mandatory read-only reconstruction, the transaction sub-agent placed literal backtick-n text between three Git commands. Git received branch\ngit as an option value and rejected the combined command before branch or HEAD reconstruction completed. No file, candidate, device, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper treated textual newline escape sequences as shell statement boundaries instead of issuing the three scalar Git commands independently.
entries.prevention: Run git status --short --branch, git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD and git rev-parse HEAD as independent exact commands or distinct directly authored shell statements; admit every result only from its own zero exit and never place literal backtick-n text between native commands.

entries.mistake: The transaction sub-agent combined dense required document reads into output that truncated the active handoff. The partial output is zero complete-reconstruction evidence, and the sub-agent stopped before mutation or retry. No candidate, device, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The sub-agent grouped a dense append-only handoff with other owners instead of measuring it and reading the exact current sections in bounded independent ranges.
entries.prevention: Read the active handoff independently, measure it before any required complete read, use nonoverlapping bounded ranges, and read the exact C34L 14:50 and 14:36 sections through their continuation boundary before implementation.

entries.mistake: After REG2735 and REG2736 were appended, one shell call projected the registry count, final ID and SHA-256 and then invoked the implementation memory gate. Both operations visibly succeeded, but the gate result is not admitted because release work requires one authoritative gate per shell call. No candidate or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The post-append verification treated a scalar projection and the owning machine gate as one convenience batch instead of preserving independent evidence boundaries.
entries.prevention: Run registry parse/count/hash projection in its own call, run check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1 alone, and never count a combined gate invocation as qualification evidence even when every visible line reports success.

entries.mistake: While measuring required reconstruction owners, the integration-audit sub-agent used a statement-form foreach directly before Format-Table. PowerShell rejected the diagnostic with an empty-pipe parser error, and the agent stopped without retry. No assigned owner, candidate, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The sub-agent repeated the REG2731 parser shape instead of materializing loop results into a named collection before formatting.
entries.prevention: Assign loop output to a ticket-specific array before any pipeline, keep measurement and formatting separate, and parser-check the bounded diagnostic before relying on its reconstruction output.

entries.mistake: Before its later parser stop, the integration-audit sub-agent grouped required reconstruction owners into output that truncated. The partial output is zero complete-read evidence, and the agent made no edit or retry. No assigned owner, candidate, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The agent combined substantive required owners without first measuring and paging them independently.
entries.prevention: Read each substantive wrapper, launcher, checker and handoff owner in an independent bounded call; measure large owners, page them through verified nonoverlapping ranges, and reject grouped truncated results in full.

entries.mistake: During a read-only producer-owner inventory, the evidence sub-agent placed a colon immediately after $rootPath in a double-quoted PowerShell string. Parsing failed before any search executed, and the agent stopped without retry or mutation. No assigned owner, candidate, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic interpolated a variable followed by punctuation without an explicit variable-name boundary, repeating the permanent colon-after-variable prevention.
entries.prevention: Use ${rootPath}: when punctuation must follow an interpolated variable, prefer format strings or separate scalar fields, and parser-check the bounded inventory command before relying on producer discovery.

entries.mistake: On its bounded reconstruction retry, the integration-audit sub-agent attempted to read REG2737 through a guessed retained-evidence filename that does not exist. Get-Content stopped before the intended owner was read, and the agent made no edit or retry. No candidate, build, Play or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The agent reconstructed a new regression filename from an assumed topic instead of resolving the exact durable owner from a bounded inventory or the parsed registry entry.
entries.prevention: Resolve every REG owner through rg --files docs/quality or the entry's literal evidence path, never derive a filename from numeric ID and remembered topic, and reuse only the returned exact path.

entries.mistake: After correcting Git and handoff reconstruction, the transaction sub-agent read the 2716-line regression memory with one raw Get-Content call. The command exited zero but its output truncated, so the partial result is zero complete-read evidence. The agent stopped without retry or mutation, and no candidate or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The agent applied the bounded-read rule to the handoff but not to the similarly dense regression-memory owner.
entries.prevention: Measure the current memory line count, read it in verified nonoverlapping bounded ranges through the final line, and never accept a successful raw read when the tool reports truncation.

entries.mistake: After completing seven bounded reads covering the full 2716-line regression memory, the transaction sub-agent attempted to read REG2742 through a guessed filename that does not exist. Get-Content exited one, and the agent stopped without discovery, retry, gate invocation or mutation. No candidate or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The agent reconstructed a new regression filename from the event summary after being instructed to resolve the literal evidence path from the registry.
entries.prevention: Read the current entry's literal evidence path from the parsed registry before opening any newly registered REG document, never turn a summary phrase into a filename, and reuse only the returned exact path.

entries.mistake: Source readback of the newly authored fixture-only retained-evidence checker found nine defined negative cases but a terminal summary literal of negative=8. The checker had not executed, and the agent stopped before correction or test. No real candidate or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The terminal summary count was manually typed before the final negative-case inventory was reconciled.
entries.prevention: Derive the reported negative total from a counter incremented by every executed negative fixture, assert it equals the declared inventory, and only then run the checker on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: After all three evidence/recovery scripts parsed on both PowerShell hosts, the first PS7 positive fixture rejected before retained-evidence validation because a normalized forward-slash state path was combined with a Windows backslash parent from Split-Path. Only a unique tmp fixture was created; no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The fixture root derived from the normalized relative state path was not itself normalized before exact aggregate-root comparison.
entries.prevention: Normalize every repository-relative fixture path and derived parent to forward slashes before exact comparison, assert detailed/aggregate/evidence roots share one normalized prefix, preserve the failed fixture and retry only under a new unique root.

entries.mistake: The first executable PowerShell 7 lifecycle fixture stopped before any transition because its fixture constructor called Clone on ordered count and authority dictionaries. OrderedDictionary does not expose that method. The transaction sub-agent stopped without retry or correction; only a unique temporary fixture was created and cleaned, and no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The fixture helper assumed PowerShell ordered dictionaries implement the same clone surface as a hashtable or another mutable collection.
entries.prevention: Build each fixture object from an explicit newly constructed ordered projection of the eight counts and four authorities, assert detailed and aggregate objects are distinct references before the first transition invocation, and rerun from a new unique root only after registration and the bounded correction.

entries.mistake: After the REG2746 constructor correction, the next first PowerShell 7 lifecycle fixture stopped during atomic detailed-state replacement because File.Replace rejected a null backup argument as an empty path. The transaction sub-agent stopped without retry or correction; the unique temporary fixture was cleaned, and no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The atomic writer assumed the four-argument System.IO.File.Replace overload accepts a null backup filename consistently across the required PowerShell and .NET hosts.
entries.prevention: Use an explicit repository-local backup path for File.Replace, remove that backup only after successful replacement, leave failures fail-closed, and exercise both new-file and existing-file atomic writes on PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell before qualification.

entries.mistake: After the REG2747 helper correction, a read-only Select-String diagnostic used a double-quoted source pattern containing $positive. Outer PowerShell expanded that token to an empty value, producing a false no-match. The agent stopped without retry, checker edit, or test, and no candidate or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic treated a PowerShell source fragment as an interpolated runtime string instead of preserving the variable token literally.
entries.prevention: Use a single-quoted literal or correctly escaped regex for source text containing PowerShell variables, assert the search pattern still contains the literal token before searching, require exactly one bounded match, and retry only after registration and the updated memory gate.

entries.mistake: The next PowerShell 7 lifecycle fixture stopped during journal commit because strict mode rejected direct assignment to undeclared committedUtc on the prepared PSCustomObject. The transaction sub-agent stopped without retry; the unique fixture was cleaned, and no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The journal implementation treated a deserialized PSCustomObject like an open dictionary and assigned lifecycle properties absent from the prepared schema under Set-StrictMode Latest.
entries.prevention: Declare every prepared, reconciled, observed, and committed journal field in the initial schema or add fields through one explicit checked property helper, assert the exact allowed property set for each status, and resume only after registration and the updated memory gate.

entries.mistake: Primary review found that the C34L recovery owner requires state.phaseGateProofs.buildSucceeded while handling the pre-transition build-in-progress state. The non-mutating candidate gate writes the proof file, but the missing transition is what would persist that state binding, so the binding cannot lawfully exist at the crash boundary. Recovery had only parsed; no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: Recovery reused a post-transition state binding as the source of a pre-transition proof instead of deriving the exact immutable attempt proof owner and validating its bytes against the current preimage.
entries.prevention: Derive the exact attempt-scoped 11b build-succeeded proof path, validate its hash and full ticket/attempt/preimage/count/authority schema directly, reject alternate or multiple owners, and exercise this exact recovery-audit crash boundary through fixture data on both hosts without a production bypass switch.

entries.mistake: After the strict-mode schema correction, the next PowerShell 7 lifecycle fixture completed one transition and rejected the following lawful transition because reconciliation required every historical committed postimage to equal the current targets. The agent stopped without retry; the fixture was cleaned, and no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: Journal reconciliation conflated immutable historical commit validation with current-head validation instead of validating an ordered transaction chain.
entries.prevention: Validate every historical journal immutably, require each committed postimage to equal the next transaction preimage, require only the newest terminal journal postimage to equal current detailed and aggregate bytes, reject forks/gaps/duplicates/unreconciled newest journals, and exercise consecutive transitions plus every crash boundary on both hosts.

entries.mistake: Primary review found that lifecycle evidence and recovery validate attempt, but prerequisite gate proofs, wrapper calls, transition proof records, journals, and retained-history matching do not bind the selected attempt end to end. The prior green fixtures did not include a wrong-attempt prerequisite proof. No production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The final proof schema attempt dimension was implemented only in produced evidence and recovery, not across the candidate-gate caller, transition, journal, and retained history interfaces.
entries.prevention: Require proof.attempt to equal transition Attempt, pass the selected attempt through wrapper proof generation and transitions, pass explicit attempt 1 from the launcher, persist ticket and attempt in proof records and journals, require retained-history parity, and add dual-host wrong-attempt negatives.

entries.mistake: Primary review found that crash reconciliation validates journal payload hashes and chain continuity but does not rehash retained prerequisite proofs or match journal proof metadata to the newest lifecycle proof record in both postimages. Missing or altered proof owners and semantic metadata tamper were not covered by the prior green fixtures. No production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The journal checker treated postimage payload hashes as sufficient transaction evidence and left the independent retained-proof and semantic-metadata trust boundary open.
entries.prevention: During reconciliation resolve and confine the exact proof owner, require its current SHA-256 and full ticket/attempt/transition/phase/pass/preimage/count/authority schema, match the newest proof record in both decoded postimages to the same tuple, and add dual-host missing/tampered proof-file plus metadata-tamper negatives.

entries.mistake: The first PowerShell 7 lifecycle fixture after the REG2752/2753 corrections stopped because strict-mode postimage validation read Count from a singleton proof-history result that PowerShell had unrolled to a scalar. The agent stopped without retry or correction, and no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The history validator did not normalize every pipeline and property result to an array before count and index operations, so the one-record runtime shape differed from the multi-record case.
entries.prevention: Normalize detailed history, aggregate history, filtered records, and paired enumerations with explicit array subexpressions before Count or indexing, and exercise zero, one, and multiple records under strict mode on both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: Before qualification, bounded readback found that the integration gate expected five global occurrences of -Attempt $preflightAttempt while the wrapper correctly contains eight because three terminal-result calls use the same token. The raw count would falsely reject. The agent stopped before patch or gate, and no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The static gate counted a shared token globally while reasoning about a specific set of proof and transition caller regions.
entries.prevention: Assert attempt propagation inside uniquely delimited helper, gate, transition, terminal-evidence, and launcher caller regions, and use any complete-file token count only as a non-semantic inventory diagnostic.

entries.mistake: After both-host transaction suites passed, a final read-only handoff command piped a statement-form foreach block directly to Format-Table and PowerShell rejected the empty pipeline element. The agent stopped without retry. A separate full status output truncated and is also inadmissible. No assigned or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The final evidence command repeated the known statement-form foreach pipeline parser shape instead of materializing rows before formatting.
entries.prevention: Assign loop output to a ticket-specific array before formatting or serialization, collect bounded file summaries, and keep branch, HEAD, and scoped status in independent commands while rejecting the failed and truncated outputs in full.

entries.mistake: During primary read-only review, a double-quoted rg regex containing $Attempt was interpolated by outer PowerShell and became an invalid unclosed group. rg exited 2 and the search was not retried. No file, candidate, or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic again treated PowerShell source text containing a variable token as an interpolated runtime string instead of preserving it as a literal regex.
entries.prevention: Use a single-quoted regex or fixed-string search for source patterns containing dollar-variable tokens, prefer separate literal searches over mixed alternation, and assert the pattern still contains the literal token before invocation.

entries.mistake: Readback of the new 18:20 handoff section found that the inline code span for prebuild-failed -FailureStage crossed a Markdown line break. The facts and hashes remain correct; the primary stopped before correction, and no candidate or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The handoff paragraph was manually wrapped inside an inline-code span instead of keeping the complete parameter phrase on one physical line.
entries.prevention: Keep short inline-code parameter phrases on one physical Markdown line, reread the inserted top section with line numbers, and reject inline-code delimiter pairs that cross a paragraph line break.

entries.mistake: Primary readback found that the newly registered PRE-AAB-4 manifest named prebuild as the first of eight candidate phases even though the established executable matrix begins with preprompt. Wave two had not started and no candidate or external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: The manifest was drafted from transition vocabulary instead of projecting the exact phase set from the qualified candidate-gate fixture and its callers.
entries.prevention: Project phase names from the executable owner, assert eight distinct exact values and caller parity before pinning a ticket hash, and update the manifest, assessment and machine-state pin atomically before execution.

entries.mistake: The PRE-AAB-1 agent requested a 700-line dense regression-memory page whose terminal result was truncated. The successful exit is not accepted as a complete mandatory read; the agent stopped without retry or mutation.
entries.rootCause: The page was bounded by line count but not by the effective output-token cap for dense content.
entries.prevention: Measure dense owners and read them through smaller independent non-overlapping pages, reject every truncation warning and cover through EOF before implementation.

entries.mistake: The PRE-AAB-3 agent searched the registry id property for shorthand REG2729, received no match and threw REG2729 missing. The agent stopped without retry or mutation.
entries.rootCause: An incident number was treated as the complete durable registry ID without discovering the exact ID or document path.
entries.prevention: Resolve incident owners with rg --files or project full registry IDs by their exact numeric segment, then read only the discovered literal path; never invent shorthand registry keys.

entries.mistake: The PRE-AAB-2 agent added a new 319-line journey evidence writer in one patch instead of a small scaffold plus bounded sections. Readback caught the process defect before parser or behavioral testing; the untracked owner is preserved and no production or external state changed.
entries.rootCause: The final owner size was estimated below the bounded-edit threshold rather than measured and staged before the Add File patch.
entries.prevention: Create a minimal parseable scaffold for every near-threshold owner, add functions and execution in bounded reviewed patches, measure exact lines and bytes after each section, and preserve rather than rewrite an already-created owner solely to conceal process history.

entries.mistake: The PRE-AAB-2 parser wrapper used a diagnostic string with a colon immediately after an interpolated path variable. PowerShell rejected the wrapper before any assigned source parser ran; the agent stopped without retry or mutation.
entries.rootCause: A known colon-after-interpolated-variable parser class was repeated in diagnostic-only wrapper text.
entries.prevention: Build parser and test diagnostic rows with the format operator or explicit concatenation and never place a colon directly after an interpolated variable name.

entries.mistake: Primary coordination named only REG2763 without its exact durable filename, after which the PRE-AAB-1 agent guessed a nonexistent path and Get-Content failed. The agent stopped without retry; two prior selection-only JSON files remain preserved and no candidate or external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: The resume message omitted the exact evidence path and the receiver guessed a conventional filename instead of discovering it.
entries.prevention: Include the exact durable incident path in every resume instruction; when absent, resolve it with bounded rg --files before any Get-Content and never infer a filename from the incident description.

entries.mistake: Before the REG2762 notice arrived, the PRE-AAB-3 agent added a 689-line blocker/browser integration checker in one patch. After reading the new entries and passing the memory gate, it measured and stopped before parser, test, retry or further mutation; no browser or external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: Contract logic, fixture builders and the negative matrix were combined without a parseable scaffold and bounded measured section patches.
entries.prevention: Scaffold every large checker first, add helper and fixture sections in small patches with exact line/byte readback, and preserve plus bounded-review an already-created owner rather than delete or recreate it to hide process history.

entries.mistake: The PRE-AAB-3 PowerShell 7 parser wrapper embedded parser source variables in an outer double-quoted -Command string. The outer host expanded them and produced an empty pipeline parser error before the assigned checker parser ran; the agent stopped without retry or test.
entries.rootCause: Parser code crossed an interpolating PowerShell command-string boundary instead of using a literal script block or direct executable owner invocation.
entries.prevention: Use direct -File for executable owners and a single-quoted literal script block or already-qualified non-interpolating parser wrapper for parse-only checks; never transport parser source variables through double-quoted -Command text.

entries.mistake: The first PowerShell 7 producer fixture wrote under a producer-specific temporary prefix, while the authoritative retained-evidence checker accepts only its exact retained-evidence fixture prefix. The round trip failed before negatives; the fixture is preserved and no production or external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: The new checker invented a parallel fixture namespace rather than projecting the authoritative retained-checker confinement contract.
entries.prevention: Use the exact tmp/c34l-retained-evidence-fixtures-* root with state and aggregate inside it, keep the retained checker strict, preserve the failed fixture, and rerun only under a fresh unique root after memory replay.

entries.mistake: Independent audit found that green PRE-AAB-3 fixtures missed canonical ledger aliases, source-phase readiness composition, durable browser proof mirroring, canonical unique-root fixture confinement and cryptographic session freshness. PRE-AAB-4 was paused before mutation; no browser, release or external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: The integration contract validated external input shape and raw path strings but did not project canonical file identity and session-bound browser evidence through both candidate states and the emitted prerequisite proof across source and preupload phases.
entries.prevention: Canonicalize and compare manifest owner identity, compose source ledger exclusion, mirror browser path/hash/bytes/session/routes in both states and proof output, canonicalize exact fixture run roots, require bounded producer-issued session freshness, and add dual-host negatives for each boundary before phase-matrix work.

entries.mistake: The independent PRE-AAB-2 auditor read the dense 1,092-line transition owner with one Get-Content -Raw result and received a truncation warning. The auditor stopped without retry, fixture execution or edit; no external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: The known dense owner was not measured and read through bounded non-overlapping pages before audit work.
entries.prevention: Read the transition in independently returned pages no larger than 200 lines, reject any truncation warning and cover exact EOF before resuming the audit or running producer fixtures.

entries.mistake: Independent audit found that PRE-AAB-3 requires browser proof transition upload-succeeded at preupload, while the canonical lifecycle maps upload-authorized to preupload and upload-succeeded to postupload. Green fixtures did not compare the tuple with the lifecycle map; no release or external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: The browser proof schema chose an outcome transition name independently from the qualified lifecycle transition-to-phase map.
entries.prevention: Bind browser proof to upload-authorized/preupload, keep Play outcome evidence at upload-succeeded/postupload, project tuples from the canonical map and add wrong-transition plus cross-phase dual-host negatives.

entries.mistake: Primary REG2768 and REG2770 registrations listed the not-yet-created C34L candidate-gate script as a current gate. The memory gate rejected the missing repository evidence path and no retry or implementation action followed.
entries.rootCause: A future enforcement dependency was placed in the active registry gate list rather than described as pending prose.
entries.prevention: Require every registry gate and evidence path to exist literally at registration time; keep future owners in prose and add them to later completion evidence only after creation and qualification.

entries.mistake: Readback found upload_authorized_preprompt in the new PRE-AAB-3-FIX1 manifest instead of the canonical upload-authorized/preupload tuple. The ticket was not yet hashed, pinned or executed and no external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: Two valid phase names were concatenated during manual lifecycle tuple transcription.
entries.prevention: Project transition and phase as separate exact values from the canonical map, scan every manifest lifecycle token before hashing and reject concatenated tuples.

entries.mistake: The batch assessment table placed order 3-FIX1 after order 4 even though the dependency list requires the repair first. Identities and hashes were correct; no repair execution or external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: An append-style table insertion was used for a dependency-ordered human execution table.
entries.prevention: Compare assessment row order with the numbered dependency sequence before scope replay; keep human execution tables dependency-ordered even when machine registration arrays append history.

entries.mistake: The transition-repair assignment named REG2729 without its exact path and the agent guessed a nonexistent descriptive filename. Get-Content failed and the agent stopped without discovery, retry, edit or test.
entries.rootCause: Primary coordination omitted the literal required owner and the receiver inferred a filename rather than using bounded path discovery.
entries.prevention: Include exact paths for every mandatory incident in agent assignments; otherwise resolve with rg --files before Get-Content and never infer a descriptive filename.

entries.mistake: The PRE-AAB-1 FIX1 agent requested a 160-line slice of the dense blocker/browser checker and the result was truncated by available model context. The agent stopped without retry, edit or test.
entries.rootCause: The page was bounded by lines without accounting for dense bytes per line and the current result budget after compaction.
entries.prevention: Read the dense checker in independent non-overlapping pages no larger than 80 lines, reject every truncated result and cover exact EOF before FIX1 mutation.

entries.mistake: The PRE-AAB-1 FIX1 agent invoked an unverified absolute PowerShell 7 executable and an abbreviated guessed memory-gate filename. The executable was not resolved, the gate did not run and the agent stopped without retry, edit or test.
entries.rootCause: Qualified runtime and gate-owner paths were retyped from convention instead of reused or resolved from the saved environment.
entries.prevention: Invoke the available pwsh command with exact scripts/check-codex-development-regression-memory.ps1, resolve both owners read-only before use and never hard-code installation or abbreviate established gate paths.

entries.mistake: The first PRE-AAB-3-FIX1 PowerShell 7 self-test rejected its positive browser fixture because producedUtc did not satisfy the new exact UTC timestamp validator. The agent stopped without diagnostic, retry or patch; cleanup completed and no external action occurred.
entries.rootCause: Timestamp fixture serialization and validation were added independently without one shared invariant round-trip wire format.
entries.prevention: Define one invariant UTC formatter and exact parse/round-trip contract, generate the positive fixture through it and add malformed, non-UTC, expired and future-issued negatives on both hosts.

entries.mistake: The fresh PS7 fixture correctly retained the pretransition upload authority in browser proof and correctly advanced current state after upload-authorized, but persisted-mode checker logic compared the preimage proof vector with post-state and rejected. The agent stopped without retry or patch.
entries.rootCause: Pretransition prerequisite-proof semantics and post-transition current-state semantics were collapsed into one vector comparison.
