entries.rootCause: Precreation confinement required the immediate parent rather than validating the nearest existing ancestor and the exact missing contract-owned chain.
entries.prevention: Validate nearest existing ancestor and reparse-free canonical mapping, create only exact producer-owned components, re-resolve before write, and add absent/wrong/reparse/file/sibling/partial-chain fixtures.

entries.mistake: The first integrated authoritative PS7 run advanced through Play and OPPO but the journey final writer referenced captureValues before initialization under its receipt-only parameter set.
entries.rootCause: Parameter-set control flow reached a shared validation/serialization site before every valid branch constructed the required capture-derived structure.
entries.prevention: Initialize exact branch data before shared sites or keep branches separate, assert StrictMode variables, cover production receipt/fixture receipt/legacy fixture/invalid cross-parameter cases, then rerun PS7 before WinPS.

entries.mistake: The first direct PS7 v3 source-attestation suite rejected its legacy missing fixture outside the v2-era exact expected class.
entries.rootCause: The fixture oracle was not aligned to contract v3 mandatory receipt validation order and class.
entries.prevention: Capture only the sanitized actual class, ensure the fixture removes only one intended v3 requirement, align one exact oracle, audit remaining negatives for masking, then rerun direct and combined suites on both hosts.

entries.mistake: After the v3 missing oracle advanced, the direct PS7 source-attestation type fixture rejected outside its v2-era exact expected class.
entries.rootCause: Remaining negative mutations/oracles were not comprehensively remapped to contract v3 validation order and authoritative receipt bindings.
entries.prevention: Inspect sanitized type class, inventory every remaining label/mutation/oracle before rerun, isolate each mutation after all earlier v3 invariants, keep exact classes, then run direct and combined suites on both hosts.

entries.mistake: The full default PS7 v3 combined gate reached the legacy OPPO prohibited-ADB-install negative but rejected outside its old expected class.
entries.rootCause: The legacy negative mutation/oracle was not yet aligned to authoritative receipt preconditions and v3 validation order.
entries.prevention: Capture only sanitized class, construct an otherwise valid authoritative OPPO receipt with only the prohibited observation changed, keep all real device actions zero, audit remaining default negatives, then rerun PS7 before WinPS.

entries.mistake: The existing Play-installed r60.72 launch returned ok but MoolSocial was not the resumed foreground activity at the guarded follow-up check.
entries.rootCause: The exact launcher/lock/crash/system destination is unknown because privacy policy correctly stopped inspection outside MoolSocial.
entries.prevention: After registration inspect only sanitized foreground package and allowed MoolSocial process/fatal/ANR facts; never inspect non-MoolSocial UI, and hand off any private/system surface to the founder.

entries.mistake: The primary guessed regression-memory phase testing even though the gate accepts device for OPPO diagnostics.
entries.rootCause: A gate enum was inferred instead of using the exact validated interface.
entries.prevention: Use exact -Phase device -BuildMode none for device work; never guess ValidateSet values; treat rejection as blocking until registered and rerun.

entries.mistake: Three authentication inventory agents independently emitted the full known-large dirty worktree because AGENTS.md literally required that command; all outputs truncated before later action.
entries.rootCause: The older full-status instruction conflicted with the newer bounded coordination policy.
entries.prevention: Require independent scalar branch/HEAD, non-emitting porcelain-z digest, branch-header-only projection and literal claim-scoped status; prohibit full dirty-status output and machine-check the instruction tokens.

entries.mistake: The strengthened coordination gate falsely rejected required AGENTS prose because its exact token crossed a Markdown line wrap.
entries.rootCause: Literal Contains checks treated semantic Markdown whitespace as byte-exact authority.
entries.prevention: Normalize whitespace before prose checks and retain exact checks only for stable code literals/headings; rerun the gate before any subagent resumes.

entries.mistake: The X inventory agent grouped all mandatory owners with dense regression memory in one result, which truncated before gates or later action.
entries.rootCause: Mandatory reconstruction was treated as one aggregate output instead of independent owners and bounded memory pages.
entries.prevention: Read each mandatory owner independently, page regression memory in non-overlapping <=250-line results through EOF, never group it, and machine-check the instruction tokens.

entries.mistake: The X inventory agent interpreted current bounded checkpoint as the complete append-only active handoff and the output truncated before gates or later action.
entries.rootCause: Policy did not define an exact leading-section boundary discovery algorithm.
entries.prevention: Discover only first two level-two heading lines, read lines 1 through before the second heading in independent <=250-line pages, prohibit full handoff reads, and machine-check the tokens.

entries.mistake: X and Facebook inventory agents independently raw-read the 5,166-line MVP scope state and both outputs truncated before gates or later action.
entries.rootCause: Mandatory policy lacked a bounded semantic projection for the append-heavy JSON owner.
entries.prevention: Parse without full emission; project metadata/root names/current ticket-disclosure-authority-execution-checkpoint-provider subtrees only; query named history on demand; machine-check the rule.

entries.mistake: The coordination gate exited 0 while its pass line retained literal format placeholders instead of concrete policy/task/claim/generation evidence.
entries.rootCause: The PowerShell result string did not apply the format operator to the full placeholder expression.
entries.prevention: Format one complete expression with exact values, assert no placeholder remains, and qualify identical concrete output on PS7 and WinPS before subagents resume.

entries.mistake: The supported-auth agent bounded the top-level MVP state but enumerated every nested historical pre-ticket assessment and the output truncated before gates/action.
entries.rootCause: The bounded projection rule did not define exact current checkpoint scalar and selected-assessment fields.
entries.prevention: Project five checkpoint scalars plus selectedTicketAssessment only, read history by explicit property, prohibit enumeration, and machine-check the rule.

entries.mistake: The bounded X status digest emitted one VoidTaskResult helper object despite correctly suppressing all status paths/body.
entries.rootCause: CopyToAsync().GetResult() was not assigned to null and entered the PowerShell success pipeline.
entries.prevention: Assign helper returns to null, enforce an exact five-field digest output allowlist, reject extra output, and machine-check the instruction tokens.

entries.mistake: The guarded OPPO check used the first generic dumpsys activity top ACTIVITY row as sole foreground authority and disagreed with the founder-visible MoolSocial state.
entries.rootCause: Generic ACTIVITY row ordering may not identify the top-resumed package on this OPPO, or foreground changed at the query instant.
entries.prevention: Require sanitized agreement from topResumed/mResumed activity and WindowManager current-focus/focused-app fields before UI inspection; never rely on the first generic ACTIVITY row.

entries.mistake: Two private account identifiers were included in founder chat while reporting the repeated r60.72 Google failure.
entries.rootCause: The device handoff did not constrain the founder report to sanitized outcome/error class strongly enough before the retry report.
entries.prevention: Never repeat or persist identifiers; founder reports only sanitized completed/cancelled/public-error outcomes; stop r60.72 retries; require enumerated error telemetry and a new qualified Play candidate.

entries.mistake: The C34P primary attempted to read an exact source-map path inherited from a stale prior-task coordination claim, but the planned owner did not exist.
entries.rootCause: The prior task claim remained active after closure and was incorrectly treated as existence evidence for an output that had never been created.
entries.prevention: Remove closed prior-task claims, require exact existence checks for planned evidence owners, and resolve current authentication owners only from bounded file inventories plus exact symbol searches without guessing a replacement path.

entries.mistake: The C34P primary requested the complete Apple-inspired product design memory in one raw result and the tool truncated the output.
entries.rootCause: The substantive owner was not line-counted before a complete read even though its accumulated history exceeds the safe output boundary.
entries.prevention: Measure substantive required owners first and read dense documents in independent non-overlapping pages of at most 250 lines through verified EOF; reject every truncated page.

entries.mistake: The C34P primary passed the complete MVP-state line array to Select-String -InputObject for physical top-level key line discovery, so the first required key was falsely reported missing.
entries.rootCause: Collection input did not preserve the physical file line ownership required by Select-String line-number output.
entries.prevention: Use Select-String -LiteralPath once per anchored top-level key, project only one scalar LineNumber, require exactly one result for every key, then read only the resulting non-overlapping literal ranges.

entries.mistake: The C34P primary attempted one combined patch across the current-ticket ID, complete selected assessment and retained C34L label; context verification rejected the patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: A long dense-owner replacement made the complete transition depend on every rendered context line matching exactly instead of using small verified state hunks.
entries.prevention: Patch one bounded MVP-state field group at a time from freshly read exact context, parse and project each accepted hunk before the next, recompute the manifest hash from disk, and run both scope gates only after complete readback.

entries.mistake: A two-line C34P disposition/owner hunk matched another historical C34L assessment; the current selected assessment stayed unchanged while a historical subtree was modified.
entries.rootCause: The hunk used repeated field values without the unique current C34P ticket or manifest context inside an append-heavy JSON owner.
entries.prevention: Locate and restore the wrong historical node by the unique inserted owner literal, then require the current C34P ticketId or another unique current anchor in every later hunk and verify both current and named historical values immediately.

entries.mistake: The C34P primary retyped one C34L dependency token with a space instead of its exact underscore, so the small dependencies hunk was atomically rejected.
entries.rootCause: Exact machine-state context was reconstructed from visual memory instead of copied verbatim from the current JSON line.
entries.prevention: Re-read and copy the single literal current dependencies line byte-for-byte for patch context, change only that line, and immediately parse/project the current dependency array before another hunk.

entries.mistake: The re-read current dependency line looked identical to the one-line patch context, but apply_patch still rejected the hunk; the rendered line was not byte-faithful evidence.
entries.rootCause: Visible PowerShell rendering did not expose the byte or character difference preventing exact patch matching, and repeating it would not be evidence-based.
entries.prevention: Inspect only the physical line byte length and non-ASCII positions, do not issue the same hunk again, and use unique adjacent short anchors or a byte-faithful bounded raw slice for the next operation with immediate parsed readback.

entries.mistake: The C34P byte-inspection command used an interpolated $i immediately followed by a colon, and PowerShell rejected the command before execution.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic repeated the durable PowerShell variable-colon interpolation prohibition.
entries.prevention: Use the format operator for position/code pairs, avoid interpolation in the corrected read-only diagnostic, emit only bounded comparison scalars, and never retry the parser-rejected form.

entries.mistake: The Facebook subagent's raw-byte status digest emitted two VoidTaskResult helper values in addition to the five allowed scalars and stopped before any later action.
entries.rootCause: Two GetAwaiter().GetResult() calls were not assigned to null, repeating the helper-output contamination already preserved by REG2945.
entries.prevention: Suppress every async helper return, require exactly five allowlisted digest lines with no VoidTaskResult text, reread the literal incident, refresh regression memory and pass the coordination gate against the primary-provided generation before resuming.

entries.mistake: The Facebook subagent created a 353-line new source in one apply_patch instead of scaffold plus bounded section patches, then stopped before its test owner or tools.
entries.rootCause: The planned source size was not estimated and the over-300-line bounded-construction rule was not applied before the first write.
entries.prevention: Primary-review the preserved source in exact non-overlapping <=100-line windows; use fresh local hunks for corrections; build the missing test owner through bounded sections; format only assigned owners and wait for the serialized test window.

entries.mistake: The primary focused Flutter analyzer rejected the auth fake's unused providerFailure optional parameter after X and Facebook generic dispatch were removed.
entries.rootCause: The fake was expanded for two failure seams, but only the Google credential seam remained reachable after the simultaneous fail-closed provider correction.
entries.prevention: Remove the unused constructor parameter, field and branch; retain the reachable Google failure seam; format the exact test; run the no-diff format check and rerun the same focused analyzer before tests.

entries.mistake: The X subagent's focused analyzer exited zero but reported two use_null_aware_elements info findings in its test owner and the subagent stopped before retry or tests.
entries.rootCause: Two conditional collection elements guarded nullable values explicitly instead of using the current analyzer-preferred null-aware collection-element form.
entries.prevention: Reread the literal incident and exact local region, replace only the two reported elements, format and no-diff-check the test owner, rerun the same analyzer, and wait for the primary's serialized test window.

entries.mistake: The primary placed statement-form if expressions directly inside PSCustomObject property values in a four-owner metric projection, causing a pre-execution parser rejection.
entries.rootCause: Conditional metric values were not resolved into explicit scalars before object construction, repeating the durable PowerShell object-property rule.
entries.prevention: Compute exists, lines and bytes as local scalars inside the loop, construct uniform rows afterward, materialize loop results before serialization, and still read dense sources in independent bounded windows.

entries.mistake: The focused X PKCE test failed +4 -8 because Uri.replace(query: null) retained the query; valid callbacks were rejected as wrongRedirect before state, denial, expiry and cardinality checks.
entries.rootCause: The contract incorrectly assumed null clears an existing Uri query and fragment, while Dart treats null as retain-current for this API.
entries.prevention: Use one fresh query-and-fragment-free Uri base projection for authorization and callback comparisons, retain the direct base assertion, rerun format and clean analysis, then run one primary-authorized serialized focused test.

entries.mistake: The passed X source described revocation as requiring only token, omitting the public client_id required by the X OAuth 2.0 public-client revocation request, and its test missed the complete field inventory.
entries.rootCause: Revocation coverage checked endpoint, method, content type and no client secret but did not assert every required public-client form field.
entries.prevention: Require the exact token+client_id form-field set, retain the no-client-secret/no-network/no-persistence assertions, clean-analyze both owners and run one new serialized focused test that supersedes the earlier pass.

entries.mistake: The X PKCE source hand-implemented SHA-256 despite the mobile package already pinning the maintained crypto dependency, adding unnecessary security-critical code.
entries.rootCause: Dependency-free was misread as no package imports rather than no new provider SDK/network dependency, so an existing tested cryptographic owner was not inventoried or reused.
entries.prevention: Use package:crypto for SHA-256, remove the complete manual primitive, retain RFC 7636 known-vector coverage, format and clean-analyze both owners, then run one serialized focused test; inventory pinned crypto before new security code.

entries.mistake: The first C34P static gate rejected the qualified crypto import because it required the package URI without the actual `as crypto` alias.
entries.rootCause: The static oracle asserted one interchangeable import spelling instead of the freshly read formatter-stable declaration or a stable package URI invariant.
entries.prevention: Bind the gate to the exact current aliased import, retain independent no-manual-round-constants and RFC7636 assertions, then parse and run the corrected gate on PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.

entries.mistake: At founder resume, the primary printed workspace and repository AGENTS.md in one command/result even though every mandatory owner requires an independent command/result.
entries.rootCause: A convenience reconstruction command was reused instead of applying the independent-owner rule at the new execution boundary.
entries.prevention: After registration, read the workspace and repository AGENTS owners in two independent results, replay regression memory and coordination against the refreshed generation, and only then select blocker tickets or edit owners.

entries.mistake: The Facebook native subagent's bounded status digest returned exitCode=null because its helper disposed the native process before projecting ExitCode; it stopped before any write or tool action.
entries.rootCause: The process lifetime ended before all five mandatory evidence fields were copied into durable scalar values.
entries.prevention: Wait for completion, copy ExitCode to a ticket-named non-null integer scalar, only then dispose process and streams, emit exactly five allowlisted lines, refresh memory/coordination on the new generation, and reread the literal incident before retry.

entries.mistake: The REG2966 retry preserved exitCode=0 but emitted a sixth VoidTaskResult line from an unsuppressed stdout task GetResult; the Facebook subagent stopped before any write or tool action.
entries.rootCause: The correction fixed process lifetime but failed to suppress every asynchronous helper return, repeating REG2945 and REG2956.
entries.prevention: Assign both stdout/stderr GetResult calls to null or void, assert exactly five lines and zero VoidTaskResult text, refresh all agent gates, and permanently transfer the work to primary if the class recurs a third time.

entries.mistake: The primary combined founder disclosure, authorization, checkpoint and provider-gate FIX1A changes in one state patch; exact checkpoint context failed and the operation was atomically rejected.
entries.rootCause: Four distant state sections were coupled and one checkpoint value was manually transcribed instead of applying the registered one-group/readback discipline.
entries.prevention: Read and patch disclosure, authorization, checkpoint and provider gate independently with immediate parsed readback; verify FIX1A manifest/current/selected/prior identities and rerun delivery plus MVP execution gates before implementation resumes.

entries.mistake: The independent FIX1A checkpoint hunk used a displayed parsed approvalState projection as literal removal context; apply_patch could not match it and rejected the operation atomically.
entries.rootCause: A semantic JSON projection was treated as byte-preserving patch context, contrary to the registered raw-line state-edit rule.
entries.prevention: Locate and read the one physical approvalState line inside the verified checkpoint boundary, copy it verbatim into a one-line patch, parse immediately, and use the same raw-line approach separately for provider nextTicket and state.

entries.mistake: After locating the exact raw approvalState line, the primary manually changed external_provider to external provider in patch removal context; exact verification rejected it atomically.
entries.rootCause: The raw line was retyped instead of transferred byte-for-byte, repeating the machine-token transcription class.
entries.prevention: Use the exact returned raw line with every underscore and space unchanged in a one-line patch, parse checkpoint immediately, then independently locate provider-gate raw lines before editing them.

entries.mistake: After provider nextTicket changed successfully, the visibly printed raw provider state line still failed exact one-line patch matching; the hunk was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: The apparent raw line had an unproven character or spacing difference; repeating it without ordinal comparison would be guesswork.
entries.prevention: Compare physical line and intended removal literal by length/ordinal/first mismatch without emitting the body, then patch the unique two-line block anchored by the corrected FIX1A nextTicket and parse immediately.

entries.mistake: The all-eight coordination-policy owner patch response exceeded the available model context, so its mutation result could not be trusted from the tool response alone.
entries.rootCause: The policy mutation and surrounding output crossed the response boundary before a concise success result was available.
entries.prevention: Use a bounded post-mutation JSON parse that proves each intended owner occurs exactly once and that no owner overlaps exist; never retry a truncated patch before that reconciliation.

entries.mistake: The primary invoked the coordination checker without its mandatory role, task and expected registry-generation parameters; PowerShell rejected the invocation.
entries.rootCause: The checker was treated as though it supported a parameterless repository-wide mode despite its mandatory identity and generation contract.
entries.prevention: Read the parameter block and invoke with exact AgentRole, AgentTask, UseRecordedClaim, ExpectedRegistryEntryCount and ExpectedRegistrySha256 values; a binding rejection never authorizes execution.

entries.mistake: The X-broker subagent received an empty structured result from a bounded same-owner append and was stopped before the mandatory owner readback, leaving that append unverified.
entries.rootCause: The primary registry-movement stop arrived between the patch response and the required bounded readback, so the response alone was insufficient evidence of success or failure.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, read back the owner before any retry; accept an exact-one landed section without reapplying, or apply only the proven-absent bounded section once and immediately read it back.

entries.mistake: The primary attempted to inspect the claimed FIX1 delivery checker, but the filesystem reported that the claimed script path does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The coordination claim was treated as proof that the owner had already been materialized, although claims define write ownership rather than file existence.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, enumerate only bounded C34P script filenames, reconcile any alternate name, and invoke the proven file or create the claimed checker as a small scaffold plus bounded patches.

entries.mistake: REG2975 listed the absent FIX1 delivery checker in its evidence array, causing the regression-memory gate to reject the entry because evidence paths must exist.
entries.rootCause: The missing subject of the incident was mistaken for a durable evidence artifact even though absence must be described in narrative or structured fields.
entries.prevention: Reference only verified existing artifacts in evidence arrays; record missing paths in mistake or incident narrative, then remove the invalid reference and repin the corrected registry hash before retry.

entries.mistake: A targeted rg invocation included an integration-test path that the preceding inventory had already proven absent, causing a native missing-file diagnostic.
entries.rootCause: The planned creation owner was not filtered out of the existing-file search input list.
entries.prevention: Construct targeted search inputs only from verified existing paths or search a bounded existing directory with exact include patterns; never pass a proven-absent owner to a native read command.

entries.mistake: The required REG2974 bounded X-broker owner readback returned process exit code zero but completely empty stdout, leaving every intended scalar unproven.
entries.rootCause: The multi-statement PowerShell projection did not provide a durable single serialized result even though the process itself completed successfully.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, create one compact JSON projection, assert nonempty stdout and exact parsed properties, and only then decide whether the prior bounded source append landed or is absent.

entries.mistake: The X-mobile subagent issued its first bounded add-file scaffold immediately before the stop notice, received an empty structured result, and could not perform the mandatory readback.
entries.rootCause: Registry movement interrupted the required post-mutation verification boundary, so the tool response alone could not prove whether the scaffold landed.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, project existence, line count, hash and one scaffold signature as compact JSON; continue without retry if present, or create once only if proven absent.

entries.mistake: REG2979 listed the X-mobile source owner as evidence even though its existence remained intentionally ambiguous, repeating the REG2976 prevention class.
entries.rootCause: The incident subject was again treated as a durable evidence artifact before owner existence had been verified.
entries.prevention: For mutation-ambiguity incidents, cite only verified registry, policy and incident-document paths; keep the ambiguous owner in narrative fields until refreshed-gate readback proves existence.

entries.mistake: The Facebook adapter assumed grantedPermissions and declinedPermissions getters on flutter_facebook_auth 7.2.0 AccessToken, and nine constructors retained prefer_initializing_formals infos.
entries.rootCause: The adapter was written against an assumed richer access-token surface instead of the pinned plugin's actual base AccessToken API; constructor lint cleanup was deferred until analyzer discovery.
entries.prevention: Map a successful exact-public_profile SDK request through the real result surface, retain explicit denial only on the injected test seam, convert constructors to initializing formals, then require format/no-diff/analyze before Flutter tests.

entries.mistake: The REG2981 lint remediation used same-class generative redirection with private named initializing formals, producing 18 missing or undefined named-parameter analyzer errors.
entries.rootCause: Dart redirect call sites resolved against the public constructor parameter names rather than the private field-formal names assumed by the correction.
entries.prevention: Preserve public named factory constructors, delegate to private positional initializing-formal constructors, and require format/no-diff plus zero-issue focused analysis before Facebook tests.

entries.mistake: The X-broker subagent issued its first bounded backend-test scaffold immediately before a registry stop and could not perform the mandatory readback after an empty structured patch result.
entries.rootCause: Registry movement interrupted the post-mutation verification boundary, leaving test-owner existence unproven from the response alone.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, project existence, line count, hash and one signature as compact JSON; continue without retry if present, or create once only if proven absent, and keep the ambiguous path out of evidence.

entries.mistake: After one REG2982 constructor correction landed, the next Facebook client-constructor patch reused remembered pre-format context and was atomically rejected.
entries.rootCause: The exact current indentation and constructor layout were not reread after the preceding formatted correction changed the region.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, read only the current constructor region, patch that one constructor with exact present context, and immediately read it back before touching the next constructor.

entries.mistake: The X test imported nonexistent package:moolsocial_v2 and the source retained five prefer_initializing_formals infos, producing 49 focused analyzer findings.
entries.rootCause: The test package name was assumed instead of read from pubspec, and constructor lint cleanup was deferred; 44 symbol and const findings cascade from the unresolved import.
entries.prevention: Read the exact pubspec package name and current five constructors, correct only those owners, format/no-diff, and rerun the same two-owner analyzer before interpreting downstream findings or running tests.

entries.mistake: Facebook signIn returned _completeSignIn(response) without await inside its try, so asynchronous FirebaseAuthException and generic credential failures bypassed sanitized catch mapping; 9 adapter tests passed and 2 failed.
entries.rootCause: Returning the Future transferred error completion outside the lexical async try/catch boundary even though the success path appeared structurally enclosed.
entries.prevention: Await the completion Future inside the try, then require format/no-diff, zero-issue focused analysis and a serialized rerun of only the failed adapter test file; retain the green 19/19 contract evidence.

entries.mistake: The first shared-auth integration analyzer found three callback-interface undefined-method errors, one missing accountIneligible switch case, and two revocation-seam initializing-formal infos.
entries.rootCause: The callback local retained its declared SocialAuthGateway type across the separate type check, the mobile adapter added a truthful terminal outcome after integration drafting, and the named constructor assigned fields manually.
entries.prevention: Bind an explicitly promoted SocialAuthCallbackGateway local, exhaustively map accountIneligible to its sanitized terminal failure, use a private positional initializing-formal constructor, then format/no-diff and rerun the identical nine-owner analyzer before tests.

entries.mistake: The cold Instagram callback test expected exact return to /app/social?sub=photos even though photos is not an accepted social sub-route; canonicalization correctly fell back to /app/social, so 46 tests passed and the invalid fixture failed.
entries.rootCause: The new test fixture was chosen without first reading the existing accepted social sub-route allow-list of shorts, videos, feed and create; the callback lifecycle itself preserved valid query-bearing routes.
entries.prevention: Read the router/canonicalization allow-list before exact-return fixtures, assert foreground videos and cold feed preservation plus unsupported-route fallback, then rerun the affected test before the full focused set.

entries.mistake: A bounded rg evidence lookup included the coordination-claimed FIX1 qualification report path even though that owner had not been materialized, producing a native missing-file diagnostic.
entries.rootCause: The coordination claim was again treated as file-existence proof instead of write ownership; only the prior C34P source report existed and yielded the retained 110/110 cycle lines.
entries.prevention: Project existence before multi-path native reads, pass only verified files, and create the claimed FIX1A qualification report only after current source/backend/regression evidence is complete.

entries.mistake: The Facebook revocation endpoint negative matrix treated explicit default HTTPS port :443 as invalid, but Dart normalized it to the identical valid URI; 17 tests passed and this one fixture failed.
entries.rootCause: The fixture assumed URI source spelling remains observable after parsing even when the explicit port equals the scheme default.
entries.prevention: Remove only the indistinguishable :443 fixture, retain all semantically different endpoint negatives, format/no-diff/analyze, and rerun exactly the adapter test file in a serialized window.

entries.mistake: The first FIX1A source-gate execution referenced mvp.currentTicket.ticketId, but that property does not exist in the persisted MVP state schema, so the gate stopped before source assertions.
entries.rootCause: A semantic reconstruction label was used as a literal JSON selector without projecting the exact top-level persisted property names.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, project only MVP top-level keys and bounded ticket identity nodes, patch the one proven selector, and rerun PowerShell 7 before Windows PowerShell compatibility.

entries.mistake: The FIX1A gate required literal revokeAccessToken(accessToken in the X broker even though the implemented and tested revocation method uses different local parameter or call spelling.
entries.rootCause: The gate asserted an unstable local variable name instead of a semantic revocation method signature and awaited call-site contract.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, project exact X revocation signature and call lines, assert stable method plus awaited invocation tokens, and rerun the same PowerShell 7 gate.

entries.mistake: After the current approved UI lock passed, the primary invoked the historical C30X FIX1 Screen03 creation gate under selected C34P FIX1A scope, and it correctly rejected the changed selected ticket.
entries.rootCause: A ticket-bound creation/acceptance gate was treated as a generic successor replay gate even though it deliberately requires its original scope state.
entries.prevention: Do not edit or retry the C30X historical gate under C34P; use the approved UI lock, current C34P gates, protected Screen03 session tests, and only an explicit generic-successor replay gate when available.

entries.mistake: The resumed primary grouped both mandatory instruction reads with a prohibited full git status and raw complete handoff read, emitting and truncating the dirty-path and append-only handoff output classes.
entries.rootCause: Repository-specific independent and bounded reconstruction rules were applied only after the concurrent diagnostic had already started, repeating the grouped-owner recurrence.
entries.prevention: Read each instruction owner independently, discover only the first two handoff headings and read the leading checkpoint in bounded pages, and reconcile Git only through independent branch/HEAD scalars plus a non-emitting status digest.

entries.mistake: The bounded raw-byte dirty digest retained bytes, records, SHA-256 and zero stderr but disposed its process before copying ExitCode, so the required exit-code field was blank.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper repeated REG2966 by releasing the process object before projecting its completed native exit into a stable scalar.
entries.prevention: Capture stdout/stderr completely, wait for exit, copy ExitCode into a task-specific scalar, then dispose and emit exactly the five allowlisted digest fields with no blanks.

entries.mistake: The primary projected all narrative fields for 46 C34P registry-tail entries in one result and the 15,911-token output was truncated.
entries.rootCause: The entry count was bounded but aggregate rendered size was not measured before emission.
entries.prevention: Project IDs/count/hash separately, locate the last exact ID and line, and read only measured independent bounded groups or the small literal append tail; reject every truncated group.

entries.mistake: The /root recorded claim retained a nonexistent superseded FIX1 integration-test owner, yet UseRecordedClaim passed because the checker did not assert recorded-owner existence.
entries.rootCause: A superseded planning path remained after FIX1A materialization and the recorded-claim validation covered uniqueness and membership but not leaf existence.
entries.prevention: Remove the nonexistent claim, retain the exact existing FIX1A owner, require every recorded owner to exist as a repository leaf, and add a negative fixture proving a missing recorded owner fails closed.

entries.mistake: The replay-protected public-auth backend consumes App Check tokens while the production Flutter supplier acquires a normal cached session token, and mock adapter tests do not execute that composition.
entries.rootCause: Backend consume semantics and mobile token acquisition were implemented in separate owners without a source or behavior gate binding consume true to Flutter limited-use-token acquisition.
entries.prevention: Use FirebaseAppCheck.getLimitedUseToken for every X/Instagram public-auth request, reject blank output, retain backend consume and replay rejection, add an executable source composition assertion, and hold live completion until the verifier IAM role is founder-read back.

entries.mistake: The first policy readback placed unary -not directly before a parameterized Test-Path invocation, and PowerShell rejected the command before parsing policy state.
entries.rootCause: The complete cmdlet invocation was not first resolved or parenthesized as a boolean expression.
entries.prevention: Resolve Test-Path into an explicit scalar, negate only that scalar, and keep parsing, claim selection and missing-owner counting as simple sequential statements before projection.

entries.mistake: A 12/12 X PKCE suite contained one test that explicitly approved offline.access behind an optional refresh lifecycle even though the selected child forbids refresh tokens and offline access.
entries.rootCause: A preselection protocol-planning branch survived the minimum-scope correction and the source gate asserted its literal instead of exact absence.
entries.prevention: Remove the optional refresh lifecycle and offline scope, replace the permissive test with exact two-scope and absence coverage, make the gate reject offline.access in all X owners, and rerun pure, mobile and backend X suites.

entries.mistake: The primary inferred a 156-test successor total from the prior narrative 155 plus one new assertion, while the exact current 16-file manifest passed with a bounded count of 158.
entries.rootCause: The prior report named reused suite families without every literal file/count, and the successor total was arithmetically inferred instead of taken from the current executable manifest.
entries.prevention: Freeze all 16 literal current test paths, accept only the bounded native 158 pass summary, run two fresh identical cycles after the registry refresh, and list every suite path in durable evidence.

entries.mistake: Cursor reported emitting a full Git status output for the preserved evidence-heavy MoolSocial worktree; the path inventory is not repeated or retained here.
entries.rootCause: The repository-specific full-status prohibition and non-emitting digest algorithm were not applied before Cursor's inspection command.
entries.prevention: Every Cursor or Codex task reads current instructions and memory first, uses independent branch and HEAD scalars plus the five-field non-emitting status digest, and emits only literal claim-scoped status paths.

entries.mistake: The mvp_module_readiness subagent used a throw string containing $root: and PowerShell rejected the read-only summary command before execution.
entries.rootCause: A colon immediately followed an interpolated variable name, repeating the permanent PowerShell variable-colon parser class.
entries.prevention: Use the format operator for path and exit-code diagnostics, refresh memory and coordination gates against the primary-provided generation, and never retry the rejected command text.

entries.mistake: The primary attempted one long replacement of the current selectedTicketAssessment and apply_patch rejected it atomically because one reconstructed context line differed from the current JSON.
entries.rootCause: A dense append-heavy state subtree was reconstructed into patch context instead of changing small freshly verified field groups.
entries.prevention: Never retry the long replacement; patch one unique scalar or one small exact array at a time, parse and project after every hunk, and run the scope gate only after ticket hash, assessment and execution state agree.

entries.mistake: A Cursor B0 wrapper containing staged diff, worktree diff and conflict queries emitted an unbounded LF-to-CRLF stderr warning stream with filenames and returned wrapper exit zero.
entries.rootCause: The Git diagnostics did not capture stdout, stderr and native exit independently, allowing conversion-warning path bodies to escape into audit output.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the command; use in-memory process capture with separate streams and emit only bounded counts or hashes, or derive staged/conflict state from the bounded porcelain aggregate.

entries.mistake: The FIX5 pending gate required providerConsoleWrite to remain zero even after the founder lawfully enabled Identity Platform and the sanitized count advanced to one.
entries.rootCause: The pending branch represented only the initial fixture instead of the ticket's incremental provider-configuration lifecycle.
entries.prevention: Allow a nonnegative provider-console write count while pending, continue requiring every deployment/private/email/SMS/build/Play/OPPO/production/funds count to remain zero, and retain the qualified branch's complete fact matrix.

entries.mistake: The first read-only verification command for the REG3006 evidence path completed without returning its expected line-count and SHA-256 projection.
entries.rootCause: The execution result did not preserve the expected scalar output, leaving file existence, length and hash unverified from that command.
entries.prevention: After refreshed gates, verify only the literal REG3006 path with minimal Test-Path, line count and SHA-256 output plus full exit metadata; do not group another owner or diagnostic.

entries.mistake: After the forced shutdown, the primary created two incident evidence documents after branch/instruction reconstruction but before replaying the mandatory memory and coordination gates.
entries.rootCause: Outage recovery resumed after partial reconstruction instead of waiting for both current-generation machine gates before any write.
entries.prevention: After every power loss, finish branch, HEAD, bounded handoff, policy generation, memory and both machine gates before any evidence, registry, state, source, browser or external action, and confirm no session was in flight.

entries.mistake: The founder copied Meta's placeholder-based Windows key-hash example into PowerShell, where quoted executable strings were not invocable pipeline elements and parsing failed before execution.
entries.rootCause: The provider example was treated as a ready PowerShell command without resolving placeholders or replacing its shell-specific native pipeline form.
entries.prevention: Never retry the example; export the certificate with keytool to a unique temporary file, compute SHA-1 Base64 with .NET, copy only to the founder clipboard, delete the temporary certificate in finally, and never emit the hash to chat or repository evidence.

entries.mistake: The corrected Facebook development-key-hash workflow invoked keytool by unresolved command name and Windows PowerShell raised CommandNotFoundException.
entries.rootCause: The workflow assumed Java keytool was on PATH instead of resolving one exact configured JDK executable before invocation.
entries.prevention: Never retry the unresolved name; after refreshed gates use bounded repository configuration and literal-path checks to resolve one keytool.exe, invoke that exact file, keep the hash clipboard-only, and clean temporary certificate and fingerprint variables in finally.

entries.mistake: A local Android debug-keystore prompt received an unrelated online-account password; the founder later retried successfully before the rejected attempt was registered.
entries.rootCause: The credential domain of the keytool prompt was not stated before invocation, so a Firebase or Google Cloud account password was confused with the local debug-keystore password.
entries.prevention: Name the exact credential domain before every password-bearing command, prohibit unrelated account credentials, stop and register any rejected prompt before retry, and keep successful fingerprints founder-only and clipboard-to-provider.

entries.mistake: The Facebook development-key-hash outcome was inferred from a cumulative PowerShell transcript containing multiple prior attempts, so both success and failure markers were present and the latest attempt remained ambiguous.
entries.rootCause: Attempts reused one terminal without unique boundaries and full history was shared instead of one isolated sanitized exit classification.
entries.prevention: Never paste full terminal history; use a fresh process or unique attempt marker and report only MOOLSOCIAL_HASH_COPY_OK or one bounded failure class, with no password, fingerprint, path or clipboard value.

entries.mistake: The founder's successful key-hash script completed try/catch, then finally was entered separately and PowerShell treated it as an unknown command, leaving temporary cleanup unexecuted.
entries.rootCause: One compound try/catch/finally parser unit was split across terminal submissions.
entries.prevention: Never split try/catch/finally; use one invoked scriptblock, verify exact uniquely prefixed temporary certificate cleanup through literal paths before provider save, and close the interactive process to dispose remaining objects.

entries.mistake: The primary submitted one dense automated command combining temporary-certificate enumeration, confinement checks and deletion; the execution policy rejected it before process creation.
entries.rootCause: Deletion was embedded in a complex nested shell string instead of using the interactive session's already-resolved exact temporary file variable.
entries.prevention: Never retry the dense command; dispose objects and remove only the literal $certPath already held by the founder's interactive shell, clear variables, close the terminal, and do not rescan or construct a destructive target.

entries.mistake: A Facebook readiness patch expected repeated Android field names without a matching provider-specific context and was rejected, exposing that an earlier short patch may have targeted the Google/YouTube subtree.
entries.rootCause: Repeated property names across provider objects were patched without a unique provider-object anchor and immediate parsed projection.
entries.prevention: Project only the affected provider subtrees, patch each under its literal provider anchor, parse and reproject after every accepted hunk, then run FIX5 in both PowerShell hosts.

entries.mistake: The primary instructed Windows PowerShell 5.1 to clear the clipboard with an empty string, which Set-Clipboard normalized to null and rejected.
entries.rootCause: Clipboard behavior was assumed across PowerShell hosts without accounting for Windows PowerShell 5.1 empty-string normalization.
entries.prevention: Never retry the empty string in Windows PowerShell 5.1; overwrite with one harmless space, expect no output, and close the terminal.

entries.mistake: The Facebook callback malformed-input test cast four cases as one [Buffer,string] tuple instead of an array of such tuples, widening loop values and failing TypeScript.
entries.rootCause: The tuple type annotation was applied to the outer array expression rather than a separately declared tuple-array variable.
entries.prevention: Declare Array<readonly [Buffer,string]>, infer each case, then rerun typecheck, focused callback tests and the full backend suite before deployment or provider callback save.

entries.mistake: The qualified Android Email Link continue path was not live-validated earlier; bounded readback now proves /app returns 404 while assetlinks.json returns 200.
entries.rootCause: The Android/runtime contract accepts /app, but public hosting source/deployment has no matching fallback resource.
entries.prevention: Do not guess another URL; add a minimal /app fallback source, test locally, keep hosting deployment separately held, then require authorized live 200 plus exact release defines and later real-email OPPO acceptance.

entries.mistake: The India-only SMS region PATCH used a user access token without X-Goog-User-Project, and Identity Toolkit rejected the request while smsRegionConfig remained null.
entries.rootCause: The Admin API's quota-project requirement for user credentials was omitted from the bounded PATCH.
entries.prevention: Never retry the prior command; add exactly one Dev-bound X-Goog-User-Project header, retain the sms_region_config-only mask and IN-only body, and emit only sanitized policy/error fields without the token or full config.

entries.mistake: The primary passed backend/functions/src/auth/*test.ts as a positional rg path on Windows, producing OS error 123 before search.
entries.rootCause: A Unix-style filesystem wildcard was used instead of rg's -g option with a literal directory.
entries.prevention: Never retry the wildcard path; search the literal auth directory with -g '*test.ts', then run focused and full backend tests before TTL configuration.

entries.mistake: The founder interrupted two synchronous gcloud TTL waits after the requests were accepted, producing local errors while the server operations continued.
entries.rootCause: Long-running TTL administration was invoked synchronously instead of --async plus sanitized state polling.
entries.prevention: Never rerun the accepted writes; use --async for future TTL changes and poll only exact ttlConfig.state values until both collection groups are ACTIVE.

entries.mistake: A local grouped gcloud probe suppressed role-describe diagnostics and returned false for all six expected predefined roles, yielding no role evidence.
entries.rootCause: The local gcloud context or predefined-role identifier form was not first qualified against the authenticated Dev Cloud Shell.
entries.prevention: Never retry the grouped local probe; validate one exact role at a time in authenticated Cloud Shell with sanitized booleans, then bind only validated roles without returning full IAM policy data.

entries.mistake: A screenshot was returned while the Facebook App Secret field was revealed or selected, so the unused current secret must be treated as exposed.
entries.rootCause: Visual readback was requested after opening a founder-only credential surface instead of re-hiding it before any screenshot or chat interaction.
entries.prevention: Reset the unused secret, copy the rotated value only into a pre-waiting hidden Cloud Shell prompt, re-hide it, and return only the Secret Manager version marker; never capture a revealed secret screen.

entries.mistake: The visible Dev deployment PowerShell disappeared before any public client IDs were entered, leaving the external process outcome unobservable.
entries.rootCause: The external process had no durable session handle or explicit visible-prompt acknowledgement before deployment execution.
entries.prevention: Before retry, read back only function existence; then open one visible -NoExit shell, confirm its prompt, and have the founder type the deployment command before entering four public parameters.

entries.mistake: The authorized Dev deployment started before local Firebase credential freshness was verified; predeploy passed but the CLI rejected the expired session before parameter entry.
entries.rootCause: Local Firebase CLI authentication had expired independently of the authenticated Cloud Shell session.
entries.prevention: Before retry, run interactive firebase login --reauth in the same visible shell, never use login:ci or expose a token, recheck function absence, replay gates and deploy only moolSocialPublicAuth.

entries.mistake: The full successful Firebase reauthentication transcript was returned, including a private OAuth URL, consumed state and account identifier.
entries.rootCause: Interactive authentication output was copied instead of returning only a literal sanitized success marker.
entries.prevention: Never return login URLs, chooser content, identifiers, codes or tokens; after private login report only FIREBASE_REAUTH_SUCCESS and verify deployment state separately.

entries.mistake: The Dev deployment used functions:moolSocialPublicAuth even though firebase.json declares the provider codebase, so Firebase found no matching function.
entries.rootCause: The deployment filter omitted the repository's literal codebase qualifier.
entries.prevention: Never retry the unqualified filter; validate the installed CLI syntax and deploy only provider:moolSocialPublicAuth in the Dev project.

entries.mistake: The completed Firebase reauthentication transcript was returned again with the private OAuth URL, consumed state and account identifier.
entries.rootCause: Terminal history was copied instead of only the new deployment command's final sanitized error.
entries.prevention: Never copy terminal history; return only new-command outcome lines and omit every login URL, account identifier, state, code and token.

entries.mistake: The codebase-qualified deployment created moolSocialPublicAuth and saved parameters but ended with an error and no Deploy complete marker.
entries.rootCause: The post-create error was mixed with full terminal history and requires bounded classification after registration.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or invoke; classify only the final error, then read back function state, runtime service account, secret bindings and public invocation IAM before callback configuration.

entries.mistake: The full deployment attachment again contained earlier private Firebase reauthentication history.
entries.rootCause: Full PowerShell history was copied instead of only the new command's final sanitized marker.
entries.prevention: Never copy full shell history; return only current-command markers or crop below authentication history with every URL and identifier excluded.

entries.mistake: The public Run Invoker binding was attempted before effective domain-restricted-sharing policy was classified, and IAM rejected allUsers.
entries.rootCause: Effective organization policy restricts principals to an approved customer/domain and excludes the special unauthenticated principal.
entries.prevention: Never retry or weaken policy implicitly; read back only the effective constraint class, then require explicit founder choice between a reviewed exception and authenticated public proxy architecture.

entries.mistake: The successful --no-invoker-iam-check update was read back through a nonexistent top-level invokerIamDisabled field, producing a false oracle.
entries.rootCause: The readback assumed a v2 API shape instead of the installed gcloud describe representation.
entries.prevention: Never rerun the update; project the documented annotation/field as a boolean and prove public reachability only through status-code application rejection tests without outputting the URL.

entries.mistake: The Instagram deauthorization URL was pasted into the Step 3 webhook Callback URL instead of Step 4 Business login settings.
entries.rootCause: Adjacent webhook and business-login controls were not distinguished by modal title and exact field labels before paste.
entries.prevention: Keep webhook URL/token blank; require the Step 4 Business login settings modal with OAuth, deauthorization and data-deletion labels before any paste.

entries.mistake: Facebook Basic settings included moolsocial.com as an App domain without a matching web platform, and Meta rejected the entire save.
entries.rootCause: An optional web-domain field was populated for the native-only app despite Web OAuth and web platform scope being intentionally absent.
entries.prevention: Remove the optional App domain instead of adding a Website platform; retain native-only settings and save only privacy, terms and signed deletion callback values after prefix/suffix verification.

entries.mistake: A Meta Basic settings screenshot included the Android key hash and Install Referrer Decryption Key without redaction.
entries.rootCause: The screenshot was not cropped above the founder-only Android credential/configuration section despite an explicit privacy boundary.
entries.prevention: Never return the Android section; crop to exact edited fields, keep purchase/subscription/referrer features disabled, and require rotation or documented non-use of the referrer key before review.

entries.mistake: Cursor B2 embedded a PowerShell backtick-tab token inside a JavaScript template literal, causing SyntaxError before shell execution.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell and JavaScript escape grammars were composed in one orchestration wrapper.
entries.prevention: Preserve the valid B1 worktree; never retry the wrapper text; use no embedded PowerShell backticks, direct argument arrays or a separate script owner, and emit only bounded manifest/count/hash outcomes.

entries.mistake: Cursor B2 encountered a tracked owner matching a broad secret-exclusion pattern and stopped before copying or emitting it.
entries.rootCause: Lexical secret path classes can overmatch tracked sanitized code/config/evidence owners, so path matching alone cannot classify content.
entries.prevention: Never retry or weaken broadly; primary privately classifies the exact Git owner and either adds one literal hash-bound sanitized allowlist or retains exclusion, then Cursor refreshes generation and retries in the existing worktree.

entries.mistake: The private tracked-owner classifier returned one JSON object, but the JavaScript wrapper assumed an array and called map.
entries.rootCause: Singleton ConvertTo-Json output was not normalized to an array before wrapper projection.
entries.prevention: Normalize object-or-array JSON explicitly, retain paths only in private session storage, and emit only sanitized metadata until classification passes.

entries.mistake: The frozen-checkout process census classified its own diagnostic command as one repository writer and one source command.
entries.rootCause: The candidate process set included the current PowerShell PID, whose command text contained both classifier expressions.
entries.prevention: Exclude the current PID before classification and emit only bounded writer/source counts; never accept the self-inclusive result.

entries.mistake: A registry-tail diagnostic serialized the complete top-level registry object and emitted unbounded output.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic wrapped the top-level object rather than projecting its entries array before selecting the tail.
entries.prevention: Project only registry.entries and emit bounded scalar count, ID and SHA fields; prohibit full registry serialization.

entries.mistake: Preflight requested help for nonexistent scripts/check-mvp-scope.ps1 and therefore ran no MVP execution gate.
entries.rootCause: A shortened historical filename was assumed instead of locating the current repository-owned RequireExecutionAuthorized gate.
entries.prevention: Use bounded filename/content discovery to resolve the exact gate, then invoke only that script with RequireExecutionAuthorized.

entries.mistake: A read-only runtime search included nonexistent backend/functions/src/publicAuth.ts and returned only partial mobile output.
entries.rootCause: The broker filename was assumed instead of resolving the current tracked owner.
entries.prevention: Resolve the literal broker path with a bounded rg --files filter, then search only verified existing owners in an independent command.

entries.mistake: A bounded public/auth semantic filename filter found no broker owner.
entries.rootCause: The broker may be exported from a generically named module, so semantic filename matching is not authoritative.
entries.prevention: Enumerate only backend/functions/src filenames, verify literal owners, then run content discovery over those existing files.

entries.mistake: Cursor's corrected process census used currentProcessExcluded=true in its final PowerShell output object and exited one.
entries.rootCause: A JavaScript/JSON boolean spelling was used instead of PowerShell's $true literal.
entries.prevention: Use $true or a bounded scalar text marker, typecheck the output expression first, and never retry the rejected bare-true command text.

entries.mistake: Read-only direct fetches to two official Meta developer-documentation pages returned HTTP 429.
entries.rootCause: The external Meta documentation surface rate-limited the fetch client.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or bypass the rate limit; retain existing console evidence and wait for normal official or signed-in readback availability.

entries.mistake: The final dirty-digest wrapper compressed foreach($v in $b) into foreach($v in$b), causing a parser error before Git started.
entries.rootCause: Mechanical command compression removed required PowerShell token whitespace.
entries.prevention: Reuse the proven expanded digest wrapper verbatim and never compress parser-sensitive PowerShell loops.

entries.mistake: Cursor completed B2 reconstruction after mandatory primary incident registrations moved its pinned registry generation.
entries.rootCause: Independent primary readback work generated registry writes while external B2 reconstruction was still in flight.
entries.prevention: Freeze primary registry writers during incremental B2 refresh and B3; preserve reconstructed owners, update only changed generation owners, regenerate the complete manifest and replay both gates before qualification.

entries.mistake: The first File Explorer Home accessibility observation emitted unrelated Recent-item filenames and account text.
entries.rootCause: The full Home accessibility tree was requested before confining observation to the keystore search control or an exact scoped folder.
entries.prevention: Never recapture File Explorer Home accessibility; use bounded filename-only search over explicitly authorized common folders and emit only count/selection markers.

entries.mistake: After Firebase runtime environment readiness succeeded, the cleanup finally block was pasted separately and PowerShell rejected it.
entries.rootCause: A top-level try/catch/finally recipe was copied in fragments, detaching finally from its originating statement.
entries.prevention: Never retry detached finally; run standalone Remove-Variable cleanup and wrap future multi-block founder-paste recipes in one invocation.

entries.mistake: The retained C34L r60.76 final-candidate readiness gate was invoked for a non-test authentication bootstrap AAB and rejected lifecycleTransitionPath drift.
entries.rootCause: The bootstrap exists only to obtain Play signing fingerprints and has no C34L final release-evidence lifecycle state.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or weaken C34L for bootstrap; keep bootstrap unavailable for acceptance and replay C34L only for the later final auth candidate after Play signing registration.

entries.mistake: The initial authentication owner inventory included the complete mobile test/golden tree and nonexistent guessed backend/web paths, causing truncated output.
entries.rootCause: Verified auth owners were grouped with an unbounded test root and unverified path assumptions.
entries.prevention: Inventory existing roots independently and filter mobile tests by exact authentication/provider filename tokens before emitting bounded owners.

entries.mistake: The callback trace grouped large source roots and an invalid Windows wildcard path, producing duplicate truncated output and a path error.
entries.rootCause: A broad cross-root search was used instead of exact literal slices from already identified callback owners.
entries.prevention: Read exact callback gateway/session file slices; never repeat broad cross-root callback searches or positional Windows wildcard paths.

entries.mistake: Founder guidance stored the upload keystore path in MOOLSOCIAL_UPLOAD_KEYSTORE_PATH while current Gradle and release owners require MOOLSOCIAL_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE.
entries.rootCause: A stale remembered environment name was used before reading the current Gradle signing contract.
entries.prevention: Mechanically derive signing variable names from current Gradle/wrappers before every build; use MOOLSOCIAL_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE as the sole canonical path variable.

entries.mistake: The combined FIX6 test patch assumed a nonexistent exact Instagram test-title anchor and was rejected atomically.
entries.rootCause: Independent test owners were bundled behind a remembered anchor without reading the exact local context.
entries.prevention: Read exact context and patch each test owner independently; never bundle unverified test anchors in one patch.

entries.mistake: The Flutter analyzer yielded after 30 seconds, but the wrapper forwarded only initial output and discarded its session handle and final exit result.
entries.rootCause: The orchestration projected result.output instead of retaining session_id and polling with write_stdin.
entries.prevention: Retain every yielded exec session identifier and poll it to terminal completion; never claim an analyzer result from initial output alone.

entries.mistake: The shared C34P authentication gate rejected the currently authorized FIX5 child ticket because it requires the parent ticket literally.
entries.rootCause: The gate's ticket assertion does not model the explicit authorized child lineage of the shared parent contract.
entries.prevention: Allow only the parent or an explicit list of authorized auth descendants, retain all contract assertions, and add an unrelated-ticket negative fixture.

entries.mistake: The shared C34P gate hardcodes buildAuthorized=false from FIX1A and rejects the founder-authorized pre-AAB descendant execution vector.
entries.rootCause: Shared contract validation was coupled to the original source-only ticket authority instead of the selected authorized descendant.
entries.prevention: Validate the exact current ticket execution vector, allow build only for explicit pre-AAB authority, and retain secret/private/external/device prohibitions with negative fixtures.

entries.mistake: The repaired shared gate emitted externalWrites=0 despite not checking action history and while FIX5 external provider actions are part of the retained state.
entries.rootCause: The final output retained an original FIX1A history claim after the gate was generalized to FIX5 authority.
entries.prevention: Report only checked facts; emit external provider authority rather than action history and require PS7/WinPS output parity.

entries.mistake: The FIX1A all-eight authentication gate rejected the current FIX5 authorized descendant because it requires FIX1A literally in MVP state.
entries.rootCause: The gate does not model explicit authorized descendant lineage while retaining the same accepted source children.
entries.prevention: Allow only FIX1A or explicit FIX5 selection with an unrelated-ticket negative fixture; retain all source/child assertions and truthful output.

entries.mistake: The combined FIX7/FIX6/gate/policy patch contained an invalid hunk at a new file-update boundary and was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Independent JSON and PowerShell owners were combined behind a hand-written placeholder hunk marker.
entries.prevention: Create and update each owner in a separate exact patch; never combine JSON tails and new file boundaries behind placeholder hunks.

entries.mistake: The sanitized OPPO package readback attempted to assign app process text to PowerShell's read-only PID automatic variable.
entries.rootCause: A reserved case-insensitive automatic-variable name was reused.
entries.prevention: Use task-specific variable names such as appPidText and emit only a bounded process-present boolean.

entries.mistake: The local comparison normalized all hexadecimal characters from clipboard text and assumed the total must be exactly one 64-hex fingerprint.
entries.rootCause: The parser did not extract one strict colon-separated or contiguous SHA-256 token from a copied Play field containing extra text.
entries.prevention: Extract exactly one strict 32-byte fingerprint token locally, reject zero/multiple matches, clear clipboard, and emit only MATCH/MISMATCH.

entries.mistake: The expected success marker appeared beside an active keytool new-password prompt, so the current store password cannot be qualified from the transcript.
entries.rootCause: Interactive keytool prompts and a separate marker block were pasted while prompt input remained active.
entries.prevention: Change to a fresh generated password, finish every keytool prompt before marker execution, and never type marker text as password input.

entries.mistake: The founder accidentally submitted the final Play upload-key reset request before the planned action-time confirmation checkpoint.
entries.rootCause: The final external request control remained in the same manual browser flow as certificate upload and the stop boundary was crossed.
entries.prevention: Do not cancel or duplicate a correct pending request; future irreversible browser submission gets a separate screen/turn and explicit final-action marker.

entries.mistake: A timezone-anchored one-time Codex reminder used immediate create with DTSTART and was rejected.
entries.rootCause: The invocation did not use the product's suggested-create mode required for anchored wall-clock semantics.
entries.prevention: Use suggested-create for timezone-specific DTSTART reminders and verify the returned automation before claiming success.

entries.mistake: The Firebase certificate fingerprint field received the page URL after the clipboard was overwritten during navigation.
entries.rootCause: Clipboard priming occurred before navigation instead of immediately before the destination paste.
entries.prevention: Prime the exact local fingerprint immediately before paste, replace the full field, and save only after Firebase recognizes the SHA type.

entries.mistake: One encoded process-launch payload combined a new window, interactive secret prompts and extensive sideload runtime configuration and was blocked by local policy.
entries.rootCause: Secret collection was embedded in an automated process launch instead of a founder-invoked repository prompt script.
entries.prevention: Use a value-free repository prompt script invoked manually by the founder in an existing shell; emit readiness markers only.

entries.mistake: The sideload helper parser check ran from apps/mobile while resolving a repository-root-relative scripts path, so it failed before affected Flutter tests started.
entries.rootCause: One command mixed a mobile-package working directory with an unqualified repository-root script path.
entries.prevention: Resolve the helper by absolute repository path and keep its parser check independently addressable before running mobile tests from apps/mobile.

entries.mistake: The first attempt to claim the sideload self-test owner assumed conventional JSON tail formatting and was rejected by apply_patch.
entries.rootCause: The patch context was inferred from a projected owner array instead of the raw leading-comma policy tail.
entries.prevention: Read the exact bounded raw policy lines before patching a mechanically evolved owner tail.

entries.mistake: The second owner-policy patch still used a conventional trailing JSON context for the existing sideload script and was rejected.
entries.rootCause: The exact raw punctuation was not inspected after the first context failure.
entries.prevention: After any patch-context failure, inspect the literal raw line range and reproduce its punctuation before retrying.

entries.mistake: The coordination gate ran after the sideload self-test was claimed but before that claimed file existed.
entries.rootCause: The owner claim and owner creation were split across a gate boundary that requires every recorded owner to exist.
entries.prevention: Complete the bounded coordination repair by creating the claimed owner before rerunning the gate.

entries.mistake: The founder's exact sideload authorization changed the selected FIX5 ticket while its MVP selected-ticket assessment retained the prior manifest hash.
entries.rootCause: The ticket authority and pinned MVP manifest hash were not updated atomically in the bounded authorization preparation sequence.
entries.prevention: Recompute and pin the exact selected-ticket hash and exact sideload-only execution scope before rerunning the MVP gate.

entries.mistake: A runtime-define string array was passed through nested pwsh -File, so later elements became positional arguments and the APK gate did not execute.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell native-process argument expansion was treated like in-process script array binding.
entries.prevention: Invoke the APK gate directly in the current PowerShell process when passing string arrays.

entries.mistake: The gated release APK build reached Gradle configuration and failed because defaultConfig resValue entries were present while custom resource values were disabled.
entries.rootCause: The Android application module did not explicitly enable buildFeatures.resValues for the current Android Gradle Plugin.
entries.prevention: Enable android.buildFeatures.resValues, prove it with a source control test, refresh the source manifest, and authorize only one registered retry.

entries.mistake: A stale ignored GeneratedPluginRegistrant.java in the Android main source set referenced the development-only integration_test plugin and failed release Java compilation.
entries.rootCause: An ignored generated source file was absent from durable source qualification but remained compiler-visible in the local dirty checkout.
entries.prevention: Preserve the stale file as evidence, remove it from the main source set, and fail prebuild if that ignored registrant path reappears.

entries.mistake: Moving the stale ignored registrant out of the source tree made historical REG1818 evidence missing and the regression-memory gate failed.
entries.rootCause: Compiler-source cleanup was performed by moving a file that also serves as retained historical evidence.
entries.prevention: Restore the exact evidence file and exclude its path through Android source-set configuration instead of deleting or moving it.

entries.mistake: The AGP 9 Android source-set receiver rejected java.exclude during the targeted release Java precheck.
entries.rootCause: A Configuration.exclude API shape was assumed for the Android Java source directory set.
entries.prevention: Use the supported setSrcDirs contract after proving the main Java root contains only the ignored historical registrant.

entries.mistake: The release build reached packageRelease but the supplied key password could not recover alias moolsocial-upload from the readable JKS.
entries.rootCause: Founder-held store and key passwords were not locally validated together before the build consumed them.
entries.prevention: Use a local hidden re-prompt and Java keystore API validation through inherited environment before setting build variables; never pass passwords on the command line.

entries.mistake: An optional installed-base APK pull and local signer comparison command was rejected by local command policy before execution.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic combined device pull, temporary file handling and certificate comparison in one command shape rejected by local policy.
entries.prevention: Do not retry when existing Play App Signing and candidate upload-certificate evidence already prove the signature transition boundary.

entries.mistake: The authorized device command stopped before uninstall because the raw package-output record count was not exactly one; REG3081 later proved the package was present.
entries.rootCause: The initial stop condition treated raw ADB record count as normalized package presence.
entries.prevention: Filter the exact normalized package line immediately before branching and skip uninstall only when that exact line is absent.

entries.mistake: The predecessor package was falsely described as absent after a raw ADB output count check stopped the command.
entries.rootCause: Package presence was inferred from total raw record count instead of filtering the exact normalized package line.
entries.prevention: Normalize ADB output and count only the literal package:com.moolsocial.app line before branching.

entries.mistake: One apply_patch operation created REG3081 evidence and corrected REG3080 evidence together.
entries.rootCause: Closely related incident corrections were combined despite the one-owner-per-operation rule.
entries.prevention: Create and correct incident owners in separate patch calls with independent readback.

entries.mistake: The qualified public-auth sideload rendered the update-required fallback because live device-review mode accepted only the YouTube public-review/private-proof profile.
entries.rootCause: The startup runtime-mode gate was not extended with the explicit signed public-auth sideload contract when that profile was introduced.
entries.prevention: Permit either the existing YouTube contract or both explicit sideload and local-signing facts, retain negative coverage, and build a distinct successor version.

entries.mistake: The first broad r60.78 affected cycle exceeded the tool output budget and returned without its terminal pass/fail line.
entries.rootCause: Verbose Flutter test output was emitted directly instead of reduced to a bounded terminal summary.
entries.prevention: Capture test output in memory, retain the exit code, and emit only the final completed count and terminal state.

entries.mistake: The installed checksum-matched r60.78 candidate stayed on the plain navy native launch frame with a live process and no fatal marker.
entries.rootCause: Production main awaited multiple asynchronous platform/bootstrap stages before any Flutter-owned normal runApp and provided no bounded stage recovery.
entries.prevention: Render a named Flutter bootstrap frame before async platform work, bound each stage, and require installed-checksum cold-start first-frame evidence before auth testing or promotion.

entries.mistake: The first bootstrap timeout patch was rejected because its final auth-return context did not match formatted main.dart.
entries.rootCause: Several distant startup hunks were combined without exact current readback of the last range.
