entries.prevention: Do not repeat the foreground action; use read-only dumpsys activity/window label variants, require a non-empty categorized owner, and never proceed to UI automation from an empty focus projection.

entries.mistake: The first in-memory OPPO UI hierarchy projection referenced the hyphenated XML attribute content-desc as an unquoted PowerShell property, causing a parser error before adb or UI hierarchy evaluation.
entries.rootCause: The command applied dot notation to a hyphenated XML attribute instead of reading it through quoted PSObject property access.
entries.prevention: Parser-test bounded PowerShell XML projections first and access hyphenated attributes as $_.PSObject.Properties['content-desc'].Value; never send unparsed UI/device commands.

entries.mistake: After parser correction, the bounded uiautomator dump /dev/tty query returned no XML payload on this OPPO, so the public screen hierarchy could not be safely projected in memory.
entries.rootCause: This device/build does not expose the hierarchy XML through the assumed /dev/tty transport; no raw hierarchy or app action occurred.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the same transport; use a separately bounded device-temporary hierarchy file with exact cleanup or ask the founder for one public-screen readiness marker when manual focus is faster.

entries.mistake: The sideload environment preparation hardcodes Google sideload signing and every public-provider qualification fact to true after only selecting the package and a web OAuth client; it does not prove the APK signing certificate is registered for the Android OAuth client or authoritatively read back the live provider/broker configuration before enabling buttons.
entries.rootCause: Boolean readiness inputs were treated as founder-entered build facts instead of outputs of fail-closed, non-emitting certificate/configuration gates. The APK prebuild gate checked equality with those booleans, not the underlying provider evidence.
entries.prevention: Derive Google sideload readiness from a non-emitting signer-to-Android-OAuth certificate match, derive each provider flag only from authoritative Dev readback or a current sealed receipt, reject hardcoded true readiness, and block every future APK/AAB when proof is absent or stale.

entries.mistake: On r60.81 Screen 03, Apple is correctly labelled not available but the nested provider surface is still exported clickable=true on OPPO.
entries.rootCause: _ProviderButton sets Semantics enabled from availability but assigns InkWell.onTap from busy state alone, so unavailable methods remain actionable and conflict with their accessibility state.
entries.prevention: Set the actual tap handler to null unless both available and enabled, preserve the truthful unavailable label, and add widget/semantics coverage proving every unavailable provider is non-clickable.

entries.mistake: On r60.81 Screen 03, Mobile OTP is exported clickable=true even though the exact sideload profile sets mobile attestation qualified=false and JourneySession.mobileOtpAvailable is therefore false.
entries.rootCause: The v5 method chooser always wires the Mobile OTP tap handler and does not bind button availability or semantics to session.mobileOtpAvailable.
entries.prevention: Render Mobile OTP truthfully unavailable and non-clickable until attestation is qualified, preserve zero real SMS actions, and add runtime-profile widget/semantics tests for the held method.

entries.mistake: Screen 03 tells users they agree to Terms and acknowledge the Privacy Policy, but OPPO exports the legal copy as non-clickable and the v5 source renders plain Text with no route or URL actions.
entries.rootCause: The login legal acknowledgement was copied as presentation only and was not bound to the existing public Terms and Privacy destinations or independent semantic links.
entries.prevention: Provide separately focusable Terms and Privacy actions to the exact approved public pages, retain same-origin safe navigation, and add widget/semantics plus rendered-public-page availability tests.

entries.mistake: The first combined signer-gate creation/integration patch assumed the APK wrapper invoked its machine gate immediately after runtimeDefines, but intervening current source made that context false; apply_patch rejected the entire multi-file patch atomically.
entries.rootCause: New file creation and multiple existing-owner integrations were attempted in one oversized patch without reading the exact current wrapper and test-control insertion ranges first.
entries.prevention: Create new gate and fixture owners in separate bounded apply_patch actions, read exact literal integration ranges, then patch each existing wrapper/control independently and confirm zero partial change after any rejection.

entries.mistake: The first bounded status-promotion patch transcribed REG3246 legal-navigation as legal_navigation, so apply_patch rejected all five status changes atomically.
entries.rootCause: The exact existing status text was not copied from a bounded ID/status readback before composing the multi-entry patch.
entries.prevention: Read exact ID plus status lines and preserve punctuation literally before status-only patches; treat atomic rejection as zero partial change and register before retry.

entries.mistake: A redundant coordination-binding patch attempted to replace the already-superseded 98D9 registry hash even though the policy had already been updated to 58CD, so apply_patch rejected the stale from-context atomically.
entries.rootCause: The immediate policy readback was skipped after the prior successful registry status promotion and binding update.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current registry binding before every hash patch, patch only from its literal present value, and treat a stale-from rejection as zero partial change requiring registration before replay.

entries.mistake: The Google/YouTube read-only audit subagent attempted to emit the complete 538-line coordination JSON in one result; the result was truncated and mandatory complete-read proof was lost.
entries.rootCause: The mandatory owner was not split into bounded independent pages sized below the command output budget before delegation continued.
entries.prevention: Read large mandatory JSON owners in independent non-overlapping bounded pages, verify the final line/EOF, and stop without provider inspection whenever any page or aggregate result is truncated.

entries.mistake: The Facebook read-only audit subagent dirty-digest helper emitted System.Threading.Tasks.VoidTaskResult and then failed on a null MemoryStream with ambiguous HashData and ToHexString overload errors.
entries.rootCause: The helper incorrectly relied on CopyToAsync task AsyncState as the output stream and allowed an awaited void task result to reach the output channel.
entries.prevention: Keep an explicit MemoryStream reference, suppress every task return value, await copy and stderr tasks independently, capture exit metadata before disposal, and emit only bytes, records, SHA-256, stderr bytes and exit code.

entries.mistake: The X read-only audit subagent attempted to emit the complete 538-line coordination JSON in one result; the result was truncated and mandatory complete-read proof was lost.
entries.rootCause: The mandatory owner was not split into bounded independent pages sized below the command output budget before delegation continued.
entries.prevention: Read large mandatory JSON owners in independent non-overlapping bounded pages, verify the final line/EOF, and stop without provider inspection whenever any page or aggregate result is truncated.

entries.mistake: The primary emitted the bounded handoff, coordination policy, and two coordination JSON pages through one aggregate execution result; the combined result was truncated and complete JSON-read proof was lost.
entries.rootCause: Individually bounded nested commands were still aggregated into a response whose total token volume exceeded the direct tool output budget.
entries.prevention: Return each large mandatory page in a separate tool result, keep each page independently below the output budget, verify EOF, and never infer a complete read from individually bounded commands when their aggregate transport is truncated.

entries.mistake: The primary added three non-overlapping subagent claims whose report owners had not yet been created, which would make the mandatory coordination gate reject all three retries.
entries.rootCause: Claim allocation was patched before the claimed leaf-owner existence precondition was checked, repeating the missing-owner class already covered by REG2997 and REG3071.
entries.prevention: Create and read back each bounded report scaffold before adding or replaying its claim, require every recorded owner to exist as a leaf, and run the coordination negative/positive owner checks before subagent retry.

entries.mistake: The primary searched journey_services.dart as the required FirebaseSocialAuthGateway owner, but the exact fixed-string symbol lookup returned no matches and therefore provided no source evidence.
entries.rootCause: A summarized prior owner association was used instead of resolving the current declaring file from a bounded mobile-lib inventory and exact symbol search.
entries.prevention: Resolve authentication declaring owners with rg --files under the verified mobile lib root, then run a no-match-safe exact symbol search and read only the returned literal owner in bounded windows.

entries.mistake: The X read-only audit subagent rendered a raw backend index.ts source window that included source-declared runtime service-account identities and the Dev project identifier despite an explicit sanitized-identity-only instruction.
entries.rootCause: A bounded line range was treated as safe by size without first classifying or redacting identity-bearing configuration literals in that owner.
entries.prevention: For backend deployment/runtime owners, emit only redacted booleans, counts and line numbers derived in memory; never render raw source windows that can contain project, service-account, endpoint, client or credential identifiers.

entries.mistake: The first bounded OPPO MediaStore help projection placed a Unix-style double-dash after PowerShell's -match operator, causing a parser error before the adb content help command executed.
entries.rootCause: The ripgrep end-of-options prevention was incorrectly transferred to the PowerShell regex operator, whose right-hand operand must be a direct string expression.
entries.prevention: Use PowerShell -match with one single-quoted regex operand and reserve -- only for native tools that declare it; parser-check the complete read-only media command before the authorized screenshot lookup.

entries.mistake: The bounded screenshot selector assumed the OPPO MediaStore result would expose exactly one newest line prefixed Row: 0; the query produced no unique parseable match and was stopped before copying any device file.
entries.rootCause: The parser encoded an unverified output-row format and exact Screenshots-album spelling instead of first proving the device's sanitized result shape.
entries.prevention: First emit only the read-only query exit code, non-empty row count, row-prefix class, and property-name schema with all values suppressed; then parse the exact observed format and allow only the bounded Screenshot album spelling variant before selecting one newest image.

entries.mistake: A raw registry-tail read intended to confirm the latest entry exceeded the available model context and returned truncated ambiguous output.
entries.rootCause: The verification rendered a structural tail from the large registry instead of projecting only bounded scalar metadata.
entries.prevention: Verify registry evolution with parsed scalar count, last ID, JSON validity, and non-emitting SHA-256; request an exact ID-only projection only when a field-level check is required, and never infer success from a raw truncated tail.

entries.mistake: The first registry-binding refresh patch assumed the coordination policy used a recordCount field and therefore failed exact-context verification without changing the file.
entries.rootCause: The patch context was composed from memory instead of projecting the bounded binding object's actual property names.
entries.prevention: Before each binding refresh, parse and emit only the binding object's property-name set and current scalar values, then patch the exact observed keys; register any context mismatch before retry.

entries.mistake: The first bounded coordination binding projection assumed a top-level regressionRegistryBinding object, but that property was absent and no binding values were returned.
entries.rootCause: The JSON object path was recalled imprecisely after reconstruction instead of deriving it from the current document's bounded top-level property names.
entries.prevention: Project only top-level property names first, select the exact current binding property, and then emit its bounded scalar keys and values before patching; never treat a missing projection as an empty valid binding.

entries.mistake: The first refreshed primary coordination-gate invocation supplied the task but omitted UseRecordedClaim and no explicit owner list, so the gate correctly rejected it.
entries.rootCause: The invocation was reconstructed from the parameter block without preserving the already-recorded /root claim selection used by the qualified checkpoint.
entries.prevention: For an existing coordinated task, always invoke the gate with UseRecordedClaim and the exact registered task name; use explicit ClaimedOwners only when intentionally validating a new unrecorded claim.

entries.mistake: The sanitized OPPO screenshot query succeeded with candidate rows, but the row-prefix classifier required Row at column zero and therefore did not derive the property-name schema.
entries.rootCause: The parser did not tolerate device-shell leading whitespace even though values were correctly suppressed from output.
entries.prevention: Normalize only leading whitespace before classifying MediaStore Row prefixes, continue suppressing all values, and prove the property-name schema before selecting or copying exactly one newest screenshot.

entries.mistake: The registered whitespace-tolerant MediaStore row classifier still did not recognize the first non-empty line although the read-only query returned the same bounded candidate count.
entries.rootCause: The device output contains an additional unproven wrapper or prefix class beyond ordinary leading whitespace.
entries.prevention: Before another row-selection attempt, emit only a redacted prefix template and character-class metadata that removes all field values, paths and filenames; derive the exact parser from that sanitized shape and keep the single-file copy stopped until proven.

entries.mistake: The bounded MediaStore query passed its SQL-like where expression as host-side adb arguments, which the remote shell split and answered with the content usage page; the usage lines were initially classified only as unrecognized candidate output.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell argument grouping did not preserve the complete where and sort expressions across the adb-to-device shell boundary.
entries.prevention: Send the entire read-only content query as one remote-shell command string with device-shell quoting intact, detect a usage prefix as failure before counting rows, and keep values suppressed until an actual Row schema is proven.

entries.mistake: The first correctly transported bounded MediaStore command returned a ten-line error response rather than usage or result rows, and the error body was intentionally not emitted.
entries.rootCause: Sanitized diagnostics proved java.lang.IllegalArgumentException with an invalid column classification naming only display_name; Android MediaStore exposes this projection as _display_name.
entries.prevention: Use the exact Android MediaStore _display_name projection token, retain the bounded Screenshot album predicate, and continue suppressing all messages, paths, filenames and values until a real Row schema is proven.

entries.mistake: The read-only Dev Firebase Authentication provider URL redirected the isolated in-app browser session to Google account re-verification instead of exposing provider status.
entries.rootCause: The isolated browser session did not carry a currently verified Google Console authentication state even though command-line authentication had been refreshed separately.
entries.prevention: Never click through or enter account data during an automated provider-status readback; stop at re-verification and use an already-authorized non-emitting CLI/API readback or request a precise founder handoff.

entries.mistake: After the isolated browser required re-verification, the attempted read-only selection of the user's already-signed-in Chrome surface reported that Chrome control was unavailable.
entries.rootCause: No controllable Chrome extension channel was connected to the current Codex task, so the existing signed-in Chrome state could not be safely reused.
entries.prevention: Do not substitute uncontrolled desktop automation or repeat selection; use an authorized non-emitting CLI/API readback, or ask the founder to complete the exact console readback manually when no such surface exists.

entries.mistake: The Google/YouTube audit's bounded Android manifest projection emitted a source-declared Dev project identity embedded in an authentication-link host despite the stricter instruction to suppress project identities.
entries.rootCause: The projection bounded line count but did not redact identity-bearing host values before rendering them to the parent task.
entries.prevention: For auth manifest inspections, emit only boolean presence, counts and normalized component or scheme classes; redact every host, project, client, application, account and runtime identity before any subagent output.

entries.mistake: The Facebook audit normalized optional activity-alias XML nodes into arrays containing null and then invoked GetAttribute on those null entries, emitting InvalidOperation errors before a partial JSON row.
entries.rootCause: The bounded manifest projection did not filter optional XML node collections for null before attribute access.
entries.prevention: Filter optional XML node arrays with a non-null predicate before GetAttribute, treat any preceding PowerShell error as invalidating later partial JSON, and register before a corrected read-only retry.

entries.mistake: The Facebook audit retry attempted to null-filter an optional activity-alias collection, but StrictMode terminated earlier when the absent XML child property itself was accessed.
entries.rootCause: Direct dynamic XML property access is not safe for absent optional elements under PowerShell StrictMode; null filtering occurs too late.
entries.prevention: Resolve optional manifest elements with SelectNodes or XPath so absence returns an empty node list, never with direct dynamic child-property access under StrictMode; after this recurrence, stop further manifest probing unless the XPath projection is essential to a decision.

entries.mistake: After a sanitized configuration-count projection, the Google/YouTube audit tested a convention-derived generated release resource path before resolving the actual path inventory and obtained a false result that is not valid absence evidence.
entries.rootCause: The generated Gradle output location was inferred from convention instead of discovered from the current build tree with a bounded file inventory.
entries.prevention: Use rg --files on the exact Android build subtree and match only the expected generated google-services resource filename before reading it; treat guessed-path false as inconclusive and never as absence evidence.

entries.mistake: The authorized bounded inventory of the exact Android app build subtree returned exit 2 because the generated build root is currently absent; the wrapper rejected all output and no generated-resource conclusion was accepted.
entries.rootCause: No live generated Android app build tree remains available for readback, and producing one would require a separately authorized build action.
entries.prevention: Do not retry, guess another generated path, or rebuild for audit evidence; record generated release google-services resources as not currently inspectable while keeping source config shape, package alignment, client-type counts and installed signer registration as separate proven facts.

entries.mistake: A bounded readiness search passed a wildcard as part of a literal Windows path argument for the FIX8 docs folder; ripgrep returned an invalid-filename error while also emitting matches from other valid paths, so the mixed output was rejected.
entries.rootCause: Shell wildcard path syntax was used where ripgrep on Windows required a concrete directory plus --glob filtering.
entries.prevention: Pass only existing concrete directories to rg and express filename patterns with one or more --glob arguments; reject every mixed partial result when any search target errors.

entries.mistake: The Google/YouTube report postcondition used an exact Contains needle spanning prose that wrapped across an ordinary Markdown newline, so it returned false although the pending-acceptance statement is present and the report patch and hash were proven.
entries.rootCause: The validator compared raw Markdown layout instead of normalizing whitespace before semantic sentence matching.
entries.prevention: Normalize consecutive whitespace in documentation before exact prose postconditions, keep file hash and completed-state checks separate, and never treat a raw line-wrap mismatch as missing evidence.

entries.mistake: The next readiness search again included a literal scripts/*.ps1 Windows path beside two explicit files; ripgrep rejected that target and the partial matches from the explicit files were not accepted.
entries.rootCause: The newly registered concrete-path plus --glob prevention was not applied to the immediately following command composition.
entries.prevention: After this recurrence, do not add any wildcard path argument to rg on Windows: search only explicit existing files or one concrete directory with --glob, and parser-review the entire target list before execution.

entries.mistake: A combined sanitized Google/X/Facebook boolean projection had an unmatched statement-block brace and failed at PowerShell parse time before reading or emitting provider values.
entries.rootCause: Too many nested inline pipeline and PSCustomObject blocks were compressed into one command without a parser-safe intermediate structure.
entries.prevention: Project one provider object at a time with named intermediate variables and shallow JSON output; parser-review brace balance before execution and register any parse failure before retry.

entries.mistake: After the founder saved the Meta OAuth redirect and enabled Facebook in Dev Firebase Authentication, a force-close/reopen founder-private OPPO Facebook attempt still returned the same generic sign-in-not-completed failure.
entries.rootCause: Firebase provider absence was one proven blocker but not the complete root cause; the remaining native-token, Firebase credential, account-collision or post-auth session boundary is still unclassified because r60.81 collapses the diagnostic to a generic outcome.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat blind Facebook login attempts or claim the issue fixed from console enablement alone; capture exactly one sanitized error-class/code receipt with all token, account, app, project and credential values suppressed, then repair and test the proven remaining boundary before any successor build.

entries.mistake: Two bounded read-only follow-up agents were dispatched after the FIX8 ticket changed but before its selected-ticket assessment manifest hash was refreshed; both correctly stopped when the execution-authorized MVP gate rejected the stale binding.
entries.rootCause: The primary updated the current FIX8 ticket and replayed registry/coordination controls without atomically refreshing the ticket SHA-256 in the MVP selected-ticket assessment before parallel dispatch.
entries.prevention: Whenever the current ticket changes, immediately recompute and bind its exact SHA-256 in preTicketSelectionCheckpoint.selectedTicketAssessment, then replay the execution-authorized MVP gate before dispatching any agent or performing source inspection, mutation or test; one gate failure invalidates all parallel siblings until the binding is repaired.

entries.mistake: A bounded coordination-claim line locator placed a pipeline directly after a foreach statement block, and PowerShell rejected the command with an empty-pipe-element parser error before any policy content was emitted.
entries.rootCause: The foreach statement was not wrapped in an array subexpression or assigned to an intermediate variable before piping its results to ConvertTo-Json.
entries.prevention: Never pipe directly from a PowerShell foreach statement block; assign the collected PSCustomObject rows to a named array first, then serialize that array in a separate statement, and register any parser failure before retry.

entries.mistake: The X readiness follow-up used one multi-file repeated-token search across JourneySession, LoginScreenV5 and JourneyService owners; its output exceeded the bounded model result and was truncated before the audit could establish complete coverage.
entries.rootCause: A high-frequency token search was combined across several large owners instead of reading one exact relevant region per file with a small explicit line bound.
entries.prevention: For social-auth failure propagation, inspect one explicit file and one exact line region per command, avoid repeated generic tokens, set a small output budget, and reject every truncated projection before conclusions or retries.

entries.mistake: A sanitized Google readiness projection assumed providers.google existed and cast missing nested properties to false, yielding a plausible but invalid all-false result.
entries.rootCause: The command guessed the provider node name instead of first projecting the exact provider property names from the current state schema, and PowerShell silently converted null values to false.
entries.prevention: Before projecting provider facts, emit only the exact provider node names, require one exact Google-related node, assert every requested property exists, and never cast a missing property to bool; reject an all-false projection unless schema presence is independently proven.

entries.mistake: The Google-only follow-up agent's first implementation-phase regression-memory gate returned only an output-truncated result, so no authoritative gate pass was available and the agent stopped before inspection.
entries.rootCause: The delegated execution channel could not retain the gate result at the current large registry generation, making another subagent retry slower and less reliable than the already-qualified primary path.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the Google audit through a subagent in this cycle; keep the Google-only acceptance unit in the primary task, run each mandatory gate in one bounded shell call, and require a complete one-line pass with exit zero before local inspection or tests.

entries.mistake: The primary combined Google runtime matches with two complete PowerShell gate/test file reads in one result, and the aggregate output was truncated before an authoritative complete audit could be retained.
entries.rootCause: Several individually bounded commands were parallelized into one model result whose combined output budget exceeded the retained response limit.
entries.prevention: For the Google-only acceptance unit, run one exact file-region read or one test per result, never combine complete scripts with runtime source searches, and reject every truncated aggregate even when some visible fragments look useful.

entries.mistake: A FIX8 ticket section-name projection again piped directly from a foreach statement block and PowerShell rejected it with the same empty-pipe-element parser error registered in REG3280.
entries.rootCause: The newly registered named-array prevention was not applied when composing the next compact projection command.
entries.prevention: After this recurrence, do not use foreach in inline projection commands during this ticket: construct one fixed PSCustomObject with explicitly named sections, or assign results before a separate serialization statement; parser-review for a block immediately followed by a pipe.

entries.mistake: Google was tested again on the connected OPPO after repository-only qualification, but the device still contained rejected r60.81 because no successor APK had been built or installed; the same old failure therefore remained.
entries.rootCause: The handoff did not state prominently enough that passing source tests and prebuild fixtures cannot mutate an already-installed APK, and that the consumed r60.81 authorization did not authorize a successor build/install.
entries.prevention: Before any founder provider test, read back and state the installed version/checksum and require it to match the newly qualified successor; label source-only passes as not-on-device, prohibit testing rejected r60.81 again, and obtain one explicit successor build/install authorization before expecting corrected OPPO behavior.

entries.mistake: The FIX8 build-input manifest generator included the build wrapper and public-auth control test but did not include the invoked Google Android OAuth signing gate or its negative-fixture test, so a successor fingerprint could omit the exact Google corrective controls.
entries.rootCause: The Google server-client equality gate was added after the r60.81 manifest owner list was authored, and the transitive invoked-script closure was not updated at the same time.
entries.prevention: Bind scripts/check-google-android-oauth-signing-readiness.ps1 and scripts/test-google-android-oauth-signing-readiness.ps1 into every FIX8 successor source manifest, add a static control assertion for both owners, and reject sealing when any invoked prebuild gate or its fixture test is outside the fingerprint closure.

entries.mistake: The reusable FIX8 build-input generator was about to seal the r60.82 successor while still emitting an r60.81-specific success state and rejection prefix, which would mislabel otherwise current evidence.
entries.rootCause: The generator filename and output strings were originally authored for r60.81 but later reused for successors without separating stable generator identity from candidate version identity.
entries.prevention: Emit version-neutral FIX8 successor state and rejection labels from the reusable generator; bind candidate version only in the unique output path, ticket and APK machine state, and reject evidence whose embedded state names an earlier candidate.

entries.mistake: The primary sealed the unique r60.82 source-aggregate manifest into its new artifact directory before adding that exact output path to the primary coordination owner claim.
entries.rootCause: The output existence check and manifest generation were sequenced before the new candidate evidence owner set was registered in the coordination policy.
entries.prevention: Before any successor evidence write, add every exact intended manifest, prebuild receipt, APK, provenance and device receipt path to the primary owner claim, pass coordination, then write one owner at a time; preserve and validate the already written manifest rather than overwriting it.

entries.mistake: The primary predeclared the complete intended r60.82 evidence and artifact file set, but the coordination gate requires every recorded owner path to exist and rejected the first not-yet-created qualification file.
entries.rootCause: The owner-allocation rule was applied as a future-path declaration even though the current machine gate implements ownership only for already-existing filesystem owners.
entries.prevention: Do not add nonexistent future evidence paths to activeClaims; retain claims only for existing owners, use already-claimed durable evidence where possible, and for wrapper-created artifacts validate and add exact claims immediately after the authorized atomic tool action rather than causing a prebuild gate failure.

entries.mistake: One patch attempted to update the FIX8 confirmed-regression list, device authorization, release authorization and authority sections together; a device-authorization context did not match and apply_patch rejected the entire operation.
entries.rootCause: Several distant ticket sections were combined without independently reading the exact current text of every hunk, contrary to the one-bounded-owner-region rule.
entries.prevention: Patch one exact ticket section per operation, read it back immediately, and only then patch the next section; treat an apply_patch context rejection as zero mutation and register before retry.

entries.mistake: The existing secure sideload environment helper would mark Facebook, Instagram and X runtime qualifications true and require Meta inputs, while the authorized r60.82 machine state permits only Google and requires every unrelated provider to remain fail-closed.
entries.rootCause: The helper was authored for the earlier all-provider public-auth preflight and had no provider-scoped mode when the founder changed FIX8 acceptance to one provider at a time.
entries.prevention: Add and test an explicit Google-only helper mode that keeps every unrelated provider fact false, omits unrelated Meta credential prompts and requirements, preserves hidden release-signing and Google equality checks, and reject any build before Flutter or Gradle when helper facts differ from the exact machine-state allowlist.

entries.mistake: A diagnostic serialized large active-claim owner arrays and then tried to expand a nonexistent agentTask property, producing truncated output followed by a PowerShell property error.
entries.rootCause: The coordination schema uses task rather than agentTask, and the projection included owners when only task names were needed.
entries.prevention: Do not serialize coordination owner arrays for task discovery; project only task and role with fixed properties, and use the known /root recorded claim directly for the primary gate.

entries.mistake: The first Google-only static-control assertion used a double-quoted expected source fragment containing PowerShell variable names, which would interpolate the test process variables instead of matching the literal helper source.
entries.rootCause: The assertion fragment was written as an expandable PowerShell string even though it represented source text rather than a runtime value.
entries.prevention: Represent source-code fragments containing dollar-prefixed names with single-quoted PowerShell literals and doubled embedded quotes; parse and inspect the test before its first execution.

entries.mistake: A post-seal diagnostic assumed the source manifest contained a coordination-policy row and called StartsWith on the missing match, producing a null-method error.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic did not guard the optional Select-String result before comparing its hash prefix.
entries.prevention: Use a fixed projection of match count and conditionally compare only when exactly one row exists; never call a method on an unverified optional manifest match.

entries.mistake: The forced r60.82 resource-link gate reached and completed :app:processReleaseResources but returned exit one because --warning-mode=fail promoted third-party Flutter-plugin Gradle deprecations to a build failure; its verbose dependency output was also truncated before the final bounded readback.
entries.rootCause: The gate coupled resource-link correctness to unrelated dependency deprecation cleanliness and streamed the entire Gradle log instead of retaining a bounded diagnostic tail.
entries.prevention: Run the exact forced release resource task with warning-mode summary and plain console, capture its complete output internally, emit only a bounded tail on nonzero exit, and continue to fail closed on the task exit code plus compiled and packaged launch-resource readback.

entries.mistake: The production APK wrapper called the plugin-manifest namespace gate in strict mode, which rejected the already-inventoried 14 package attributes in current third-party Flutter dependencies and would make every authorized APK/AAB build impossible despite AGP ignoring those attributes.
entries.rootCause: The gate supported inventory mode but had no pinned reviewed-baseline acceptance mode for immutable Pub-cache dependencies, while the wrapper invoked its unconditional rejection path.
entries.prevention: Pin the exact reviewed plugin-name allowlist and count in the repository gate, pass only when the live inventory matches it exactly, fail on any new, removed or renamed offender, keep direct-dev plugins separately bounded, and never patch the machine Pub cache.

entries.mistake: The production APK/AAB wrappers also called the Built-in Kotlin dependency gate in strict mode even though the current reviewed inventory contains three third-party plugins that still apply the legacy Kotlin Android plugin, so the next strict step would reject every build.
entries.rootCause: Like the namespace gate, the Kotlin gate exposed inventory mode but had no exact reviewed-baseline acceptance contract for external dependencies pending upstream migration.
entries.prevention: Pin exactly firebase_app_check, mobile_scanner and speech_to_text plus the reviewed release/dev plugin counts; pass only that immutable baseline, stop on any drift, keep the future-migration warning visible in evidence, and never patch the machine Pub cache.

entries.mistake: The founder-facing r60.82 build handoff could be executed independently from C:\WINDOWS\system32 and the pasted invocation contained the previously seen invalid script path build-buy-device-review\.ps1, so PowerShell rejected it before the script started.
entries.rootCause: The handoff depended on a separate earlier working-directory command and did not make the action command itself absolute, atomic and self-validating despite the prior registered recurrence for this exact path-shape failure.
entries.prevention: For every founder-executed PowerShell action across UI/UX, API, backend, GCP/Firebase, deployment, APK/AAB, sideload and OPPO work, provide one atomic copy-paste command with an absolute repository path, Set-Location in the same command when repository context is required, Test-Path -PathType Leaf before invocation, and the exact script filename ending directly in .ps1; never rely on shell history, a previous line, the current directory or a directory separator immediately before .ps1.

entries.mistake: The Google-only secure environment helper invoked a repository PowerShell readiness gate and then read $LASTEXITCODE; because no native process necessarily set that automatic variable in the caller session, strict mode threw before SIDELOAD_BUILD_ENV_READY.
entries.rootCause: $LASTEXITCODE is a native-process status channel and is not a valid success contract for PowerShell-to-PowerShell script invocation; the same stale pattern could also make wrapper gate outcomes depend on unrelated earlier native commands.
entries.prevention: After every PowerShell-script gate invocation, rely on terminating errors and capture the immediate PowerShell success flag in a named boolean; reserve $LASTEXITCODE only for an immediately preceding native executable, statically reject the pattern in APK/AAB controls, and fixture-test it in a fresh strict-mode session where $LASTEXITCODE is absent.

entries.mistake: The fresh strict-mode fixture assigned Get-Command pwsh application results directly and then invoked .Source, but this environment exposes both the bundled runtime and WindowsApps aliases, producing one invalid space-joined executable name.
entries.rootCause: Executable discovery assumed a singleton ApplicationInfo result instead of selecting and validating one concrete leaf path.
entries.prevention: For every founder or automated executable handoff, enumerate candidates, select exactly one intended ApplicationInfo deterministically, expand only its Source property, validate it with Test-Path -PathType Leaf, and invoke that scalar absolute path; add this to the mandatory APK/AAB foundation fixture.

entries.mistake: The Google-only APK runtime summary still labeled SigningAndMetaInputs as present even though the corrected preparation mode deliberately removes Meta inputs and the machine state keeps Facebook disabled.
entries.rootCause: The provenance summary was inherited from the earlier all-provider PublicAuthSideloadPreflight profile and was not made conditional when Google-only preparation was introduced.
entries.prevention: For Google-only successors, record signing inputs as present-not-logged and Meta inputs as absent-google-only; statically bind that exact truthful label into the mandatory APK/AAB foundation test and reject stale all-provider provenance before packaging.

entries.mistake: After issuing the authorized r60.82 cold start, the readback command assigned adb pidof output to $pid, but PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive and $PID is reserved and read-only, so the readback stopped before a retained result.
entries.rootCause: The existing REG-20260821-3061 prevention for reserved PowerShell process identifiers was not applied when composing the new inline device readback.
entries.prevention: Never declare pid, PID or other automatic-variable names in PowerShell; use a task-specific name such as $moolAppProcessId, statically scan inline device commands for reserved assignments before execution, and after this recurrence do not repeat the device mutation—read back the already-running state only.

entries.mistake: After authoritative in-place installation and cold-start readback of r60.82, the founder performed one Google sign-in attempt on OPPO and the app still reported that Google sign-in was not completed.
entries.rootCause: Not yet classified: build provenance, signer registration and server-client equality passed, so the remaining failure must be traced without assumption across the UI action, Flutter gateway, native Google SDK result, Firebase credential exchange, runtime exception mapping and post-auth navigation.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.82 Google acceptance after this single attempt; do not ask the founder to repeat it, retain only sanitized failure evidence, audit the entire Google path one bounded layer at a time, add origin-specific non-private diagnostics and negative fixtures, and require a newly authorized successor only after source correction and full Google-only preflight qualification.

entries.mistake: After the authorized bounded memory-gate retry passed, the Google readiness subagent invoked the coordination checker with unsupported parameter -TaskName, causing a PowerShell ParameterBindingException before the coordination gate executed.
entries.rootCause: The invocation used a remembered semantic parameter name instead of copying the current checker declaration, whose exact task parameter is -AgentTask.
entries.prevention: Before every coordination replay, read the checker's current parameter block and use the literal invocation: -AgentRole subagent -AgentTask '/root/google_youtube_readiness' -UseRecordedClaim -ExpectedRegistryEntryCount <count> -ExpectedRegistrySha256 <sha> -RepositoryRoot <root>. A parameter-binding rejection is zero coordination evidence and requires primary registration plus a refreshed generation before retry.

entries.mistake: The primary ran the authorized MVP execution gate after truthfully updating the FIX8 ticket for the r60.82 Google failure but before refreshing the selected-ticket manifest SHA-256, so the delivery lock rejected the stale assessment hash.
entries.rootCause: The required ticket-mutation sequence was interrupted by the subagent incident registration and gate replay, and the selected-assessment reseal step was not completed before invoking the MVP gate.
entries.prevention: After every selected-ticket byte mutation, compute its exact SHA-256, patch only the live selectedTicketAssessment.manifestSha256 field, read it back, and only then invoke the MVP gate. A known stale manifest hash must never be sent to the gate as a diagnostic.

entries.mistake: After authorizing the Google readiness subagent to replay its refreshed gates, the primary continued patching the selected FIX8 ticket, changing its bytes before the subagent reached the MVP gate and causing the subagent's selected-ticket manifest hash rejection.
entries.rootCause: The primary did not freeze the selected ticket and MVP binding for the subagent's gate window; a truthful state update was executed concurrently with the authorized audit preflight.
entries.prevention: Complete every required ticket state update first, recompute and bind its exact SHA-256 once, pass the primary MVP gate, then explicitly freeze the ticket/MVP owners until the subagent reports its gate result. Never authorize a subagent preflight while the primary still has pending selected-ticket mutations.

entries.mistake: During the frozen Google-only source audit, the subagent ran a contextual ripgrep over journey_session.dart, main.dart and the containing apps/mobile/lib root, duplicating scope and producing 910 of 971 lines with an explicit truncated-output warning.
entries.rootCause: The command combined exact files with their parent source root and requested context around a broad intent pattern, multiplying overlapping matches beyond the bounded evidence channel.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete truncated result. Resolve one exact declaration line in one verified owner, then read explicit non-overlapping source ranges of at most 100 lines. Never combine a file with its containing root or use broad context output for the Google chain audit.

entries.mistake: After all refreshed gates passed, the Google readiness subagent mixed the nonexistent explicit path apps/mobile/lib/app.dart with the existing apps/mobile/lib root; ripgrep emitted os error 2 alongside matches, making the complete lookup non-authoritative.
entries.rootCause: A remembered conventional application-owner filename was supplied without exact bounded discovery even though the live owner is apps/mobile/lib/app/moolsocial_app.dart.
entries.prevention: Discard every mixed match/error result. Use only the proven existing owner apps/mobile/lib/app/moolsocial_app.dart and explicit non-overlapping ranges of at most 100 lines; never add a remembered sibling path to an otherwise valid root search.

entries.mistake: A requested 51-line main.dart source range exceeded the remaining tool-result context and was explicitly truncated, so it could not provide authoritative Google composition evidence.
entries.rootCause: The bounded range was still too large for the live compaction boundary and the audit did not first locate a single exact anchor for a smaller projection.
entries.prevention: Discard every truncated source result. Locate one literal anchor and read only independent 10-to-20-line windows around that anchor; never infer content or completion from a truncated range.

entries.mistake: The resumed primary audit tried to read nonexistent docs/quality/regression-memory.jsonl and docs/quality/coordination-policy.json instead of the established repository owners.
entries.rootCause: Short conventional filenames were reconstructed from memory instead of resolving exact live paths with rg --files.
entries.prevention: Never guess regression or coordination filenames. Resolve exact owners first; use docs/quality/CODEX-DEVELOPMENT-REGRESSION-MEMORY.md, config/codex-development-regression-registry.json and config/codex-subagent-coordination-policy.json only after existence is proven.

entries.mistake: A bounded regression-memory presence query again piped directly from a top-level foreach statement block and PowerShell rejected it with the empty-pipe-element parser error already covered by REG3280.
entries.rootCause: The resumed inline command did not apply the known requirement to assign the loop output to a task-specific array before piping.
entries.prevention: Never pipe directly from a top-level foreach statement in Windows PowerShell. Assign bounded loop results to a task-specific array, then pipe that array, or emit each scalar independently.

entries.mistake: After ripgrep disclosed the exact owner apps/mobile/lib/core/auth/public_auth_failure.dart, the combined command still tried to read a remembered apps/mobile/lib/features/journey01/public_auth_failure.dart path and failed.
entries.rootCause: The source-read portion was composed from the conventional feature location instead of copying the exact path returned by the immediately preceding lookup.
entries.prevention: Split discovery from reading. Copy only the exact discovered owner into a later bounded read and never combine a remembered path with an authoritative lookup result.

entries.mistake: A recursive multi-extension search across the complete google_sign_in_android package emitted 581 lines and an explicit truncated-output warning, so its partial matches were not authoritative evidence.
entries.rootCause: The dependency audit searched generated sources, tests and documentation together instead of reading the already identified implementation owner and exact error-mapping range.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete search result. Read only google_sign_in_android.dart at the exact bounded error-mapping range; never recursively search the entire dependency package when one owner is already known.

entries.mistake: The dependency audit attempted to read google_sign_in_android/android/build.gradle without first proving whether the package uses Groovy or Kotlin Gradle scripts, and the path did not exist.
entries.rootCause: A conventional Groovy Gradle filename was assumed instead of enumerating the dependency's exact Android build owner.
entries.prevention: Resolve exact dependency build-script paths with a bounded rg --files lookup before reading; never assume build.gradle when build.gradle.kts may be the live owner.

entries.mistake: A coordination query selected the complete primary owners array while checking only two Android paths, producing 383 lines and an explicit truncated-output warning.
entries.rootCause: The projection returned the entire owners collection instead of two bounded boolean membership results.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete result. For owner checks, project only task plus exact boolean membership for each requested path; never emit a primary claim's full owner array.

entries.mistake: The new Google compatibility failure-sanitization fixture constructed PlatformException without importing package:flutter/services.dart, so firebase_social_auth_gateway_test.dart failed to compile while the separate 13 composition tests passed.
entries.rootCause: The production owner already imported Flutter services, but the test owner had only flutter_test and the required symbol import was omitted from the patch.
entries.prevention: Every fixture using PlatformException must explicitly import package:flutter/services.dart; treat a test-load compilation error as a failed cycle and replay the exact focused set only after registration and gate refresh.

entries.mistake: After adding the required services import, the fixture still declared const PlatformException even though that constructor is non-const, causing the repeated focused test-load compilation failure.
entries.rootCause: The exception fixture copied const style from GoogleSignInException without checking PlatformException constructor semantics.
entries.prevention: Construct PlatformException without const in every fixture; format and compile the exact test owner before accepting any combined focused cycle.

entries.mistake: The Google-only audit started the complete mobile Flutter suite even though the affected Google/Firebase/session/UI owners already had an exact focused set; after 4 hours 19 minutes it had 738 passes, 15 skips and 123 failures concentrated in unrelated visual, golden, design and Buy areas and was still running.
entries.rootCause: The validation scope expanded from the bounded Google authentication chain to the repository's complete mobile regression universe without first proving that the full suite had a qualified green baseline or a useful Google-specific stopping condition.
entries.prevention: For a bounded provider repair, run the exact affected Google/Firebase/session/startup owners plus established shared-auth lifecycle gates. Do not start the complete mobile suite unless its current baseline is independently qualified and the task explicitly requires every product surface. Never update unrelated goldens or UI baselines to make a provider repair appear green.

entries.mistake: Repeated polls of the complete mobile suite emitted explicitly truncated chunks, including outputs originally containing tens of thousands of tokens, so the exact 123-failure inventory could not be reconstructed authoritatively from the captured channel.
entries.rootCause: A high-volume parallel test process was allowed to stream broad progress and failure detail through a bounded result channel instead of writing an intentionally bounded machine-readable summary or running exact owners independently.
entries.prevention: Discard every truncated chunk and never infer the complete failure set from it. Do not replay this unbounded suite for the Google repair. Use exact test-owner invocations with bounded output, preserve their exit codes, and register any unexpected failure before a retry.

entries.mistake: The primary invoked check-codex-subagent-coordination-policy.ps1 without its mandatory AgentRole, AgentTask, ExpectedRegistryEntryCount and ExpectedRegistrySha256 parameters, so PowerShell rejected the command before policy evaluation.
entries.rootCause: The resumed audit relied on a remembered no-argument gate form instead of reading the exact live parameter declaration or reusing the previously qualified explicit invocation.
entries.prevention: Before invoking this coordination checker after compaction or registry movement, read only its declared param block and supply the exact current role, task, registry count and registry SHA-256. Never treat a parameter-binding rejection as a policy pass.

entries.mistake: The final :app:compileDebugKotlin invocation used Gradle's default warning-rich console, producing 491 lines and an explicit truncated-output warning even though the process exited zero and the retained tail contained BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
entries.rootCause: Known project and plugin migration warnings were allowed to dominate the bounded evidence channel instead of selecting a quiet plain console for this exact compile qualification.
entries.prevention: Do not accept the truncated invocation as authoritative. Re-run the exact Kotlin compile only after registration and refreshed gates with --quiet, --console=plain and --warning-mode=none, preserve its exit code, and require complete non-truncated output before qualification.

entries.mistake: The current FIX8 Google audit invoked the inherited C33E FIX2 implementation gate and it rejected because its recorded C33F successor release ticket SHA-256 no longer matches the live ticket bytes.
entries.rootCause: The historical Google gate includes a byte pin to a separate successor-release ticket whose live generation moved after that gate state was recorded; applicability and ownership were not checked before treating it as a current FIX8 oracle.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or rewrite the pin speculatively. After registration and refreshed mandatory gates, compare the exact recorded and live C33F ticket hashes without emitting private values, identify the authorized mutation history, and either refresh the owning lifecycle state through its established gate workflow or classify this historical gate as non-applicable to FIX8 with durable evidence.

entries.mistake: The C34P FIX5 public-auth readiness gate rejected the live FIX8 successor ticket as having a changed identity or release lifecycle after the r60.82 acceptance failure and current Google compatibility repair.
entries.rootCause: The inherited gate's exact FIX8 lifecycle assertion was authored for an earlier ticket generation and applicability was not confirmed against the current truthful post-r60.82 repair phase before invocation.
entries.prevention: Do not retry or relax provider readiness. After registration and mandatory gate refresh, inspect only the exact FIX8 assertion and ticket lifecycle fields; update the gate solely to recognize a truthful fail-closed repair-qualified state while preserving zero build/install authority and every provider-readiness requirement, then test the changed oracle with positive and negative fixtures before replay.

entries.mistake: On the r60.82 OPPO candidate, selecting Google displayed the generic sign-in-not-completed result because the Android google_sign_in Credential Manager path reported GoogleSignInExceptionCode.canceled before Firebase credential exchange, even when the underlying boundary could be provider or configuration failure rather than founder cancellation.
entries.rootCause: google_sign_in_android 7.2.16 maps Android GetCredentialCancellationException to canceled and documents that Credential Manager may return that cancellation after account selection for configuration or provider errors, so the Dart gateway could not distinguish a real Back/cancel from the observed native failure and incorrectly ended the flow locally.
entries.prevention: Android Google identity now uses an isolated pinned Google Play Services Auth compatibility bridge that requests the exact Web client ID, returns only an ID token to the existing Firebase credential exchange, preserves genuine cancellation, sanitizes configuration/network/provider failures, rejects concurrent requests, makes failed initialization retryable and owns sign-out. Both APK and AAB wrappers must run the permanent bridge-readiness gate before packaging; device acceptance still requires a separately authorized successor install and founder-private OPPO login.

entries.mistake: The post-repair seal update attempted to patch the FIX8 ticket and qualification document together but omitted the second explicit file header, so apply_patch searched for the document anchor in the ticket and atomically rejected the complete patch.
entries.rootCause: The combined patch was composed with one file section even though its later context belonged to a second owner, repeating the multi-file boundary class covered by REG3207.
entries.prevention: Treat the rejected patch as zero change. After registration and refreshed gates, patch the ticket and evidence document in two independent apply_patch calls, each with its own explicit owner header, then parse/read back both before refreshing the selected-ticket hash.

entries.mistake: The final non-emitting porcelain-v1 NUL-delimited dirty digest rejected its own read because git status exited zero but produced non-empty stderr; the command emitted neither dirty paths nor stderr contents.
entries.rootCause: The huge Windows worktree can produce path-length or inaccessible-directory warnings during complete untracked enumeration, and the first invocation did not prequalify the known long-path setting or classify stderr safely before requiring it to be empty.
entries.prevention: Treat the digest as failed and do not reuse its hidden stdout. After registration and refreshed gates, classify stderr only by bounded known-warning booleans without emitting paths or text, enable Git long-path handling for the read-only status process when applicable, and require exit zero plus empty stderr before accepting a new non-emitting record count and SHA-256.

entries.mistake: prepare-moolsocial-sideload-build-environment.ps1 assigns one providerQualified=true value to every X, Instagram and Facebook runtime readiness fact whenever GoogleOnly is absent, without authoritative Dev readback for each provider-specific dependency.
entries.rootCause: The script treats selection of a full-provider profile as proof of live provider readiness, conflating intended scope with verified Firebase/provider/broker/redirect/revocation configuration and recurring the false-fact class recorded by REG3243.
entries.prevention: Never derive provider qualification from a profile switch. Require a non-secret machine-state fact per provider and per dependency, bind each fact to authoritative readback evidence, fail closed when any fact is missing, and keep that provider physically non-actionable in the APK. Add positive and negative build-control fixtures before enabling one runtime define.

entries.mistake: build-buy-device-review.ps1 emits MetaInputs=absent_google_only for every PublicAuthSideloadPreflight build, even when the full-provider path requires and consumes Facebook App ID and client-token inputs.
entries.rootCause: The provenance summary is keyed only by the broad runtime profile name and does not derive its non-secret presence label from the exact Facebook-enabled machine state used by the build.
entries.prevention: Derive only a present_not_logged or absent_fail_closed Meta label from the exact required Facebook runtime state and the private-input presence check, never emit values, and add build-control fixtures proving both Google-only and full-provider provenance branches before packaging.

entries.mistake: The bounded firebase functions:list --json Dev readback exited nonzero before the public-auth function could be projected; the wrapper deliberately emitted no raw CLI, account, credential or function payload.
entries.rootCause: The Firebase CLI session, project access or command surface was unavailable in the current desktop process even though earlier founder reauthentication and historical Dev evidence exist.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the same Firebase command or infer live function state from historical evidence. After registration and refreshed gates, use one independent explicit-project Google Cloud Gen2 describe readback with output captured and projected to non-secret fields only. If that also fails, immediately request the exact founder reauthentication action.

entries.mistake: The independent explicit-project gcloud Gen2 describe for moolSocialPublicAuth also exited nonzero, so current function state, runtime identity and non-secret binding counts could not be authoritatively refreshed; no raw output was emitted.
entries.rootCause: The current desktop Google Cloud CLI credential context or function-read permission is unavailable despite the historical Dev deployment evidence and prior browser authentication flow.
entries.prevention: Do not retry either CLI readback or infer live state. Immediately request founder gcloud auth login plus explicit Dev project selection without asking for tokens. Resume one bounded Gen2 describe only after the founder returns GCLOUD_DEV_READY; if permission still fails, classify permission versus API state without emitting account data and request the exact console IAM step.

entries.mistake: The cross-provider test inventory combined the existing Firebase gateway test with three guessed conventional provider test filenames; ripgrep returned path-not-found errors for the X, Instagram and Facebook guesses alongside valid matches.
entries.rootCause: The audit inferred standalone test owner names from production filenames instead of resolving exact live owners with a bounded rg --files projection before content search.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete mixed output. After registration and refreshed gates, resolve only exact provider-related test paths with rg --files, then search each proven owner set without adding remembered filenames.

entries.mistake: The first post-reauthentication explicit-project Gen2 function readback exceeded the available output context and was truncated, so its exit state and intended non-secret projection were not authoritatively available.
entries.rootCause: The readback allowed a command result larger than the bounded scalar evidence required for readiness, making an otherwise read-only result semantically ambiguous after the founder completed gcloud authentication.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete truncated result and infer no live state. After registration and refreshed regression, coordination and MVP gates, read one allowlisted non-secret scalar per invocation with a strict output cap; classify and register any nonzero, empty, multi-line or truncated result before another retry.

entries.mistake: The bounded post-reauthentication Dev function readback proved ACTIVE state, the expected public-auth runtime identity and a valid Node.js runtime, but its secret-binding keys did not exactly equal the nine-key source contract; only the false boolean was emitted.
entries.rootCause: The live function may be behind the current FIX7/FIX8 source contract or the projected Gen2 binding shape may differ; the failed exact-set result does not safely distinguish those causes without a new bounded diagnostic.
entries.prevention: Infer neither missing binding identity nor deployment readiness from the false result. After registration and refreshed gates, compare only hashed/sorted key-name sets and counts without emitting names or values, then classify live drift versus projection-shape mismatch. Require exact source/live agreement before any full-social build or deployment decision.

entries.mistake: The first hashed secret-binding diagnostic defined and invoked a single-letter H helper; PowerShell resolved the invocation to its built-in history alias, causing parameter conversion failure before a count or hash comparison was produced.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic used a terse helper name without checking PowerShell's case-insensitive command and alias namespace, despite the permanent rule to use task-specific identifiers for development scripts.
entries.prevention: Never use single-letter or common PowerShell command names for functions, variables or helpers. After registration and refreshed gates, use one explicit task-specific helper name such as Get-MoolSocialBindingSetSha256, validate its CommandType is Function inside the same process, and accept only complete exit-zero bounded output.

entries.mistake: The interrupted full-social work created scripts/check-full-social-founder-dev-readiness.ps1 before adding that exact repository-relative owner to the primary coordination claim.
entries.rootCause: The source file was introduced before the owner-claim update was completed, leaving the new checker outside the machine-enforced claim even though related existing wrappers were already owned by the primary.
entries.prevention: Freeze the created file without editing or executing it. After registration, bind both the checker and its exact future fixture-test path to /root in the same refreshed coordination generation, replay the gate, then inspect and patch one owner at a time.

entries.mistake: The policy patch combined the registry-binding update with a remembered adjacency between the Google identity fixture and signing refresh owners that did not exist in the live primary owner array, so apply_patch atomically rejected all hunks.
entries.rootCause: The patch used an inferred local ordering instead of first reading the exact bounded lines surrounding each independently required policy anchor.
entries.prevention: Treat the rejected patch as zero change. After registration, discover the literal registryBinding lines and one proven nearby script-owner anchor, then patch the binding and owner additions in separate explicit hunks within the same policy owner and parse/read back the exact results before gate replay.

entries.mistake: The refreshed primary claim included scripts/test-full-social-founder-dev-readiness.ps1 before that future fixture owner existed, so the coordination gate rejected the complete generation as missing an owner.
entries.rootCause: The recovery attempted to preclaim a not-yet-created file even though the coordination policy requires every recorded owner to exist and a separate already-owned build-control test can host the fixtures.
entries.prevention: Do not create a claim/file ordering loophole. Remove the nonexistent owner, retain only the existing claimed checker, implement positive and negative fixtures inside scripts/test-public-auth-sideload-build-controls.ps1, and require a clean coordination replay before any checker edit or execution.

entries.mistake: The exact nine-owner cross-provider Flutter test command exited zero and its visible tail said all tests passed, but the compact progress stream exceeded the output budget and was truncated before a complete authoritative result could be retained.
entries.rootCause: The compact reporter still rewrites verbose per-test progress for a multi-owner suite, while the command sent the complete stream through the bounded desktop result instead of separating execution evidence from the concise readback.
entries.prevention: Do not infer qualification from exit zero plus a terminal line when any output truncation marker exists. After registration and refreshed gates, rerun the same exact owners with the JSON reporter redirected to a unique temporary file, retain full session and exit metadata, parse every line locally, and emit only terminal success plus exact test-result counts before deleting the agent-owned temporary file.

entries.mistake: The first replacement for the truncated focused test used a long inline PowerShell command with computed temporary files and cleanup; the desktop execution policy rejected the complete process launch before Flutter started.
entries.rootCause: The recovery combined execution, redirection, parsing and destructive temporary cleanup in one opaque command instead of using a short explicit repository-contained evidence path and a separate bounded readback.
entries.prevention: Treat the rejection as zero execution and never retry the same command. After registration and refreshed gates, run the exact test once with JSON redirected to an explicit unique artifacts/quality evidence file, retain it rather than deleting it, then parse that fixed file in a separate read-only command and emit only terminal/count metadata.

entries.mistake: The non-emitting long-path Git dirty digest exited zero with empty stderr and emitted the intended JSON, but CopyToAsync.GetAwaiter().GetResult() also leaked a System.Threading.Tasks.VoidTaskResult line outside the exact output allowlist.
entries.rootCause: The asynchronous stdout-copy task result was not explicitly assigned to null before the allowlisted digest object was written, recurring the VoidTaskResult class already recorded for PowerShell async helpers.
entries.prevention: Reject the complete digest despite its JSON values and emit no dirty paths. After registration and refreshed gates, assign every async GetResult return to an explicit task-specific null variable, require exactly one JSON line plus exit zero and empty stderr, then accept a freshly recomputed digest only.

entries.mistake: The Facebook return-truth audit combined a complete native-adapter read with a broad multi-owner symbol search; the desktop result exceeded its budget and truncated the adapter/test evidence.
entries.rootCause: The audit requested whole-file and broad search output even though only the signIn implementation, gateway mapping and focused test ranges were needed for the bounded repair decision.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete combined output and infer no Facebook source state from it. After registration and refreshed gates, locate exact line numbers without content, then read only independent non-overlapping ranges for signIn, result mapping and implementing test fakes before one-owner patches.

entries.mistake: The approved UI-lock replay rejected MainActivity.kt because the authorized native Google identity bridge changed its whole-file hash from the immutable Screen 02 expected value, even though the provider repair intended no accepted presentation change.
entries.rootCause: A backend/native authentication seam was added inside a file governed by a whole-file presentation lock, and the Google repair qualification did not first reconcile that mixed-owner boundary with a non-weakening lock strategy.
entries.prevention: Do not update accepted reference hashes, weaken the UI lock or build around the failure. After registration and refreshed gates, compare the accepted MainActivity baseline with the current file, isolate only the provider bridge behind a separately owned native component where feasible, and preserve or prove the exact accepted presentation/bootstrap region before replaying the unchanged UI lock.

entries.mistake: The first accepted-baseline projection diagnostic used the PowerShell -split operator with a negative limit, which retained each multi-line string as one element and yielded a semantically invalid one-line comparison.
entries.rootCause: The command imported a split-limit convention from another runtime without verifying PowerShell's negative-limit behavior before using its line counts to localize projection drift.
entries.prevention: Discard every count and position from that diagnostic. After registration and refreshed gates, compare normalized text hashes first, then use a verified parameterless newline split with independently counted newline bytes only if localization remains necessary.

entries.mistake: The first presentation-preserving Google bridge extraction called registerForActivityResult on a FlutterActivity-typed owner; release Kotlin compilation rejected the method and dependent callback fields as unresolved.
entries.rootCause: The implementation assumed the current FlutterActivity static API exposed AndroidX ComponentActivity result registration without first proving that hierarchy or casting contract in the pinned Flutter embedding.
entries.prevention: Do not retry compilation or restore the 148-line mixed MainActivity bridge. After registration and refreshed gates, inspect the pinned Flutter embedding class hierarchy without editing machine caches, then use only a compile-proven Activity Result owner or a minimal exact MainActivity delegation seam. Require release Kotlin compile plus unchanged accepted-baseline projection before build authority can open.

entries.mistake: The first r60.83 FIX8 lifecycle patch combined status, active provider, source repair, blockers and deferred providers; the live blocker/deferred array context differed from the earlier bounded projection, so apply_patch rejected every hunk atomically.
entries.rootCause: The update reused a remembered nested array shape instead of reading exact current line ranges immediately before each independent lifecycle section patch.
entries.prevention: Treat the rejected patch as zero change. After registration and refreshed gates, locate status, activeProviderAcceptanceUnit, sourceRepair, releaseAuthorization, authority and deviceAcceptance independently; patch and parse/read back one exact section at a time before recomputing the selected-ticket hash.

entries.mistake: The first r60.83 selected-ticket hash readback serialized the entire preTicketSelectionCheckpoint, including all historical assessments, and exceeded both command and model output limits instead of emitting only the bounded current FIX8 assessment.
entries.rootCause: The projection passed the checkpoint parent object directly rather than selecting only checkpointId, path, sha256, state, currentTicketId and the exact selectedTicketAssessment child mandated by AGENTS.md.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete output, including any leading ticket hash. After registration and refreshed gates, project only the six allowlisted checkpoint fields, selecting preTicketSelectionCheckpoint.selectedTicketAssessment explicitly; never enumerate or serialize historical assessment siblings.

entries.mistake: The first r60.83 APK-state projection serialized the complete requiredRuntimeDefines object and emitted Firebase client identifiers alongside safe provider booleans, despite the task's no-identifier output boundary.
entries.rootCause: The inspection selected the runtime-define parent object instead of projecting only define names and boolean qualification values while keeping founder/client inputs presence-only.
entries.prevention: Discard the entire output and never repeat or reuse any emitted identifier. After registration and refreshed gates, inspect candidate/source/authorization scalars separately and project only qualification booleans plus non-empty presence facts; patch values in place without reading or printing their contents.

entries.mistake: The full-social branch of prepare-moolsocial-sideload-build-environment.ps1 still assigned the historical FIX5 candidate id whenever GoogleOnly was absent, while r60.83 requires the FIX8 candidate across every process and artifact fact.
entries.rootCause: The earlier Google-only repair updated only one branch of a historical two-profile candidate assignment, leaving the newly authorized full-social path with a stale environment label even though the build wrapper later overrides its runtime candidate value.
entries.prevention: Do not rely on the wrapper override or prompt the founder. After registration and refreshed gates, make one exact validated CandidateId parameter govern both preparation modes, remove the historical fallback, add a static regression assertion, rerun build controls and produce one fresh successor seal before hidden input entry.

entries.mistake: The first final r60.83 seal note patch used a remembered two-line OPPO acceptance paragraph whose live wrapping differed, so apply_patch rejected the complete documentation change.
entries.rootCause: The patch anchored to prose wrapping instead of reading the current document tail after intervening qualification additions.
entries.prevention: Treat the rejected patch as zero change. After registration and refreshed gates, read only the bounded current tail and append the final seal note using one literal verified anchor; parse/read back the exact hash and path before continuing.

entries.mistake: The final r60.83 authority readback projected remembered ticket and APK-state property paths and also named a nonexistent conventional MVP-state owner, producing null authority fields and a path-not-found result.
entries.rootCause: The bounded readback assumed nested schema and owner names from prior context instead of discovering the exact current JSON sections and live MVP owner before projecting scalars.
entries.prevention: Discard all null and path-not-found projections. Discover exact owners with rg --files, inspect only bounded live schema ranges, then read releaseAuthorization, authority, founderDirective, buildResult and installResult by their proven names before a build or install.

entries.mistake: The post-readback diagnostic requested scripts/check-mvp-scope-gate.ps1, but the repository's exact live owner has a different filename, so the combined command ended with path-not-found.
entries.rootCause: The command guessed a shortened conventional gate name instead of resolving the exact current script owner before reading its parameters.
entries.prevention: Discard the combined command output and never retry the guessed path. Resolve the exact MVP gate with rg --files, read only that owner's parameter header, and invoke the discovered script once with exact required arguments.
