entries.mistake: The first refreshed coordination lookup treated activeClaims as an array of agentRole records and returned an empty primary claim even though the policy uses a different exact schema.
entries.rootCause: The lookup reused an assumed generic claim shape instead of enumerating only the current activeClaims property names before selecting the recorded primary task.
entries.prevention: Discard the empty projection. After registration and binding refresh, inspect only activeClaims type and immediate property names, then read the exact recorded primary task and invoke the coordination gate with UseRecordedClaim and the proven task value.

entries.mistake: A line-bounded APK-state read intended to inspect source metadata continued into requiredRuntimeDefines and emitted identifier-bearing configuration, recurring REG3348.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic bounded by line count rather than selecting exact JSON properties, so a nearby private-boundary object was included despite the no-identifier output rule.
entries.prevention: Discard the entire diagnostic and never repeat or use any emitted identifier. Before build, parse JSON and emit only exact candidate/source authorization booleans, counts and hashes; never use raw line ranges against an owner containing runtime configuration.

entries.mistake: The final non-emitting dirty digest grew abruptly from the last accepted checkpoint to more than ten times the record count after Android qualification commands materialized intermediates.
entries.rootCause: The digest correctly included all untracked files, but the post-qualification generated-output population had not yet been classified separately from preserved source/evidence dirt before the release checkpoint.
entries.prevention: Do not clean, delete, hide or accept the expanded digest. After registration and refreshed gates, classify every record into exact bounded generated-output versus non-generated categories without emitting paths, require empty stderr and exit zero, then rely on the independent 647-owner source-seal comparison before build.

entries.mistake: The first independent APK manifest readback assigned a filtered analyzer-path pipeline without an outer array wrapper; one result collapsed to a string and index zero became only its first character, causing command-not-found.
entries.rootCause: The command assumed PowerShell preserved a one-element pipeline as an array before selecting index zero.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete qualification command and do not rebuild or install. After registration and refreshed gates, wrap the filtered analyzer candidates in an explicit array, require exactly one selected executable, then rerun signature/package/version/plugin checks once.

entries.mistake: The authorized adb install -r process ran, but the following PowerShell receipt object used bare true/false tokens instead of $true/$false, causing command failure before the captured install result was emitted.
entries.rootCause: The external mutation and its result-projection syntax shared one command, and the projection used JSON boolean spelling rather than PowerShell boolean literals.
entries.prevention: Consume the one install authorization and never retry adb install. Register first, refresh gates, then determine outcome only through independent installed package/version and cold-start readbacks. Future mutation commands must persist or emit the external receipt before constructing any summary object and must use PowerShell-native booleans.

entries.mistake: Release actions without an explicit versioned predecessor/candidate history make it harder to prove which APK or AAB was built, installed, rejected, accepted or promoted and permit accidental regression to an older artifact.
entries.rootCause: Earlier lifecycle evidence distributed version, checksum, action count and installed-version facts across separate tickets and terminal output instead of requiring one append-only history at every release boundary.
entries.prevention: For every future APK or AAB, require candidate version name, version code, source seal, artifact SHA-256, build count and disposition. Before and after every OPPO install, record the authoritative installed version and require in-place history continuity. For AAB/Play, record predecessor and candidate versionCode plus artifact/release disposition. Reject every unversioned, history-free, duplicate or ambiguous action before mutation.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the independently version-verified r60.83 OPPO install reports that Google sign-in still does not complete.
entries.rootCause: The retained sanitized OPPO receipt is auth-unknown, proving the Google path reaches an exception boundary that the r60.83 native/Firebase mapping does not classify specifically.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.83 for Google acceptance, perform no rebuild/reinstall/retry, read only fixed sanitized provider/stage codes, and require exact real-device provider-to-Firebase-session proof before any successor authorization.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the independently version-verified r60.83 OPPO install reports that YouTube sign-in still does not complete.
entries.rootCause: The retained sanitized OPPO receipt is auth-unknown, matching Google and proving failure occurs in the shared Google identity boundary before a distinct YouTube continuation receipt.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.83 for YouTube acceptance, perform no rebuild/reinstall/retry, separate shared Google identity from YouTube continuation receipts, and require exact device completion before any successor authorization.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the independently version-verified r60.83 OPPO install reports that Facebook sign-in still does not complete.
entries.rootCause: The retained sanitized OPPO receipt is auth-facebook-firebase-provider-failure, isolating failure to Facebook's Firebase credential-exchange boundary after provider interaction rather than button wiring.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.83 for Facebook acceptance, perform no rebuild/reinstall/retry, retain only fixed stage codes, and require native callback plus Firebase session proof on OPPO before a successor artifact.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the independently version-verified r60.83 OPPO install reports that X sign-in still does not complete.
entries.rootCause: The retained sanitized OPPO receipt is auth-provider-unavailable, proving the runtime rejects X before authorization launch despite the qualified console/source readiness record.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.83 for X acceptance, perform no rebuild/reinstall/retry, retain only fixed stage codes, and require exact callback-to-session completion on OPPO before a successor artifact.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the independently version-verified r60.83 OPPO install reports that Instagram sign-in still does not complete.
entries.rootCause: The retained sanitized OPPO receipt is auth-provider-unavailable, proving the runtime rejects Instagram before authorization launch despite the qualified Business Login/source readiness record.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.83 for Instagram acceptance, perform no rebuild/reinstall/retry, retain only fixed stage codes, and require exact callback-to-session completion on OPPO before a successor artifact.

entries.mistake: The first provider-source metric inventory piped directly from a top-level foreach block and PowerShell rejected the empty pipe element before reading any owner.
entries.rootCause: The command repeated the exact prohibited pipeline shape already covered by REG3312 instead of collecting rows into an explicit task-specific array.
entries.prevention: Treat the parser rejection as zero evidence. After registration and refreshed gates, populate an explicit results array inside foreach and pipe only that completed array to serialization; never repeat the direct foreach pipeline form.

entries.mistake: The first broker-source search guessed backend/src and backend/test roots that do not exist in the production checkout.
entries.rootCause: The forensic command used conventional package layout instead of resolving exact TypeScript owners from the current repository inventory.
entries.prevention: Discard the complete lookup and infer no backend state. After registration and refreshed gates, use rg --files to resolve exact function and test roots, then search only returned owners without retrying guessed paths.

entries.mistake: A source-constant comparison searched the APK machine-state owner directly and emitted two public runtime endpoint values, recurring the stricter REG3348/REG3354 no-runtime-identifier output rule.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed safe source constant discovery with an identifier-bearing machine-state owner instead of comparing values internally and projecting only booleans.
entries.prevention: Discard and never repeat or reuse the emitted values. After registration and refreshed gates, parse source and machine state internally, compare normalized endpoints, scopes and callbacks, and emit only exact-match booleans and counts.

entries.mistake: The first Facebook result-taxonomy patch anchored its message switch to remembered wording that differs from the live contract, so apply_patch rejected every hunk atomically.
entries.rootCause: The enum/code/message update used one unverified prose anchor after intervening source changes instead of reading the exact current switch range immediately before patching.
entries.prevention: Treat the rejection as zero change. After registration and refreshed gates, read only the exact enum, safe-code and safe-message range, then patch that verified block without relying on remembered wording.

entries.mistake: Three Flutter test processes ran concurrently in the same mobile checkout; the shared group failed during compiler cache copy because another process had already created the target track.dill file.
entries.rootCause: Workspace-level Flutter test cache ownership is not concurrency-safe even when test file sets are disjoint.
entries.prevention: Retain the two independently completed groups, classify the shared group as not executed, and after registration and refreshed gates rerun only that group alone. Serialize every future Flutter test command in this checkout; parallelize non-Flutter read-only work only.

entries.mistake: The serialized shared-auth Flutter run displayed a terminal 69/69 pass line but exceeded the desktop output budget, so its complete stream was not retained.
entries.rootCause: Compact reporter progress still emitted enough path-rich lines and device-review receipts to truncate the tool result.
entries.prevention: Discard the streamed result for qualification. After registration and refreshed gates, rerun the exact serialized suite once with JSON output redirected to a retained repository evidence file, parse every line plus terminal success and counts, and emit only the bounded summary.

entries.mistake: The release Kotlin compile session closed after an empty final stdout poll, but the polling wrapper emitted only output text and discarded the returned exit-code field.
entries.rootCause: The final write_stdin result was projected as stdout alone instead of serializing exit_code and session state before closure.
entries.prevention: Do not infer compile success from a closed session or warning-only output. After registration and refreshed gates, rerun the cached compile once and serialize the complete exec result including exit_code; every later session poll must retain exit status explicitly.

entries.mistake: The first read-only Identity Platform configuration command exited 2 because that command surface is unavailable in the installed gcloud distribution.
entries.rootCause: The forensic path assumed an Identity Platform gcloud command group without first resolving its availability in the installed CLI.
entries.prevention: Discard the result and do not retry the unsupported command. Register first, wait for the exact screenshot boundary, then resolve one supported Firebase CLI or authenticated REST read-only owner and project only provider/domain booleans without identities or values.

entries.mistake: The first two-screenshot resolver called Trim on an empty/null ADB directory-check projection and stopped before any screenshot listing or pull.
entries.rootCause: The command assumed adb shell would always emit one string for a false directory predicate instead of capturing output as an explicit array and joining null-safely.
entries.prevention: Record zero file access. After registration and refreshed gates, capture each directory predicate and listing as explicit arrays, join null-safely, select only the two latest standard screenshot images, emit no remote paths, and pull only those two files to non-overwriting evidence owners.

entries.mistake: One of the two founder-authorized latest OPPO screenshots contained a private email address and was temporarily copied into the repository evidence directory for inspection.
entries.rootCause: The bounded collection could not know whether the screenshot contained identity text before visual inspection, while the ticket forbids retaining an address in durable evidence.
entries.prevention: Never transcribe, hash, cite or retain the private address. Register only the sanitized UI failure state, delete the two exact local screenshot copies without touching OPPO originals, and require future screenshots to be attached with identity redacted when practical.

entries.mistake: The first privacy cleanup combined computed target validation, two Remove-Item operations and summary projection in one PowerShell command; desktop policy rejected process creation before execution.
entries.rootCause: A simple exact-file cleanup was expressed as a long computed destructive script rather than one literal non-recursive command per already verified copy.
entries.prevention: Treat rejection as zero deletion. After registration and refreshed gates, issue one simple native PowerShell Remove-Item command per exact literal local copy, verify absence separately, use no recursion or computed path, and leave OPPO originals untouched.

entries.mistake: The follow-up one-file literal Remove-Item command was also rejected by desktop process policy before execution.
entries.rootCause: The environment blocks shell-based deletion of the copied image even when the target is exact and non-recursive.
entries.prevention: Do not retry shell deletion or switch shells. After registration and refreshed gates, use the repository patch mechanism to delete only the two exact local copy owners, verify absence read-only, and keep OPPO originals untouched.

entries.mistake: The repository patch mechanism rejected deletion of the first JPEG copy because binary bytes are not valid UTF-8 text.
entries.rootCause: apply_patch can delete text owners only after reading them as UTF-8 and cannot process the copied binary evidence file.
entries.prevention: Do not retry patch deletion, switch shells, or retain the address intentionally. Ask the founder immediately to run two exact literal Remove-Item commands in their PowerShell, then verify absence read-only; OPPO originals remain untouched.

entries.mistake: The first retained Email Link local cycle completed with 26 passed, one failed, zero skipped and terminal success false.
entries.rootCause: The legacy Email Link parity suite expected tapping an unavailable Facebook provider to open a recovery dialog, but the current approved FIX8 contract correctly renders unavailable providers with a null onTap and no dispatch.
entries.prevention: Reject cycle one. Keep the shared approved rule that unavailable providers are physically non-actionable, assert null onTap plus zero gateway/dialog dispatch in every parity suite, then run one new non-overwriting serialized Email Link cycle.

entries.mistake: The first retained failure parser assigned to $error, colliding case-insensitively with PowerShell's reserved read-only $Error automatic variable.
entries.rootCause: The bounded parser reused a common single-word variable instead of a task-specific failure-event name.
entries.prevention: Discard the parser output. After registration and refreshed gates, use $emailFailureEvent and other task-specific names, project only failed test name plus bounded assertion, and verify screenshot-copy absence separately in the same read-only result.

entries.mistake: A combined source read passed the stale path scripts/build-buy-device-review/.ps1 and a scripts/*.ps1 wildcard directly to rg on Windows, producing path-not-found and invalid-filename errors.
entries.rootCause: The command guessed the build-wrapper path and relied on shell wildcard expansion that rg does not receive consistently in PowerShell instead of resolving owners with rg --files first.
entries.prevention: Reject that query result. Resolve exact repository owners with rg --files, pass only verified literal paths to later reads, and use rg --glob for filename selection rather than Windows wildcard path arguments.

entries.mistake: The first bounded firebase hosting:sites:list Dev readback exited one because the Firebase CLI credentials had expired.
entries.rootCause: The desktop Firebase CLI authentication session was no longer valid even though earlier console and gcloud sessions had succeeded.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the Hosting query, start reauthentication, or infer a custom-domain binding. Preserve the console proofs for provider enablement and authorized domains, keep Hosting custom-domain attachment unresolved, and ask the founder for a domain-only Hosting console screenshot if that fact is required.

entries.mistake: The Firebase SDK version probe passed both the real android/gradle.properties owner and a guessed package-root gradle.properties path to rg, causing a path-not-found diagnostic even though the real owner yielded the BoM version.
entries.rootCause: The command inferred an optional duplicate property-file location instead of resolving the package inventory before the content query.
entries.prevention: Discard the mixed probe as a clean command result while retaining only the independently visible real-owner fact. Resolve package files first and query verified literal owners only; do not retry the missing root path.

entries.mistake: The first syntax-only multi-file parser command piped a foreach statement directly into ConvertTo-Json, producing an empty-pipe-element ParserError before any target file was parsed.
entries.rootCause: The command omitted explicit collection of the foreach output before the pipeline.
entries.prevention: Do not infer target syntax status. After registration and refreshed gates, assign the foreach results to a task-specific array and serialize that array in a separate statement.

entries.mistake: r60.83 packaged MOOLSOCIAL_EMAIL_LINK_DOMAIN=moolsocial.com even though only Authentication authorized-domain status, not Firebase Hosting custom-domain attachment, had been proved.
entries.rootCause: The build configuration treated an authorized OAuth/Authentication domain as equivalent to a configured Firebase Hosting linkDomain, while the modern Firebase Email Link API requires linkDomain to name a Hosting domain.
entries.prevention: Dev successors must use moolsocial-dev-503018.firebaseapp.com with the authorized https://moolsocial.com/app continue URL. APK machine state, APK wrapper, AAB wrapper and mandatory foundation tests now reject any missing or different Email Link domain before artifact creation; a custom domain requires separate authoritative Hosting binding evidence first.

entries.mistake: The first final non-emitting dirty-digest tool wrapper failed JavaScript parsing with Unexpected string before the PowerShell or git process started.
entries.rootCause: An oversized inline JavaScript string composed around the PowerShell byte-stream program was not accepted by the orchestration parser.
entries.prevention: Do not infer a digest. After registration and refreshed gates, pass the PowerShell program directly as one verified template-literal command and return only exit, byte count, NUL-record count, SHA-256 and stderr length.

entries.mistake: The first executed final dirty digest returned exit zero but accumulated 73346 stderr bytes, so its SHA-256 could not be accepted as an unambiguous non-emitting worktree seal.
entries.rootCause: Git status traversed the huge Windows dirty tree without an explicit long-path configuration and emitted suppressed diagnostics even though the porcelain byte stream completed.
entries.prevention: Reject that digest. After registration and refreshed gates, rerun the byte-stream hash with git -c core.longpaths=true, keep all paths suppressed, and accept only exit zero plus stderr length zero with byte, NUL-record and SHA-256 metrics.

entries.mistake: The first current-registry summary command queried a guessed regressions property and failed when it attempted to index the resulting null value.
entries.rootCause: The command did not project the registry's root property names before selecting its entries collection.
entries.prevention: Never infer a registry collection name from memory. Project root property names first, register any mismatch, then read count and last ID only from the verified entries collection before refreshing the coordination binding.

entries.mistake: A read-only provider audit received the new registry count and SHA before the primary coordination-policy binding update had completed, so its exact coordination retry correctly failed closed as stale.
entries.rootCause: The primary broadcast the new registry generation immediately after registry mutation instead of first updating and reading back the coordination-policy binding and passing the primary gates.
entries.prevention: After every registry mutation, keep subagents stopped; update and read back the exact policy binding, pass the primary memory and coordination gates, then broadcast one literal generation and retry authorization. Subagents must continue to stop without follow-on action on any stale-binding result.

entries.mistake: A read-only provider audit's first refreshed regression-memory gate returned only an output-truncation notice, so the mandatory gate result was semantically unavailable.
entries.rootCause: The subagent accepted the default command-output budget for a large mandatory-memory gate whose output exceeded the available model context.
entries.prevention: Treat every truncated gate as failed and stop. On a primary-authorized retry, run the same exact gate with a bounded larger output budget or capture only its complete allowlisted summary and exit metadata; never infer a pass from partial output.

entries.mistake: A broad social-auth source search named two nonexistent backend paths and matched too many mobile files, producing path errors and truncated output.
entries.rootCause: The command guessed backend directory locations and combined provider implementation, UI, session, and test patterns into one unbounded result instead of first enumerating exact owners.
entries.prevention: Reject the broad result. Enumerate repository files first, then inspect one verified provider owner or one tightly bounded symbol range per command with an explicit output budget; never infer absence or completeness from missing-path diagnostics or truncated matches.

entries.mistake: The X and Instagram read-only audit grouped four distinct focused test-owner paths into one ripgrep command while enumerating test names.
entries.rootCause: The subagent optimized search latency across otherwise independent X, Instagram, shared Firebase, and runtime-composition test owners, conflicting with the mandatory independent-owner read discipline.
entries.prevention: Reject the grouped result. After primary registration and refreshed generation, read or search exactly one literal test owner per command, report each owner independently, and synthesize only after every bounded read completes without error or truncation.

entries.mistake: A bounded package-lock lookup used Select-String with the entire line array as one InputObject and failed to locate the expected flutter_facebook_auth entry.
entries.rootCause: The PowerShell command shape bypassed normal pipeline-per-line matching, then threw a missing-entry assertion before a valid literal-file search was attempted.
entries.prevention: Reject the absence inference. After registration and refreshed gates, search the one verified lock owner with a literal ripgrep pattern or pipe individual lines, then emit only the bounded matching package block.

entries.mistake: The X and Instagram audit's first one-owner test-name projection failed at PowerShell parse time with a missing-parenthesis error caused by mixed quote escaping in a redaction regular expression.
entries.rootCause: The command added unnecessary inline regex redaction to a nonsecret test-name projection and composed incompatible quote layers.
entries.prevention: Do not retry the mixed-quote command. After primary registration and refreshed gates, use a literal Select-String or ripgrep pattern against exactly one verified test owner with no inline redaction expression, bounded output, and complete exit metadata.

entries.mistake: The X and Instagram audit searched the bounded web-public file inventory for an assetlinks association name but allowed ripgrep's ordinary no-match exit code to surface as a failed command.
entries.rootCause: The absence probe was not explicitly normalized into a successful count-and-path projection, so its exit metadata was ambiguous under the repository failure rules.
entries.prevention: Reject the absence conclusion. After primary registration and refreshed gates, enumerate the one literal directory with rg --files, filter in PowerShell, and emit an explicit MatchCount plus bounded paths with exit zero even when MatchCount is zero; never infer authoritative absence from an unhandled ripgrep exit 1.

entries.mistake: The production Facebook native bridge replaced the SDK token's real grant and decline state with a fabricated public_profile grant and empty decline set, making the later permission check tautological.
entries.rootCause: The bridge preserved only tokenString after flutter_facebook_auth changed AccessToken into ClassicToken and LimitedToken variants, while retaining an older synthetic permission projection.
entries.prevention: Accept only a ClassicToken with nonempty token and authoritative native grant/decline lists for the current Android flow; preserve those exact sets, fail closed for unsupported or incomplete token variants, and cover the production projection directly.

entries.mistake: Immediately after a successful Firebase credential exchange, interactive completion reloaded the user before accepting the session, so a transient second network failure could roll back a valid sign-in.
entries.rootCause: Interactive credential continuity and cold-start session revalidation shared one bootstrap implementation even though their trust inputs and failure semantics differ.
entries.prevention: Thread the credential-exchange UID into interactive bootstrap, require current-user continuity and a nonempty ID token without redundant reload, and retain reload only for authenticated relaunch revalidation.

entries.mistake: The social gateway returned a Firebase UID but JourneySession discarded it, while bootstrap independently accepted any nonempty current UID.
entries.rootCause: The AccountBootstrapGateway contract had no expected-user input and therefore could not bind the authenticated credential result to the session it finalized.
entries.prevention: Pass expected UID from SocialAuthResult through completion, reject current-user mismatch with a fixed sanitized code, roll back, and test each shared identity path.

entries.mistake: The Android native identity future and Firebase signInWithCredential future had no bounded timeout, allowing a lost return or stalled exchange to leave login pending indefinitely.
entries.rootCause: Only the later account-bootstrap phase had an explicit timeout; upstream asynchronous seams relied on provider SDK completion indefinitely.
entries.prevention: Apply separate bounded native-return and Firebase-credential timeouts with fixed safe codes, preserve cancellation separately, and prove retry and one-shot completion.

entries.mistake: The Google native bridge stored its pending MethodChannel result only in the current Activity instance, so recreation or destruction could interrupt or lose the provider return.
entries.rootCause: The compatibility bridge used startActivityForResult and an in-memory pendingResult instead of lifecycle-aware Activity Result ownership with reconstructable state.
entries.prevention: Move to lifecycle-safe one-shot Activity Result ownership or an ActivityAware plugin, preserve sanitized interruption semantics, and add Kotlin coverage for recreation, duplicate result, null intent and destruction.

entries.mistake: The native Google sign-out bridge returned success for every completed task, including failed tasks, allowing stale identity cache after rollback.
entries.rootCause: The addOnCompleteListener callback did not inspect task success or exception.
entries.prevention: Return success only for a successful task, emit a fixed sanitized cleanup error otherwise, retain the original bootstrap failure as primary, and test failed sign-out followed by retry.

entries.mistake: JourneySession retained only the latest social-auth receipt, so later stages overwrote the evidence needed to locate a failed installed attempt.
entries.rootCause: The receipt model was a single string rather than a bounded per-attempt sanitized sequence.
entries.prevention: Retain a bounded stage sequence with a nonidentity attempt counter, exclude tokens/accounts/emails/IDs, clear it on the next attempt, and assert exact sequences in local tests.

entries.mistake: Android declares autoVerify HTTPS callbacks under moolsocial.com/app, but the bounded Hosting public-source inventory contains no .well-known/assetlinks.json association artifact.
entries.rootCause: Callback manifest wiring advanced without a signing-authoritative Hosting association owner or gate.
entries.prevention: Add a generated association artifact from registered package and allowed Dev/Play signer fingerprints, exact JSON content type/cache rules, and a gate; never guess or print fingerprint values and do not deploy without separate authorization.

entries.mistake: Raw App Check, external-browser launch and Firebase custom-token exceptions collapsed into the generic auth-broker-unexpected stage.
entries.rootCause: Production closures in main.dart exposed raw dependency futures to the adapter's final Object catch instead of translating them at their owning seam.
entries.prevention: Wrap each seam in a fixed sanitized configuration/network/UI/Firebase failure, keep timeout distinct, and add one production-seam test per exception and empty result.

entries.mistake: The mobile broker accepted backend revocation_failed but did not map it explicitly, converting a known fail-closed server stage into auth-broker-unclassified.
entries.rootCause: The accepted-code allowlist and safe-code mapping table evolved independently.
entries.prevention: Add fixed auth-revocation-failed mapping and a parity table test that proves every accepted backend error code has one explicit mobile mapping.

entries.mistake: Backend authorization_denied became the same cancelled outcome and auth-cancelled receipt as a user closing the provider flow.
entries.rootCause: BrokeredPublicAuthOutcome lacked a distinct denied terminal state and the shared gateway/session contract modeled only authenticated, pending and cancelled outcomes.
entries.prevention: Add a denied outcome with fixed customer copy and receipt, preserve true cancellation separately through gateway and JourneySession, and test denial end to end.

entries.mistake: JourneySession accepted any recognized callback as handled success when already authenticated without consuming or rejecting broker state.
entries.rootCause: An early convenience short-circuit preceded callback completion and bypassed the broker's one-time state and replay controls.
entries.prevention: Remove the success shortcut; fail closed with a fixed stale/already-authenticated receipt or consume and reject without account swap, and test duplicate callback plus authenticated relaunch.

entries.mistake: Partial social-auth rollback swallowed sign-out failure, so Firebase identity could remain active while the UI reported failed bootstrap and allowed an unsafe retry.
entries.rootCause: Rollback deliberately preserved the original visible error but had no secondary cleanup state or retry block.
entries.prevention: Record a fixed rollback-failed state, keep Ready blocked, prevent another attempt until cleanup succeeds, bound cleanup, and preserve the original failure without exposing raw details.

entries.mistake: Existing tests proved abstract availability facts but did not evaluate the exact sealed successor define profile to prove every requested adapter and production provider was present before artifact creation.
entries.rootCause: Runtime-profile provenance and functional adapter composition were checked by separate gates without one exact-manifest integration assertion.
entries.prevention: Add one exact-profile pre-artifact test/gate that composes the registered define manifest, proves all five providers, distinct callbacks, nonnull adapters, App Check and Firebase bootstrap, and fails before APK or AAB creation.

entries.mistake: Focused tests covered individual gateways and sessions but did not compose a real provider result through JourneySession and router, nor directly cover the Kotlin callback mapper/lifecycle boundary.
entries.rootCause: Qualification accumulated seam tests without one cross-layer acceptance owner for interactive success, mismatch, timeout, rollback and route readiness.
entries.prevention: Add composed Dart tests for each shared provider class and pure Kotlin bridge-result/lifecycle tests; require exact stage sequences and zero Ready transition on every failure.

entries.mistake: Two newly registered defects named the planned apps/mobile/android/app/src/test directory as if it were retained evidence before that directory existed, causing the mandatory regression-memory gate to fail closed.
entries.rootCause: The batch reused a future test target as an evidence owner instead of limiting evidence to existing source, ticket and test files.
entries.prevention: Registry evidence arrays may contain only existing repository owners. Future test targets belong in gates or prevention text until created; validate every newly added evidence path before refreshing the policy binding and running the memory gate.

entries.mistake: After fixing two missing future Kotlin-test references, the next memory-gate retry found the same nonexistent directory in the Google sign-out incident's gate list.
entries.rootCause: The correction targeted the paths named in the first failure instead of validating every gate and evidence path across the entire newly appended incident batch before retry.
entries.prevention: Before the next gate retry, project every gate and evidence path in all new entries, require Test-Path true for each, correct the full batch in one bounded registry edit, refresh the exact binding, and only then rerun memory once.

entries.mistake: A bounded rg --files check against the previously used scripts/build-buy-device-review literal path returned an IO missing-path error while validating a registry evidence reference.
entries.rootCause: The registry batch reused a historical command path as an evidence owner without first verifying its exact current filesystem representation in the preserved dirty tree.
entries.prevention: Do not infer deletion, rename or build readiness from the failed literal probe. Use verified existing machine-state and build-control owners in registry evidence; before any separately authorized artifact, inventory scripts once from the scripts root and require the wrapper's exact resolved leaf path.

entries.mistake: A coordination-claim schema probe serialized the first active claim including the primary's large owner array, producing truncated output instead of the intended compact field-name projection.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic object included the complete First claim after already projecting FirstProperties.
entries.prevention: Never serialize active-claim owner arrays for coordination diagnostics. Project only task, role, owner count and exact requested task matches; reject any truncated policy projection and rely on the machine gate for full overlap validation.

entries.mistake: The X OAuth regression-test apply_patch response exceeded the tool output limit and was truncated, so the result could not authoritatively establish which intended hunks were applied.
entries.rootCause: Several independent test changes were submitted in one patch whose returned diff exceeded the bounded output channel.
entries.prevention: Treat every truncated patch result as ambiguous. Register it before retry, refresh the exact registry binding and mandatory gates, inspect only the intended bounded regions, and apply any missing changes in small independently verifiable hunks.

entries.mistake: A bounded lookup included the historical scripts/check-mvp-scope-state.ps1 path, which is not present in the current checkout, so ripgrep returned an IO error.
entries.rootCause: The post-compaction gate reconstruction reused a remembered script leaf name instead of first projecting the current scripts inventory.
entries.prevention: Register the failed lookup before retry. Resolve the exact current MVP gate path with one bounded scripts inventory, then invoke only the verified leaf and preserve its RequireExecutionAuthorized semantics.

entries.mistake: The new production dependency safe-code table called the X adapter test helper without its required transport named argument, so the focused suite stopped at test compilation after 78 passing tests.
entries.rootCause: The table exercises pre-transport failures, but the helper signature still requires an explicit transport seam even when that seam must remain unused.
entries.prevention: Every adapter fixture must satisfy the complete helper contract. Supply an explicit transport closure that throws if reached, then rerun the bounded focused suite only after refreshing registry binding and mandatory gates.

entries.mistake: A default rg --files projection omitted the hidden .well-known association path and led to a false assessment that the Android App Links source was absent.
entries.rootCause: The bounded inventory did not use a hidden-file-aware mode and its empty match was treated as authoritative for a dot-directory.
entries.prevention: For every dot-directory or association-file audit, use an exact Test-Path or hidden-file-aware inventory and never print association credential values. Qualify the hosted fallback alongside the existing association instead of treating it as a replacement.

entries.mistake: The prior Email Link repair explicitly supplied the default firebaseapp.com Hosting domain as ActionCodeSettings.linkDomain instead of allowing Firebase Authentication to select that default domain automatically.
entries.rootCause: The repair was based on an Android/default-domain fragment before reading the complete Flutter Email Link contract, which states that linkDomain is optional custom Hosting-domain configuration and cannot be a default Hosting domain.
entries.prevention: For the default Firebase Hosting Email Link path, require an empty runtime link-domain value so FlutterFire receives null, retain the exact default-domain Android /__/auth/links intent filter, and gate against dynamicLinkDomain or an explicitly supplied default domain.

entries.mistake: A bounded Get-Content projection of the public-auth sideload control assertions unexpectedly exceeded the tool context and returned truncated output, so it could not be used as authoritative edit evidence.
entries.rootCause: The requested line range was still too verbose for the active output envelope and relied on positional context instead of exact semantic anchors.
entries.prevention: Stop on any truncated read, register it before retry, then use compact exact-string searches with two lines of context and patch only the independently matched assertions.

entries.mistake: The refreshed primary coordination gate invocation supplied the exact task and registry binding but omitted the mandatory explicit ClaimedOwners argument.
entries.rootCause: The compact reconstructed command retained the prior task identity but did not carry forward the repository's explicit owner projection.
entries.prevention: After every registry rebinding, read the recorded exact task claim and pass its complete owner set explicitly; never retry a rejected coordination command from memory.

entries.mistake: A recursive search for YouTube runtime define usage included historical machine states and exceeded the output envelope, returning a truncated result.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic scope was broader than the active FIX10 owners and mixed current implementation with numerous historical candidate files.
entries.prevention: Restrict runtime-cohort diagnostics to the active build wrapper, active machine state, active prebuild gate, and exact mobile source owners; never infer completeness from truncated historical search output.

entries.mistake: The journey-session test lookup passed a Windows wildcard path directly to rg, which Windows rejected as an invalid filename shape.
entries.rootCause: The lookup mixed one exact path with a shell-style wildcard argument instead of resolving candidates through the repository inventory.
entries.prevention: On Windows, resolve test candidates with rg --files and a pattern filter, then pass only exact literal paths to content searches.

entries.mistake: The 115-test focused auth run displayed its terminal All tests passed line, but the tool envelope also reported truncated output, so the run cannot be accepted as authoritative evidence.
entries.rootCause: The compact reporter still emitted per-test progress and device-review diagnostics across nine files, exceeding the output limit.
entries.prevention: For multi-file Flutter qualification, use the JSON reporter and emit only the terminal done event while preserving the native Flutter exit code; never infer success from any truncated transcript.

entries.mistake: The new Firebase account-bootstrap constructor assigned two parameters to same-named private fields in an initializer list, producing two prefer_initializing_formals analyzer infos.
entries.rootCause: The constructor repair preserved explicit assignment syntax instead of following the repository's clean-analyzer initializing-formal convention.
entries.prevention: Use initializing formals for the interactive and revalidated user-ID seams, format the exact owner, and require a zero-issue flutter analyze before qualification.

entries.mistake: REG3423 placed the command text flutter analyze in its gates array, which the regression-memory contract interpreted as a missing repository evidence path.
entries.rootCause: The entry described the intended validation command instead of referencing only repository-backed gate files in the path-validated gates field.
entries.prevention: Keep registry gates and evidence arrays path-only; describe non-file commands in prevention text and retain their results in the durable qualification evidence rather than inventing a path.

entries.mistake: The direct Gradle compileReleaseKotlin plus lintRelease invocation emitted an oversized intermediate task transcript that the tool truncated.
entries.rootCause: Gradle plain-console task progress across the app and all plugins was allowed through instead of being reduced to a bounded terminal summary.
entries.prevention: Use a quiet or summary-preserving Android verification wrapper for successor checks and accept only a separately complete terminal result; do not treat a truncated intermediate chunk as success evidence.

entries.mistake: A compact foreach statement that emitted objects directly into a trailing pipeline was parsed as containing an empty pipe element.
entries.rootCause: The one-line statement mixed a foreach language construct, inline object emission, and a trailing pipeline without wrapping the construct as an expression.
entries.prevention: Use Get-Item piped to ForEach-Object or collect the foreach results into an explicit task-specific variable before formatting; avoid dense statement-plus-pipeline compositions.

entries.mistake: The shared public-authentication gate rejected the current MVP execution authority even though the selected ticket is the explicitly authorized FIX8 auth successor.
entries.rootCause: The gate's exact ticket-selection assertion remains bound to an earlier C34P ticket projection and has not been reconciled with the current FIX8 descendant authority.
entries.prevention: Permit only the exact selected authorized FIX8 descendant alongside the original ticket, validate its registered ticket file and classification, and never generalize acceptance to arbitrary successor IDs.

entries.mistake: The FIX1A all-provider gate rejected the shared gateway because it requires the literal FacebookLoginOutcome.accountCollision in that file.
entries.rootCause: Collision handling was centralized into the sanitized Firebase failure classifier, but the older static gate still assumes provider-specific collision branching remains in the shared gateway owner.
entries.prevention: Verify exact behavioral tests for Firebase account collision and Facebook credential exchange, then make the gate accept only the centralized sanitized collision contract rather than a stale provider-specific source token.

entries.mistake: The FIX5 provider-readiness gate rejected the current FIX8 ticket identity or release lifecycle after r60.83 had already consumed its authorized build/install and was rejected by OPPO auth testing.
entries.rootCause: The static lifecycle assertion remains bound to the pre-r60.83 or intermediate release state rather than the durable consumed-and-rejected no-build state.
entries.prevention: Qualify the exact current FIX8 ticket ID, one consumed build and install, rejected auth status, false build/install authority, and fresh-action-time authorization boundary; reject any looser lifecycle.

entries.mistake: A broad multi-anchor search over the FIX8 ticket exceeded the available output context and was truncated before the current lifecycle reconciliation could be accepted.
entries.rootCause: Too many heterogeneous ticket anchors and their surrounding lines were projected in one command instead of reading one exact property subtree at a time.
entries.prevention: Use parsed JSON projections or one exact anchor per bounded read, accept only complete output, and never infer ticket state from a truncated multi-anchor transcript.

entries.mistake: The first non-emitting dirty-worktree digest helper was rejected by the command policy before git status executed.
entries.rootCause: The helper used a Start-Process redirection composition whose quoting was transformed into a command form rejected by the execution policy.
entries.prevention: Use a bounded native process stream capture that never emits filenames, report only the exact digest allowlist, and register any rejection before retrying.

entries.mistake: A coordination-policy projection included the complete /root owner array and exceeded the output limit even though only the registry binding scalars were needed.
entries.rootCause: The read filter bounded the task but not its very large owners property.
entries.prevention: Project registryBinding alone or the root task name, role, and owner count; never emit the complete primary owner array for a scalar generation update.

entries.mistake: Get-Command -LiteralPath against the coordination script emitted the unrelated command catalog and truncated instead of returning that script's syntax.
entries.rootCause: The syntax discovery used an unsuitable Get-Command invocation for a filesystem script path.
entries.prevention: Read only the script's bounded param block or invoke Get-Command with the resolved script path through the supported name argument; never accept a global command-catalog expansion.

entries.mistake: The regression-memory gate was invoked with the nonexistent FailureClass parameter and stopped before validation.
entries.rootCause: A compacted handoff shorthand was treated as literal command syntax instead of confirming the current script parameter contract.
entries.prevention: Read the gate's bounded param block before invocation after any resumed context and use only its exact current parameter names and validate sets.

entries.mistake: After the exact r60.83 consumed-and-rejected lifecycle was added, FIX5 advanced but rejected the later comprehensive successor audit sequence or held-boundaries assertion.
entries.rootCause: That later assertion still contains an exact intermediate audit-state assumption that was not included in the first release-lifecycle reconciliation.
entries.prevention: Inspect only the bounded failing assertion, preserve every held authority and historical action count, and add an exact r60.83 local-qualified no-build alternative without weakening provider, device, email, Play, SQL Connect, or production boundaries.

entries.mistake: The FIX5 gate was invoked with RequireQualified after the successor lifecycle passed even though functional OPPO/provider/live-email reproof remains pending.
entries.rootCause: Local implementation qualification was momentarily conflated with the stronger live-provider acceptance state.
entries.prevention: Use the successor lifecycle mode for the current no-build local checkpoint; invoke RequireQualified only after checksum-matched device/provider evidence exists, and never weaken the qualified facts to manufacture a pass.

entries.mistake: The C33J FIX2 Email Link gate rejected the ticket identity/seal/classification/authority assertion after the ticket advanced from implementation-authorized to locally qualified with live-email and device reproof pending.
entries.rootCause: The gate recognizes only the earlier pre-implementation state literal and not the exact current no-build, no-live-email local qualification state.
entries.prevention: Accept only the exact current ticket state with its sourceQualification facts and all Firebase Hosting, live-email, build, Play, device, backend, and secret authorities still false; do not loosen functional success.

entries.mistake: After the C33J FIX2 ticket assertion was updated, the gate advanced and rejected its separate generic-successor qualification binding.
entries.rootCause: A second exact binding still carries the prior immutable ticket hash or pre-implementation projection.
entries.prevention: Inspect only the generic-successor binding, update it to the newly computed ticket hash and exact held current state, and preserve the current FIX8 selection plus all closed external-action authorities.

entries.mistake: After the historical FIX2 binding was updated, the gate advanced and rejected the active-or-generic successor selection and closed execution boundary.
entries.rootCause: The final selection assertion remains pinned to a prior generic-successor state or authority projection despite the current authorized FIX8 source ticket and held external actions.
entries.prevention: Accept only the exact current FIX8 generic replay while runtime/test writes remain authorized and Firebase Hosting, live email, build, Play, device and secret actions remain false; never turn local replay into live acceptance.

entries.mistake: The C33J parent Email Link native-parity gate rejected its generic-successor qualification binding after the FIX2 ticket and prior assessment advanced to the current local-qualified hash.
entries.rootCause: The parent gate independently pins the historical FIX2 hash and implementation-state projection.
entries.prevention: Update only that exact FIX2 historical binding to the recomputed ticket hash and held local-qualified state, preserving the parent and FIX1 hashes plus all external-action boundaries.

entries.mistake: After the parent gate's FIX2 hash binding was updated, it advanced and rejected the active MVP selection, qualified succession or execution boundary under the current FIX8 source ticket.
entries.rootCause: The parent gate still requires the historical C33J backend-write posture even during an exactly qualified generic successor replay whose selected FIX8 ticket authorizes bounded backend source work.
entries.prevention: Accept the exact FIX8 generic replay only with runtime/test/backend source authority and Firebase Hosting, live email, external service, build, Play and device actions false; preserve functional acceptance as pending.

entries.mistake: The first parent execution-boundary patch used the nonexistent selection mode C33J_active.
entries.rootCause: The active-mode names were assumed from the ticket family instead of read from the helper's exact return values.
entries.prevention: Read and enumerate the helper's exact bounded return literals before patching selection branches; accept parent_active, FIX1_active and FIX2_active only under the historical closed backend posture.

entries.mistake: The C33J parent gate advanced beyond lifecycle checks but required the missing literal subtitle Use any email address.
entries.rootCause: Its native-reference parity anchors have not been reconciled with the current independently passing approved Screen 03 lock and source copy.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current locked source and accepted reference evidence, update only the stale gate anchor if approval proves the replacement, and never edit Screen 03 presentation to satisfy an obsolete static literal.

entries.mistake: REG3443 initially referenced a guessed screen03_login_account_handoff.dart path that does not exist.
entries.rootCause: The source owner path was inferred from the screen name instead of verifying the repository file before adding it to a path-validated registry field.
entries.prevention: Use a verified existing owner path in every registry gates/evidence field and locate the exact source only after the incident is registered; never guess repository paths.

entries.mistake: The C33J parent gate advanced after its copy-anchor repair but required the old emailLinkAvailable expression _deviceReviewMode || emailLinkRuntimeAvailable.
entries.rootCause: The runtime availability policy was hardened by the FIX8 public-auth profile work while this older gate retained the permissive device-review expression.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current runtime assignment and update only the stale gate anchor when it proves the qualified fail-closed policy; never reintroduce device-review availability as an unconditional bypass.

entries.mistake: The C33J parent gate advanced after runtime-availability reconciliation but required the old direct statement await session.prepareEmailLinkReturn(platformRouteName).
entries.rootCause: Email Link callback preparation moved into the current startup/app bootstrap owner while the historical gate remained pinned to a direct main.dart call.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current callback handoff across main and app/session owners, require the complete delegated call chain in the gate, and never reintroduce duplicate callback processing merely to satisfy an obsolete source token.

entries.mistake: The C33J parent gate passed lifecycle, UI and runtime anchors but required the missing historical test title visible unavailable provider never dispatches its gateway.
entries.rootCause: The focused test matrix was renamed or replaced during later provider-availability hardening while the older static inventory retained the original title.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current ten test titles, verify equivalent or stronger unavailable-provider coverage, and update only the stale title inventory while preserving the exact count and behavior checks.

entries.mistake: The reconciled C33J parent gate passed its 11-test assertion but its success output still reported focusedMatrix=10.
entries.rootCause: The human-readable terminal summary was a separate hardcoded literal and was not updated with the assertion count.
entries.prevention: Keep gate assertions and terminal evidence counts synchronized and rerun the gate after any matrix-count change; never report a stale passing count.

entries.mistake: The C33J FIX1 foreground-return gate rejected its generic-successor qualification binding after the FIX2 ticket and prior assessment advanced to the current local-qualified hash.
entries.rootCause: FIX1 independently duplicates the historical FIX2 hash and implementation-state projection already reconciled in the parent and FIX2 gates.
entries.prevention: Update only the exact FIX2 binding in FIX1, preserve the parent and FIX1 historical pins, and keep live email, Hosting, build, Play, device and secret authorities closed.

entries.mistake: After FIX1's historical FIX2 binding was updated, it advanced and rejected the active succession or closed external boundary under the current FIX8 source ticket.
entries.rootCause: FIX1 retains the historical C33J backend-write posture and lacks the exact current FIX8 generic-replay branch already required by the parent and FIX2 gates.
entries.prevention: Accept only the exact current FIX8 generic replay with bounded runtime/test/backend source authority and Firebase Hosting, live email, external service, build, Play, device and secret actions false.

entries.mistake: The C33K Firebase Email Link live-readiness gate was invoked in Prewrite mode while live-email and Firebase-write authority remain false.
entries.rootCause: A local source-qualification sweep was extended into an action-time live-email prewrite gate without first confirming whether that phase is designed to require an authorized external write.
entries.prevention: Inspect the bounded prewrite assertion, classify an authority-required rejection as an intentional held boundary, and never edit state or gates to manufacture live-email authorization or success.

entries.mistake: The C33M generic-successor replay compatibility self-test rejected its embedded C33J generic binding even though the real parent, FIX1 and FIX2 gates pass individually.
entries.rootCause: The trilogy harness contains copied gate fixtures or expected literals that were not updated with the current FIX2 hash, implementation state and exact FIX8 replay boundary.
entries.prevention: Reconcile the fixture with the real gates' exact current bindings and held authorities, retain all negative cases, and require the consolidated compatibility test to pass after individual gate success.

entries.mistake: The workspace and repository AGENTS.md files were requested in one terminal call and the combined output exceeded the available context, so the mandatory instruction read was ambiguous and incomplete.
entries.rootCause: Two independent mandatory instruction owners were grouped into one unbounded output instead of reading each file independently and paging the long repository owner through EOF.
entries.prevention: Read the workspace AGENTS.md independently, then read the repository AGENTS.md independently in non-overlapping bounded pages through EOF; never accept truncated instruction output or group mandatory owners in one emitting command.

entries.mistake: The non-emitting dirty-worktree digest printed two System.Threading.Tasks.VoidTaskResult lines before the allowed bytes, records, SHA-256, stderr-bytes and exit-code projection.
entries.rootCause: CopyToAsync task GetResult return values were invoked as bare PowerShell expressions instead of being explicitly suppressed.
entries.prevention: Wrap every async GetResult invocation in [void], suppress all helper returns, and accept the preservation digest only when output contains exactly the five allowlisted fields.

entries.mistake: The 585-line coordination-policy JSON was read raw and the terminal result truncated before EOF, leaving a mandatory owner incomplete.
entries.rootCause: The owner length was not measured before choosing an unbounded raw read despite the permanent dense-output truncation controls.
entries.prevention: Measure the owner first, then read it independently in non-overlapping bounded pages through verified EOF and never accept a truncated raw policy read.

entries.mistake: The MVP execution gate was invoked after the FIX8 ticket authorization status changed but before the selected-ticket assessment manifest SHA-256 was refreshed.
entries.rootCause: The release-authorization transition was sequenced as ticket patch then gate instead of ticket patch, exact live hash computation, bounded MVP hash update, parse/readback and gate.
entries.prevention: After any selected-ticket byte change, compute its exact live SHA-256, update the selectedTicketAssessment manifest hash before invoking MVP scope, and verify the ticket ID/path/hash triple first.

entries.mistake: A known APK-state authority field was searched across the entire scripts directory and the live state file in one command, and the result exceeded the available context.
entries.rootCause: A broad content search was used even though the exact JSON owner and exact APK gate checker were already known.
entries.prevention: For known state fields, inspect only a bounded parsed projection from config/apk-regression-gate-state.json and the exact owning checker when needed; never retry a broad scripts-directory content search or accept truncated output.

entries.mistake: The coordination checker was invoked with an assumed -Role parameter that its current parameter block does not support.
entries.rootCause: A remembered command signature was reused instead of reading the exact current checker parameter block before invocation.
entries.prevention: Before invoking a stateful release gate, read its bounded current param block and use only declared parameters; register any parameter-binding rejection before a corrected retry.

entries.mistake: The shared public-authentication gate was invoked after the FIX8 ticket moved to the authorized r60.84 seal, while its exact FIX8 manifest or held-authority binding still represented the prior state.
entries.rootCause: The selected ticket and MVP execution state were refreshed for r60.84, but the shared-auth gateway's exact downstream binding had not yet been reconciled to that authorized transition.
entries.prevention: After an authorized selected-ticket byte transition, inspect and refresh every exact downstream manifest/authority binding in dependency order, verify hashes and held scopes, then rerun the shared gateway before any build or device mutation.

entries.mistake: Multiple search hits in the shared-auth checker each emitted overlapping context windows, expanding a small target into a truncated 738-line result.
entries.rootCause: The inspection loop rendered context per match instead of selecting the single known assertion range once.
entries.prevention: After locating a known assertion, read one non-overlapping bounded line range exactly once and reject any truncated inspection result before patching or retrying the gate.

entries.mistake: A PowerShell foreach statement was piped directly into ConvertTo-Json in a form the parser treated as an empty pipe element.
entries.rootCause: The projection did not assign foreach results to an explicit array before serialization.
entries.prevention: For multi-file PowerShell projections, collect rows in an explicit array variable first and serialize that variable; register parser failures before a corrected read.

entries.mistake: The FIX5 readiness gate rejected the authorized r60.84 FIX8 ticket because its successor identity/release-lifecycle assertion still represented an older transition.
entries.rootCause: The r60.84 ticket and MVP bindings moved forward, while the downstream FIX5 compatibility gate was not yet extended with the exact one-build/one-install authorization and held scopes.
entries.prevention: Every versioned FIX8 successor authorization must be added to downstream lifecycle gates with exact version, action counts, source seal and held authority checks before build preflight is accepted.

entries.mistake: After the FIX8 r60.84 lifecycle was recognized, the FIX5 gate advanced and rejected a separate comprehensive-successor-audit sequence or held-boundary assertion.
entries.rootCause: The compatibility gate contains an additional audit-state assertion still pinned to the prior consumed/rejected candidate sequence rather than the freshly authorized r60.84 prebuild state.
entries.prevention: Versioned successor transitions must reconcile both the ticket lifecycle and every downstream comprehensive-audit sequence with exact counts and held external/private boundaries before a build is allowed.

entries.mistake: The FIX5 gate passed r60.84 lifecycle and audit-sequence checks but its final RequireQualified assertion rejected current provider facts, action counts, or held promotion boundaries.
entries.rootCause: The -RequireQualified mode belongs to the original all-eight live-provider promotion state and correctly requires its pristine provider facts and zero build/device counts; it is not the FIX8 successor compatibility mode for the current five-social Dev candidate.
entries.prevention: For a held FIX8 successor, run the FIX5 compatibility gate without -RequireQualified and use the dedicated full-social founder-Dev readiness gate for Google, YouTube, Facebook, X and Instagram; never rewrite provider facts or action counts to manufacture all-eight promotion readiness.

entries.mistake: The APK wrapper applied its generic non-empty runtime-input rule to MOOLSOCIAL_EMAIL_LINK_DOMAIN even though the preparation, APK gate and AAB wrapper intentionally require an empty value to omit linkDomain and use Firebase's default Hosting domain.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper listed the optional domain among runtime names but lacked the one explicit empty-value exception already required by the Email Link Hosting contract.
entries.prevention: Permit empty only for MOOLSOCIAL_EMAIL_LINK_DOMAIN, continue rejecting every other blank runtime input, normalize a missing process value to an empty define, and require the shared APK/AAB sideload-control test to prove the default-domain exception and all exact Hosting assertions before every future artifact build.

entries.mistake: REG-20260823-3465 recorded the build wrapper as scripts/build-buy-device-review/.ps1, which is not the actual repository leaf path.
entries.rootCause: The path was copied from the displayed PowerShell exception location rather than resolved against the repository file inventory.
entries.prevention: Before registering gate or evidence paths, validate each exact repository-relative leaf with Test-Path and use the resolved inventory path; never copy display-normalized exception paths into durable evidence blindly.

entries.mistake: The independent APK plugin-integrity replay used -RequireMappingAware without supplying the ProguardFolderPath required for mapping-aware inspection.
entries.rootCause: The checker parameter block was read, but the exact successful wrapper invocation and its conditional mapping-folder argument were not read before replay.
entries.prevention: For every post-build verifier replay, copy the exact bounded successful wrapper call including conditional mapping inputs, validate those paths exist, and register any invocation rejection before retry or device installation.

entries.mistake: The r60.84 compatibility updates added only the buildCount=0 prebuild lifecycle, so truthful journaling of the successful build would leave the shared-auth and FIX5 gates unable to recognize the buildCount=1 install-pending state.
entries.rootCause: The versioned lifecycle was implemented as a single prebuild snapshot rather than an explicit prebuild, postbuild/install-pending, and postinstall state machine.
entries.prevention: Every authorized APK/AAB lifecycle gate must define and test all action-count transitions before the first action: prebuild, build-consumed/install-pending, and install-consumed/acceptance-pending, while forbidding rebuild, uninstall, data clear, Play, Production and private agent actions.

entries.mistake: The post-build journal patch assumed two identical successorBuildAuthorized=true lines in the live FIX8 ticket, and apply_patch rejected the unmatched context atomically.
entries.rootCause: A prior projection was translated into duplicate textual replacements without first reading the exact bounded owner blocks and occurrence counts.
entries.prevention: Before journaling an external action, read each exact target block with line-bounded context, count every replacement token, and patch ticket and APK state in independently verifiable atomic steps; register any context rejection before retry.

entries.mistake: The same PowerShell foreach-to-pipeline parser error recorded in REG-20260823-3461 recurred while locating exact ticket journal blocks.
entries.rootCause: The permanent explicit-array accumulator rule from REG3461 was not applied before composing a new multi-pattern projection.
entries.prevention: Ban direct piping of foreach statement results in release commands; always initialize $rows=@(), append PSCustomObject rows inside foreach, and serialize $rows only after the loop. Treat this reusable pattern as mandatory for every APK/AAB journal projection.

entries.mistake: The MVP post-build journal patch used a parsed selected-ticket hash value as patch context without first reading the exact textual line and indentation, so apply_patch rejected it atomically.
entries.rootCause: Structured readback was treated as sufficient patch context even though apply_patch requires the exact live textual owner representation.
entries.prevention: Use parsed projections for semantic validation, but before every patch read each exact target line with a bounded literal search; patch one owner atomically, parse it, and verify semantic fields before proceeding.

entries.mistake: The post-install ticket patch guessed the r60.84 history block indentation and apply_patch rejected the full patch atomically after the single authorized install had already succeeded.
entries.rootCause: The block-by-block exact textual patch rule from REG3469 and REG3471 was not followed for the nested release history transition.
entries.prevention: Never combine guessed nested history context with an action journal. Read exact target lines after the action, patch each owner block separately, parse and verify it, and never repeat the already consumed install regardless of journal-patch failure.

entries.mistake: The OPPO cold-start command assigned adb pidof output to $pid, which collides case-insensitively with PowerShell's read-only automatic $PID variable and made the combined readback ambiguous.
entries.rootCause: A common reserved PowerShell variable name was reused in a release-device verification command.
entries.prevention: Ban $PID/$pid and other automatic-variable names in release scripts; use a task-specific name such as $moolAppProcessId, separate mutation from readback, and never rerun the launch when a readback-only correction can classify the already completed action.

entries.mistake: The first complete-read attempt for config/codex-subagent-coordination-policy.json exceeded the tool output budget and returned a truncated middle section.
entries.rootCause: The large coordination policy owner was requested as one raw output instead of first measuring it and reading independent bounded pages.
entries.prevention: For every large mandatory JSON owner, measure lines without emitting content, then read independent non-overlapping pages of at most 250 lines through verified EOF; any truncation is incomplete and blocks retry or action until registered.

entries.mistake: The initial regression-memory page plan used Measure-Object -Line, which reported 3515 while the actual Get-Content array contained 3547 lines and would have left the final 32 lines unread.
entries.rootCause: Measure-Object -Line was treated as an exact physical-line authority even though it did not match the array cardinality used for indexed paging in this owner.
entries.prevention: For indexed PowerShell paging, establish EOF with the exact Get-Content array Count used by the page slices, read non-overlapping ranges through Count minus one, and reject any last page whose final text is semantically incomplete.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the exact installed r60.84 candidate did not complete Google Sign-In, despite earlier source, mock, configuration and pre-APK gates being green.
entries.rootCause: Unclassified at registration: the retained founder outcome does not yet distinguish UI dispatch, native Credential Manager/Google Identity, package-signing OAuth selection, Firebase credential exchange, account collision, shared-auth bootstrap or post-login navigation/session failure.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.84 permanently; trace and instrument every Google stage with sanitized receipts, prove exact installed APK/package/signing/OAuth provenance, add stage-specific negative tests and accept only one new successor after founder-completed real Google Sign-In plus authenticated relaunch/navigation verification on OPPO.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the exact installed r60.84 candidate did not complete the YouTube sign-in path.
entries.rootCause: Unclassified at registration; shared Google identity remains a plausible dependency, but the failed outcome alone does not prove the exact stage or cause.
entries.prevention: Keep YouTube implementation and acceptance on hold, preserve r60.84 as rejected, and perform no YouTube retry or repair until the Google-only successor is founder-accepted on OPPO and a separately authorized provider ticket is selected.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the exact installed r60.84 candidate did not complete Facebook sign-in.
entries.rootCause: Unclassified at registration; no provider, native-SDK, Firebase exchange or shared-bootstrap cause is inferred from the founder-visible failure alone.
entries.prevention: Keep Facebook implementation and acceptance on hold, preserve r60.84 as rejected, and perform no Facebook retry or repair until Google is founder-accepted and the founder explicitly authorizes the next provider.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the exact installed r60.84 candidate did not complete X sign-in.
entries.rootCause: Unclassified at registration; provider availability, OAuth authorization/return, broker exchange, Firebase custom-token exchange and shared bootstrap remain distinct unproved stages.
entries.prevention: Keep X implementation and acceptance on hold, preserve r60.84 as rejected, and perform no X retry or repair until Google is founder-accepted and the founder explicitly authorizes the next provider.

entries.mistake: Founder testing on the exact installed r60.84 candidate did not complete Instagram sign-in.
entries.rootCause: Unclassified at registration; provider eligibility/availability, OAuth authorization/return, broker exchange, Firebase custom-token exchange and shared bootstrap remain distinct unproved stages.
entries.prevention: Keep Instagram implementation and acceptance on hold, preserve r60.84 as rejected, and perform no Instagram retry or repair until Google is founder-accepted and the founder explicitly authorizes the next provider.

entries.mistake: A bounded raw range read of the dense APK regression state exceeded the available model context and was truncated before the intended state fields could be established.
entries.rootCause: The read projected a dense raw JSON range instead of selecting only the required scalar fields and tiny independently bounded subobjects.
entries.prevention: Treat the truncated output as no evidence. Inspect APK state only with parsed scalar projections plus exact locators and tiny 10-to-20-line slices; never retry the same dense range.

entries.mistake: A broad filename search for regression-memory owners traversed artifact evidence and returned truncated output instead of one authoritative registry path.
entries.rootCause: The search was not restricted to exact current owner directories or an exact incident identifier, so immutable artifact filenames overwhelmed the result.
entries.prevention: Use the known canonical registry path directly, or use an exact incident-ID file-list search limited to config and docs; never repeat the broad artifact-inclusive search.

entries.mistake: A command piped the parsed registry root object to Select-Object -Last 2, serialized the entire registry and truncated output instead of returning the final two entries.
entries.rootCause: The projection omitted the registry's entries property before applying Select-Object.
entries.prevention: Assign the parsed root to a task-specific variable and select from its .entries array explicitly before serialization; cap output and use scalar summaries whenever possible.

entries.mistake: The coordination-policy replay was invoked without its mandatory AgentRole, AgentTask, ExpectedRegistryEntryCount and ExpectedRegistrySha256 arguments, so the gate did not execute.
entries.rootCause: The invocation relied on a remembered no-argument form instead of the script's current mandatory parameter contract.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current claim role and task from the policy, bind the freshly computed registry count and SHA-256, and pass all four mandatory arguments on every coordination replay.

entries.mistake: The coordination gate was given the mandatory role, task and registry binding but omitted both explicit ClaimedOwners and the UseRecordedClaim switch, so it rejected before validating the recorded claim.
entries.rootCause: The retry reconstructed only the four mandatory parameters named by PowerShell's binder and did not include the gate's mutually exclusive claim-source contract.
entries.prevention: For the existing primary /root claim, invoke the gate with -UseRecordedClaim in addition to the exact mandatory role, task and current registry binding; do not synthesize a parallel owner list.

entries.mistake: A PowerShell command attempted to pipe directly from a foreach statement after its closing brace and failed to parse with an empty-pipe-element error.
entries.rootCause: The command omitted an explicit array assignment around foreach output before JSON serialization.
entries.prevention: Populate a task-specific results array with @(foreach (...) { ... }) and serialize that variable in a separate statement; never pipe directly from a bare foreach block.

entries.mistake: A signing-input source search included a guessed scripts/build-android-apk.ps1 path that does not exist, while a downstream Select-Object stage masked rg's native failure status.
entries.rootCause: The command mixed one unverified conventional wrapper path with the exact scripts directory and relied on pipeline completion instead of validating every search owner first.
entries.prevention: Resolve exact existing script owners with rg --files first, search only those literal paths, and never use a later PowerShell pipeline stage as evidence that an earlier native command succeeded.

entries.mistake: The production APK plugin-integrity gate rejected the exact preserved r60.84 artifact because it could not find io.flutter.plugins.firebase.core.FlutterFirebaseCorePlugin.
