entries.rootCause: The release APK was minified and the first gate invocation omitted the fresh r60.84 Proguard mapping owners. The independently mapping-aware inspection passed registrant, Firebase Core, package identity and integration-test exclusion, proving the raw class-name miss was an inspection-mode defect rather than a missing Firebase Core class.
entries.prevention: Every minified release APK integrity check must supply the fresh mapping, seeds and usage folder and require mapping-aware inspection. Treat an unmapped class-name miss as no plugin evidence and never qualify a release APK from the unmapped mode.

entries.mistake: The Google-only sideload environment preparation rejected the selected FIX11 ticket identifier as an unauthorized candidate before it could perform the secret-safe OAuth/signing readback.
entries.rootCause: The preparation wrapper's candidate authorization contract has not been reconciled from the consumed FIX8/r60.84 flow to the permanent FIX11 Google-only forensic ticket.
entries.prevention: Update and test the wrapper's exact allowed candidate contract for FIX11 while keeping build/install authorization machine-held; run its negative wrong-candidate fixture and Google-only preflight before any successor APK build.

entries.mistake: A Google identity test search included the conventional apps/mobile/android/app/src/test owner even though that directory does not exist in this checkout.
entries.rootCause: The search mixed verified Dart and gate owners with an unverified conventional Android unit-test root.
entries.prevention: Resolve Android test directories with rg --files or Test-Path before searching, use only exact existing owners, and add any new Android fixture under a deliberately created scoped owner rather than assuming one exists.

entries.mistake: A secret-safe read-only Identity Toolkit Admin API request for the Dev google.com provider configuration returned HTTP 403, so provider-enabled and configured-client truth was not established.
entries.rootCause: The active non-private gcloud context could obtain an access token but is not currently authorized to read the project's default supported IdP configuration, or the required Admin API permission is otherwise unavailable.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the same REST call or infer provider state. Require a Firebase/Google Cloud console readback or an account with firebaseauth.configs.get, emit only enabled/client-match booleans, and never print account, token, client or secret values.

entries.mistake: The REG3486 bare-foreach pipeline parser defect recurred while projecting locked package versions; the command did not execute.
entries.rootCause: The version projection again placed a pipeline immediately after a foreach closing brace instead of serializing an explicitly assigned results array.
entries.prevention: For every multi-item PowerShell projection, first assign $moolResults = @(foreach (...) { ... }), then serialize $moolResults in a separate statement. Treat any compact bare-foreach pipeline form as forbidden.

entries.mistake: A non-private accounts:createAuthUri probe using the exact Android Firebase API input returned HTTP 403, so it did not establish that google.com is enabled or that the live authorization URI selects the expected Web OAuth client.
entries.rootCause: Unclassified at registration. Android API-key application restrictions, API enablement, or provider/project configuration can all reject a desktop-origin probe; the 403 alone does not identify which condition applies.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat desktop public-auth probes with the Android key or infer provider state from this rejection. Require the sanctioned console/config readback and later the signed OPPO flow; emit only booleans and never auth URIs, sessions, keys or client identifiers.

entries.mistake: A compound patch for the FIX11 Google-only environment wrapper was atomically rejected because one remembered YouTube fact block did not match the live source exactly.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined candidate authorization, provider hold logic, required inputs, runtime facts and output copy into one context-sensitive edit instead of using the exact freshly read live blocks.
entries.prevention: Treat the rejected patch as zero change. Re-read only the precise small wrapper ranges and apply independent tiny hunks for candidate, GoogleOnly guard, provider setup, required inputs, facts and output; parse and run negative fixtures after each logical group.

entries.mistake: Removing the rejected legacy Google bridge also removed protected MainActivity provider-seam markers, so the approved UI lock rejected the implementation before tests.
entries.rootCause: The implementation treated seam markers as disposable comments even though the lock contract uses them to isolate authorized provider changes from the immutable accepted owner.
entries.prevention: Read the lock's exact marker contract, restore every required marker once in its accepted order, and confine the Credential Manager migration to the authorized seam regions without changing protected content outside them.

entries.mistake: After REG3495 moved the registry, the primary replayed regression memory and coordination but restored the required MainActivity seam markers before replaying the MVP scope gate and approved UI lock.
entries.rootCause: The marker repair was treated as a prerequisite to the UI gate, but the independent MVP scope replay was incorrectly omitted from the pre-action sequence.
entries.prevention: After every registry movement, replay regression memory, coordination and MVP scope before any repository edit. If the UI lock is expected to reject until a repair, run it only after the scoped repair but never omit the independent MVP authorization gate.

entries.mistake: After the protected seam markers were restored, the approved UI lock reached its nested Google identity readiness check and rejected because that gate still requires the removed direct Play Services Auth legacy bridge.
entries.rootCause: The implementation migrated runtime code first while the coupled readiness gate still encoded the rejected r60.84 startActivityForResult architecture as mandatory truth.
entries.prevention: Update the readiness gate and fixtures in the same FIX11 ticket to require the locked google_sign_in_android Credential Manager owner, forbid the custom legacy channel and direct Play Services dependency, and retain Firebase exchange, retry, cancellation and sanitization assertions before replaying the UI lock.

entries.mistake: The migrated Google identity gate simultaneously required a MainActivity seam comment containing startActivityForResult and forbade that same legacy token anywhere in the activity, causing a self-conflicting rejection.
entries.rootCause: The negative assertion scanned comments as well as executable source, while the new explanatory comment named the exact forbidden legacy API.
entries.prevention: Reword the protected seam comment and its required gate token to avoid the legacy API spelling, retain the executable-source negative assertion, and add a gate self-test covering required/forbidden token disjointness.

entries.mistake: The first focused Flutter run failed to compile because dart:io was removed from review_journey_services.dart even though existing HttpClient, SocketException, HttpException, ContentType and HttpStatus owners still require it.
entries.rootCause: The import was classified from the removed Platform.isAndroid use alone without checking every remaining symbol in the large shared service file.
entries.prevention: Restore dart:io, run analyzer/import diagnostics on the entire owner after localized auth edits, and never remove a shared import based on one deleted call site.

entries.mistake: The refactored social-auth branch checked Google null cancellation inside one branch but later accessed userId.isEmpty and passed userId to the authenticated result while the static type remained String?.
entries.rootCause: Flow analysis did not promote the final variable across the provider-dependent assignment branches to a non-null String.
entries.prevention: After the explicit cancellation return, bind a final non-null authenticatedUserId with a guarded null failure, and use only that value for empty-session validation and success construction.

entries.mistake: The five-owner focused Flutter invocation produced 476 lines and the tool truncated the aggregate output, even though the final summary identified the two compile-failed owners and other suites continued.
entries.rootCause: Multiple verbose widget/session owners and debug receipts were combined into one process without a retained compact reporter or per-owner evidence files.
entries.prevention: Treat truncated output as no complete run evidence. After compile repair, execute the failed owners separately with the compact reporter, then run the already-executed supporting owners in bounded serial groups and retain exit summaries.

entries.mistake: The regression-memory replay rejected REG3499 because its gates array contained a Flutter command with arguments instead of a repository-relative owner path; REG3500 repeated the same invalid shape.
entries.rootCause: The incident registration used a human-executable command in a machine field whose schema validates every value as an existing repository evidence owner.
entries.prevention: Regression gates entries must be exact existing repository-relative script or test paths only. Put invocation details in prevention prose and validate the registry before updating the coordination binding.

entries.mistake: The FIX8 runtime-composition test still required globalSocialLoginAuditEnabled: _globalSocialLoginAuditMode after FIX11 intentionally excluded YouTube Dev App Check from the Google-only forensic lane.
entries.rootCause: The production source and new FIX11 gate were updated, but the historical source-contract test retained the pre-FIX11 global social audit expression.
entries.prevention: Update the historical test to require the exact Google-only exclusion expression and add negative assertions that unrelated YouTube/private-provider runtime facts cannot re-enter the FIX11 profile.

entries.mistake: Even the isolated runtime-composition test owner produced 1,005 lines and truncated because a failed contains matcher rendered the entire main.dart source; two failing tests were reported but only one failure was completely visible.
entries.rootCause: The source-contract test uses whole-file contains matchers whose failure diagnostics echo the full production source, overwhelming compact reporter output.
entries.prevention: Inspect and update stale expectations from source without rerunning first, then execute name-filtered static contract tests independently before the bounded widget/session remainder; never use truncated output as complete failure evidence.

entries.mistake: The first scoped Flutter analyze over the five modified Dart owners exited with one issue, so the implementation is not analyzer-qualified.
entries.rootCause: The removed custom method-channel compatibility tests no longer use flutter/services.dart, but their shared test owner retained that import and the scoped analyzer rejected it as unused.
entries.prevention: Remove the obsolete import, then rerun the identical five-owner analyzer set. When deleting compatibility fixtures, verify their test-only imports in the same focused analyzer cycle.

entries.mistake: PowerShell captured the analyzer's native stderr as RemoteException objects and ConvertTo-Json truncated their nested representation at depth two instead of emitting the analyzer issue text.
entries.rootCause: The failure projection filtered and serialized native error objects without first converting each captured item to a plain string.
entries.prevention: Convert all captured analyzer output to [string] immediately, filter bounded text lines only, and serialize scalar strings; never pass NativeCommandError or RemoteException objects to JSON evidence.

entries.mistake: The post-registration analyzer readback converted output to plain strings but its regex retained only the final issue count and dropped the actual machine-format issue line from a five-line result.
entries.rootCause: The filter assumed verbose analyzer separators such as ' - warning - ', while the active Flutter analyzer emitted a different compact bullet or field format.
entries.prevention: Because the entire sanitized readback is only five plain-text lines, emit all five lines on the next read instead of guessing another diagnostic regex; then fix the exact issue once.

entries.mistake: The final non-emitting git status digest process exited zero and produced a digest but also captured 73,346 stderr bytes, so that digest is not a qualified stderr-clean checkpoint.
entries.rootCause: Sanitized classification confirmed 266 Git warnings, all in the could-not-open-directory filename-too-long category, while enumerating the preserved dirty worktree after forced Android resource/Kotlin gates. No path or evidence name was emitted.
entries.prevention: Retain the nonzero-stderr condition explicitly: the digest is a complete digest only over paths Git could enumerate and is therefore provisional. Do not delete generated or user evidence to force a clean result.

entries.mistake: The apply_patch call that registered REG3508 reported that its output exceeded the available model context and was truncated, leaving mutation success ambiguous.
entries.rootCause: The patch tool emitted an unexpectedly large result for a small tail append; success could not be inferred from the truncated tool response.
entries.prevention: Before any retry, parse the registry with a bounded scalar projection and inspect only entry count, tail ID and hash. Append only the missing incident in a minimal patch, then replay bound memory and coordination gates.

entries.mistake: A bounded parameter-inspection command guessed two final gate script names that do not exist: check-uaw-c34p-mvp-state-manifest.ps1 and check-approved-ui-lock.ps1.
entries.rootCause: The replay preparation relied on remembered descriptive gate names instead of first resolving the canonical repository filenames.
entries.prevention: Resolve canonical gate paths with a filename-only rg --files query before invoking or inspecting them, then replay only exact existing paths.

entries.mistake: Filtering active claims by serializing each full claim caused the primary claim's very large owner list to be emitted and the command output to truncate.
entries.rootCause: The predicate converted whole claim objects to JSON instead of comparing the bounded task and role scalar fields directly.
entries.prevention: For coordination lookup, project only task and role scalars or invoke the known primary recorded claim directly; never serialize owner arrays merely to locate a task.

entries.mistake: The sanitized dirty-digest command exceeded the initial wait and returned no output because the orchestration wrapper forwarded only the command output, not a possible continuing session identifier.
entries.rootCause: A potentially long Git enumeration was wrapped with a fixed wait while discarding exec_command metadata needed to poll a continuing session.
entries.prevention: Before retry, reconcile whether a Git process remains. On retry, serialize the full exec_command metadata so a returned session can be polled, and avoid emitting status paths.

entries.mistake: The mandatory public-auth sideload build-control self-test rejected the current FIX11 wrapper because its Google-only or full-social founder Dev readiness fail-closed assertion did not match the current implementation.
entries.rootCause: The preparation script had moved to FIX11 Google-only inputs, but the APK machine state's exact runtime allowlist and the mandatory self-test still encoded r60.84 full-social facts. The build wrapper also lacked a direct FIX11 readiness invocation and rejected an intentionally empty held-YouTube provider URL.
entries.prevention: Bind the wrapper, machine state, APK exact-allowlist gate and self-test to the same FIX11 candidate. Require the forensic gate at action time, require Google-only true, require held-provider flags false, allow only the explicitly held empty YouTube URL, and retain historical full-social checks only for historical profiles.

entries.mistake: After the FIX11 wrapper and runtime-state repair, the mandatory build-control self-test reached and rejected a separate assertion that social authentication still collapses a required real-device stage before APK/AAB.
entries.rootCause: The historical control required an on-MissingPluginException token from the removed custom Android bridge and did not require the replacement official-plugin Google stage sequence, sanitized telemetry prefix, GSI-N01 recovery, or their focused fixtures.
entries.prevention: Bind the artifact-control test to the complete official-plugin Google native and Firebase stage codes, the sanitized telemetry prefix, GSI-N01 presentation, and exact gateway/runtime fixtures. Do not require a legacy bridge exception token after bridge removal.

entries.mistake: The Google Android identity readiness test reported that its negative fixture passed instead of being rejected.
entries.rootCause: The negative fixture still tried to rewrite the removed native requestIdToken(serverClientId) bridge call. The replacement made no change, so the migrated official-plugin readiness gate correctly saw an intact fixture and passed.
entries.prevention: Assert that every negative mutation changes its fixture, then corrupt a currently required official Credential Manager invariant. FIX11 now replaces GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate() in the Dart gateway and requires the gate to reject the missing production token.

entries.mistake: The combined two-owner Flutter test command passed all 44 tests, but compact progress and sanitized debug receipts exceeded the tool output budget and truncated the middle of the stream.
entries.rootCause: The compact reporter rewrote progress for every test while Google stage debug receipts were also emitted; combining both owners recreated the already registered output-volume class.
entries.prevention: Do not use a raw combined compact stream as the durable receipt. Preserve the exit code and emit only a bounded final summary, or run owners separately with bounded tail projection; never infer success from a truncated middle without the final all-tests-passed line.

entries.mistake: The scoped version-name/version-code uniqueness scan exceeded its initial wait, while the orchestration wrapper emitted only command output and again discarded a possible continuing session identifier.
entries.rootCause: The previously registered long-running command session-metadata mistake recurred in an rg scan expected to be short.
entries.prevention: Before retry, reconcile running rg processes. For every potentially long inventory command, serialize the complete exec result so a session ID can be polled; never project output alone. Do not allocate the version from an ambiguous scan.

entries.mistake: The bounded Wait-Process reconciliation also exceeded its wait and returned no projected output because the wrapper again omitted continuing-session metadata.
entries.rootCause: A second potentially blocking command was used while repairing a lost-session incident, repeating the same metadata projection flaw instead of using an immediate scalar process-count check.
entries.prevention: Do not use Wait-Process through an output-only wrapper. Reconcile with immediate process-count scalars; when launching any long command, always serialize the complete exec result and poll the explicit session ID.

entries.mistake: A combined ticket, evidence-matrix and robustness-assessment patch failed because the assessment paragraph context did not exactly match the current file.
entries.rootCause: The patch reused a wrapped paragraph from memory instead of reading the current exact assessment tail before composing a multi-file update.
entries.prevention: Verify atomicity with bounded scalar markers, read the exact current target paragraph, and apply smaller per-file patches with exact context. Recompute and rebind the ticket hash only after all intended evidence writes succeed.

entries.mistake: The founder launched the secure local preparation in Windows PowerShell 5 instead of PowerShell 7, and the version guard rejected execution before any password prompt.
entries.rootCause: The handoff said to open PowerShell 7 but did not provide a copy-paste launcher that resolves and starts pwsh.exe explicitly from the existing Windows PowerShell window.
entries.prevention: Provide one literal pwsh.exe launch command first, verify the new window reports PowerShell 7, and only then provide a plain local script command. Keep the preparation guard and require rejection before secrets or build actions on older PowerShell.

entries.mistake: The subsequent pasted guard and preflight command contained backslashes before environment-variable underscores and before the build script extension, so neither represented the authorized literal command.
entries.rootCause: A long multiline handoff was copied through a formatting path that introduced escape characters and line-continuation ambiguity.
entries.prevention: Replace the long chat command with a locally stored, parser-checked preflight launcher and give the founder one short literal invocation. The launcher must stop after preparation failure and must remain PreflightOnly until a separate verified build step.

entries.mistake: The registry patch response for REG3520 and REG3521 was truncated, leaving the mutation result ambiguous.
entries.rootCause: The patch tool response exceeded the available model context even though the intended registry mutation was bounded.
entries.prevention: After any truncated mutation response, perform a scalar count, tail-ID, hash and exact-ID occurrence reconciliation before another write. Use small follow-up patches only after mutation truth is known.

entries.mistake: The first scalar reconciliation addressed a stale registry filename and failed before reading registry state.
entries.rootCause: The check relied on an unverified summary-derived filename instead of resolving the canonical repository filename first.
entries.prevention: Resolve registry filenames with a filename-only repository lookup before scalar parsing whenever the exact path has not been independently verified in the current turn.

entries.mistake: The coordination gate was invoked without its mandatory AgentRole, AgentTask, ExpectedRegistryEntryCount and ExpectedRegistrySha256 parameters.
entries.rootCause: The replay treated the coordination gate like a parameterless mandatory gate instead of reading its current parameter contract first.
entries.prevention: Read the coordination gate parameter block before every replay and pass the current canonical registry generation and hash explicitly.

entries.mistake: The parameter-complete coordination replay used the forensic ticket ID as AgentTask, but the policy has no active owner claim under that task string.
entries.rootCause: The replay conflated the work ticket identifier with the coordination policy's canonical agent task name.
entries.prevention: Read activeClaims before replay and use the canonical /root task with UseRecordedClaim for primary-agent work unless the policy is deliberately and separately updated.

entries.mistake: The no-build safety projection returned null for signed-APK and action-count facts because it used a stale nested property path.
entries.rootCause: The scalar check relied on a remembered state shape instead of reading the current FIX11 state property names first.
entries.prevention: Inspect only the current state object's property names, then project the exact canonical fields; treat null safety facts as unresolved, never as zero or false.

entries.mistake: The assumed Program Files PowerShell 7 executable path does not exist on this laptop even though pwsh is callable in the build environment.
entries.rootCause: The handoff path was inferred from a common installation layout rather than resolved from the laptop's actual command discovery state.
entries.prevention: Resolve Get-Command pwsh to an existing local executable and use that exact path in the one-command handoff; never hardcode the default installation path without verification.

entries.mistake: The launcher design probe projected nonexistent aggregateManifestPath and aggregateSha256 fields and returned null source facts.
entries.rootCause: The probe used remembered labels instead of the current source object's manifestPath and manifestSha256 schema.
entries.prevention: Read source property names before value projection and make launchers consume only the canonical manifestPath and manifestSha256 fields after exact state validation.

entries.mistake: The combined launcher parser-check command failed to parse because a colon immediately followed the unbraced file variable in an error-format string.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc check used $f: instead of ${f}: inside an interpolated PowerShell string.
entries.prevention: Brace variables that precede colons in PowerShell interpolation and parser-check the check harness itself before relying on its test result.

entries.mistake: The first cycle-03 independent replay marked two rows private because its heuristic treated any source filename containing password or secret as a machine credential input.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc classifier conflated legitimate source/test owners about secret handling with forbidden machine-local credential artifacts such as keystores and local signing property files.
entries.prevention: Classify forbidden private inputs by exact machine-file types and signing-property paths, while separately scanning manifest row format, containment and content hashes. Do not infer credential exposure from a legitimate test filename alone.

entries.mistake: The final scalar verification projected a nonexistent or incorrect MVP ticket collection and reported the ticket hash binding as false.
entries.rootCause: The check inferred the collection name instead of locating the current FIX11 ticket entry in the large MVP state schema.
entries.prevention: Locate the exact ticket ID line and enclosing schema before scalar projection, then require both the dedicated MVP gate and the direct ticket-hash comparison to pass.

entries.mistake: While the founder terminal visibly showed assembleRelease running, a sanitized command-line filter returned zero matching build processes and zero candidate APKs.
entries.rootCause: The filter assumed the relevant parent or Gradle process command line would retain the launcher, wrapper or task string; that assumption was not valid for the observed Windows process tree.
entries.prevention: Treat a zero result from a narrow process-command-line filter as inconclusive during a founder-owned build. Do not retry or infer termination; wait for the terminal result, then reconcile the unique artifact, state and action count independently.

entries.mistake: The one authorized r60.85 APK build completed and produced one artifact, but apk-regression-gate-state.json retained prebuild_passed, approved_for_one_build and signedApkCreated=false while its generic build result still described consumed r60.84.
entries.rootCause: The successful local build wrapper verifies and reports the artifact but does not atomically journal the FIX11 successor build result into the machine state.
entries.prevention: Immediately forbid rebuild, independently qualify the unique APK, then reconcile FIX11 and generic build-result fields to one consumed r60.85 build before any install authorization. Future successor wrappers require an atomic post-build state transition test, but the sealed built source must not be changed before this APK is qualified.

entries.mistake: A post-build dex probe expected literal unminified package names for the Google Sign-In plugin, Google Identity and Firebase Core; three checks returned false even though the mapping-aware production plugin gate passed registrant and Firebase Core integrity.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc probe ignored R8 shrinking, optimization and obfuscation and treated literal package text as the authoritative packaged-code contract.
entries.prevention: For minified release APKs, use the preserved mapping-aware plugin-integrity gate, generated registrant evidence, dependency lock provenance and bounded Credential Manager/Firebase Auth packaged evidence. Do not infer missing plugins solely from absent literal unminified dex package strings.

entries.mistake: The first combined post-build state and ticket reconciliation patch failed because it expected successorBuildBlocked=false while the current device qualification already records true.
entries.rootCause: The patch composed most fields from current reads but reused one stale remembered device-state value.
entries.prevention: Verify atomicity with scalar state and ticket markers, read the exact current device qualification block, and apply smaller state and ticket patches using only exact current context.

entries.mistake: After state reconciliation, the aggregate post-build qualification predicate returned false even though its projected build count, install count, authority and artifact hash facts appeared correct.
entries.rootCause: The compound predicate hid which exact field or type comparison failed.
entries.prevention: Keep installation blocked, register the failed aggregate, then project every predicate as a named boolean and correct only the evidenced mismatch before recomputing qualification.

entries.mistake: The named predicate verifier looked for successorApkSha256 and successorApkInstalled under testAndEvidencePlan, which is an array, while the newly journaled artifact facts are in the forensicFindings object.
entries.rootCause: The verifier inferred the enclosing ticket object from nearby line numbers instead of reading the exact schema path.
entries.prevention: Read the ticket property type and exact enclosing object before qualification; compare post-build artifact facts through forensicFindings and keep array-valued test plans out of scalar projections.

entries.mistake: The first install orchestration wrapper failed JavaScript parsing with Unexpected identifier before the PowerShell command or adb process started.
entries.rootCause: A PowerShell backtick-newline escape was embedded inside a JavaScript template literal and terminated or corrupted the wrapper source.
entries.prevention: Treat the journaled install as reserved but not externally attempted, register zero device action, create and parser-check a bounded local PowerShell install launcher with exact state/hash/version guards, and invoke that launcher once without inline cross-language quoting.

entries.mistake: The first automated r60.85 cold start succeeded with a live process and zero crash/ANR evidence, but the sanitized UI hierarchy did not contain the Google entry-point label.
entries.rootCause: The in-place install preserved r60.84 app data and navigation state, so cold start is not guaranteed to land on Screen 03; the first check did not classify the current preserved route.
entries.prevention: Do not clear data or assume the sign-in screen. Register the result, classify the current route using only sanitized known-app markers and source navigation contracts, then give the founder minimal on-screen navigation steps without opening an account chooser programmatically.

entries.mistake: After the qualified r60.85 APK was installed once in place and cold-started, the founder tapped Google Sign-In and reported that it failed with the same old error.
entries.rootCause: Unresolved pending sanitized r60.85 auth-stage evidence; local source, mock, configuration, signature and APK gates did not prove the live Credential Manager/provider/Firebase/session path.
entries.prevention: Reject r60.85 for Google acceptance, forbid another tap or rebuild from assumptions, capture only allowlisted stage/error codes from the current process and sanitized on-screen recovery state, then repair or rebuild only from direct causal evidence.

entries.mistake: r60.85 durably emitted auth-google-firebase-credential-failed after identity return, but discarded the normalized FirebaseAuthException code and left neither logs nor current UI able to distinguish collision, disabled account, provider configuration, invalid credential, API restriction, network or unclassified failure.
entries.rootCause: The FirebaseAuthException catch maps error.code to a sanitized PublicAuthFailure but emits only one generic credential-failed stage before throwing the public message.
entries.prevention: Emit a strict allowlisted normalized Firebase failure-class receipt alongside the credential-failed stage, persist the last safe receipt for founder readback, and add negative tests proving no raw message, email, UID, token or credential payload can be emitted. Do not build another candidate until the underlying Firebase exchange cause is also evidenced or the successor safely covers the exact configuration defect.

entries.mistake: The first post-failure parser read MOOLSOCIAL_GOOGLE_AUTH stages but omitted the separate MOOLSOCIAL_SOCIAL_AUTH receipt stream and therefore overstated that no normalized Firebase failure class was durable.
entries.rootCause: The forensic parser was scoped to the newly added lower-level stage prefix and did not include the established JourneySession receipt prefix.
entries.prevention: Every Google live-failure parser must join both receipt streams by attempt: lower-level native/Firebase stages plus the JourneySession terminal normalized code. r60.85 attempt 1 is now classified auth-started to auth-firebase-unclassified without another tap.

entries.mistake: The primary raw-read config/codex-subagent-coordination-policy.json and the command result was truncated because the policy contains thousands of historical owner entries, leaving the mandatory reconstruction readback semantically incomplete.
entries.rootCause: The policy owner was read as unbounded text instead of a parsed projection limited to registry binding, the exact /root claim, incident protocol, generation rules and release serialization.
entries.prevention: Never raw-read the coordination policy again. Parse it and emit only the policy identity, registry binding, exact canonical task claim, required protocols and relevant release controls; verify the JSON parse and projected owner membership before running the coordination gate.

entries.mistake: A dependency-source search passed wildcard directory names directly to rg on Windows; rg rejected both wildcard paths and exited 1, making the result partial.
entries.rootCause: The command treated Windows path arguments as shell-expanded globs even though the selected PowerShell invocation passed them literally to rg.
entries.prevention: Do not retry this search. Resolve only literal dependency paths inside the authorized production checkout, verify each path first, and pass literal paths to rg.

entries.mistake: The primary read FlutterFire plugin source from the user-global Pub cache outside C:/GUARANTEED OUTCOME even though the workspace AGENTS policy confines reads to that workspace unless the founder expands scope.
entries.rootCause: A locally cached direct dependency was treated as implicitly in scope instead of applying the explicit workspace path boundary.
entries.prevention: Perform all remaining dependency and SDK forensics only against copies, generated metadata and compiled artifacts already located inside C:/GUARANTEED OUTCOME/MOOLSOCIAL-PRODUCTION. Do not read the global Pub or Gradle caches again in this task.

entries.mistake: The first REG3545 entry referenced ../AGENTS.md, and the regression-memory gate rejected it because evidence paths must resolve inside the repository.
entries.rootCause: The incident concerned the workspace-level policy, but its evidence list used an out-of-repository relative path instead of a valid repository-owned policy/evidence path.
entries.prevention: Before appending a regression entry, resolve every evidence path from the repository root and require Test-Path -LiteralPath for each path. REG3545 now references repository AGENTS.md plus the durable registry.

entries.mistake: A repository-wide rg search for the r60.85 auth markers continued through the huge preserved dirty tree and retained evidence for more than seventy seconds without completing; the primary stopped the exact retained session.
entries.rootCause: The exclusions did not cover the repository's complete large retained-artifact topology, so a broad fallback search was not predictably bounded.
entries.prevention: Do not retry a repository-wide marker search. Inspect only the exact FIX11 ticket, r60.85 artifact directory, APK state, known source owners and a bounded device readback when separately gated.

entries.mistake: The mandatory 2,419-line product design memory was raw-read in one command and its output truncated, leaving the readback incomplete.
entries.rootCause: The primary did not first determine the file length and paginate the mandatory owner within the available output limit.
entries.prevention: Read the design memory only in independent non-overlapping pages of at most 250 lines through verified EOF, then record the exact line count and SHA before resuming Google forensics.

entries.mistake: The primary raw-read the FSC02E API-key-restriction metadata, which included a private account email field, instead of projecting only the non-private restriction facts required for Google Sign-In forensics.
entries.rootCause: An existing evidence JSON was assumed safe because it declared that no key string was present; that assertion did not mean every other field was non-private.
entries.prevention: Never raw-read provider, Firebase, Google Cloud, device or authentication evidence JSON. Parse it in memory and emit only a literal safe-field allowlist that excludes account, email, user, token, identifier, credential, key string and raw message fields.

entries.mistake: A local comparison emitted apiKeyAllowedSignerMatchesR6085=false even though the APK had no V1 META-INF certificate entry and its modern V2/V3 signer certificate was therefore never read.
entries.rootCause: The compound predicate collapsed signer-unreadable and signer-mismatch into the same false boolean.
entries.prevention: A signer comparison is valid only after the APK's modern signing certificate is independently readable. Emit signerReadable separately and never report matches=false when signerReadable=false; use the repository's modern APK-signature verifier and suppress all certificate values.

entries.mistake: The installed apkanalyzer printed resources-value usage but returned exit 1 because it does not recognize --help as a help option.
entries.rootCause: The command assumed GNU-style --help support instead of using the tool's usage contract already exposed by its missing-required-argument response.
entries.prevention: Do not retry help. Invoke resources value with the now-confirmed required --config, --type and --name options plus the exact APK; retain exit metadata and emit only safe comparison booleans.

entries.mistake: The consolidated safe Firebase configuration/restriction comparison failed at parse time because the restrictionSignerMatchesTicketTarget expression was missing one closing parenthesis.
entries.rootCause: Two nested inline normalization expressions were compressed into one object-literal property without first assigning scalar variables.
entries.prevention: Assign both normalized certificate strings to separate scalar variables, validate their length, then construct the safe comparison object. Do not use nested replace/method expressions in the object literal.

entries.mistake: A direct APK-to-Android-OAuth comparison required colon-delimited certificate hashes and therefore reported zero Android OAuth clients even though the authoritative prebuild gate had found three valid registrations.
entries.rootCause: The ad hoc matcher did not reuse the repository gate's accepted SHA-1 representation rule before normalization.
entries.prevention: Reuse check-google-android-oauth-signing-readiness.ps1 semantics: accept the bounded hex/colon representation, remove non-hex separators, require exactly 40 hex characters, then compare. Never infer a missing client from a presentation-format mismatch.

entries.mistake: The resumed FIX11 reconstruction attempted to pipe directly from a statement-form PowerShell foreach while collecting AGENTS owner metrics, so PowerShell rejected the command before either metric was produced.
entries.rootCause: A compact diagnostic repeated the permanent statement-loop-to-pipeline parser class instead of materializing an explicit results array or reading each mandatory owner independently.
entries.prevention: Mandatory owners remain independent command results. Any future bounded aggregation first assigns foreach output to a ticket-specific array, and the PowerShell text is parser-checked before execution.

entries.mistake: The resumed FIX11 reconstruction raw-read the coordination-policy JSON and the tool output truncated, repeating REG3543 and leaving that result semantically incomplete.
entries.rootCause: The first read ignored the owner's large historical claim array instead of measuring and paging the file or using the policy-approved bounded projection.
entries.prevention: Never raw-read this policy owner. For complete reconstruction, use independent non-overlapping pages through EOF; for later checks, parse and emit only identity, registry binding, exact recorded task, protocols and release controls.

entries.mistake: The first resumed non-emitting dirty-digest wrapper supplied multiple Git application Source values to ProcessStartInfo.FileName, so process start failed and the subsequent null-error cascade produced no valid digest.
entries.rootCause: Get-Command returned more than one Git application candidate and the wrapper treated the collection as one executable path without exact candidate-count validation.
entries.prevention: Resolve Git candidates into an explicit array, select the exact executable already proven by scalar Git commands, require one existing leaf, then run the in-memory status process. Abort before object construction if process start, stream capture, byte hashing, stderr or exit metadata is incomplete.

entries.mistake: The resumed FIX11 reconstruction requested design-memory lines 501 through 750 in one output and the tool result exceeded the remaining model-context boundary, so that page was truncated and cannot count as a complete policy read.
entries.rootCause: The 250-line page respected the older line-count ceiling but not the smaller live output budget remaining after the forensic reconstruction and compaction.
entries.prevention: Discard the truncated page. Replay mandatory registry and coordination gates, then continue from line 501 in independent non-overlapping pages of at most 100 lines through verified EOF, lowering the page size again if any page is incomplete.

entries.mistake: While preparing the mandatory truncation incident, the resumed audit attempted to read a nonexistent assumed path named config/development-regression-registry.json.
entries.rootCause: The command reconstructed the registry name from memory instead of using the repository's exact owner path config/codex-development-regression-registry.json.
entries.prevention: Use exact owner paths already established by AGENTS and gate evidence. If a path is absent from compacted context, resolve it with bounded rg --files output before reading and never infer a near-match filename.

entries.mistake: The diagnostic-successor preflight attempted to assign a new MemoryStream inside the CopyToAsync method argument, and PowerShell rejected the command with a missing-parenthesis parser error before Git status started.
entries.rootCause: The compact wrapper used an assignment expression in a .NET method-call argument where PowerShell parsing was ambiguous.
entries.prevention: Assign the MemoryStream to a ticket-specific variable on its own statement before invoking CopyToAsync. Parser-check the wrapper and accept a digest only when process start, both streams, exit code, record count and SHA-256 all complete without stderr.

entries.mistake: A bounded diagnostic-successor source lookup included the nonexistent guessed owner scripts/check-apk-regression-pre-build.ps1, causing rg to return a path error while the other exact owners were inspected.
entries.rootCause: The audit inferred a semantic prebuild gate filename instead of resolving the repository's actual scripts from a bounded file inventory or the build wrapper's exact imports.
entries.prevention: Do not guess gate filenames. Read the exact gate paths invoked by build-buy-device-review.ps1 or resolve only matching script names with rg --files scripts before inspecting or invoking them.

entries.mistake: The first r60.86 diagnostic source-manifest helper used -cjoin for a case-sensitive independent-replay comparison, and PowerShell rejected the script before any output manifest was created.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell supports -join but has no -cjoin variant; case sensitivity belongs on the outer string comparison operator.
entries.prevention: Use ordinary -join to materialize each manifest string and compare those strings with -cne. Parser-check the helper before retry and refuse any overwrite if an output appeared unexpectedly.

entries.mistake: A non-secret r60.86 machine-gate replay converted every requiredRuntimeDefines state property into an input, and the gate rejected that set because its names differed from the exact build-wrapper allowlist.
entries.rootCause: The diagnostic replay treated the broader registered state projection as the exact emitted build input set instead of using build-buy-device-review.ps1's authoritative runtime-name construction.
entries.prevention: Do not manually reconstruct build runtime inputs from the whole state object. Use the qualified build wrapper in the secure same-session preflight, where the exact allowlisted names and held-provider values are constructed and validated without emitting credential values.

entries.mistake: The first exhaustive Google/Firebase diagnostic test found that the strict telemetry sanitizer converted Firebase's legitimate one-word codes canceled and cancelled to unavailable.
entries.rootCause: The safe-code grammar required at least one hyphen even though the existing Firebase cancellation mapping explicitly supports two standardized one-word codes.
entries.prevention: Allow only the exact one-word codes canceled and cancelled in addition to the bounded lowercase hyphenated Firebase-code grammar. Keep arbitrary one-word values, messages, emails, identifiers and credential payloads unavailable.

entries.mistake: The no-APK Google preflight invoked scripts/test-public-auth-sideload-build-controls.ps1 from apps/mobile, so the repository-relative script path was not found while the separate Flutter pre-APK audit passed.
entries.rootCause: Two tools with different required working directories were placed in one command without anchoring the repository script to an absolute or parent-root path.
entries.prevention: Run repository PowerShell gates from the repository root and Flutter tests from apps/mobile in separate calls. Retry only the gate that did not execute.

entries.mistake: The no-APK sideload control rejected FIX11 because the ticket still recorded a maximum of two successor builds while the current founder instruction permits only one next uniquely versioned APK after all local checks pass.
entries.rootCause: The ticket retained the earlier diagnostic-plus-final upper bound and was not narrowed when the founder superseded sequencing with one next APK and a mandatory OPPO acceptance gate.
entries.prevention: Bind current authority to exactly one next release APK and one in-place OPPO install. If that APK proves a source defect requiring another APK, stop and obtain a new explicit successor authorization rather than relying on the older two-build ceiling.

entries.mistake: The Google-only MVP delivery gate rejected FIX11 after the ticket's successor build authority was narrowed from two builds to one because the selected-ticket assessment still contained the prior ticket hash.
entries.rootCause: The mandatory one-field ticket authority update and its derived selected-ticket manifest hash binding were not refreshed atomically.
entries.prevention: When a mandatory ticket authority field changes, recompute and update only the exact selected-ticket manifest hash binding before replaying the MVP delivery and scope gates; do not change scope or acceptance content.

entries.mistake: The coordination replay used guessed parameter names TaskPath and Role, so PowerShell rejected the command before the gate executed.
entries.rootCause: The command reused semantic labels instead of reading the gate's declared AgentTask and AgentRole parameter names.
entries.prevention: Read the exact param block before invoking the coordination gate and use AgentTask, AgentRole, UseRecordedClaim, ExpectedRegistryEntryCount and ExpectedRegistrySha256 exactly.

entries.mistake: The independent r60.86 source-seal replay found one of 650 bounded source owners no longer matched the stored diagnostic manifest.
entries.rootCause: The stored source seal was generated before the final bounded source-owner state was stable or a later owner edit was not followed by a new versioned seal.
entries.prevention: Identify the one mismatched owner without emitting file contents, verify whether it is an intended Google-only change, then create a new non-overwriting versioned source seal and independently replay all owners before any secure preflight or build.

entries.mistake: The r60.87 baseline-lock reconstruction raw-read the complete coordination-policy JSON and the tool output truncated, repeating REG3543 and REG3555.
entries.rootCause: The primary used an unbounded raw policy read instead of the required parsed projection or independent bounded pages.
entries.prevention: Never raw-read the coordination-policy JSON. Parse and emit only policy identity, registry binding, the exact /root claim membership required for the operation, incident and generation protocols, and release controls; use bounded independent pages only when a complete textual read is mandatory.

entries.mistake: The r60.87 source-manifest inventory exceeded the tool yield window, but the JavaScript wrapper projected only stdout and discarded the returned live session identifier.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper did not preserve the complete exec result before attempting to report the command output.
entries.prevention: Use bounded manifest checks that complete inside one call. For any command that may yield, retain and report the complete exec result including session_id and exit_code before further action; never project stdout alone.

entries.mistake: The r60.87 manifest inventory invoked a repository-wide untracked and ignored file enumeration, which emitted a large long-path warning stream from preserved historical evidence and truncated the result.
entries.rootCause: The classification command searched the entire huge dirty tree instead of restricting Git queries to the 652 literal source-manifest paths.
entries.prevention: Discard the truncated result. Classify only literal source-manifest owners using a pathspec file or bounded batches, capture stderr separately, and accept the result only with exit zero and empty stderr.

entries.mistake: The first r60.87 baseline-lock replay failed because at least one manifest-owned administrative checker changed beyond the single recorded post-acceptance exclusion.
entries.rootCause: The baseline-lock support edits changed manifest-owned coordination/checker files while the immutable source replay excluded only the coordination-policy owner.
entries.prevention: Before replay, compare only the 652 literal manifest owners, classify each mismatch by exact path, and add an explicit administrative disposition only for non-runtime Git-baseline support owners. Runtime source mismatches remain blocking.

entries.mistake: The administrative-exclusion correction patched the r60.87 baseline record and its checker in one apply-patch operation.
entries.rootCause: The correction grouped two logically related owners instead of applying and reading back one owner at a time.
entries.prevention: Every subsequent repository mutation in this baseline operation changes exactly one owner per apply-patch call and reads that owner back before another mutation.

entries.mistake: The first curated r60.87 staging wrapper failed while writing the NUL-delimited literal path stream because the Git child closed its stdin pipe early.
entries.rootCause: The wrapper allowed a child-process exit to surface as a PowerShell stream-write exception before retaining Git stderr, exit code, and the resulting index state.
entries.prevention: Before any retry, prove the Git child is absent and inspect only the staged path count. Replace the streaming wrapper with bounded literal argument batches, retaining exit code and stderr for every batch and stopping at the first nonzero or nonempty-stderr result.

entries.mistake: The bounded literal-path staging replacement failed on its first batch with Git exit 128 and three retained error lines; zero batches completed.
entries.rootCause: The aborted NUL-stream staging wrapper left the exact temporary .git/index.lock after its Git child exited; the first bounded batch therefore failed before staging with 'File exists'. No Git process or staged path remained.
entries.prevention: After proving zero repository Git processes, zero staged paths, and the exact lock target inside this repository, remove only the stale .git/index.lock. Replay generation gates, then use bounded literal argument batches that always retain exit and stderr metadata.

entries.mistake: The combined stale-index-lock verification and Remove-Item command was rejected by the execution policy before PowerShell started.
entries.rootCause: The cleanup attempt combined verification and a blocked Remove-Item operation in one command instead of retaining independent verification and using one exact allowed file deletion primitive.
entries.prevention: Replay generation gates, verify the literal repository .git/index.lock target and zero Git processes in a read-only command, then perform one literal non-recursive deletion with an allowed exact-file API and immediately verify absence.

entries.mistake: The first post-staging unstaged-difference check manually retyped one FIX15 support path with an incorrect case-spelling segment, so its 670-path result was not authoritative.
entries.rootCause: The verification reconstructed a long manual support list instead of consuming the exact paths already present in the Git index and validated source manifest.
entries.prevention: Discard that check. Restage the updated registry and policy, then derive all remaining verification directly from git diff --cached and the sealed manifest; never retype the curated support list again, and require every derived path to exist.

entries.mistake: The curated r60.87 baseline commit added apps/mobile/android/app/google-services.json to Git and pushed it to origin; GitHub Secret Scanning then reported a possible valid Google API key in commit 9b585a71.
