entries.mistake: After final integration passed 194 affected tests plus one intentional capture skip, full analysis and approved locks, check-user-facing-copy.ps1 rejected facebook_native_sdk_adapter.dart for the prohibited word endpoint; the integration branch remains local and unpushed.
entries.rootCause: The combined final gate had not previously classified whether this authentication-source occurrence is inherited by both sealed tips, customer reachable, or a static false positive outside the contextual Chat correction.
entries.prevention: Preserve the verified integration branch unpushed; compare the exact owner blob across governance, sealed Codex, sealed Cursor, repair and production; inspect only the bounded flagged statement and its customer mapping; if reachable, create one exact owner-qualified child fix and tests, otherwise add only a semantic negative fixture without weakening the prohibited customer-copy rule; rerun the full copy gate before fresh integration.

entries.mistake: The first semantic interpolation-filter patch was rejected with zero copy-gate change because its final hunk guessed the escaped PowerShell regex source instead of matching the live line exactly.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined function, fixtures, loop state and regex replacement while crossing JavaScript, patch and PowerShell escaping layers.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, read the exact bounded blocked-word loop and patch the helper, fixtures, sanitized line and matcher as four small live-anchored operations; parse and run the focused copy gate once before any integration rebuild.

entries.mistake: The small matcher hunk still failed with zero change because the patch payload inserted a backslash before PowerShell's literal backtick-escaped quote, so it did not equal the freshly read source line.
entries.rootCause: The retry again hand-escaped a line crossing JavaScript and PowerShell instead of constructing the exact backtick character programmatically.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, construct the one old and new matcher lines with character code 96 inside the patch orchestration, verify only that exact line changes, then parse and run the copy gate without another hand-escaped retry.

entries.mistake: The focused copy-gate replay reached the new interpolation helper and failed when Get-Content supplied a blank source line because the mandatory string parameter did not allow an empty string.
entries.rootCause: The helper contract modeled every source line as non-empty even though blank lines are valid and must sanitize to the same blank value.
entries.prevention: Add AllowEmptyString to the exact helper parameter, extend its fixture with an empty-input equality assertion, then rerun the focused copy gate once before coordination pre-commit.

entries.mistake: After the Facebook interpolation false positive and empty-line helper contract were corrected, the copy gate advanced and rejected x_oauth2_pkce_network_adapter.dart for the next inherited quoted word payload.
entries.rootCause: The gate stops at the first Write-Error under ErrorActionPreference Stop, so the prior run could not expose this later occurrence or classify whether it is protocol-only or customer-visible.
entries.prevention: Compare the exact X adapter blob across sealed baselines, inspect only the bounded flagged statement and its mapped customer error, then either correct reachable customer copy or add one semantic protocol-data negative fixture without weakening literal visible payload detection; rerun once after memory refresh.

entries.mistake: After protocol-only safeCode named arguments were excluded and the copy gate advanced, it rejected the next inherited X adapter quoted word internal at the safe-code mapping region.
entries.rootCause: The non-visible metadata rule covers safeCode named arguments but not internal diagnostic-code literals returned by a safe-code mapping function, and the gate still stops after its first emitted Write-Error.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, inspect only the bounded safe-code mapping and public-message boundary, classify the exact code literal, make violation reporting non-short-circuiting while retaining the final throw, and add a semantic safe-code-return negative fixture without excluding visible Internal copy.

entries.mistake: The non-short-circuit copy gate reported X adapter line 602 for quoted internal after the first safe-code mapping exclusion.
entries.rootCause: The remaining occurrence has not yet been classified as a dependency safe-code mapping or reachable public copy.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact bounded mapping and its publicMessage consumer; permit only a structurally proven auth-code return and keep visible Internal copy rejected.

entries.mistake: The non-short-circuit copy gate reported x_oauth2_pkce.dart line 84 for quoted endpoint.
entries.rootCause: The occurrence has not yet been classified as developer-only ArgumentError validation or reachable customer copy.
entries.prevention: Inspect only the exact constructor/validator and call boundary; permit a developer assertion only through a semantic ArgumentError fixture while retaining visible endpoint rejection.

entries.mistake: The non-short-circuit copy gate reported review_journey_services.dart line 1645 for quoted internal.
entries.rootCause: The occurrence has not yet been classified as an input error-code pattern mapped to separate customer-safe copy or direct visible text.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact switch arm and returned message; permit only code-to-safe-message mapping syntax and keep literal visible Internal copy rejected.

entries.mistake: The non-short-circuit copy gate reported review_journey_services.dart line 2029 for quoted bootstrap.
entries.rootCause: The occurrence has not yet been classified as a diagnostic/telemetry literal or reachable customer copy.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact statement and downstream surface; permit only structurally non-visible diagnostics with a negative fixture and retain visible Bootstrap rejection.

entries.mistake: Fresh integration v2 was locally created and verified from repair tip 0b83816, then the broader copy gate required a later qualified repair tip 5e20dc9 before v2 was pushed.
entries.rootCause: The final combined copy gate ran after the first fresh integration merge, so its legitimate repair follow-up advanced the only approved feature branch beyond v2's second parent.
entries.prevention: Preserve unpushed v2 unchanged as stale evidence; never reset, amend or add a second merge; bind a new v3 work ID, ticket, branch, worktree and exact merge subject, admit only remote-qualified 5e20dc9 from a fresh governance-tag checkout, and rerun all final gates before push.

entries.mistake: After v3 passed 194 frontend, 594 backend and 7 hosting tests plus analysis, copy and lock gates, check-interaction-contracts.ps1 rejected the inherited template /app/auth/$operationPath as an unregistered literal route.
entries.rootCause: The static route extractor does not distinguish Dart interpolated route templates from literal navigable destinations.
entries.prevention: Preserve v3 unpushed; inspect the exact extractor and registered-route oracle, ignore only route strings containing a Dart interpolation token, add positive literal and negative interpolated fixtures, retain final missing-literal rejection, and complete all static gates on the repair branch before binding another integration identity.

entries.mistake: The interpolated-route fixture and normalization passed, but the interaction gate still rejected normalized /app/auth/dynamic because the router's corresponding auth destinations are not present in its literal path extraction set.
entries.rootCause: The first correction assumed simple interpolation normalization would match a literal parameterized router path without first proving how auth callback destinations are composed in journey_router.dart.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, inspect only the auth route composition and the adapter operation allowlist; require the template prefix plus exact finite operation set through a semantic fixture, skip only that proven template, and retain rejection for arbitrary interpolated app routes.

entries.mistake: After the exact external auth callback template was excluded, the interaction gate advanced and rejected inherited email_link_runtime_configuration.dart target /app as an unregistered navigation destination.
entries.rootCause: The extractor scans every quoted /app string without distinguishing Firebase email continue-URI base paths from in-app GoRouter navigation calls, and still short-circuits at the first Write-Error.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, inspect the bounded email continue-URI contract, add an exact owner/content semantic exclusion with positive and wrong-owner fixtures, make violation reporting non-short-circuiting while retaining the final throw, then classify all remaining targets in one pass.

entries.mistake: After non-short-circuit interaction reporting, the gate emitted thirteen inherited targets across JourneySession, Buy invoice and legacy containment: eight trailing-slash dynamic prefixes, one braced invoice route and four legacy compatibility targets.
entries.rootCause: The literal extractor evaluates quoted route fragments independently from adjacent identifiers/interpolation and does not distinguish legacy containment destinations from primary registered GoRouter paths.
entries.prevention: Register every emitted target as an atomic machine ticket, compare each exact source construction with router or containment ownership, build a semantic target classifier that accepts only proven dynamic prefixes, parameterized invoice routes and exact legacy containment targets, retain arbitrary prefix/literal rejection fixtures, and rerun the complete gate once.

entries.mistake: After the interaction gate passed, check-buy-approved-reference.ps1 rejected evidence/buy-complete-v1-verification.json because its working hash differs from the immutable manifest hash.
entries.rootCause: The broad final gate has not yet classified whether the evidence owner is an inherited common sealed-tip byte representation, a line-ending projection or prohibited reference drift.
entries.prevention: Compare raw and canonical hashes plus Git blob identity across governance, production, Codex, Cursor and repair; never rewrite the immutable expected hash; permit only an exact branch-limited two-sealed-tip/current-byte or canonical text representation with negative drift fixtures, otherwise stop for evidence-owner correction.

entries.mistake: Regression memory rejected REG-20260826-3759 because its evidence array copied the gate's approved-root-relative label evidence/buy-complete-v1-verification.json as if it were a repository-root path.
entries.rootCause: The registration did not resolve the gate label through approved-references before writing the permanent repository evidence owner.
entries.prevention: Resolve the exact filename with rg --files, replace only the invalid evidence member with the canonical repository path, update the registry binding and rerun memory before reference classification.

entries.mistake: After interaction and immutable Buy reference gates passed, check-social-protected-baseline.ps1 rejected the integrated tree because its fixed inventory expects 119 files while the sealed runtime/Chat tree contains 231.
entries.rootCause: The historical protected baseline gate requires exact legacy inventory cardinality and has no machine-bound overlay proof for the founder-authorized Codex and Cursor feature tips.
entries.prevention: Inspect the gate schema and exact added/changed/deleted inventory relative to its protected baseline; retain every historical owner/hash check, permit only a branch-limited overlay whose current protected subtree equals the final remote-qualified repair tip, add missing/changed/extra negative fixtures, and never rewrite the historical baseline manifest.

entries.mistake: REG-20260826-3761 initially referenced a guessed config/social-protected-baseline.json owner, but exact rg --files discovery found only the gate script and no separate config manifest.
entries.rootCause: The registration assumed a conventional external baseline manifest before reading whether the live gate embeds its baseline inventory.
entries.prevention: Remove the nonexistent evidence member, bind only existing owners, inspect the live gate after refreshed memory, and do not invent a replacement manifest path.

entries.mistake: The combined policy update for the Social protected gate was rejected with zero change because its registryBinding hunk used an older count/hash anchor after later copy/interaction registrations had already advanced the working policy.
entries.rootCause: The patch combined the new owner additions with a remembered binding preimage instead of reading the current two live binding lines.
entries.prevention: Recompute the final registry generation, read the exact current binding and owner neighborhoods, then patch binding and owner arrays as separate operations before memory replay.

entries.mistake: After the sealed Social overlay gate passed, check-buy-protected-baseline.ps1 stopped because its default artifacts/quality/buy-protected-baseline-r40-3-20260801-49/BASELINE.json is absent from the isolated repair worktree.
entries.rootCause: The protected Buy gate assumes a local retained baseline artifact and has no confined immutable fallback to the production checkout used by the regression-memory dependency model.
entries.prevention: Inspect the gate parameters and exact production artifact availability; prefer an explicit existing baseline path when supported, otherwise add a confined read-only production fallback with path/hash identity and missing/tampered negative fixtures; do not copy or regenerate the baseline.

entries.mistake: After protected Buy passed through its sealed overlay, check-buy-backend-contract-boundary.ps1 rejected acceptance_policy_governance_contract.test.ts as an unapproved backend owner.
entries.rootCause: The boundary allowlist predates sealed commerce contract/test additions and short-circuits at its first Write-Error, so the complete owner delta is unknown.
entries.prevention: Make owner violation reporting non-short-circuiting while retaining final failure, inventory every emitted owner, compare exact backend subtree identity with the remote-qualified repair product merge, add a branch-limited sealed overlay or exact owner additions with forbidden-owner negative fixtures, and never broaden data egress or provider roots.

entries.mistake: After the sealed backend boundary passed, check-buy-data-egress-boundary.ps1 rejected buy_v2_shop_chat.dart for an unapproved clipboard write.
entries.rootCause: The historical Buy egress gate predates Cursor's explicit selected-message Copy action and has not distinguished user-invoked local clipboard output from automatic/network data egress.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact clipboard call, message-selection/action guard and tests; allow only the sealed byte-exact Chat owner on branch-limited repair/integration overlays or an exact user-action pattern, retain automatic clipboard and network/storage negative fixtures, and make violation reporting complete before replay.

entries.mistake: The combined data-egress policy update was rejected with zero change because it again bundled owner additions with a stale registryBinding preimage during the same accumulating static-gate correction commit.
entries.rootCause: The binding anchor was copied from an earlier generation instead of read from the live dirty policy immediately before patching.
entries.prevention: Compute the final registry generation, read the live binding, patch binding alone, then patch exact owner-array adjacency separately; never combine a moving generation preimage with unrelated owner additions.

entries.mistake: After Buy egress passed, check-brand-integrity.ps1 -Surface App rejected the integrated Buy theme motion because it expects exactly one canvas and one header integration.
entries.rootCause: The historical brand static assertion predates the sealed Cursor Buy screen structure and has not been compared with the current motion/theme ownership or tests.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact brand assertion and sealed Buy theme symbols, prove one effective canvas owner and truthful header behavior through source/tests, update only the static oracle or branch-limited sealed projection with duplicate/missing negative fixtures, and retain all other App brand checks.

entries.mistake: A read-only Buy theme symbol search passed apps/mobile/lib/ui_v2/buy/*.dart as a literal Windows path to rg, which rejected the invalid filename after the gate-path search succeeded.
entries.rootCause: The command used a shell-style path glob instead of searching the directory root with rg's --glob option.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, search the exact Buy directory root with --glob '*.dart' and discard the failed symbol inventory.

entries.mistake: The sealed Buy canvas/header branch passed its first conditional assertions, then brand integrity still rejected missing buy-header-signature-shop from a later unconditional historical cinematic-header token block.
entries.rootCause: The first oracle correction scoped only the integration-source header tokens and did not include the subsequent motion-source cinematic header assertions owned by the same removed header design.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, inspect the complete contiguous historical header assertion block, guard all obsolete cinematic-header tokens under the non-sealed branch, and require the sealed branch's exact header-absence/navigation-motion structure plus existing Buy tests before one replay.

entries.mistake: The brand follow-up binding patch was rejected with zero change because the accumulating static-gate work again made the remembered policy generation stale.
entries.rootCause: The command did not scalar-read the live policy binding immediately before applying the registry update.
entries.prevention: For the remainder of this bounded correction, always emit only current registry count/hash and current policy count/hash, then patch those exact two lines alone before any other policy hunk.

entries.mistake: After both cinematic header assertion groups were correctly scoped, brand integrity advanced and rejected an obsolete longQueryBandHeight search-band token absent from the sealed Cursor Buy structure.
entries.rootCause: Historical Buy integration assertions continue beyond the header groups into a legacy search-band contract, so piecemeal token guards remain incomplete.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, locate the exact end of the contiguous historical Buy integration block, keep shared palette/motion primitives and later non-Buy brand checks unconditional, and for sealed Buy require the byte-exact audited screen plus current Buy screen/navigation/search tests instead of any obsolete token in that block.

entries.mistake: After the complete historical Buy search/header block was scoped, brand integrity advanced and rejected the sealed Chat source for not containing the old canonical launcher icon expression.
entries.rootCause: The Chat brand assertion predates the standalone native Chat/inbox navigation accepted in the sealed runtime tree and has not been compared with the current Mool return control and exact-return tests.
entries.prevention: Inspect the exact Chat source owner, current Mool/back control and C10D return tests; accept only a byte-exact sealed Chat projection with current brand/navigation symbols and missing/changed negative facts, while retaining the historical launcher assertion on ordinary branches.

entries.mistake: After sealed standalone Chat branding was accepted, brand integrity advanced and rejected the protected Social Mool entry in screen04_universal_components.dart.
entries.rootCause: The historical assertion requires a specific grid_view icon regex and has not been reconciled with the sealed Social navigation projection already covered by RT-07/08 and Mool return tests.
entries.prevention: Compare the exact Social/creator entry owners with the audited product merge, require their current Mool labels, action identities and return semantics under a branch-limited byte-exact projection, retain the historical regex on ordinary branches, and add negative fact fixtures.

entries.mistake: Fresh integration v3 was locally verified and kept unpushed, then the full static App gates required branch-limited oracle corrections that advance the qualified repair tip again.
entries.rootCause: V3 was created before every check.ps1 static component had completed, so later legitimate gate repairs changed only scripts/config/docs after its automatic merge.
entries.prevention: Preserve v3 unchanged and unpushed; bind one final v4 ticket/branch/worktree/subject in the same static-gate repair commit, run every static gate plus combined tests before v4 creation, admit only the final remote repair tip, and do not issue another integration identity before all final gates are complete.

entries.mistake: The final repair graph fixture rejected its sealed-parent/merge boundary condition after the post-merge static-gate owner set and v4 binding were expanded.
entries.rootCause: At least one expected scalar in the combined fixture condition remains stale relative to the live policy; the failure message groups parent, merge, correction-count, owner-count and conflict-count facts.
entries.prevention: After refreshed memory, project only those allowlisted scalar facts from policy and fixture source, update the single stale expectation, then rerun the focused graph fixture before any commit.

entries.mistake: The first Language-sheet correction passed simulated bottom-inset cases, but OPPO review showed the Hindi option clipped to 38 physical pixels at the bottom of a zero-inset application viewport.
entries.rootCause: The sheet used the reported view padding plus only the smallest spacing token; Android can already subtract system navigation from the application viewport and report zero bottom view padding, leaving no guaranteed internal clearance for the final option.
entries.prevention: Every compact sheet must retain an unconditional bottom clearance in addition to reported safe padding, assert equal full-height actions with and without reported insets, and verify the final action bounds on the acceptance device before founder handoff.

entries.mistake: The global Privacy and preferences hero exposed the internal phrase 'Language and service area apply across every main action.' to customers.
entries.rootCause: The accepted profile sweep retained a cross-module implementation explanation instead of describing the customer benefit in ordinary account language, and the copy gate did not classify 'main action' as internal terminology.
entries.prevention: Describe shared preferences by their user benefit without module, route, screen, workflow or main-action terminology; mount the hero in customer-copy tests and review all newly visible profile copy before the next UI-review APK.

entries.mistake: The first FIX1 OPPO install command passed the deeply nested retained-evidence APK path directly to ADB, which failed its local stat before transmitting any bytes to the device.
entries.rootCause: The candidate path exceeded the reliable Windows path boundary for the ADB client even though the file existed and had already passed artifact identity checks; the retained C17G prevention was not applied to this new UI-review candidate.
entries.prevention: For every Android install from a long evidence path, create one short-path transport copy, prove its SHA-256 equals the gated artifact, install only that copy, and preserve the original artifact and failed no-mutation attempt.

entries.mistake: The bottom-clearance correction protected the final Language choice by adding excessive blank sheet padding, producing a visually oversized popup around only two short choices.
entries.rootCause: Clearance was treated as empty-space padding instead of designing a compact intrinsic sheet with explicit full-height actions and removing the separate drag-handle band.
entries.prevention: Two-choice profile sheets must use compact intrinsic height, no redundant drag-handle band, minimal safe bottom spacing, and equal actions of at least 56 logical pixels so available space serves readable wording and touch comfort rather than blank area.

entries.mistake: The Service area sheet opened with Save and Use current location visible while Remove service area rendered below the usable OPPO viewport with zero accessibility bounds.
entries.rootCause: The intrinsic bottom sheet stacked a field and three actions without a compact action layout or guaranteed safe bottom clearance; its final recovery action was allowed to extend behind the Android navigation region.
entries.prevention: Service area must use a compact phone-fitted sheet where Save, current location and Remove remain fully visible with equal minimum tap targets; keyboard appearance must preserve scroll or repositioning, and OPPO evidence must prove nonzero bounds for the final recovery action.

entries.mistake: The first dynamic keyboard-inset test harness referenced ValueListenable and ValueNotifier without importing Flutter foundation, so the focused test failed at compilation before exercising the UI.
entries.rootCause: The harness assumed material.dart re-exported the foundation listenable type contract instead of declaring the direct dependency used by the test signature.
entries.prevention: Every test file must explicitly import the library that owns new public types, and a focused compile run must pass before interpreting any widget-fitment result.

entries.mistake: The first origin-return ticket worktree attempted a full checkout of retained historical artifacts and exhausted the Windows volume at roughly 40 percent, leaving no target directory and an unoccupied branch ref.
entries.rootCause: The repository contains large immutable APK and device-evidence owners that are unnecessary for profile source work, while free-space qualification was not performed before a full worktree checkout.
entries.prevention: Before creating another large-repository worktree, qualify free bytes and use a no-checkout sparse worktree that excludes historical artifacts while including exact mandatory evidence files; preserve all retained evidence and never delete it to force checkout success.

entries.mistake: Cache cleanup removed the tracked .dart_tool directory and the clean-support guard then failed to restore package_config.json and package_graph.json because their parent directory no longer existed.
entries.rootCause: The restoration helper writes saved bytes directly but does not recreate deleted parent directories before WriteAllBytes; flutter clean deletes the complete generated directory.
entries.prevention: Do not run flutter clean through this guard until its parent-directory behavior is corrected; if this exact failure occurs, recreate only .dart_tool and restore the four tracked generated owners with checkout-index, then prove both closed worktrees remain clean.

entries.mistake: When Privacy and preferences was restored without a Navigator history but carried a valid Food return location, Back ignored that origin and navigated to Work home.
entries.rootCause: The destination used a hard-coded Work fallback whenever context.canPop was false, even though global profile is shared by every main action and restored routes can retain an exact return query.
entries.prevention: Global profile destinations must prefer a validated in-app return location when history is unavailable, reject circular or external returns, and use the neutral Mool hub rather than a module-specific fallback; tests must cover direct restore and ordinary stack pop separately.

entries.mistake: The first cross-module profile/navigation run used --no-pub in a fresh sparse worktree whose tracked package configuration did not contain share_plus, so seven wider tests failed during compilation before executing behavior.
entries.rootCause: Focused profile tests did not compile the Social share owner, and the broad suite was started without first hydrating the locked dependency graph inside the same clean-support operation.
entries.prevention: In every fresh or sparse worktree, run flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile and the affected broad Flutter suite in one clean-support invocation; do not interpret missing-package compilation as a product regression.

entries.mistake: The first OPPO origin-return replay rejected the post-Back hierarchy because it required both literal 'Order Food' and 'Search food' fragments, even though the captured hierarchy size matched the Food screen and had not yet been classified by stable identities.
entries.rootCause: The device assertion coupled navigation acceptance to mutable customer copy instead of a stable route-specific semantic owner, and combined two facts in one failure condition.
entries.prevention: Classify the retained returned hierarchy before retry, assert Food using stable semantic/action identities such as the Food global profile and search surface, and report each missing fact independently without changing the installed candidate.

entries.mistake: Personal profile, Privacy and preferences, Security, and Help each rendered a large outlined circular Back control that competed with the page title and looked unlike a restrained native navigation affordance.
entries.rootCause: The four destination AppBars duplicated IconButton.outlined styling and an iOS-specific chevron instead of sharing one transparent platform-adaptive profile Back owner.
entries.prevention: All global-profile destination AppBars must use one shared 44-point transparent Back control with BackButtonIcon platform adaptation, no border or filled circle, and source tests that reject duplicated outlined or hard-coded chevron implementations.

entries.mistake: Buy displayed a custom animated orange, white and green circular pointer ring on every tap while the global theme also enabled InkSparkle, making feedback conspicuous, slow-feeling and inconsistent with professional native controls.
entries.rootCause: Tap acknowledgement was implemented as an app-wide pointer overlay instead of relying on each control's bounded highlight or restrained press scale; the global sparkle factory added another circular effect.
entries.prevention: Remove the Buy pointer overlay and tricolour painter, use NoSplash globally, retain only bounded low-opacity highlights and existing short press scales, and enforce source/widget tests that reject the ring, InkSparkle and semantic interception.

entries.mistake: The first tap-feedback test declared Semantics with const, but the pinned Flutter SDK exposes a non-const constructor, so the test failed before behavior execution.
entries.rootCause: The test assumed constructor constness instead of compiling against the repository-pinned Flutter API.
entries.prevention: Use const only for verified constructors in the pinned SDK and complete a focused compile before interpreting interaction behavior.

entries.mistake: The first no-ring widget test rejected Material's unrelated internal CustomPaint even though the Buy tap-ring keys and painter source were absent.
entries.rootCause: The assertion searched the complete widget tree by a generic framework type instead of the removed overlay's owned keys and source symbol.
entries.prevention: Verify ring removal through exact mool-buy-tap keys and _MoolTapRingPainter source absence; never treat unrelated framework CustomPaint widgets as evidence of the custom ring.

entries.mistake: The first affected-suite command included the complete ui_v2/motion directory, which contains obsolete R51.3-R51.13 header experiments and historical goldens that fail against the accepted current Buy structure.
entries.rootCause: Directory-level selection treated historical review experiments as one current regression suite instead of selecting the active tap owner and current Buy screen tests.
entries.prevention: For this ticket run the exact tap-acknowledgement test, design-system test and active Buy screen suite; preserve historical golden failures without updating or using them as acceptance authority.

entries.mistake: The first Personal-profile origin-return change appended a return query before Social's exact route comparison, so the destination no longer received surface=social and rendered the light profile theme inside Social.
entries.rootCause: Origin continuity and contextual surface were composed in separate route layers, while the Social caller detected the Personal destination through exact full-string equality rather than an already-complete destination URI.
entries.prevention: The shared profile launcher must compose return and contextual surface query parameters into one destination URI before handing it to any module; Social tests must prove the dark profile surface and exact Back return together.

entries.mistake: The first r61.12 RuntimeUiReview wrapper attempt stopped before APK generation because the sparse UI worktree omitted backend/functions/src/index.ts, which the mandatory public-auth build-control self-test reads.
entries.rootCause: The sparse checkout included mobile source and the build scripts but not every read-only source owner transitively inspected by the authorized wrapper's self-tests.
entries.prevention: Before any sparse-worktree Android build, materialize the complete read set of the authorized wrapper and its self-tests, including backend/functions source and local mobile packages, then run the wrapper preflight before artifact generation.

entries.mistake: The first fully hydrated r61.12 build assembled the raw debug APK but exhausted the Windows volume while Flutter copied it to outputs/flutter-apk, so the wrapper failed and no artifact was authorized.
entries.rootCause: Prebuild checked source and gates but did not reserve enough free space for Gradle intermediates plus both the assembled APK and Flutter's final output copy.
entries.prevention: Before retrying an Android review build, preserve any failed raw or partial APK as unpromotable evidence and require at least four GiB of free local space immediately before the wrapper; only the wrapper-copied artifact may be installed.

entries.mistake: The signed-out Security page exposed a Sign in action that navigated directly to /sign-in without starting JourneySession authentication, so the production router could immediately return the ready user elsewhere instead of fulfilling the tap.
entries.rootCause: The isolated Security widget test asserted only a route string and did not exercise the real router stage machine, return location, cancellation or restored-route continuity.
entries.prevention: Security Sign in must call beginSignIn with its complete current URI as both return and cancel location before navigation; real-router tests must prove sign-in remains open, cancellation returns to Security, and the nested originating main-section return is retained.

entries.mistake: Help opened Security and Preferences with plain routes, so ordinary Back worked only while the Navigator stack survived; restored child routes rejected /app/ask as a safe return and lost both Help and its originating main section.
entries.rootCause: The tests covered immediate push/pop but not a reconstructed child route containing a nested Help return URI, and the shared safe-return allow-list omitted the Help destination.
entries.prevention: Help topic taps must compose the complete current Help URI and contextual surface into the child route, /app/ask must be accepted as a safe nested profile return, and tests must destroy stack history then prove child Back to Help and Help Back to the exact main origin.

entries.mistake: The first Help-topic continuity assertion read router.routeInformationProvider while a pushed child page was active; the provider still exposed the root Work location, producing a false missing-return failure.
entries.rootCause: The test used a root router information oracle for nested Navigator state instead of reading GoRouterState from the mounted Help, Security or Preferences destination element.
entries.prevention: For pushed profile destinations, assert the active URI through GoRouterState.of on a stable mounted destination key; reserve routeInformationProvider assertions for go/replace roots whose ownership is independently proven.

entries.mistake: Food, Travel, Care, Work, Pay and provider/workspace scaffolds each rendered a separate outlined circular Back control with a hard-coded iOS chevron, diverging from the approved sleek native profile control.
entries.rootCause: Ten vertical scaffolds copied IconButton.outlined and Icons.arrow_back_ios_new_rounded instead of consuming one app-wide platform-adaptive navigation control.
entries.prevention: All shared vertical scaffolds must use one 44-point transparent MoolNativeBackButton with BackButtonIcon, restrained local highlight, stable semantics and no duplicated outlined circle or platform-specific arrow source.

entries.mistake: The global profile exposed Help & support and an Open support Chat CTA even though every main section already owns a Chat entry, creating a duplicate path that opened the generic global inbox without profile-specific intent fulfilment.
entries.rootCause: Account destinations and contextual communication were mixed in one profile panel instead of keeping profile for identity/preferences/security and routing support through the single shared context-aware Chat owner.
entries.prevention: The global profile must not expose Help or support Chat; every main section must invoke one shared Chat screen with exact context and return continuity, and Shop must consume that owner through integration rather than clone it.

entries.mistake: The r61.18 OPPO panel showed 'Create a provider worksp…' because the global contextual card forced every title into one line inside the narrow profile panel.
entries.rootCause: The shared context title used maxLines 1 with ellipsis even though professional action titles such as Create a provider workspace need two lines at the approved panel width.
entries.prevention: Global profile context titles must allow two proportional lines while preserving the CTA and detail, with a compact Work panel test and OPPO visual readback rejecting title truncation.

entries.mistake: A delegated-checkpoint read requested 24 turns even though the live thread reader accepts at most 10, so the read was rejected before returning any checkpoint content.
entries.rootCause: The continuation request used a remembered broad history size instead of the live tool's enforced parameter range.
entries.prevention: Every continuation read must use the callable tool's current bounded parameter contract, request at most 10 turns, and page only when the returned cursor proves older history is required.

entries.mistake: A grouped exact-ticket search across config and quality roots completed without a usable projection, so it established no ticket identity or owner evidence.
entries.rootCause: Two independent searches, exit classifications and a structured projection were combined across a large quality root instead of preserving one bounded result at a time.
entries.prevention: Ticket identity recovery must search config and quality roots in separate calls, normalize exit 1 independently and accept only explicit bounded counts plus exact returned matches.

entries.mistake: The first minimal coordination-binding patch inserted a pending hash placeholder instead of the exact current registry SHA-256, temporarily leaving the policy unparsable by its machine gate.
entries.rootCause: The binding edit was issued before recomputing the registry digest after the immediately preceding incident registrations.
entries.prevention: After every registry append, parse the registry, emit its exact count and SHA-256, then copy those scalars directly into one bounded binding patch with no placeholder state.

entries.mistake: The corrected 10-turn source-thread read still requested 30000 characters per item even though the live reader accepts at most 20000, so no history was returned.
entries.rootCause: Only the previously rejected turn-limit field was corrected; the second live bounded parameter was not validated before retry.
entries.prevention: Before every thread-history call, validate both turnLimit at no more than 10 and maxOutputCharsPerItem at no more than 20000, then reuse those exact bounds on every cursor page.

entries.mistake: The first codex_ui coordination replay rejected the established ticket history as not beginning with one non-merge commit without exposing whether native exit or parsed parent shape caused the rejection.
entries.rootCause: The new compatibility assertion combined native process status and parsed parent cardinality after additional PowerShell evaluation, making the failing subcondition opaque.
entries.prevention: Capture the git parent command exit immediately, normalize its one returned row separately, assert the exact two-token non-merge shape and retain a focused negative merge fixture in the checker path.

entries.mistake: The codex_ui gate repeated its non-merge rejection after immediate exit capture even though an independent projection proved exit 0, one parent row and two exact commit tokens.
entries.rootCause: The parent command, row normalization and token cardinality remained coupled inside one compound compatibility block, so the gate still produced a false rejection for valid linear history.
entries.prevention: Validate native exit, row count and token count as three independent assertions, then assign the parent only after all three pass; keep the exact valid current-history projection as the positive fixture.

entries.mistake: The separated parent check proved native exit and one row but still rejected the split token count although the same literal history projected one child and one parent.
entries.rootCause: PowerShell collection cardinality inside the checker remained an unreliable oracle for the native one-line commit-parent contract.
entries.prevention: Validate the one parent row against the exact child-space-parent SHA pattern, then extract the parent from that already-qualified row without using array count as the history oracle.

entries.mistake: The exact parent-row regex also rejected the established linear first ticket commit despite independent Git evidence of its single parent.
entries.rootCause: Formatted native parent-row text remained an unnecessary parsing boundary for a fact Git can expose directly.
entries.prevention: Resolve the first parent with git rev-parse commit-caret, require one SHA, and independently require the commit to be absent from a min-parents-two probe; do not parse formatted parent rows.

entries.mistake: The replacement merge probe used rev-list on the first ticket commit and found an older merge ancestor, falsely classifying the first ticket commit itself as a merge.
entries.rootCause: The probe traversed reachable history instead of projecting only the selected commit's direct parent list.
entries.prevention: Use git show format-percent-P on the exact first ticket commit, require one parent SHA and compare it with rev-parse commit-caret; never use an ancestor-walking query for commit-local merge classification.

entries.mistake: The direct percent-P versus rev-parse parent comparison also rejected the same valid linear ticket history, leaving formatted parent representation as a false-failure source.
entries.rootCause: Two native parent representations were compared textually even though the real invariant is zero merge commits inside the exact ticket range.
entries.prevention: Resolve the base with rev-parse commit-caret, then query merges only in base-dot-dot-HEAD and require zero; this scopes the oracle to the ticket and removes parent-format comparison.

entries.mistake: The range-scoped merge check rejected the existing Chat ticket although its visible commit sequence appeared linear, so the compatibility gate still lacked an exact merge identity projection.
entries.rootCause: The checker reported only aggregate presence and did not prove which exact commit and parent count produced the result before blocking the established ticket.
entries.prevention: After registration, project only merge commit IDs and parent counts in the exact ticket range; preserve existing history and admit it only through a literal compatibility rule if the founder-approved sequence requires one retained merge.

entries.mistake: The first focused Conversation Info analysis failed because the new identity card referenced a nonexistent MoolColors.outline token.
entries.rootCause: A conventional design-token name was inferred instead of copied from the exact current MoolColors declaration.
entries.prevention: Before adding a shared design token reference, inspect the declaring design owner and use only an exact existing member; focused analysis must pass before widget execution.

entries.mistake: The MoolColors token correction was applied after REG3813 moved the registry generation but before replaying the regression and incremental UI implementation gates.
entries.rootCause: The correction followed the exact design-token inspection directly and skipped the mandatory generation refresh boundary created by incident registration.
entries.prevention: After every registry append and binding update, the next mutation must be preceded by the implementation regression gate and the existing codex_ui incremental gate; no source correction may intervene.

entries.mistake: The first Conversation Info widget cycle failed when the paused composer placed a themed OutlinedButton inside a Row and inherited the app-wide infinite-width minimum.
entries.rootCause: The global full-width button theme was reused in a horizontal action slot without a finite local width and minimum-size override.
entries.prevention: Every button inside a Row must own finite width and a local finite minimum size of at least 44 logical pixels; compact tests must render the paused state before qualification.

entries.mistake: The compact Conversation Info test called ensureVisible for the off-screen blocking tile before the lazy ListView had constructed it, producing a no-element failure.
entries.rootCause: The test treated an unbuilt lazy child as an existing off-screen render object instead of scrolling its persistent list owner until construction.
entries.prevention: Compact tests must use bounded dragUntilVisible on the keyed Conversation Info list before measuring a later lazy child; ensureVisible runs only after one element exists.

entries.mistake: The post-Conversation Info gate set invoked the historical C10D static checker, which still requires the retired MoolGlobalNavigationV2 Chat dock spelling and rejected the already-approved shared contextual Chat architecture.
entries.rootCause: A predecessor gate was selected by filename without auditing its active source-shape assumptions against the current global contextual Chat ticket.
entries.prevention: Successor Chat qualification uses the current contextual shell test, exact-return C10D widget journey and incremental lane gate; the historical static checker is not replayed without an explicit successor mode.

entries.mistake: The first cleanup of Flutter-generated tracked metadata was rejected because a standard git reverse-diff hunk with line ranges was passed into the repository apply_patch format.
entries.rootCause: Git unified-diff syntax was assumed to be directly interchangeable with the custom apply_patch update format.
entries.prevention: For exact generated-text restoration, construct one apply_patch whole-file replacement from independently read current and HEAD content, or use formatter-owned regeneration; never pass raw git diff range headers.

entries.mistake: A grouped RuntimeUiReview build-control search across the complete scripts and config roots returned no usable projection, so it established no current machine-state path or build contract.
entries.rootCause: Several broad literal patterns and two roots were combined instead of reading the already-known wrapper and its exact foundation gate independently.
entries.prevention: Runtime UI build recovery reads one exact wrapper or checker owner per command, then inspects only the returned state-path contract; no combined scripts-plus-config search is used.

entries.mistake: The first r61.34 candidate state expanded the short commit output into an incorrect full HEAD instead of copying the exact git rev-parse scalar.
entries.rootCause: Candidate JSON was authored before the full 40-character HEAD was independently projected and copied.
entries.prevention: Project git rev-parse HEAD immediately before candidate-state creation, copy that exact scalar without manual completion, then parse and compare state HEAD before any machine gate.

entries.mistake: The first r61.34 APK gate reused premium-motion evidence paths from an old Buy candidate that are absent from this isolated Chat worktree, so prebuild failed closed.
entries.rootCause: The canonical policy fields were copied together with candidate-specific historical evidence paths instead of binding the current Chat contract and disposition owners.
entries.prevention: Keep the canonical motion policy and coverage authority, but bind candidateContract and disposition to current existing Chat ticket owners before the first APK gate; verify every path independently.

entries.mistake: The first r61.34 OPPO Chat-node parser failed before output because it accessed the hyphenated content-desc XML attribute through PowerShell dot syntax.
entries.rootCause: Android UIAutomator attribute names were treated as ordinary PowerShell object properties despite the hyphen token.
entries.prevention: Device hierarchy parsers read hyphenated attributes through GetAttribute with exact literal names, emit only bounded text/clickable/enabled/bounds fields and never repeat the completed capture.

entries.mistake: The installed r61.34 OPPO conversation showed a visible RIGHT OVERFLOWED BY 16 stripe because Video, Voice and a new Info icon competed with the conversation identity in the compact AppBar.
entries.rootCause: Widget coverage opened the new destination but did not reject the final three-action AppBar geometry at the OPPO width before building.
entries.prevention: Retain the approved Voice and Video actions, open Conversation Info by tapping the familiar conversation identity/title, and require compact large-text header fit plus OPPO screenshot evidence before acceptance.

entries.mistake: The first r61.35 header correction patch was atomically rejected because it used the pre-format Info IconButton layout rather than the exact current formatted source.
entries.rootCause: The source hunk was composed from earlier chat context after formatting had changed the onPressed layout.
entries.prevention: Read the exact current title and trailing ranges immediately before each bounded patch, change the scaffold callback and removed icon in separate verified hunks, then format again.

entries.mistake: The first r61.35 OPPO tap on Order MS-240782 produced a blank blue app surface with only system bars instead of the conversation thread.
entries.rootCause: The first retained frame does not yet classify whether the route lost its Flutter content, the app process failed, or the capture landed on a transient window.
entries.prevention: Do not repeat the tap; retain the screenshot and hierarchy, then inspect bounded activity focus, process presence, hierarchy ownership and sanitized fatal markers before choosing a source or device correction.

entries.mistake: The r61.34 overflow was attributed to the new global Conversation Info icon, but the captured screen was Cursor's Shop-specific order conversation and never rendered that global Info action.
entries.rootCause: The device route was inferred from the shared Chat entry instead of identifying the visible screen's exact source owner and semantic contract before selecting a correction.
entries.prevention: Before a device defect changes source, prove the visible owner from route semantics and current source inventory; Shop remains Cursor-owned, while this ticket qualifies Conversation Info only through a non-Shop global Chat context such as Work.

entries.mistake: The r61.35 Last Seen recovery visually rendered a full-height Continue in Chat button, but OPPO UIAutomator exported bounds [48,1380][672,1442], only about 31 logical pixels high.
entries.rootCause: The shared Chat bottom sheet protected the visual system inset but did not lift its final action above the app's additional Android exported-semantics clipping boundary.
entries.prevention: Apply the existing shared Android exported-semantics bottom clearance to Chat recovery sheets, retain the visual 48-pixel button and require OPPO exported clickable height of at least 44 logical pixels.

entries.mistake: r61.36 still exported Continue in Chat at about 31 logical pixels because the semantics clearance was computed inside the modal route after useSafeArea removed the caller's top viewPadding.
entries.rootCause: The shared token was correct, but its input context no longer retained the Android system inset needed to calculate the lift.
entries.prevention: Compute exported-semantics clearance from the conversation context before showModalBottomSheet, pass the scalar into the safe-area wrapper and test that exact caller-to-sheet boundary.

entries.mistake: The first caller-owned clearance change made the shared sheet parameter required but updated only the unavailable-capability caller, leaving two existing Chat sheet constructors uncompilable.
entries.rootCause: The constructor-consumer inventory was not completed before the API change was analyzed.
entries.prevention: Inventory every _ChatBottomSheetSafeArea constructor first, compute caller-owned clearance for each sheet launch and update all consumers in the same source wave before focused analysis.

entries.mistake: The first r61.37 build refresh invoked the regression-memory build gate and incremental pre-build gate in one shell call, contrary to their independent evidence ownership.
entries.rootCause: Two already-known passing commands were compressed for latency instead of preserving one authoritative gate and exit per process.
entries.prevention: Run regression memory, incremental pre-build and APK state validation as three separate shell calls with their own exit metadata before the wrapper preflight.

entries.mistake: The first Open Feed/Person+ collision test found the separated compact action group ended at y=499 while the 320x568 navigation boundary begins at y=496.
entries.rootCause: A centered SliverFillRemaining empty state used symmetric padding and left no rounding reserve above the fixed NavigationBar.
entries.prevention: Give the empty inbox content an asymmetric bottom reserve, keep both actions at least 44 pixels, and require their final rects to remain wholly above the compact navigation boundary.

entries.mistake: The first asymmetric-padding correction left the compact empty-inbox action bottom unchanged at y=499, so the exact empty-state geometry owner was not corrected.
entries.rootCause: A similar Center/Padding pattern was patched without first proving that the modified range was the _EmptyInbox action owner and that its layout affected the action-group position.
entries.prevention: Read the exact _EmptyInbox range, bind a keyed action-group transform or alignment directly to that owner and verify its rect moves above y=496 before the full suite.

entries.mistake: The Open Feed/Person+ test assumed the NavigationBar began at y=496, but the rendered keyed NavigationBar begins at y=499 and the action ends exactly at that boundary.
entries.rootCause: A calculated viewport-minus-nominal-height constant replaced the final rendered navigation geometry.
entries.prevention: Compare action rects with the actual chat-native-navigation rect, require no overlap with each other or navigation, and remove padding added only to satisfy the false constant.

entries.mistake: The rendered-navigation oracle found one empty-inbox action rect still overlaps the live chat NavigationBar at compact size.
entries.rootCause: The prior y equality observation did not identify which action rect or the exact navigation top before the strict overlap assertion ran.
entries.prevention: Project feed, start and navigation rect scalars in the focused test, then shift the keyed action group by the smallest explicit layout offset that proves zero overlap and stable 44-pixel targets.

entries.mistake: The first complete Open Feed journey test assumed the empty-inbox Open Feed action existed at its mounted Work route, but the rendered state exposed no such key.
entries.rootCause: The test coupled feed-route acceptance to an unproven initial emptiness state instead of entering Discover through the established nonempty Person+ journey.
entries.prevention: Seed one truthful existing thread, enter Discover through chat-new, then open Feed, return to the loaded people list and complete the connect-to-direct-Chat intent.

entries.mistake: The corrected Open Feed journey entered Discover first, which loaded people and legitimately removed the empty-state chat-discover-open-feed control before the next tap.
entries.rootCause: The test still selected a transient empty-state action rather than the persistent Social Chat menu action available with populated discovery.
entries.prevention: Mount Social-context Chat, open the persistent chat-more menu, choose Open public Feed, then verify Social Feed, Back to loaded Discover and direct Chat completion.

entries.mistake: The Social-context Feed test supplied /app/social?sub=feed as an unencoded nested return query, so Chat did not classify the entry as Social and omitted Open public Feed from its menu.
entries.rootCause: A nested route containing its own query was embedded directly instead of using the production chatRoute encoding contract.
entries.prevention: Encode the complete Social return URI as one query value, prove the Social Chat title/menu, then select the persistent Feed action.

entries.mistake: The persistent Open public Feed menu action remained absent because production exposed it only when Chat originated from Social.
entries.rootCause: Feed discovery was context-gated even though the shared communication contract requires the same public discovery intent from Work, Travel, Care, Food, Workspaces and other Chat entries.
entries.prevention: Expose one shared Open public Feed menu action in every Chat context, route to the existing Social Feed owner and preserve the exact originating Chat route on Back.

entries.mistake: After Chat opened the shared Social Feed, Android Back followed the approved Social shell contract instead of popping directly to the originating Chat route.
entries.rootCause: The test assumed generic Navigator pop semantics across a Social root that intentionally owns Back through the global shell.
entries.prevention: Preserve Social Back ownership, use the visible Social global Chat action as the forward continuation into messaging, then verify Chat Back returns to the Feed and the intent remains escapable through approved global navigation.

entries.mistake: On the r61.40 OPPO review runtime, Android Back from the open attachment tray exited the conversation instead of dismissing the tray first.
entries.rootCause: The composer PopScope blocked the route pop, but the shared ChatPageScaffold treated every blocked pop as a request for its exact-return fallback and navigated to the inbox.
entries.prevention: Let the active child surface consume a blocked pop before ChatPageScaffold uses its route fallback, close the tray and notice atomically, and prove the first Back retains the conversation in a deterministic widget test and on OPPO.

entries.mistake: The strengthened Feed author-message journey expected one Android Back from the direct conversation to return immediately to Feed.
entries.rootCause: The acceptance oracle skipped the shared Chat inbox level that intentionally sits between a direct thread and its originating Feed route.
entries.prevention: Verify the native hierarchy as thread to shared inbox to originating Feed, then continue through Discover and a second direct conversation without bypassing the existing shared destination.

entries.mistake: After scrolling Conversation Info to a call-availability switch, the existing local-change confirmation card could be inserted above the viewport and provide no immediate visible success feedback.
entries.rootCause: Session-local setting confirmation was owned only by a summary card near the top of a scrollable settings list.
entries.prevention: Keep the durable summary card and also show one floating in-context confirmation for every Chat, voice-call or video-call availability change; prove it at compact size after scrolling.

entries.mistake: The expanded global destination test retained the old assertion that Care Chat allowed only the clinic thread after task-helper and order-support deep routes were deliberately added.
entries.rootCause: The implementation and deep-return cases were updated before the earlier clinic-isolation oracle was synchronized to the audited Care destination set.
entries.prevention: Update the resolver allowlist assertion in the same bounded change as new Care destinations and require every allowed deep thread to return visibly under its actual thread-type filter.

entries.mistake: The context-aware safety tests called ensureVisible on a Conversation Info tile that had not yet been built below the compact lazy ListView viewport.
entries.rootCause: The test treated a lazily built destination as an offscreen rendered element instead of scrolling the owning Conversation Info list until the tile existed.
entries.prevention: Scroll the actual keyed Conversation Info Scrollable until the Safety destination is rendered, then assert its context-specific label and tap recovery.

entries.mistake: The transient Android Back test entered Work Chat and then tried to open the Home Basket People thread, which the approved Work business filter correctly hides.
entries.rootCause: The test fixture selected a conversation that was incompatible with its contextual origin filter before exercising the transient surfaces.
entries.prevention: Use the unfiltered Mool Chat origin or a thread matching the selected context whenever a test is about shared transient-surface Back behavior rather than filtering.

entries.mistake: The first aggregate r61.43 APK state used a P1-CHAT candidate prefix, which the authoritative APK gate rejected as an unsupported candidate family before any build.
entries.rootCause: The audit ticket shorthand was reused as the build candidate id instead of retaining the repository's established UAW candidate family contract.
entries.prevention: Use a UAW-CODEX candidate id for Chat RuntimeUiReview APKs, bind it consistently in machine state and runtime defines, and run the direct APK gate before the wrapper.

entries.mistake: On the r61.43 OPPO runtime, Search Assistance rendered truthful copy but its Search conversations action was clipped behind the system navigation bar.
entries.rootCause: The inbox-owned modal did not reuse the exported-semantics and bottom-inset clearance already proven for Chat capability and action sheets.
entries.prevention: Own one shared ChatBottomSheetSafeArea, apply it to every Chat sheet, keep scrollable keyboard padding inside it and assert the final 44-pixel action above the OPPO safe bottom.

entries.mistake: The r61.43 Work Conversation Info called Ramesh Kumar a business because safety wording was derived only from the thread's operational Business filter type.
entries.rootCause: Conversation filtering taxonomy and the real safety target identity were treated as the same concept.
entries.prevention: Model an optional person, business or conversation safety target, set the review helper explicitly to person, decode optional backend values and retain a safe type-based fallback.

entries.mistake: The first Search motion test expected the third Home Basket row to use the 240ms base duration even though the approved finite entry policy adds a bounded 20ms stagger per row.
entries.rootCause: The test asserted the base motion token instead of the final indexed duration owned by the rendered row.
entries.prevention: Calculate the bounded index stagger in the oracle, keep the final duration finite and still require every indexed row to resolve to zero under reduced motion.

entries.mistake: The first cross-surface motion test searched all tween builders below a message row and matched both the row-entry owner and its nested reaction owner.
entries.rootCause: The generic incoming-motion primitive exposed only a structural tween type, not a state-specific test identity.
entries.prevention: Key each incoming tween by its real state owner and assert the exact row, reaction, empty or status motion without descendant-count assumptions.

entries.mistake: The expanded suite cast the stable Search motion owner key directly to AnimatedSwitcher and also selected a generic descendant switcher after additional motion owners were introduced.
entries.rootCause: The tests conflated the semantic/hit owner widget with its inner visual animation and did not give the Chats/People/Discover section switcher an exact identity.
entries.prevention: Keep stable owner keys on motion wrappers, inspect their exact visual child when needed and assign a dedicated key to every independently asserted section animation.
